He then recited a verse: "The Great Way is not difficult; It simply avoids picking and choosing. When non-action is practiced, There is nothing left undone. If you wish to know the Buddhas of the three periods, Look at the present moment before your eyes. He then added
The Great Old Man saw that the man was still there. The Layman said, "I will only venture to ask you because you were a fellow student with my teacher.
The Master said, "If that is so, bring it up from the beginning and we shall deliberate together.
The Layman said, "Great Old Man, you must not speak of right and wrong with me. The Master said, "I take pity on your old age. The Layman said, "My fault! My fault!"
When Master Shilin saw Layman Pang approaching, he held up his whisk and said, "This does not fall within Danxia’s mechanism;
try and say a single phrase. The Layman snatched away the whisk and instead raised his own fist. The Master said, "That is precisely Danxia’s mechanism.
The Layman said, "Let us see who does not fall [into the trap]. The Master said, "Danxia suffers from dumbness; Master Pang suffers from deafness. The Layman said, "..."
The Master said, "Exactly so. The Master remained silent. The layman said, "I told you it was merely a coincidence. On another day, he asked the layman, "I have a question to ask;
Master, do not be stingy with your words. The layman said, "Please go ahead and ask. The Master said, "So you *are* stingy with your words?
The layman said, "Regarding this very inquiry, I did not realize I had fallen into his trap. The Master then covered his ears. The layman said, "..."
A Master of the Dharma. A Master of the Dharma.
Master Liang was a native of Shu. He was quite proficient in lecturing on the sutras and śāstras.

Upon visiting Mazu, Mazu asked, "I have heard it said that you, Master of the Dharma, lecture extensively on the sutras and śāstras; is this true? The Master replied, "I do not dare. Mazu asked, "With what, then, do you lecture? The Master replied, "With..."

The Master was giving a lecture on the *Awakening of Faith*. The Patriarch said, "The mind is like a skilled performer; the intellect is like the conductor. How can you hope to understand it through lecturing?
The Master raised his voice and said, "If the mind cannot be lectured upon, could empty space be lectured upon? The Patriarch said, "In fact, it is empty space that can be lectured upon.
The Master did not accept this and departed. As he was descending the steps, the Patriarch called out, "Lecturer! The Master turned his head. The Patriarch said, "It is."
"What is it? The Master attained a sudden and great enlightenment, whereupon he prostrated himself. The Patriarch said, "Why does this dull-witted monk prostrate?
The Master replied, "I thought that no one could equal me in the sutras and treatises I have studied.

Today, having been questioned by the Great Master, all the achievements of my life were instantly dissolved like ice. Having offered his thanks, he withdrew and went into seclusion in the western part of Hongzhou."
"Mountains. There is no further news.
A monk asked Master Heiyuan, "What is the teacher who does not appear in the world? The Master said, "Sudhana’s staff."
Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "A charcoal seller for ten years does not know the star beside the scale.
A monk asked Master Miling: "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said: "Ugliness is left to your own disdain."

"Unstained by the colors of clouds and mists. When the Master was about to pass into extinction, he left behind this verse: "The patriarchs are inconceivable; they are not permitted to remain forever in the world.
Let the great assembly reflect carefully: in the end, it is simply this. Having spoken these words, he became still.
Pang Jushi came to Master Qifeng. The Master said, "Why does a layman enter the monastic quarters so frequently? What are you looking for?
The Layman looked back at both sides and said, "Who says such a thing? The Master then gave a shout (*tuo*). The Layman said, "Right here."
The Master said, "Is this not the Way of the Open Court? The scholar said, "What about that which is behind? The Master turned his head and said, "Look! Look!
The scholar said, "The grass-robber has been utterly defeated. The scholar then asked, "How many li is it from here to the mountain peak?
The Master said, "Where have you come from? The scholar said, "It may indeed be called steep and hard; one cannot ask such things. The Master said, "How much is it? The scholar said, [silently].
"One, two, three. The Master said, "Four, five, six. The scholar asked, "Why do you not speak of seven? The Master said, "As soon as you speak of seven, there is already eight.
The scholar said, "I can abide here. The Master said, "Feel free to add more. The scholar gave a shout and departed; the Master followed him, also shouting.

When Master Dayang met with Master Yizhan, he asked him: "Lately there have been certain teachers who instruct people regarding what is before their eyes, telling them to realize the matter right before them and using this as a means of guiding others.
Do you understand the state when the literary patterns have not yet emerged? Yizhan said, "I wish to pose a question here; I do not know if it would be appropriate. The Master said: "Go ahead."
The Master replied, "You have already understood; do not speak of 'yes' or 'no. The monk asked, "Do you still recognize what is right before your eyes?
The Master said, "If it is right before your eyes, how would you go about recognizing it? The monk said, "In any case, it is subject to scrutiny. The Master asked, "By whom? The monk said, "By me.
The Master then gave a shout. The monk stepped back and stood there. The Master said, "You only know how to look forward; you do not know how to look behind. The monk said, "Snow."
On top of that, frost was added. The Master said, "In either case, there is no advantage.
A monk from Mount Hongluo in Youzhou had a verse for his disciples which said: "The son of Mount Hongluo dwells near the barbarians."
Among those who have attained liberation, half are Xis. When conversing and exchanging questions and answers, they understand nothing at all; it is pitiful that they only know "na-si-qi.
One day, Master Bailin encountered Layman Pang on the road and asked, "Have you gained strength from Mount Nanyue?"
[The Master] said, "Have you ever brought this phrase forward to anyone? The Layman said, "I have. The Master asked, "To whom did you bring it forward?
The Layman pointed to himself with his hand and said, "Master Pang. The Master said, "Truly a marvelous one; even Śāriputra and Subhūti could not praise him enough.
The Layman then asked, "Whom does the phrase by which you, Master, have attained power reach? The Master put on his bamboo hat and walked away. The Layman [followed].
He said, "The road is well-prepared. The Master did not look back again.
The Ox-Herd of Zhentou Monastery used to prepare his own meals to provide for the assembly of monks.

When it was time for the midday meal, he would carry the rice bucket to the front of the hall, perform a dance, and laugh loudly, saying, "Sons of the Bodhisattvas, come and eat! [A monk asked Changqing about the ancients clapping their hands.]

"Calling the monks to eat—what is the meaning of this? Changqing said, "It is very much like celebrating and praising because of the meal. A monk asked Daguang, "I do not understand what it is that you are celebrating and praising. Daguang performed a dance. The monk bowed, and Daguang said, "This wild fox spirit! Dongchan Zhi said, "The ancients personally prepared the food with their own hands;

having finished the dance, they called people to come and eat. What was their intention? Do you understand? As for Changqing and Daguang, were they clarifying the meaning of the ancients, or were they analyzing it for him on their own account? Now I ask you, Venerable Sir."

Every day, when holding your alms bowl and carrying your vessel, when welcoming [food] and sending it forth—should you act exactly as the ancients did, or is there a distinct principle? If you say there is a distinction, how do you manifest that distinction?

If you say they are the same, then when you happen upon their dance, you are again called a wild fox spirit. Do you have a point of realization here? If you have not yet realized it, where does your eye for traveling on pilgrimage lie?
A monk asked Master Heishui of Luojing, "What is the secret chamber? The Master said, "Cutting off one's ears and lying in the street.
The monk asked, "Who is the person within the secret chamber? The Master then changed hands and beat his breast.
A monk asked Master Lishan, "When all forms return to emptiness, where does emptiness return? The Master said, "The tongue does not leave the mouth. The monk asked, "Why does it not leave the mouth?
The Master said, "Because inner and outer are one and the same. Another asked, "Without passing through the kalpas of a *saṃgha*, one attains the Dharma-body.
I ask the Master to point this directly. The Master said, "The son inherits his father’s vocation. The monk asked, "How should one comprehend this? The Master said, [Silence].

When the Master did not apply any reprimand or censure, the monk said, "In that case, the assembly will surely rely upon you. The Master said, "Setting the assembly aside for a moment, what is the Dharma-body?
The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Ask me, and I shall tell you. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "Blooming flowers in the sky; a mirage. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, "Not..."
[The Master] asked, "How do you see it? [The monk] said, "Why is it so? The Master said, "Precisely because it is so.
When the Venerable Ruyuan of Shaoyou was ascending the hall, he said, "The direct meaning from the West—how could it be that there is no one among you who can express it?
Come forward and try to say it! At that time, a monk came forward and prostrated. The Master struck him and said, "It is!"

"At what time did he emerge from his head? He immediately returned to the abbot's quarters. (The monk related this to Changqing. Changqing said, "Not bad, not bad. Zifu spoke on his behalf, saying, "For the sake of the Master, he did not spare his own life.
When Yangshan was a novice, his voice was loud as he recited the sutras. The Master scolded him, saying, "This novice recites the sutras just like weeping.
Yangshan asked, "Huiji is only like this; I wonder how it is with the Master? The Master then looked at him. Yangshan—
[The Master] said, "If it is so, how does this differ from weeping? The Master then ceased speaking.
One day, when Master Songshan was drinking tea with Layman Pang, the Layman held up his tea bag and said, "Everyone has their share."
"Why is it that you cannot speak? The Master said, "Precisely because everyone possesses it, I cannot speak.
The Layman asked, "Why then can my elder brother speak? The Master said, "One must not remain without words. The Layman said, "Truly so."
"Clearly so," the Master said, and he proceeded to drink tea. The layman said, "Brother, you are drinking tea; why do you not bow to your guest?
The Master asked, "Who? The layman replied, "Pang Gong. The Master said, "Why bother to bow further?

Later, when Danxia heard of this, he remarked, "If it had not been for Songshan, I might have been confused by that old fellow for a while. When the layman heard this, he sent someone to convey his words to Danxia.
[The Master] said: "Why do you not grasp it before the bag has even been lifted?
Now, Master Chuanshan was a native of Shu. While he and Layman Pang were conversing, the Master asked, "Do you still remember the principle [you realized] when you saw Stonehead?
The Layman replied, "I am still able to rely on you, Master, to bring it up again. The Master said, "I knew all along that you had long been a practitioner."
The Layman was arrogant. He said, "Master, you are old and decrepit; you are no more than Pang Gong. The Master said, "Those two were contemporaries;
how much difference is there between them? The Layman said, "Pang Gong was vigorous and healthy; he was superior to you, Master.

The Master said, "It is not that he was superior to me; he simply lacked your head-wrap (fukuto). The Layman took off his head-wrap and said, "Now he looks exactly like you, Master. The Master merely laughed heartily.
While the Master was picking tea, the scholar said, “The Dharma-realm admits no person; does the Master still see me? The Master replied, “It is not that I, the teacher, am answering your question.
The scholar said, “To have a question and an answer is merely the ordinary. The Master then continued picking tea without listening.
The scholar said, “Do not take offense at my having just asked so casually. The Master still paid him no heed. The scholar shouted, “This!”
"You ill-mannered old man! Wait until I present each of these matters to those with clear vision. The Master then cast aside his tea basket and returned directly to the abbot’s quarters.
Zen Master Dadi of Xinzhou had received the imperial edict from Jiangxi, yet he constantly concealed his name; whenever students came to question him...
He would simply strike the ground with his staff to indicate the answer; thus, he was called "The Master Who Strikes the Ground.
One day, a monk hid the staff away and then posed a question to him. The Master merely opened his mouth.

The monk asked a follower, "If the Master strikes the ground whenever someone asks him a question every day, what is the meaning of this? The follower immediately took a piece of firewood from inside the hearth.
[The Master] took a piece [of wood] and threw it into the cauldron.
Zen Master Xiuxi of Tanzhou asked from Guishan, "When sound and form are pure and true, what is the Way? The Master said, "Why do you disturb the Way?
Guishan then moved from east to west and stood there. The Master said, "Had you not done so, it would have been a disaster."
Mount Guishan then moved from west to east and stood before him. The Master descended from his meditation seat;
just as he had taken two steps, Guishan seized him and asked, "When sound and form are pure and true, what is the matter? The Master then gave him a slap.
Guishan said, "Thirty years from now, there will not even be anyone left to serve tea. The Master replied, "What would you do with this fellow Guishan? Guishan—
He laughed heartily.
While the Master of Biśu in Jiangxi was lying down, Daowu approached and pulled the blanket over him. The Master asked, "What are you doing?"
I said, "It is the covering. The Master said, "Is it that which lies at the bottom, or that which sits upon it? I said, "It is not in either of these two places.
The Master said, "What then of the covering? I said, "Do not speak in confusion. While the Master was by the fire, I asked, "What is this?
The Master said, "Harmony. I said, "If so, you have escaped right from the head. The Master said, "How much distance has there been between us?"
At that time, I simply shook my sleeves and departed. One day, as I was returning from outside, the Master asked, "Where have you been?
I replied, "I have been visiting a relative. The Master said, "Why do you use these two pieces of skin [your mouth] to fan the air?
I replied, "I borrow them. The Master said, "If he has nothing to lend you, what would you do? I replied, "Precisely because he has something, I therefore borrow it."
When the Venerable of the Cao Tang Hermitage in Jingzhao finished his formal training under Daji, he went to the place of the Venerable Haichang.
Haichang asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Daochang. Haichang said, "What is this place here?
The Master replied, "A thief does not strike a poor man's house. A monk asked, "Before there was a single dharma, where was this body? The Master made a gesture.
A circular diagram with the character for "body" (身) written within it.
Master Dongan had a monk take his leave. The Master asked, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "Fundamentally, there is nowhere to go. The Master said:
The teacher said, "Be a good preceptor. [The monk] replied, "I dare not. The teacher said, "When you travel to various places, explain this clearly to others.

While the monk was standing in attendance, the teacher asked, "What is today’s date? [The monk] replied, "I do not know. The teacher said, "I, however, remember it. [The monk] asked, "What is today’s date?"
The Master said, "It is a cloudy and dark day today.
Dongshan, the Abbot of Xingping in Jingzhao, came to pay his respects. The Master said, "Do not prostrate yourself before this old man.
Dongshan said, "The one being prostrated to is not the old man. The Master said, "If it is not the old man, he would not accept your prostration. Dongshan said, "He does not stop either. —Dongshan.
Baizhang then asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? Dongshan said, "It is precisely your own mind.
Dongshan said, "Even so, this is still a point of doubt for me. Baizhang said, "If that is the case, then go ask the wooden man.
Dongshan said, "I have a phrase that does not borrow from the mouths of the various sages. Baizhang said, "Try to speak it. Dongshan said, "It is not."
Shanshan took his leave. The Master asked, “Where are you going? Shanshan said, “Following the stream, with no fixed destination.
The Master said, “Is it the Dharma-body following the stream, or the Reward-body following the stream? Shanshan said, “I do not interpret it in either of these ways.
The Master then clapped his hands. (Baofu said: “Dongshan has his own house; he speaks differently, saying, ‘How many people can find it?’”)
Master Xiaoyao asked Master Lusi, "Every thought-moment clings to objects; every mind is eternally still. The Master said, "Last night, someone also spoke this way.
Lusi asked, "What did they say? The Master said, "I do not know. Lusi said, "Please, Master, tell me.
The Master struck him across the mouth with his whisk. Lusi shook out his sleeves and departed. The Master called to the assembly, "The crown..."
"Fix your eyes upon the gate.
A monk asked Zen Master Fuxi, "What is it like when the ancient mirror is without blemish? The Master remained silent for a long while. The monk said, "What is your meaning, Master?
The Master replied, "This mountain monk is deaf. The monk asked again. The Master said, "It is still somewhat lacking. [The monk] asked, "How is it?"

"It is oneself. The Master asked, "What are you asking? He replied, "Is there not some skillful means? The Master said, "What were you just now asking? He replied, "How can you be so topsy-turvy? The Master said, "Today you deserve to receive a blow from my staff. [The monk] asked: [The Master] said, "It is oneself.

The Master asked, "What are you asking? He replied, "Is there not some skillful means? The Master said, "What were you just now asking? He replied, "How can you be so topsy-turvy? The Master said, "Today you deserve to receive a blow from my staff. [The monk] asked:
"When conditions disperse, they return to emptiness. Where does emptiness return? The Master then called to the assembly of monks; the monks responded with "Yes. The Master said, "Where is emptiness?
They replied, "Please, Venerable Sir, tell us yourself. The Master said, "The Persian eats black pepper."
When National Teacher Shuilao of Hongzhou first visited Mazu, he asked, "What is the very meaning of the coming from the West?
Mazu said, "Prostrate yourself. As soon as the Master prostrated, Mazu stepped on him right at the chest, knocking him down. The Master attained great enlightenment;
rising up, he clapped his hands and laughed heartily, saying, "How marvelous! How marvelous! Hundreds of thousands of samādhis and immeasurable wondrous [powers]!"
"Meaning! You must recognize the root source upon a single hair-tip. Having said this, he bowed in thanks and withdrew. Later, while residing there, he would often tell the assembly:
"Ever since I took that one bite from Mazu’s kick, I have been laughing without end until now.
A monk drew a circle, pinched it with his hand, and directed it toward the Master's body. The Master pushed it away three times, then also drew a circle and pointed back at him.
The monk bowed. The Master struck him, saying, "This man of empty pretenses! A monk asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa?
The Master said, "Movement brings forth shadows; awakening gives rise to ice. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master clapped his hands and laughed heartily. In all his encounters with students, he was generally like this.
Master Fubei was visited by Ling Xingpo, who came to pay her respects. The Master offered her a seat and tea.
Ling Xingpo then asked, "To whom do you entrust that phrase which cannot be spoken even with one's full strength? The Master replied, "Fubei has no superfluous words.
Ling Xingpo said, "Before reaching Fubei, I could not help but harbor doubts. The Master said, "If you have some other excellence, feel free to bring it forth. Ling Xingpo folded her hands and wept.
He said, "The azure heavens add further grievance and suffering. The Master remained silent. The old woman said, "In speech you do not know the biased or the correct;

in principle you do not recognize the inverted or the crooked. To act as a teacher for others is to invite calamity. Later, a monk reported this to Nanquan. Nanquan said, "How bitter! Fubei has been broken down by this old woman.
When the old woman later heard of this, she laughed and said, "Master Wang still lacks some skillful means."
Guangzhai was still "stuck" [on this point]. One day, while traveling, the Chan practitioner Chengyi encountered an old nun and asked her, "What is it that Nanquan still lacked?
The nun wept and said, "How tragic! How painful! Chengyi was at a loss for words. The nun asked, "Do you understand? Chengyi stood there with his palms joined.
The nun said, "Dead Zen monks, as numerous as hemp and millet. Chengyi reported this to Zhaozhou, who said, "I..."
"If one sees this foul old woman, ask her until her mouth is gagged. One asked, "I wonder, Master, how did you question her?
Zhaozhou struck him. The other asked, "Why did you strike me instead? Zhaozhou said, "If I do not strike a fellow like you, who am dead while still alive, when will I ever do so?
He struck him several more times. When the old woman heard of this, she said, "Zhaozhou deserves to eat from my hand."
[The Master] struck him with his staff. Later, a monk recounted this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou wept and said, "How tragic! How painful!

When the old woman heard these words, she joined her palms and sighed, "Zhaozhou’s eye of wisdom pierces through the four worlds. Zhaozhou then instructed the monk to ask her, "What is Zhaozhou’s eye?
The old woman then raised her clenched fist. The monk returned and recounted this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou then composed a verse, which begins: "When the occasion arises, face to face..."
"Face-to-face! To meet face-to-face is the swift application of the opportunity. I tell you, Laywoman Ling: why do you weep? What have you lost?

The laywoman replied with a verse: "The weeping, Master, you already know; Now that it is known, who else could know it? At that time in the kingdom of Magadha, How many would have lost the opportunity before their eyes!"

The Monk of Longshan in Tanzhou (also known as Yishan) asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From where the old master resides. The Master said, "What words did the old master speak?
The monk said, "If he speaks, there are a thousand phrases and ten thousand sentences; if he does not speak, there is not a single character.
The Master said, "In that case, it is like a fly laying its eggs. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him. Dongshan and Mi—
As the Senior Master (Shibo) was passing by, he saw vegetable leaves floating in a mountain stream. He said, "This deep mountain is uninhabited; why are there vegetables flowing down the current?

Could there be a practitioner of the Way living here? They then discussed going further upstream through the grass. After traveling five or seven li, they suddenly saw the Master, whose emaciated form and extraordinary appearance struck them with awe.
Setting down their luggage, they paid their respects. The Master said, "There is no path in this mountain. How did you, Venerable Sir, come from..."
“From where have you come? Dō said. “Setting aside for a moment that there is no path, from where did you enter, Master?

The Master replied, “I have not come from among the wandering clouds and waters. Dō asked, “How long has it been since you arrived at this mountain, Master? The Master replied, “It has not passed through spring and autumn.”
Dong said, "The Abbot has resided here first; this mountain has been inhabited for a long time. The Master said, "I do not know. Dong asked, "Why do you not know?
The Master said, "I have not come from the realm of humans or devas. Dong asked, "What principle did the Abbot realize that you reside on this mountain?
The Master said, "I saw two clay oxen fighting and entering the sea; until this very day, there has been no further news. Dong...
When Shanshi had completed his formal salutations, he asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master said, "Green mountains shrouded by white clouds.
He asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "Never leaving the door for many years. He asked, "How far apart are guest and host?
The Master said, "Waves upon the waters of the long river. He asked, "When guest and host meet, what words are spoken? The Master—
He said, "The pure breeze brushes against the white moon. Dongshan then took his leave. The Master then composed a verse, saying:

"I have always dwelt in a thatched cottage of three bays; A single path of divine light leaves all phenomena at rest. Do not bring right and wrong to judge me; In this floating life, artificial analysis is irrelevant.
Because of this, he burned his hermitage and entered the deep mountains, where he was no longer seen. Later generations called him Master Yinshan (The Hidden Mountain).
The layman Pang Yun of Xiangzhou was a native of Hengyang County in Hengzhou. His courtesy name was Daoxuan.
His family had originally followed the Confucian profession, but in his youth he awakened to the weariness of worldly toil and resolved to seek the ultimate truth.

At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era of the Tang dynasty, he visited Shitou and asked, "Who is it that does not consort with the myriad dharmas? Shitou covered his mouth with his hand, whereupon Pang attained sudden enlightenment. Thereafter...
He became friends with Danxia. One day, Shitou asked him, "Since you first met this old monk, how have you conducted your daily affairs?
The scholar replied, "If you ask about my daily affairs, there is no place to open my mouth. He then presented a verse: "In daily affairs there is nothing different;
Only I myself am in harmony. At every turn there is neither grasping nor rejecting; In every place there is no discord or conflict. Zhu... [text fragment]
"Who gave him the name 'Purple'? On this mountain, he is utterly free from a speck of dust. His spiritual powers and wondrous functions consist of carrying water and hauling firewood.

Touzi said, "Do you follow the black [robe of the monk] or the white [robe of the layman]? The scholar replied, "I wish to follow what I admire. He subsequently did not shave his head or dye his robes.
Later, he went to visit Mazu and asked, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion? Mazu said, "Wait for you..."

"To drink up the waters of the West River in a single gulp"—this is what I tell you. Under these words, the Master suddenly realized the profound principle (*xuanzhi*) and remained there to serve [the teacher] for two years.
He composed a verse which says: "Having sons, they do not marry; having daughters, they do not wed. The whole family sits together in a circle, speaking of the discourse on non-arising.
From that time on, his wit and eloquence became swift and sharp, and he was sought after by all quarters. Thereupon, he took his leave of Yaoshan.
Zhaozhou was at Mount Shan. The Abbot of Mount Shan ordered ten Zen guests to escort him to the gate.
Zhaozhou then pointed to the snow falling from the sky and said, "Fine snow—every flake falls nowhere else. A guest named Quan said, "Where does it fall? Zhaozhou then gave him a slap.
Quan said, "One must not be careless. The scholar said, "If you call yourself a Zen guest like that, the Old Man Yama will not let you off.
Quan asked, "What about you, Layman? The scholar struck him again and said, "To see with one's eyes yet be as if blind; to speak with one's mouth yet be as if mute.

He had formerly frequented lecture halls and, while taking joy in the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, when he reached the passage on "no self" and "no person," he posed a question, saying, "The seat..."
The Master said, "Since there is neither self nor person, who is it that speaks and who is it that listens? The Master received no reply.
The Layman said, "Although I am but a layperson, I have a rough understanding of faith and aspiration. The Master asked, "What, then, is your intention, Layman?
The Layman answered with a verse: "No self, and furthermore no person; How could there be distance or intimacy? I urge you to cease wandering through the seats; It is not like seeking directly."
"True. The nature of the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā is utterly devoid of even a speck of dust without. What I have heard and accepted as true is entirely expressed through provisional names.
When the Master heard this verse, he joyfully looked up and sighed in admiration. Wherever the Layman went, many veteran masters would visit him to engage in dialogue and exchange questions;
yet he responded to each according to their capacity, never constrained by fixed rules or standards of measurement. During the Yuanhe era, he traveled north.
He lived wherever he pleased along the Xiang and Han rivers. He had a daughter named Lingzhao, who regularly sold bamboo water-strainers to provide for their daily needs.
A scholar composed a verse for him: "The mind is as it is, and the environment is likewise; Neither real nor unreal, Neither concerned with existence nor constrained by non-existence.
Not a sage or holy one, but an ordinary person who has finished his affairs. Easy indeed, easy! Right within these five aggregates lies true wisdom."
The One Vehicle is the same throughout the worlds of the ten directions; how could there be two in the signless Dharma-body?
If one abandons afflictions to enter Bodhi, one does not know in which direction the Buddha-ground lies. To protect life, one must kill; only when killing is exhausted does one dwell in peace.

He thatched a hut and cleared away the weeds, dwelling in tranquil seclusion beneath the forest trees. As the days passed and months rolled by, he became known to the fourfold assembly.

They established the Píngtián Chan Monastery for him to reside in. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "The divine light is never obscured; it is a sublime legacy for all ages. Having entered this gate, do not harbor intellectual understanding.
He then descended from his seat. A monk approached for an audience; the Master struck him once with his staff. The monk stepped forward and seized the staff.
The Master said, "I was in a bit of a hurry just now. The monk struck the Master once with his staff. The Master said, "An adept! An adept! The monk bowed.
The Master seized him and said, "It was you, Dharma brother, who were in a hurry. The monk laughed heartily. The Master said, "This monk has been thoroughly defeated today.
Later, when Linji visited the Master, he first encountered an older sister-in-law at the crossroads working in a field.
Ji was driving the ox when he asked his sister-in-law, "Which way does the road to Pingtian lead? His sister-in-law struck the ox with a stick and said, "This beast wanders everywhere;
even upon reaching this road, it does not know it. Ji spoke again, saying, "I am asking you, which way does the road to Pingtian lead?
His sister-in-law replied, "This beast is five years old and still cannot be used. Ji thought to himself:
Wishing to observe the man before him, he first examined his attendant, immediately intending to "pull out the nail and extract the wedge.
Upon meeting the Master, the Master asked, "Have you seen my sister-in-law yet? Ji replied, "I have already taken her in. The Master then asked, "Where did you recently depart from?
Ji said, "From Huangbo in Jiangxi. The Master said, "I knew well that you had come to see a master. Ji said, [nothing more].
He came specifically to pay his respects to the Master. The Master said, “We have already met. Linji said, “According to the etiquette between guest and host, one ought to perform three prostrations.
The Master said, “Since it is the etiquette between guest and host, then go ahead and prostrate. He then presented a verse to the assembly, saying: “The Great Way is vast and empty;
it is the ever-present, single true mind. Do not think of good or evil; let the spirit be pure beyond all things. Following conditions as you eat and drink, there is nothing more.”
Furthermore, what was his end? He passed away at this very monastery, and his memorial stupa remains there.
A monk asked Chan Master Changguan of Wufeng in Ruizhou, "What is the realm of Wufeng? The Master said, "Precipitous. The monk asked again.
"What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "Obstructed. The monk took his leave. The Master asked, "Where are you going? He replied, "To Mount Tai.
The Master held up one finger and said, "If you have seen Mañjuśrī there, come back here and I will meet with you.
The monk was speechless. The Master asked another monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From the village. The Master said, "Did you see any oxen?"
The Master said, "I see. The monk asked, "Do you see the left horn or the right horn? The monk was speechless.

The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "I see neither left nor right" (Yangshan added, "But can you still distinguish left from right?"). Another monk took his leave. The Master said, "As you go to various quarters, do not slander me by saying I am here.
The monk replied, "I did not say that the Master is here. The Master asked, "Then where do you say I am?"
The monk raised one finger. The Master said, "You have already slandered me.

Chan Master Shenzan of Guling in Fuzhou was ordained at Dazhong Temple in his native region. Later, while traveling on pilgrimage, he attained enlightenment under Baizhang.
Upon returning to his place of ordination, his original teacher asked him, "During the time you were away from me, what accomplishments have you gained?"
[The Master] said, "I have no work to do," and so [Nanquan] sent him to perform manual labor. One day, while bathing, [the Master] ordered the teacher to remove the dirt from his back.
The teacher then patted his back and said, "What a fine Buddha hall this is, yet the Buddha is not holy. The Master turned his head and looked at him;
the teacher said, "Though the Buddha is not holy, he is at least able to emit light. On another day, as the Master was reading a sutra by the window, a bee flew in.
The student tried to get out through the window paper. The Master saw him and said, "The world is this vast and wide, yet you refuse to leave.
To bore into old paper—when will that ever end? He then spoke a verse: Refusing to leave the Gate of Emptiness, You throw yourself at the window—how very foolish!
Boring into old paper for a hundred years, When will you finally emerge? The Master set aside the scripture and asked, "Whom did you encounter while traveling on foot?"
"I have observed that your speech has been extraordinary from beginning to end. The Master said, "I, this humble one, was shown a place of rest by Venerable Baizhang;
I now wish to repay his compassionate virtue. Thereupon, the Abbot informed the assembly and prepared a vegetarian feast, requesting the Master to preach the Dharma.
The Master then ascended the seat and proclaimed the tradition of Baizhang, saying: "The numinous light shines alone, utterly transcending the sense organs and their objects.
Its essence reveals the true permanence, unconstrained by words and letters. The nature of mind is undefiled; it is fundamentally perfect and complete.

Simply by detaching from delusive conditions, one is the Buddha of Suchness. At these words, the Founder attained realization, exclaiming: "I never expected that in my old age I would hear such a matter of the ultimate principle!"

Later, the Master resided at Guling. After gathering disciples for several years, as he approached the time of his passing, he shaved his head, bathed, and struck the bell to summon the assembly, saying:
"Do you all recognize the samādhi of no sound? The assembly replied: "We do not recognize it. The Master said: "Listen silently."
"Do not think otherwise. The entire assembly listened intently. The Master remained solemn and passed into stillness (*parinirvāṇa*). His stupa remains at his original mountain.
