[The monk] asked, "Is it possible to obtain a great treasury of the teachings by means of a single breath? The Master said, "What kind of 'spiced-cake mallet' do you have?
Bring it here quickly! [The monk] asked, "What is the teaching of this entire lifetime? The Master said, "Shang Daren, Qiu Yiji. [The monk] asked again.
"What is Chan? The Master said, "A fierce fire frying oil. A monk came for an audience. The Master asked, "Are you a newcomer? He replied, "I am.
The Master said, "Set aside this entanglement for a moment; do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Carrying a cangue, he submits his petition."
The Master led him out himself. As the monk was about to leave, the Master said, "Come! Come! I am truly asking you: from where have you come?
The monk replied, "From Jiangxi. The Master said, "The Abbot of Letan is behind you; he fears you will speak recklessly. Do you see him? The monk had no reply.
Question: "Before the temple gate stands the Vajra. If it encompasses [the world], it is the vast expanse of heaven and earth; if it does not encompass it, not even a single hair can be encountered.
What then? The Master said: "HŪṂ. HŪṂ. I have never seen such a thing. The Master then asked: "First leap three thousand feet forward, then retreat eight hundred paces backward.
How will you do it? [The monk] said: "Yes. The Master said: "First, I shall issue a written confession of your transgressions. He then struck him.
The monk was about to leave when the Master said, "Come here; I shall have some 'entanglements' with you. He spread out his hands, saying, "This is the entire universe and the great earth.
Now tell me, how deep is the water of Lake Dongting? The monk replied, "It has never been measured. The Master asked, "And what of Lake Dongting itself?
The monk said, "Precisely because it is the present moment. The Master said, "You do not even understand this entanglement," and struck him. A monk asked: "If..."
"What is the phrase that is unobstructed wherever it encounters? The Master said, "I do not speak in such a manner. The monk asked, "How then would you speak?
The Master said, "The arrow has already traveled a hundred thousand miles to the Western Heavens; it now waits within the Great Tang Empire.
While reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, a monk asked, "What sūtra are you reading? The Master said, "The Great Cloud of Radiance; the Azure Cloud of Radiance."
A purple cloud of light appeared, and [the Master] pointed toward the front and asked, "What kind of cloud is that over there?

[The monk] replied, "It is a black cloud to the south. The Master said, "It will surely rain today. [The Master] asked, "That which is not formed by the character 'yi' (以) and is not the character 'ru' (入)—what sūtra passage is this?
The Master snapped his fingers once and asked, "Do you understand? [The monk] replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The recitations and praises above have been without..."

Limiting himself to superior causes, the frog leaps up to heaven; the earthworm suddenly traverses the Eastern Sea. He asks a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replies, "From north of the River.
The Master says, "There is a Venerable Zhaozhou there; have you been to him? The monk replies, "I have recently left there.
The Master asks, "What words did Zhaozhou use to instruct his disciples? The monk recounts the story of the tea. The Master—
He then laughed heartily and said, "How shameful! But tell me, what was Zhaozhou’s meaning? [The monk] replied, "It was merely a provisional expedient for the occasion.
The Master said, "What a pity! Zhaozhou has been splashed with a ladle of dung by you! He then struck him.
The Master turned and asked the śrāmaṇera, "How do you understand this? The śrāmaṇera immediately prostrated himself, and the Master struck him as well.
The monk went to the śrāmaṇera and asked, "Why did the Master strike you just now? The śrāmaṇera replied, "If it had not been for me, the Master would not have struck me.
A newly arrived monk entered and was just about to prostrate when the Master rebuked him, saying, "Śrāmaṇera, why did you steal the constant [practice]?"
[The Master] was sitting there eating fruit. [A monk] said, "As soon as this student arrived, why did the Master say he was stealing fruit? The Master said, "The stolen goods are right here.
He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? [The monk] said, "From Mount Yang. The Master said, "You do not even observe the five precepts."
The monk asked, "In what way, Master, have you spoken falsely? The Master replied, "A śrāmaṇera does not belong here.

As he was about to pass away, the Master summoned his disciples and said, "The conditions for this place have come to an end; I shall now depart. He then sat in the full lotus posture and entered nirvana.

The people of the commandery used fragrant wood to cremate him, and śarīra relics fell like rain. They collected his sacred remains and fashioned a statue in the temple. He lived to the age of ninety-eight.
The seventeenth day of the twelfth month, year sixty-six.
Chan Master Chunan of Qianqing Mountain in Hangzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Fuzhou.
He first visited Fengbo, who said to him, "I am not your teacher; your teacher is Huangbo, who is beyond the Yangtze River. The Master took his leave and subsequently visited Huangbo.
Huangbo asked, "How is it when you have not yet manifested the images of the three realms? The Master said, "Is there anything at all right now?

Huangbo said, "Setting aside for a moment existence and non-existence, how is it right now? The Master said, "Neither present nor past. Huangbo said, "The Dharma-eye of our lineage is already within your person.
Later, after taking up residence [at Dongshan], he ascended the hall and said: "Sons of the Buddha, even if you were to understand the teachings of the Buddhas of the three periods..."

Filling a vessel with water and attaining hundreds of thousands of samādhis is not equal to practicing the untainted path (*anāsrava-mārga*) for a single thought-moment, thereby escaping the fetters of the causes and effects of humans and devas.
At that time, a monk asked, "How does one practice the untainted path? The Master said, "Apprehend it before the 'you' [the listener] existed.
The monk asked, "If you did not exist, who was taught to apprehend it? The Master said, "The one who apprehends is also non-existent. The monk asked again.
"What is easy? The Master said, "Wearing clothes and eating food; not needing to read sutras or study the teachings;
not needing to practice the Way, prostrate, burn the body, or refine the crown of the head—is this not easy? [The student] asked, "What is difficult?

The Master said, "If even a subtle thought arises, one immediately possesses the five aggregates and the three realms. Birth and death, and the cycle of saṃsāra, all arise from your single thought. Therefore, the Buddha..."

He instructed the various bodhisattvas, saying: "The Buddha protects and keeps me in mind. Although the Master responded to the needs of sentient beings without weariness, he remained constantly in a state of tranquil meditative concentration for periods of over a month or ten days.
In the fifth month of the sixth year of the Wende era, he passed away. His stupa was erected in the western corner of the monastery.
In the second year of the Dàshùn era, when Sūn Rú of Xuānzhōu raided Qiántáng, he opened the stupa and beheld the Master’s entire body, solemn and intact.
With his nails and hair grown long, he bowed in thanks and departed.
Chan Master Lingguan of Mount Wushan in Fuzhou (commonly known as Old Guan at that time) usually kept his door bolted; few people saw him.
Only a single lay devotee would arrive at mealtime to deliver offerings, and only then would the master open the door. One day, Xuefeng took the opportunity to knock on the door. The Master—
The gate was opened. Shishuang Feng suddenly grabbed him by the chest and said, "Are you a common person or a sage? The Master spat at him and said, "You wild fox spirit!
He then pushed him out and closed the gate. Feng said, "I only wanted to know my elder brother. While clearing weeds, the Master asked a monk, "Where are you going?
The monk replied, "I am going to West Monastery to pay respects to Master An. At that moment, there was a green snake upon a bamboo stalk; the Master pointed at it.
The snake said, "If you wish to recognize the old wild fox spirit of West Court, it is simply this. The Master asked West Court, "What kind of thing can be placed upon this patch of ground?
West Court replied, "A Buddha without marks would be well-placed there. The Master said, "This fine patch of ground has been defiled by my brother with filth.
While he was pulling out noodles, a monk came for an audience. The Master pulled out some noodles and showed them to him; the monk then—
He departed. When the Master returned at dusk, he asked his junior attendant, "Where was that monk just now? The junior attendant replied, "He left right away.
The Master said, "That is so, but he only obtained one peg" (Xuánjué said: "Where is it that he is short by one peg?"). He then asked, "What is the Buddha?"
The Master extended his tongue to show it to him. The monk prostrated in thanks. The Master said, "Stop! Stop! What did you see that you prostrate?
The monk replied, "I thank the Master for his compassion in showing me the mark of the extended tongue. The Master said, "These days, an ulcer has grown on my tongue."
The monk arrived and knocked on the door. The attendant opened the door and immediately went out. The monk entered and prostrated, then asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
The Master said, "Who was that person who just went out? As the monk prepared to step forward, the Master pushed him out and shut the door.
When Caoshan was traveling on pilgrimage, he asked, "What is the Dharmakāya Lord, the Teacher of Vairocana? The Master—
[Caoshan] said, "If I were to tell you, it would be something else entirely. Caoshan related this to Dongshan, who said, "What a fine koan!
It simply lacks a follow-up question. Why not ask, 'Why did he not say anything? Thereupon, Caoshan came forward and posed that further question.
The Master said, "If you say that I do not speak, then my mouth is rendered mute; if you say that I do speak, then my tongue is rendered stammering.
Cao Shan returned and related this to Dongshan, who deeply approved of it.
Chan Master Zongche of Luohan Monastery in Hangzhou was the son of the Wu family of Huzhou. He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The bones are crushed. (The Master frequently used this phrase when responding to the occasion; at the time, he was called "Master Bone-Crusher.

A monk asked, "What is the Southern School and the Northern School? The Master said, "The mind is the school. The monk asked, "Is there still the need to study the teachings? The Master said, "The teachings..."

Regarding this mind, a question was asked: "The nature-ground (xingdi) is often shrouded in obscurity; how does one attain awakening? The Master said: "When the clouds of affliction are swept away by the wind, the great void becomes vast and clear.
He asked: "How does one achieve clarity? The Master said: "A single orb, pure and bright, radiates its light across ten thousand miles."
The layman Pei Xiu, styled Gongmei, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.

While he was serving as the Governor of Xin’an, Master Yun had recently left the assembly at Huangbo Mountain in Lingnan to enter the Dà'ān Vihāra, where he mingled with the laborers, sweeping and cleaning the halls.
When the Governor entered the temple to burn incense, the administrators received him; while observing the murals on the walls, he then asked:
"What kind of image is this? The attendant replied, "It is the true likeness of a high monk. The Duke said, "The true likeness may be viewed; where is the high monk? The attendant had no reply.
The Duke asked, "Is there any Chan practitioner here? He replied, "Recently there was a monk who came to the temple to take up service;
he bears a strong resemblance to a Chan practitioner. The Duke said, "May he be invited here so that we may question him? Thereupon, [the attendant] hurriedly went to search for him.
Huangbo arrived. Upon seeing him, the Duke was delighted and said, "Just now I had a question, but the virtuous ones were reluctant to speak.
I now request the Master to provide a single word in response. Huangbo said, "I pray the Duke will pose his question. The Duke repeated the previous story, and Huangbo spoke in a resonant voice:
Pei Xiu responded. Baizhang asked, "Where is it? At that moment, Pei Xiu understood the meaning, as if he had recovered the pearl from within his topknot.

He said, "My teacher is truly a good spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra). Your pointing out to others is so precise; why have I remained submerged here until now? The assembly of the monastery was astonished.
From then on, he invited [Baizhang] into the government offices and treated him with the etiquette of a disciple. Although [Baizhang] repeatedly declined, he would not stop. Furthermore—
He earnestly entreated [Baizhang] to remain at Huangbo Mountain to further promote the ancestral Way. Whenever he had leisure, he would personally enter the mountain to pay his respects;

if he grew thirsty for profound discourse, he would immediately invite him into the prefectural seat. Having thoroughly penetrated the intent of the patriarchs and being extensively versed in the characteristics of the teachings, the Chan scholars of all quarters all remarked that Minister Pei had not emerged from Baizhang’s gate in vain. This continued until he was transferred to govern Xuancheng.
He further contemplated visiting and paying homage [to the Master], and thus established a monastery (*vihāra*) and invited him to reside there.

Although Guifeng was a master who thoroughly integrated Chan and doctrinal study and was highly esteemed by Pei, he did not equal [the Master] in terms of turning his heart toward Huangbo and serving him with total devotion.
Furthermore, he composed the inscription for Guifeng’s stele, stating: "I, Xiu, am to the Master a brother in the Dharma, a friend in righteousness, and [a relative] in gratitude..."
It is evident that spiritual friends serve as both internal and external protectors of the Teaching.
Furthermore, he compiled the *Essential Sayings of Huangbo*, personally inscribed a preface for it, and placed it at the beginning of the collection to remain as a guardian of the mountain gate.

He also personally inscribed the titles for five hundred cases of the Tripitaka, which have been treasured to this day. Additionally, Master Guifeng composed the *Chan Yuan Quan*, the *Yuan Ren Lun*, and the *Yuanjue*.
He composed prefaces for the commentaries on the sutras and the *Dharmadhātudarśana*. He was devoted to the inner scriptures and had deeply penetrated the essence of the Dharma assemblies;
a text of his vow-inscription remains transmitted to the world.
Chan Master Fazu of Daisui in Yizhou was a successor of Chan Master Changqing An.
A native of the Wang family in Zizhou, he attained awakening at a young age and resolved to seek out teachers.
He left the household life at Huiyi Temple; after receiving full ordination, he traveled south, where he first visited Yaoshan, Dowu, and Yunyan.
Dongshan next went to the assembly of Daowei outside the mountain passes. For several years he did not eat to fullness, nor did he seek warmth when lying down;
he refined his practice through austerity, and his conduct was beyond the common. Daowei held him in deep esteem.
One day Daowei asked him, "Since you have been here with me, Lay Brother, you have never asked a single turning word. The Master replied, "Where would you have me apply my mouth?"
Miaoyan said, "Why do you not say, 'What is the Buddha? The Master then made a gesture with his hand to cover Miaoyan’s mouth.

Miaoyan sighed and said, "You have truly attained the marrow. From then on, his fame spread throughout the four seas. Later, he returned to Shu and stayed at Longhuai Temple in Pengkou Mountain, Tianpeng.
For three years, he brewed tea by the roadside and gave it away to all who came. On one occasion, while heading toward the mountain behind, he saw a...
The ancient monastery was named Dasui. Its many peaks rose steeply and beautifully, and its mountain stream was clear and cool.
Within it stood a tree over forty feet in circumference with a single opening facing south; its interior was hollow and unobstructed, a natural hermitage formed without the use of an axe.

At that time, it was known as the Wooden Chan Hermitage. The Master resided there for more than ten years, his shadow never leaving the mountains, yet his reputation spread far and wide to all four directions.

Regarding Xuanxue (Dark Learning), people from a thousand li away rushed to follow its influence. The Ruler of Shu held it in high esteem and repeatedly dispatched envoys to summon the Master, but each time the Master declined on account of old age and illness.
He was granted the title of Grand Master Shenzhao (Divine Illumination). Ascending the hall, he said: "This nature is originally pure and possesses all myriad virtues.

It is only due to the two conditions of defilement and purity that distinctions arise. Therefore, the sages awaken to it, employing it exclusively in a state of purity to achieve the Way of Enlightenment."
Ordinary beings are deluded by this; they are consistently immersed in defiled activity and submerged in saṃsāra. Yet its essence is non-dual; therefore, the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra says:
"There is no duality, nor two divisions; there is no distinction, nor any interruption. A monk asked: "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed..."
“I do not yet know whether this is destroyed or not. The Master said, “It is destroyed. The monk said, “If that is so, then it follows along with him.

The Master said, “It follows along with him. The monk did not accept this. Later, he went to Touzi and recounted the previous conversation. Touzi then prepared incense and prostrated from afar, saying:
Xichuan Gufo appeared in the world and said to a monk, "Return quickly and repent. The monk returned, only to find that Master Daisui had already passed away.
He went again to Touzi, but Touzi had also passed away. The monk asked, "What is the mark of a great man?
The Master replied, "There is no notice pasted upon his belly. The monk asked, "Where are you going? He replied, "I am going to live in a hermitage on the western mountain. The Master said, "I—"
"Calling to you from the top of the eastern mountain—can you come at once? He replied, "No. The Master said, "You have not yet attained stability in your hermitage.
A monk asked, "When birth and death arrive, what then? The Master said, "When you meet tea, drink tea; when you meet rice, eat rice. The monk said, "..."
"Who is it that receives offerings? The Master said, "Close your bowl. Beside the hermitage was a tortoise. A monk asked, "All sentient beings have skin wrapped around their bones;
why does this sentient being have bones wrapped around its skin? The Master picked up his straw sandals and placed them over the tortoise's back.
The monk was speechless. The monk asked, "What is the essential dharma of all Buddhas? The Master raised his whisk and said, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "Yes."
"No. The Master said, "The fly-whisk and the whisk-broom. [The monk] asked, "What is the student's own self? The Master said, "It is my own self.
[The monk] said, "Why then is it the Master's own self? The Master said, "It is your own self. [The monk] asked, "What is the singular matter of Dàsui?
The Master said, "East, west, south, and north. [The monk] asked, "The Buddha-dharma pervades all things."

[The student asked: "Regarding the 'place,' where does one instruct a student to stand? The Master said: "The great ocean allows the fish to leap; the vast sky permits the birds to fly. [The student] asked:
"When father and son are most intimate, yet part ways at a fork in the road, what then? The Master said: "Precisely because there are father and son."
Question: "What is the seamless stupa? The Master said, "Five feet high. The student said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "A whole brick. Question:
"After the Master passes away for a hundred years, to whom will the Dharma be entrusted? The Master said, "The pillar and the brazier. The student asked, "Will they receive it?
The Master said, "The brazier and the pillar. An attendant led a group of practitioners to pay their respects. The Master asked, "As for those who have attained through practice—"
[The Master] called out, “East! and asked, “What is this? The monk said, “One cannot call it ‘East. The Master scolded him, saying, “You stinking donkey!
If you do not call it ‘East,’ what would you call it? The monk was speechless. A monk asked, “What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, “Painting a winnowing basket with red earth.
The monk said, “I do not understand how this principle works. The Master said, “The winnowing basket has lips; the rice cannot leap out.”

The Master asked, "Monk, what teaching are you lecturing on? The monk replied, "The *Śata-dharma-śāstra*. The Master raised his staff and asked, "From what does it arise? The monk replied, "It arises from conditions (*pratyaya*).
The Master said, "Alas! Alas! The Master asked, "Where are you going, monk? The monk replied, "I am going to Mount Wutai to pay homage to Samantabhadra.
The Master raised his whisk and said, "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are both right here. The monk drew a circle in the air and threw it away.
Afterwards, he prostrated himself. The Master called for an attendant to bring a cup of tea and give it to this monk.
During the period when the assembly of monks was in session, the Master made his mouth assume the appearance of being afflicted by a wind-illness and said, "Is there anyone who can cure my mouth?

The monks vied with one another to bring medicinal herbs, and when the laypeople heard of this, they also sent many medicines. The Master accepted none of them. After seven days, the Master himself...
He pinched his mouth shut to correct him and said, "For so long a time you have beaten these two pieces of skin, yet to this day no one has been able to cure them.
He then sat upright and passed away.
Chan Master Lingshu Rumun of Shaoyang was a native of Min. The Liu rulers of Guangzhou held him in high esteem for generations and appointed him as the Great Master Zhisheng.
A monk asked, "What is the ultimate principle of the Buddha-dharma? The Master simply extended his hand. The monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "A thousand-year field has eight hundred owners. The monk asked, "What is the thousand-year field?"
The Master of Eight Hundred said, "This dilapidated house has no one to repair it. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, "Child, do not act like a laborer.
The monk said, "I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "You have come from Qianzhou. The monk asked, "Why is it so difficult to understand?
The Master said, "A wind-cart atop the head of the Fire God. There was a nun who presented him with some porcelain.
He gave the bowl to the Master. The Master lifted it up and asked, "Where does this come from? He replied, "It comes from Dingzhou" (Fadeng says otherwise:
"Not far from here"). The Master then smashed it to pieces; the nun had no reply. (Baofu spoke on her behalf: "The one who deceives the enemy perishes. He asked, "How old are you, Preceptor?"

The Master said, "Today I am born; tomorrow morning I shall die. He was asked again, "Where, Reverend, are your roots of birth? The Master replied, "The sun rises in the east; the moon sets in the west.
For over forty years, the Master transformed and edified those in the region south of the Ling Mountains, leaving behind many extraordinary traces.

When the Lord of Guangzhou was about to mobilize his troops, he went in person to the monastery to request the Master’s judgment on whether it was auspicious or not. The Master had already known this beforehand; he sat peacefully and passed away. The Lord [lamented].
The angry administrator asked, "When did the Master fall ill? He replied, "I have never been ill. Just now, I sealed a letter and instructed that it be presented to His Majesty.
When the administrator opened the letter, he found a note inside that read: "The Eye of the Human and Heavenly Eyes, the Head Seat of the Hall.

The administrator realized the Master’s intent and immediately called off the military action. He then summoned the First Seat to ascend the hall and preach the Dharma (this was Yunmen). [The Master entered his] coffin.
Regarding the ritual for interring him in a stupa, the ruler prepared everything extensively. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Lingshu, and a stupa was erected for his true body.
Chan Master Lingyun Zhiqin of Fuzhou was a native of Changxi in that same province. Initially at Mount Guiyang (Weishan), he attained enlightenment upon seeing peach blossoms.
He composed a verse which said: "For thirty years I have sought a swordsman; How many times have fallen leaves withered only to sprout again?"
[The verse says: "Since the moment I first beheld the peach blossoms, until this very day, I have had no further doubts.

When Guishan examined the verse and interrogated him regarding his realization, it matched perfectly with his own understanding. Guishan said, "Having attained awakening through conditions, you shall never again fall back or lose it.

Guard and maintain it well yourself. (A monk reported this to Xuansha, who said, "How precise, how truly precise! Yet I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate depth. The assembly doubted these words. Xuansha asked Dizang, "I have spoken thus; how do you understand it? Dizang replied, "It is not the cassia tree.")

[Daoyi] said, "Chen! You are about to run and kill all the people in the world. After he had settled there, he ascended the hall and addressed the assembly: "O worthy ones, all that is long or short ultimately falls into impermanence.

Observe the vegetation of the four seasons: leaves fall and flowers bloom. How much more so for the cycles of kalpas since the beginningless past—the heavens, humans, and the seven realms of existence, where earth, water, fire, and wind undergo the rotation of formation and destruction.
While the fruits of karma are nearly exhausted, the suffering of the three evil paths has never increased or decreased by so much as a hair’s breadth."

Only the spirit and consciousness within the root and stem remain constant. Those of superior capacity encounter virtuous friends who extend illumination to them; they attain liberation in that very place, which is itself the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
Those of middling or inferior capacity, being deluded and ignorant, are unable to awaken or reflect; they sink into the three realms and wander through birth and death.
For their sake, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni established teachings in both the heavens and among humans to provide proof and manifest the path of wisdom. Do you all understand this?
A monk asked, "How can one escape birth, old age, sickness, and death? The Master said, "The green mountains have never moved; drifting clouds come and go as they please.
The monk asked, "What is it like when the sovereign goes forth into battle? The Master said, "Outside the Chongming Gate, one does not ask about Chang'an.
The monk asked, "How does one have an audience with the Son of Heaven? The Master said, "A blind crane descends into the clear pond; a fish passes beneath its feet."

"Why is it that fame and merit are not achieved? The Master said, "When the Sovereign possesses the Way, the three frontiers are at peace; why labor to build the Great Wall ten thousand *li* away?
[The student] asked, "What of the time when weapons are laid down and one surrenders oneself to return to court? The Master said, "The clouds of compassion moisten all boundless lands;
though the withered tree has no flowers, what can be done about it? Changsheng asked, "Before the primordial chaos was divided, it contained..."

"Where does one who is born come from? The Master said, "It is like a dew-pillar conceiving a fetus. The monk asked, "What is it like after death? The Master said, "It is like a fragment of cloud touching the vast clarity.
The monk asked, "I wonder, does that vast clarity still receive being touched? The Master did not answer. The monk said, "If that is so, then sentient beings do not come [into birth].
The Master again did not answer. The monk asked, "When one has reached a state of pure clarity where all traces of 'points' have vanished, what then? The Master—
[The monk] asked, "Is this not the flow of true permanence? The Master said, "It is like a mirror that is constantly bright.
[The monk] asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is this matter beyond?
The Master said, "Once you have broken the mirror, we shall meet. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "A well."
Dizong Linqin said, "I, this student, do not understand. The Master said, "This year the peach and plum are expensive; each single fruit is worth a thousand pieces of gold.

A monk asked, "The *maṇi* jewel does not conform to the colors of others. In what color does it abide? The Master said, "White. The monk said, "If that is so, then it does conform to the colors of others.

The Master then took off one of his sandals, tossed it before him, and the monk departed. Upon arriving at Xuefeng, the Master asked, "Where have you come from?"
The monk said, "Lingyun has come. Yunfeng asked, "Is Lingyun well? The monk replied, "I have a message to deliver. Yunfeng asked, "Where is it?
The monk took off one sandal and tossed it before Yunfeng’s face; Yunfeng then desisted.
Chan Master Shou Shan Shi Jie of Fuzhou once studied under Dongshan. Dongshan asked, "Where is your native place, Venerable?
The Master replied, "If you are asking me truthfully, Master, I am a man from Min. Dongshan asked, "What is your father’s name?

The Master replied, "Having just received this question from the Master today, I have truly lost all recollection of what came before or after. Later, while residing at his own temple, the Master said:

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "All you venerable elders, you should fortunately take up these words of truth as mutual exhortation. All you brothers should each personally realize this for yourselves:
when the sentiments of both ordinary and sage are exhausted, the true and eternal is revealed. You need only at once cast off all former delusions and the defilements of clinging to sensory objects;
let your mind be like empty space. At some future time, you will surely recognize a little of what is good and what is evil. (Mín)
The Commander asked, "How many years old are you, Master Shoushan? The Master replied, "I am of the same age as empty space. He asked, "How many years old is empty space?
The Master replied, "It is of the same age as Shoushan."
A monk asked Master Yaoshan of Ruzhou, "What is the meaning of the West [coming]? The Master said, "Mid-winter is bitterly cold.
The monk asked, "What is the master’s profound depth? The Master said, "Wait until your tongue falls to the ground, and then I will tell you.
The monk asked, "What is the sixteen-foot golden body? The Master said, "When the judge renders his verdict, the official may amend it. —Changqing.

The Master said: "Where have you come from? Yunqing said: "I simply maintain [this state]; where have I come from?"
Chan Master Wenju Huirì of Chongfu Monastery in Guanhuan, Quanzhou, was the son of the Huang family of Fuzhou. He possessed extraordinary qualities from birth.
Upon reaching adulthood, he served as a jailer for the county, yet he frequently abandoned his duties to visit Master Guanding of Shenguang Temple and Master Xiyuan An.
The officials were unable to restrain him. Later, he went to pay his respects to Chan Master Tanka at the Wansui Pagoda and received the tonsure.
He did not wear the *kāṣāya* robe nor had he received full ordination; he wore only a sash made of variegated silk.
He then went to Shen Guang, who said, "I am not your teacher. Go and pay respects to the West Hall. The Master took a small green bamboo staff and entered the Dharma Hall of the West Hall.
Seeing him from afar, the Master of the Hall smiled and said, "Go to the Nirvāṇa Hall. The Master responded with an assent and entered, rolling his bamboo staff along.
At that time, there were about five hundred monks afflicted with an epidemic. The Master pointed at them one by one with his staff, and each rose as soon as he was pointed at.
The King of Min honored him deeply and established a monastery for him to reside in. Thereafter, many miraculous signs occurred. He passed away during the Qianning era of the Tang dynasty.
When Master Fuheng of Tiantai’s Floating River was visited by Xuefeng leading his assembly, Xuefeng asked, "There are currently two hundred people staying here for the summer retreat;
is this permissible? The Master took his staff and drew a line, saying, "If you cannot place it there, then speak. Xuefeng then desisted.
A monk asked Master Lushui of Luzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Do you see the flower garden railing in front of the courtyard? The monk was speechless.

Chan Master Yuanming of Wenshu Monastery in Guangzhou was the son of the Chen family of Fuzhou. After he attained the essential meaning under Daopei, he traveled to Xuefeng to seek further instruction;

there he found that the Dharma has no differing flavors. He once visited Mount Wutai and beheld a manifestation of Mañjuśrī, whereupon he established a monastery according to the site and named it after Mañjuśrī.
During the Kaibao era, the Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Li Chongju, went on inspection to protect the region.
In the south, while entering a monastery, he beheld an image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and asked a monk, "Why does Kṣitigarbha have his hand outstretched?
The monk replied, "The jewel in his hand was stolen by a thief. Li then asked the Master, "Since it is Kṣitigarbha, why was he robbed by a thief?
The Master said, "He has been caught today. Li bowed in gratitude.

The Venerable Master Yan-yang of Xinxing in Hongzhou, whose name was Shanxin, was a successor of Chan Master Zhaozhou Shen. When he first visited Zhaozhou, he asked, "What is it like when one brings nothing at all?
Zhaozhou said, "Put it down. The Master said, "Since I am bringing nothing at all, what is there to put down?"

"What is it? The Governor said, "I cannot let it go; take it away. Upon these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Later, after he had taken up residence, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "A clod of earth. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "The earth is shaking. The monk asked again—
"What is the Sangha? The Master said, "Eating porridge and eating rice. Question: "What is the water of Xinxing?
The Master said, "In the river before you. Question: "How does it manifest form in response to things? The Master said, "Bring me the bed over here."
The Master always had a snake and a tiger that followed him; he would take food from his own hand and give it to them.
A monk asked Chan Master Huiguang of Guangxiao Monastery in Yangzhou: "When the flower of awakening first blooms, it fills the entire Sahā world.

Since the Patriarchal Seal came from the West, what matter should be discussed? The Master said: "When emotion arises, wisdom is obstructed. The monk said: "This is the meaning of the Teachings (Śāsana). The Master said: [It is not.]

The Master said: "When weary, then rest. The Master asked Song Qichou, the State Chancellor: "Do you understand how to speak of this? Song said: "If it were 'the Way,' one could not even touch it.
The Master said: "Is it that there is something one cannot touch? Or is it that there is nothing one cannot touch? Song said: "Neither is it so."
[The monk] said, "Ma? The Master said, "Is it that which cannot be grasped? Song had no reply. The Master led the assembly out;

The Master said, "The former master truly did not say such a thing. Do not slander the former master, Reverend.
Layman Zhang asked, "How can one cope with old age? The Master said, "How old are you? Zhang said, "Eighty. The Master said, "That is fine."
[The Master] said, "It is called 'aging'. The man asked, "Ultimately, what is it like? The Master said, "Even at a thousand years old, it is still not finished.
A layman asked, "I have killed oxen throughout my life; do I still have sin? The Master said, "There is no sin. The man asked, "Why is there no sin?"
The Master said, "Kill one; restore one.
A monk from Guoqing Monastery in Longzhou asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said:

The Master said, "Auspicious clouds rise in competition; the rocky caves remain unimpaired. He asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "The table and chair; the brazier and the window. He asked, "Who is the renunciant? The Master said, "Copper heads and iron brows; bird beaks."
Lüshen asked, "What is the fundamental duty of one who has left the household life? The Master said, "Good morning; take care at night.
He asked, "Before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring him flowers?
The Master said, "It is like a person from Shanfu sending wealth to an iron ox. He asked, "After he saw him, why did they no longer bring flowers? The Master said, [The same as before].
"A wooden horse travels eight hundred *li* before dawn. A monk asked, "How does one subdue the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day?
The Master said, "To strike ice seeking fire; even after kalpas, it will not be encountered. A monk asked, "The twelve divisions of the teachings are for the purpose of silencing a child's crying.

Chan Master Xinjian of Wuzhou did not ordain junior disciples. A monk asked him, "Master, you are old; why do you not keep a young attendant to serve you?
The Master said, "If there is one who is blind and deaf, have him seek me out. When the monk took his leave, the Master asked, "Where are you going?
The monk replied, "To Kaiyuan Temple in the Prefecture. The Master said, "I have a letter for you to deliver to the Abbot of that temple."
"Can you take it away? [The monk] said, "I would be honored. The Master said, "I suspect you will be at a loss as well.
A monk asked the Abbot of Duofu in Hangzhou, "What is the single grove of bamboo at Duofu?

The Master said, "One stalk, two stalks, leaning. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Three stalks, four stalks, bent. [Another monk] asked, "What is the patched robe? The Master said, "..."
Regarding the matter of what is beneath the robe, the Master said, "There are many who harbor doubts about this. [The monk] asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "Hiding one's head within the moon."
When Master Xi Mu of Yizhou was ascending the hall, a layman raised his hand and said, "The Master is nothing but a donkey.
The Master replied, "I am being ridden by you, old monk. The man was speechless. Three days later, he returned and said, "Three days ago, I was robbed by bandits.
The Master took up his staff and drove him out. On another occasion, the Master suddenly called out to his attendant; the attendant responded.
"Yes. The Master said, "Wait until the night is deep and quiet; we shall deliberate with him together.
Chan Master Changsha Cen’s Dharma heir, Chan Master Xuedou Changtong of Mingzhou, was a native of the Li family of Xingzhou. He went to visit Changsha, who asked, "From where have you come?"
The Master said, "A man from Xingzhou. The Sandalwood Monk said, "I say you did not come from there. The Master asked, "Has the Abbot ever lived here before?
The Sandalwood Monk assented, and he was thus permitted to enter the room. After he had taken up residence, a monk asked, "What is the secret chamber?"
The Master said, "The wind-signal does not pass through. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the sealed chamber? The Master said, "All the sages seek to behold him, yet they do not see him.
The monk bowed. The Master said, "A thousand sages cannot conceive of him; ten thousand sages cannot deliberate upon him. Heaven and earth may perish, yet he does not perish;
empty space may encompass all, yet he is not encompassed. He is peerless among all things; throughout the three periods of time, no one can sing his praises. The monk asked, "How is this so?"
"This is the place from which all Buddhas of the three periods emerge. The Master said, "He is unwilling to acknowledge that you exist within the three periods.

After the monk had been silent for a long time, the Master asked, "Have you realized it? [The monk] said, "No. The Master said, "If not, then for now take it up where one cannot grasp the Buddha; it is ever-present within the moment.
When consciousness is exhausted and effort vanishes, if it stirs even for a flash, that already harms it—how much more so with words and phrases? (Tianyou)
In the seventh month of the second year, he manifested parinirvāṇa. His stūpa was erected in the southwest corner of the temple.
As for Master Zhuyou, who was the Dharma heir of Master Shiti:
once, when an attendant requested that he take a bath, the Master said, "Since one does not wash away dust, nor does one wash the body, you..."
"How is it? he asked. The man replied, "The Master should go first; I will bring the soap pods. The Master laughed heartily.
A newly arrived monk stood before the Master for a short while and then departed. The Master said, "What point of clarification was there?"
The monk returned again. The Master said, "You have discerned it. The monk asked, "After discerning it, what then?
The Master said, "It can be buried away. The monk cried out, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master said, "Just now you were like that, but even now you are still not right. The monk then went out.
One day, seeing the attendant carrying his bowl toward the hall, the Master called to him. The attendant responded, "Yes? The Master said, "How..."
[The monk] said, "I am going to the hall for the midday meal. The Master said, "Do I not know that you are going to the hall for the midday meal?
[The monk] said, "Apart from this, what else would you say? The Master said, "I am simply asking you about your own fundamental matter. [The monk] said, "..."
"If the Master asks about the fundamental matter, I have indeed gone to the hall for the midday meal. The Master said, "You do not fail in your role as my attendant.
[He was] a successor of Chan Master Zong of Zihu.
A monk asked Master Shengguang of Taizhou, “What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, “Lychees of Fuzhou; *càitóng* trees of Quanzhou.
The monk asked, “What are the two characters for ‘Buddha-dharma’? The Master said, “If you wish to speak, then speak. The monk said, “...”
The Master requested the Way from him. The Master said, "The barbarian monk with pierced ears smiles and nods his head. Longhua Zhao approached; the Master seized him and asked, "What is it?
Zhao said, "Do not err. The Master then let go of him. Zhao said, "I have long admired the Radiant Light (Shengguang). The Master remained silent. Zhao then took his leave.
As the Master saw him off at the gate, he said, "After this parting, where shall we meet? Zhao laughed.
[The Master] rebuked him and departed.

When Master Fushí of Zhāngzhōu ascended the hall, he said: "I, this mountain monk, have opened a divination shop. It can determine people’s wealth or poverty and settle their life or death. A monk asked:
"Setting aside life and death, as well as wealth and poverty, and not falling into the five elements—please, Master, speak directly. The Master [replied]:
[The Master] said: "Gold, wood, water, fire, and earth.
A monk asked Zen Master Zitong, "What is the realm of Zitong? The Master said, "Can you put sand into your eyes?
The monk said, "I do not even recognize the great, wonderful realm of Zitong. The Master said, "I do not conceal this matter from you," the monk [said].
As he was about to leave, the Master descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Today we have a fine case; I have not yet received so much as a single coin for it.
The monk replied, "Fortunately, I happened to meet a monk like me. The Master pushed him away and said, "Calamity does not come alone."
When the monk Huo came to visit Master Rirong Yuan, the Master clapped his hands three times and said, "A fierce tiger stands in the gateway;
who is there to oppose it? Huo replied, "A swift hawk soars toward the heavens; who can catch it? The Master said, "Both are difficult to withstand."
Huo said, "Stop! There is no need to resolve this public case yet. The Master brandished his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters;
Huo was left speechless. The Master said, "This fellow is as good as dead!"
The monk Dao Wu of Guannan in Xiangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Chang of Guannan.
While passing through a village and countryside, he heard a shamanist musician playing for a deity who said, "The conscious spirit is non-existent.
Upon hearing this, he suddenly attained awakening. Later, he went to consult Chan Master Chang, who certified his understanding. He subsequently traveled to the gate of Deshan.
The flavor of the Dharma became even more manifest. After he took up residence, whenever he ascended the hall, he would wear a lotus-patterned hat and a monastic robe while holding a ritual tablet.

Accompanied by the beating of drums and the blowing of flutes, he would chant aloud: "Lord Sanlang of Lu! Whether you are a conscious spirit or an unconscious spirit, the spirit comes from the void and returns to the void.
Having said this, he would immediately descend from his seat. On another occasion, he said: "The drum of Guannan is struck; the song of Deshan is sung. A monk asked: [What is it?]
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master took up a fan and bowed, saying, "Yes. At other times, he would take a wooden sword, rest it across his shoulder, and dance.
A monk asked, "Where did you get that sword in your hand? The Master threw it to the ground. The monk then placed it back in the Master's hand.
The Master said, "Where did you get that? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "I grant you three days to answer."

He offered a turning phrase, but the monk had no reply. The Master himself stepped in, brandishing a sword across his shoulder and performing a dance, saying, "One must act like this before one succeeds.

He said, "I am contemplating a place among forests and springs where I may spend my final years. At that time, his disciple Qijing selected a site at Mount Danxia in Nanyang to construct a hermitage.
Within three years, those who studied the profound teachings reached nearly three hundred in number, and he established a large monastery. He ascended the hall and said:
"You, all you people of this house, must protect with utmost care that single spiritual essence. It is not something you can create, fashion, name, or describe. Furthermore—
To speak of "thoroughly recommending" or "not recommending": when I saw Shitou in the past, he too taught only that one must strictly protect oneself.
This matter is not something you can discuss. Each of you has your own patch of ground; what more is there to doubt?
Is Zen something you can intellectually understand? How could there be a Buddha to be attained? The very word "Buddha"—never...
"Delightful to hear! You should examine this for yourself: skillful means, compassion, joy, and equanimity are not obtained from without, nor do they reside within the mind.
Skillful means is Mañjuśrī; expedient means is Samantabhadra. What more do you intend to pursue?"
Do not go seeking through scriptures and fall into emptiness. Nowadays, students are in a state of constant clamor and agitation; they all take up Zen meditation and inquire about the Way.
In my place here, there is no Way to be cultivated and no Dharma to be realized. Every sip of drink and every morsel of food has its own allotted portion.
Do not harbor doubts; such people exist everywhere. If you can recognize Śākyamuni, then he is just an old ordinary man.
You must examine this for yourself; do not let one blind person lead a crowd of blind people as you walk together into a pit of fire.
Playing double-six in the dark at night—how could you ever win? There is nothing more to it; take care. A monk arrived to pay his respects at the foot of the mountain.
Upon seeing the Master, he asked, "Where has Mount Danxia gone? The Master pointed to the mountain and said, "In that deep, dark blue expanse.
The monk asked, "Is it not just this very thing? The Master replied, "A true lion cub turns at a single nudge. He then questioned a monk.

"Where did you spend the night? he asked. The monk replied, "I spent the night at the foot of the mountain. The Master said, "Where did you eat your meal? He replied, "I ate my meal at the foot of the mountain.
The Master said, "Does the person who brought the food to give to you, the *dārali* (junior master), possess eyes or not?

The monk was speechless. [Later, Changqing asked Baofu: "When one brings food to give to another, there is a share of gratitude; why then do you say they do not possess eyes? Baofu said, "Both the giver and the receiver are blind men. Changqing said, "If one exhausts all their skillful means (*jī*), would they still be blind? Baofu said, "Say that I am blind."

"Is that so? Xuangjue challenged him, saying, "Tell me, did Changqing clarify Danxia’s meaning, or was he simply using his own family wealth? In the sixth month of the fourth year of the Changqing era, he addressed his disciples, saying:

He prepared hot water for a bath and said, "I wish to depart. Thereupon, he donned his bamboo hat, took up his staff, and put on his sandals; with one foot still not touching the ground, he passed away.
His disciples erected a stupa for him, posthumously titled Chan Master Zhitong, and named the stupa Miaojue (Wondrous Enlightenment).
A monk from Jiangling came to visit Chan Master Dachu (also known as Dacun) of Tanzhou. The Master asked, "When did you set out from Jiangling? The monk lifted up his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*).
The Master said, "Thank you for coming from so far; go down. The monk circumambulated the meditation seat once and then departed.
The Master said, "If it were not like this, how could one know the true nature of your eyes? The monk clapped his hands and said, "It would kill me!"
The monk said, "I have mistakenly judged the various quarters. The Master said, "You have grasped the principles of the Chan school quite well. The monk related this to Danxia.

Danxia said, "That may be acceptable regarding the Dharma-way of Dachuan, but it is not so here. The monk asked, 'I wonder how it is done here? Danxia replied, 'It is still three steps ahead of Dachuan. The monk bowed. Danxia said, 'Many have mistakenly judged the various quarters. Dongshan remarked, "Had it not been Danxia..."
It is difficult to distinguish between jade and stone).
When Chan Master Baotong Dadian of Ling Shan in Chaozhou first visited Shitou, Shitou asked, "Which one is your mind?
The Master replied, "The one that perceives these words. Shitou then shouted at him and sent him out. After ten days had passed, the Master asked again, "As for what happened previously..."
"It is not that. "Setting this aside, what else is mind? Baizhang said, "Set aside your raising of eyebrows and blinking of eyes;
bring me the mind. Huangbo said, "There is no mind to be brought. Huangbo said, "Originally there is mind; why do you say there is no mind?
To say there is no mind is entirely a slander. At these words, Baizhang attained great enlightenment. On another day, while standing in attendance, Huangbo asked, "Are you practicing Chan?"
The monk was a "white-trampling" (formal) monk from the prefecture and county. The Master said, "I am a Chan practitioner. The monk asked, "What is Chan?
The Master said, "Raising an eyebrow and blinking an eye. The monk said, "Setting aside raising an eyebrow and blinking an eye, show me your original face.
The Master said, "Please, Reverend, examine me setting aside raising an eyebrow and blinking an eye. The monk said, "I have already set it aside."
The Master said, "I have already presented it. Zhaozhou asked, "Since you have presented it, what is my mind like?
The Master said, "It is no different from the Master's. Zhaozhou said, "That does not concern you. The Master said, "Fundamentally there is nothing. Zhaozhou said, "You, too, are nothing.
The Master said, "Since there is nothing, that is the true thing. Zhaozhou said, "The true thing cannot be grasped; this is the intent of your mind’s discernment."
It is thus. You must protect and uphold this with great care. After the Master settled there, students gathered from the four quarters.
He ascended the hall and said: "Those who study the Way must recognize their own original mind. Only by pointing directly to the nature of the mind can one see the Way.

I see that many of the current generation merely identify with raised eyebrows, blinking eyes, a single word, or a moment of silence, and they immediately grant seal-of-approval (inshō) to others, taking these as the essence of the mind. This is truly not yet understanding."
I shall now clearly explain this for all of you; each of you must listen and receive it. Simply eliminate all deluded movements of thought, and that which perceives is your own true mind.
This mind has no interaction whatsoever with external objects, nor with the state of maintaining stillness and silence.
This very mind is the Buddha; it does not require cultivation or refinement. Why is this? Because it responds to conditions and illuminates accordingly, yet remains cool and detached.
Ling used [it] for himself. He exhausted its point of application, yet it was utterly unobtainable. To call this "wondrous function" is precisely the original mind;
it must be guarded and maintained with great care—it cannot be treated lightly. A monk asked, "When those within [the Way] meet one another, how is it?
The Master said, "Already, they are not within. The monk asked, "What is it to be within? The Master said, "Do not make such a question. Han Wengong... one.
One day he went to visit the Master and asked, "How many years have you been in the world? The Master held up his rosary and said, "Do you understand? The official said, "I do not understand.
The Master replied, "One hundred and eight [beads] for day and night. The official did not comprehend this and returned home. The next day he came again;

arriving at the gate, he saw the Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera) and recounted the previous conversation, asking what its meaning was. The Head Seat clicked his teeth three times. Upon seeing the Master, he... [proceeded as before].

The official asked the same question as before. The Master also tapped his teeth three times. The official said, "I see that the Buddha-dharma is not of two kinds. The Master asked, "What is your reasoning?
The official replied, "Just now, when I asked the Head Seat, he answered in exactly the same way. The Master then summoned the Head Seat and asked, "Was it you who answered in this manner?
The Seat replied, "It was I. The Master immediately struck him and expelled him from the monastery. One day, the official again addressed the Master.
The official said, "My duties as military governor are many and complex. Regarding the essential points of the Buddha-dharma, I beg the Master for a single word.

The Master remained silent for a long time. The official was at a loss. At that moment, Sanping was serving as attendant; he struck the meditation seat three times. The Master asked, "What is this? Sanping replied: [silence].
"First one moves by means of concentration; afterwards, one extracts [the self] by means of wisdom. The Master then said, "The patriarchal style of our Abbot is lofty and steep.
My disciple has found a point of entry through the attendant. A monk asked, "The waves of the sea of suffering are deep; what shall serve as the boat or raft? The Master replied:
Using wood to make a boat or raft, he said, "In that way, one may cross over. The Master said, "The blind remain blind as before; the mute remain mute as before.
One day, while walking along the corridor with his itch-scratcher, he encountered a monk who came forward to pay his respects.
The Master struck him across the mouth with the itch-scratcher and asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Old wild fox Dadian!"
He never failed anyone.
Chan Master Changzi Kuang of Tanzhou, having returned from paying homage at the ancestral pagoda at Caoxi, went to visit Shitou.
Shitou asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Lingnan. Shitou said, "Has the one set of merit at the head of Dayu Ridge been completed yet?"

The Master said, "You have accomplished this for a long time; you simply lack the 'dotting of the eyes' (the final realization). Baizhang asked, "Do you not wish to have your eyes dotted? The Master replied, "I request it at once.
Baizhang then lowered one foot. The Master prostrated himself. Baizhang asked, "What principle did you perceive that you prostrate yourself?
The Master said, "According to what I have seen, it is like a single speck of snow upon a red-hot furnace. (Xuange said: Now tell me, was this the Longshu?)

Zizujian asked: "Does one who possesses eyes respond? Or does one who lacks eyes respond? If they possess eyes, why did you ask him to apply eye-salve? If they lack eyes, you also say he has long since achieved perfection.

How do you deliberate upon this? Fadelen spoke on his behalf, saying: "The Master may indeed be said to have blurred vision. A monk came to visit. He circumambulated the meditation seat once and stood there upright. The Master said:
"If this were the Dharma-seat of Shitou, not even a single drop would be needed. The monk again circumambulated the meditation seat once. The Master said: "But it is precisely thus."
At that time, [the Master] did not readily state where [the monk] had come from. The monk then departed. The Master called out to him, but the monk paid no heed.

The Master said, "This fellow still lacks instruction. The monk turned back and asked, "Is there a person who does not receive it from another, who does not receive instruction, and who does not fall into stages?
Do you grant permission for such a one? The Master said, "Meeting him is not meeting him; if you meet him, there must be something. The monk—

The Master then stepped back three paces. The monk, however, circled the meditation seat once. The monk said, "Not only is the eye of the school made clear, but the lineage of the teacher is also well-founded.
The Master then struck him three times and asked the monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From the Controlling Stone Hermitage on Mount Jiuhua.
The Master asked, "Who is the abbot there? He replied, "A venerable elder under Mazu. The Master asked, "What is his name?"
"What is it? he asked. [The other] said, "I do not understand his Dharma-name. The Master said, "He does not understand it; you do not understand it either.
[The other] said, "Where are the eyes of this venerable elder? The Master said, "If the Abbot himself had come in person, he would have had to receive a blow of the staff today as well.
[The other] said, "Fortunately, we encountered the Master, who let me off. The Master said, "A hundred years from now, it will be difficult even to find a monk like this. Pang Jushi.

When the scholar arrived, the Master ascended the seat. Once the assembly had settled, the scholar stepped forward and said, "Each of you should examine yourselves well," and then stood to the right of the meditation platform.
At that time, a monk asked, "Without touching the master of the house, please let the Master answer. The Master replied, "Do you recognize Master Pang? The monk said, "I do not.
The scholar then seized him by the collar, saying, "Alas! Alas! The monk was speechless. The scholar then released him.
After a short while, the Master turned and asked, "Did that monk just now receive a blow of the staff? Layman Shi replied, "I would wait until he was willing before it could be so.
The Master said, "Layman, you see only the sharpness of the chisel's tip; you do not see the squareness of the chisel's head. Layman Shi said, "Speaking in such a manner..."
"So-and-so has already attained it. When outsiders heard this, they said, "This is certainly not good. The Master asked, "What is so bad about it?
The scholar replied, "You, Master, see only that the tip of the awl is sharp; you do not see that the point of the chisel is keen. Later, when Li Xingpo arrived, the Master questioned her.

"Do you remember the events that took place when we were in Jangzhou? The old woman said, "If it were not for you, Master, I would not know. The Master said, "There is much falsehood and little reality in what you say.
The old woman said, "What is there to hide? The Master said, "I am mindful that you are a woman; I let you go with your staff. The old woman said, [and continued].
"I shall never see any fault in the Venerable Elder," [the woman] said. The Master asked, "Where does the old monk’s fault lie?
The woman said, "The Master has no fault; how could I have any fault? The Master asked, "What is it like for one who has no fault?
The woman then raised her fist and said, "In this way, everything becomes inverted. The Master said, "Truly, there is nowhere to hide. When the Master saw a monk, he seized him and said:
The Lion’s Cub was a member of the jackal clan. A monk made a gesture with his hand as if brushing his eyebrows. The Master said, "Even so, you still lack the roar.
The monk grabbed the Master, who said, "You are particularly fond of performing this particular maneuver. The Master gave him a slap. The monk clapped his hands three times.
The Master asked, "If you see someone of like mind, would you be willing to act thus? He replied, "Ultimately, it does not depend on anyone else."
The Master made a gesture of plucking his eyebrows. The monk said, "You still lack a roar. The Master said, "I suspect it does not depend on anyone else.
Seeing the monk bowing in greeting, the Master said, "Every step is a place of your own realization; do you know this yet?"
The monk said, "I do not know. The Master said, "If you knew, what would I be able to do? The monk bowed.
The Master said, "I am not capable; you are indeed well-suited."
The Master Shili of Jingzhao Prefecture asked Shitou, "What is the student’s fundamental matter?
Shitou said, "Why do you seek it from me? He replied, "I do not seek it from my teacher; how then can I attain it?
Shitou asked, "Have you ever lost it? Thereupon, the Master realized its essential meaning.
Chan Master Huilang of Zhaoti Temple in Tanzhou was a native of Qiujiang in Shixing.
Initially, he went to visit Mazu. Mazu asked him, "What do you seek in coming here? He replied, "I seek the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. Mazu said, "The Buddha has no knowledge or vision;
knowledge and vision are but demons. Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from Mount Heng. Mazu said, "Since you have come from Mount Heng, you have not yet recognized Caoxi."
"Essential Instruction: You should return to him quickly; it is not fitting for you to go elsewhere. The Master returned to Shitou and asked, "What is the Buddha?
Shitou said, "You have no Buddha-nature. The Master said, "As for all wriggling and moving sentient beings, what of them?
Shitou said, "Wriggling and moving sentient beings, however, do possess Buddha-nature. The Master asked, "Why then does Huirang lack it? Shitou said, "It is because you do not accept it."
He accepted this. Under these words, the Master attained faith and entry. After he took up residence, whenever a student arrived, he would always say, "Go! Go! You have no Buddha-nature.
His manner of responding to students was roughly like this (at that time, he was called Dàlǎng).
When Chan Master Zhenlang of Xingguo Temple in Changsha first visited Shitou, he asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Shitou replied, "Ask the pillar. Zhenlang said, "I do not understand. Shitou said, "I do not understand either."

The Master suddenly attained awakening. After he had taken up residence [at the monastery], a monk came to seek instruction. The Master called out, "Venerable One! The monk responded. The Master said, "You have failed me.
The monk asked, "Why do you not recognize me? The Master then rubbed his eyes and looked at him; the monk was left speechless (at that time, he was known as Xiao Lang).
Chan Master Shilou of Fenzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "I do not yet recognize my original nature; I beg the Master for a skillful means to point it out.
The Master said, "Shilou has no ears. The monk said, "I know myself that I am at fault. The Master said, "The old monk also has his faults."
The monk asked, "Where does the Master's fault lie? The Master said, "The fault lies in your being in the wrong place. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
He asked another monk, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "From the land of Han. The Master said, "Does the ruler of the land of Han respect the Buddha-dharma?
He replied, "Alas! Fortunately I encountered you to ask me this; had I been questioned by someone else, disaster would have ensued. The Master said, "How so?"

[The monk] asked, "How is it? He replied, "People do not even see me; what Buddha-dharma could there be to value? The Master said, "How many years of summer retreat have you completed since receiving the precepts?
He replied, "Thirty years. The Master said, "Excellent that you do not see anyone," and then struck him.
Chan Master Fotu of Famen Temple in Fengxiang Prefecture habitually held a string of prayer beads and recited three names:
first, Śākyamuni; second, Yuanhe; and third, Fotu. As for all others, what are they? They are merely "wan-die-qiu" (clumsy, stumbling fellows).
He would pass over one bead, and at the end, begin again; his conduct was so extraordinary that the people of the time could not fathom it.

I replied, "I certainly will not say anything. I ask that you instead go to Chuanzi at Huating. Xuefeng asked, "What is this man like?"
I said, "This man has not a single tile above him and not enough room for the point of a锥 (chui) below him. If you, Master, are to go there, you must change your robes before you depart.
Yunmen then dispersed his assembly and packed his belongings, proceeding directly to Huating. As soon as Chuanshi saw him, he asked, "Virtuous One, in what monastery do you reside?
Yunmen replied, "As for a monastery, I do not reside in one; were I to reside in one, it would not be like this. Chuanshi asked, "'It would not be like this'—what would it be like?"
Muzhou said, "It is not the Dharma of the present moment. The Master asked, "Where did you learn this? Muzhou said, "It is not something that reaches the ears or eyes.
The Master said, "A single phrase that fits the head is a tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas. The Master then asked, "The line hangs down a thousand feet;
the intent lies in the deep pool. Three inches away from the hook—why do you not speak? As Muzhou was about to open his mouth, he was struck by the Master.
With a single stroke of the oar, he struck him into the water. As soon as Shanshan had boarded the boat, the Master said again, "Speak! Speak!
Just as Shanshan was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him once more. Shanshan attained a sudden, great awakening and nodded his head three times.

The Master said, "The line on the tip of the pole is for you to play with; its meaning differs from that of the clear waves. Shanshan then asked, "Regarding casting the line and throwing the hook—what is your intention, Master? The Master... [replied].

[The Master] said, "I wish to escape birth and death. Baoshan said, "There is one person who does not receive the precepts, yet for whom there is no birth and death to escape.
Do you know this or not? The Master said, "If that is so, then what use are the Buddha-precepts? Baoshan said, "This śrāmaṇera still has his teeth hanging on his lips.

The śrāmaṇera replied, "He has a bit of breath left. I said, "Do not trust him entirely; you must further examine him before you can be certain.

That evening, as he was ascending the hall for the formal discourse, the Master called out, "Where was the śrāmaṇera who came this morning? The Master stepped forward from the assembly and stood there. The Master asked:
"I have heard that Chang'an is very bustling. Do you know of it? The Master said, "My country is at peace" (Fayan’s alternative version says: "Who did you see say this?").

Mount said, "Did you obtain it from reading the scriptures? Or did you obtain it from requesting instruction? The Master said, "I did not obtain it from reading the scriptures, nor did I obtain it from requesting instruction.
Mount said, "There are many people who do not read the scriptures and do not request instruction; why is it that they do not obtain it? The Master said, "I do not say that they do not obtain it;
it is simply that they are unwilling to accept it. Mount looked toward Daowu and Yunyan and said, "No."
Xindao took his leave of Master Yaoshan one day. Yaoshan asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "I am currently causing some disturbance among the assembly.
I intend to go and pitch a thatched hut by the roadside to receive travelers and provide them with tea and soup. Yaoshan said, "The matter of birth and death is of great importance.
Why do you not go and receive the precepts? The Master said, "Once one knows this kind of matter, one simply lets it be. What else could one call it?"
Regarding the observance of the precepts, Shanshan said, "Since you are thus, you must not leave my side. From time to time, I shall wish to see you.
After the Master had been staying at the hermitage, he returned one day and encountered the rain. Shanshan said, "You have come? The Master replied, "Yes.
Shanshan said, "It is quite soaked. The Master said, "I am not playing this drum or flute. Yunyan said, "There is no hide; what is there to play?"
[The monk] struck the drum. Daowu said, "There is no drum; what hide are you beating? Yaoshan said, "Today there is truly a magnificent musical performance.
A monk asked, "Is there anything that even a single phrase cannot encompass? The Master replied, "It does not conform to worldly conventions.
At the time of the midday meal, Yaoshan was personally beating the drum. The Master entered the hall dancing while holding his bowl. Yaoshan then threw down the drumstick and said:
"What is this, the first harmony or the second? The Master said, "This is the second harmony. Daoshan asked, "What is the first harmony?
The Master went to the rice bucket, scooped up a ladle of rice, and went out.

Li Ao, the Prefect of Dingzhou, had long admired the profound transformation of Yaoshan, yet despite repeated invitations, the Master did not go. Li Ao then went to visit him in person. Yaoshan held up a scroll and paid him no heed.
An attendant said, "The Governor is here. Being of a narrow and impetuous temperament, Li Ao remarked, "A face is not as good as a reputation," and brushed his sleeves, departing at once.
Yaoshan said, "How can the Governor value his ears while disparaging his eyes? The Governor turned back.
He bowed in thanks and asked, "What is the Way? Shanshan pointed up and down with his finger and asked, "Do you understand?
Baoshou replied, "I do not understand. Shanshan said, "Clouds in the blue sky; water in the pitcher. Baoshou was filled with joy and prostrated himself, reciting this verse:
"My body has been refined until it resembles the form of a crane; Beneath a thousand pine trees lie two cases of scripture. When I came to ask about the Way, there was no further teaching given."
"Clouds in the blue sky, water in the pitcher. (Xuánjué said: "Now tell me, does Governor Li’s statement praise him or clarify him? One must possess the eye of a traveling monk to discern this.
The Governor asked again, "What are precepts, concentration, and wisdom? Dàoxuān replied, "In my place, there are no such idle furnishings. The Governor could not fathom the profound meaning.
Dàoxuān said, "If you, Governor, wish to maintain and take responsibility for this matter, you must go to the very summit of the highest mountain."
Standing up, [he said]: "Walking at the bottom of the deep sea—this is a thing of the inner chamber. If one cannot let go of it, it becomes a leakage. An old master was sitting alone;
[the monk] asked him, "When you sit upright in the hall, what should you attend to? The master replied, "The Dharma-body is still and silent; there is no going and no coming.
(Fayan commented elsewhere: "What have you come here to do? Fandeng commented elsewhere: "This is not your realm.")
When Zen Master Cuiwei Wuxue of Jingzhao Prefecture first questioned Zen Master Danxia Ruan, he asked, "What is the teacher of all Buddhas?
Danxia scolded him, saying, "Fortunately, you are already pitiable enough; why must you insist on taking up the handkerchief and broom? The Master stepped back three paces. Danxia—
Dongshan said, "Wrong. The Master stepped forward. Dongshan said, "Wrong, wrong. The Master lifted one foot, spun his body once, and walked out.
Dongshan said, "You have attained it, indeed; you have surpassed all other Buddhas. From this, the Master understood the essential meaning.
Later, while residing there, Touzi asked him, "I wonder, when the Second Patriarch first saw Bodhidharma, what did he obtain? The Master replied, "When you see me now, what do you obtain?"

Touzi attained sudden enlightenment into the profound principle. One day, as the Master was walking within the Dharma Hall, Touzi stepped forward to pay his respects and asked, "How does the Master instruct people regarding the secret essence of the West? The Master paused for a moment.
Touzi said, "I beg the Master to grant us an instruction. The Master replied, "Do you want another ladle of foul water? Touzi then bowed in thanks. The Master said, "Do not..."
Duo-gen said, "When the time comes, the roots and sprouts will grow of themselves. Once, while the Master was making offerings to an Arhat, a monk asked, "Danxia burned the wooden Buddha;
why does the Master make offerings to an Arhat? The Master said, "Even when burning, it cannot be burned; as for making offerings, let him offer as he pleases.
The monk asked, "When you make offerings to an Arhat, does the Arhat actually come or not? The Master said, "You..."
"Do you still eat rice every day? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "There are few who are truly quick-witted.
Zen Master Xingkong of Xiaoyi Temple in Jizhou came to visit; the Master extended his hand toward him. The monk stepped forward.
The monk stepped back. The Master said, "Your parents have both passed away; why do you show no sign of grief? The monk laughed loudly.
The Master said, "In a moment, I shall offer you my condolences. The monk performed a somersault and left. The Master cried out, "Heaven! Heaven!
After the monk had finished his formal greetings, the Master asked, "Going off like that—does it accord with the principles of the Buddha-Dharma or not? The monk replied, "I..."
The monk bound his tongue and remained silent. The Master asked, "And how about this old monk? The monk replied, "I am no skilled hand.
The Master then leaned back and joined his palms; the monk likewise joined his palms. The Master clapped his hands three times, and the monk brushed out his sleeves and departed.
The Master said, "The crow does not go before, the hare does not follow behind. How many people here wander in bewilderment? Only you, Dāilì, have realized the fundamental source."
Yuan: "Tongued in silence, when have you ever been attached to emptiness or existence?
Master Micang arrived for a new audience; he circled the Master three times, struck the meditation seat, and said, "I do not see the Host."
The monk did not descend to join the assembly. The Master said, "Where have your conceptual consciousnesses gone and come from?
The monk replied, "As expected, they are not there. The Master then struck him with a staff. The monk said, "I nearly fell into conceptual consciousness.
The Master said, "Having encountered someone at the edge of the village grass, what conversation could there be? The monk said, "For now, I shall go to join the assembly."
A monk asked Chan Master Yian of Danxia Mountain, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "What is the Venerable One?
The monk said, "In that case, there would be no difference. The Master said, "Who told you so?"
