The monk said, "How could it be out of place? The Master said, "If it is not out of place, then you take it back.

As the monk was about to take it, the Master struck him, saying, "This is precisely being presumptuous and overreaching. The monk said, "If that is so, then it must indeed be presented to the Master. The Master said: [He took the portrait.]
"Stop! Stop! A monk from Silla, a successor of Chan Master Dachu, came to visit.
Just as he spread his sitting cloth and was about to prostrate, the Master seized him and said, 'Not yet.'"

When the monk was departing from his own country, he took up a single phrase on the way. The monk remained silent. The Master then pushed him out, saying, "He asked you a single phrase, yet you spoke two.
The monk went to visit another master. He spread out his sitting mat. The Master said, "If you understand it here, you will have wasted your entire life.
The monk said, "I do not understand it here; how then shall I proceed? The Master said, "If you do not understand it here, furthermore—"
The monk headed toward him, and the Master struck out. As the monk entered for an audience and was just unfolding his sitting mat, the Master said, "There is no need for conventional greetings;
bring me back the principle of the time before patterns and traces had arisen. The monk replied, "I have a mouth; it would be idle to keep it mute.
Why do you toil so hard to seek a fan for the month of December? The Master raised his staff as if to strike. The monk seized it and said, "Bring it [back]!"
"Before I have even raised my staff, what is the principle? The Master said, "Those who follow me go south;
those who do not follow me die staying in the east or west. [The monk] said, "Setting aside for a moment following or not following, I ask the Master to point out east, west, south, and north.
The Master then struck him. When Master Piyun came and had just entered the abbot's quarters, the Master immediately asked, "Have you not yet seen the Elder of Dongyue?"
At that time, [Zhaozhou] asked, "How do you act for the sake of sentient beings? Yunmen said, "I see only clouds rising over the azure peaks;

who knows the moon has fallen into the cold pool? The Master said, "Even this is difficult to attain. Yunmen asked, "Is it because you have not yet seen it? The Master gave a shout. Yunmen opened both hands.
The Master said, "There is no limit to those who falsely accuse others. Yunmen covered his ears and departed. The Master said, "Dead!"
[The Master] said, "This fellow has been so all his life. Layman Luoping came to visit the Master. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? Luoping said, "From Nanxi.
The Master said, "Have you brought news from Nanxi? He replied, "As for 'news,' it has already ceased; as for 'ceasing,' it has not yet ceased.
The Master said, "The most painful thing is that which has not yet ceased. Luoping asked, "Tell me, what is it that has not yet ceased? The Master said, "To see it once more."
[The monk] faced [the Master]. For a thousand years he has forgotten his name. He shook his sleeves and departed with his staff.

The Master said, "What limit is there to one who plays with dead snakes? A monk came for an audience; as he was about to prostrate, the Master said, "Wild fox, what have you seen that you prostrate yourself?
The monk said, "Old bald slave, what have you seen that you ask such a question? The Master said, "Alas! Alas! Today the Immortal Heaven has forgotten."
The monk said, "The former was lost and the latter gained; one must simply act when the time is right, for in the end, one does not compensate for what has been lost.

The Master said, "How could it be otherwise? The monk asked, "Who would find this sweet? The Master laughed heartily and said, "Far, far indeed! The monk looked around in all directions and then departed.
While Master Fuzhou Puguang was standing in attendance with his monks, he opened his chest with his hand and said, "Do you understand the old monk's business?
A monk replied, "There is still this here. The Master then covered his chest and said, "It is not that it is too obvious.
The monk asked, "What is there to avoid? The Master said, "Truly, there is nowhere to avoid it. The monk asked, "How is it right now? The Master then struck him.
Chan Master Sanping Yizhong of Zhangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Datian Tong.
He was the son of the Yang family of Fuzhou. Initially, he visited Shigong, who would constantly draw his bow and set his arrow to test the responses of practitioners.
When the Master approached the Dharma seat, Shigong said, "Watch the arrow! The Master then pushed open his chest and said, "This..."
"That was an arrow that kills people. How about an arrow that brings people to life? Guǒ snapped his bowstring three times. The Master then prostrated himself.
Guǒ said, "For thirty years I have drawn my bow and set my arrows, yet I have only managed to shoot half a saint. He then broke his bow and arrows.
Later, he visited Dàdiān and brought up this previous conversation. Dàdiān said, "Since it is an arrow that brings people to life, why did you..."
On the bowstring, discernment is level and without counterpart. Dadian said, "Thirty years from now, it will be difficult to find anyone who can bring up this story.
The Master asked Dadian, "Without pointing east or marking west, please give me a direct indication. Dadian said, "A stone man crouches at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou.
The Master said, "That is still pointing east and marking west. Dadian said, "If you were a phoenix chick, [you would not need such things]."
[The Master] went toward him to seek [the answer]. The Master prostrated. Dadian said, "If you do not grasp the latter phrase, the former discourse will be difficult to complete.
The Master resided at Sanping. He ascended the hall and said, "People nowadays who come forth all study running and seeking, and fabrication.
How can they take this as their own eye? What adequacy is there in it? Do you wish to learn? You need nothing else. Each of you..."
There is the fundamental matter; why do you not realize it? Why are you so resentful in heart and so constrained in speech? What benefit is there in this? I have explained it clearly to you.
If you seek the path of cultivation or the transformative gateways established by the various sages, there are the texts of the Great Canon for that purpose.
However, regarding the matters of the School of the Patriarchs (Zongmen), you must by all means not apply your mind erroneously. [The Monk: ...
Question: "Is there still a path of study within the School of the Patriarchs? The Master said: "There is one path as slippery as moss. The student asked: "Can a student grasp it? The Master said:
"Do not harbor conceptual intentions; you must look for yourself. Question: "What is it like when the black bean has not yet sprouted?
The Master said: "Even the Buddha does not know. A lecturer-monk asked: "Regarding the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, I..."
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A whisk made of tortoise hair and a staff made of hare horns.
Great Virtue, where would you store them? The monk said, "How could tortoise hair and hare horns possibly exist?

The Master said, "The flesh weighs a thousand catties, yet the wisdom lacks even a grain. He ascended the hall and said, "If you all have not yet met a true teacher, that is one thing; but if you have..."

Seeing the author come, one should immediately grasp his essential meaning and head toward the mountain crags and valleys to live on wood and grass—only then will there be a slight degree of resonance.
If you instead rush about seeking intellectual understanding or semantic phrases, you are looking for your hometown from ten thousand *li* away.

[The Master] said, "Tell me, what is Sanping’s surname? The monk said, "Where is the question? The Master said, "When did you ask me that?

Go! You have brought the *ācārya* to ruin. The weary fish stays in the shallows; the dull-witted bird roosts in the reeds.

The wandering clouds and waters are not the *ācārya*; the *ācārya* is not the wandering clouds and waters. This old monk has attained mastery over the wandering clouds and waters; how about you, *ācārya*?

The Dharma Master from Western Sichuan, having ceased his lectures, traveled extensively to visit Master Huayan at Xiangzhou. He asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarchal intent? What is the meaning of the Scriptural teachings?"
"Are they the same or different? Yan said, "They are like the two wheels of a cart, or the two wings of a bird.

The Master said, "You seem to think that the Chan school possesses some special excellence, but in truth, there is none. He then returned to Shu. Later, hearing that the Master’s reputation had spread throughout all quarters, he sent a junior monk to ask him about this.
The Master replied, "Carving sand yields no talk of inlaying jade; binding grass contradicts the intention of a Way-man."
Upon hearing this mention, the Master bowed from afar and said, "It turns out there is indeed a special excellence within the Chan school. He ascended the hall and said:

"To gain understanding through hearing creates patterns in the mind; while it may seem beautiful at first glance, harboring it for long becomes a sickness. The green mountains and white clouds have never met before;
the shuttle-head remains unattached to the warp-thread, and though the brushstrokes run wild, the intent remains distinct."—Jiaxiang I.
The Way. The wise know it to be remote; auspicious grass has no roots, and the worthy do not prize it. Question: "What is the Way? The Master said: "The great sun floods the eyes;
ten thousand miles away, not a single speck of cloud hangs. [The student] said: "I do not understand. The Master said: "In the clear, pure water, the swimming fish are naturally deluded.
Question: "What is the fundamental source? The Master said: "When drinking water, one does not lose sight of its source. Question: "The ancients spread their hair..."

[The student] covered the mud. [The Master asked: "What are you doing? The Master said: "The nine crows have been shot down; one film still remains. One arrow falls to the ground, and the world is plunged into darkness. [The student] asked:
"Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said: "The wind blows across the lotus leaves, filling the pond with green;
the traveler ten *li* away has already covered one more stage. [The student] asked: "When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then? The Master said: "Directly..."

"One must brandish the sword. If one does not brandish the sword, the fisherman will nest in his hut. Later, a monk asked Shishuang, "What is it like when one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha?
Shishuang said, "He has no land; where would you encounter him? The monk returned and related this to the Master (Linji).

After the Master finished his discourse in the Dharma hall, he said, "In the establishment of the gate and its provisional teachings, none is equal to me. Yet, in entering into the profound discourse on principle, I am still inferior to Shishuang."
[The Master] stepped back a hundred paces. A monk asked, "What is it like when two mirrors reflect each other? The Master said, "The oyster presents its priceless treasure;
the dragon spits out the pearl from its belly. A monk asked, "What is the matter within silent stillness? The Master said, "The sleeping palace is empty of people.

After the Master had finished drinking tea, he brewed another bowl for himself and passed it to his attendant. As the attendant was about to receive it, the Master withdrew his hand and asked, "What is this?"
[The monk] said, "There is no opponent. The Abbot asked, "If this is the intent of the Teaching, I have no doubt. But as for the matters within the Zen Gate, how is it?
The Master said, "I, an old monk, only know how to transform the raw into the cooked. [The monk] asked, "What is the principle of the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*)?
The Master said, "A rootless tree upon a rock; the mountain holds unmoving clouds. [The monk] asked, "What is a teacher who has emerged from the cave? The Master said, [as before].

The Master said, "In the void there is no image; beneath your feet wild clouds arise. When the Master was serving as the head cook at Mount Gui, Guishan asked him, "What vegetables are we eating today?
The Master replied, "Two years share the same spring. Guishan said, "Attend well to your duties.
The Master replied, "The dragon dwells in the phoenix’s nest. Guishan asked, "How does one recognize the treasure within the house? The Master replied, "Amidst the bustle, who can compete?"
[The Master] said, "One may become a man of leisure. [The student] asked, "What is a 'concordant phrase'? The Master said, "The lotus leaf is round and round, as round as a mirror;
the water chestnut horn is sharp and sharp, as sharp as an awl. He asked again, "Do you understand? [The student] said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "The wind blows the willow catkins like a fur ball; the rain beats the pear blossoms as butterflies fly. [The student] asked, "What is 'one old and one not old'? The Master...
He said: "The green mountains have never moved; the mountain stream flows eternally. Holding the Night-Bright Talisman in hand, how many know the dawn? Ascending the hall, he said:
"The golden crow and the jade hare vie with one another for brilliance. When the sun is sat upon, the world is plunged into darkness.
The upper lip and the lower lip have never known each other. I tell you clearly: do not let your eyes look back. Why?
The sun and moon are not sufficient to be called bright; heaven and earth are not sufficient to be called great. The axe does not move through the air; the skillful craftsman leaves no trace.
Seeing one's nature leaves no room for a Buddha; awakening to the Way leaves no place for a teacher. An ordinary old monk says:
"To see Gautama with one's own eyes is like looking at yellow leaves. The entire Tripitaka is this old monk’s sitting mat; the profound intent of the Patriarchs is..."
He tore his straw sandals; it would have been better for him to remain barefoot. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "This question has neither host nor guest.
The monk asked, "With whom do you usually converse? The Master said, "Mañjuśrī went to fetch water for me;
Samantabhadra has not yet returned with the flowers. He ascended the hall and said, "I have lived on this mountain for twenty years, and never..."

Regarding the matter of citing the affairs of the Zen school: A monk asked, "I have heard the Master say that while residing on this mountain for twenty years, you have never once cited an affair of the Zen school.
Is this true? The Master said, "It is. The monk then overturned the meditation seat, and the Master ceased speaking.
On the following day, during the communal labor, the Master had a pit dug and ordered his attendant to invite the monk from the previous day, saying, "Old man..."
"For twenty years, this monk has spoken nothing but meaningless words. Today he invites the Venerable Elder to beat this old monk to death and bury him in a pit—please, please do so!
If you do not beat this old monk to death, then the Venerable Elder must beat himself to death and bury himself in the pit before it will be right.
The monk returned to the hall, packed his belongings, and departed in secret. [Later, the Master] ascended the hall and said: "Grasp the old monk at the tips of the hundred grasses!"
"Recognize the Son of Heaven in the midst of the bustling marketplace. When Head Monk Houtou visited, the Master asked, "Where have you come from?
He replied, "From Hunan. The Master said, "Have you ever been to Shishuang? He replied, "I passed through his main road; how could I not have reached him?
The Master said, "I have heard that Shishuang has a 'ball' kōan; is this true? He replied, "The Master must also watch closely before it will do. The Master said:
"What is this ball? He replied, "It cannot leap out. The Master said, "What is the ball-stick?
He replied, "It has no hands or feet. The Master said, "Go for now; I have not yet met you, Venerable One. The next day, he ascended the seat and the Master said:

"Have you arrived recently? The head monk responded with an assent. The Master said, "There is no dharma before one's eyes; the intent lies before one's eyes. It is not a dharma of the present moment;
it is beyond the reach of ears and eyes. The head monk said, "Though you ask today, it is nonetheless not so.

The Master said, "A sliver of moon is difficult to illuminate; it has nothing to do with heaven and earth. The head monk said, "Do not stir up a boiling cauldron," and then he gave a shout of *xianchan*.
Daowu made a gesture as if to overturn the meditation seat. The Master said, "Wait, wait. Where have you failed me, Senior?
Daowu raised his fist and said, "Can you endure this right before your eyes? The Master said, "An adept! An adept! Daowu again made a gesture as if to overturn the meditation seat.
The Master said, "The assembly, look at this warrior! If it comes to deploying the gate and courtyard, this mountain monk is not his equal;
but as for discourse that accords with principle, he is still one degree below this mountain monk. He ascended the hall and said, "The eye does not hang upon the door."
If the mind does not rest in the profound mystery, one will simply fail to produce the numinous grass; this remains merely the status of the Five Indias.
When the radiance of the pearl and the essence of the moon have not yet emerged, there is no old monk here, nor is there a *kalyāṇamitra* at the crossroads of the five paths.
Question: "What is the realm of Jia Shan? The Master said: "A monkey carries its young back into the green peaks; a bird carries flowers and drops them before the emerald cliffs. (Fayan)
[The Master] said, "For twenty years, I have only taken this as a matter of objective conditions. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Dongshan.
The Master asked, "What words or phrases did Dongshan use to instruct his disciples? He replied, "He usually teaches students to train in three paths. The Master asked, "What are these three paths?
He replied, "The Path of Mystery, the Bird’s Path, and the Extended Hand. The Master asked, "Do such words actually exist? He replied, "They truly do. The Master said:

The *Guichi Qianli Chao* records: "The forest-dwelling practitioner grieved. After the Master had once again expounded the profound pivot [of the Dharma] for a period of twelve years, on the seventh day of the eleventh month in the first year of the Zhonghe era of the Tang dynasty, he summoned his attendants and said: 'I have discussed the Way with the assembly of monks for many years;
each of you should know for yourselves the deep purport of the Buddha-Dharma. My illusory body shall now depart when its time is exhausted. You all must be diligent.'"
"Protect [this teaching]. As long as I am alive, do not allow yourself to be swayed by the common world and give rise to grief. Having finished speaking, he passed away suddenly.
He was enshrined in a stupa at his home mountain, and posthumously bestowed the title of Great Master Chuanming (Chuanming Dashi).
Chan Master Lingzun of Anle Monastery on Mount Qingping in Ezhou was a successor of Chan Master Cuiwei. He was a native of Dongping.
Having first visited Cuiwei, he asked, "What is the true meaning of the coming from the West? Cuiwei replied, "I will tell you when there is no one else here. The Master...
After a long silence, [Nanyue] said, "There is no one here; I ask the Master to speak. Weiming stepped down from his meditation seat and led the Master into the bamboo grove.
The Master spoke again, "There is no one here; I ask the Master to speak. Weiming pointed to the bamboo and said, "This stalk is so very long; that stalk is so very short.
Although the Master understood these subtle words, he had not yet penetrated their profound meaning. He departed and went to reside at Dayun Temple.

[The Master] ascended the hall. He cited the karmic occasion of his first meeting with Cuiwei and said to the assembly: "The former master went to such depths for my sake; it was I who failed to recognize his kindness.
From that time on, the Master transformed and guided others, subsequently moving to Qingping. Ascending the hall, he said:

"O senior monks, those who have left the household life must understand the Buddha’s intent before they can succeed. If one understands the Buddha’s intent, it matters not whether one is a monk or a layperson."
Whether male or female, noble or humble, it is sufficient simply to find peace and happiness according to the abundance or scarcity of one's household.

All of you elders have long dwelt in the monasteries and have traveled extensively to consult the venerable masters; how, then, do you understand the Buddha’s intention? Come forth and let us all deliberate upon this together.
Do not let your spirits run high. Otherwise, in the end, nothing will be accomplished and your life will pass in vain.

If you have not yet realized the Buddha’s intent, even if you were to produce water from your head and fire from your feet, burn your body and mortify your arms, possess great wisdom and eloquence, gather a following of a thousand or two thousand, preach the Dharma like falling clouds and rain, and cause celestial flowers to shower down as you lecture—you would achieve nothing but a heterodox teaching.
To contend over right and wrong is to remain very far indeed from the Buddha-dharma.

Since you all have fortunately encountered a time when the physical body is healthy and free from various calamities, why not draw near and apply some effort? It would be well to embody the Buddha’s intent.
A monk asked, "What is the Mahāyāna? The Master said, "A well-rope. The monk asked, "What is the Hīnayāna? The Master said, "A string of coins. [The monk] asked, "What is..."
The pure and peaceful family style. The Master said, "A peck of flour makes three steamed buns. Question: "What is Chan?
The Master said, "A monkey climbing a tree, tail following head. Question: "What is 'outflow' (āsrava)? The Master said, "A bamboo sieve. Question: "What is 'no outflow' (anāsrava)?
The Master said, "A wooden ladle. Question: "When presented face-to-face, what then? The Master said, "Hand it over."

He served as the *karmadāna* (chief cook). Beyond these, his various skillful means for guiding sentient beings did not conform to worldly sentiments; whether acting in accordance with or contrary to circumstances, expanding or contracting as needed, his speech transcended all conventional measures.
In the sixteenth year of the Tianyou era, he passed away at his mountain monastery. He was posthumously granted the title of Chan Master Faxi.

Chan Master Datong of Touzi Mountain in Shuzhou was a native of the Liu family from Huaining in that same prefecture. In his youth, he followed Chan Master Man of Baotang in Luoyang to receive the tonsure.
Initially, he practiced the *ānāpāna* (breathing) meditation; subsequently, he studied the teachings of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, through which he realized the ocean of nature (*dharmatā*).
He then visited Cuiwei, where he attained sudden enlightenment to the fundamental tenets (as recorded in the chapter on Cuiwei). Thereupon, he traveled extensively at will. Later...
He returned to his native land and retired to Mount Touzi, where he dwelt in a thatched hut. One day, when Master Zhaozhou arrived at Tongcheng County, the Master also came out from the mountain;
they met on the road, and Zhaozhou went forward to ask him, "Are you not the master of Mount Touzi?
The Master replied, "Offer me some money for tea and salt. Zhaozhou first returned to his hermitage and sat down; the Master followed later, carrying a water jar.
Yonggu returned to the prefecture, who said, "I have long admired Touzi. Yet, upon arriving, I saw nothing but an oil-seller. The Master said, "You recognize only the oil-seller;
you do not yet know Touzi. The prefect asked, "What is Touzi? The Master lifted up an oil jar and said, "Oil! Oil!
The prefect asked, "When one who has died the great death comes back to life, what is it like? The Master said, "Not."

[The Master] permitted them to travel by night, [instructing] that they must arrive at dawn. The Governor said, "I have already waited for the white; he waits further for the black. He ascended the hall and said:
"All of you who come here intend to seek fresh words and phrases, to compose four-six parallel prose like gathered blossoms, hoping to have something worth saying in your mouths.

why is it swallowed by the six sense-objects (*ṣaḍ-viṣaya*)? The Master said, "By not acting as great, there is no self or others.
The Master resided at Mount Toudi for over thirty years. Those who came and went to be inspired and seek instruction constantly filled his quarters. Even though he...

With fearless eloquence, he would respond immediately to whatever question was posed; like the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching, his subtle words were many, though I have recorded but a small portion here.
During the Zhonghe era, when the Nestled Bandits (Chao Kou) rose up in violence and the empire fell into chaos, a madman brandishing a blade asked the Master, "Why do you stay here?
The Master then preached the Dharma according to the occasion; upon hearing it, the ringleader prostrated himself, cast off his weapons, and changed his clothes.
Having given these away, he departed. On the sixth day of the fourth month in the fourth year of the Qiandehua era, he manifested a slight illness.

When the assembly requested a physician, the Master said to them, "The activity of the four elements is a constant process of aggregation and dispersion; you need not worry, for I shall take care of myself.
Having spoken, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away. He was posthumously titled the Great Master Ciji (Compassionate Salvation).
A monk asked Chan Master Runu of Mount Daochang in Anji Prefecture, “What is the intent of the teachings?
The Master said, “Look for yourself. The monk bowed; the Master said, “The bright moon spreads across the sky; the forms of mountains and rivers naturally divide.
Another asked, “How can one ensure that the nature of hearing does not follow conditions? The Master said, “Listen and see. The monk bowed; the Master said, “A deaf man.”

[The Master] sang the tune of the *hujia* (huqin) flute; the good and bad, the high and low notes were not heard by [the interlocutor] himself. [The interlocutor] said, "If that is so, then the nature of hearing is perfectly intact.
The Master said, "A stone stands in mid-air; fire burns within water. [The interlocutor] asked, "Does empty space have boundaries?"
The Master said, "You know too much. The monk bowed. The Master said, "A three-foot staff carries the sun and moon;
when a single mote of dust flies up, it can block the heavens. A monk asked, "What is the wayman? The Master said, "In his movements there is no trace;
in rising and sitting, he is beyond human knowledge. The monk asked, "How is it so? The Master said, "The three furnaces have exhausted their power, leaving no smoke or flame; ten thousand acres..."
At Hōjū-ji, the water of the Hirata stream does not flow. A monk asked, "What is it like when not a single thought arises?

The Master said, "What can be done? The monk was speechless. The Master spoke again: "Having burst through the Dragon Gate, clouds and rain merge; mountains, rivers, and the great earth leave no trace.

The Master had double pupils in his eyes and hands that reached below his knees. Having received the secret instructions from Cuī, he settled at this mountain, where he cleared the weeds and established [his seat].
At the hermitage, disciples gathered from the four quarters. He extensively expounded the Dharma and transformed beings, until it eventually became a monastic community (*saṃghārāma*).

to close your mouth is to perish. Apart from these two paths, I pray that you, Master, will speak quickly. The Master covered his ears with his hands.
Tiantai Fangshou said, "The first step is easy; the second step is difficult. The Master said, "What such pressing urgency is there?
Tiantai said, "Were it not for this very thing, you would not escape being scrutinized by those in all quarters. The Master did not reply.
Zen Master Zao Shan Guangren ascended the hall while the assembly was gathered.

The Master said, "If there is none, then I shall ascend the seat. He then mounted the platform. A monk came forward and bowed. The Master said, "As for failing me, let that be the responsibility of the assembly; why [do you bow]?"
He then returned to the abbot’s quarters. The following day, a monk asked, "What was the meaning of your previous words? The Master said, "At mealtime there is rice for you to eat;

The monk bowed. The Master said, "Suffering! Suffering! The monk said, "I beg the Master to point it out directly. The Master then extended his feet and said, "Stretch [them]."

Chan Master Juhui of Daguang Mountain in Tanzhou, a fifth-generation descendant of Qingyuan and a dharma heir of Chan Master Shishuang Chu,
was a native of Jingzhao. When he first visited Shishuang, he sat in meditation for long periods without reclining.
He slept on a bed of hemp grass and wore shoes of straw. He sacrificed his life for the Dharma. Changshuang subsequently appointed him as the head of the Xingkong Pagoda Monastery.
One day, Changshuang, knowing that the conditions were ripe, tested what the Master had attained and asked, "The state releases examination candidates every year;
do they still get to pay their respects at the palace gate? The Master replied, "There is one person who does not seek advancement. Changshuang asked, "On what basis? The Master said, "He..."
Furthermore, he did not seek fame. Yang Changzhuang asked, "Aside from today, will there be another time [for you to leave]?
The Master said, "He (Dharma) would not even say that today is. Thus they exchanged questions and answers without impediment for over twenty years.
When the assembly requested him to take charge of a monastery, a monk asked, "Is it that Bodhidharma was the Patriarch? The Master said, "No. The monk said, "If he was not..."
"This is the Patriarch. [The monk] asked, "And why has he come again? The Master said, "It is precisely because you do not realize it. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after realization?

The Master said, "Only then will you know that he is not the Patriarch. [Someone] asked, "How was it before the primordial chaos had divided? The Master said, "At that time, who would there have been to provide an account? Ascending the hall, the Master said:
"The teachings of a lifetime are merely for the purpose of adjusting the hands and feet of people of this age. Even if one were to strip them away until nothing remains..."
In the end, one merely becomes a person who has settled their affairs; this cannot be taken as the matter beneath the patched robe. Therefore it is said:
"For forty-nine years, he could not fully clarify it, nor could he raise its banner. When you arrive here, what should you do?
If you continue to chatter and prattle, I fear you will only bring about further entanglement. Take care.
Chan Master Daogyan of Jiufeng in Ruizhou was a native of Fuzhou. He once served as the attendant to Shishuang.

When Shishuang passed away, the assembly requested the Head Seat to succeed him as abbot. The Master addressed the assembly, saying, "One must first comprehend the meaning of our late teacher before one may do so.
The Head Seat asked, "What meaning did our late teacher have? The Master replied, "Our late teacher said: 'Rest! Cease! Be cold and still...'"
"Leaving the deep pool; leaving ten thousand years in a single thought; leaving the cold ashes and withered wood; leaving the incense burner in the ancient temple;
leaving the single white silk sash. As for the rest, I ask no more. What is 'leaving the single white silk sash'?

The Seat-holder said, "This merely clarifies matters on the side of a single color. The Master said, "I see now that you have not yet grasped the meaning of our former teacher. The Seat-holder said, "You..."

The Master closed his eyes and stuck out his tongue; then he opened his eyes and stuck out his tongue. He said, “Originally there are many faces. The monk asked, “What did you just see?
The monk was speechless. Another asked, “What is a lion? The Master said, “It roars well. The monk patted [him].

The Master said, "Your tongue does not leave your mouth. When the Master was about to pass away, three days prior, he ordered his attendant to summon the First Seat.
The Master was lying down when he let out a single breath. He called to his attendant, saying, "The Master is thirsty; I want some hot water to drink. The Master then lay facing the wall.
As he approached the end of his life, he ordered the assembly to gather; he then extended both hands and showed them his tongue.
At that time, the third seat said, "Everyone, the Master’s tongue-root has become stiff. The Master said, "Alas! Alas! It is truly as the third seat says."
The Master of the Seat said, "My tongue-root has become stiff; it is time for me to depart. Having finished speaking, he passed away in silence.
He was posthumously titled Great Master Shàolóng. Regarding Cén Déhuì Kōng Chánshī of Dèngzhōu Dèshān: A monk asked, "What is the one phrase? The Master said, "Ask further.
The monk asked, "What is the *siddhārtha* (salt) of the Master? The Master said, "Last night at the third watch, I saw the moon bright."

one goes and returns again within the forest of sword-trees.”

A monk asked Zen Master Bajiao of Yingzhou, "How should one proclaim the ancestral Dharma-lineage? The Master said, "It has already been pierced through by the cold eyes of others.

If you seek a directive beneath these words, east and west are already divided."
A monk asked Zen Master Haiyan of Zhengmi Temple on Mount Yunmen in Yuezhou, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe?

The Master said, "Not only was Sēngyáo unable; Zhìgōng himself could not have captured it either. The monk asked, "Why could Zhìgōng not capture it himself?"
The Master said, "The painted colors have not been brought. [The monk] asked, "Has the Master, too, been able to capture it? The Master said, "I, too, have not been able to capture it.
[The monk] asked, "Why has the Master not been able to capture it? The Master said, "It does not borrow its color from me."
[The student] asked, "How shall I depict this? [The Master] said, "It is not reached by being tight.
[The student] asked, "What is it like to be within the secret chamber? The Master said, "One does not sit atop the colored ox."
When Chan Master Shizhu of Fengxiang Prefecture was traveling, he arrived at Dongshan. At that time, Master Qian gave him this instruction: "There are four kinds of people.
One person has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in speech, yet cannot take a single step in practice.

Another person has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in practice, yet cannot utter a single word in speech. Another person can both speak and practice. And another person can neither speak nor practice."

"Who is that person? A teacher stepped forward from the assembly and said: "One who has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in speech yet cannot practice it—this is simply because they lack a tongue, not because they are forbidden from practicing.
One who has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in practice yet cannot utter a single word of it—this is simply because they lack feet, not because they are forbidden from speaking.
One who can both speak and practice—it is simply that the seal and its case correspond perfectly."
"Those who say one cannot speak and cannot act are like those who seek life by cutting off their own breath; they are like the son of a barren woman wearing a cangue and shackles.
Sanshan said, "What about your own portion, Master? The Master said, "In my own portion, everything is thoroughly penetrating, standing tall and clearly manifest.
Sanshan said, "As for Minggong Xiù on the sea, what about him? The Master said, "Two illusory people meeting."
Clapping his hands, he laughed heartily.
Chan Master Cunsou of Datong Monastery on Mount Qiyuan in Hezhong Prefecture initially lectured on the sutras and śāstras;
later, at the abode of Shishuang, he forgot the trap (the means). After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "What is the place where you, the Master, found strength? The Master said, "No."
Dwelling in a position beyond principle, how could he be merely sitting upon a white ox cart? A monk asked, "What is it like when the lotus has not yet emerged from the water?
The Master said, "Are you not asking about the lotus after it has emerged from the water? The monk was speechless. The Master rarely spoke in his daily life, responding only when questioned.
He was posthumously titled Chan Master Zhenji (True Tranquility).
Chan Master Xuantai of Nanyue was profound, serene, and spoke little. He never wore silk or fine fabrics; thus, he was known at the time as "Tai the Patchwork Robe.
When he first met Deshan, he ascended the Dharma hall. Later, he visited Shishuang and subsequently entered his room [as a disciple].
For twenty years, he served as the scribe, befriending Guanxiu and Qiji. Afterwards, he resided at a hermitage called Jingangtai, where he vowed never to establish a formal gate.

His disciples from all quarters who came to him as juniors were all treated with the etiquette due to friends. He once observed that Mount Heng was being severely damaged by the local mountain folk, who practiced slash-and-burn agriculture (*shaye*).

Consequently, he composed the "Ballad of the Slash-and-Burn Mountain" (*Sheshan Yao*), which says: "Children of the slash-and-burn mountain! Children of the slash-and-burn mountain! You know nothing at all.
Year after year you hew down the peaks of the green mountains. Among them, the colors of Mount Heng are the most beautiful—the cypress and pine trees..."
The sharp axe destroys the steadfast branches; the numinous birds and wild cranes have no place to rely. White clouds retreat as blue smoke flies;

monkeys and apes find their paths cut off as they emerge from the cliffs. The roots of the *zhi* and *shu* herbs are lost as the weeds grow lush. Year after year, once felled, they are again cleared away.
"A thousand autumns end, yet it is ultimately difficult to restore the beginning. It was further said: "This year they shall not plant; next year they will again clear the slopes facing Dangyang.
The state’s mountain domains are currently like this; I know not how such a principle can be addressed. This report spread far and wide and reached the imperial court.
An edict was issued to prohibit the practice, so that the monasteries within the mountains were no longer subjected to spreading fires. This was due to the Master's efforts.

As he was about to manifest his passing into extinction, he summoned a monk and ordered him to prepare firewood. He left behind this verse: "This year I am sixty-five; The four elements shall soon depart from their lord.
The Way is of itself profound and mysterious; Within it, there are no Buddhas and no Patriarchs. There is no need for shaving the head, Nor is there any need for bathing.
A single mound of fierce flames— Ten thousand needs are fully satisfied. He sat upright with one leg pendant and passed away. His remains were collected after cremation.
Śāriputra, a pagoda was erected beside Yingyun Pavilion.
A monk asked Chan Master Yungai of Tanzhou, “How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said, “A jade hare hides within the moon.
The monk asked, “And after he appeared? The Master said, “A golden crow flies across the sun. [The monk] asked, “It cannot be fathomed by ordinary sentiment.”
"How is it at this time? the Master asked. Fengxue replied, "The wit of the tongueless child is exhausted. Fengxue went to visit the Master.

The Master asked, "When the stone horn pierces the path through the clouds, what is your intention as you carry your staff? Fengxue said, "Red clouds enshroud the jade elephant; the peaks embrace the mountains, reflecting upon the rivers and springs.
The Master said, "You have come along with me. Fengxue said, "The Master must also lower his voice. The Master said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea."
Chan Master Pumen of Longhu in Shaowu Commandery was the crown prince of Emperor Xizong of the Tang dynasty. From his youth, he abstained from meat;
as he grew older, he had no desire for worldly affairs. Although Emperor Xizong doted on him, he employed every means to mold and direct him, yet in the end could not change his mind.

At the beginning of the Zhonghe era, when Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, the Master cut his hair and wandered away, with no one knowing his whereabouts. He arrived at Shishuang and asked: "The Patriarch..."
The Master asked about the matters of the separate transmission: "Would you be willing to entrust them to me? Baoshuang said, "Do not slander the Patriarchs.

The Master said, "The principles of the world are grand and flourishing; how could they be something fabricated? Baoshuang said, "Is this not a reality? The Master said, "What is your own understanding of this?"
Shuang said, "Wait until the mountain in front of you nods its head, and I shall tell you. Under these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.

He took his leave and, upon reaching the outskirts of Shaowu, saw that the mountains were lush, deep, and beautiful. He then pushed aside the grass and reached a place where smoke was rising; there dwelt an ascetic practitioner.
Upon seeing the Master arrive, the practitioner said, "Master, you shall flourish here," and after bowing deeply, he departed. The Master...
After he had lived there for more than ten years, one day an old man came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where do you dwell? What do you seek by coming here?

The old man replied, "I dwell on this mountain. However, I am not a human; I am a dragon. Because I have failed in my duty regarding the rain, the heavens have issued a punishment and I am due to die.
I pray that you will grant me your protection. The Master said, "You have incurred the offense of the Supreme Deity; what power do I have to exert on your behalf?"
Although this was so, he could easily change his form; in an instant, the old man’s whereabouts were lost. Looking beside him, there was a small snake that had slithered into his sleeve.
At dusk, thunder and lightning shook the mountains while wind and rain broke forth together. The Master sat upright and unmoved. When dawn came and the sky cleared, he let down his sleeve;
the snake fell to the ground and departed. After a short while, the old man bowed and wept, saying, "Had it not been for a Great..."
Master Cizbei thought, "This mountain has been defiled by blood and filth. How can I repay this kindness?
He then hollowed out beneath a cliff to create a spring, saying, "This spring shall serve as a provision for the many assemblies of the future. It is now known as Longhu (Dragon Lake).

When the local people heard of these events, they contributed both wealth and labor to build a monastery together. Monks flocked there like clouds, and the Master propagated his teachings for over thirty years.

As he approached the time of his passing, he struck the bell to assemble the community and spoke this verse: "I fled the world's hardships to leave the household life; The Master pointed out a place of rest for me.
I have dwelt on this mountain and gathered the assembly for thirty years; Ordinarily, I did not wish to bestow [this teaching] lightly. Today I shall speak it clearly to you:
When I close my eyes, listen all together! He passed away peacefully. His stupa was enshrined at his home mountain.
He was posthumously titled Chan Master Yuanjue.
The scholar Zhang Zhuo, having been directed by Master Chan Yue to visit Shishuang, was asked by Shishuang, "What is your surname? He replied:
His surname was Zhang and his name was Zhuo. Shuang said, "Even 'cleverness' cannot be found; from where does 'clumsiness' come? The Master suddenly attained realization and presented this verse:
"Radiant, silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges; Ordinary beings, sages, and all living creatures share my home. When a single thought does not arise, the whole body is revealed;
As soon as the six sense organs stir, they are obscured by clouds. To sever afflictions is to increase the illness again; To pursue..."
To turn toward True Suchness is also erroneous. Accord with worldly conditions without obstruction; nirvana and birth-and-death are equal to flowers in the sky.

Chan Master Yuan’an of Luofu Mountain in Lizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Hui of Jia Shan. He was a native of Linyou in Fengxiang. He left home to become a monk in his childhood and completed [his training].

Jie Tong studied both the sutras and the śāstras, and later became a *śiṣya* (attendant) under Linji. Linji once praised him before the assembly, saying, "Under Linji’s gate, there is but a single arrow;
who dares to face its point? Having received this seal of approval, the Master considered himself sufficient.
One day, while standing in attendance, a *Dharmakathika* (lecturer) visited Linji. Linji asked, "Suppose there is a person regarding the three vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings..."
"Attaining clarity. There is one person who does not attain clarity regarding the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
Tell me, are these two people the same or different? The Master said, "If they have attained clarity, they are the same; if they have not attained clarity, they are different.
The Teacher said, "What kind of place is this, where you speak of 'same' and 'different'? Jie looked at the Teacher and asked, "And what about you? The Teacher then gave a shout.
When Huairang was escorting his preceptor back, he asked the Master, "Was it not you who just now shouted at the old monk? The Master replied, "It was. Huairang then struck him.
Later, when the Master took his leave of Huairang, Huairang asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "I am going to the South.
Huairang drew a line with his staff and said, "Only go if you can pass through this. The Master then shouted. Huairang struck him again. The Master made a gesture...
He paid his respects and departed. The next day, Linji ascended the hall and said, "In the gate of Linji there is a red-tailed carp;
shaking its head and wagging its tail, it has gone toward the south. I know not in whose pickle jar it will be drowned.
Having finished his travels, the Master went directly to Jia Shan to establish a hermitage. For a year he did not visit Jia Shan, who then composed a letter and dispatched a monk to deliver it.

The Master went out to meet him and sat down immediately upon receiving him. He extended his hands again to request something, but the monk had no reply. The Master struck him and said, "Go back and report this to the Abbot.
When the monk returned and reported it, Mount [Shishuang] said, "If this monk had opened the letter, he would surely have come within three days."
"If you do not open this book, this man cannot be saved. The Master indeed arrived three days later;
seeing that Jia Shan did not bow, he stood before him with his hands folded in greeting. Jia Shan said, "A rooster nesting in a phoenix’s lair—it is not its kind.
Begone! The Master said, "I have come from afar to seek your teaching; I pray the Master will receive me. Jia Shan said, "Before my eyes there is no śrāmaṇera; in this place..."
"There is no old monk. The Master then shouted. Xingshan said, "Stop! Stop! Do not be so hasty and reckless. The clouds and moon are the same; the streams and mountains are each different.
It may well be that you can cut off the tongues of all people in the world, but Master, how will you make a tongueless person speak?
The Master paused in thought. Xingshan struck him. From this, he took the teaching to heart. (Xinghua spoke on his behalf: "Just know how to become a Buddha; do not worry about sentient beings. One.

Ri asked Shanshan, "How does one realize the place where neither Buddha nor Māra reach? Shanshan said, "The candle illuminates the images for a thousand li; yet the old monk in the dark room remains deluded.
Ri asked again, "When the morning sun has already risen and the night moon does not appear, what then?

Shanshan said, "The dragon carries the pearl in its mouth; the swimming fish do not look back. As Shanshan was about to pass away, he left behind this final instruction: "Look, look! This is the single branch of Stonehead."
"It has already perished. The Master said, "Not so. Shanshan asked, "Why? The Master replied, "In his own home, there is naturally a green mountain.
Shanshan said, "If it is truly thus, then our lineage shall not fall. When Jia Shan passed away, the Master arrived at Cenyang.
There he met an old acquaintance and spoke of the events in Wuling. The acquaintance asked, "In the blink of an eye, several years have passed; where did you flee from the turmoil? The Master—

[The student] said, "It is right here in the midst of the marketplace. [The Master] said, "Why not go to a place where there are no people? The Master said, "What difficulty is there in a place where there are no people?

[The student] said, "How can one evade [the world] while in the midst of the marketplace? The Master said, "Though one is in the midst of the marketplace, for the time being people do not recognize [one];

therefore, others cannot fathom [one]. He asked again, "Buddha after Buddha correspond with one another; Patriarch after Patriarch transmits to one another. Why do they not bestow [anything] upon each other?"
"How is it when the song is sung? The Master said, "Before the door of a rustic elder, one does not speak of court affairs. [The monk] asked, "What matters should be discussed then?

The Master said, "Unless one meets another who is different, I will never open my fist. [The monk] asked, "If someone has not come from the court and they meet, would you still speak of this understanding?
The Master said, "Regarding the mechanism beyond measure, it is merely a vain labor to witness it with the eyes. The Master subsequently went to Liyang.

He established a hermitage at Lopu Mountain as a place for his leisurely retreat. Later, he moved to Su Creek in Langzhou, where seekers of the profound Way from all quarters flocked to him like travelers on a busy thoroughfare.
Entering the hall, he said: "The final word is the ultimate barrier; it locks off the vital passageway, allowing neither ordinary beings nor sages to pass."
Ordinarily, when speaking to people, they say: "Let everyone under heaven rejoice as they please; I alone am unwilling.

If you wish to know those of superior character, they do not affix the words and teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs to their foreheads, like a tortoise carrying a map—only to bring about the omen of its own destruction—or like a phoenix entangled in a golden net, wondering when it might soar into the azure heavens. One must directly clarify the essence beyond the literal meaning.
Do not seek the standard within words. Thus, even a stone man whose mechanism resembles yours can sing the *bāgē*;

if you were like that stone man, you would surely respond to the *xuěqǔ*. This single path pointed out is known as superficial by the wise. A monk asked, "What is it like when one sees immediately upon a flash?
The Master said, "The morning star divides the dawn light; how can it compare to the brilliance of the sun? Again he asked, "In such a case..."
"If one does not stand when coming thus, and does not vanish when going thus, what then? The Master said: "The firewood-seller values his fuel; the silk-clad man is light. A question was asked:
"It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making an offering to a single mindless practitioner.
I do not yet understand: what fault do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have, and what virtue does the mindless practitioner possess? The Master said: "One..."
A single white cloud stretches across the mouth of the valley; how many returning birds are utterly lost in their nests? [The monk] asked:

"How is it when the sun has not yet risen? The Master said: "The waters of the vast ocean are exhausted, yet the dragon still hides; the clouds rise into the azure heavens, yet the phoenix still flies.

[The monk] asked: "What is the matter of original nature? The Master said: "A single grain lies in a desolate field; though the seedlings are not weeded, they flourish of themselves. [The monk] said: "If they are not weeded..."
"Do not let him be buried by the grass; he is not gone. The Master said: "His flesh and bones differ from common weeds; as mere tares and weeds, they can never truly conceal him. Question:

"What of one who does not harm the lives of living beings? The Master said: "Flowers bloom and mountain shadows shift; the deluded wander in vain confusion. Question: [Untranslated] The Master said: [Untranslated]

[The student] said, "How was it in ancient times and how is it now? The Master said, "The numinous tortoise has no divining cracks; the empty shell need not be drilled. [The student] asked, "What then of that empty shell?
The Master said, "When all views are exhausted, there is no realm of mechanism; therein neither the heterodox nor the orthodox can be established.
[The student] said, "In that case, there is no place to rest. The Master said, "The profound image begins before form exists; vain effort is exhausted by the application of colors and ornamentation."

Question: “When the dragon’s mechanism does not emit mist, how does it benefit all things? The Master said: “The Way is fundamentally nameless; it exists neither in light nor in darkness. [The questioner] asked:
“As for that matter which is not caught by light or darkness, how is it so? The Master said: “It is easy to mention within words, but difficult to bring forth beyond the external. Question:
“When one is not born into the house of the Tathāgata and does not sit upon the Lotus King throne, what is it like? The Master said: “Tell me.”

"How heavy is the brazier? [The student] asked. "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "In the den of the lion, there are no other beasts;
where the elephant king walks, there is no trace of foxes. [The student] asked, "What is it like when they are brought forth all at once? The Master said:
Presenting the raw jade without knowing the occasion is merely a laborious invitation to have one's feet cut off. He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Jingnan.
The Master said, "If a person were to go like this, would you meet him? The monk said, "I do not meet him. The Master said, "Why do you not meet him? The monk said: [He remained silent.]
"If one encounters him, their head will shatter into pieces. The Master said, "The *ācārya*’s three inches are very tight.
When Yunmen saw this monk in Jiangxi, he asked, "Is there such a saying? The monk replied, "Yes. Yunmen said, "Luofu would have retreated three thousand li."
Question: "How is it to practice in the inconceivable realm? The Master said: "The green mountains constantly lift their feet; the white sun does not shift its wheel. Question:
"How is the matter of standing alone in a withered and desolate field? The Master said: "A heron leaning against a snowy nest may still be distinguished;
a crow alighting on black lacquer is difficult to discern. Question: "What is the guest within the host? The Master said: "Constantly asking the way when meeting people."
Zhangmi, who was stationed there, asked, "What is it to raise both guest and host together? The Master said, "A withered tree has no horizontal branches;

when a bird comes, it finds no place to set its foot. He asked, "What is it like when one is perpetually in a state of dim obscurity? The Master said, "Casting a jewel into the sands of a deep abyss."
The Master said, "Consciousness is naturally different. [The student] asked, "If that is so, then even when extending one's hand, one does not encounter the Master?

The Master said, "Do not mistake the cry of a crane for the song of a warbler. [The student] asked, "Everyone understands the three dots of the character *yuan* (round); but as for the 'house style' (*jiaweng*) of Lu Pu, what is it like?"
The Master said: "A single clap of thunder, and the sound of the cloth drum vanishes. Question: "What is it like at the exact time of midday?
The Master said: "Midday still lacks half; only when the sun sets does it become full. To understand the meaning within this, place the head on the tail of the ox."
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The rustling bamboo by the window; though frost has fallen, it does not grow cold.
As the monk prepared to offer further words, the Master said, "I hear only the sound of the wind striking; how many thousand stalks must there be?
He ascended the hall and said, "Sun Bin has closed his shop. Let any diviners come forward! A monk said, "I request the Master to perform a divination for me. The Master said, "In your house..."
The Patriarch died. The monk had no reply. (Fayan, acting for him, clapped his hands three times. [The Master] asked: "What is the meaning of coming from the West?
The Master struck the meditation seat with his whisk and said, "Do you understand? [The monk] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "A sudden thunder in the heavens startles the universe;
yet the shrimp at the bottom of the well does not raise its head. [The Master] asked: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Snow covers the solitary peak."
"No announcement was made. The rain nourished the stone shoots; the shoots had to grow. A monk asked, "The Dharma-body is unconditioned and does not fall into any numerical categories.
Is this so? The Master said, "It would be better to cherish your eyebrows. The monk asked, "How can one avoid this fault?

The Master said, "A clay tortoise may last for a thousand years at your pleasure, but it will never understand how to follow the clouds and cranes. The monk said, "Even Sun Bin himself would suffer such a scathing critique. The Master said, "No."
"A bull with its nostrils pierced—what defense does it have? The monk then let out a bellow like a bull. The Master said, "This beast! The monk then gave a shout.
The Master said, "Tucking the tail while showing the teeth—this is still not the hand of a master. He asked, "Leaping off from a ten-thousand-fathom precipice and letting go of the hands—"
"How can one avoid perishing when the body is lost? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru is tied with a lotus fiber. [The student] asked, "What kind of realm is this?
The Master said, "Looking up at the heart of the lotus atop the banner-pole of the world-system (*kṣetra*). [The student] said, "If that is so, then it is profoundly still and clear.
The Master said, "Turning the body once more on the summit of Mount Sumeru. [The student] said, "If that is so, then it is full of apprehension and urgency."
The Master said, "In vain you follow the decoy pigeon; for nothing you lose your body in the net. [The monk] asked, "How can one avoid following it?

The Master said, "The neck of the jar is narrow; though the goose intends to fly through to the heavens, it cannot. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when the dew does not hang upon the myriad trees?"

The Master said: "Where there is a tiger, crows must caw; where there is no person, birds are not startled. A monk asked: "If a person comes who can overturn heaven and earth, will you still receive him?
The Master held up his whisk. The monk said: "In that case, one has met a wise sovereign. The Master said:
"Vague and indistinct, like a tune just beginning to be heard, it is then blown by the wind into another key. A monk asked: "Neither Buddha nor Mara reaches here."
"How can one distinguish this state? The Master said, "Yaññadatta’s head was not lost; it was his failure to recognize it in the mirror. Question: "What is the means to escape birth and death?
The Master said, "Holding onto water to prolong life by artifice, one does not hear the wondrous celestial music. Question: "From what do the four great elements arise?
The Master said, "The clear water is originally waveless; bubbles are stirred up by the wind. [The questioner] asked, "When the bubbles subside and return to the water..."
“How is it? The Master said, “Neither turbid nor murky; fish and dragons leap as they please. Question: “How can one leave birth and death behind?
The Master said, “In a single thought, forget all artifice; the Great Void is without blemish. Question: “What is the Way?

The Master said, “To maintain artifice is still to linger in traces; to remove the stump and the path is open. Question: “What is that which cannot be contained within the Great Canon of Teachings? The Master...

[The Master] said: "The rain nourishes the three types of grasses, and the single piece of jade naturally shines. A question was asked: "When a single hair swallows up the vast ocean, what more can be said therein? The Master said:
"If a household possesses the *Bai Ze* map, there will certainly be no such monsters. (Baofu offered a different version, saying: "...")

"In my home, there is no *Bai-zai* diagram, nor are there such demons and spirits. The questioner asked, "What is it like at the moment of stillness? The Master said, "At that time, thunder responds to the season, shaking the mountains and startling the hibernating insects.
The questioner asked, "How is it when there are a thousand kinds of movements? Is it not different from this moment of stillness? The Master said, "The spiritual crane soars beyond the void;
the dull bird does not leave its nest. The questioner asked, "How is it [then]? The Master said, "An old man bows to a youth; all the people of the world [do the same]."

[The Master said: "Difficult to believe. [The Questioner] asked: "When the various sages come in such a manner, with what shall one make offerings? The Master said: "Though the Earth-Roamer (Tu-su) holds a mendicant’s staff, he is not a Brahmin.
[The Questioner] asked: "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said: "The sun and moon revolve together, radiating their brilliance."
"Whose family has a separate path? He replied, "In that case, then light and obscurity follow different routes, and matters are not uniform.
The Master said, "If you simply do not lose your sheep yourself, why must you weep at the fork in the road? He asked, "When a student intends to return to his hometown, what then? The Master said:
"The family is ruined and the people are lost; where will the son go? [The monk] said, "If that is so, then I shall not return.
The Master said, "The remaining snow before the courtyard melts under the sun; who will sweep away the drifting dust within the room? Thereupon he spoke a verse:

"Resolute in my intent, I return to my home, Boarding a boat to cross the Five Lakes. Raising the oar, the stars and moon vanish; Pausing the rowing pole, the sun stands solitary. Untying the mooring rope, I depart from the heterodox."
To the bank. Raise the sails and set out upon the direct path; once you have arrived home, all shall be swept clean, sparing you from being a fool within the house.
A monk asked, "Movement is the sprout of the Dharma King; stillness is the root of the Dharma King. I do not ask about the root and the sprout;

what is the Dharma King? The Master raised his whisk. The monk said, "This is still but the sprout of the Dharma King. The Master said, "If the dragon does not emerge from its cave, who can do anything about it? Attendant.
Someone said to the Master, “Dharma Master Zhao has composed the *Four Treatises*; they are truly extraordinary.

The Master replied, “Master Zhao is indeed extraordinary, yet he has not yet seen the Patriarch. The man was speechless. (Fadeng spoke on his behalf, saying: “Where, O Monk, is [the Patriarch]? Yunju Xi said:

“Where is the place where Master Zhao did not see the Patriarch? Is it because there are so many words? Or rather, how many words does Master Zhao have? Question: “What is the single path of the living mechanism? The Master—
He said: "Striking the void produces resonance; striking wood produces no sound. He said: "The Dharma opens like two mountains; its words are spread throughout all quarters.
In the eighth month of the first year of the Guanghua era, he instructed his attendants: "In the way of renunciation, one does not keep superfluous possessions. This is the time for sowing seeds."
One should certainly practice economy and reduction; all matters concerning construction and maintenance shall be entirely suspended. Time flows swiftly, and the Great Way is profound and mysterious.

If one merely follows along with worldly habits, by what means could one realize it? Although his exhortations were earnest and sincere, the assembly took them as routine and failed to heed his warnings.
In the winter, he manifested a slight illness yet did not cease receiving visitors or answering inquiries. On the first day of the twelfth month, he addressed the assembly, saying: "I..."
"It is not that clarity is subsequent. Now I have a matter to ask you all: if you say this is it, you are placing a head upon a head;

The Master then ceased questioning him. That night, he ordered an attendant to summon Cong and asked, "Ācārya," [and continued to question him].
"Today’s response is most reasonable. You have truly grasped the meaning of the former master. The former master said: 'There is no dharma before the eyes;

The Master said, "You have understood. The monk replied, "Yancong has truly not understood. The Master shouted at him and drove him out, saying, "Suffering! Suffering! (Xuánjué remarked:

“How can you be deluded by such trifles as a hair? The Master said, “Amoghapāśa. The monk asked, “What object is being forged and smelted in the great furnace and fierce flames?

The Master said, “Forging Buddhas and forging Patriarchs. The monk asked, “How do you forge the Buddhas and Patriarchs? The Master said, “Karma is within them. The monk asked, “What do you call this karma?
The Master said, “Even the power of the Buddha is not equal to it. The monk asked, “For forty-nine years he did not speak a single word. As for...”
“What is the phrase that does not speak of the bottom? The Master said, “A single shoe went west; the Wayman did not look back.
[The student] asked, “Is this perhaps where the Master finds rest? The Master said, “If it is an official horse, there is no need for a seal.

The Master said, "True gold is unwilling to be bartered; who would be willing to exchange it for a lump of clay? [The monk] said, "If that is so, then you are unwilling to go [to the Buddha].
