"What is it? the Master asked. "For the sake of speaking with you," [the monk] said. "If one speaks of external matters, how can they be clarified? the Master asked. "Through long days and many years, the sinews and bones are formed," he replied.
[The monk] asked, "When one does not oppose the armies of Māra, how does one realize the Way? "The waters of the sea do not require a ladle to scoop them out," the Master replied.
[The monk] asked, "When one does not dwell on the cloud-covered mountains and constantly resides upon the bottomless boat, what then? "It is indeed so," the Master replied.
Matured natural fragrance. [The monk] said, "Please speak further, Master. The Master said, "Before the gate is a true son of the Buddha.
[The monk] said, "Why does the student not see it? The Master said, "Everywhere is Old Teacher Wang."
A monk asked Chan Master Kewen of Panlong Mountain in Yuanzhou, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go?
The Master said, "The stone ox follows the ancient road; the lamp shines brightly in the day. Another asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said:
The foolish child abandons his father and flees.
Chan Master Yuelun of Huangshan in Fuzhou was the son of the Xu family of Fudang. Initially, he visited Sanfeng, but their karmic conditions did not harmonize.
Subsequently, hearing that Jia Shan was flourishing in his teaching, he went there to seek him out. Jia Shan asked, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Yuelun."
Shan drew a circle and said, "How does this compare to that? The Master said, "If you speak in such a manner, Reverend, many in all quarters will not approve.
Shan asked, "What about you, Dharma-heir? The Master said, "Do you see the lunar disc?"
Mount [Shan] said, "If you speak in such a manner, many people here will not approve of you.
The Master then humbly accepted this and went to seek instruction. One day, Jia Shan called out in a loud voice, "Where are you from?
The Master replied, "I am a man from Min. Jia Shan asked, "Do you know me? The Master replied, "Does the Master know me? Jia Shan said, "No."
"Nevertheless, you must first repay this old monk for the price of his straw sandals; only then will I repay you for the price of Luling rice.
The Master said, "If that is so, then you do not know the Master. I do not yet understand what the price of Luling rice is. Baizhang said, "A true lion cub, truly able to roar.
Thereupon, the Master entered the room to receive the seal of transmission and attended him for seven years. When the assembly requested him to reside at Huangbo, he accepted.
Shan ascended the hall and said: "The Patriarch came from the West specifically to sing this matter.

It is simply that people have failed to realize it, instead seeking it outwardly—casting themselves into the waters of the Red River to search for pearls, or going to the Jade Mountains to look for jade. Therefore it is said: 'Those who enter through the gate...'"
"It is not a family treasure. To mistake the shadow for the head—is this not a great error? A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "In the halls of Liang, no effort was expended; in the realm of Wei, all traces of mind were severed. The monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "The stone ox frequently spews mist throughout the three springs; the wooden horse’s neighing fills the roads. The monk asked, "How can one come to see [it]?"
"Your original face. The Master said, "There is no need to hang up a stone mirror; when dawn breaks, the rooster cries out of its own accord.

A questioner asked, "Regarding the single phrase of the School of the Patriarchs, I request the Master’s deliberation. The Master said, "Huangfeng stands alone, detached and elegant beyond the mundane world; as the years pass and the months go by, it is cold and piercing.

A questioner asked, "Without discerning the words within [the middle way], how can one provide guidance? The Master said, "The sword has long since been lost; you are merely marking the boat's place on the water."
Question: "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said: "A stone ox lies upon the water;
east and west, it moves with freedom. Question: "What is the meaning of the present moment? The Master said: "The autumn wind has its own melody; the crescent moon knows no fixed direction. Question:
"Where is the place where a student applies their mind? The Master said: "The door of awakening is not closed; do not be deluded by the moon. Question: "What is... (The question is cut off.)
"Blue Sky Path. The Master said, "The crane perches upon a tree beyond the clouds; it does not weary of the bitter winds and frost. [A monk] asked, "How is it with matters of the past?
The Master said, "The dragon calls from the clear pool; the waves and ripples are naturally solemn. The Master entered nirvana in the third year of the Tongguang era.
His stupa was erected in the northwest corner of the monastery.

A monk arrived to pay his respects to Chan Master Shao Shan Huanpu at the capital of Luoyang. As the monk rose from his prostrations, the Master said, "A man of great talent hides his skill in a humble dwelling.
The monk stood to one side; the Master continued, "You have lost the timber for a ridgepole. The monk asked, "What is the realm of Shao Shan?
The Master replied, "Ancient and modern monkeys and birds cry out; emerald colors are shrouded in thin mist. The monk asked, "What is the essence within this realm?"
A monk approached. The Master said, "Step back and look. The monk entered for an audience. The Master asked, "Are you not that talkative old man Yin?
Yin replied, "I dare not say so. The Master asked, "How many mouths do you have? He replied, "My whole body is it. The Master asked, "Where do you usually defecate?
He replied, "I defecate within the mouth of Shaozhou. The Master said, "If there were a mouth of Shaozhou, it would be fine; but if there were no mouth of Shaozhou—"
"Where do you intend to defecate? Because [Dongshan] was speechless, the Master struck him. Layman Zun Bunan visited the Master; they met at the foot of the mountain.
Zun asked, "To which place does the road of Mount Shao lead? The Master pointed his finger and said, "O! It goes toward that dark green expanse.
Zun stepped forward, seized him, and said, "I have long heard of Mount Shao; is this not it? The Master said, "Yes."
"It is exactly so. What business do you have with me, Preceptor? Zun said, "I intend to ask a question; will you answer it, Master?
The Master said, "Look at you—you are not made of 'golden teeth' (a tiger). How could you possibly draw your bow to shoot Wei Chi?
Zun said, "The phoenix flies straight into the misty heights; who fears the wild sparrows in the woods? The Master said, "The painted drum before the hall is for you to strike as you please."
"Try displaying your family style like an old monk. Dun said, "A single phrase transcends the thousand sages; the pine and vines do not equal the moon's orb.
The Master said, "Even if you were to emerge directly outside the realm of Wei-yin, you would still be half a month's journey behind Shao-shan.
Dun asked, "Where does the fault lie? The Master said, "Such bold and unconventional words are known only by people of this age. Dun said, "If that is so,"
A true gem differs from those in the mud; it does not brush away the dust of myriad affairs. The Master said, "Under the workshop of Lu Ban, one merely exerts cleverness.
Zun said, "The student acts thus; I do not yet know what your intention is, Master. The Master said, "At night, the Jade Maiden casts her shuttle."
He was weaving brocade at his western dwelling. Daozun asked, "Is this not the very style of your house, Master?
The Master said, "A plowman fashions a jade water-clock; it is not the work of a master craftsman. Daozun said, "That is still merely literary expression.
What is the true style of your house, Master? The Master said, "I stand across the universe; who is there to show their head? Daozun was speechless. The Master then departed with him.
They returned to the mountains. As soon as the formalities were concluded, the Master called him forward and said:
"The *dārala* has the spirit to pierce the heavens; this old monk has the scheme to enter the earth. The *dārala* swallows the vast ocean in one gulp; this old monk carries Mount Sumeru on his back.
The *dārala* comes forward with sword in hand; this old monk awaits him with spear raised. As for the single path leading upward—speak quickly! Speak quickly! Zun replied: "Illumination."
The mirror is set upon its stand; I ask the Master to take a look. The Master said, "I do not look. Zhen asked, "Why do you not look? The Master said, "The water is shallow and there are no fish;
it is but a vain labor to cast down the hook. Zhen had no reply, and the Master struck him. A monk asked, "What is the mark of 'One Suchness' (yīrúxiàng)?
The Master said, "The egret flies white through the Milky Way; the distant mountains are a deep, profound blue. He asked, "In a place where right and wrong do not reach, is there still..."
"Is there a phrase or not? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What kind of phrase is it? The Master said, "A single mass of white clouds does not reveal its ugliness.
After his passing, he was posthumously titled Chan Master Wuwei (Fearless).
Chan Master Lingchao of Shanglan in Hongzhou first resided at Mount Shanglan in Ruizhou, where he propagated the Way of Jiaoshan and gathered a multitude of disciples.
Later, he established a Chan monastery at Hongjing, naming it after Shanglan; his transformative teachings flourished even more greatly.
A monk asked, "What is the fundamental matter of Shanglan? The Master said, "Not borrowed from the thousand sages; how could it be..."
Wanji asked, "If one neither borrows nor seeks, what then? The Master said, "Can it be placed in your hand?
A monk asked, "How does one discern [the truth] before the blade? The Master said, "Before the blade, no shadow is revealed; do not seek it on the tip of the tongue.
A monk asked, "What is the singing of a tongueless person? The Master said, "The melody shakes the azure heavens; the notes are *gong* and *shang*."
"Not an offense. Question: "Two dragons contend for a pearl; who is the one that obtains it? The Master said: "The pearl covers the ground; even when seen with the eyes, it is like mud. Question:
"After Shancai saw Mañjuśrī, why did he instead go south? The Master said: "To learn from those who have entered the chamber."

"Knowledge thus penetrates all directions. [A monk] asked, "Why did Maitreya instead send him to see Mañjuśrī? The Master said, "The Way is vast and boundless; it is inexhaustible when encountered by people.
In the first month of the first year of the Dàshùn era of the Táng dynasty, he addressed the assembly, saying, "I originally intended to remain here for ten years.
Now that my work of transformation is complete, I shall depart immediately. After the midday meal, he struck the bell, sat upright, and passed away. His posthumous title was—

Chan Master Yuanzhen was a Chan master at Sizhan Monastery in Yanzhou. A monk asked him, "In ancient times, there was the saying 'when invited, one does not turn back. Now I invite the Master to enter a well; will you go or not?
The Master said, "Deep down, there is no other source; those who drink from it eliminate all afflictions. The monk asked, "What is [the meaning of this]?"
"The style of our Master’s house. The Master said, "One who understands this must know that the moonlight is cold. He asked, "How was it before the Buddhas appeared in the world?
The Master said, "In the royal palace, all news is cut off. He asked, "How was it after they appeared in the world? The Master said:
Flourishing and withering each differ.
When Chan Master Hailu of Taiyuan was invited by someone to provide offerings for Tripitaka Master Guanding, the master prepared the seating;
having finished arranging them, the Master sat down in that very seat. At that time, the Dharma Master Yunshe asked, "In what year did you, Venerable Sir, begin your practice?"
The Master said, "Head Lecturer, come forward. Zhaozhe approached. The Master said, "As for Kātyāyana, in what year did he practice the Way?
Zhaozhe was at a loss. The Master shouted, "This bed-wetting ghost! A monk asked, "Why are there so few people in the Master’s monastery?
Why are there so many people in Dinghui Monastery? The Master said, "Where the grass is deep, wild deer abound; where the cliffs are high, the *xièzhài* (unicorn) dwells."
Xi asked, "What is it to answer spontaneously without being questioned? The Master said, "The melody of the pines resonates like the sound of a lute.
Chan Master Baishui of Jiazhou was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?

The Master said, "The four oceans have no dwelling place; a single drop moistens the entire universe. He was asked, "Regarding the single path of Caoxi, what should be discussed there? The Master said, "The mountain pines by the stream..."
Cranes arrive and gather; within the moon, fragrant cassia and phoenixes return. A question was asked: "What is this sutra? The Master said:
"The shuttle-casting barren woman resounds through the vast void; the mud-ox at the bottom of the sea cries out frequently at night."
A monk asked Chan Master You of Mount Tiangai in Fengxiang Prefecture, “What is the water of Mount Tiangai?
The Master said, “The four seas overflow, yet not a single drop is violated. The monk asked, “When a student intends to study the sutras, what should he do?

The Master said, “Since you are a great merchant, why seek small profits? The monk asked, “When one is unmoved by external objects, what is that? The Master said, “Although there are [disturbances] in the borderlands,” [he remained unmoved].
Ling. This was not a year of Great Peace.
Chan Master Linggui of Sanjiao Mountain in Qizhou, the Dharma heir of Chan Master Qingping Zun, first visited Qingping. Qingping asked, "Why have you come? The Master replied:
He came to pay his respects. Baizhang asked, "Whom do you pay your respects to? The Master said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Abbot.
Baizhang scolded him, saying, "You dull-witted monk! The Master then prostrated himself. Baizhang struck the Master on the neck once with his hand. From this, the Master attained realization.
Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Come tomorrow and I will tell you. Do not speak of it now."
Not permitted.

Zen Master Ganteng of Touzi, a dharma successor of Zen Master Tongchan of Touzi, was asked by a monk: "When the Master ascends the precious seat, whom do you intend to receive and instruct? The Master replied: "Like the moon."

Fuchu went to Qianxi and said, "In that case, the whole ground is without deficiency. Qianxi said, "Do not speak like that. A monk asked, "The father does not surrender; why then does the son surrender?
Qianxi said, "Is this not the business within another's house? The monk asked, "Does the relationship between father and son belong to the realm of effort or not?
Qianxi said, "It does not. The monk asked, "If it does not belong to the realm of effort, what then? Qianxi said, "The father..."
The disciples each removed their own [robes]. They asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "You and I understand each other.
While the Master was traveling in the mountains, he saw a cicada’s exuviae. An attendant asked, "The shell is here; where has the cicada gone?
The Master took the shell, shook it by his ear three or five times, and made the sound of a cicada. Thereupon, the attendant attained awakening.
Chan Master Niu-tou Wei of Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the three periods have not been able to employ even a single bit of artifice.
The teachers throughout the land have mouths like flat carrying-poles. How do you all fare? It is truly not easy; unless one knows that which truly is, none others can know it.
A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Rice from mountain fields and unpolished grain."
[The Master] served rice and plain yellow pickled vegetables. [A monk] asked, "If a distinguished guest were suddenly to arrive, what would you do?
The Master said, "If you eat, let you eat; if you do not eat, go wherever you please. [A monk] asked, "I do not ask about the pearl beneath the chin of the black dragon;
how can one recognize the treasure within the home? The Master said, "In the midst of busyness, how can one become a person at leisure?"
A monk asked Zen Master Chengzhao of Xichuan Qingcheng Xiangshan: "When the Buddhas encounter difficulty, they hide their bodies within the flames.
I wonder, when a patch-robed monk encounters difficulty, where does he hide his body? The Master said: "A Persian placed inside a crystal jar.
The monk asked: "What is the newly risen moon? The Master said: "Too many people do not see it."
A monk asked Chan Master Tianfu of Shan Prefecture, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, “The Yellow River has not a drop of water;
Mount Hua and Mount Yue have all sunk away.”
A monk asked Zen Master Zungu of Zhongliang Mountain in Xingyuan Prefecture: "In the empty kalpa, there was no one able to ask about the Dharma;
now that there is someone asking about the Dharma, how can it be settled? The Master said: "The Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika sits inside a jar. The monk asked:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "The Daoist carries a leaking cup."
A monk asked Chan Master Guyin of Xiangzhou, "What is the mechanism of the white clouds that is untouchable? The Master said, "A crane wearing a crow's face;
the floating world is not abandoned."
A monk asked the Zen Master of Mount Jiuzhong in Anzhou, "I have heard much of Mount Jiuzhong from afar; yet now that I have arrived, I see only a single peak.
The Master said, "You, O *dārala*, see only one peak; you do not see the nine peaks. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the nine peaks?
The Master replied, "The water is swift and the flower-crested waves surge."
A monk asked Chan Master Panshan of Youzhou (the Second Patriarch): "How can one escape the three realms? The Master said, "How long has it been since you have been inside them?
The monk asked, "How can one escape them? The Master said, "Green mountains do not obstruct the flying white clouds. The monk asked again.
"I have heard it said that afflictions are like a magically conjured person, and like the son of a barren woman. How is this principle to be understood?
The Master replied, "Venerable, you are exactly like the son of a barren woman."
A monk asked Zen Master Jiuzhong Jinghui, "How can one pass over the deep pit of liberation? The Master said, "Do not seek to pass.
The monk asked, "How then can one pass? The Master said, "Seeking to pass is also not it."
Zen Master Gannin Enjun of Tōkyō was the son of the Lin family from Xingtai. When he first entered the patriarchal seat, he traveled extensively through Heng, Lu, Min, and Shu.
Once, while passing through a deep valley at Fenglin, he suddenly beheld precious treasures manifesting. His companions looked at one another, intending to take them;
the Master said, "When the ancients tilled their gardens, they encountered gold as if it were mere rubble. Wait for my *gān*... [The text here is incomplete].
Fuding covered his head and said, "I require this for the Sangha of the four quarters. Having finished speaking, he departed and went to visit Touzi. Touzi asked, "Where did you stay last night?
The Master replied, "The Immovable Site of Enlightenment (*acalabodhimaṇḍa*). Touzi said, "Since you say it is immovable, by what means have you arrived here? The Master replied:
"Is this not movement? Tanyou asked. Tanyue replied, "Originally, it does not dwell anywhere. Touzi silently granted his approval.

Subsequently, he resided at Guanyin, where the assembly regularly numbered several hundred. When Emperors Gaozu and Shizong of the Zhou dynasty were living in seclusion, they would invariably pay him homage whenever they ascended to the abbot’s quarters.

Upon their accession to the throne, they specially bestowed upon him purple robes and appointed him as the Great Master of Pure Precepts (Jingjie Dashi). As he was about to pass away, he offered his final instructions.
When his disciples had finished their duties, he passed away with a serene countenance and palms joined.
During the time when Chan Master Siming of Haozhou was among the assembly, a monk asked: "What is the meaning of 'the novice and probationary student who is the Venerable'?"
The Master said, "Yes. The monk asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "A maggot in excrement, its head emerging and submerging.
A monk asked Zen Master Zhao Fu of Fengxiang Prefecture: "Both Dongya and Wuya have gone out on patrol; why does the Master [remain behind]?"
Mo did not leave the community. The Master said, "The roles of abbot and disciple differ; why do you, Ācārya, find this strange?
This concludes the section on Chan Master Daguang Hui, a successor in the sixth generation under Qingyuan.
At Gushan in Tanzhou, Chan Master Youyuan was asked by a monk, "How can a solitary child find a way back home?
The Master said, "The path is impassable for one who understands. The monk said, "In that case, there is no place of veneration?

The Master said, "I say that your alms bowl has fallen to the ground and you cannot pick it up. Another asked, "What is it like when one turns at a single push? The Master said, "A wild horse runs wild."
At that time, the whip and reins snapped; the stone man clapped his hands and laughed heartily.
A monk asked Zen Master Longxing of Tanzhou, "What is it like when one gives a single push and it turns? The Master said, "Your faculties are not sharp."

Chan Master Wuyin of He Mountain in Jizhou was the son of the Wu family of Fuzhou. At the age of seven, he left home to become a monk under Xuefeng.

He descended from his seat and sighed in admiration. Lord Li of Jiangnan summoned him and asked, "Where have you come from, Master?

In the second month of the first year of the Jianlong era, he manifested a slight illness. On the second day of the third month, he took leave of the assembly, saying, "Students who come later do not yet know Heoshan;
recognize him right now! Be careful! Having finished speaking, he passed away in peace. His posthumous title was [bestowed].
Chan Master Faxing. A monk asked Chan Master Mou of Letan in Hongzhou, "What is the place where the student exerts effort? The Master said, "This is precisely the place where one exerts effort.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What was the meaning behind Baizhang rolling up his mat? The Master said, "Take care."
He then descended from his seat.
One day, Master Shao of Liutong Monastery in Taizhou, a successor of Chan Master Xingquan, was asked by Xingquan: "Where have you come from? The Master replied:
[The Master] was clearing a slash-and-burn field. Quan asked, "What is it like after the fire has burned? The Master said, "An iron snake cannot penetrate it.
After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "How is the matter that does not pass through the throat or the lips? The Master said, "Wait until you have used a single spade to cleave Mount Jūnzì;

even then, I will not speak to you. A monk asked, "There is a poisonous snake on the South Mountain; how can one approach it? The Master [said]: *Note: The text provided ends abruptly at "The Master," suggesting the original source may have been truncated.*
He said, "It is not only you, Ācārya; even a thousand sages cannot come near it. A man asked, "I have heard that there is a 'Single Sword' teaching in the South.
What is this Single Sword? The Master said, "Do not meet its edge. The man asked, "What about when one's head falls off? The Master said:
"I say that [the sword] does not meet the blade; what head would it have? The man bowed in thanks and departed. [Someone] asked: "Before one's parents were born, where did that person stand?
The Master said: "The hexagram signs had not yet arisen; Sun Bin lost his calculation. [Someone] asked: "What is the summit of the great thousandfold world?
The Master said: "It does not level with the other peaks. The Master concluded his summer retreat and entered Mount Tiantai to the Huading Peak.
He concealed his traces, and no one knew where he ended his life.
Zen Master Zhihan of Mount Yungai in Tanzhou was a successor of Zen Master Yuan of Mount Yungai. A monk asked: "What is the surging wave upon the summit of Mount Sumeru?"
Tian asked, "Master, Mañjuśrī is truly making a commotion. The Master said, "What is the matter within the state of ultimate reality?

The Master said, "I do not display great compassion before the stimulus of the mind. He asked, "What is it like to be a person of that other shore? The Master said, "No shadow is revealed before the blade's edge;
no trace can be found after the phrase has passed."
A monk asked Zen Master Wo-long of Silla, "What is the mark of a great man? The Master said, "He does not extend his hand from within the purple silk curtain.
The monk asked, "Why does he not extend his hand? The Master said, "It would not be noble. The monk asked, "How should one apply the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day?
The Master said, "A monkey eating a fur-bug. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the deep pool? The Master said—
[The monk] said: "The silken line hangs down but does not reach; the deep stream of Panxi is in vain for casting the hook. [The monk] asked: "What is the matter beyond the pool?
The Master said: "In the day, the golden crow crows; within the moon, the jade hare is startled."
A monk asked Zen Master Deng of Tiantai in Pengzhou, “Where has the ancient Buddha gone?
The Master said, “The central mansion is lofty; year after year it produces numinous sprouts. The monk asked, “How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished?
The Master said, “No effort is applied. The monk asked, “How is it after it has been polished? The Master said, “It does not illuminate. The monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Red.”
Upon the lotus seat, the celestial crown was not to be seen.
A monk asked Zen Master Soryong of Sinrae, successor to Zen Master Gusanjang: "When both black and white have perished and the Buddha-eye is opened, what is it like? The Master said:
[The student] said, "I fear you will remain within. He asked, "What is the Prince Born at Birth? The Master said, "He cannot be led out from the deep palace.
[The student] asked, "What is the Prince Born at Dawn? The Master said, "He does not take his place in the palace.
[The student] asked, "What is the Prince Born Last? The Master said, "In every place there is no fixed mark; he does not deploy the mechanism of the ten thousand men."
A monk asked National Teacher Baeryam of Silla, “What is Chan? The Master said, “An ancient tomb is not made into a home.

The monk asked, “What is the Way? The Master said, “Vainly exhausting the tracks of carriages and horses. The monk asked, “What are the Teachings? The Master said, “The palm leaves could never contain them all.”
A monk asked Zen Master Daeryong of Silla State, "The ancients said: 'Upon reaching Tongguan Pass, one simply stops.
One stops once one has understood; one stops before one has understood. The Master said, "It is simply because it is the livelihood within the path of delusion.
The monk asked, "Apart from the path of delusion, is there still a livelihood within that [state]? The Master said, "One may realize its essence, but one cannot abide in it. The monk said, "Since..."
"This is the realization of the essence. Why should it not be attained? The Master said, "The realization of the essence is a matter for what kind of person?
[The monk] asked, "What is the reality within it? The Master said, "It does not act as something noble. [The monk] asked, "How is it that all places are pure?"
The Master said: "When jade branches are severed, every inch is treasure; when sandalwood is split, every fragment is fragrant. A question was asked:
"How is it that there is no obstruction within activity? The Master said: "A single mass of white clouds flies about in disarray."
A monk asked Zen Master Chengjue Jing of Mount Yungai in Tanzhou, the Dharma heir of Zen Master Zhongyungei, "The land is at peace; to whom does the merit belong?"
The Master said, "Under the Silver Terrace Gate, congratulations are not extended. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when function is transformed and there is no fixed position?

The Master said, "The affairs of the royal house remain as they are. [The monk] asked, "What are the matters beyond the threshold? The Master said, "After the sound of the painted drum has ended, the general does not nod his head."
A monk asked Chan Master Shiyin of He Mountain in Jizhou, “When the Prince has not yet ascended the throne, who shall govern and transform the realm?
The Master said, “Within the inner palace, the orders of the frontier garrisons are not enforced; the General himself brings about the years of Great Peace.

The monk said, “If that is so, then the merit of governing and transforming is still not appropriate. The Master said, “There is indeed what is appropriate. The monk asked, “What is this appropriateness? The Master said, “Ten...”
The entire realm and its lands belonged entirely to the King. A questioner asked, "If one traces back to the source over a long period of time, why is it that one does not see it?

The Master said, "It is because the number of steps is too many. The questioner said, "In that case, one should not go seeking it at all. The Master said, "That would be the same as avoiding drowning only to throw oneself into fire.
A questioner asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "One who takes it upon themselves [to define him] is no adept."
A monk asked Chan Master Congshi of Zhaxi in Youzhou, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Within this, there is no purple or black.
The monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "It does not connect with the white clouds. The Master then asked a monk, "What have you come here to do?"
[The monk] said, "I have come to pay my respects. The Master said, "Though you may let the white clouds rise to the mountain peak, how can you expect the green mountains not to knit their brows?
Chan Master Yanbin of Mount Wuya in Qizhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Lupu An, was asked by a monk: "Before one has yet taken human form, what is one doing?"
[The Master] said: "A three-legged stone ox gallops upon the hill; a single branch of auspicious grass is distinguished before one's eyes. [A monk] asked:

"What is it like when a lone horse and a single spear charge straight in? The Master said: "Even if you were Xiong Xin, skilled at wielding the spear, you would still be a hundred paces behind King Qin.
[A monk] asked: "Having fought long on the battlefields, why is it that fame and merit have not been achieved? The Master said: "Two eagles follow..."
The arrow fell; Li Guang’s reputation was not in vain. Question: "Who is it that pierces the willow leaf at a hundred paces and hits the mark? The Master said:

"If the General had not mounted the Bridge of Convenience, his gold-tipped arrow would have been laboriously wasted on picking up the shaft. Question: "What is it like when the rainbow drinks from the roots of the clouds?
The Master said: "The Golden Wheel Emperor descends upon Jambudvīpa; atop the iron crown, the golden flower is extraordinary. [The student] said: "Precisely at such a time..."
"How is it now? The Master said, "Nowadays, one does not sit in the Hall of Spiritual Radiance; the painted drums have ceased their music, and the eight-rowed dance has ended.
Chan Master Chuanchu of Qingfeng in Fengxiang Prefecture was a native of Jingzhou. One day, Luopo asked him, "Where have you come from, Attendant?
The Master replied, "I have come from sweeping the snow. Luopo asked, "How deep is the snow? The Master replied, "The trees..."
This was the end of the exchange. Lupu said, "It is indeed so; you shall surely dwell in a snow cave hereafter. Later, he visited Baishui.
Baishui asked, "I have heard it said that Luopu has a 'path of vital energy' (shengji yilu). Is this true? The Master replied, "It is.
Baishui said, "Cease the path of life and come from the path of the familiar (shu). The Master said, "On the path of life, there are countless dead people; on the path of the familiar..."
“An alive person does not cling. Shuiluo said, “This is the bottom of Luopu; what about yours?
The Master said, “Not only Luopu, even Jia Shan could do nothing about it. Shuiluo said, “Why could Jia Shan do nothing about it? The Master said:
He did not perceive the single path of the life-force of the Way. After he had settled into his realization, a monk asked: "Before Buddha and Mara have appeared, where does one respond?
The Master said: "Listen, all you venerable elders, as I answer. The monk asked: "The Great Matter has already been clarified;

why then is it as if one has lost one's parents? The Master said: "Without the spring breeze, the flowers do not bloom; yet once the flowers have bloomed, the breeze blows them away. The monk asked: "How is it?"
"This is one color. The Master said, "There is not a single drop of water; the surging waves resemble silver mountains.

He asked, "What is the single phrase for the moment of action? The Master said, "Just bring it forth. [The student] said, "Please, Master, speak it. The Master said, "It pierces right through the skull."
He was unaware of pain or itching. [The student] asked, "What is the one phrase for a person of clear understanding? The Master said, "A swift horse does not move an inch;
a dull bird soars upward and leaves the path."

Chan Master Shanjing of Yong’an Monastery in the capital district of Jingzhao was the son of the Wang family of that commandery. His mother dreamed of a golden image and became pregnant upon awakening.
In his youth, the Master studied Confucian learning and became widely proficient in various doctrines. At the age of twenty-seven, he suddenly grew weary of the world’s floating illusions.

He went in secret to Mount Zhongnan to attend upon Chan Master Guangdu and shave his head. During the Tianfu era of the Tang dynasty, he traveled south to visit Lopu, who recognized his potential and permitted him to enter the inner quarters of the lineage.
He was subsequently appointed to oversee the garden duties and diligently managed the affairs of the community. One day, a monk took his leave of Lopu.
Lopu asked, "The mountains surround you on all four sides; where will you go, O *dārala*? The monk was unable to answer. Lopu said, "The limit..."
"You have spoken well for ten days; I shall now follow you. That monk then practiced walking meditation (caṅkrama) and searched in the dark until he happened to enter the garden.
The Master asked him, "Venerable sir, since you were about to depart, why are you here now? The monk explained the reason in detail and earnestly requested that the Master speak on his behalf.
The Master said, "How can dense bamboo obstruct the flow of water? How can a high mountain hinder the flight of wild clouds? His words were thus.

The monk was filled with joy and leaped up. The Master instructed him, saying, "You must not say these words were spoken by such-and-such a person. The monk then reported this to Baofu, asking, "Who said that?
[The monk replied,] "Such-and-such a person said it. Baofu said, "That was not your words. The monk explained in detail how the gardener had instructed him. That evening, Baofu arrived...
Ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Do not underestimate Yuantou; one day there will be five hundred people in his seat.

Later, when he resided at Yongan, his followers numbered over five hundred, which indeed accorded with Lupu’s prediction. A monk asked, "When one knows that there is [the Way] but cannot attain it, what then?
The Master said, "What is there to know? The monk said, "It cannot be that there is nothing. The Master said, "If that is so," [then...]

[The monk] said, "I have attained accord with the Way. The Master said, "The Way is indeed not non-existent; however, your words are biased. The Master continued, "When the water freezes, the fish find it hard to leap;

when the mountains are cold, the flowers bloom late. [The monk] asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "A wooden horse bears the slanting sun; entering the grass, there is no trace. [The monk] asked, "What is 'one color'?
The Master said, "It is easy to distinguish flour from snow, but difficult to discern ink [from black]."
Zhongmei asked, "What is the matter that lies beyond the patched robe? The Master said, "The dragon-fish does not leave the sea;
the moon in the water does not swallow the light. He asked, "When it cannot be known by wisdom and cannot be recognized by consciousness, what then?
The Master said, "The crane and the egret stand side-by-side, sleeping in the snow; startled by the bright moon, both hesitate. He asked, "Before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch..."
"How is it at that time? The Master said, "The numinous pine in its extraordinary setting is envied by all who behold it. [The student] asked, "What is it like after seeing it?

The Master said, "The leaves have fallen and the branches are broken; when the wind comes, it finds no melody. [The student] asked, "How does one give birth to the family of the Tathāgata? The Master said:

Wearing his robe and gazing toward the dawn, he remarked, "For kalpas it has been unclear. He asked, "What is it like after the light appears? The Master said, "Not even a single phrase can be grasped.
He asked, "What is it like not sitting upon the Tathāgata’s seat? The Master said, "The stone maiden returns late, clutching her head;

there is no trace left within the Jeta Grove assembly. The Master went to wander the [Shu] region to avoid the chaos of Emperor Zhaozong’s flight from the capital, during the Kaihan era of the Later Han.

In the winter of the Bingwu year, he struck the *khandi* gong to assemble the monks; after entrusting his final instructions, he entered the abbot’s quarters, turned toward the east, and passed away on his right side.
He was posthumously titled Chan Master Jingwu.
A monk asked Chan Master Zhudu of Dengzhou, "If one does not encounter the Master within the seas, who is the sovereign within the realm?
The Master said, "The golden rooster always announces the dawn; it is only that people themselves do not hear it. The monk asked, "What is the bright mirror in the darkness?
The Master said, "It cannot be obscured. The monk asked, "I wonder what it illuminates? The Master said, "What thing would it not illuminate? The monk asked, "How..."
"In the ground of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi), not a single speck of dust is accepted; within the gate of Buddha-activity, not a single dharma is abandoned.

The Master said, "In the true and eternal, dust does not stain; the ocean receives the flow of a hundred rivers. [The student] said, "I request the Master to answer from beyond sound and form. The Master said:
A wooden man constantly engages in dialogue; though he possesses a nature, he cannot speak.
When Chan Master Jiading of Dongxi in Jiazhou first questioned Luopu: "The moon-tree has no branches, yet it provides long-lasting shade.

I pray that you, Master, will directly point to the subtle mystery. Luopu said: "In the place where the myriad phenomena flourish, things do not rely upon one another; the clear waters form a thousand waves."
"A solitary peak stands apart by itself. At this, the Master grasped the essential meaning. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "Master, why was the snake charmer swallowed by the snake?
The Master said, "How many times did he knock at the gate before being invited out? He simply thrust his body straight inside to look.
An official asked, "Since this is a pure monastery, why do you beat the fish-drum? The Master said, "One must strike it right through to the blue heavens."
[The Master] said: "Outside [the gate], one avoids seeing those who were marked on the forehead at Longmen.

A monk asked Zen Master Wo-long of Jingzhao Prefecture: "The brilliant sun accords with the celestial expanse; the pearl-light shines upon the old capital. The ferry crossing connects to the Dharma-ocean;
what is your intention today? The Master said: "When the precious sword is brandished, how could it be encompassed by light or darkness?"
Chan Master Tongxuan Shiwei of Fucing Yuan in Quanzhou, successor to Chan Master Xiaoyao Zhong. A monk asked: "The branches spread across the ridges; you truly inherit the lineage of Xiaoyao.
Now that you have ascended the precious throne, we pray you will sound the Dharma-thunder. The Master said: "Xiaoyao dwells far beyond all things; beyond things, the rosy clouds do not reach."
Sheng asked, "What is the true intent of the one who came from the West? The Master said, "Standing in the snow was not yet the toil; severing the arm was finally the point.
Sheng said, "If that is so, then 'one flower opens five petals, its fragrance reaching down to this very day.
The Master said, "When the causes are perfected beyond the three realms, the fruits are fully known throughout the ten directions."
Chan Master Baiyun Wuxiu of Jingzhao Prefecture was asked by a monk, "When one encounters a fierce tiger on the road, how does one subdue it?
The Master said, "Take refuge in the Buddha and the Dharma. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Baiyun? The Master said, "The sea traveler’s sorrow beside the tower under the moonlit night."
Chan Master Jingwu of Yong’an on Mount Lu, successor to Chan Master Panlong Wen, was asked by a monk: “What is the matter of leaving home? The Master said:
“To let go completely at a ten-thousand-fathom precipice. The monk asked: “What is the matter of not leaving home? The Master said: “Utterly distinct from the snow.”
[The Master] was nesting on a ridge. This was unlike Xu You hanging up his single gourd. A questioner asked: "When the six gates are blocked, how does one convey the message?
The Master said: "With whom do you, O *Ācārya*, associate outside? Question: "When one sheds the head-cage and unloads the shoulder-load, what then?
The Master said: "Changing bones and washing the entrails to enter the Purple Pass; at Yanmen, one must strictly avoid picking up reeds again. Question: "From the time of the ancestors..."

"What do the various sages show people? The Master said, "There is a unique patriarchal method of transformation that transcends the dragon’s flight; it soars beyond the phoenix’s roost and leaves the dust behind.
[The student] asked, "What is one who knows how to act as a guest? The Master said, "Even precious carriages and rare finery are cast aside."
"Who could, throughout kalpas, stand at another's door? Question: "What is the meaning of the Westward Coming? The Master said: "The mud ox roars from the bottom of the sea;
the wooden horse neighs amidst the clouds. Question: "When many hands sift for gold, who is it that obtains it? The Master said: "The Yellow Emperor never traveled to the Red Water;
the divine pearl was found by the *wangxiang*, yet remains utterly void. Question: "When the snow covers the reeds, what then? The Master—
It is said: "Though the frozen ice may manifest auspicious colors, once the great sun shines forth, it leaves people bewildered.
When Chan Master Shandao of Mount Muping in Yuanzhou first visited Luopo, he asked: "Before a single bubble has even arisen..."
"How does one discern the course of the water? Pu said, "Shift the boat to familiarize yourself with the current; raise the oars to distinguish the waves.
The Master did not attain realization and went to consult Panlong. He asked the same question as before. Long said, "Shifting the boat does not change the water;
raising the oars immediately confuses the source. From this, the Master attained awakening. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The head of a stone ram."
[The Master] looked toward the east. [A monk] asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master said, "The hole in the staff.
He asked, "What is the Immovable Honored One? The Master said, "Wandering aimlessly. He asked, "What is the single phrase of Muping? The Master said, "It fills the void.
[The monk] said, "I do not ask about filling the void; what is the single phrase? The Master then struck him. Whenever there was...
When a newcomer arrived, he was not permitted to pay his respects immediately; instead, he was first ordered to carry three loads of earth. Then, a verse was shown to him:
"The Southern Mountain path slopes toward the low Eastern Mountain; Newcomer, do not decline these three turns of mud. Alas, you have traveled this road for many days;

Though it is clear before your eyes, you remain ignorant and thus lost. The Master’s crown protrusion (uṣṇīṣa) bore spiral curls. Li of Jinling, hearing of his reputation, invited him to serve as an offering.
[He] raised [him] and treated him with the etiquette due to a teacher. [Fayan] once asked, "What is Muping? The Master said, "No need for the axe.
[Fayan] asked, "Why no need for the axe? The Master said, "Muping. Chan Master Fayan composed a verse in his praise:
The man from Mount Muping, Ancient in appearance and sparse in speech; We meet as strangers on the road, Yet our hearts are as bright as the autumn moon. Tattered robes...
The thread was not from a silkworm; there is a bird that assists the song. The city gates come today; a single bubble has already been understood.
After his passing, his disciples built a stupa for him, and he was posthumously titled Chan Master Zhenji.
Chan Master Chongfu Zhi was asked by a monk: "It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making offerings to a single mindless man of the Way.
I wonder what fault the Buddhas have, and what virtue the mindless man of the Way possesses? The Master said: "When the snow is deep, one should stay near the fire;
when the body is warm, one perceives spring as slow. The monk asked: "What is it like when a poor man offers a pearl? The Master said: "What?"
[He] arrived at the dwelling. [A monk] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "There is a portion for turning back the carriage.
Chan Master Longxi of Shanfu ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the seamless stupa?
The Master said, "The adornment of a hundred jewels is now complete; how long have the four gates been wide open? The Master then said, "Even if you were to explain it like this..."
"Even a seamless stupa cannot avoid the old monk driving in his stake. How can you avoid it? No one in the assembly could respond.
The Master said, "Go down."

Chan Master Tongquan (or Tōngquan) of Tǒngzhou was a successor of Chan Master Lún of Huángshān. He went to visit Huángshān, who asked, "The Gate of Heaven is closed; in the ten directions there is no path.
If someone can speak, they may wave their hand and leave through the Zhang River. The Master said, "The hibernation chamber does not open; the dragon has no dragon."
[The Master] spoke this phrase. Mount [Shan] said, "Is it as you say? The Master said, "If it is, speak directly that it is; if it is not, speak directly that it is not.
Mount [Shan] said, "Waving his hand, he departs through the Zhang River. Mount [Shan] asked again, "When it is said, 'Wherever Bian He goes, the Jingshan is magnificent;
the jade seal is passed on by the Son of Heaven,' what then? The Master said, "The divine crane does not rest beneath the forest trees; the village elder does not..."
During the Taiping era, Shanshen approved of him. After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "What is the matter that has been transmitted?

The Master said, "The dragon spits forth water of eternal life; the fish swallow endless bubbles. The monk said, "Please, Master, explain this further. The Master said, "Beating the drum, they turn the prow of the boat;
the oars pierce the moon within the waves."
A monk asked Zen Master Wenshu of Tanzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Shao Shan Pu, "What is the matter before Mount Zhurong? The Master said, "Auspicious grass grows before the cliff.
The monk asked, "When a Benevolent King ascends the throne, the myriad people receive his grace. Now that you, Reverend, have appeared in the world, what auspicious signs are there?"
The Master said, "Ten thousand miles to Changsha, one boards an iron boat. [The student] asked, "What is this fundamental adornment?
The Master said, "The scene upon the chrysanthemum fields; the traveler's path is long."
A monk asked Chan Master Miyō of Yaoshou, "I beg the Master to grant an instruction regarding the words spoken in the secret chamber. The Master said, "The waters are broad in the south;
the winds are many in the north. The monk said, "I do not understand. I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said, "It is easy for a bird to roost at the foot of a forest."
It is difficult for people to avoid the pitfalls of right and wrong.
Once, while Master Shanben of Jialing Peak in Xiangzhou—a Dharma successor of Chan Master Siming—was bathing, a monk asked him: "The Master is a person free from defilement; why [is this so]?"
He bathed, and the Master said, "The water of concentration is full and serene; here one bathes this stainless person. A question was asked:

"Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master replied, "On the peak of Vulture Mountain, green grass reaches the heavens; in the Deer Park, foxes and rabbits cross paths."

The Dharma heir of Chan Master Tengxia of the seventh generation under Qingyuan, Chan Master Yaoshan of Lidezhou, ascended the hall and said: "Now, a Bodhisattva who studies Prajñā has no fear of gain or loss. There is a matter..."

[The monk] approached. At that time, a monk asked, "You are a descendant of the ancestral lineage of Yaoshan; we request the Master to proclaim its essence. The Master said, "Ten thousand functions cannot pick it out.
The monk asked, "Why can ten thousand functions not pick it out? The Master said, "Its conditions are the riverbanks and valleys.
The monk asked, "What is the house style of Yaoshan? The Master said, "Falling leaves are not as they were at first. The monk asked, "When the Dharma-thunder roars, what then? The Master—
[The student] asked, "The universe has never thundered. [The student] asked, "Why has it never thundered? The Master said, "Throughout the entire Sahā world, there has never been a roar.
[The student] asked, "What is this matter of not roaring? The Master said, "No one in the whole country knows."

A monk asked Master Zang of Nantai Temple on Mount Heng, successor to Chan Master Yungai Jing: "From afar I have come to seek the Teacher; I pray that the Teacher will grant me an audience. The Master said:
[The Master] did not open the door. [The monk] asked, "What is the realm of Nantai? The Master said, "When the pine tones sweep by, the rocks remain unstained;
beneath the solitary peak, the mounds are difficult to align. [The monk] asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Wild fruits are planted before the cliff."
A guest who had come and gone said, "In that case, I thank you for your hospitality. The Master asked, "What is its flavor?
Another asked, "What is the Dharma Hall? The Master replied, "It has no walls. Another asked, "What is it like when one disregards all conditions? The Master remained silent for a long time.
A monk asked Chan Master Zhengjue of Yungai Mountain in Tanzhou, “What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, “The four seas have never been traversed. The monk asked, “How is it that a single speck of dust contains the Dharma-realm? The Master said, “The entire body is not round.

The monk asked, “How is it that nine generations are distinguished within a single kṣaṇa? The Master said, “Amidst profuse activity, no colors are displayed. The monk asked, “What is...? (The question is left incomplete.)
This is the true meaning of the Zen school. The Master said: "A monk from the Western Regions ten thousand *li* away does not enter the waves.
Chan Master Bing of Wuya was a successor of Chan Master Xinggu of Mount Dajian in Anzhou. A monk asked: "When a deceased monk undergoes transformation, where does he go?"
The Master said, "Last night at the third watch, I performed the ritual at the Southern Suburb. [The monk] asked, "Vimalakīrti remained silent; what was the meaning of this?
The Master said, "A dark, black stone ox, transcendentally never leaving its door. [The monk] asked, "What is that matter over there? The Master said:
The lacquered-black cowherd boy does not extend his hand; beside the silver cage, wild clouds fly past the cranes.
A monk asked Chan Master Xinglang of Mount Wuya in Qizhou, "Before one has yet taken human form, what was one doing?
The Master said, "The stone ox on the sea sings three beats; a single red thread is divided within the palm. [The monk] asked, "Kāśyapa..."

[The Master] was wearing an upper robe (*ūrdhvaka-vastra*). A monk asked, "Who is it that is fit to wear this? The Master said: "The natural child of formlessness does not don the robe that transcends the mundane.
A monk asked West China’s Chan Master Lingkan, a successor of Chan Master Qingfeng, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Master said: "The place of emergence."

"It is not the Buddha's doing; when spring comes, the grass turns green of itself. A monk asked, "What is it like when one is in a state of mere mundanity? The Master said, "Try taking a step forward and see.
A monk asked Zen Master Duanji of Mount Zigai in Jingzhao Prefecture, "When the four marks have all been exhausted, what do you establish as [the truth]?"
"True. The Master said, "Where have you come from? He asked, "What is it like when the waters of the Wei River flow due east? The Master said, "From the beginning, there has been no interruption."
A monk asked Chan Master Huazhou Kaishan Huazhou: "What practice must one perform to not contradict the thousand sages? The Master said: "Sublime conduct is peerless;

when the mind is profound, the essence is naturally distinct. The monk asked: "With ears but not approaching clear water to wash, who is it that dwells in the seclusion of white clouds when there is no mind?
What is it like then? The Master said: "No tree to hang a thousand pieces of gold. The monk said: "It hangs [there]."
"What is it like afterward? The Master said, "Profound and vast; it is difficult for people to discern. A question was asked: "What is a master amidst the dust?

The Master said, "Reaching everywhere within the thicket of brambles; moving freely and at will within the grove of sandalwood. A question was asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The moon is hidden in the clear pool; the golden light shines at midday."
A monk asked the Chan Master Chuanfa of Youzhou, "Are the meaning of the Teachings and the meaning of the Patriarchs the same or different?
The Master said, "The golden threads bloom in splendor; the ancient cavern is deep with white clouds. The monk asked, "Why do others have many disciples, while you have none?
The Master said, "Dragons hide in abundance on the islands; phoenixes do not perch upon thatched huts."
A monk asked Chan Master Guixin of Jingzhong Monastery in Yizhou, "How is it when the lotus has not yet emerged from the water?
The Master said, "The buds fill the pond. The monk asked, "How is it after it has emerged? The Master said, "The leaves fall, and one does not know autumn. [The monk] asked again.
"How is it when one ascends the great ocean without relying on an inflatable life-raft? The Master said, "The red-beaked bird flies beyond the three realms;
even the green-haired beast knows how to brew tea. A monk asked, "What is a person who possesses mastery?
The Master said, "He goes straight away through sword-trees and frosty forests. The monk asked, "What is a person who lacks mastery? The Master said, "Śākyamuni is in you, O *ācārya*."
Later, a monk asked Zen Master Qingmian of Mount Qingfeng, "The grape wine has been aged for a long time; for whom is it opened today?
The Master said, "Only the drinker knows. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "There is not a single drop in Lake Anavatapta."
Drop! The four seas flow on naturally.
One day during the Song dynasty, Emperor Taizong of the Song, while visiting Xiangguo Monastery, saw a monk reading a sutra and asked him, "What is this?"

The Emperor said, "Which sutra? The monk replied, "The *Renwang Jing* (Benevolent Kings Sutra). The Emperor said, "Since this is my own sutra, why is it in your hands? The monk was speechless. (Xuedou spoke on his behalf:
"Heaven has no partiality; it aids only virtue. By chance, the precious stupa was opened. The Emperor asked the monk, "Who are you? He replied, "I am the stupa master.
The Emperor said, "Why do you act as the master of my stupa? The monk was speechless. (Xuedou spoke on his behalf: "The entire nation...")
[Everyone] knew [this]. One day, during an audience with the monks, the Emperor asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Sleeping Clouds Hermitage on Mount Lu.

The Emperor said, "I have heard that where the clouds sleep deeply, one does not face the court. Why have you come here? The monk had no reply. (Xuedou spoke on his behalf: "It is difficult to escape the ultimate transformation.
After the monk entered for his next audience, he reported, "Does Your Majesty still remember? The Emperor said, "Where did we meet?"
The monk addressed the Emperor, saying, "Since our parting at Vulture Peak until this very day. The Emperor asked, "What proof do you have? The monk had no reply. (Xuedou spoke on his behalf:

"This poor monk has come specifically for this purpose. The capital temples had been consumed by fire, and the Tripitaka scriptures were completely reduced to ashes. The monk wished to request that they be granted from the imperial storehouses.
The Emperor summoned him and questioned him: "In the past, Mokṣala was not burned; why is he burned now? The monk had no reply. (Xuedou spoke on his behalf:

"Your Majesty has not forgotten the entrustment. The Emperor once dreamed that a divine being informed him, saying: "I request Your Majesty to give rise to the Bodhicitta. Consequently, at the early court audience, he proclaimed and questioned those in attendance:
"How does one give rise to the Bodhicitta? No one in the court had a reply. (Xuedou spoke on their behalf: "Truly, this is rarely heard in ancient or modern times. Zhi.
When Master Ji presented the "Diagram of the Three Realms," the Emperor asked, "In which realm do I reside? Ji had no reply. (Baoning Yong offered this on his behalf:

"Your Majesty, where would you not be honored as the Sovereign? One day, after the court session had ended, the Emperor held up his bowl and asked Chancellor Wang Sui, "Since it was something that could not be lifted at the head of Dayu Ridge, why is it now in my hands? Sui had no reply.
In the third year of the Zhenghe era of Emperor Huizong, the patrol officer of Jiazhou submitted a report stating:

"Along the roadside in our district, there was a great ancient tree that had been broken by the wind. Within it sat a monk in meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), his beard and hair covering his body and his fingernails encircling him."

The Emperor issued an edict ordering that he be carried into the capital by palanquin. He commanded the Tripitaka Master Dharmatāla of the Western Heaven to rouse him from his samādhi using a golden gong.
Upon emerging, the Master was asked, "In which era did you live? He replied, "I am Huichi, the younger brother of Dharma Master Huiyuan of Donglin.
While traveling to Mount Emei, I entered samādhi beneath this tree. Is Dharma Master Huiyuan still well? The Tripitaka Master said, "Dharma Master Huiyuan was a man of the Jin dynasty."
Seven hundred years have passed since he passed away. Daochi remained silent and did not speak again. Daocang asked, "Since you have arrived here, Master, where do you wish to go?

Daochi replied, "Chenliu County. He then entered meditative concentration once more. The Emperor composed three verses and ordered that an image be painted for distribution. The verses read: [Verse 1] [Verse 2] [Verse 3]

For seven hundred years, this ancient master—within his state of meditative concentration, who could know his message? How can it compare to departing westward with a single shoe; what need is there to labor over life and death like wood encased in bark?
To hide a mountain in a marsh is also to hide one’s own person; when there is no place in the world to hide, the Way becomes accessible.
Send word to Zhuang Zhou: do not attempt to deliberate upon this; within the tree is not the man carrying a burden. [The body of] sentient beings is not...
This is insentient. Each and every person is the body within samādhi. If you can realize that Bodhi originally has no tree, there is no need for the arduous toil of questioning Lu Neng.
Emperor Xiaozong summoned Chan Master Lingyin Fozhao Guang and questioned him, saying: "Śākyamuni Buddha entered the mountains to practice..."
"The Way takes six years to achieve. What is it that is achieved? I beg the Master to explain this clearly. He replied, "I thought Your Majesty had forgotten;
you have not yet understood the matter of the Dharma-heir."

The Great Master Shixing was visited by his fellow practitioner, Chan Master Rongxun. Upon ascending the hall, he took the staff in his right hand, leaned it against his left side, and after a long silence, said:
"If this matter were not with my elder brother, Master Rongxun, it would be truly difficult to fully comprehend.
He then descended from the seat.
The Chan Master Yushan of Chaling had never traveled as a wandering monk. Once, when a transformation-monk arrived from Mount Lu, they discussed matters concerning the Zen school.
The visitor instructed him to contemplate the question: "When one is atop a hundred-foot pole, how does one take a further step? Fandeng replied, "Agh! (O!).
For three years he practiced in this manner. One day, while riding a donkey across a bridge, he stepped upon a plank and fell;
at that moment, he suddenly attained great enlightenment. He then composed a verse: "I possess a divine pearl, Long locked away by the dust of worldly toil.

Today, the dust is cleared and its light shines forth, Illuminating ten thousand peaks of mountains and rivers. From then on, he no longer traveled to seek teachers elsewhere. This master was the Venerable Baiyun Yuan.

Upon attaining the realization of his Master, Yun wrote a verse of praise: "Having advanced further from the top of a hundred-foot pole, A single step upon the mountain stream bridge submerges mountains and rivers.
From this moment forth, he shall not emerge from the banks of the Tea River; His chanting and laughter are nothing other than *ra-li-ra*."

Dharma Master Sengzhao encountered the persecution of the Qin Emperor. As he was about to undergo execution, he spoke this verse: "The four elements originally have no master; The five aggregates are fundamentally empty.
To bring my head before the white blade Is like cutting the spring breeze. Xuansha said, "How great was Dharma Master Zhao! Even at the moment of death, he was still speaking in his sleep."
The Chan Master Guanhui of Chan-yue composed a poem that says: "When Chan practitioners meet, they merely snap their fingers;
How many people can truly know this mind? Master Daisui raised this and asked, "What is this mind? The Master had no reply. (Gui-zong Rou offered on his behalf:
"How many people can truly know it?")
Formerly, Chan Master Jingzhao asked Master Lengyan: "The sutra says, 'If one can turn things over, one is identical to the Tathāgata;
if one is turned by things, one is called an ordinary person. Now, regarding the Shengyuan Tower, how would you turn it?
Lengyan had no reply. (Fenyang spoke on his behalf: "Both are already old.")
Master Gōngqī was on his way to Luóhàn when he encountered a young gentleman riding an ox.
The Master asked, "Which way does the road to Luóhàn go? The gentleman patted the ox and said, "Speak! Speak! The Master shouted, "This beast!
The gentleman replied, "Which way does the road to Luóhàn go? The Master then patted the ox and said, "Speak! Speak! The gentleman said, "Even if it were as you say..."
There were still some hooves and horns remaining. The Master struck him, whereupon the official slapped the ox and ran away.

During his youth, Chan Master Yinci of the Tang Dynasty was once carrying a mallet to strike at the earth when he saw a large clod of soil. He playfully struck it violently with the mallet, and it shattered;

at that moment, he attained great enlightenment (later, an elder heard of this and said: "The entirety of the mountains, rivers, and the great earth has been reduced to a hundred fragments by a single blow from Chan Master Yinci").

Chan Master Yung-ching of Mount Tung-shan in Fu-chou was a native of Ch’üan-chou (his clan name is lost). Having failed the imperial examinations for a second time, he went to Yun-t’ai Ta-hou Temple to shave his head and receive full ordination.
He then visited Ta-yu, Chih-shen, and T’ien-ying. Later, upon meeting an eminent elder under the lineage of the Arhats, he finally attained thorough realization of his own nature.
His reputation for the study of the Way spread throughout the monastic community, and he was known as "Ching San-chiao" (the Three Teachings of the Peak). A monk asked:
"What is the Master’s daily activity? The Master said, "I eat; you suffer from hunger. [The monk] asked, "Since every dharma does not reach another, what then?
The Master said, "When you commit a transgression, I know it all. [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s single fly-whisk?
The Master said, "It shatters the den of spiritual cultivation. [The monk] said, "In that case, there is originally not a single thing."
The Master said, "Who is it that knows there is nothing? [The layman] said, "It is the student’s fault. The Master said, "It would have been better to reflect on this further.
The Layman asked about Dongshan’s saying: "There is a thing that reaches up to heaven and down to earth; I wonder what kind of thing it is?
The Master said, "Carrying an iron rack, eating an iron staff. [The Layman] said, "Heaven and earth turn black; mountains and rivers flee. The Master said, "Before the Hall of Lord Yan."
"Add one ghost; it lies beneath Mount Beimang for a thousand years. A scholar cried out, "How joyful! How joyful! The Master said, "This too is a wild fox swallowing a mouse.
A Daoist from Jiulong Guan and three scholars requested that he ascend the hall. [The Master said:

"In the Confucian gate, they draw the Eight Trigrams and compose contracts, yet they do not save beings from the cycle of the six realms. In the Daoist gate, they pay homage to the Nine Sovereigns and refine the true qi, yet..."

He has mastered the calculations of the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas*. Our Śākyamuni World-Honored One penetrates the calculations of the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* and rescues those transmigrating through the six realms of existence.

With great vows, he gathers in humans and devas, like the wind-circle supporting the sun and moon; with great wisdom, he shatters birth and death, as if the kalpa-fire were consuming the finest autumn hair.
Those who enter my gate will naturally transform heaven and earth and perceive ghosts and spirits in their hidden depths, enabling them to...
Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, the great earth, and the vast oceans enter into a single pore; yet all sentient beings neither perceive nor know this.
I preach this Dharma-gate as being like space, which contains all myriad phenomena: the one becomes the infinite, and the infinite becomes the one.
If a person attains the one, then all matters are completed. Take heed!
Chan Master Chongyun of Yunyou in Wuzhou (now known as Fayun) first visited Xuefeng and subsequently relied upon Shishuang, whereupon he attained awakening.
He returned to his hometown to live in seclusion, covering his body with nothing but a single robe. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and said:
"A single arrow from Yunyou—empty space has no front or back; shot forth throughout the ten directions, yet for all intents and purposes, no one sees it. At that time, a monk asked: "How is it?"
"This is the Master’s single arrow. The Master said, "Throughout the entire world, there are no skulls.
Regarding the Chan Master Shuangxi Bunuo, Chan Master Song composed a poem in jest to mourn him, saying: "In my generation, you were the one to succeed the Patriarch;

Your life's conditions and conduct were worthy of emulation. Throughout your life, you remained ever on the Path; Recognizing your own ailment, you were too indolent to seek a physician. Your appearance was ancient... [The text continues with the description of his calligraphy.]
Difficult to write! His spirit was so lofty that no one in the world knew it. Where shall the compassionate clouds spread? The solitary moon is naturally suited to him alone.
After the master finished reading, he took up his brush and replied: "Who else has a spiritual affinity with me for my entire life? Only you, Xianqing, truly know my heart.

Had I not intended to part from you at first, I feared I might have missed composing this poem for my fellow practitioner. He then threw down his brush and passed away while sitting, at the age of sixty.
Later, the door of the stupa opened of its own accord, and his true countenance remained solemn and majestic.
Chan Master Tong of Touzi in Shuzhou was asked by a monk: "What was it like before Bodhidharma had come? The Master said: "On both banks, fishermen sing their songs.
The monk asked: "What was it like after he came? The Master said: "The great ocean surges with wind and waves. The monk asked: "What is the solitary [peak]?"
[The Master pointed to] the tall pines of steadfast character atop the mountain peak. The Master said, "Capable of being the lord of all phenomena, they do not wither according to the four seasons.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma here at your monastery? The Master said, "The wall on the east strikes the wall on the west."
Chan Master Fahai Li of Chuzhou was ordered by the imperial court to convert his monastery into a Shenxiao Palace.
The Master ascended the seat and addressed the assembly, saying: "It is precisely because one has not yet attained thorough penetration that one speaks of right and wrong;

it is because one lacks true realization that one distinguishes between 'that' and 'this. If even my own body does not exist, what need is there to speak of anything external to the body? View this with the correct eye."

Come! A scene of shared laughter. Now that the Sage Ruler has issued his decree, turning monasteries into temples of the Shenxiao [God of the Blue Heaven], it is like adding a crown to the Buddha’s head.
Calculating it, what could be wrong with this? Today, this mountain monk cannot help but slung my staff across my shoulder.
Hanging his alms-bag high, he establishes his dwelling within the seamless stupa; beneath the rootless tree, he whistles at the moon and chants with the wind.
He leaves it to those immortal guests who ride the clouds and lofty recluses who drive their cranes to come here to incantate water, write talismans, and perform rites by clenching their teeth.
In years to come, when he attains the Way and ascends on a white cloud during the day, he will be able to repay the unrequitable debt of gratitude and assist in the state of non-action.
"This transformation—fear only that it may not be jade; if it is jade, how marvelous! Yet, even so, tell me:
how shall this mountain monk express his turning-about phrase? Do you understand? Having said this, he cast down his whisk and immediately passed into stillness.
The Prefect submitted a memorial regarding these matters. By imperial decree, the temple was renamed Zhenshen (True Body).

On the day the Zen Master Ming of Tianning in Ruzhou changed his status from a lay devotee (*deśi*) to a monk, the Master ascended the seat; after concluding his expression of gratitude for the imperial favor, he said:
"The wooden tally is grasped at hand as it comes; The sitting cloth is laid down when the time is right. Clouds disperse and waters flow away; Heaven and earth are silent and still."
"Empty! he said, then closed his eyes and passed away.
Later, a monk asked Chan Master Renwang Qin of Shu, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "Hearing the name is not as good as seeing the face.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "A monkey performing in a bustling marketplace. The monk asked, "What about..."
"What is this Way? He replied, "A tiger looking at a water mill.
[The name of] the Abbot of Iron Chain Mountain in Jinling (his name has been lost) was asked by a monk: "I have long heard of the Iron Chain; I wonder what its true face is like?"
The Master pointed to a pillar. A monk said, "Thank you for showing me. The Master asked, "On what basis do you speak thus?
The monk then struck the pillar. The Master said, "Now tell me, where does the search lie? The monk made a gesture of measuring the space. The Master said, "..."
Today I have met a fellow practitioner.
As for Master Louzi, it is unknown where he was from, and his name and lineage have not been passed down.

One day, while wandering through the streets and markets, as he was adjusting his socks and sash beneath a wine tower, he heard someone on the upper floor singing a song that went: "Since you have no..."
"Mind! I am finished. Suddenly he attained great enlightenment and was thus named Louzi (The Tower Master).
Once, when the Dharma Master Shenzhao Benru requested instruction on the *Sūtra King* from the Venerable Ziming, the Master [Ziming] cried out in a thunderous voice:
"Your name is Benru (Original Suchness). The Master immediately attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "At every turn I encounter the path home; At every point I reach my native land.
This matter has been manifest from the very beginning; Why wait for deliberation?"
The Dharma Master Yuanzhi Zhengwu of Shangzhushan in Lin’an was the son of the Lin family of Tāizhōu.

He relied upon the Dharma Master Xiān of the White Lotus Society and inquired about the Way of the Total Transformation. Xiān pointed to a walking lamp and said: "A lamp such as this is devoid of intrinsic nature and transcends all negation."

Fundamentally empty and quiescent, the principle is complete therein. Yet, among the six classes of ordinary beings and the four types of noble ones, their perceptions differ; thus, transformation is present.

The Master did not attain realization at first, but later, while sweeping the floor and reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*, he reached the passage: "Know that dharmas are eternally without nature; the seeds of Buddhahood arise from conditions.
Only then did he understand the essential meaning. He informed Huìlián, who approved. Since the Master had led his disciples, he had long been troubled by the learning of his own school.
These people were confined by names and forms and bound by written records; they even regarded the transmission of the Tiantai school as merely a study of texts.
The Southern School held them in contempt, so he went to pay his respects to Master Ciyun Yuan of Huguo.

During a conversation at night, the Master cited the verse by Su Dongpo on staying at Donglin Temple and remarked, "It is not easy to reach such a state. Ciyun replied, "I have not yet seen the path."

"What do you mean by 'arriving'? he asked. The Master replied, "It is just as they say: 'The sound of the brook is itself the broad and long tongue; the color of the mountains—is it not the pure body?
If one has not reached this state, how could there be such a message? The hermit said, "That is merely the talk of a man outside the gate.
The Master said, "If you will not begrudge me, please explain it for me. The hermit said, "Then simply from right here, exert yourself with fierce intensity..."
He watched intently to catch him in the act. If he could catch him in his vulnerability, he would also know where his own *mūlādhāra* (the root source of life) was located.
The Master did not sleep the entire night. At dawn, when the bell rang, he removed his secret concealments and spoke another verse, saying:

"Master Dongpo is far too talkative; he wishes to pass through the barrier of sound and form. If the stream were sound and the mountain were form, then without mountain or water, one would be a person of great sorrow. He specifically told this hermitage master (Cian), who said, "I told you before that you are a man from outside the gate. The Master bowed in thanks. Not long after, there was one who was soliciting contributions to repair the roof tiles of Mazu’s Hall and requested a verse to promote the endeavor. The Master wrote: The Master of Dongpo is far too talkative; He wishes to pass through the barrier of sound and form. If the stream were sound and the mountain were form, Then without mountain or water, one would be a person of great sorrow. He specifically told this hermitage master, who said, "I told you before that you are a man from outside the gate. The Master bowed in thanks.
