“I beg the Master for a skillful means regarding the matter right here and now. The Master said, “Were it not for your question, I would not have spoken either.
[The student] asked, “What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, “No one is idle during the day.”
Chan Master Conggan Chaozheng of the Lianhua Yongfu Monastery in Fuzhou was asked by a monk: "In the Confucian gate, the Five Constant Virtues are taken as the ultimate standard.
I wonder, in the Gate of the Patriarchs, what is taken as the ultimate standard? The Master remained silent for a long while. The monk said, "If that is so, then students will act with haste.
The Master said, "A staff would be well-suited for you. Another asked: "The scriptures say, 'There is only the One Vehicle Dharma.'"
"What is the Dharma of the One Vehicle? The Master said, "Tell me, what am I doing here?
[The monk] said, "In that case, you do not understand the meaning of the teaching. The Master said, "Even so, I have not let you down.

[Another monk] asked, "If one does not grasp it from the point of the question, that is still the student’s point of questioning. How about you, Master? The Master said, "Go drink tea. He ascended the hall for formal instruction.
Changqing said, "When the law is exhausted, there are no subjects. Yongfu said, "That is not so. If the law were not exhausted, how could one possibly have subjects?
At that time, a monk said, "I ask the Master to exhaust the law. The Master said, "I do not want you to pay your taxes. The monk asked, "I shall not ask about other matters;

I simply beg the Master to show compassion regarding the direct path. The Master said, "If it does not please you, perform three prostrations. The monk asked, "The great assembly gathers like clouds..."

The assembly gathered and requested the Master to preach the Dharma. The Master asked, "Do you hear? They replied, "If one were to pause and reflect further, it would be difficult to reach [the truth].
The Master said, "In reality, it is attained. He was asked, "The Maṇi Hall has four corners, yet one corner is always exposed.
What is this ever-exposed corner? The Master said, "It cannot be pointed out further. One day, as the Master ascended the hall, he stood by his seat and addressed the assembly, saying, "Two..."
Since the Honored One did not manifest his transformation simultaneously, he returned to his quarters.
Chan Master Guiben of Yun’gai Shuangquan Monastery in Xiangzhou was a native of Jingzhao Prefecture. Initially, he went to visit Xuefeng.

Following the prostrations, [the Master] sat with his legs crossed upon a meditation seat at the foot of the peak. At this moment, the Master attained realization. Later, while residing there, a monk asked: "What is the meaning of the 'Double Spring'?
The Master said: "A pity for that pair of eyebrows. The monk said: "I do not understand. The Master said: "The labor of Yu was never required;
the matter of the rushing torrent remains unknown. Another asked: "What is the true intent of the coming from the West? The Master then—
He grabbed him, and the monk’s complexion changed. The Master said, "There is no such thing here. The Master’s fingers were long and slender, exceptionally so compared to others;
he was thus known as the Great Master of Hand Characteristics.
A monk asked Master Linquan of Shaoshan, "What is one speck of dust? The Master said, "Unconsciously it becomes a mountain.
A monk asked Master Nanyuan of Luoyang, "What is the non-arising of all phenomena? The Master said, "It has already arisen.

There was a Confucian scholar who had read extensively throughout antiquity and was commonly called Zhang Baihui (Zhang Hundred Meetings). He visited the Master. The Master asked, "Are you not Zhang Baihui?"
"Do you understand? He replied, "I dare not say so. The Master drew a line in the air with his hand and said, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "If you do not even understand one, from where could you have obtained 'hundred meetings' (baihui)?"
A monk asked Chan Master Keshou of Dongyan in Yuezhou, "What is the true master of Dongyan? The Master said, "It is wide open.
The monk asked, "What is your way of acting intimately for the sake of others? The Master said, "The great ocean does not harbor a corpse."
Question: "What is the path that leads upward? The Master pointed to his collar and showed it to him. Question: "The student has come from afar;
I request the Master to provide a skillful means. The Master said: "The skillful means have already been provided."
A monk asked Chan Master Xingzhou of Fahai Monastery in Dingzhou, "What is it like when the wind is calm and the waves are still?
The Master said, "It blows down the southern wall. The monk asked, "What is the treasure within the Way? The Master said, "Its radiance is not revealed.
The monk said, "Is that so? The Master said, "If it were, it would be revealed."
A monk asked Chan Master Tong of Longjing in Hangzhou, "What is the dragon of Longjing? The Master said, "Its spirit is naturally distinct;
the divine artisan cannot paint it. The monk asked, "Why can it not be painted? The Master said, "It stands out from the crowd without horns;
it does not conform to its kind. The monk asked, "Is it able to bring forth rain? The Master said, "It universally moistens all without limit."

Everywhere grains were forming. [The monk] asked, "Is there anything of the School Gate (the Chan tradition) here? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter of the School Gate?
The Master said, "From the beginning it has had no form or shape; responding to things, it is never deficient."
Chan Master Zongjing of Longxing Monastery in Hangzhou was a native of Taizhou. He first visited Xuefeng, where he vowed to serve as the head cook for over ten years.
Once, while working in the monks' hall, he bared one shoulder to hang a curtain.

Upon seeing this, Xuefeng remarked, "In the future, you shall dwell in a monastery with a thousand monks, yet not a single one among them will be a true seeker of the Dharma (nanzizi). The Master repented his error and returned to Zhejiang.

He resided at the Six Supernatural Powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) Cloister. King Qian summoned him to reside at Longxing Temple, where there were over a thousand followers, all of whom were practitioners of the Three Studies (trīṇi śikṣāṇi) engaged in lecturing and recitation—exactly as Xuefeng had predicted. A monk asked, "What is the extraordinary proclamation of the Six Supernatural Powers?

The Master said, "It is being carried away by everyone in the world. The monk asked, "What is the house style of the Six Supernatural Powers? The Master said, "A single piece of cotton cloth for a patched robe."

[The master gave him] a little over one *jin*. The student asked, "What is the one path for a student to advance forward? The Master said, "Who would dare deceive you? The student asked, "Is there no expedient means?
The Master said, "That would already be a case of being unjustly suppressed. The student asked, "What is the house style of the Master?"
The Master said, "In the early morning there is congee; at the time of the midday meal, there is rice. The monk asked, "Please tell me further, Master. The Master said, "This old monk is weary.
The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master simply laughed loudly.
Chan Master Chiqian of Nanchan in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "As for famous phrases and wondrous sayings, everyone everywhere has already spoken of them.
Is there anyone among this assembly today who can transcend the primary meaning and bring forth a question? If there is such a person..."
Thus, one does not fail those who rely on them. A monk asked, "What is the primary meaning? The Master said, "Why do you not ask about the primary meaning? The monk said, "I am asking now.
The Master said, "That has already fallen into the secondary meaning. The monk asked, "The ancient Buddhas have their own melodic strains; I request that the Master harmonize with them.
The Master said, "I will not harmonize with your confused and chaotic noise. The monk asked, "I do not understand why the Master does not harmonize with it. The Master said:
"Where have you come from? "From Yuezhou.
Master Shaner Nai of Yue Mountain, Zen Master Jianzhen, first gained a taste [of the Way] upon visiting Xuefeng.

Later, at the invitation of the Prince of Min, he was seated for a meal at Qingfeng Lou. After sitting for a long time, he raised his eyes and suddenly beheld the sunlight; he attained sudden, thorough enlightenment. And...
There is a verse that says: "Ascending the Qingfeng Tower for the official vegetarian feast, On this day, my lifelong eyes were opened wide.
Only now do I believe that the events of the distant Putong era Were not brought from Mount Xiang. He presented this to Xuefeng, who approved it. After he took up residence [at Qingfeng],...

A monk asked, “What is the Buddha-body? The Master said, “Which Buddha-body are you asking about? The monk replied, “The body of Śākyamuni Buddha. The Master said, “His tongue covers the three thousandfold world-system.
As he was nearing the end of his life, the Master presented this verse: “The visual faculty perishes along with forms; The auditory consciousness vanishes following sounds.
There is no separate principle for returning to the source: Today is the same as tomorrow. He then passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.
Chan Master Xuǎnè of Fúcqíng Yùán in Quànzhōu was a native of Gāolì (Korea). When the Regional Governor, Lord Wáng, asked him, “What is the matter within the lineage transmission?
the Master rebuked him. A monk asked, “What is bodhi at every turn? The Master said, “Dharma brother, you have lost half a year’s worth of provisions.
The monk asked, “Why is it so? The Master replied, “It is simply because he is scheming for another’s peck of grain.”
[The Master] said, "Rice. A questioner asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "Shrimp and earthworms. A questioner asked, "The scripture says:
'There is but one firm and dense body, which manifests within all dust-motes. What is this firm and dense body? The Master said, "Donkeys, horses, and cats."
He said, "I beg the Master for instruction. The Master replied, "Even donkeys and horses do not understand this. He asked, "How does one discern and clarify it within each and every thing?
The Master extended one leg and showed it to him.
A monk asked Master Ren of Nantai in Quzhou, "What is the realm of Nantai? The Master said, "I do not know its value.
The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, "Where are you right now, lay brother?"
When Master Dongchan of Quanzhou first opened the hall for his inaugural sermon, a monk asked: "The King of Men has extended an invitation; the Dharma King has appeared in the world.

How should one proclaim the School of the Patriarchs so as not to err regarding the ancestral wind? The Master said: "Can you handle it? The monk said: "If one does not enter the water, how can one know there are fish?
The Master said: "Do not speak idle words. The monk asked: "What is the most supreme [expression] of the Buddha-dharma?"
At Qinchichu, the Master said, "A transgression. The monk asked, "I have come as a latecomer; I beg the Master for the very first phrase. The Master said, "Where have you come from?
The monk asked, "What is the matter that belongs to the student's own portion? The Master said, "Suffering. The monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Fortunately, you are already pitiable enough, yet you insist on seeking it in a foreign land."
Chan Master Congxi of Daxianshan in Hangzhou was a senior disciple of Xuefeng. Having received the seal of approval from his own master, he thoroughly understood the essentials of the school.
He often said, "I strike the drum of Guannan and sing the song of Xuefeng. Later, he entered Zhejiang to visit the King of Qian;
the King revered his spiritual transformation and commanded him to reside on this mountain to propagate the Dharma. A monk asked, "If it were not for the King’s invitation..."

Not because of the gathering of the assembly, [the student] requested, "I beg the Master to directly point out the very meaning of coming from the West. The Master said, "That monk over there has passed over here.
[The student] said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said, "How can you be so lacking in discernment?
[The student] asked, "When one builds a cart inside the gate, the tracks must fit when one goes out. What is 'building a cart inside the gate'? The Master said:
[The Master] said, "I do not ask about the making of the carriage. What is the track? [The monk] said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "A skilled craftsman applies his work without revealing the axe or hammer."
A monk asked Master Yongtai of Fuzhou, "I have heard that you, Master, saw a tiger—is this true? The Master made the sound of a tiger.

The monk made a gesture as if to strike him. The Master said, "You dead man! The monk asked, "What is the Buddha of True Nature? The Master clapped his hands and said, "I do not understand! I do not understand!"
Chan Master Shoune Miaokong of Longshouchang Monastery in Chizhou was a native of the Lin family in Fuzhou. A monk asked, "Before reaching the Dragon Gate, how does one find a place to settle?
The Master said, "It is difficult to maintain one's life. A newly arrived monk came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
The monk replied, "Nowhere other than my own mind. The Master said, "It is no easy matter to come here. The monk also said, "It is no easy matter to come here. The Master [laughed].
He gave him a slap on the palm. The student asked, "What is the mind that has been transmitted? The Master said, "I have instructed you repeatedly not to speak of it to others.
The student asked, "What is the ancestral vehicle (zongcheng) from above? The Master said, "Can it be placed within your mouth, O *jialuo*?
The student asked, "I pray the Master grant me a direct encounter at the point of essential simplicity. The Master said, "How very simple and essential!"
A monk asked Master Mengbi of Jianzhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “I do not deceive you. The monk said, “Is that so?
The Master said, “You are deceiving him. When the King of Min invited the Master for a meal, he asked, “Have you brought your brush with you?”
The Master said, "This is not the embroidered brush of Mount Ji; it is not ashamed to be the rabbit-hair pen from within the moon.

Since Your Majesty has deigned to inquire, this mountain monk dares not fail to present [this answer]. He asked again, "What is the Dharma King? The Master said, "It is not the family style of Dream-Pen Village."
Chan Master Yuan Yan of Jile in Fuzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the家风 (household style) of Jile? The Master said, "It fills the eyes and cannot be fully seen.
The monk asked, "All phenomena are fundamentally rootless; I wonder what it is that you teach the student to take up and realize? The Master said, "Do not speak in your sleep.
The monk asked, "I have long dwelt in a dark room and have not yet reached its source. Today I have come here; I beg the Master for [instruction]. The Master said...
[The student] bowed. The Master said, "Do not close your eyes and pretend it is night. [The student] said, "If that is so, then the *udumbara* flower has blossomed.
To accommodate the present age, how would you show us the supreme ancestral style? The Master said, "Do you recognize it or not? [The student] said, "If that is so, then my doubts have been stilled.
The Master said, "Do not speak in your sleep before the assembly. [The student] asked, "Regarding the arrival of Kāśyapa Mātanga in the Han..."
Question: "How was it when Bodhidharma came to Liang? The Master said: "Is there any error now? [The monk] said:
"If that is so, then the principle has produced the Three Vehicles and the flowers have blossomed into five petals. The Master said: "What do you mean by 'Three Vehicles' and 'five petals'? Get out!"
A monk asked Chan Master Ruti of Mount Furong in Fuzhou, "What is the ancient melody? The Master remained silent for a long while and then said, "Do you hear it?
The monk replied, "I do not hear it. The Master presented this verse: "The ancient melody sounds majestic; its rhythm is the same as in the present age.
If one were to point with the first finger, even the Buddhas and Patriarchs would lose their tracks."
A monk asked Master Qihe of Luojing, "What is Qihe? The Master joined his two hands and said, "Jubao, Jubao.

(Fengxue said: "One cry of the crane resounds through the universe; do not let the flock of chickens claim they know the hour. The monk asked, "When a fine horse does not enter Western Qin, what then?
The Master said, "Where would it go?"
A monk asked Master Xichan of Mt. Gui in Tanzhou, "At this very moment, how does one draw near?
The Master said, "How do you intend to draw near? The monk said, "Is there not some expedient means? The Master said, "The Kaiyuan and Longxing editions of the Great and Small Tripitaka.
[Another] asked, "What is swift supernatural power? The Master said, "New clothes become tattered rags. [Another] asked, "What is... (the question was left unfinished).
[The Master] was at Huangxian Bridge. He said, "How many people have been deceived? A monk asked, "Without resorting to verbal elaboration, what is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Do not make the sound of a jackal."
When Chan Master Yanzong of Chaoshan in Jizhou came to pay his respects to Zifu, the Master descended from his meditation seat to receive him.
Zifu asked, "How many years has the Abbot resided on this mountain? The Master replied, "A dull bird nests in the reeds; a weary fish rests in the marsh."

[The monk] said, "In that case, you are a true man of the Way. The Master said, "Sit and drink some tea. [The monk] asked, "What is Chaoshan? The Master said, "No corpses are lodged here. [The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person among the mountains?
The Master said, "Planting red lotuses upon rocks. [The monk] asked, "... (The question is omitted in the source). The Master said, "... (The answer is omitted in the source).
"What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Above all, avoid violating court protocol.
A monk asked Chan Master Puming of Mount Putong in Yizhou, "What is Buddha-nature? The Master said, "You have no Buddha-nature.
The monk said, "All sentient beings, down to the crawling insects, possess Buddha-nature. Why then do I, as a student, lack it? The Master said, "Because..."
“You seek it outwardly. The questioner asked, “What is the pearl of the profound mystery? The Master said, “This is not it.
The questioner asked, “What then is the pearl of the profound mystery? The Master said, “It has been lost.”
A monk asked Master Yong of Liangjia Hermitage on Mount Shuangquan in Suizhou, “What was the meaning of Bodhidharma’s nine years of facing the wall?
The Master said, “I could not sleep. The Master asked Elder Huguo, “Within the realm of Suiyang, whether male or female, let each pose a question;
let every question be distinct. With what will you respond to them? Huguo held up his empty hand.
In the center, he drew a circle. The Master said, "I thank you for your compassion, Elder. Guo said, "I dare not. The Master lowered his head and did not look at him.
Guo asked, "How can one suddenly bring all conditions to rest? The Master said, "Adding frost upon snow."
A monk asked Chan Master Chaowu of Baofu Monastery in Zhangzhou, "What is it like when a fish has not yet passed through the Dragon Gate?

The Master said, "Nurturing its nature in the deep pool. The monk asked, "What is it like when it has passed through? The Master said, "As soon as it ascends to the celestial heights, the multitudes find it difficult to follow.
The monk asked, "What is it like after it has ascended? The Master said, "Hanging clouds cover all; its moisture reaches the great thousandfold world-system. The monk asked, "Is there still..."

[The student] said, "There is none who receives the moisture. The Master said, "There is. [The student] asked, "What is it that does not receive the moisture? The Master said, "A bare stump propping up the great sun."
When the Venerable Fu of Taiyuan was first lecturing on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* at Guangxiao Temple in Yangzhou, a practitioner of Chan who was stranded by snow went there to listen to the lecture.
When the discourse reached the three causes of buddha-nature and the dharma-body of the three virtues, he spoke extensively on the subtle principles of the dharma-body.
The Chan practitioner laughed in derision. After the Master finished his lecture, he invited the Chan practitioner to drink tea and said, "My own aspirations have always been narrow and inferior;

I have merely followed the texts to explain the meaning. Having just been ridiculed by you, I hope you will instruct me. The Chan practitioner replied, "I truly laughed because you, Master of Commentaries, do not recognize the Dharma-body.
The Master asked, "In such an explanation as yours, what is there that is not correct? The Chan practitioner said, "I ask the Master to explain it further."
"Universal. The Master said, "The principle of the Dharma-body is like the great void: vertically it exhausts the three periods of time, horizontally it spans the ten directions;

it encompasses the eight extremities and includes the two polarities. Responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nowhere it does not pervade. [The student] said, "I do not say that what you, Master of the Seat, have said is incorrect;
however, you have only described the extent and boundaries of the Dharma-body. You have truly not yet recognized the Dharma-body itself. The Master said:
"Since this is so, Zen Master, you should explain it to me. The master asked, "Head Lecturer, do you believe this? The teacher replied, "How could I dare not believe it?
The master said, "If that is so, Head Lecturer, suspend your lectures for ten days. Sit upright in quiet meditation within your room;
withdraw your mind and collect your thoughts, letting go of all conditions of both good and evil at once. The teacher followed these instructions exactly, from the first watch of the night until—

At the fifth watch, he heard the sound of drums and horns and suddenly attained awakening. He immediately went to knock on the door. The Chan practitioner asked, "Who is it? The Master replied, "It is I.
The Chan practitioner scolded him, saying, "I have instructed you to transmit and uphold the Great Teaching and to preach the Dharma in place of the Buddha.

Why did you come here last night drunk and lying in the street? The Master said, "Chan Master, while you have been lecturing on the sutras all along, you have been using the noses of your biological parents..."
Kong Niunie said, "From this day forward, I shall never again dare to act in such a manner. The Chan master said, "Go for now;
we shall meet tomorrow. The teacher then ceased his lectures and traveled extensively throughout all quarters, his fame spreading across the land.

Once, while traveling through Zhejiang and attending a dharma assembly at Mount Jing, a monk asked him one day in front of the Great Buddha Hall, "Have you, Venerable Sir, ever been to Wutai? The teacher—

The monk said, "I have been there. The Master asked, "Did you see Mañjuśrī? The monk replied, "I saw him. The Master asked, "Where did you see him? The monk replied, "I saw him in front of the Buddha Hall at Mount Jing.
Later, when the monk traveled to Minchuan, he recounted this to Xuefeng. Xuefeng said, "Why did you not tell him to come over the mountain pass?
Upon hearing this, the Master packed his belongings and set out. He first arrived at the Xuefeng monastery to rest his staff. Because of this—
He divided some tangerines among the monks. Changqing asked, "Where did you bring these from? The Master said, "From beyond the mountain ridges.

Changqing said, "It was no easy matter to travel such a long distance; how did you manage to carry them back? The Master replied, "Tangerines! Tangerines! The next day he went up the mountain. When Xuefeng heard of this, he assembled the community.
Upon arriving at the Dharma Hall, the Master looked toward Xuefeng and then immediately went down to attend to the monastery affairs. The following day...
He went up to pay his respects and said, "I offended you, Master, yesterday. Feng said, "Since you know it was such a matter, let it be.
One day, when Feng saw the Master, he pointed at the sun and showed it to him. The Master shook his hand and walked out. Feng said, "Do you not agree with me?
The Master replied, "When you, Master, shake your head, I wag my tail. Where is there any disagreement? Feng [laughed].
He said, "In every place, one must also conceal it. One day, during the evening *samādhi* (assembly), Feng was lying in the central courtyard.
The Master said, "Within the jurisdiction of the five prefectures, only this old monk is slightly superior [to others]. Feng then rose and departed.
Feng once asked the Master, "I have heard it said that Linji has three phrases; is this true? The Master replied, "It is. Feng asked, "What is the first?"
The Master raised his eyes and looked at him. Xuefeng said, "This is still the second phrase. What is the first phrase? The Master folded his hands and withdrew.
From this point on, Xuefeng held him in deep esteem; within the master's chamber, they attained mutual understanding, and the way of teacher and disciple was in perfect accord.
He no longer traveled elsewhere but remained there to manage the bathhouse. One day, Xuansha went up to pay his respects to Xuefeng.
Xuefeng said, "There is a little mouse here; it is currently in the bathhouse. Xuansha said, "Wait, let me examine him for you, Master.
Having finished speaking, he went to the bathhouse and encountered the Master (Shishuang) pouring water. Xuansha said, "I have come to see the Senior Monk. The Master said, "We have already met."
The monk said, "In which kalpa did we ever meet? The Master said, "Why do you nod off? The monk then entered the abbot’s quarters.
Xuefeng said, "I have already scrutinized him. [The monk] asked, "How did you scrutinize him? The monk recounted the previous dialogue.
Xuefeng said, "You have been robbed by a thief. Gushan asked the Master, "Before one's parents were born, where was the nose?"
The Master said, "Brother, you speak first. Guishan said, "I am alive right now; where do you say I am? The Master did not approve.
Guishan then asked, "How about that? The Master took the fan in his hand and said nothing.
Guishan, unable to fathom this, struck the Master with a fist. The Master then went to Drum Mountain (Gushan).
The King invited him, and Xuefeng escorted him to the gate. Upon returning to the Dharma Hall, Xuefeng said, "A single arrow of the Sage has shot straight into the nine-layered capital.
The Master said, "He is not yet there. Xuefeng said, "He is a man of thorough penetration.
The Master said, "If you do not believe me, wait until I go to examine him myself. He then pursued him halfway and asked, "Elder brother, where have you been heading?"
[The Master] asked, "Where do you go? Guishan said, "I am going into the nine-layered city. The Master said, "What if you suddenly encounter the three armies surrounding you?
Guishan said, "He has his own path that penetrates the heavens. The Master said, "In that case, you have left the palace and lost the hall."
Shan said, "Where would he not be called Honored One? The Master shook his sleeves and turned back. Feng asked, "What was that about?
The Master said, "A fine sacred arrow—broken in mid-flight. He then recounted the previous conversation. Feng said, "The fellow’s words remain.
The Master said, "This old frozen lump still has a trace of hometown sentiment. The Master stood before the storehouse. A monk asked, "How is it?"
"This very touch is Bodhi. The Master kicked the puppy; it let out a cry and ran away. The monk had no reply. The Master said, "A little puppy does not deserve more than a single kick.
While Baofu was picking melons, the Master arrived. Baofu said, "If you can say something, I will give you a melon to eat.

The Master said, "Hand it over. Baofu passed a slice to him. As soon as the Master received it, he departed. Although the Master did not appear in the world, his reputation spread throughout all quarters.
Muzhe was originally the Venerable Fu of Taiyuan. Later, he returned to Weiyang, where the Censor-in-Chief Chen retained him at his residence to provide for his needs.
One day, the Master said to the Censor, "Tomorrow I shall lecture on the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* once, as a way of repaying your kindness.
After the Censor had prepared the vegetarian feast and tea, the Master ascended the seat. After a long silence, he struck the sounding block once and said, "Thus have I heard," and then called out.
"Shangshu," [the master] called. "Shu," [the disciple] replied. The master said, "At one time the Buddha was... and then he suddenly passed away.
Master Nan Yue Banruo Weijinbao was a native of Fuzhou. He took Xuefeng as his teacher and was a close friend of Xuansha. He had penetrated deeply into the profound mysteries.
One day he asked Upāsaka Jian, "I have heard that you have written a commentary on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*; is this true? Jian replied:
"I dare not," [the monk] replied. The Master asked, "How would you annotate the two Mañjuśrīs? He said, "I beg the Master to examine them. Thereupon, the Master raised his sleeves and departed.
The Master once composed the *Baolin Zhuan* (Record of the Baolin Temple) in four fascicles, recording the lineages of the Chan school from after the Zhenyuan era.
He also separately authored the *Nanyue Gaoseng Zhuan* (Biographies of Eminent Monks of Nanyue), both of which circulate in the world today.
A monk asked Chan Master Zhiyuan Xianjiao of Baimiao in Anzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Tanziguoshi: "Who transmits the mind-seal of all Buddhas?"
The Master said, “Master Bodhidharma. [The monk] asked, “How was it that Master Bodhidharma was able to transmit the Dharma? The Master said, “Tell me, who was it that transmitted it?
[The monk] asked, “What is the direct, single path? The Master said, “Cut off. [The monk] asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, “Suffering. [The monk] asked, “What is the Way? The Master said, “Universal. [The monk] asked, “What is the student’s own self? The Master said, “Self.”
The Master said, "Lost. Question: "What is it to attain the state where there are no mountains, rivers, or great earth? The Master said, "Not giving rise to views. Question:
"Who is the one within the assembly at Kāśyapa’s place of practice in the Piṇḍola Cave? The Master said, "Śākyamuni Buddha."
Question: "What is the Bodhisattva Red-Crested King? The Master said: "Why do you ask about that red-headed fellow?

The Master said, "It cannot be extinguished by the eight winds. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then darkness will not arise."
The Master said: "In broad daylight, there are no idle people.

Chan Master Shenlu of Ruifeng Monastery in Wenzhou was a native of Fuzhou. Having long served as the attendant to [Chan Master] Ruiyan, he later founded and established his own monastery, to which students of the Way flocked.
The Master had a verse that said: "Solitary and serene, dwelling alone with a contemplative mind; who..."
Faith produces wondrous sounds from no strings; throughout the day in the Dharma Hall, he sits only in stillness. No one else asks about the original mind.
At that time, the Venerable Pengyan asked, "What is the original mind? The Master called out, "Pengyan! Pengyan responded, "Yes.
The Master said, "Go and serve tea for the old monk. Thereupon, Pengyan attained realization.
Chan Master Huījī Chāohuì of Mount Hánglóng in Ézhōu was a dharma successor of Chan Master Xuánquán Yàn. He was the son of the Zhāng family of Qīnghé.
Initially, he visited Yántóu and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Yántóu replied, "Do you know how to make rice cakes? The Master said, "I do."
Tou said, "For now, let us save the rice cakes. Later, he arrived at Xuánquán and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Xuánquán picked up a stalk of soapberry and asked, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. Xuánquán set down the soapberry and made the gesture of doing laundry.
The Master then prostrated himself and said, "I now know that the Buddha-dharma has no distinctions. Xuánquán said, "What did you see to say such a thing?"
The Master said, "I once asked Yantou, 'Do you know how to rescue rice-cakes? To rescue rice-cakes is simply to untie what is stuck.
When you, Master, brought up the soap-nut, that too was to untie what is stuck. Therefore it is said there is no difference. Master Quan laughed heartily, whereupon the Master attained realization.
Later, when he was residing [in his own temple], a monk asked, "I do not ask about matters concerning the Patriarchs or Buddhas; how is it?"
"This is an ordinary matter," the Master said. "I have lived on this mountain for fifteen years. The questioner asked, "What is the Master's family style?

The Method of Opening the Mountain. Zen practitioners from the four quarters fill the hall and chambers. When ascending the hall, they meet with full force; those who can match this excellence are rarely found.

To die together and live together—such a one is not encountered even once in ten thousand. Those who seek words and chase phrases are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. To cite the ancients and the present is to destroy the very lineage of the barbarians.
As for the single path that points directly upward, even "cracking and pecking" is still at odds. When meeting a Confucian scholar, he merely grasps his whip and turns back.
"First! What the śramaṇa sees is truly a bitter pity. To cast away pure gold and follow the crowd to gather mere soil—inform all you young children:

do not wander aimlessly in vain. Even if one understands his profound mystery, it is still accompanied by shards and rubble; it is better to cast it aside once and for all and soar across the great void.

[The monk] asked: "How is it after it has emerged from the den? The Master said: "Ten thousand miles of swirling dust. [The monk] asked: "How is it when it wishes to emerge but does not?
The Master said: "Perilous. [The monk] asked: "What about matters regarding the future? The Master said: "Sealed! [The monk] asked: "What is the penetration?"

The Master said, "Cast it onto the ground of the Vajra. Question: "What were Mañjuśrī and Vimalakīrti discussing when they conversed?

The Master said, "The *gejin* headcloth and the gauze cap have already been set aside over here. Question: "What is the Master? The Master said, "The Great Dipper turning its body after [the constellation] Hou."
Regarding the family style, the Master said, "To bite into it successfully is to be a skilled hand. A questioner asked, "When the crane is released from its cage and departs with the mist, what then?
The Master said, "What can you do about that single dot upon its head? A questioner asked, "As for smokeless fire, what kind of person can face it?
The Master said, "One who does not spare his eyebrows. The questioner said, "Can the Master face it as well? The Master said, "You tell me."
"How many stalks of eyebrows are there? A newly arrived monk had just ascended the Dharma Hall when the Master raised his whisk and then cast it down.
The monk said, "Take care," and descended. The Master said, "A true adept! A true adept! A monk asked, "What is it like when one is fully equipped with a sword?

It was cold. Entering the hall, as soon as the assembly had gathered, the Master said, "The wind at the peak is somewhat stiff; this is not where you should settle your body or establish your life.
Return for now to a warm room to deliberate. He then returned to his quarters. The assembly followed him there and stood still.
The Master spoke again, "As soon as you reach a warm room, you will see people nodding off," and he drove them all away at once with his staff. The Master then asked Guotai about the ancients.
Daojuzhi recited the three-line mantra ten million times and was thus able to be called one who transcends all men.
How could one remove those three lines for him so that he might be called one who transcends all men? Daoyi held up a finger.

A visitor came and asked, "I have this great illness; right now I am suffering from intense pain.
Nowhere can I find relief. Is there anyone who can save me? The Master replied with a letter: "This Vajra arrow has struck the crown of your head and passed through to the other side.
Later, a monk from the assembly went to stay in a hermitage for one year and then returned to pay his respects.
The Master bowed and said, "The ancients said: 'If you do not see someone for three days, do not look upon them as you did before.

The Master pried open his chest and asked, 'Tell me, how many hairs do I have on my gallbladder? The monk had no reply. The Master then asked, 'When did you leave your hermitage? The monk said, 'This morning.
The Master said, 'To whom did you entrust your broken-legged cauldron when you came here? The monk again had no reply."
[The student] spoke. The Master then shouted him out and asked, "I have heard you say, 'I dwell at the summit of Mingzhao and propagate the mind of the ancient Buddhas.
What is the summit of Mingzhao? The Master said, "Change your eyes. [The student] asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said:
"Are you still short of breath? He asked, "This student has come from the clouds and waves; I request the Master to spread out his bowl. The Master said, "I shall crush your crown!
The student replied, "Even so, one must go to Xiantuo. The Master then struck him and drove him out. The Master had a verse for the assembly which said:
"One snap of Mingzhao’s fingers—few can match it. This is the supreme, wondrous mechanism of the True School. A spark of stone-fire, how suddenly it passes!"
When he was about to pass away, his son, who had been born that very morning, should have known [the time]. As he was about to depart this life, he ascended the hall to address the assembly.
Having finished his final instructions, a monk asked, "Where will you go after the Master’s hundred-year term is over? The Master lifted up one foot and said, "Look beneath my feet.

He emitted a hundred jewel-lights. Then, extending his feet, he said, "How much have I emitted now? The other replied, "The World-Honored One of old; tonight it is the Master.
The Master brushed his eyebrows with his hand and said, "Do not let this be in vain. He then spoke a verse:
"Displaying full majesty amidst a thicket of blades, May you all protect and uphold it well. An iron ox gives birth to a calf within the fire— At the parting of ways..."
"Who can understand my kōan? Having finished this verse, he sat upright and passed away; his stupa and monastery remain there.

The Master said, "Cold and heat press one another. Chan Master Qingping Weikang of Jizhou ascended the hall. Without shifting his expression, he immediately conveyed the sense of victory and defeat. Chan Master Qingping Weikang of Jizhou ascended the hall. Without moving his spirit or expression, he immediately manifested the intent of winning and losing. Is there anyone? Come forth! At that moment, a monk stepped forward and prostrated. The Master said, "Not a true adept. Then...

A monk asked Chan Master Yizhao of Jinzhu Mountain in Wuzhou, "What is the patriarchal style of the Master?

What is meant by "the myriad phenomena are simultaneously quiescent"? The Master said: "What is there? Question: "What is meant by 'the myriad phenomena arise together'? The Master said: [The myriad phenomena arise together.]

The Ropes-Bed Recliner. A monk asked Master Lingyan of Guanzhou, "What is the treasure within the Way? The Master said, "The earth slants toward the southeast; the heavens are high in the northwest. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Before the falling light, the function is unique. [The Master] composed a verse on Shigong: The bowstring snaps, the arrow flies; The tiger roars, the dragon leaps. If you can see it here and now, You will know the ancient’s heart. If you hesitate for even a moment, You fall into the pit of doubt. Do not seek it in the past or future; It is right before your eyes. If you can grasp it in this very instant, You will transcend the three realms. If you cannot, you remain stuck in birth and death. Do not look for it in words or phrases; It is the very function of your own mind. If you can turn it back upon yourself, You will be free from all attachments. If you cannot, you are bound by the eight winds. Do not seek it in scriptures or commentaries; It is the direct pointing of the patriarchs. If you can see it with your own eyes, You will realize the Buddha-mind. If you cannot, you wander in delusion. Do not seek it in form or emptiness; It is the luminosity of your own nature. If you can maintain it without wavering, You will dwell in the realm of reality. If you cannot, you are lost in the sea of suffering. Do not seek it in meditation or wisdom; It is the original face of your own self. If you can recognize it in this very moment, You will attain the great liberation. If you cannot, you are caught in the net of views. Do not seek it in the mountains or forests; It is the very essence of your daily life. If you can act with total spontaneity, You will manifest the Way in every situation. If you cannot, you are trapped in the cycle of existence. Do not seek it in the past or the future; It is the present moment of your own experience. If you can let go of all grasping, You will enter the gate of the Dharma. If you cannot, you remain in the darkness of ignorance. Do not seek it in the north or the south; It is the center of your own being. If you can rest in non-action, You will be at peace in the world. If you cannot, you are tossed about by the winds of passion. Do not seek it in the east or the west; It is the source of all phenomena. If you can see through the root, You will understand the ultimate truth. If you cannot, you are lost in the branches and leaves. Do not seek it in the beginning or the end; It is the middle way of your own realization. If you can embody it in your conduct, You will walk the path of the sages. If you cannot, you remain in the mire of worldly affairs. Do not seek it in the heights or the depths; It is the level ground of your own mind. If you can maintain equanimity, You will dwell in the state of nirvana. If you cannot, you are subject to the laws of karma. Do not seek it in the heavens or the hells; It is the freedom of your own liberation. If you can realize it for yourself, You will transcend all bounds. If you cannot, you are confined by your own limitations. Do not seek it in the known or the unknown; It is the mystery of your own awakening. If you can penetrate the secret, You will be one with the Buddhas and patriarchs. If you cannot, you remain separate from the enlightened ones. Do not seek it in the scriptures or the treatises; It is the living breath of your own spirit. If you can breathe it freely, You will live in the world without attachment. If you cannot, you are bound by the fetters of desire. Do not seek it in the past or the future; It is the eternal now of your own presence. If you can dwell in this moment, You will be at home in the universe. If you cannot, you are a stranger in the world. Do not seek it in the body or the mind; It is the unity of all things. If you can realize this oneness, You will be free from all duality. If you cannot, you remain divided by oppositions. Do not seek it in the self or the other; It is the harmony of all beings. If you can participate in this harmony, You will be in accord with the Way. If you cannot, you remain alienated from the truth. Do not seek it in the sacred or the profane; It is the commonality of all existence. If you can embrace it as such, You will find peace in the midst of chaos. If you cannot, you are lost in the turmoil of the world. Do not seek it in the wise or the foolish; It is the equality of all people. If you can treat everyone with respect, You will manifest the virtue of compassion. If you cannot, you remain bound by prejudice. Do not seek it in the high or the low; It is the impartiality of your own heart. If you can act without discrimination, You will be a true vessel of the Dharma. If you cannot, you remain a vessel of delusion. Do not seek it in the beginning or the end; It is the continuity of your own life. If you can flow with the current, You will be in harmony with nature. If you cannot, you remain stuck in stagnation. Do not seek it in the light or the dark; It is the clarity of your own vision. If you can see through the veil of illusion, You will perceive the true nature of reality. If you cannot, you remain blinded by appearances. Do not seek it in the world or the beyond; It is the bridge between all realms. If you can cross over without hesitation, You will reach the shore of enlightenment. If you cannot, you remain adrift in the ocean of suffering. Do not seek it in the teacher or the student; It is the transmission of the lineage. If you can receive it directly, You will be a true heir of the Buddhas. If you cannot, you remain a mere follower of words. If you cannot, you remain subject to the flow of moments. Do not seek it in the self or the non-self; It is the liberation of your own mind. If you can let go of all grasping, You will be released from the bonds of ego. If you cannot, you remain imprisoned by the self. Do not seek it in the mountains or the rivers; It is the vastness of your own spirit. If you can soar above the mundane, You will transcend the limits of the world. If you cannot, you remain tethered to the earth. Do not seek it in the known or the unknown; It is the mystery of your own existence. If you can embrace the unknown, You will be open to the infinite. The monk replied, "It is full of endless debate and discussion. The Master said, "How can it compare to my place here, where we plant fields and eat the food we earn?"
[The monk] said, "What can one do about the three realms? The Master said, "What do you call 'the three realms'?
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the South. The Master said, "What words did the masters there use to instruct their disciples?
The monk replied, "They say that although gold dust is precious, it cannot enter the eye. The Master said, "I say that Mount Sumeru is in your eye. One day... [text continues]
Zhongta was serving as an attendant to Xuansha. Xuansha struck Zhongta with a staff and said, "Is this the name, or is it the essence?
Zhongta did not respond. Xuansha then asked the Master, "How do you understand this? The Master said, "This monk received a blow and does not know where it came from."
The monk reported, "Baofu has already passed away. The Master said, "Now that Baofu has passed away, Dizang enters the stupa" (A monk asked Fayan, "What was the meaning of the ancients?
Fayan said, "Heaven! Heaven!"). Later, he moved to Lohan Temple, where he extensively expounded upon the profound essentials. He ascended the hall and said:
"The profound mystery of the Gate of the Patriarchs—is it simply like this, or is there something else extraordinary? If there is something else extraordinary, you should bring it forth."
"Look here. If there were not [these two], then go. One must not take these two characters and treat them as the very vehicle of the school (zongcheng). Why?
These two characters refer to the vehicle of the school and the vehicle of the teachings (jiaocheng). As soon as you speak of the vehicle of the school, it becomes the vehicle of the school;

as soon as you speak of the vehicle of the teachings, it becomes the vehicle of the teachings. Zen Master, the vehicle of the Buddha-dharma’s school has, from the beginning, been established by your own mouth."
To establish names and create conceptual grasping—this is precisely what it is. For a moment, one speaks of the level here, of the real;
one speaks of the perfect, of the eternal. O Zen masters, what do you call "level and real"? What do you take to be "perfect and eternal"? You have traveled on pilgrimage to other houses;
you must distinguish the principles. Do not let yourselves be buried by them. Do not merely grasp some fragments of sound, form, names, and words, and store them in your hearts.
[The Master] said, "Head! You say you understand and that you are well able to discern. But what exactly do you understand? What exactly do you discern?
That which can be memorized and retained is a name; that which can be discerned is sound and form. If it were not for sound, form, name, and so forth..."
How do you remember and discern this? The wind blowing through the pine trees is sound;
the croaking of a frog or the cawing of an old crow is also sound. Why not listen there and make your choice?
If you have some conceptualization or mental image regarding that, then as for the Master’s own words—how much conceptualization does he have compared to yours? Do not err. Thus it is said:
Now, as these sounds and forms resound vibrantly, do they reach you or not?
If they do reach you, then your numinous nature, the adamantine secret, must undergo destruction and departure. Why is this so? Because the sound penetrates and shatters your ears.
Form pierces your eyes; its causes and conditions immediately block them. Illusory delusions run about and kill you. The essence of sound and form is such that they cannot be contained.
If they do not reach you, from where could sound and form possibly come? Do you understand? Try to discern for yourself whether they reach you or do not reach you.

[The student] says, “If that is so, then it is my fault. The Master says, “Retreat with care. [The student] asks, “What are the sages?”
