The Master said, "It depends on you. [The student] asked, "What is the Eye of the Ten Directions? The Master said, "Blink your eyebrows and see.

He invited Baofu for a meal and sent someone to deliver a message, saying, "We request that the Master, out of compassion, deign to honor us with his presence. Baofu said, "Compassion is for whom? The Master said, "For me."
To speak thus is entirely lacking in compassion. While enjoying the moon, he said, "The clouds move;
the rain departs. A monk said, "It is not that the clouds move; it is the wind that moves. The Master said, "I say that neither the clouds move nor does the wind move.
The monk asked, "Master, earlier you said the clouds moved. The Master replied, "Who is at fault? The Master saw a monk and raised [the matter].
The Master said, "Do you understand? A monk replied, 'I thank the Master for his compassion in showing this to me.
The Master said, 'When you see me raise my whisk, you immediately say, "He is showing it to me. Every day you see mountains and rivers; does he not show them to you as well?
Then, seeing another monk approach, the Master raised his whisk. The monk praised him and prostrated. The Master said, 'Upon seeing me raise my whisk, you immediately prostrate.'"
He prostrated and offered praise. [The Master] swept the floor and stood up with his broom. [The monk asked: "Why do you not offer praise? [The Master] asked: "The teachings state:
'If one sees that all marks are no-marks, then one sees the Tathāgata. What, then, is a no-mark? The Master said: "A lantern. [The monk] asked:
"What is leaving the household life (renunciation)? The Master said: "Whom do you call a master? [The monk] asked: "Where does this monk come from?"
[The Master] said, “Qinzhou. The monk replied, “What object have you brought? [The Master] said, “I have brought no object.
The Master said, “Why do you speak falsely before the assembly? The monk had no reply. The Master then asked, “Is it not true that Qinzhou produces songbirds?
The monk said, “Songbirds are found in Longxi. The Master said, “That is not much of a difference. He then asked another monk, “Where have you come from?”
[The monk] said, "To repay his kindness. The Master said, "Why do you not remain right there? [The monk] said, "Monastics are not fixed in one place.
The Master said, "Since you are a monastic, why are you not fixed? The monk had no reply. (Xuánjué provided this substitute response: "I thank the Master for your inquiry.
When Imperial Tutor Wang presented robes to the assembly of monks at Xuefeng, the Seat-Holder Congyan was absent. A junior brother received the robes on his behalf under the name of Congyan. Congyan—
[The monk] returned. His younger brother said, "I have already submitted the name for my elder brother. Xiangyan said, "Tell me, what is my name? The younger brother had no reply.
The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "My elder brother is so greedy. He asked again, "Where is the greed?
Again, he spoke on his behalf, saying, "Submitting the name twice. (Yunju Xi said: "Where is the place where Upādhyāya Xiangyan submits the name twice? The Master [was thus] with Changqing and Baofu.
They entered the prefecture and saw a screen painting of peonies. Baofu said, "What a fine peony blossom! Changqing said, "Do not let your eyes deceive you.
The Master said, "What a pity for such a fine blossom. (Xuange said: Do these words of the three venerable elders have any distinction of intimacy or distance? As for Layman Luo Han speaking thus...)
"Where does it land? He asked a monk, "While you were at Zhaoqing, was there anything unusual you heard? Try to bring it up. The monk said, "I dare not misquote.
The Master said, "How would you quote the ultimate reality? The monk said, "Why do you, Master, act like this? The Master said, "Your speech has fallen into error.
At the evening assembly, the monks heard the sound of a horn. The Master said, "The Arhat [hears] three..."
He ascended the hall once a day. Imperial Tutor Wang assisted him during two periods of the day.

Wang asked, "What is the student's original mind? The Master said, "This is your original mind. Wang asked, "You occupy the precious seat and preach the Dharma to save people; I wonder, what kind of people do you save?
The Master said, "You also occupy the precious seat; what kind of people do you save? Wang asked, "When looking at one’s form in a mirror, one sees..."
"Not difficult. [The monk asked: "What is the mirror? The Master said, "Do you see the form? [The monk] asked, "If one attains the root, there is no need to worry about the branches.
What is the branch? The Master said, "It is all here. Once, while the Master was ill, a monk asked, "How is the Master's health?
The Master propped his staff against the ground and said, "Tell me, does this hurt? The monk said, "Whom is the Master asking? The Master said, [pointing to himself].
He asked him, "Does it still hurt? The Master replied, "It turns out you have been engaging with me in intellectual reasoning all along.

In the autumn of the third year of the Tiancheng era, he returned once more to the old site in Min City. After visiting all the Buddhist temples in the vicinity, he entered parinirvāṇa. His remains were cremated and the relics were collected;
a stūpa was erected in the western corner of the monastery. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Zhenying.
Chan Master Zhongji Mingzhen of Tiantong Temple in Hangzhou was a native of Taizhou. Having received the Dharma from Xuansha, he returned to the region of Zhejiang.

King Qian Wusuku invited him to appear in the world to propagate the Dharma. He ascended the hall and said: "If one were to directly raise the banner of the school and sing forth the fundamental matter alone, it would be no different from a block of顽石 (hard rock).
If one speaks of cutting off all news of ordinary people and sages, there would be no great earth or mountains."
The River: Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, it is all but a single eye. This is said because there is no other way; do you understand this?
If you still do not understand, listen to this verse: "Blind, deaf, mute, and speechless—this is the *ṛṣi* (sage).
Though eyes are full before them, people of the age cannot cope. One must realize the wondrous within the present moment: Body and mind, the myriad phenomena, and the vast array of stars. Monk.

Question: "What is the unmoving pivot? The Master said: "Layers upon layers of green mountains. Question: "What is the silent, boundless expanse? The Master said: "A single band of white clouds. Question:
"What is returning to the root and attaining the essential meaning? The Master said: "The horns of a rabbit have grown. Question:
"What is following after illumination and losing the source? The Master said: "The hair of a tortoise has fallen. Question: "When the lotus flower has not yet... [text fragment]
"How is it when emerging from the water? The Master said, "Who does not know? "How is it after emerging from the water? The Master said, "Its fragrance is witnessed by the eyes.
Question: "How is it when the bright moon shines in the sky? The Master said, "This is precisely the moment of dividing the light;
what need is there to point toward the Jade Tower?"
On the day of the opening of the hall at Xianzong Monastery in Fuzhou, Chan Master Chifu Qingfa was asked by a monk: "Master, having ascended the precious seat, what matter should you discuss?
The Master said: "I have cleared open the ear-holes for you to listen. The monk asked: "Why did the ancients say it is not where the ears or eyes reach?
The Master said: "A golden thorn tree does not grow pears. The monk asked: "What is the place that has never been reached by the ancients or the moderns?"
"Please, Master, speak. The Master said, "How will you ask? [The student] asked, "When many hands sift gold together, who is the one who obtains it?
The Master said, "Raising a hand across a thousand miles; cease your efforts and look as you please. [The student] asked, "The flowers are exquisite upon the flying peaks;
what is the matter before the terrace of the immortal realm? The Master said, "The priceless great jewel appears within the light; the ignorant guests, in their confusion, vie with one another."
"What a pity! [The student] said. "The *udumbara* flower blooms and all people behold it; as for the meaning of the Supreme Vehicle (*zōngchéng*), what is it like?

The Master said, "If you, *ācārya*, ask about the meaning of the Supreme Vehicle, it is better to remain in stillness—*svāhā*. [The student] asked, "What is the realm of the Buddhas in Min? The Master said, "The workings of creation are ultimately difficult to fathom;

the spring breeze is in vain and light. [The student] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The workings of creation are ultimately difficult to fathom; the spring breeze is in vain and light. (Note: The Master’s response here repeats the previous answer.)
Zhongbao asked, "The tears of the great-grandson also fall. He asked, "After all the sages have withdrawn their radiance and returned to the source, what is it like?

The Master said, "Three times the cries of the monkey are cut short; ten thousand miles away, the traveler listens with sorrow. He asked, "I do not yet understand how people of the present age can coincide with the mechanism of the ancients.
The Master said, "I will tell you with a sincere heart: one must strictly avoid [seeking it] before it has been born."
Chan Master [Name] of Guotai Monastery in Wuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Without departing from this very place, everything is the wondrously luminous true mind.
Therefore, Master Xuansha said: 'Few in the world know my final word. How can they compare to Guotai, who possesses the final phrase?
A monk asked: 'What is the final phrase of Guotai? The Master said: 'O Venerable Sir..."* *(Note: The source text appears to be truncated at this point.)*
Lei asked, "Why was he born so late? He then returned to the abbot’s quarters and asked, "What is Vairocana?
The Master said, "I and my elder brother are both your disciples. Lei asked, "I do not ask about when Bodhidharma came; what is the matter of the future?"
The Master said, "I personally met King Liang. [The King] asked, "What is it like when an ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said, "An ancient mirror.
[The King] asked, "What is it like after it has been polished? The Master said, "An ancient mirror."
Chan Master Daohi of Shengshan Bailong Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of that same prefecture. He ascended the hall and said:
"Without even lifting a foot—who is it whose majestic light shines? Do you understand? If you say it is your own place of arrival, it has been so from the very beginning;
yet, let me tell you, there is no connection. A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said: "From where have you come? The monk asked: "How is it..."

"This is the great purport of the Buddha-dharma. The Master said, "You should have prostrated three times already. The monk asked, "Without holding back what has come before, I ask the Master to speak directly.
The Master said, "I can. The monk asked, "What is the true and correct Way? The Master said, "Riding a donkey while searching for a donkey.

The monk asked, "I request the Master to answer the 'no guest and no host' dialogue. The Master said, "I remember it from years past. The monk asked, "How about right now? The Master said, "It is not."
[The Master] was merely deaf, yet also had failing eyesight. A questioner asked, "When mind is forgotten and body is merged, what is it like?
The Master said, "What else would you see in a dream? A questioner asked, "I, this student, intend to pose a question; I request the Master to provide a judgment. The Master said, "I will not judge.

The questioner asked, "Why do you not judge? The Master said, "You must know that I am a master craftsman. A questioner asked, "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; I request the Master to proclaim the essence of the School."

The Teacher said, "Rarely do I encounter one who listens. [The student] asked, "Without involving the tips of the lips, I beg the Master for instruction. The Teacher said, "Bring forth that which does not involve the tips of the lips.
[The student] said, "If it is so, then all living beings will have something to rely upon. The Teacher said, "Do not speak idle words. [The student] asked.
"Please, Preceptor, answer with a word of vital spirit. The Master said, "Bring paper and brush; I shall write it down for you to take away.
He asked, "What is the 'mouth of thought'? The Master said, "Come out and I will tell you. He said, "I have just now come out. The Master said, "How many people have you deceived thus far?"
Chan Master Huìqiú Jìzhào of Ānguó Yùàn in Fúzhōu (also known as Zhōngtǎ) was a native of Pútían in Quánzhōu.

Within the quarters of Xuánshā, he was foremost among those who engaged in inquiry and examination. He once asked, "What is the primary moon? Xuánshā replied, "What would you do with that moon of yours?
From this, the Master attained awakening. In the second year of the Kaiping era of the Liáng dynasty, when Xuánshā was about to pass away, the Military Governor of Mǐn...
The Wang family sent their son to inquire after his illness and requested that he secretly indicate who would succeed him in preaching the Dharma. The Śramaṇa said, "Qiuzi shall obtain it.
King Wenyi silently took note of this final instruction and then asked Drum Mountain (Gushan), "Who is fit to hold the seat of the Dharma at Wolong?
Drum Mountain named twelve venerable elders from the city who possessed the full eye of the Dharma, all of whom were capable of appearing in the world [to teach]. King Wenyi likewise...
[The Master] remained silent. On the day of the opening of the hall, officials and monks gathered together at the Dharma assembly. The King suddenly asked the assembly, "Who is the Venerable Qiú?
Thereupon, the people pointed out the Master. The Wang family immediately requested him to ascend the seat.
After a long while, the Master said: "Do not resent its solitude; do not say it is inadequate. Since its boundaries are not yet fully understood, how can one attempt to deliberate upon it?"
I habitually use its resonance; I merely strike it once or twice to assist others in triggering their realization.

As for seeking someone throughout the ten directions of the world who could serve as my companion, such a person cannot be found. A monk asked, "By what skillful means can one enter directly into the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Entering is itself the skillful means. The monk asked, "From which mountain does the cloud arise? From which ravine does the wind come?"

[The Master] said, "Exerting one's full effort in all actions, one does not depart from the central stupa. He ascended the hall and said, "This matter of porridge and rice here is for the sake of you, my brothers, whom I proclaim;
yet it is ultimately impermanent. If you wish to attain the essential, it is rather the mountains, rivers, and the great earth that reveal it to you.
Since that Way is eternal, it can also lead to ultimate realization. As for those who enter through the gate of Mañjuśrī, everything..."
The unconditioned—earth, wood, tiles, and rubble—will assist you in triggering the catalyst.

If you enter through the gate of Avalokiteśvara, all sounds and voices—even those of frogs and earthworms—will assist you in triggering the catalyst. If you enter through the gate of Samantabhadra, you will arrive without moving a step.
These three gates of skillful means are shown to you, like using a single broken chopstick to stir the waters of the great ocean, causing them to...

Those fish and dragons know that water is their life. Do you understand? If one lacks the eye of wisdom to examine this with discernment, then no matter how many hundreds of clever and ingenious methods you employ, they will not lead to the ultimate realization.
A student asked, "I have recently entered the monastic community, yet I do not understand my own fundamental matter. I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master pointed at him with his staff and said, "Do you understand? The student replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "I am acting for you in this very way."

This instead results in suppressing and demeaning others. Do you still understand? If we consider the matter from the perspective of one’s own person, as for that which has been there from the beginning, it has never been lacking—whether for those newly entering the monastic community or for the Buddhas of the past. It is like the water of the great ocean:
from the first moment of birth until their final death, all fish and dragons receive and use this water with complete equality. Question: This is the unerring orthodox tradition.
"Please, Master, speak the truth. The Master said, "Then you shall speak for me. The monk asked, "What if there is someone who does not understand?
The Master said, "Wait for that one who does not understand to come. The monk asked, "Do the Buddhas have a teacher? The Master said, "They do.
The monk asked, "Who is the teacher of the Buddhas? The Master said, "No one can recognize him. After sitting in the hall for a long time, a monk came forward and bowed.
The Master said, "Do not let the skull be crushed. A monk came to inquire of him, saying, "Set aside your attendants, and I ask to see you.
The Master said, "Try to see by raising your eyebrows. The monk asked, "What about when it is not like that? The Master said, "He has gone to the north of the mountain."
A monk asked, "What is the matter regarding the ancestral vehicle? The Master remained silent for a long time. The monk asked again, and the Master immediately shouted him out.
Another asked, "What is the matter at the top of Dayu Ridge? The Master said, "I suspect you are unable to take this on. The monk asked, "How much does it weigh?

The Master said, "For one such as you, even through kalpas of time, there is nothing to be done. The Master then questioned the head of the monastery: "As for what the former master said, 'All... (The text here is incomplete).
"The worlds of the ten directions are the true human body. Do you still see the Sangha hall? Liao said, "Master, do not let your eyes deceive you.
The Master said, "The former master has passed away, yet his flesh is still warm."
A monk asked Master Cheng Chan of Nantai on Mount Heng, "I request the Master to proclaim the fundamental principle of Xuansha.
The Master said, "Where did you receive this news? The monk asked, "What is your way of extending grace to others? The Master said, "When one meets a person, do not lose yourself.

The monk asked, "When the pond is clear and the moon appears, what kind of realm is that? The Master said, "It is none of your business. The monk said, "If I am merely asking for instruction, why should it be a hindrance? The Master—
[The student] said, "Searching for the moon in the pond, it cannot be found. He asked, "Why is there a fish-scale pattern [on the ground] at a distance of four finger-widths from the earth?
The Master said, "There is a 'measure of the holy' (ārya-pramāṇa) present. [The student] asked, "For whom was this measure established? The Master said, "It was not established for the holy ones."
Chan Master Mingfa of Luofeng in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Every person is fully endowed with it; every person manifests it.
How can one blame this mountain monk? Take care! A monk asked: "The mark of the cessation of all dharmas cannot be proclaimed in words.
What is the mark of cessation? The Master said: "Question and answer are both complete. The monk said: "If that is so, then the *tathatā* dharma-realm is without..."
"There is no 'other' apart from oneself. The Master said, "This needlessly causes people to grieve. A question was asked: "How was it before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?

The Master said, "His virtue was so profound that ghosts and spirits revered him. The questioner asked: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "His entire being is holy and unfathomable. A question was asked: [The text ends here.]
"What is the single phrase of Luofeng? The Master said, "Suffering. The questioner asked, "What is the person of original nature? The Master said, "Regretful;
the realm of pine and vines is perilous."
A monk asked the Master of Sleeping Dragon Mountain in Quanzhou, “What is bodhi as it meets the eye? The Master drove him away with his staff.
The monk then ran off. The Master called out, “Stop! Stop! When you encounter a true adept in the future, bring this up for him to examine.

He ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said, “I have lived on this mountain for thirty years and have acquired its strength. At that time, a monk asked, “Master, what have you acquired from it?”
"Physical strength. The Master said, "Crossing the stream, crossing the ridge; leaning east, leaning west. (Zhaogqing said, "I do not speak in this way. A monk asked, "How would you speak, Teacher?")
[He] rejoiced that [the Master] walked by leaning on his staff as it touched the ground).
Zen Master Guangxu Zhide of Yunfeng on Mount Tiantai ascended the hall and said: "It is simply that sentient beings do not realize what they use every day.
It is like the three thousand great chiliocosms, the sun, moon, and stars, and the Yangtze, Yellow, Huai, and Ji Rivers—all of these..."
Sentient beings enter from one pore into another pore; yet the pores do not become smaller, nor do the worlds become larger.
The beings therein neither perceive nor know this. To make it easy to understand: even the daily activities of the Venerable Elder are likewise unknown to him.
Once, a monk asked: "By day the monk carries the image, by night the image carries the monk. What is the meaning of this? The Master said:
"Preceptor, have you not come from the tea hall?
The hermit Qirú of Mount Dazháng in Fuzhou was a native of that very province. He had long harbored solitary integrity and was determined to explore the Way of the Patriarchs.
Having entered the chamber of Xuánshā, he attained a brilliant realization of its profound essence. Xuánshā recorded this, saying: "Your meditation has already transcended the ordinary. Thus...
Later, he did not even have a single person to attend him. From that time on, the Master no longer sought to gather disciples nor kept any young attendants.
He lived in seclusion on Mount Xiaojie, hollowing out a large, decayed cypress tree to serve as a small hermitage, just large enough to accommodate his body.
Whenever traveling monks arrived, he would respond to their inquiries as they came; he gave no fixed instructions. A monk asked, "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them?"
The Master said, "When the tally arrives, it is executed. The monk asked, "In that case, one would be taken away by birth and death. The Master said, "A-ya, a-ya.
The monk asked, "What was the meaning of holding the *khakkhara* (staff) in India? The Master picked up his staff, struck the ground with it, and shook it.
The monk asked, "I do not yet understand what the significance of this is. The Master said, "This is Zhang’s beating. As the monk was about to offer further words, [the Master struck him].
The Master struck him with his staff. A monk asked Zen Master Yuntai Qin, "What is the true word?
Qin said, "Namo Buddhāya. The Master replied differently, "What? What? The two elders Qinghuo and Chongxu had heard of the Master’s reputation but had never met him.
One day they went to visit him together and found him gathering chestnuts. Qinghuo asked, "O Way-farer, as for the hermitage..."
"Where is the Master? The Master said, "From where have you come? He replied, "From down the mountain. The Master said, "How did you manage to get here?
He asked, "What place is this? The Master gestured for him to sit and said, "Come, have some tea down there."

The two officials were then inspecting this master. They proceeded to his hermitage and found his lofty discourse deeply compelling. Sitting in conversation by his side, they did not realize that night had fallen.

Suddenly, they saw jackals and tigers rushing to the front of the hermitage, yet they naturally circled about him in a state of docility. Thereupon, Huo composed a poem, saying: "His journey is no ordinary journey; who knows the depths of his intent to go or stay?
A single meal remains unsated, yet ten thousand households find no peace in their lives. It was not... [the text here is incomplete].
The Way is difficult to subdue; an empty fist cannot contend with it. Where the dragon roars and clouds arise, he lets out two or three idle sighs.
The two masters sought out Dazhang Mountain and established a hermitage, inviting the Master to reside there. Seated alone in both places, he passed away after fifty-two years.
On the day Chan Master Yongxing Shenglü of Mount Liánhuá in Fuzhou was invited by the King of Min to open the hall for formal teaching, before ascending the seat, he stood before it and said:
"Great King and assembly, listen! There has already been a true and authentic proclamation.
This entire assembly has heard it; how could there be anyone who has not heard? If there were anyone who had not heard, we would be deceiving one another."
Only then did he ascend the seat. A monk asked, "The Great King has invited the Master to appear in the world; I do not know how this present assembly compares to that on Vulture Peak.
The Master said, "It penetrates the ancient and transmits to the present. The monk asked, "What is the Master’s house style?
The Master said, "Within a single hair-tip, the entire realm of sands appears; the sun and moon manifest therein."
When the Venerable Master Jing of Tiantai Guoqing Temple first encountered Xuansha, who was addressing the assembly, saying,
"If you all can for a lifetime act as if you had lost your parents, I guarantee that you will attain thorough penetration," the Master took up these previous words and asked:
"Just as it is said in the teachings: 'One must not use the mind of known objects to fathom the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed knowledge and vision.
But how about this? [Zhao]zhou] said: 'Suppose you have thoroughly investigated and exhausted the very root of that mind of known objects; would you then be able to fathom it? "

The Master entered the Path through faith from this point on. Later, he resided at Tiantai for over thirty years without descending the mountain. He extensively mastered the Three Studies (Tripiṭaka), and his conduct was solitary and peerless.

Beyond his practice of meditative stillness, he constantly perused the Dragon Canon (the Buddhist scriptures). He was revered by those both far and near, who called him the "Elder Great Stillness" (Dajing Shouzuo).
Once, someone asked him: "Disciple, whenever I sit in meditation at night, my thoughts fly about in confusion; I do not yet understand how to subdue them."
"Regarding this method, I pray that you will deign to instruct me. The Master said: "Suppose, when sitting at ease during the quiet of night, your thoughts fly about in confusion.
Take this very mind that is flying about and investigate the place from which it flies. When you investigate and find no place, then where does the thought of confusion exist?
Turn back and investigate the investigating mind itself; then where is the mind that is able to investigate? Furthermore, the wisdom that is able to illuminate is fundamentally empty."
The objects of conditions are also quiescent. That which is quiescent yet not-quiescent is because there is no person who can bring about quiescence.
That which illuminates yet does not illuminate is because there is no object to be illuminated. When both object and wisdom are quiescent, the mind and its deliberations are at ease.

One does not seek out branches externally, nor does one dwell in meditative concentration internally. When these two paths are both extinguished, the single nature is serene. This is the essential path for returning to the source.
The Master, having observed the meaning of "illusion" within the teachings, composed a verse and asked the assembly of students:

"If all dharmas are like illusions, then committing various transgressions and evils should entail no fault. Why, then, do the actions one performs not perish, such that one must rely on the Buddha’s compassion to provide guidance and transformation?
At that time, the Elder Xiaojing replied: "An illusory person creates illusory Mount Cakravāḍa."

Illusory karma can summon illusory objects of affliction; failing to understand that illusions arise from illusion, one undergoes various illusory sufferings. To realize that what is like an illusion is itself unconditioned (asaṃskṛta).
Both the two venerable elders of Jingzhai passed away at their original mountain monastery.
Chan Master Daokuang of Zhaoqing Monastery in Quanzhou was a successor of Chan Master Changqing Leng; he was a native of Chaozhou.

When Master Leng first resided at Zhaoqing, the Master entered the inner quarters to attend him and served as the head of the kitchen (*tongtou*). He frequently engaged in conversation with the assembly of monks. One day, Changqing saw him.
Fengqing said, "What are you doing all day long, fussing and fumbling with your mouth? The Master replied, "If one does not work for a day, one does not eat for a day.

Fengqing said, "In that case, you are sharpening your bow and misdirecting your arrows. The Master said, "I am specifically waiting for Weichi to come. Fengqing asked, "After Weichi has arrived, what then?
The Master said, "I will have his sinews and bones spread across the ground, and his eyes bulge out. Fengqing... [ceased speaking].
He then departed. When Qing was summoned, the Master succeeded him in the position of abbot. He ascended the hall and said: "To realize it before the sound is to betray one's entire life;
to seize the opportunity after the phrase is to utterly miss the essence of the Way. Why is this so? O Great Assembly, tell me: how should one have acted from the very beginning?
Furthermore, I say: Zhaoqing has spoken it all at once for you; do you still understand where it lands?"
"Ma. At that time, a monk stepped forward and said, "The assembly has all dispersed at once; does this still accord with your Master’s intention?
The Master said, "I would give you twenty blows of the staff. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Though you have the intent of the blind turtle, you lack the progress of the bright moon.
The monk asked, "What is the progress of the bright moon? The Master said, "This is the intent of the blind turtle. [The monk] asked again.
"What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "Neither practicing nor not practicing. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West's coming?
The Master said, "A mosquito on an iron ox. The monk asked, "What is the sword in the scabbard? The Master remained silent for a long time. The monk was at a loss.
The Master said, "You must also feel grateful to Zhaogqing before you can understand. The monk asked, "What is the single phrase that upholds the school? The Master said, "No."
"You have fallen into a state of dull attachment that invites calamity. The monk bowed and rose. The Master spoke again: "You must not fall into a state of dull attachment that invites calamity.
I entrust you with this: what is the single phrase that upholds the School? The monk was speechless. The Master asked:

"When Mañjuśrī was struck by the sword, he did not acknowledge it at that moment—how was that? The Master said: "He was not yet a masterful man. The monk asked: "What is a masterful man? The Master said: "It is."
“You have fallen into error,” [the Master] said. [The monk] asked, “What is the家风 (family style) of Zhaoqing?
The Master said, “It is better to be pure and poor and enjoy oneself than to be turbid and wealthy and have much anxiety. [The monk] asked, “What is the single thread of Nanquan’s path?

The Master said, “I do not refuse to tell you, but I fear that once you have compared it, you will go on comparing further. [The monk] asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, “Seven topsy-turvy turns.”
The Eight Perversions. Question: "The faculties and thoughts of this student are slow and hesitant; I beg the Master to exercise his compassion and open a single path for me.
The Master said: "This is the 'old woman’s heart' (compassionate concern). He said: "I have received your compassionate grace through the breaking open of the Flower of Compassion (*karuṇāpuṣpa*).
As for the ancestral vehicle (*zōngchéng*) from above, how is it? The Master said: "It must be so that you ask in person for it to be attained. Question: "Where has the monk come from?"
The Master said, "Bring me some split firewood. The monk said, "Is there anything that cannot be split? The Master said, "There is.
The monk asked, "What is it that cannot be split? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "If you cannot say it, ask me and I will tell you.
The monk asked, "What is it that cannot be split? The Master said, "This would deceive people to death. Then the Master picked up his alms-bag.

He asked a monk, "Tell me, how much is it worth? The monk had no reply. (Nanquan Rouru [Guizong Rou] spoke on his behalf, saying: "Leave it to others to increase its price. Because the earth shook, a monk asked:
"Is there also one who is unmoving? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is this unmoving one?
The Master said, "It moves from the east and returns to the west. [The monk] asked, "When the rain of Dharma falls everywhere, is there any place that is not moistened? The Master said:
[The monk] said, “There is. [The monk] asked, “What is the place where there is no moisture? The Master said, “Water cannot wet it.

[The monk] asked, “What is the profoundly deep place of Zhaoying? The Master said, “I will drown you along with it. [The monk] asked, “What is one who is within the nine-layered city? The Master said:
"Do you all understand and hear this together? While ascending the hall, the assembly crowded around the Dharma seat. The Master said, "There is nothing here.

Why do you all trouble yourselves so much, jostling and pressing one another? If you even conceive a thought, there is already no connection. To go further, door to door, would be ten thousand miles away.
Now that you have come up here, each of you must exert your full attention; let us settle this all at once. At Qingzhao Monastery.
"I cast this to all of you; is it well? He then asked, "Can you receive it? The assembly had no reply.

Look at those ancients—only one or two were so swift that as soon as they saw it, they took it away on their backs. That was quite something. If there were such a person here..."
It was not merely that he provided the four types of offerings; even having the ground made of lapis lazuli and the walls of white silver would not yet be considered noble.
Śakra led the way before him, and Brahmā followed behind; he churned the great river into cream and curd, and transformed the great earth into gold.
"Even this is not yet sufficient. You have merely attained such as this; there is still one more step remaining. Do you understand it thoroughly? Take care.
A monk asked Chan Master Baoci Xiaowu of Baoen Monastery in Wuzhou: "The student is at the beginning of his practice; I pray that the Master will show me a way of entry.

"Do not sound out of turn. [A monk] asked, "What is the house style of Baoen? The Master said, "I know that you, Dali, have been with the assembly for but a short time.

The monk asked, "Why is it like this? The Master said, "How could one possibly be so constrained? A monk asked, "What is the sword of Mañjuśrī? The Master said, "I do not know.

I wonder what the meaning of the ancients was? The Master rebuked him, saying, "If it were so, it would be out of order. The Master then said, "Your words have fallen into error."

The Master said, "Yanping belongs to Jianzhou. [The monk] said, "In that case, one would lose both body and life.
The Master said, "The tide in the Qiantang River."
Chan Master Congxin of Cui Peak in Chuzhou ascended the hall and said, "I shall not spread my seat further. Take care!

When Chan Master Mingyuan of Jueiling in Xiangzhou first visited Changqing, Changqing asked, "What is your name?

The Master then gave this instruction. Later, while sitting by the fire, a monk asked, "When not a single dharma stands before one and application is without deficiency, what then?

On the day of the opening of the hall at Longhua Temple in Hangzhou, Chan Master Yanguo Shixiang Degui addressed the assembly, saying:

"I grant you thirty blows. A monk asked, "I have heard that Chaojue has a 'key to the lock' (suǒkǒu jué).

The monk said, "If there were a specific place [to point to], I would be failing the Master. The Master said, "I only fear you cannot distinguish the refined from the coarse. He asked, "As for what is called 'preaching'..."
"The Dharma should be taught according to the Dharma. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "What doubt or error is there? Question:
"What was the intent behind the ancients' 'facing the wall'? The Master struck him. Question: "Without relying on verbal explanations, I ask the Master for the direct path. The Master said:

Chan Master Zhimo of Yunshan Fozhai Monastery in Wenzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the house style of Fozhai?
The Master said, "When seeing off guests, one does not go more than three paces; when inviting guests, it is done only before the thatched hall.

It is not for the sake of sightseeing through prefectures and counties, nor for seeking out famous mountains and sacred sites; it is surely for the sake of this one great matter.
Now, I wish for you all to bring forth a message of realization through the inquiry into your own fundamental nature.
Yunshan dares to bear witness to this; not only will Yunshan bear witness, but even the Zen groves and Buddha-lands shall bear witness as well. Is there anyone...?

Auspicious omen. The Master said: "When not a single thing arises, the whole body is revealed; who knows the radiance before one's eyes? He was asked: "What is the single phrase that points directly?

Manifest before one’s eyes, pervading heaven and earth; the myriad phenomena of the universe are the very style of one’s own house. Buddhas and sentient beings are fundamentally without distinction;

Chan Master Yican Kaimei of Wugu Mountain in Quzhou was the son of the Xu family of Wuxing.

On the evening before his birth in the third year of the Qianfu era of the Tang dynasty, a wondrous fragrance filled the room and a crimson light appeared like a painting. During the Guangqi era, he accompanied his father while stationed in Xin’an;

though his father forcibly arranged a marriage for him, the Master did not desire it and subsequently traveled to various regions. Having attained a karmic resonance with Jingqing, he returned to visit his father.

The Master’s mother then established a separate dwelling to the south of the city wall to fulfill the Master’s aspiration. Beside this dwelling was the shrine of Minister Chen, where there was a statue of Chan Master Lin.

When the Master went to pay his respects, he lost sight of where the Master had gone. Later, while the Prefect was performing a sacrifice at the shrine, he saw the Master in meditative absorption (*samādhi*) amidst a thicket of bamboo behind the temple;
ants were gnawing at his robes and withered leaves buried him up to his thighs. Some have said that this was [the Master].
Xu Zhen was the son of Jiang. From this samādhi, he would emerge and enter it at will.

Chan Master Nü of Zihu did not yet know the depth of the Master’s realization and asked, "The state of concentration you dwell in is merely that of the Hīnayāna. At that time, the Master was just drinking tea;
he lifted up his tea bag and said, "Is this great or small? Nü was struck with awe. He subsequently went to visit De of Tangshan on Mount Kuocang.
Master Yan asked, "What is your surname? He replied, "My surname is Xu. Yan asked, "Who permitted you [to become a monk]? He replied, "There is no distinction.
Yan silently recognized his potential and subsequently granted him the tonsure and ordination. Once, he ordered him to pick peaches; ten days passed without his returning.

When Yan went to search for him, he saw the master leaning against a rock while plucking peaches, poised in meditative concentration (*samādhi*). Yan snapped his fingers to rouse him from it. Later, during the Kaiyun era, he traveled to Jianglang Rock, where he beheld...
In the stone grotto, he said to his disciple Huixing, "I shall enter meditative absorption within this space;

you must stack stones to block the entrance and do not harbor thoughts of me. Huixing followed these instructions. The following year, Huixing, feeling that his teacher was aged, went to open the grotto to look upon him.
His hair was white and fell over his shoulders, yet his chest remained warm. He slowly arose from his concentration with no change in his countenance. [He] returned to Wugu to attend [the Master].

When Minister Shangsheng Gong was stationed in Xin’an, he ordered the monk Shou Rong, a scholar of the Abhidharma, to interrogate Master Fu regarding the characteristics of meditative concentration (*samādhi*).
The Master did not engage him in debate; Rong, however, held him in low esteem. At that time, the people of Xin’an vied with one another to paint portraits of the Master and honored them.
Everyone obtained śarīra relics. Consequently, Rong felt ashamed and submitted; he prostrated before the image to apologize for his transgressions and also obtained śarīra relics.
He sighed, saying: "From this day forward, I shall not dare to measure [the Dharma] with my shallow understanding. King Qian Zhongyi was moved by the Master’s appearance in a dream;

he dispatched an envoy to have the image painted and brought back. It happened that the King suffered from an eye ailment; when he unfurled the image and paid homage, it appeared exactly as seen in the dream, and śarīra relics rained down accordingly, [healing] his eye ailment.

He was suddenly cured. Consequently, he was granted the honorary title "Kaiming" (Illuminator). When he composed verses of praise, thousands of precious vessels and ritual implements were offered to him.

At the beginning of the Duan-gong era, Emperor Taizong, having heard of the Master’s power of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), issued an edict for his native prefecture to accord him special honors and dispatch him to the imperial court. The Master declined the summons with all his might.

The Sangha arrived again with an imperial decree, specifically ordering that he be conveyed by palanquin to have an audience in the private hall. The Emperor commanded him to sit and bestowed tea upon him, inquiring about his meditative concentration (*dhyāna*).

His responses were concise and exhaustive, deeply resonating with the Emperor's intent. He requested leave to return home, but was again summoned for an audience; having obtained permission to return to the mountain, the roads were blocked by the crowds of carriages escorting him.
In the first year of the Chunhua era, he passed away. He was one hundred and fifteen years of age and fifty-seven years since his ordination (*varṣa*). His remains were cremated.

The white light belonged to the heavens; the śarīra were of five colors. The people of the land fashioned images from his bones, which remain to this day; when the various prefectures and districts pray for rain or fine weather, they receive answers as swift as an echo.

The Master said, "Before the hour of the rat today," and having finished speaking, he passed away forever.
Master Ming of Xianzong Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Fortunately, there is such a tradition of our school; why do you not resolutely carry it forward?
If you can succeed to it, you will not be within the three realms. If you were outside the three realms, you would destroy them;
if you were within the three realms, you would be obstructed by them. To be neither obstructed nor destroyed—this is to transcend the three realms. This is it."
"Transcending the triple world—penetrating thus, one is fit to be a seed of the Buddha-dharma; humanity and the heavens shall have cause for reliance.
At that time, a monk asked: "If grasping the clouds does not depend on the power of wind and thunder, how can one pass through the body amidst the surging waves? The Master said:
"How can you abandon the root to pursue the branches?"
Chan Master Xiang of Anguo Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall. After a long silence, he cried out: "This is truly groundless! Nevertheless, there is no choice but to do so.
If among you there are those who have not yet seen through this, I shall further open up a skillful means.
Do you understand? At that time, a monk asked: "Without involving skillful means, I beg the Master to bestow his compassion. The Master said: "You ask, and I answer. Then—
“This is a skillful means. Question: “The manifestation of form in accordance with beings is like the moon in water. What is the moon? The Master raised his whisk. The monk said:
“Why did the ancients say that the moon in water has no form? The Master said: “What do you see? Question: “What is the matter within the School of the Lineage (Zongcheng)?
The Master said: “After the Huai army has dispersed. Question: “What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: “After the Huai army has dispersed.”
The Master said: "It is difficult to deceive the eyes of the multitude.

Chan Master Shuilong Pu was a dharma successor of Chan Master Qinghuo of Baofu Monastery in Zhangzhou. He was a native of Fuzhou; from his youth, he was intelligent and quick-witted, and he paid homage at Drum Mountain (Gushan).
The National Teacher (Guoshi) shaved his head and received full ordination. Later, he visited Master Ru of Dazhang Mountain (the dialogue is recorded in the chapter on Master Ru).
Subsequently, he studied under Shuilong (Sleeping Dragon). Shuilong asked, "Where have you come from, Layman Huo? Have you attained awakening yet?
He replied, "I once visited Master Dazhang and gained a point of conviction. Thereupon, Shuilong ascended the hall, gathered the assembly, and called out, "Layman Huo, come forth!"

"Come forward. Burn incense before the assembly and speak of your realization; the old monk will provide you with witness. The Master stepped out from the assembly and held up the incense, saying, "The incense has already been offered.

As for realization—whether it is realized or not? Long was greatly pleased and granted him permission. He ascended the hall and said, "I, this mountain monk, shall now act as a mediator for all of you.
Those who agree, remain silent; those who do not agree, speak. After a long pause, he said, "Agreement and..."
"Inharmonious! It all depends on this very moment. This mountain monk carries a few matters with me; take care. A monk asked, "What is it like when a poor household suffers a robbery?
The Master said, "He cannot empty the bottom of the house. The monk asked, "Why can he not empty the bottom of the house? The Master said, "The thief is a member of the family.
The monk asked, "If he is a member of the family, why does he instead become a family thief? The Master said, "Internally..."
[The student] said, "Since there is no correspondence, the external cannot act [upon it]. The Master said, "When suddenly seized and defeated, what then?
The student said, "When seized and defeated, where does the merit reside? The Master said, "Even the reward has never been heard of. The student said, "If so, then one toils but achieves no merit.
The Master said, "Merit is not non-existent; it is accomplished but not dwelt upon. The student said, "Since it is already accomplished..."
[The monk] Gong asked, “Why do you not remain [in the world]? The Master said, “Have you not heard it said: ‘Peace was originally brought about by the generals;
yet we do not allow the generals to witness that peace’? Another asked, “What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, “The Hu man weeps; the Han man grieves.”

The Master suddenly left the assembly, intending to enter the mountains to await his passing. He then left behind this verse: "Let the people of the world cease speaking of the difficulty of the road;
The path of birds and the sheep’s gut are but a few inches apart. Take care, O water by the banks of the Zhu Creek! You shall return to the vast ocean, and I shall return to the mountains.
He then went to Guihu to establish a hermitage. Not long after, he said to his disciples: "After my passing, you shall give my remains as alms."
"Do not place [my remains] among the various insects and ants. Having spoken these words, he entered Mount Hutou, sat upon a flat rock, and passed away solemnly.
His disciples, following his final instructions, kept him for seven days; yet, in the end, there was no place where insects or ants had come to devour him.
Thereupon, he was cremated, and the ashes were scattered throughout the forests and fields.
A monk asked National Teacher Jinlun, the Dharma heir of Chan Master Jinlun, "What is the first phrase of Jinlun? The Master said, "An obtuse fellow."
Question: "What is the single arrow of the golden wheel? The Master said: "It has passed. The questioner asked: "When one arrow is released at the opportune moment, who is there to meet it?
The Master said: "It is overturned."
Chan Master Zhihong Hongji of Dazhong Mountain in Dingzhou was a successor of Chan Master Baizhao Yuan. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "It is you yourself.
The monk asked, "How should one understand this? The Master said, "Do you still find fault with a bowl that has no handle? [The monk] asked, "How..."

"This is subtle and wondrous. The Master said, "The wind carries the sound of water to the pillow; the moon shifts the shadow of the mountains onto the bed. [The monk] asked, "What is the ultimate point?
The Master said, "How vexing is the moon of the three spring months; it does not equal the radiance of the nine autumn months.
[The monk] asked, "When the physical body decays, what is the indestructible Dharma-body? The Master said, "Mountain flowers bloom like brocade; the mountain stream waters are limpid."
At Lanxiang, on Mount Baima in Xiangzhou, Chan Master Xing’ai was asked by a monk, “What is the pure Dharma-body?
The Master said, “A frog at the bottom of the well swallows the moon. The monk asked, “What is the true eye of Baima? The Master said, “Looking southward.”
**The Northern Dipper.** At Zhugan Yuan in Baimiao, Anzhou, Chan Master Huichu was asked by a monk: "What is it that requires every phrase to follow the mysterious path?
The Master said: "Traveling along the road straight to Hunan. The monk asked: "What is a lion cub? The Master said: "Virtue."
Shanshi succeeded Longtan. He asked, "What is the one phrase by which you, Master, benefit people? The Master said, "I have never had any enmity with you;
this one phrase has been right here all along. Shanshi asked, "I do not know in what place it resides. The Master said, "You dull-witted fellow!"
Chan Master Qingjiao of Mount Sizhu in Qizhou was a native of the Wang family of Fuzhou.
A monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed? The Master replied, "Auspicious clouds rise by Kai-shi Cliff; the Dharma-thunder roars before Baoshou Peak.
At the end of his life, he left behind this verse: "I am eighty-eight years old; my head is covered with white hair. With dignity I remain..."
The Twin Peaks: Clearly, the moon over a thousand rivers; Huangmei propagated the ancestral teachings, and Baidiao inherited the patriarchal secret. Day after day he instructed his descendants:
"Do not allow this lineage to be severed."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhizao of Sanjiaoshan in Qizhou, "The teachings are many, yet the fundamental principle returns to a single thread.
Why does the Master speak so much of 'Zhou', 'Yu', 'Ye', and 'Zhe'? The Master said, "It is for you that I speak of 'Zhou', 'Yu', 'Ye', and 'Zhe'."
[The monk] said, "I ask the Master: what is it from antiquity to the present? The Master struck the rope-bench with his hand.
A monk asked Zen Master Puxian of Xingjiao Temple in Jinzhou, "I do not ask about the true teaching that fills the dragon palaces and overflows the ocean treasuries;
what is the Dharma transmitted outside the teachings? The Master said, "In the eyes, in the ears, in the nose. [The monk] said, "Only..."
The Master asked, "Is this so? The monk said, "What is it? The monk then gave a shout; the Master also gave a shout. The Master asked, "Where have you recently come from, monk?
He replied, "From the military camp. The Master said, "Did you encounter any bandits? He replied, "I captured some today. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows of the staff."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhenguan of Sanjiaoshan in Qizhou: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed?
The Master said: "Suddenly, when the right command is issued, one immediately sees [him] descend the hall steps."
A monk asked Zen Master Xingchong of Mount Taiyang in Yingzhou, "What is the inexhaustible treasury? The Master remained silent for a long while.
The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Come closer. As soon as the monk drew near, the Master said, "Go."

The Dharma successor of Chan Master Huanglong Ji of the eighth generation under Qingyuan was Chan Master Shanzhao of Zigai in Luoyang. A monk asked, "What is it like when one attains life within death? The Master said, "Embrace."

The blade scrapes the bone, its smoke熏 (xūn) the heavens and earth; amidst the searing heat of the funeral pyre, one seeks rebirth within the coffin. Question: "What is it like when one dies immediately upon being born?
The Master said: "Fortunately, the awakening is swift."
A monk asked Zen Master Huanglong Jida of Meizhou, "What is the *nā* (monk’s robe)? The Master said, "The needle has passed; the thread does not return.

The monk asked, "What is the *pai* (cloak)? The Master said, "Laid horizontally across the four worlds; hung vertically to cover the single universe. The monk asked, "When the Way arrives in full measure, what then?
The Master said, "If you want soup, I give you soup; if you want rice, I give you rice. [The monk] asked, "How did Huanglong emerge? The Master said, [as before].
"World-Honored One, when the garuḍas fill the sky and fly about, what then? The Master said, "I ask you, garuḍa: have you been able to eat your fill?
When Zen Master Zao-shu was in his second term of residence, he asked a monk, "Where did you set out from? The monk replied, "From Min Province. The Master said, "Excellent!"
“Ah! the monk said. “I thank you for your instruction. The Master said, “What a pity! The monk bowed. The Master said, “When I speak thus, where does it fall?
The monk was speechless. The Master said, “He has no wound; do not inflict one upon him. A monk visited.
The Master asked, “Before you arrived here, where did you establish yourself and sustain your life? The monk joined his palms and stepped forward. The Master—
The monk also joined his palms and stepped forward to stand side by side with the Master. The monk said, "I have not yet reached this point; with whom does the Master stand side by side?
The Master pointed behind him and said, "Is it not he? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "You deceive yourself alone, and you also deceive me.
The monk prostrated himself. The Master said, "This is truly deceiving yourself. Later, while the monk was hoeing the ground, he saw the Master.
When the monk arrived, he was not certain [of his conduct]. The Master said, "Having seen whom have you become so uncertain? The monk replied, "I saw the Master but did not inquire after him;

my ritual protocol was incomplete. The Master asked, "In that case, you have failed me, old monk. The monk returned and reported this to the Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera), saying, "The Master has been quite formidable lately.
The Head Seat asked, "In what way? The monk recounted the previous conversation. The Head Seat said, "The Master has been quite formidable lately..."
This may be called being earnest for others. Upon hearing this, the Master struck the Head Seat seven blows.

The Seat said, "I have spoken thus; I have committed no fault. Why do you strike me so recklessly? The Master replied, "In vain have you consumed so much of my salt and sauce. He struck him another seven blows.
As a monk was taking his leave, the Master asked him, "If you go to various places and someone asks you about the Dharma and the Way here at my monastery—"
"How will you respond? he asked. The monk said, "I shall speak when you ask. The Master said, "Where is there a Buddha without a mouth?
The monk said, "Even this is difficult. The Master held up his whisk and said, "Do you see it?

The monk said, "Where is there a Buddha without eyes? The Master said, "Even this is difficult. The monk circumambulated the meditation seat once and departed. The Master said, "You are truly capable."
As he was about to respond, the monk gave a shout. The Master said, "I do not recognize you. The monk said, "What is the use of recognition?
The Master struck the meditation seat three times.
A monk asked Zen Master Cheng of Xuandu Mountain in Xingyuan Prefecture, "I am delighted to have come to the abbot’s quarters; what is the style of your house?
The Master said, "The western wind opens the morning dew; the bright moon is right in the sky. The monk asked, "How do you provide salvation? The Master said:
On the Golden Cock Tower, a drum struck once. [A monk] asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "Nothing is like it.
When the Monk of Black Water in Jiazhou first visited Huanglong, he asked, "What is it like when snow covers the reeds?
Huanglong said, "Fierce! The Master said, "Not fierce. Huanglong said again, "Fierce! The Master said again, "Not fierce. Huanglong—
He struck him. At this, the Master attained realization and immediately prostrated himself.
A monk asked Zen Master Huanglong Zizhao of Ezhou, “What is the fundamental source of all Buddhas? The Master said:
"What is the source of this very question? [The monk] said, "In that case, all Buddhas would be no different.
The Master said, "At Yanping, the sword has already become a dragon; yet there are still those who seek its bottom by marking the boat."

A monk asked Chan Master Changfu Da of Meizhou, "When a student comes to question you, you respond; but when no one asks, what is your intention? The Master said, "I thank my elder brother for pointing this out.
The monk asked, "I do not ask about the original source; what is the matter of today? The Master said, "This question of yours, elder brother, is excellent.

The monk said, "What is it like when the student does not understand? The Master said: *Note: The final response of the Master is left as "師曰" (The Master said) in the source text, as the specific words are not provided.*

[The Master] said, "You may deceive me if you wish. [The monk] asked, "In this country there is a precious sword; who has seen it? The Master said, "It is not easy for you, elder brother, to have traveled so far.
[The monk] asked, "What is the shape of this sword? The Master said, "I shall tell you whether you want to hear it or not.

[The monk] said, "Please tell me. The Master said, "It is difficult to encounter, difficult to meet. [The monk] asked, "When the stone ox lies upon the water, what is it like? The Master said, "Among the extraordinary..."

Furthermore, there is another point: false conceptualization neither floats nor sinks. A student asked, "What is it like when one proceeds in this very manner? The Master said, "The sun sets in the heavens;
earth is taken up and turned into gold."
The Realized Man Lü Yán, styled Dōngbīn, was a native of Jīngchuān. During the late Tang dynasty, he failed to pass the imperial examinations three times.
While at a wine shop in Cháng'ān, he happened to meet Zhōnglí Quán, who bestowed upon him the arts of prolonging life; from then on, no one could fathom his abilities.
He once traveled to Guīzōng on Mount Lúshān and wrote upon the wall of the bell tower: "One day of leisure and self-mastery, the six spirits are harmoniously united."
He reported that all was well. "The treasure is within the *dantian*; cease seeking the Way. Facing objects with no mind; do not inquire after Chan.

Not long after, while traveling through Huanglong Mountain, he beheld purple clouds forming a canopy and suspected there might be a person of extraordinary character. He entered to pay his respects, arriving just as Huanglong was striking the drum to ascend the hall.
Upon seeing him, Huanglong thought it must be Master Lü and, wishing to entice him forward, said in a stern voice: "There is a thief by your side!"
The man named Lü Yigan stepped forward and asked, "A single grain of millet conceals the world; within a half-measure of a cauldron, mountains and rivers are boiled.

Tell me, what is the meaning of this? Longtan pointed at him and said, "This is a corpse-guarding ghost. Lü replied, "But how can one deny that he carries the medicine of longevity and immortality within his bag?
Longtan said, "Even if he passes through eighty thousand kalpas, in the end he will still fall into emptiness and oblivion. Lü was slightly taken aback.
He brandished his flying sword to intimidate him, but the sword could not penetrate. Lü subsequently prostrated himself twice and requested instruction on the ultimate goal.
The Dragon rebuked him, saying: "I do not ask about boiling mountains and rivers within a half-measure cauldron; how is it that a world is hidden within a single grain of millet?
At these words, Lü attained sudden realization and composed a verse: "I cast away my gourd-bag and smash my zither; Now I no longer crave gold within the mercury."
"Ever since I first met Huanglong, I have realized for the first time that my previous efforts were misplaced.

Huanglong instructed him to provide protection, after which he went to visit Chan Master Jue of Zhidu on Mount Tan. [Huanglong] said: "I traveled through Shaoyang and Chenzhou and descended eastward along the Xiang River;

now I have met Master Jue. Observing his Chan study, it is brilliant and precise; his fundamental nature is pure and clean. Sitting quietly with knees pressed together, he withdraws his radiance to illuminate within."
Aside from a single robe, he has no other clothing; aside from a single bowl, he has no other food.

Having reached the far shore of birth and death and shattered the shell of afflictions, at this time when the Buddha’s dharma-garment lies silent and untransmitted, and the principles of Chan hang suspended on the verge of extinction, will it not be up to our Master to support and revive them?
I have composed this one quatrain as a record: The realized one extends his heart to save all beings; Only when the mind is vast can one truly ferry others across.

The transmission of the Dharma by the sages and worthies does not depart from the truth. I pray that the Master will explain the meaning of the "coming from the West. Among the seven patriarchs, there is currently no one [to equal them].
[This is the record of] Chan Master Mingzhao Qian, the dharma heir of [his predecessor].

Chan Master Yu of Puzhao in Wuzhou ascended the hall and said, "Thirty years from now, there will be many who, at this very point, will have their wits lost and their tongues tied.
After a long silence, he said, "Do you understand? Truly, were it not for a true lion cub..."
Strive to recognize the pivot of what has already arisen. At that time, a monk asked, "How is it when the lion has not yet emerged from its cave?
The Master said, "The various beasts are in vain. The monk asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the cave? The Master said, "Foxes are cut off for ten thousand miles.

The monk asked, "How is it when it intends to emerge but does not? The Master said, "Those who confront it perish. The monk asked, "What about matters regarding the future? The Master said, "Decisive."
As he was about to face the blade, a monk prostrated. The Master spoke this verse: "Decisive at the moment of facing the blade, The natural mechanism of the lion.
With a single snarl, he transcends the three realms; None but the Patriarchs can know it."
Chan Master Chushan of Shuangxi in Wuzhou ascended the hall and said: "If you have not yet attained thorough penetration, there is no need to present [your realization].
The ten directions of the world are vast and luminous; atop the solitary peak, the faculty of discernment shines through. There is no need to look at the Big Dipper. A monk asked:
"The spiritual peak-sword of the nine summer months—please, Master, do not reveal its edge. The Master said: "Before the golden lock was struck, why did you not ask? The monk said: "..."
