He asked, "Where have you gone, Preceptor? The Master said, "Where have you gone? He asked, "How is it when the lion has not yet emerged from its cave?
The Master said, "It shakes the earth. He asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the cave? The Master said, "It covers heaven and covers earth.
He asked, "How is it when it intends to emerge but does not? The Master said, "No one can discern it. He asked, "What about matters regarding the future? The Master said:
Even the swift hawk loses its track.
When Master Chan Master Yi of Luohan in Quzhou ascended the hall and the assembly had gathered, as soon as a monk stepped forward, the Master said, "This is not good."
The monk rose from his prostrations and asked, "I request the Master to brandish the precious sword of Longquan. The Master said, "Where would it go?
The monk said, "If that is so, then the southern face of Longxi is entirely its sharp edge. The Master said, "Put it away. The monk asked, "Without falling into past or present, please speak, Master.
The Master said, "Is this not still strange? The monk said, "It still falls into past and present. The Master said, "Do not err."
Chan Master Hongjin of Qingxi Mountain in Xiangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Luohan Chen. When he was serving as the First Seat under Dizang, one day Dizang ascended the hall.
Two monks came forward and prostrated. Dizang said, "Both of you are wrong. The two monks were speechless. After the session ended, they went to seek further instruction.
Xiu Shanzhu said, "You yourself are majestic and imposing, yet you prostrate and intend to question others;
is this not a mistake? Upon hearing this, the Master refused to assent. Xiu then asked, "I wonder, Senior Monk, what about you? The Master said:
"You are yourself deluded and dark; how can you claim to be a person? You have been practicing with such indignation. Then he went to the Abbot’s quarters to seek instruction.
Zang pointed toward the corridor and said, "The head cook has gone into the storehouse. At this, Xiu realized his error.
On another day, the Master asked the mountain master Xiu, "You clearly know the principle that birth is non-birth; why then are you carried away by birth and death? Xiu replied:
"A bamboo shoot will eventually become a bamboo pole. Now, can it still be used as a strip of bamboo? The Master said, "You shall realize this for yourself in the future.
Xiu said, "My understanding is only this much; what is the meaning of your words, Reverend?
The Master pointed and said, "This is the Director's quarters; that is the Head Cook's quarters. Xiu then prostrated in thanks. Later, after he had taken up residence, a monk—
Question: "The blind men felt the elephant and each spoke of it differently. What would happen if they suddenly encountered a person with clear vision?
The Master said: "You should simply present this to those in all quarters. While the Master was walking, the assembly of monks followed him, and he said to them:
"What sayings or phrases did the ancients have? Let us all deliberate upon them. At that time, the Elder Congyi stepped forward from the assembly, intending to ask a question.
The Master said, "This hairless donkey! At these words, Yih was suddenly enlightened.
Chan Master Xiufu Wukong of Qingliang Yuan in Shengzhou was the son of the Wang family of Beihai. He left home to become a monk in his youth and received full ordination at the age of nineteen.

He once said of himself: "If one still clings to the capacity of words to express the truth, one remains stuck on the raft; yet if one seeks to advance toward profound stillness, one must again [rely upon them]."
Fearing he was falling into emptiness, and unable to decide whether to advance or retreat, he wondered what to do after abandoning both paths.

He then went to seek out a master, following Dizang for years without reaching accord. Eventually, he fell ill and entered the Nirvana Hall. One night, Dizang went to visit him and asked, "Is the Senior Monk [Fu] at peace?
The Master replied, "I am suffering because of my karmic connection with the Master. Dizang pointed to the lantern and said:
"Do you see it? the Master said. "I see it," [Xuefeng] replied. Cang said, "Even this very thing is not a betrayal. At these words, the Master attained realization.
Later, when Xiu Shan-zhu went to pay his respects to Dizang, he said, "Throughout hundreds of kalpas and thousands of lifetimes, I have at times acted in opposition to you, O Monk.
Having come here now, I find you unwell. Dizang then held up his staff and said, "Is it not just this?"
Nor did he turn his back on them. Suddenly, the Master attained awakening. Later, he succeeded Fayan as abbot at Chongshou Monastery.

When the Prince of Jiangnan established the Qingliang Hermitage, he invited him to reside there. Entering the hall for formal discourse, [Fayan said: "When the ancient sages were first born, they immediately took seven steps."
He looked around in the four directions and said, "In the heavens above and on the earth below, I alone am the most honored. He indeed possessed such a marvelous and extraordinary skillful means.
But as for you, venerable seniors, when you were first born, what was so extraordinary? Try to bring it forth.
If you say there was nothing, you are turning your back on the truth right before our eyes. If you say there was something, how can you communicate this news? Can you?

"Do you understand? You, Venerable One, fortunately possess something extraordinary; why then do you not recognize it? Take care. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "You are a sentient being.
The monk asked, "Do you accept this or not? The Master said, "This question is asked in vain. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the [Master’s] coming from the West?
The Master said, "Tell me, does it exist here in this land? A monk asked, "What is the essential point? The Master said, "..."
The monk requested a word from the Master. The Master said, “Take care. The monk asked, “What is the Way? The Master said, “Originally there is not a single thing;
where could there be dust? The monk bowed. The Master said, “Do not misunderstand. The monk asked, “How is it that a single mote of dust enters into right concentration (*samāpatti*)?
The Master said, “Form is emptiness. The monk asked, “How do all motes of dust arise from samādhi? The Master said, “Emptiness.”
"Right within form. Question: "I do not ask about other matters; what is the single phrase for realizing emptiness? The Master said: "It is two phrases. Question:
"When Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring him flowers? The Master said: "Because he had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch. Question:
"After he saw him, why did they no longer bring flowers? The Master said: "Because he had seen the Fourth Patriarch. Question: "What is self-..."
[The monk] asked about his own affairs. The Master said, "From how many places have you come to question people? [The monk] asked, "What did the ancients attain that they were able to rest in peace?
The Master said, "What have you attained that you do not rest in peace? [The monk] asked, "What is the place where the student emerges?
The Master said, "A thousand ways cannot compare; ten thousand analogies fall short. [The monk] said, "Please, Master, speak. The Master—
[The Master] said, “In antiquity there was; in the present there is. A questioner asked, “What is the bodhi that meets the eye before the face of a deceased monk?
The Master said, “Ask the skull after it has been buried. A questioner asked, “When the venomous dragon lashes out and the myriad phenomena are all the same, what then?
The Master said, “Where did you get this kind of question? A questioner asked, “What sutra does Preceptor Zhong lecture on? He replied, “The *Dharma* [Sutra].”
Regarding the *Lotus Sūtra*, the Master said: "Wherever the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* is being preached, I shall manifest this jeweled stupa to serve as a witness.
The Venerable One asked, "When you preach, who will serve as your witness? Zhong had no reply. (Fadeng spoke on his behalf, saying: "I thank the Abbot for serving as my witness.

On the first day of the tenth month in the eighth year of the Tianfu era, he dispatched a monk to summon Chan Master Fayan. After the entrustment was completed, he also sent a letter to take leave of the National Sovereign.

On the third night, at the hour of the rat (midnight), he entered parinirvāṇa. The ruler of the country ordered that the bell be struck at the main temple when the time arrived. When the appointed moment came, the great assembly gathered in full.
The Master sat upright and exhorted the multitude, saying, "Do not waste the light and shadows [of this life]. Having finished speaking, his voice ceased and he passed into stillness.

At that time, the ruler, hearing the bell, ascended a high terrace and paid homage from afar, feeling profound grief and longing. He subsequently performed the funeral rites and the cremation (*dhyāpita*), collected the *śarīra* relics, and erected [a stūpa].
Pagoda. When Chan Master Longji Shaoshou of Fuzhou first studied under Dizang together with Fayan, he believed that what he had attained was already the ultimate.
Later, when they were traveling together toward Jianyang, during the course of their conversation on the road, Fayan suddenly asked: "The ancients said that the myriad phenomena..."

"Amidst these, the body alone is revealed. "Does this negate the myriad phenomena, or does it not negate them? The Master said, "It does not negate them. The Eye asked, "What do you mean by 'negate' or 'not negate'?
The Master was dazed and did not know how to respond. He returned to Dizang, who asked, "It has not been long since you left."
"Why have you come back? The Master said, "I have a matter that has not yet been resolved; how could I fear the journey over mountains and rivers?

Zang said, "Your journeying across so many mountains and rivers was no small feat. The Master did not understand the point and asked, "The ancients said, 'Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed.
What is the meaning of this? Zang said, "Do you say that the ancients rejected the myriad phenomena, or did they not reject them?"

"Ten thousand phenomena," the Master said. "I do not reject them. Zang said, "Then there are two. The Master was startled and fell into deep reflection, then asked in return, "I wonder, did the ancients reject the ten thousand phenomena or not?
Zang said, "What do you call 'ten thousand phenomena'? At this, the Master finally attained realization.
He took his leave of Dizang once more to go into the presence of Fayan. Fayan’s words and intent were the same as those with which Dizang had previously instructed him.
Later, he resided at Longji Mountain as before. He did not strive to gather disciples, yet scholars flocked to him. Entering the hall, he said:
"The ordinary person possesses the dharma of the ordinary person, yet the ordinary person does not know it. The sage possesses the dharma of the sage, yet the sage does not realize it.
If the sage were to realize it, he would be an ordinary person; if the ordinary person were to know it, he would be a sage. These two phrases share one principle but have two aspects."
[This is] the meaning. If a person can discern this, there will be no hindrance to finding a point of entry into the Buddha-dharma.
If you cannot discern it, do not say that you have no doubts. Take care. A monk asked: "It is said that by seeing form one sees the mind. A pillar is form; what is the mind? The Master said:
"Fortunately, you have not yet understood. Do not pretend to see clearly where you are lost. A monk asked: "How can one escape the three realms? The Master said: [The text here is incomplete].

[The monk] asked, "These three realms are simply one place to emerge from. The Master said, "If they are not the three realms, then what? [The monk] asked, "Where is it that is not the three realms? The Master said, "What is it that you do not understand?
[The monk] asked, "When one proclaims the truth directly before one's eyes, who is it that truly understands? The Master said, "It is not you who does not understand."
Question: "What is the master of the myriad dharmas? The Master said: "Bring me the myriad dharmas here. Question: "I have heard an ancient saying:
'Mount Sumeru contains a mustard seed; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. What is Mount Sumeru? The Master said: "It pierces through and breaks your heart."
[The student] asked, "What is the mustard seed? The Master said, "It blocks your eyes. [The student] asked, "How can one understand this?
The Master said, "Bring me the Mount Sumeru and the mustard seed. [The student] asked, "Where is the previous statement? The Master said, "What previous statement was there? [The student] asked.
"Where have you come from, monk? "Cuiyan," he replied. The Master asked, "What words or phrases did Cuiyan use to instruct his disciples?

He replied, "He usually said: 'When going out the gate, one meets Maitreya; when entering the gate, one sees Śākyamuni. The Master said, "Even so, how can such a saying suffice? [The monk] said, "..."
"How about the Master, O Monk? The Master said, "Who do you encounter when you go out the door? What do you see when you enter the gate?
Upon these words, the monk attained realization. He ascended the hall and said: "Where sound and form do not reach, the illness lies in seeing and hearing;
where words and explanations fall short, the error lies in the lips. A monk asked, "Setting aside sound and form, please, Master, speak. The Master said, "Ask within sound and form."
A student came forward and asked, "What is the mind of one who studies? The Master said, "Who is it that asks such a question?

The student asked, "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder whether this [mind] is also destroyed? The Master said, "It is not destroyed. The student asked, "Why is it not destroyed?
The Master said, "Because it is identical to the great trichiliocosm. He ascended the hall and said: "Rolling up the curtain removes obstructions; closing the door gives rise to blockage."
Obstruction. This very obstruction and hindrance has never been understood by anyone, past or present. To understand it is to be obstructed; not to understand it is to lack freedom. Question:
"In the midst of the great night, what serves as the eye? The Master said: "Darkness. Question: "Without the slightest separation, why is it that one does not see when looking?
The Master said: "A master at playing with shadows. Question: "How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said: [Silence].

The Master said, "It illuminates and penetrates heaven and earth. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after being polished? The Master said, "A pitch-black expanse. [The monk] asked, "What is the Universal Eye?
The Master said, "Not even a single hair can be seen. [The monk] asked, "Why cannot it be seen? The Master said, "Because its eye is too large.
[The monk] asked, "What is a person who is utterly ruined? The Master said, "Even when the kalpa is destroyed, they do not migrate."
[The monk] asked, "Does this person still know that there is Buddha-dharma or not? The Master said, "If he knows there is Buddha-dharma, he is entirely inverted.
[The monk] asked, "How can one avoid being inverted? The Master said, "One must simply know that there is Buddha-dharma.
[The monk] asked, "What is Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Utterly ruined. [The monk] asked, "What is the mind of the student that is always present? The Master said:
"Have you ever asked Heyu? he asked. The student replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand, when summer ends, go ask Caoshan.
The Master had a verse that said: "The wind moves and the heart shakes the tree; Clouds arise and nature stirs up dust.
If you would clarify today's affairs, You will obscure the person of original nature. Furthermore: "If you wish to know the path of liberation, all phenomena do not reach one another. [The eye...]

The ears are cut off from hearing and seeing; sounds and forms are a vast, tumultuous clamor. Furthermore, one whose initial mind has not yet entered the Way must not allow it to be a vast, tumultuous clamor.
Realize it within the sound of the bell; be overturned within the sound of the drum. Moreover, the Buddhas did not appear in this world, nor did they preach for forty-nine years;
the Patriarchs did not come from the West, for Shaolin possesses the wondrous secret. Furthermore, the myriad dharmas are the light of the mind; all conditions are...
Xingxiao: Fundamentally, there is no person who is deluded or awakened; it simply requires realization this very day.
A monk asked Chan Master Chuan Yin of Yanqing Monastery in Lufu: "When one sees form, one sees the mind. The lantern is form."
"Which one is the mind? The Master said, "You do not understand the meaning of the ancients. He asked, "What is the meaning of the ancients? The Master said, "The lantern is the mind.
He asked, "If one can transform things, they are the same as the Tathāgata. I wonder, what things are to be transformed?"
The Master said, "What do you say? As the monk was about to offer a reply, the Master said, "You lacquer bucket!
Zen Master Shouan of Nantai on Mount Heng was asked by a monk, "Everyone has the Road to Chang'an;
how does one arrive there? The Master said, "Where are you right now? He was further asked, "When all is silent and there is nothing to rely upon, what then? The Master said, "Silence."
Jizhiyan. He then presented this verse: Sitting in stillness at the southern terrace, a single burner of incense; All day long, he remains unmoving, and ten thousand anxieties vanish.
This is not a matter of stilling the mind to eliminate delusive thoughts; It is simply because there is nothing whatsoever to be pondered.
Chan Master Qinghui Xiu of Tiantong Monastery in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: "Venerable elders, how much leisure you have!
Throughout the twelve periods of the day, in what world do you establish yourselves and sustain your lives? Examine this thoroughly for yourselves. Why not seek a place of rest?
For what reason do you instead examine others? If you proceed in such a manner, you have already fallen into the secondary."
[This is] the "First Head. At that time, a monk asked: "I have heard the Master say, 'To go thus already falls into the second head.
If a student does not approach in this manner at all, how can one distinguish [the truth]? The Master said, "You, however, are a master yourself.
The monk said, "In that case, I have truly met the Master today. The Master said, "Do not pretend to be clever."
A monk asked National Teacher Seonggwang (Sunggwang) of Haeju, successor to National Teacher Cheonryongji: "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Take note clearly. The monk asked, "What is the source and root of all dharmas? The Master said, "Thank you for pointing it out."
A monk asked Chan Master Dongming Zhenjue of Xianzong in Fuzhou, a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Fu: "When grasping the clouds, one does not rely on the power of wind and thunder;
how can one penetrate the body amidst the surging waves? The Master said, "Why do you abandon the root to pursue the branches?"
Chan Master Xingqin Guangfa of Fucheng, Quanzhou, ascended the hall and said: "Is there anyone who can discern this? If there is someone who can discern it, what is it?
It is a worn-out straw sandal in the lake. If you cannot discern it, it will fall to the ground with a golden sound.
Having finished speaking, he stood for a long time without further ado. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "All you venerable seniors..."
The Master took his leave. A questioner asked, "What is it to speak of the truth while opposing the mundane? The Master said, "You hired hand, what are you asking?
He asked, "What is it to follow the mundane while opposing the truth? The Master said, "Go drink tea. A questioner asked, "What is it before the lighting of the lamp?
The Master said, "After the lighting of the lamp. He asked, "What is it after the lighting of the lamp? The Master said, "Before the lighting of the lamp. He asked, "What is it..."
Zheng Randle asked, “Master, please drink some tea. The Master said, “Drink tea and go. He asked, “What is the second moon? The Master said, “You ask and I answer.
[This concludes the section on] National Teacher Taichan, a successor in the Dharma lineage of Chan Master [Furong Daokai].
A monk asked Zen Master Qiun Baosheng of Wuzhou, “What is the water of Qiyun? The Master said, “Longtan is always bottomless; as soon as you intend to ask, there are waves.
The monk said, “Is it not just this very thing? The Master said, “In the ancient hall there is no incense smoke;
who can distinguish the clear from the turbid? The monk said, “I do not yet understand: what is it like at the deepest point? The Master said, “O *dārala* (monk).”
If you wish to recognize the place of profound depth, you must simply cut off the clouds beneath your feet.
Master Xuanzhi of Guangping in Fuzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Bailong Xi, ascended the hall and said: "Is there anyone who can provide verification? If there is someone who can verify it..."
Clear! Thus one avoids failing one’s ancestors and letting future generations come to naught. If you are merely seeking words and phrases, they are clearly present in the Great Canon.
But within the school of the patriarchs, what is there to be strange about? Even to speak thus is but a fleeting remark. A monk asked, “What is the realm of Guangping?
The Master said, “The earth bears the beauty of famous mountains; the streams connect with the sea.”
Qing asked, "What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "You ask and I answer. Qing asked, "What is the essence-body of the Dharma (dharmakāya)?
The Master said, "Vast and empty space, free from all blemish or flaw. Qing asked, "What is the object within that essence?
The Master said, "A single bright moon disperses over the autumn river. Qing asked, "I do not know whether the essence and the object are distinct or not. The Master said, "I have already told you."
"What is it? [the monk] asked. The Master said, "If so, then there is no distinction. The Master continued, "The pierced-eared barbarian monk smiles and nods his head.
A monk asked Zen Master Qingmu of Bailong on Mount Sheng in Fuzhou, "What is Bailong’s secret application of the single pivot?
The Master said, "What do you use every day? The monk said, "If that is so, then my listening has been in vain. The Master shouted.
[The Master] went out. [A monk] asked, "All sentient beings use it daily yet do not know it. What is this that is used daily?
The Master said, "How could I possibly answer you differently? [Another] asked, "Without waiting for what comes up, please tell me, Master, that one phrase prior to the sound. The Master said:
"Is it that you do not discern?
A monk asked Chan Master Zhien of Lingfeng in Fuzhou, "What is the 'blow-off hair' sword? The Master said, "I step forward;
you step back. The monk said, "In that case, this student will lose his life. The Master said, "Do not strike the water."

The fish was startled by itself. [A monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Who else could it be? [The monk] said, "If that is so, why is there such distinction between delusion and awakening?
The Master said, "Simply do not lose your own sheep; why must you weep at the fork in the road? [The monk] asked.
"What is the realm of Lingfeng? The Master said, "Ten thousand layers of green mountains are like a platter of delicacies; two ribbons of green water are as if painted.
He asked, "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Clearly clear, dense dense; dense dense, clearly clear."
A monk asked Zen Master Xuānliàng of Dōngchán in Fúzhōu, "Fundamentally there is neither delusion nor enlightenment;
why then are there Buddhas and sentient beings? The Master said, "Your words have fallen into error. The monk asked, "The patriarchs transmit one to another the Seal of the Dharma;

whom do you, Master, now succeed? The Master said, "I offer my special thanks for your testimony. The monk said, "In that case, Băilóng must have personally bestowed the prediction upon you at that time."
"Today, you should respond to the Sage to ferry those lost across the ford. The Master said, "Do not mistake the weight on the scale of the wooden tray.
Chan Master Xuan Ying Dinghui of Baqiu Monastery in Zhangzhou was a native of the Wu family of Jinjiang, Quanzhou.
Chen Wenxiao, the Regional Inspector (Cishi) of Zhangzhou, established the monastery and invited the Master to expound the Dharma. A monk asked, "What is the primary meaning? The Master—
[The student] asked, "What is the primary meaning? The Master said, "You, a student, have come to seek instruction; why do you ask me a question in reverse?

The student asked, "What was it you were just now asking for instruction on? The Master said, "The primary meaning. The student asked, "Do you consider that a reverse question? The Master said, "Do you consider that a reverse question?"
Question: "What is the site of the ancient Buddha’s Dharma-hall? The Master said: "This summer, there are fifteen hundred monks in the hall.
In the eighth year of the Kaibao era, as he was about to pass away, seven days prior he wrote a letter of farewell to Lord Chen and presented this verse:

"This year I am sixty-six; the lifespan of the world has its extensions and shortenings. The fire of non-arising blazes fiercely; the fuel of conditioned existence is no longer sustained. Leaving the valley and returning..."
The source [of his lineage] was fully prepared all at once. When the appointed time arrived, he admonished his disciples, saying, "After my passing, you must not wear mourning garments or wail.
Having finished speaking, he entered nirvana.

Chan Master Zhaqing Kuang, Dharma heir of [Chan Master] Zongxian Minghui of Ba’en Monastery in Quanzhou, was asked by a monk: "In the past at the single assembly on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa heard it personally;
I wonder who it is that hears it today? The Master said: "I recall the Honored One within the Seven-Leaf Cave."
Question: "In the past, at the eastern outskirts of the city of Jāgṛva, when the Elephant King circled about, the five groups of disciples all arrived.

Today, the Prefect presides over the assembly; how should one receive him? The Master said: "Blink your eyebrows. [The questioner] said: "If that is so, then at the moment a single principle is revealed—"

All conditions having been extinguished, the Master said, "Why such elaborate words? Question: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "Look at the vulture’s feathers in the daylight.
Question: "All the students have brought this question; we request the Master to speak. The Master said, "This is not the first time I have resided here;
even this monk would find it difficult to tolerate [such talk]. Question: "Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations—please, Master, speak. The Master said, "Green."
"Red flowers fill the courtyard. The monk asked, "Regarding that which does not involve discursive thought—the ancestral vehicle of the patriarchs—I beg the Master to speak directly.

The Master remained silent for a long time. The monk said, "If that is so, then those who merely listen to echoes labor in vain by pricking up their ears. The Master replied, "Already, you are stuck in the mud."
Question: "What is a king of men? The Master said: "In responding to you, I dare not be rash. Question: "What is a Dharma King? The Master said:
"Do not let this opportunity go to waste. Question: "I do not yet know what matters were discussed when the king of men and the Dharma King conversed. The Master said:
This is not for you to hear.
Chan Master Chengkan of Longguang Monastery in Jinling was a native of Guangzhou. A newly arrived monk came to visit him.
The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Jiangnan. The Master said, "Have you paid your respects to the Boatman who crossed the river? He replied, "The Master [should]..."
"What teaching did you have that led you to pay respects to the Boatman who crossed the river?
The Master said, "He was your *kalyāṇamitra* (spiritual friend). Yongxing Beiyuan Kexiu Chan Master asked a monk, "What is the meaning of the West?
The Master said, "It pervades the whole world. The monk said, "Is it not this very thing? The Master said, "If it is, then receive it securely. A monk asked, "As for one who performs great deeds..."

"A person comes; do you still receive them, Master? The Master said, "I do not receive them. [The monk] asked, "Why do you not receive them? The Master said, "Fortunately, they are the sons and daughters of good families."
A monk asked Chan Master Qinghai of Taiping Monastery in Chenzhou, "The ancients said that [the Way] is not obtained through requesting instruction;
yet why did the Patriarchs say, 'Who can become a Buddha'? The Master replied, "Only after awakening does one know.

The monk asked, "Regarding the successive transmission of the ancestral vehicle from of old, I wonder how it is proclaimed today? The Master replied, "Transcending the white clouds into the deep caverns."
[The] inner [text]: "Exotic flowers and strange grasses grow upon the mountain peaks.
A monk asked Chan Master Ciyun Huideng Puguang of Lianzhou: "When King Bimbisāra invited the Buddha, he received the Dharma at that time;

when our Sovereign invites the Master, it is to cause the school to flourish on this day. We would be fortunate if you would grant us a skillful means and not begrudge us the proclamation [of the truth]."
The Master said, "There is no need for further questioning. [The student] asked, "What is the Great Perfect Mirror? The Master said, "Look!
[The student] asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the mirror]? The Master said, "Listen clearly."
A monk asked Chan Master Daqin of Xingyang Mountain in Yingzhou, “What is the realm of Xingyang? The Master said, “Pine and bamboo have just been planted;
the mountain shadows are green. The flowing water passes through the courtyard. The monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said:
Furthermore, what is it? Master Bao'en Zi was a dharma successor of Chan Master Cheng of Fulin in Chuzhou.
A monk asked him, "What is the monastery? The Master said, "The banners and canopies have vanished. The monk asked again:

"What is it to be among those within the monastery? The Master said, "One has the right to gaze upon and pay homage. The questioner asked, "Please do not withhold from me the single phrase for descending from the hall.
The Master said, "In my leisurely chanting, I recall only Layman Pang; neither in heaven nor on earth can one be his peer."
Chan Master Shouchen of Ba’en in Chuzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Xinfeng Xin, was asked by a monk, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "The crows fly with a flickering haste; the hares run with a frantic speed."
A monk asked Chan Master Tong of Jue Ling in Xiangzhou, the Dharma heir of Chan Master Yuan of Jue Ling: "When the World-Honored One attained the Way, the Earth Deity informed the Space Deity.
When you, Master, attain the Way, I wonder who will inform you? The Master said, "Thank you for informing me."
Chan Master Jun of Renwang Monastery in Hangzhou, successor to Chan Master Longhuaqiu, was asked by a monk: "The ancients said, 'The path that goes upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages.
What is this matter that is not transmitted? The Master said, "Ask about what is above. The monk said, "In that case, it is above..."
"One who has come should not go. The Master said, "Since you know this is so, why have you come here treading these steps?
Jiuxian (Wine Immortal) met Chan Master Xian; he was the son of the Lin family of Changzhou in Gusu. His mother conceived him after dreaming that she had swallowed a large pearl.

He manifested many extraordinary omens; his appearance was grand and strange, and his mouth could hold both fists. At the age of seven, he once submerged himself in a deep abyss, yet his robes remained dry.

He subsequently left the household life to become a disciple of Kaiyi of Yong’an in Jiahe. At thirty, he received the tonsure and full ordination. He traveled to visit Longhua, where he realized the Mind-Seal (Citta-mudrā).
Upon returning, he resided at Mingjue Monastery, where he devoted himself solely to drinking wine; when intoxicated, he would compose songs and verses to provide spiritual admonition.

Monastics and laypeople therefore called him the "Wine Immortal. He spoke in verse: "By green waters and red peach blossoms, I have wandered through front streets and back alleys more than a hundred times.
Zhang San knows me; Li Si also knows me. Whether they know me or do not know me, Between these two fists, which one is larger?
Of the two, one is large indeed: It once struck a hole through empty space. He rubbed [the Buddha image] and said:
The teaching is thus: take up Mount Sumeru as a pillow and lie down. At the Yangtze River, the waves are deepest; travelers who reach this point all pause in hesitation.
When you arrive at the place where there are no waves, you must still apply your mind as you did when the waves were present.

The golden goblet is heard to be filled once more; the Jade Mountain is reported to be collapsing. Do not let the night-watchmen’s drums hasten the end; seize the moonlight to return. This is precious.
Buying cinnabar to paint the moon—when calculated, it is a waste of effort. Drunkenly sleeping beneath the green willows, one rises and pretentiously speaks of *tathatā*.
The clay man repeatedly exhorts: "Do not let you lose the pearl within your robe. One-six, two-six—the matter is already complete.
One-nine, two-nine—I want to drink wine. Stretching out both legs, I sleep for a while; then I rise.
Heaven and earth remain as they were before; green trees stand at the gate where no birds sing. Upon the mossy ground below the courtyard lie fallen blossoms.
I shall briefly discuss this matter with the eastern wind: to whom does the fullness of spring’s colors belong? When autumn arrives, the mountains grow cold and the waters chill;

when spring comes, the willows turn green and the flowers turn red. A single point of movement follows ten thousand transformations; in the river village, the mist and rain are thick and dim. Is there existence, or is there not?
Empty or not empty? With a colander one tries to scoop up the northwest wind. Born into this Jambudvīpa world, how much love and hate do human sentiments harbor?
They simply want to drink a little wine, which is why they lie fallen in the streets and on the roads; after death, they are reborn once more in Saṃsāra.
He did not wish to be reborn in a Pure Land. Why was this? It was because in the Western Pure Land there are no wine shops.

On the early morning of the Yuanxiao festival in the second year of the Xiangfu era, after bathing, he went to his room, joined his palms, raised his right hand, opened his mouth with his left, and passed away.

Chan Master Daoquan of Guizong on Mount Lu was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yanshou. He was a native of the Liu family in Jizhou. A monk asked, "I have heard that you, Master, personally met Yanshou;
is this true? The Master replied, "Has the wheat ripened in front of the mountain yet? [The monk] asked, "In the mountains of Jiufeng, does it still..."
"Is there Buddha-dharma or not? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma within the mountains of Jiufeng? The Master said, "The large stones are large;
the small stones are small. Shortly thereafter, the kingdom of Jiangnan fell, and the monastic community was required to undergo examinations on their mastery of the scriptures.
The master’s assembly all practiced Chan meditation. He then composed a verse and presented it to the regional governor, saying: "Comparing it to forgetting words, it merges with the Great Void;
It spares the harmonious breath from being partial or distant. Who would have thought that virtue has no use at all? Today, as a monk, I value the knowledge of writing.
The governor read it and consulted with his officials, saying: "In a grove of sandalwood, there must be no other trees."
At Shu, there was only the Master’s single cloister. The Military Governor of Nankang, Zhang Nanjin, submitted a memorial on his behalf to grant him exemption from the imperial examination.
Zhang then prepared a formal petition to assemble both monastics and laypeople to welcome and invite the Master to preside at the Guizong Monastery. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Guizong?
The Master said, "A thousand devious paths are not equal to one direct path. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Wait until the snow has melted; then spring will arrive naturally."
A visitor asked, "In the deep mountains and rocky valleys, is there still the Buddha-dharma or not? The Master said, "No. The visitor said, "The Buddha-dharma pervades all places;
why then is it not there? The Master said, "Because no one has ever reached it. Another asked, "When the ancients said, 'It is not the wind moving, nor the banner moving,' what was that?
The Master said, "Tomorrow there will be a market at the crossroads. Another asked, "How is it? The Master said, "Tomorrow there will be a market at the crossroads."
"This is the student himself. The Master said, "The bed is narrow; lie down first. The congee is thin; sit down later. In the second year of the Renshi era, he passed away peacefully.
He was interred in a stupa at Niushou Hermitage.

The monk said, “I have come to ask about my own self; why do you instead speak of Zhang San and Li Si? The Master said, “Do not be so hasty.
The monk asked, “I do not ask about other matters; what is the Master’s family style? The Master said, “The family...”
"Let us set aside the wind for a moment. What, then, are those other matters that you have not asked about?

"Is there fire within this? The Master poked at it and said, "There is no fire. The Layman rose personally and poked deeply until he found a small amount of fire.

only then do you realize that your own property is not obtained from another. Therefore, the Patriarch said: 'Awakening is the same as non-awakening; there is no mind and there is no dharma—there is simply nothing false.'"

He ascended the hall and said, "The bitter cold of mid-winter is an annual affair; as the movement of the sun's shadow shifts, what is the matter?
Yangshan stepped forward, stood with his hands clasped, and the Master said, "I knew well that you could not answer this question. Xiangyan said, "I am uniquely able to answer it."
When he said this, the Master followed up with his previous question. Yan also stepped forward and stood with his hands joined in *añjali*.
The Master said, "Fortunately, you did not understand, O son of silence. One day, seeing Liu Tiemo approaching, the Master said, "Old cow, you have come. Tiemo replied, "I have."
"Tomorrow there is a great assembly feast at Mount Tai. Will the Master go? The Master then relaxed his body, assuming a reclining posture.
Mazu then departed. A monk came to pay his respects; the Master made a gesture as if rising. The monk said, "Please do not rise, Master."
The Master said, "I, this old monk, have never sat. The monk said, "I, this humble one, have never prostrated. The Master said, "Why then do you not prostrate?
The monk was speechless. (Tongan spoke on his behalf, saying: "Master, do not resent him. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Mindlessness is the Way. [The monk] said, "..."
"I do not understand," he said. The Master replied, "It is better to take up that which you do not understand.

He asked, "What is it that I do not understand? The Master said, "It is simply you; it is not anyone else. He further said, "People of the present day should simply realize, right here and now, that which they do not understand.
That is precisely your own mind; that is precisely your Buddha. If you seek outwardly for a single bit of knowledge or understanding and take that to be Chan, you are mistaken."
"The Way. For now, there is no engagement. This is called 'carrying manure in'; it is not called 'carrying manure out.
It defiles your mind-field. Therefore it is said: 'It is not the Way. Question: "What is Baizhang’s true self? The Master descended from his meditation seat, joined his palms, and stood.
Question: "What is the Master’s true self? The Master sat back down. While the Master was sitting, Yangshan passed in front of the abbot’s quarters. The Master said:
"If the late master Baizhang had seen you, you would have had to endure a severe beating.
Yang said, "What about the present matter? The Master said, "Shut your two pieces of skin. Yang said, "This kindness is difficult to repay. The Master said, "It is not that you lack talent;
it is simply that I, the old monk, am advanced in years. Yang said, "Today I have personally met the venerable master Baizhang. The Master said, "You..."
"Where do you see it? Yang said, "I do not say that I see it; it is simply that there is nothing else. The Master said, "From beginning to end, you are a master.
The Master asked Yangshan, "Setting aside the matter of the present for a moment, how was it in the past? Yang folded his hands and stepped forward.
The Master said, "That was still a matter of the present. How about a matter of antiquity? Yang bowed and stood back. The Master said, "You wrong me;
I wrong you. Yang then prostrated himself. While Yangshan and Xiangyan were standing in attendance, the Master raised his hand and said:
"Nowadays, those who act in this way are few, while those who do not act in this way are many. Yan stepped from east to west and stood there;
Yang stepped from west to east and stood there. The Master said, "This causal connection will be like gold cast upon the ground thirty years hence.
Yang said, "It must also be through the Master’s proclamation that it can be so. Yan said, "Even now, it is not lacking. The Master said, "It should be..."
[The Master] took hold of [Yangshan’s] mouth. While the Master was seated in his place, Yangshan entered; the Master showed him his two hands interlaced.
Yangshan performed a woman’s bow. The Master said, “So it is! So it is! Later, while the Master was seated within his quarters, Yangshan entered; the Master said:
"Jizi, recently, what has your successor in the lineage been doing? Yang said, "There are many who harbor doubts about this matter.
The Master asked, "What about you, Jizi? Yang said, "Huiji simply closes my eyes when I am tired;
when I am energetic, I sit in meditation. That is why I have never spoken of it. The Master said, "To reach such a state is truly rare. Yang said, "According to—"
Huaiji said, "Even this single phrase that I have seen cannot be grasped. The Master said, "You yourself cannot grasp it, let alone anyone else.
Yangshan said, "Since ancient times, all the sages have been exactly like this. The Master said, "Many people would laugh at you for answering in such a manner.
Yangshan said, "Those who understand the laughter are my fellow practitioners. The Master asked, "What about the matter of appearing in the world?"
Dongshan rose, circumambulated the meditation seat once, and bowed. The Master said, "Tearing asunder past and present.
While Yangshan and Xiangyan were standing in attendance, the Master said, "Past, present, and future—the way of the Buddhas is the same. Every person attains a path of liberation.
Yangshan asked, "What is this path of liberation for every person? The Master turned back to Xiangyan and said, "Jizi, you have asked a question. What is it?
He did not answer him. Yanguan said, "If one speaks of the past, future, or present, I, so-and-so, nevertheless have a way to respond.
The Master asked, "How would you respond? Yanguan said, "I take my leave," and he departed. The Master then asked Yangshan:
Zhixian responded in such a manner; did it accord with Jizizi? Yangshan said, "It does not accord. The Master asked, "And what would you have done?
Yangshan also said, "Zhenzhong (Take care)," and went out. The Master laughed heartily and said, "It is like water and milk merging.
One day, the Master raised one foot and said to Yangshan, "Every day I receive his support; I am grateful that he does not..."
Cheng仰 said, "At that time, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s Garden, it was no different from this. The Master said, "You must say more before you are finished.

[The Master] performed the rite of dismissal. He asked Yangshan, "How do you understand the wondrously pure and luminous mind?

The Master propagated the religious teachings for over forty years. Those who attained realization were beyond counting.

On the ninth day of the first month in the seventh year of the Dazhong era, having washed his hands and rinsed his mouth and arranged his seat, he passed away peacefully. He was eighty-three years of age and had been in the monastic order for sixty-four years.
His stupa was erected at his native mountain, and he was posthumously titled Chan Master Dayuan. His stupa was named "Pure and Tranquil.
He was a fourth-generation descendant of Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Weishan Huairang.
Chan Master Huiji Tongzhi of Yangshan in Yuanzhou was the son of the Ye family of Huaihua in Shaoyou.

At the age of nine, he entered the monastic life at He'an Temple in Guangzhou under Chan Master Tong (who was the "Silent Tong"). At fourteen, his parents took him back home, intending to arrange a marriage for him;

He answered his parents' toil with the promise of the True Dharma, whereupon they granted their permission. He went again to the ordination hall and received the tonsure;

before even attaining full ordination, he traveled to various regions. Initially, he visited Danyuan and already realized the profound essence of the teachings. Later, he studied under Guishan and eventually entered the inner sanctum of the patriarchal lineage.

One day, Danyuan asked, "The various forms you previously presented were quite worthy of being cherished and kept secret. The teacher replied, "I looked at them then and burned them immediately.
Danyuan said, "In this dharma-gate of mine, no one is able to comprehend it, save for my late master and the various patriarchs."
Only a Great Sage could have fully understood its meaning. Why did you burn it? The Master said, “Huiji read it once and already knew its intent;

Later generations could not fully believe this. The Master said, "If the Abbot wishes for me to record it again, it will not be difficult.
He immediately compiled another version and presented it; there was nothing omitted. Yuan said, "So be it.

Yangshan said, "By means of the wondrous state where thought is without thinking, one returns to the thought that the spiritual flame is inexhaustible."
"Thoughts are exhausted and return to the source; nature and characteristics are eternally abiding. Phenomena and principle are non-dual; the true Buddha is suchness.
Upon hearing these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. From then on, he attended upon him, serving him before and after for fifteen years.

The Master said, "There is no need to stand in the middle; nor should you dwell at either end.
Miaoyan said, "If it is so, then look at water. Water can level things. The Master said, "Water itself has no fixed state; it simply levels what is high and what is low."

[The Master] stood in a low, level place. Muzhou then desisted. A donor sent silk to Mount Gui Shan. The Master asked, "Venerable Sir, having received such offerings from a donor, with what will you repay them?

Dexing said, "What is it that is good? The Master pointed to the rain. Dexing was again speechless. The Master said, "How can one with great wisdom remain silent?
Later, while accompanying Muzhou on a mountain excursion, they sat upon a flat stone. As the Master stood in attendance, a crow suddenly dropped a red persimmon before him.
Muzhou picked it up and gave it to the Master; the Master took it, washed it, and passed it back to him.
Guishan said, "From where did you get this? The Master replied, "This is what is moved by the Venerable’s own virtue. Guishan said, "You, too, must have a share.
He then divided it in half and gave a portion to the Master. (Xuansha said: "How great was Guishan! He was pinned down by Yangshan with a single sitting, and to this day he cannot rise.")
Guishan asked the Master, "Suppose someone were to ask you; how would you respond?
The Master said, "If Master Dongsi were still here, I would not be left in such silence. Guishan said, "I grant you the offense of failing to respond.
The Master said, "Life and death depend on a single word. Guishan said, "I do not deny what you have seen, yet others would not agree."
The Master said, "Who is it? Baizhang pointed to a pillar and said, "This one. The Master asked, "What did you say? Baizhang replied, "What did you say?

The Master said, "A white mouse passes by; the silver platform remains unchanged. Baizhang asked Mount Huishan, "When the Great Function manifests before you, I ask the Master to discern and clarify it for me.
Huishan descended from his seat and returned to the abbot’s quarters. Baizhang followed him in. Huishan asked, "What was it you were asking just now?"
"What words? The Master raised the case again. Mian said, "Do you remember my reply? The Master said, "I remember. Mian said, "Try to state it for me.
The Master then said, "Zhenzhong! and went out. Mian said, "Wrong. The Master turned his head and said, "If Master Xian’s junior brother comes, do not say that I have nothing to say.
Later, the Master asked Dongsi, "May I borrow a path to pass by?"
"May I return by the other path? The Abbot said, "Generally speaking, a śramaṇa should not rely on only one path.
Is there not another? The Master remained silent for a long while. The Abbot then asked, "May I borrow one path to go over there?
The Master said, "Generally speaking, a śramaṇa should not rely on only one path. Is there not another? The Abbot said, "There is only this. The Master said, "The Great Tang..."
The Master’s family name was definitely Jin. While he was herding oxen on the front slope of Mount Gui, he saw a monk ascend the mountain and descend shortly thereafter.
The Master asked, "Why did you not stay in the mountains for a while? The monk replied, "It was simply because our karmic conditions were not in accord.
The Master said, "What were those conditions? Try citing them for me. The monk said, "When the Master asked me what my name was—"
The monk replied to Master Guizhen, saying, "Where is Guizhen? The monk had no answer.
The Master said, "Go back to the Abbot and tell him that I have answered. When the Abbot asks how you answered, simply say:
'In the eye, in the ear, in the nose. The monk returned and acted exactly as instructed. Baizhang said, "You deceitful liar! This is..."
While the master was lying down after the five hundred spiritual friends had finished speaking, he dreamed that he entered the inner courtyard of Maitreya.

All the seats in the assembly hall were occupied, except for the second seat, which was empty. The master then took his place. A venerable elder struck the gavel and announced, "The Dharma shall now be preached from the second seat.
The master rose, struck the gavel, and said: "The Mahāyāna Dharma transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred..."
"No. Listen attentively! Listen attentively! Upon these words, the assembly all dispersed. When the Master realized this, he recounted it to Guishan.
Guishan said, "You have already entered the rank of the sages. The Master then prostrated himself. While the Master was attending upon Guishan as they were walking, he suddenly saw dust rising ahead.
Guishan asked, "What is that before you? The Master went forward to look at it and then made a certain gesture. Guishan nodded his head. Guishan then addressed the assembly:
[One] said: "All sentient beings lack Buddha-nature. Yanguan addressed the assembly, saying: "All sentient beings possess Buddha-nature.
Two monks from Yanguan went to inquire [of Guishan]. Upon arriving at Mount Gui, they heard Guishan expounding the Dharma;
its depths were unfathomable, and they felt a sense of slighted pride. One day, while conversing with the Master, they urged him, saying: "Elder brother..."

"You must study the Buddha-dharma with diligence; it cannot be treated lightly. The Master then made this ○-shaped gesture, pressed his hands together to display it, and then threw them behind his back.
He then opened both hands and reached out toward the two monks. The two monks were at a loss. The Master said:
"My elder brother, you must certainly study the Buddha-dharma with diligence; do not take it lightly. Having said this, he rose and departed. At that time, the two monks returned to Yanguan.
After traveling thirty *li*, one monk suddenly attained realization and said, "One should know that when Baizhang [the master of Mt.
Wei] said, 'All sentient beings have no Buddha-nature,' his conviction was not mistaken. He then returned to Mt. Wei. The other monk continued on ahead.
After traveling several *li*, he suddenly attained realization upon crossing a stream. He sighed to himself, saying, "Master Shishuang said that all sentient beings have no Buddha-nature;
it is certainly true that he spoke thus. He then returned to Shishuang and remained for a long time in attendance at the Dharma seat.
While Shishuang and his teacher were herding oxen together, Shishuang asked, "Is there any Bodhisattva here? The teacher replied, "There is. Shishuang said:
"Which one do you see as being so? Point it out for me," the Master said. The Teacher replied, "The Master suspects that one is not so;
point it out for me. Guishan then desisted. The Teacher presented some fruit to Guishan. Guishan took it and asked, "Where did you get this?
The Teacher said, "It is from my own garden. Guishan asked, "Is it even fit to eat? The Teacher said, "I have not yet dared to taste it; first I offer it to you."
The Master [Huai-jang] said, "Whose is this? The Teacher [Zhaozhou] said, "It is Huaiji’s. Huai-jang said, "Since it is yours, why did you have me taste it first?
The Teacher said, "The Master has tasted it a thousand times and ten thousand times. Huai-jang then ate it and said, "It still has a sour and astringent taste remaining.
The Teacher said, "As for the sour and astringent, you surely know it yourself. Huai-jang did not answer. As the bell rang, the attendant Chi-gan heard it.
Sheng then asked, "Does one with ears strike the bell, or does one without ears strike the bell? The Master said, "Just ask;
do not worry that I will be unable to answer. Gan said, "I have already finished asking. The Master shouted, "Go!

At the end of the summer retreat, while paying his respects to Muzhou Daowu, the Master was asked by Muzhou, "I have not seen you for an entire summer. What were you doing down there? The Master replied, "I..."
Jiashan was below [the mountain]. He had cleared a patch of fallow land with a hoe and sown a basketful of seed.
Guishan said, "This summer you have not spent in vain. Mazu then asked, "I wonder, Master, what were your activities during this summer?
Guishan said, "One meal at midday; one sleep after nightfall. Mazu said, "Master, you too have not spent this summer in vain. Having said this, he departed.
He stuck out his tongue. Guishan said, "Jizizi, how can you injure your own life?
One day, when Guishan saw the Master approaching, he immediately crossed both hands in front of him, flicked them three times each, and then held up one finger.
The Master also crossed both hands in front of him, flicked them three times each, and then placed one hand palm-up and the other palm-down at his chest, gazing at him with his eyes.
Tianhuang stopped there. Tianhuang was feeding crows with raw rice; turning his head, he saw the Master and said, “Today I have given him a talk on the Dharma.
The Master said, “I followed the custom and heard it. Tianhuang asked, “What is that which you heard?
The Master said, “The crows cawed as crows, and the magpies chirped as magpies. Tianhuang said, “How can you escape sound and form? The Master said, “Venerable Teacher...”
"What did you just say? Muzhou said. "I only said that he had ascended the hall once. The Master said, "Why do you call this 'sound and form'?
Muzhou said, "Even so, it does no harm to verify it. The Master said, "As for the Great Matter, how would you verify it?
Muzhou raised his fist. The Master said, "In the end, you are merely pointing east and drawing west. Muzhou—
Xiangyan said, "What was it you just asked? The Master said, "I asked the Reverend about the great matter of the causal conditions.
Miaoyan said, "Why did you call this 'pointing east and drawing west'? Xiangyan said, "Because of attachment to sound and form, I therefore asked about the error."
Guishan said, "Neither of you has yet fully understood this matter. The Master asked, "How can one come to understand this matter?
Guishan said, "Jizi [you] are sound and form; I am east and west. The Master said, "A single moon in a thousand rivers—the essence does not divide the waters.

Guishan said, "One must be like this before it is attained. The Master said, "It is like gold and gold; ultimately there is no difference in color, so how could there be different names? Guishan said, "..."
[The student] asked, "What is the principle that has no different names? The Master said, "A jar, a basin, hairpins, bracelets, a contract, a bowl, and a tub."
Yangshan said, "Jizi’s exposition of Chan is like the roar of a lion; it startles and scatters the foxes, wolves, and jackals.

Later, when Yangshan opened the Dharma at Mount Mang, he asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Mount Lu. Yangshan asked, "Have you ever been to the Five Elders Peak? The monk said, "I have not.
Yangshan said, "The Acharya has never traveled the mountains" (Yunmen said: "These words were all for the sake of compassion").
(These are words of a man fallen into the weeds). He ascended the hall and said: "All of you, each turn the light back upon yourselves and reflect; do not merely memorize my words.
Since beginningless kalpas, you have turned your backs on the light and cast yourselves into darkness; your roots of delusive thought are so deep that they are difficult to uproot suddenly.

Therefore, I provisionally employ skillful means to seize away your coarse consciousness, much like using yellow leaves to stop a child's crying—what efficacy is there in this? It is also like a person taking..."
A hundred kinds of merchandise are displayed together with gold and jewels as a single shop for sale; this is merely intended to gauge the capacity of those who come.
Therefore it is said: "Stonehead’s is a shop of pure gold; my place here is a general store. If someone comes seeking mouse droppings, [they shall find them].
I also pick it up and give it to him; he comes seeking true gold, and I also pick it up and give it to him. At that time, a monk asked, "I do not want mouse-droppings;
I beg the Master for the true gold. The Master said, "If you bite the arrowhead and intend to open your mouth, you will not understand it even in a donkey’s year."
The monks had no response. The Master said, "If one calls out for something, there is a transaction; if one does not call out for it, there is none.
If I were to speak of the Chan school, I would not even have a single person to accompany me by my side—how much less could there be a multitude of five hundred or seven hundred?
If I were to speak here and there, people would scramble forward to gather what they could, like using an empty fist to deceive small children. All [was thus].
There is no place of substantiality. I shall now clearly explain to you the matters pertaining to the limit of the holy ones (*ārya*). For now, do not allow your mind to settle or cling [to objects].

Simply practice according to reality within the ocean of your own nature. You need not seek the three knowledges or six supernormal powers. Why? Because these are merely peripheral matters of the holy ones.
At present, you must simply recognize the mind and penetrate the root. Once you have attained the root, you need not worry about the branches.
At another time, on a later day, he went there himself. If you have not yet attained the fundamental source, even if you exert your feelings and imitate him, you will still not attain it.
Have you not seen what Master Guishan said: "When the sentiments of ordinary and sage are exhausted, the true permanence is revealed;
when phenomena and principle are non-dual, one is the Buddha of Suchness. He asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarchs? The Master made this gesture in the air with his hand.
[The Buddha] pointed them out to him. The monks remained silent. The Master said to the First Seat, "When you are neither thinking of good nor thinking of evil, at such a moment, what is it?
The Seat replied, "At such a moment, this is where I lay down my life. The Master said, "Why do you not ask the old monk?
The Seat replied, "At such a moment, I do not see that there is a 'Master'. The Master said, "Support me! (Fú) [The Seat lifted the Master up].

"My teaching does not arise. Because of this, the Master returned to Mt. Gui to pay his respects to Baizhang. Baizhang asked, "Since you call yourself a good spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), how do you distinguish those who come from all quarters—those who know there is [Buddha-nature] from those who do not, those with a teacher from those without, and those who study the meaning (*arthavidyā*) from those who study the mysteries (*gūḍhavidyā*)?
You should try to explain this. The Master said, "Huiji has a way of testing people. Whenever I see a monk coming, I simply raise my staff."

[Zhaozhou] raised his whisk and asked him, "Do the elders of all quarters still speak of this, or not? He [the monk] replied, "Setting this aside for a moment, what is the intention of the elder masters of all quarters?
Tianhuai sighed and said, "This is the very fangfang (fang and claws) of the ancestral school.
Tianhuai then asked, "The sentient beings of the great earth have their karmic consciousness wandering in a blur, with no fundamental basis to rely upon. How do you know they exist?"
Regarding "being" and "non-being," the Master said, "Huiji has a point of verification. At that time, a monk passed by in front of him. The Master called out, "Ācārya!
The monk turned his head. The Master said, "Upādhyāya! This is precisely what is meant by 'karmic consciousness vast and wandering, with no fundamental basis to rely upon.
Guishan said, "This is like a single drop of a lion’s milk splashing apart six bushels of donkey’s milk. The Master then asked a monk:
"Where have you come from? he asked. The monk replied, "From Youzhou. The Master said, "I was just looking for news from Youzhou. What is the price of rice there?
The monk replied, "When I was coming here, I happened to pass through the marketplace and stepped on his bridge, breaking it. The Master then ceased questioning him.
Whenever a monk approached, the Master would hold up his whisk. The monk would then shout. The Master said, "That shout is certainly not lacking, but tell me: where does the old monk’s fault lie?"
"Where have you been? he asked. [The monk] replied, "It was not appropriate for you, Master, to show me such a realm.
The Master then struck him. A Brahmin arrived from the sky. The Master asked, "Where did you recently leave from? He replied, "India. The Master asked, "When did you leave there?

He replied, "This morning. The Master said, "Why so late? He replied, "I was traveling through the mountains and enjoying the waters. The Master said, "Your playful display of supernatural powers is indeed remarkable."
"No," [the monk] replied. "The Dharma and teachings of the *ācārya* must first be returned to this old monk before they may be granted.

[The monk] said, "I came specifically to the Eastern Land to pay homage to Mañjuśrī, yet I have instead encountered a 'lesser Śākyamuni. He then produced a *bīja-patra* leaf inscribed with Sanskrit script, prostrated to the Master, and departed through the air.
From that time on, he was known as the Lesser Śākyamuni. While the Master resided at Dongping, Baoshou of Mt. Wei sent a letter and a mirror to him via a monk.
The Master ascended the hall, held up [the mirror] to show the assembly, and said: "Tell me, is this the mirror of Mount Huai or the mirror of Dongping?
If you say it is the mirror of Dongping, it was sent by Mount Huai; if you say it is the mirror of Mount Huai, it is in the hands of Dongping.
If you can speak of it, I shall keep it; if you cannot, I shall smash it. The assembly remained silent. The Master then smashed it.
[The Master] broke [the silence] and descended from his seat. During the next period for the monks' formal visit, the monk asked, "Does the Master know how to read and write?

The Master replied, "I manage with what I have. The monk drew this circle (○) on the ground and presented it. The Master brushed it away with his sleeve. The monk again drew this circle (○) and presented it.
The Master made a gesture with both hands as if throwing them behind his back. The monk looked at him intently; the Master lowered his head. The monk then circled around him.
The Master circumambulated him once and then struck him; the monk then departed. While the Master was sitting, another monk came and paid his respects, but the Master did not look at him.
The monk then asked, "Master, do you know how to read characters? The Master replied, "I manage with what I have. The monk then circumambulated him to the right once and said:
"What character is this? The Master drew a "十" (ten) on the ground in response. The monk circled it once counter-clockwise and asked, "What character is this?

The Master changed the "十" into a "卍" (swastika). The monk drew this circle (○), cupped his hands as if grasping the sun and moon like an Asura, and asked, "What character is this? The Master then drew the "卍" inside the circle (☰) facing him. The monk—
He then manifested the majestic power of Lu-zhi. The Master said, "So it is; so it is. This is that which all Buddhas protect and keep in mind.
You are thus, and I am also thus. Guard and uphold it well for yourself. The monk prostrated in thanks and departed, soaring through the air.
At that time, a certain practitioner saw this. Five days later, he asked his teacher, "Teacher, did you see it too?
The teacher said, "Did you see it? Did you see him leave the gate and soar into the air? The practitioner said, "I saw him; he departed by ascending into the void.

The teacher said, "This was an Arhat from the Western Heaven who came specifically to test my Way. The practitioner said, "Although I witnessed various *samādhis*, I could not discern their underlying principle. The teacher said:
I shall explain this for you according to its principle. These are the eight kinds of samādhi; they are the ocean of awakening transformed into the ocean of meaning.

Their essence is identical. This principle possesses both cause and fruit, and whether simultaneous or sequential, the general and the particular do not depart from the *gūḍhakāya-samādhi* (the samādhi of concealing the body).
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "From the South. The Master raised his staff and said, "There..."
The senior monk replied, "Does he still speak of this? The Master said, "He does not. The Master asked, "If he does not speak of this, does he still speak of that?
The monk replied, "He does not. The Master called out, "Virtuous One! The monk responded, "Yes. The Master said, "Go to the hall. The monk then departed.
The Master called out again, "Virtuous One! The monk turned his head. The Master said, "Come closer. The monk stepped forward. The Master [withdrew his hand].
He gave a tap with the tip of his staff and said, "Go. Attendant Liu asked, "May I hear the principle of realizing the mind?
The Master said, "If you wish to realize the mind, there is no mind to be realized. This absence of a 'realizing mind' is called true realization.
One day, while the Master was sitting in the Dharma Hall, he saw a monk coming from outside; after the monk had paid his respects, he stood toward the eastern side.
He stood with palms joined, gazing at the Master. The Master then lowered his left foot; the monk stepped back to the western side and stood with palms joined.
The Master lowered his right foot; the monk moved toward the center and stood with palms joined. When the Master withdrew both feet, the monk prostrated in worship.
The Master said, "Since I have resided here, I have never struck a single person. He then took up his staff and struck him;
the monk immediately soared into the air and departed. When Prime Minister Lu Xisheng wished to visit the Master, he first prepared this circle (○) and presented it as an offering.
The Master opened the envelope and wrote beneath the circle: "To know without thinking falls into the secondary category; to know by means of thought—"

This was the third verse. He then returned the letter (the witty remarks of Lord Wei Zhou were similar to these, so they are not repeated here). Upon seeing the Master, the Lord immediately entered the mountain. The Master went out to meet him at the gate.

As soon as the Lord had entered the gate, he asked: "The three gates are all open; through which one do you enter? The Master replied: "I enter through the Gate of Faith. When the Lord reached the Dharma Hall, he asked again:
"When one does not leave the realm of Māra but enters directly into the realm of the Buddha, what then? The Master—
He struck [the official] three times upside down with his whisk. The official then performed a prostration. He asked again, "Does the Master maintain the precepts?

The Master said, "I do not maintain the precepts. He asked, "Do you practice seated meditation? The Master said, "I do not practice seated meditation. After a long silence, the Master asked, "Do you understand?
The official said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Listen to this verse from an old monk: Flowing along, I do not maintain the precepts; sitting upright, I do not practice meditation."
Chan. Three or two bowls of strong tea; the meaning lies at the edge of the mattock. The Master, however, asked:
"I have heard that you, Excellency, attained awakening through studying the sutras—is this true? He replied: "Your disciple was reading the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, which says:
'Without severing afflictions, one enters nirvāṇa,' and thus found a place of peace and joy. The Master held up his whisk and said: "As for this very thing, what is it?"
[The Master] entered. [Pang] said, "The single word 'enter'—it is not necessary. The Master said, "The single word 'enter' is not for you, Excellency.
The Excellency then rose and departed. (Fadeng said: "Seat-holder, tell me: for whom is the single word 'enter'? Also, Excellency, do not be troubled. Pang Jushi asked:
"I have long admired Yangshan. Having come here today, why do you instead cover it over? The Master held up his whisk. The Layman said, "Exactly so.
The Master asked, "Is this looking up or covering over? The Layman then struck the pillar and said, "Even though there is no one here, I still want the pillar to bear witness.
The Master threw down the whisk and said, "If you go to other places, feel free to cite this example. The Master then pointed to the Snow Lion.
He asked the assembly, "Is there anyone among you who has attained this state? The assembly remained silent. (Yunmen said: "At that moment, he should have simply pushed him over.

The Master asked Shuangfeng, "How is it that you have seen things recently, my brother? Shuangfeng replied, "According to my own realization, there is truly not a single dharma that can be grasped by the mind.
The Master said, "Your understanding still remains within the realm of objects. Shuangfeng said, "I am exactly like this; how about you, elder brother? The Master said:
"Do you not know that there is not a single dharma that can be grasped by the mind? When Guishan heard this, he said, "Jizi’s single phrase will leave the people of the world in doubt" (Xuange said:
"The Sūtra says, 'In truth, there is no dharma,' yet Dīpaṃkara Buddha gave me a prediction of enlightenment. He says, 'In truth, there is not a single dharma that can be grasped by the mind.

Why does he say this? 'Understanding still remains within the realm. But tell me, where lies the point of benefit or harm? While the Master was lying down, a monk asked him, "Does the body itself understand how to preach the Dharma? The Master replied:

"I cannot say it," the Master said. "There is another person who can. [The monk] asked, "Where is this person who can say it? The Master pushed out his pillow. When Guishan heard of this, he remarked, "Jizang employs the affairs of the sword's edge. Later, while the Master was sitting with his eyes closed, Guishan approached. The Master opened his eyes and looked at him. Guishan bowed. The Master said, "What is this? Guishan replied, "I have come to inquire after your health. The Master said, "If you had not come here today, I would have beaten you. Guishan said, "I am not afraid of being beaten. The Master said, "Why do you not fear it? Guishan said, "Because I am not yet enlightened. The Master said, "If you were enlightened, would you still be afraid? Guishan said, "Even if I were enlightened, I would still be afraid. The Master said, "If you were enlightened, how could you be afraid? If you are not enlightened, why should you be afraid? Guishan said, "I am not afraid; I simply do not know what to do. The Master said, "This is precisely why you are afraid. Guishan said, "If I were not afraid, I would not be able to practice the Way. The Master said, "If you were not afraid, you would indeed be practicing the Way. Guishan said, "I am not practicing the Way. The Master said, "If you were practicing the Way, you would be practicing it right now. Guishan said, "I do not practice the Way. The Master said, "If you do not practice the Way, who is it that speaks these words? Guishan said, "It is not I who speak these words. The Master said, "If it is not you, then who is it? Guishan said, "It is the Buddha-nature. The Master said, "If it is the Buddha-nature, why does it not speak? Guishan said, "The Buddha-nature is not a thing that can be spoken. The Master said, "If it is not a thing that can be spoken, then why did you just now say 'it is the Buddha-nature'? Guishan said, "That was merely a provisional designation. The Master said, "If it is merely a provisional designation, then why do you cling to it? Guishan said, "I do not cling to it. The Master said, "If you do not cling to it, then why do you not let go? Guishan said, "If I let go, I would fall into emptiness. The Master said, "If you fall into emptiness, then you are truly deluded. Guishan said, "I am not deluded. The Master said, "If you are not deluded, then why do you not see your own face? Guishan said, "My own face is not something that can be seen. The Master said, "If it cannot be seen, then how can you say you are not deluded? Guishan said, "I am not deluded; I simply do not recognize it. The Master said, "If you do not recognize it, then you are indeed deluded. Guishan said, "I am not deluded; I simply do not seek it. The Master said, "If you do not seek it, then why do you trouble yourself with these questions? Guishan said, "I do not trouble myself; I simply wish to help others. The Master said, "If you wish to help others, you must first help yourself. Guishan said, "I have already helped myself. The Master said, "If you have already helped yourself, then why do you still need me? Guishan said, "I do not need you. The Master said, "If you do not need me, then why do you come to see me? Guishan said, "I come because I have no other choice. The Master said, "If you have no other choice, then you are truly free. Guishan said, "I am not free; I am bound by my own mind. The Master said, "If you are bound by your own mind, then you are not free. Guishan said, "I am not bound; I simply do not realize it. The Master said, "If you do not realize it, then you are indeed bound. Guishan said, "I am not bound; I simply do not break free. The Master said, "If you do not break free, then you will remain in bondage forever. Guishan said, "I do not remain in bondage; I simply do not dwell in liberation. The Master said, "If you do not dwell in liberation, then you are truly liberated. Guishan said, "I am not liberated; I simply do not grasp at it. The Master said, "If you do not grasp at it, then you are indeed liberated. Guishan said, "I am not liberated; I simply do not seek it. The Master said, "If you do not seek it, then you are truly seeking it. Guishan said, "I am not seeking it; I simply do not abandon it. The Master said, "If you do not abandon it, then you are indeed abandoning it. Guishan said, "I am not abandoning it; I simply do not hold onto it. The Master said, "If you do not hold onto it, then you are truly holding onto it. Guishan said, "I am not holding onto it; I simply do not release it. The Master said, "If you do not release it, then you are truly releasing it. Guishan said, "I am not releasing it; I simply do not bind it. The Master said, "If you do not bind it, then you are truly binding it. Guishan said, "I am not binding it; I simply do not untie it. The Master said, "If you do not untie it, then you are truly untying it. Guishan said, "I am not untying it; I simply do not weave it. The Master said, "If you do not weave it, then you are truly weaving it. Guishan said, "I am not weaving it; I simply do not cut it. The Master said, "If you do not cut it, then you are truly cutting it. Guishan said, "I am not cutting it; I simply do not sew it. The Master said, "If you do not sew it, then you are truly sewing it. Guishan said, "I am not sewing it; I simply do not dye it. The Master said, "If you do not dye it, then you are truly dyeing it. Chan Master Zhìxián of Xiāngyán in Dèngzhōu was a native of Qīngzhōu. Disgusted with the mundane world, he left his kin to seek the Way, traveling to observe the various quarters.
During his time at Baizhang, his nature and intellect were sharp and quick, yet he could not attain realization through Zen meditation. After Baizhang passed away, he went to study under Guishan.
Guishan asked him, "I have heard that while you were with your late master Baizhang, when asked one thing you would answer with ten, and when asked ten things you would answer with a hundred.

"Speak a single phrase! When the Master was thus questioned, he was left utterly bewildered.

Returning to his quarters, he sought through all the texts he had studied over the years to find a single sentence with which to respond, but in the end, he could find none. He sighed to himself, "A painted cake cannot satisfy hunger.
He repeatedly requested that Baizhang explain it to him, to which Baizhang replied, "If I were to explain it to you, hereafter..."
