The man said, "Stop, stop. The Master said, "How is it with the sword? The man said, "The eye is it. He asked, "I do not ask about anything else."
"Setting aside for a moment the upward-tending vehicle of the lineage, I request you, Master, not to answer. The Master said, "A fine monk indeed!

[The student] said, "If that is so, then I shall go to prostrate. The Master said, "Do not perform the three prostrations; let them exhaust your entire life. While the assembly was in session for inquiry, [the Master spoke thus].
The Master pointed to the incense burner and said, "Do you all see it? If you see it, prostrate yourselves at once and each return to the hall.
A monk asked, "The ultimate Way is wordless; words are borrowed to manifest the Way. What are the words that manifest the Way? The Master said:
“Be careful not to make discriminations. [The monk] asked, “What is non-discrimination? The Master said, “The Great General, the King; the Grand Guardian, the Duke.
[The monk] asked, “What is the auspicious light of the Wisdom-Sun? The Master said, “It is not far from here to Baoci. [The monk] said, “In that case, I have personally received its illumination.
The Master said, “For now, rejoice that there is no connection [between you and it].”
Chan Master Ba’en Huiming of Hangzhou was surnamed Jiang. He entered the monastic life in his youth and became thoroughly proficient in the three studies.

Determined to explore the profound essence of the Dharma, he traveled south through the regions of Min and Yue, visiting various Chan assemblies, yet found no resonance with his own mind. Later, he went to Linchuan to pay his respects to Fayan;
the teacher and disciple were of one accord in their realization. Subsequently, he returned to Mount Damei in Ninghui to dwell in a hermitage. During the Wuyue period...
Within this school, although practitioners of Chan were numerous, they placed the orthodox lineage of Xuansha outside the gates. The Master wished to rectify and guide them.
One day, a newly arrived visitor came to consult him. The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "The capital city. The Master said:

When the Elder left the capital city to come to this mountain, the capital was short of the Elder; here, the Elder is in surplus. To have a surplus implies that there are phenomena external to the mind;
to be short implies that the phenomena of the mind are incomplete. If one can explain the principle, then stay;
if one does not understand, then depart. The monk had no response. The monk asked, "What is the Master of Daimei? The Master said, "Where did you leave from today, Venerable Sir?"
[The monk asked: "Where [is it]? The monk had no reply. The Master subsequently moved to Mount Tiantai, where he established a hermitage at White Sand (Baisha).
There was a senior monk named Pengyan who was widely learned and possessed a powerful memory; he came to visit the Master to debate the essential teachings of the school (zongcheng).

The Master said: "Excessive words distance one further from the Way. Now I have a matter I wish to ask: as for the various sages and former worthies of antiquity, were there any among them who did not attain awakening?"
Wu said, "If these were the various sages and former worthies, how could there be anyone among them who had not attained awakening?
The Master replied, "When one person gives rise to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions is entirely dissolved. Now, Mount Tiantai stands towering here;
how can it be made to dissolve? Wu was at a loss for what to say. From that time on, those from other schools who came as students all took his words to heart and submitted to him.
During the Qianyou era of the Han dynasty, King Zhongyi invited him into his palace to inquire about the Dharma and commanded him to reside at Zichong Monastery.
The Master extensively expounded upon the profound teachings of Xuansha, Dizang, and Fayen; their essential principles reached the ultimate pinnacle.
Consequently, the King ordered various Zen masters, such as Cuiyan Lingcan, along with prominent figures from the capital, to determine their relative merits. Zen Master Tianlong asked: "All..."
"All Buddhas and all Buddha-dharmas emerge from this sutra. I do not yet know from where this sutra emerges. The Master said, "Speak!
As Tianlong was about to offer a word, the Master said, "It is already past. The Elder Ziyuan asked, "What is the samādhi of the present?
The Master said, "Do you hear it? Ziyuan said, "I am not suffering from deafness. The Master said, "Indeed."
However, he suffered from deafness. The Master again raised the inscription for Xuefeng’s stupa and questioned the elder masters:
"That which arises from conditions undergoes formation and destruction from beginning to end; that which does not arise from conditions remains eternally firm throughout kalpas.

Setting aside for a moment this firmness and this destruction, where is Xuefeng right now? (Fayan offered a different reading: "Right now, is this formation or destruction? The elders had no response. Even if they had had a response...
Furthermore, he was unable to withstand his rigorous interrogation. At that time, the assembly of eminent scholars bowed down in submission, and the King was greatly delighted.
He appointed [the Master] as the Chan Master Yuantong Puzhao. Ascending the hall, the Master said: "Do you all understand?

Do not say that speech and silence, movement and stillness, are nothing other than Buddha-work—do not misunderstand this! A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "You..."
"Do you see the incense altar? He replied, "I do not yet understand; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "You do not even recognize the incense altar.
He asked, "Setting aside the immediate functioning before one's eyes, what is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "Why do you not ask? He replied, "..."
"If it is so, then I shall truly depart. The Master said, "That too is a vain effort. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "I see that the original radiance and auspicious signs of Dīpaṃkara Buddha were like this. A monk asked, "What is the student’s own self?
The Master said, "What is the intention behind making such a deliberate inquiry? A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the [Master’s] coming from the West? The Master said:
One hundred and eight thousand true journeys: directly downward from the West, it does not reach the East. Question: "What is the second moon? The Master said:
"Squeezing one's eyes to look at flowers, there are many blossoms; seeing clearly, the branches of the tree are numerous."
The Dharma Master Xuanjue of Baoci Temple in Jinling, a native of Quanzhou, ascended the hall and said:

"When a traveler visits a spiritual friend and arrives at a monastic community, he sets down his water flask and alms bowl; one might say that his duties in practicing the Bodhisattva path are then complete.
Why should he come here further to discuss True Suchness and Nirvana? This is a discourse for the wrong time."
However, as the ancients have said: "It is like sifting through sand to identify treasure; once the grit and pebbles are removed, the pure gold reveals itself naturally.
This is then called the "eternally abiding world" and the "fully endowed Sangha Jewel. It is also like a rain of a single flavor falling upon a uniform ground.
It gives birth to and grows all things; they differ in size, and their flavors vary between sweet and pungent. One cannot say that the earth and the rain possess names of "large" and "small.
This is why it is said: when square, it manifests as square; when round, it manifests as round. Why is this?

Because this Dharma has neither partiality nor correctness; it manifests in accordance with conditions. This is called the "manifested form-body" (rūpakāya). Do you see it yet? If you do not see it...
"Do not sit idly. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "This question is improper.

The monk asked, "If sitting is indeed right and wrong, how can one attain the person of original nature? The Master said, "How do you sit? Hearing a dove calling, the Master asked a monk, "What sound is that?
The monk replied, "It is the sound of a dove. The Master said, "If you wish not to incur the retribution of non-existence..."

Regarding intermediate karma: do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma. The Prince of Jiangnan established Baoji Monastery and commanded the Master to extensively propagate the principles of the school.
With a congregation of over two thousand from the four seas, he was specially designated with the title of "Teacher. He ascended the hall and said:

"On this day, the worthy and sage have gathered together, and the assembly from the seas has arrived in unison. It is truly evident that the essence of the Buddha-dharma is fully present here. If one is such a worthy..."
Those who perceive it need not wait for words. Yet, since speech itself is fundamentally non-existent, why remain silent?

Thus, the myriad phenomena of the universe and the vast source of all Buddhas are like the clear light of the Sea-Seal Samādhi when manifest; yet when obscured by darkness, sentient beings become deluded and confused.
Were it not for the superior person of penetrating mind and the transcendent man of exceptional rank, how could one bring forth [this realization] amidst the various sensory objects?

Exquisite in the ultimate degree! It rolls up and unfolds the myriad phenomena; it bestows and takes away from the arrayed universe. It shows that birth is not birth, and that extinction is not extinction.

Once birth and extinction are thoroughly penetrated, this is called "true permanence. To speak of the provisional is for shadows to disperse across a thousand paths; to discuss the real is for the single void to leave no trace.

How could one possibly calculate this in terms of existence and non-existence, or birth and extinction? A monk asked, "The King has invited you once more specifically to offer prayers for the late Emperor;
how will you proclaim the Dharma today, Master? The Master said, "You are not asking about the one who proclaims it again. The monk said, "..."

"If it is thus, then there is nothing that surpasses this, whether in heaven or among men. The Master said, "There is no connection. A questioner asked, "I have traveled from afar to seek refuge with you;
please grant me your reception. The Master said, "Go back to where you were before."
Chan Master Qichou of Chongshou Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of Quanzhou. He ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "The fourfold assembly observes intently the primary principle; what is the primary principle? The Master said, "Why trouble yourself to ask further?

He then said, "If you, the great assembly, wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season. What are these conditions of time and season? [He continued: "Up..."
The assembly shall now disperse. Tell me, does it exist or not? If it does not exist, why do you disperse immediately?
If it does exist, what is the primary principle (*paramārtha*)? Elder, the primary principle is already manifest; why trouble yourself to contemplate it further?
When one realizes this clearly, one sees that the Buddha-nature is ever-shining and all phenomena are eternally abiding. Yet, if one perceives that there are phenomena which abide, this is still...
This is not yet the true source of the Dharma. What, then, is the true source of the Dharma? Elder, have you not seen the ancient say:
"When one person gives rise to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions all vanishes"? Is there still even a single dharma for intellectual interpretation?
The ancients had such a great matter of cause and condition; to act in accordance with it is precisely it. Why labor over it?
The Elder spoke at length. There were those in the assembly who did not yet understand, so they requested instruction. The monks asked, "The lamp of Fayan personally lit yours;
today, as you receive the summons of kings and nobles, what is the lamp of Fayan? The Master said, "Please ask another question.
They asked, "Regarding the point where the ancients' views were not in accord, we request the Master’s skillful means. The Master said, "What did the ancients see?"
"Where is there no uniformity? [A monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "What is the Buddha? [The monk] asked, "How should one understand this?
The Master said, "Understanding is not it. [Another] asked, "Regarding the essential meaning of the Western Come [Bodhidharma], to which generation do you belong? The Master said, "..."
"Every year on the fifteenth day of the eighth month is Mid-Autumn. [A monk] asked, "What is the Master’s single phrase for benefiting others?
The Master said, "Guanyin's raising; Shanglan's raising."
Chan Master Fajian Huiji of Jinling Baoyuan was a native of Tàihé. Initially residing at Caoshan, he ascended the hall and said:
"To know that which is illusory is itself liberation; no expedient means are required. To be liberated from illusion is itself awakening;
there is likewise no gradual progression. Distinguished elders, how will you inquire? Since there are no expedient means and no gradual progression, where does the saying of the ancients apply?"
If you have realized it, the Buddhas are constantly manifest before you. If you have not yet realized it, do not seek it within the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* (the *Perfect Enlightenment Sūtra*).
The Buddha-dharma has been thus from the beginningless past until the endless future; it has never failed to be manifest. Venerable Elders, at all times you are sustained by this majestic radiance;
you must possess the great faculty of faith to be able to shoulder this burden. Have you not seen how the Buddha praised those who are fierce and sharp?
A person may be fit to serve as a vessel for the Dharma, yet one does not necessarily reward those who have long cultivated pure karma by turning toward the good.
One must be like that broad-foreheaded, fierce butcher who, upon casting down his knife, immediately realized the fruit of Arhatship; it requires exactly this kind of realization to succeed.
Therefore, the Elder said: "It is as if the rank of Brahmā were bestowed directly upon an ordinary person. A monk asked: "Since the great assembly has gathered before the Dharma..."
[The student] said, “I understand. I pray that the Master will not be sparing with the mystery within the phrase. The Master said, “Will you deceive the assembly?
[The student] said, “If that is so, then it is entirely due to this question. The Master said, “It is of no use. [The student] asked, “An ancient said, ‘All dharmas take non-arising as their essence.
What is this essence of non-arising? The Master said, “What an excellent point of inquiry! [The student] asked, “Within the Buddha-dharma, I request the Master to [speak].”
[The Master] said, "You have understood the skillful means. [A monk] asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "Why wait to ask?
The Prince of Jiangnan invited him to reside at Ba’en Temple and appointed him as the Head of the Assembly (*zhǎozhòng*). Upon ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"Today, by imperial command, I am to preside over this monastery and expound the Dharma for the sake of the community. Just now, I observed the *weina* strike the gavel; how much [time has passed]?"
"Very well. You are instructed to contemplate the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*). But what, pray tell, is this ultimate truth?
If one can penetrate it here, how much more essential could it be! What else need now be said? Nevertheless, having received the imperial decree, I cannot remain silent.
Now, as for the essentials revealed by the Chan school, it is the eternal rule of the Dharma: perfectly manifest and luminous, transcending antiquity."
From the present day until the arrival of Bodhidharma from the West, he too merely testified for all people;
he had no dharma to be obtained that he could give to others, but simply said, "It is right here. He then instructed them to grasp it on the spot.
Although the ancients spoke of grasping it on the spot, can one still grasp it while sitting now? If you have doubts, please ask. A monk asked: "The profound mystery of the three virtues..."
The Pivot follows from the Buddha’s exposition. Regarding the profound path of the single voice, he requested the Master to clarify it. The Master said, "Do you say that it exists or not?
He asked, "What is the realm of repaying kindness? The Master said, "Everyone sees you ask. During the Kaibao era, he passed away at this very monastery.
A monk asked Chan Master Yangui of Chang'an Monastery in Luzhou, "Who is the master of this hermitage?
The Master said, "When you arrive at other places, simply say that you come from Chang'an."
Chan Master Qingxi of Yunju Mountain in Nankang Commandery was a native of Quanzhou. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Yunju?
The Master said, "What do you call 'the realm'? The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "What did I just tell you?
Later, while he was residing at Ximing Monastery in Quanzhou, the Imperial Messenger Liao entered the monastery and saw him.
He made an offering to the portrait of Master Fayan and asked, "What kind of fruit is this before the portrait?
The Master said, "It is a false fruit. The messenger said, "Since it is a false fruit, why do you use it to make an offering to the portrait?
The Master said, "I simply want you, messenger, to recognize what is false. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "His countenance is most wondrous and sublime."
Chan Master Xifeng of Zhengqin Monastery in Changzhou was the son of the Xie family of Suzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The ancient sages said:
'Perfectly identical to the great void, neither deficient nor redundant. They also said: 'Each and every dharma, each and every school;

many dharmas are one dharma-school. They also said: 'Arising is only the arising of dharmas; ceasing is only the ceasing of dharmas. They also said: 'When arising, it does not say, "I am arising"; when ceasing...'"

At that time, he did not say, "I am extinguished. Based on this account, you who have long remained as senior monks (*upādhyāya*) in the monasteries must realize that if you are beginners, brothers, you must first embody the Way.
A human body is difficult to obtain, and the True Dharma is difficult to hear; do not treat it as something ordinary. The King’s provision of food and clothing is not easily digested.
If you do not clarify the Way, each and every one of you will ultimately have to return it to him. Senior monk, you must...
"Do you understand? Take care. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Where did you get this news?
He asked again, "What is the empty nature of all phenomena? The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. He asked once more.
The assembly gathered like clouds and requested the Master to proclaim the Dharma of the Lineage. The Master said, "It has been proclaimed for a long time. A question was asked:

"The Buddha-dharma was entrusted to kings and great ministers; today, with such diligent effort, what do you intend to entrust? The Master said, "Ten thousand years! Ten thousand years! Another question was asked.
An ancient said, "The mountains, rivers, and the great earth are your true spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
How can one take the mountains, rivers, and the great earth as spiritual friends? The Master said, "What do you call 'the mountains, rivers, and the great earth'?
Question: "What are words that accord with the Way? The Master said, "You ask, and I answer. Question: "On Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa heard it directly."
[The monk] asked, "I do not yet know who has heard [the Dharma] today. The Master said, "What did Kāśyapa personally hear?

[The monk] asked, "Regarding the site of enlightenment of the ancient Buddhas, how can a student reach it? The Master said, "Where are you now? [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s perfect penetration (*yuantong*)?
The Master struck the meditation seat three times. [The monk] asked, "What is shedding the sense bases and their objects? The Master said:
"Do not engage in false conceptualization. [The student] asked, "Are the human king and the Dharma-king one or two? The Master said, "The human king and the Dharma-king.
[The student] asked, "What is the mark of the quiescence of all phenomena? The Master said, "Arising is only the arising of dharmas; ceasing is only the ceasing of dharmas.
[The student] asked, "What is the dharma that has never been born? The Master said, "How could you know it? [The student] asked, "When Wuzhuo saw Mañjuśrī, why..."
[The monk] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Do you say that Mañjuśrī still recognizes Wuzhuo? [The monk] asked, "When one attains the meaning, who possesses the wondrous new melody?
I request the Master to proclaim a single phrase of right diligence. The Master said, "What are you saying? [The monk] said, "Is there no expedient means?"
The Master said, "You do not understand my words.

Zen Master Xuanfa of Zhanzhou Luohan Temple ascended the hall and said: "Throughout the entire world of the ten directions, there is not so much as a single speck of dust of a dharma that serves as an object for your seeing, hearing, sensing, or knowing. Do you believe this? Nevertheless, even so, you must still awaken."

Only now have you attained it; do not treat this as something trivial. Have you not heard it said: "To clarify only one's own self, yet fail to awaken to what is before one’s eyes—such a person possesses only a single eye.
Do you understand? A monk asked, "When not even a speck of dust is established, why do beauty and ugliness appear before us?

The Master said, "Take note of this clearly and ask someone else elsewhere. The monk asked, "When the great assembly gathers like clouds, who is the one who attains it? The Master said, "Take note of this clearly and ask someone else elsewhere."
The Master said, "Have you ever lost it? A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "You are a wandering monk.
A monk asked, "What is the house style of Baoshou? The Master said, "View it as you please. The monk said, "In that case, the assembly has someone to rely upon."
The Master said, "How do you understand this? The monk replied, "I certainly would not dare deceive the assembly. The Master said, "Why do you find it insufficient?
He asked another monk, "Where is your place of training? The monk replied, "At the Buddha’s Footprint. The Master said, "Where is the Buddha? The monk replied, "Where is he not?
The Master raised his fist and said, "What is this? The monk replied, "Venerable Sir, please put it away. The Master said, "Let go!"
The Master gave the *ācārya* seven blows. He then asked a monk, "Where have you been this summer? The monk replied, "I was with Elder Wuyan.
The Master said, "Did you ever pay your respects to him? The monk said, "I did pay my respects. The Master said, "How could one pay respects to 'No Words' (*wuyan*)?
The monk said, "If one attains 'No Words,' where would there be no way to pay respects? The Master shouted, "It is just like..."
He asked his elder brother, "Master, you and Elder Yandu were eating steamed cakes. Yandu said, 'A hundred kinds, a thousand varieties—their substance is not two.
Master, what is this non-dual substance? Yandu picked up a steamed cake. The Master said, "You are merely clinging to the hundred kinds and thousand varieties.
Yandu said, "That too is just your own way of seeing, Master. The Master said, "And you, too, are just like Lu Gongyong."
Regarding the manner of combing his hair: as the Master was about to pass into extinction, he said to the assembly, "Tonight my four elements are not in harmony.
Clouds rise and birds fly; winds stir and dust arises. Amidst this vast expanse, is there anyone who can cure it? If one could cure it, we would never recognize each other again for eternal kalpas.
If one cannot cure it, I shall be seen by you at all times. Having finished speaking, he entered nirvana.
Chan Master Daolin of Zhangyi Monastery on Mount Zhong in Jinling was a native of Taiyuan. He first resided at Qixian on Mount Lu. Entering the hall, he said: "Is the Way distant?
It is true in every encounter. Is the Sage distant? To embody him is to become divine. I have constantly shown you this;
why do you not sit directly beneath your robes and bowl and investigate it right here? You must insist on coming up here."

What is there to investigate? Since you have come here, I have no choice but to employ a small measure of the ancients' expedient means, shaking out a bit of tortoise hair and rabbit horns to cast them down upon you. If you, venerable elders, wish for a concise and essential understanding:
"Seek it out within the Sangha hall, beneath the triple gate, and in the quarters. Is there anyone who understands?
If there is, try to speak of it; let me serve as proof for you, Elder. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Xiqian? The Master said:
"What kind of scenery is there at Xixian? [The monk] asked. "When the ancients raised their mallets or held up their fly-whisks, was that not the matter of our school?
The Master said, "The ancients have already spoken. [The monk] asked, "I am but a student newly entering the forest; I beg the Master for instruction."
The Master said: "With one hand pointing to heaven and one hand pointing to earth. Later, the Prince of Jiangnan invited him to reside at the Changyi Monastery.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Why have you all come to stand here? Good friends as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are constantly your companions;
whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they never leave you. Simply sit steadily upon your long benches. Ten.
Just as the good spiritual friend has come of his own accord to inquire, why do you, O Elder, not believe and accept this? You have been able to raise so many difficulties and easy questions.
The ancient sages lamented seeing people of the present age at a loss; they said, "It is a pity how long human sentiment has been deluded.
Facing the truth with one's own eyes, one does not realize it. This was a lament for you all, who look on yet do not know. Now tell me, what is it that you look at?
"What is it that you do not know? Why do you not examine the skillful means of the ancients? It is simply because your faith does not reach deep enough that things have come to this.
All you, venerable seniors, need only apply your minds to the Buddha-dharma; there will be nothing you cannot attain. Go and embody the Way in your daily affairs.
With these words, he descended from his seat. A monk asked, "When a hundred-year-old dark room is illuminated by a single lamp, how is it? The Master said:
"Do not speak falsely. A monk asked, "Does the Buddha-dharma undergo change and transformation? The Master said, "It is you, Elder. Another monk asked, "The great assembly has gathered;
we pray that the Master will proclaim the fundamental tenet. The Master said, "It has been a long time. A monk asked, "What is the profound principle?
The Master said, "What profound principle is there?"
Chan Master Kuangyi of Jinling Ba’en was a native of Mingzhou. The Ruler of Jiangnan invited him to reside in the Upper Hall and appointed him as Chan Master Ningmi.
Entering the hall, he looked over the assembly and said: "If you rely upon this and put it into practice, you will be free from all entanglements."
Do you still believe this? It is like the blazing, radiant clarity of the sun; do not engage in further deliberation. Deliberation cannot reach it.
Even if one were able to deliberate upon it, that would be called "limited wisdom. As the former masters said: "When the person is without mind, they accord with the Way;
when the Way is without mind, it accords with the person. When the person and the Way accord, this is called 'the state of no-affairs' (wu-shi). But from where does the person first become ordinary?"
From what does one become a sage? If you have not yet realized this, you may be said to be shrouded by deluded sentiments; thus, you cannot depart from them.
When deluded, there are immediate obstructions, involving various distinctions of opposition and relativity. Yet, when suddenly awakened, there is nothing to be attained.
It is like the case of Yantradatta, who mistook a shadow for his own head; would he not then carry his head while searching for it? Nevertheless...
At the very moment one is deluded, the head is not lost; when one awakens, it is likewise not gained. Why is this?
When people are deluded, they say they have lost it; when people awaken, they say they have gained it. Gain and loss reside in the person—what concern does this have with movement or stillness?
A monk asked, "The Buddhas preach the Dharma to universally moisten the capacities of all beings. When you, Master, preach the Dharma, who is it that hears it? The Master said:
"It is only that you have not heard. Question: "What is the single phrase for repaying kindness? The Master said: "Is it not right to speak? Question:
"When one cannot reach a point through deliberation throughout the twelve hours of the day, how should one practice? The Master said: "Where are you now? Question:
"The Patriarch came from the West; how should he be proclaimed? The Master said: "I do not go against what was requested. Question: "If..."
"What is this one phrase? The Master said, "How can my answer compare with your raising of it? The monk asked, "The Buddha appeared in the world for the sake of the one great matter;

I wonder, how is it that you, Reverend, have appeared in the world? The Master said, "Just so. The monk said, "In that case, the assembly has someone to rely upon. The Master said, "Do not misunderstand."

Wensui of Baoci Temple in Jinling was the son of the Lu family of Hangzhou. He had previously investigated the *Śūraṃgama-sūtra*, thoroughly discerning the arising of reality and falsehood from their mutual conditions;

It can be attained. Yet those of inferior or middling capacity cannot easily take it up. Why? Because the Buddha-dharma is not within the realm of mind, intellect, or consciousness.
Elder, do not treat this with such contempt. As the ancients said: "The śramaṇa’s eye holds fast the world;
its lid covers heaven and earth, continuous and without leaking so much as a hair's breadth. For this reason, all Buddhas praise it—a praise that is beyond comparison.
Metaphor: A metaphor cannot reach the Way. The venerable elder’s majestic radiance is brilliant and pervasive, spanning from antiquity to the present.
Fortunately, such is his family tradition; why not continue it? Why do you instead give rise to self-deprecation and undergo toil in vain, failing to achieve awakening?
It is precisely because of this that the Buddhas appear in the world; it is precisely because of this that they do so.
The Buddhas proclaim their entry into *nirvāṇa* solely for this reason. This is why the Patriarch came from the West specifically for this purpose.
A monk asked, "All the Sages enter the Gate of Non-duality. What is this Gate of Non-duality? The Master said, "Simply enter in this manner.
The monk asked, "If so, then it is the same throughout past and present. The Master said, "Tell me, where do you say they are the same?"
Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "You have asked exactly. [The student] said:
"If that is so, then I shall prostrate myself. The Master said: "How do you understand this? Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "How could it not be?"
He then said, "It is my fault that I cannot cast myself into the mountain ravines or vanish from the marketplace, yet instead enter the imperial court and thus trouble the sovereign with my presence.
I shall repeatedly decline and return to my former mountain. The ruler of the state then granted him the Five Peaks Qixuan Hermitage as his dwelling.
National Preceptor Hye-gu of Mount Do-pyeong in the Kingdom of Goryeo first awakened his spiritual potential within the chamber of Master Fa-yan.

His sovereign in the home country, longing for him, dispatched an envoy to invite him; he subsequently returned to his native land. There, the sovereign received the secret instructions on the mind, and his reception and honors became even more profound.
One day, he was invited into the Prince’s residence. Ascending the hall, the Master pointed to the Wei-feng Pavilion and addressed the assembly, saying:
"The Wei-feng Pavilion has already proclaimed the Dharma for you all, worthy ones. Do you understand? If you do understand, how do you understand it?
If you say you do not understand, how is it that the Wei-feng Pavilion does not understand? Take care!"
Chan Master Shaoyan of the True Body Jewel Pagoda Temple in Hangzhou was the son of the Liu family from Yongzhou.

The King of Wuyue commanded the Master to propagate the Dharma and appointed him as Chan Master Liaokong Dazhi Changzhao. He ascended the hall and said: "This mountain monk has always been of meager knowledge and insight."
During this period of leisure and relaxation, I have been reciting sutras while awaiting death.
Who would have thought that today Your Majesty, with such earnestness and gravity, would urge this mountain monk to emulate the venerable masters of all quarters by arranging this Dharma assembly?

Yet, in making this request, Your Majesty seeks nothing other than for you, noble sirs, to realize your own minds; there is no other principle involved. Have you, noble sirs, realized your minds yet? Is it not simply words?
When speaking and laughing; when sitting in solemn silence; when seeking out spiritual teachers; when discussing the Way with companions;

when gazing at mountains and playing by the water; and when the senses are completely withdrawn—is this your mind? If you understand it in the manner described above, you are entirely possessed by demonic delusions;
how can this be called "clarifying the mind"? Furthermore, there is another class of people who, apart from the delusive thoughts within the body, seek to recognize something else.
"Pervading the worlds of the ten directions, containing the sun and moon, and encompassing the great void—this is called the original true mind.

This too is the conceptualization of the non-Buddhists; it is not the realization of the mind. Do you wish to understand, sirs? The mind has nothing that is 'is,' nor does it have anything that is 'is not.
If you intend to grasp and recognize it, can it ever be obtained? A monk asked, "When the six realms are clear and serene, what then? The Master [responded]:

He said, "Great assembly, who will believe you? In the seventh month of the fourth year of the Kaibao era, the Master manifested illness. He addressed his disciples, saying, "All conditioned phenomena are impermanent;
this is precisely the mark of eternal abiding. Having spoken these words, he passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.

At Bānruò Monastery in Tāizhōu, respectfully following the formal assembly of Chan Master Tōnghuì, he ascended the hall and said: "The world is bright, radiant, and blazing, extending from antiquity to the present.
Never for a moment has there been even the slightest sign of interruption; it is without time or season, a long-standing pressure that leaves the Venerable Upāsaka with no room to breathe.
Therefore it is said: 'Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are the Venerable’s spiritual friend,' emitting light."
The earth shook; it was revealed everywhere that there is not even a thread’s breadth of a dharma that can act as an obstruction.
Why is it that now you do not understand, and instead give rise to doubt in vain? There is nothing to do; do not stand for long. A monk asked, “The *udumbara* flower blooms and all behold it;
please grant us one word on the家风 (household style) of Prajñā. The Master said, “If it were not for your question, sir, it would never have been revealed.”
He cited a person [from the past] and said, "If that is so, then how could the Vulture Peak of Prajñā ever fail to match the present and the past?
The Master said, "Do not misunderstand. A question was asked: "When Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring him flowers?

The Master said, "Where did you see [this]? [The monk] said, "After he saw him, why did they no longer bring flowers? The Master said, "First, you must grasp the meaning of my words. A question was asked: "The Spirit..."
At the first assembly on the mountain, Kāśyapa heard it personally. I do not know who will hear it at this day’s assembly. The Master said, "Try citing what Kāśyapa heard.
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then Kāśyapa has heard it personally. The Master said, "Why do you speak such nonsense? The Master himself composed a true eulogy, saying:
"The Reality is vast and empty; the artisan of Ying applies his paint. The peaks rise high, the clouds fill the void."
The moon leaps from the clear pool;
Mount Lu’s Guizong Cezheng Fashi Chan Master was the son of the Wei clan of Weizhou. His original name was Huichao.
He went to visit Fayan and asked, "I, Huichao, inquire of the Master: what is the Buddha? Fayan said, "You are Huichao."
The Master attained awakening through this. After he had taken up residence, he ascended the hall and said: "Venerable elders, seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing can only occur once.
As for that which is fully understood—is it seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, or is it not seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing?

Do you wish to understand? I have explained it thoroughly for you, venerable elders. Wait until you awaken, and then you will attain it. He stood for a long time. "Take care. A monk asked: "What is..."
The Buddha. The Master said, "I told you that there is something else entirely. Question: "What is the realm of Guizong? The Master said, "What do you see? Question:
"Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Get out! Question: "The King has invited the Master to open a great Dharma assembly.
Without falling into the trap of seeing or hearing, please speak quickly, Master. The Master said, "Idle talk. Question: "Master..."
"What do you think? The Master said, "You are talking nonsense again. The monk asked, "I have heard it said in the teachings:

'To offer this profound mind to the lands of dust—that is called repaying the Buddha's kindness. I do not ask about the lands of dust; what is meant by 'repaying the Buddha's kindness'? The Master said:
"If you are thus, then you repay the Buddha's kindness. [The student] asked: "When the insentient preach the Dharma, the entire earth hears it.

When there is the Lion’s Roar, how is it? The Master said: "Do you hear it yet? [The student] said: "If that is so, then I am the same as the insentient. The Master said: "It seems you understand quite well. [The student] asked:
"The ancients took 'not being separate from seeing and hearing' as their fundamental principle. I wonder, upon what does the Master rely?"
[The monk] made this his thesis. The Master said, "This question is very good. [The monk] said, "Yet it is still just three conditions and four conditions.

The Master said, "Do not speak in such confusion. Chan Master Shaoxian of Tong’an Yuan in Hongzhou was asked by a monk: "The King’s grace has sent down an imperial decree which you have personally received;
I beg for a word on the house style of Mount Xiong’er. The Master said, "It has already been spoken. Another asked: "I have traveled a thousand li to seek you, Master; please grant me an audience."

The Master said, "An excellent point of entry. When a monk was begging for tiles to build a hall at Mount Yungai, a palace lady asked him, "Since it is already named 'Cloud-Covered' (Yungai), why do you need to beg for tiles?
The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "Rare indeed is such a person encountered."
Chan Master Huiyuan of Qixian on Mount Lu ascended the hall and said: "As soon as one leaves the Sangha Hall and sees the Five Elders Peak, the work of a lifetime of study is finished.
What need is there to come here again? Nevertheless, you have troubled this old monk with a visit;
take care. A monk asked: "It is not the wind moving, nor is it the banner moving. I wonder, what was the ancient master's meaning?"
"What is the meaning? The Master said, "The assembly shall understand it all at once. He ascended the hall.

A monk was about to ask a question when the Master pointed at him and said, "Stop! Stop! The monk stepped forward and asked, "I beg the Master to proclaim the ancestral vehicle of the successive patriarchs.
The Master said, "The preceding words have not yet been joined; the subsequent words are difficult to pursue. The monk asked, "I do not know what the matter is today. The Master said, "Not so."
He was adept at conversing with people. Someone asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Excellent. Another asked, "What is the environment of Qixian?
The Master said, "As soon as you enter the three gates, you should know. Yet another asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Excellent."
The Master said: "This land lacks nothing.
Chan Master Congxian of Guanyin Monastery in Hongzhou was a native of Quanzhou. One day he ascended the hall; when the assembly had gathered, after a long silence, he said:
Mañjuśrī praised the layman deeply. I do not know whether the layman accepted this praise or not. If he accepted it, where would the layman be?
If he did not accept it, Mañjuśrī could not have uttered empty words. How does the great assembly understand this?
If you understand it, you are truly a monk. A monk asked: "The layman remained silent, yet Mañjuśrī praised him deeply. What is the meaning of this?"
"What? the Master asked. "You ask and I shall answer. [The monk] said: "If such a person were to suddenly appear before you, what then?
The Master said: "When walking, one reaches the end of the water; sitting, one watches the clouds arise. [The monk] asked: "What is the家风 (household style) of Avalokiteśvara?"
The Master said, "Look right before your eyes. [The monk] asked, "If a true adept were to suddenly arrive, how would you receive him?

The Master said, "In my humble home, things are simply like this; it does not necessarily mean one must depart immediately. [The monk] asked, "I have long carried a stringless lute; I beg the Master to play a melody for me."
The Master said, "How do you listen? The monk tilted his ear. The Master said, "This will ruin people!
He then said, "When Layman Lu was at the head of Dayu Ridge, he said to Venerable Ming, 'Do not think of good; do not think of evil.
Return to me, Venerable Ming, your original face. Guanyin does not speak this way today; return to me, Venerable Ming—"
"Come! When you speak thus, are you a descendant of Caoxi or not? If you are a descendant of Caoxi, why do you still exclude these four characters?
If you are not, where does the fault lie? Come forth and let us deliberate on this!
After a long silence, he said, "This assembly consists of true wandering monks. Thereupon, he descended from his seat. (The ninth month of the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo).
In the middle [of the night], the Master said to his patron, the Regional Inspector Yuan: "I, this old monk, shall return to my hometown in two or three days.
Yuan said, "The Master is advanced in years; why do you still long for your hometown? The Master replied, "I am going home to obtain some good salt to eat. Yuan did not fathom these words.
The following day, the Master passed away while sitting upright, without illness. Yuan erected a stupa for him on West Mountain.
A monk asked Chan Master Qilun of Xingshan in Luoyang, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "How could I possibly say anything to you?
He asked again, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "I still remember it from just now."
A monk asked Zen Master Qi of Xinxing Monastery in Hongzhou, “How can one escape from the three realms?
The Master said, “Do you believe? The monk replied, “I believe deeply; I beg the Master’s compassion. The Master said, “This very mind of faith extends through all antiquity and the present.
You must investigate it swiftly; why linger? To escape the three realms—within the three realms there is only [the mind].”
The Master, because of the snow, said to the assembly: "Do you all, venerable elders, see the snow? If you see it, you have eyes; if you do not see it, you have no eyes.
To have eyes is permanence; to have no eyes is annihilation. If you understand it in this way, the Buddha-body is pervasive.
A student asked: "I am departing for Letan; I beg the Master to show me a path of entry. The Master said: "What an excellent path of entry! It is the Bodhicitta."
Firm and resolute, he followed the assembly in seeking instruction and followed the assembly in performing tasks. When it was time to leave, he left; when it was time to stay, he stayed.
His leaving and staying were for no other reason than these. Upon arriving at Letan, he did not inquire after Mazu.
A monk asked Zen Master Kuangda of Ciyun in Runzhou, "The Buddha appeared in the world for the sake of the one great matter;
I wonder, how is it that you, Master, have appeared in the world? The Master said, "Just so. The monk asked, "How so? The Master said:
Not good. Chan Master Shaoming of Jianfu Monastery in Suzhou was invited by the provincial commander Qian Renfeng to serve as abbot.
The commander asked, "What is the master’s house style? The Master said, "Look everywhere."
While the Zen Master Jinchan of Guzhenyuan in Zezhou was attending Dharma Eye, Dharma Eye asked a monk, "Since leaving here, where have you been?
The monk replied, "I have come from entering the mountain ranges. Dharma Eye said, "Not easy. The monk said, "I have traveled across all those mountains and waters for nothing.
Dharma Eye said, "Those many mountains and waters are not bad either. The monk was speechless. The Master [Jinchan] then—
There was one who attained realization. After he had settled into his practice, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "It strikes right through your nostrils.
He then asked another monk, "The single, firm, and dense body manifests within all dust-motes. What is this firm and dense body? The monk held up a finger.
The Master said, "It is manifest; how do you understand this? The monk was speechless.
Chan Master Kexun of Xingfu Monastery in Xuanchou, a native of the Zhu family of Jianzhou, was asked by a monk, "Who is the true master of Xingfu?
The Master said, "You do not recognize him. The monk asked, "Is it simply this very person? The Master said, "Even if it were not..."
"Cease your madness. What has your head lost? A question was asked: "What is the Way? The Master said: "Practice it with diligence. A question was asked: "Why do you say that dharmas are empty?
The Master said: "They are not empty. He spoke a verse for the assembly: Autumn river, misty islands, clear skies; Gulls and herons stand in rows.
If one does not call upon Avalokiteśvara, How can one know the entry into the Universal Gate?
Chan Master Shoune of Shanglan Monastery in Hongzhou ascended the hall. He said: "The entire command has been taken up; there is no one left to sweep the ground.
You brothers of the monastic community, bear witness together. Those among the later generations who have doubts, please ask your questions. A monk asked:

"I pray you will open the gate of ambrosia and contemplate the primary truth. Without falling into the extremes of existence or non-existence, I request that the Master grant us instruction. The Master said: "Great!"
The assembly testified to this, saying, "If that is so, then do not humiliate us. The Master said, "Idle words.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Ask someone else."
A monk asked Master Fuchuan of Fuzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "I do not know.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Do not slander the Patriarch."
At Fengxian Temple in Hangzhou, a monk asked Chan Master Fagui Faming Puzhao:

"When Śākyamuni appeared in the world, the heavens rained four kinds of flowers and the earth shook in six ways. I wonder what auspicious signs there are today? The Master said, "The entire assembly sees them.
The monk said, "The Dharma King’s Dharma is thus. The Master said, "The Human King is present here now. A monk asked, "Regarding the Precious Seal of the Dharma Eye, Master..."
"The direct transmission—this assembly today—should be entrusted to whom? The Master said, "Who would not have their share?
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then the thunderous sound will universally shake infinite lands. The Master said, "You must listen well."
Chan Master Huilang of Huacheng Temple on Mount Lu was invited by Song Qiqiu, the Chancellor of Jiangnan, to ascend the hall.

The Master ascended the seat and said, "Today, the Lord Chancellor has requested this mountain monk to act for the sake of the assembly. Is it not because you all have received the Buddha’s entrustment and do not forget the Buddha’s kindness?
If there is anyone among the assembly who wishes to pose a question, please come forward to create karmic affinity with the Lord Chancellor. A monk asked, "The Lord Chancellor personally..."
[The Master] descended. The great assembly gathered like clouds. They requested the Master to proclaim the ancestral vehicle (zongcheng) from above.

The Master said, "Is this not to betray the Duke? A monk asked, "The Master constantly admonishes us with bitter words; why is it that we students do not clarify our own fundamental matter? The Master said, "Where, O *śrāmaṇera*, is it not clear?
The monk said, "Regarding that which is not clear, I pray the Master provide a definitive judgment. The Master said, "I told you just now."
"What? he asked. [The monk] replied, "In that case, it is entirely because of today. The Master said, "Step back," and [the monk] performed three prostrations.
A monk asked Chan Master Daohong Tongbian of Huiriji Yongming Temple in Hangzhou: "Having left the realm of Tiantai far behind..."
Coming to ascend Mount Huiri (Wisdom Sun Peak), I have long heard the Lion’s Roar. Today I request that you explain it for me. The Master asked, "Do you hear it?
He replied, "If so, then yesterday was Chongshou and today is Yongming. The Master said, "Fortunately, you are naturally quick-witted; why must you speak so confusedly?
Then he continued, "The Great Way is vast and open, eternally as it has been from antiquity to now. The true mind is all-pervasive, its wisdom as expansive as the Dharma-realm."

Vividly clear! The myriad phenomena, as vast as they are, are all the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*). Encompassing heaven and encompassing earth, spanning from antiquity to the present—does the great assembly understand?
Can you discern this clearly? A monk asked, "The King has issued a gracious command, and you, sir, have graced this assembly with your presence.
May I ask what matter is being addressed today? The Master said, "Examine it for yourself. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Where [is it]?"
[The monk] said, "In that case, it would be a hasty act. The Master said, "Stop speaking nonsense.
A monk asked National Teacher Lingjian of Goryeo, "What is a pure monastery? The Master said, "The cattle pen is.
[Another] monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Drag out that madman!"

A monk asked Master Shangquan of Jingmen, “When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it? The Master said, “I obtain it. The monk asked, “I have traveled from afar to seek you, Master;
how do you receive me? The Master leveled his staff and gazed at him. The monk bowed, and the Master let out a shout.
The monk asked, “What is it like when a foot-long jade disc is without flaw? The Master said, “I do not value it. The monk asked, “And after you do not value it, what then?”
The Master said: "A cricket flies up into the sky from within the fire.
When Chan Master Dun was first residing at Yuantong Temple in the Great Forest Monastery on Mount Lu, a monk cited a case where a monk asked Xuansha: [the rest of the dialogue follows].

Regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school (*zongcheng*), how is it discussed here? Sha said, "Few people listen. [The monk] asked, "I do not yet understand the meaning of Xuansha’s intent.
The Master said, "Wait until you have moved Stone Ear Peak, and I will tell you. (Niu Ruozong offered a different reading:
"For now, keep your voice low.")
A monk asked Zen Master Yuansheng of Renwang Monastery in Chizhou, “What is it like when farmers beat the wooden clappers? The Master said, “The monastic community has its own fundamental duty.
The monk said, “I am not asking about the monastic community’s fundamental duty; what is it like when farmers beat the wooden clappers?
The Master said, “Where is the point of your question?”
Chan Master Zhijue Yan-shou of Huiriji Yongming Temple in Hangzhou,
a descendant of the tenth generation under Qingyuan and a dharma heir of National Teacher Tiantai Shaor, was the son of the Wang family of Yuhang. From his youth...

In his youth, he turned his heart toward the Buddha Vehicle. After reaching adulthood, he abstained from meat and ate but one meal a day. He maintained the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, reciting seven lines at a time;

in barely sixty days, he was able to recite it entirely. He moved the hearts of a flock of sheep, which knelt to listen to him. At the age of twenty-eight, he served as the military commander of Huating.
It happened that Chan Master Cuoyan had moved to Longce Temple to extensively propagate the profound teachings. At that time, Wu...

King Wenmu of Yue, knowing that his master yearned for the Way, acceded to his aspiration. He then received Cuiyan as his teacher and performed manual labor to provide for the assembly, completely forgetting his status as a ruler.
His clothing was not of silk or floss, and his food lacked rich flavors; with wild vegetables and coarse cloth tunics, he passed day and night.
Subsequently, he went to Tianzhu Peak on Mount Tiantai, where he practiced meditative concentration for ninety days. There was a bird, similar to a *chīyàn* (sparrow), that nested [there].

While [Fayan] was within the folds of his robes, he went to visit National Teacher Yao. Upon seeing him once, [Yao] held him in high esteem and secretly transmitted the profound essence of the Dharma to him.

He then said to the Master, "You have a karmic affinity with the Grand Marshal; in the future, you shall greatly propagate the Buddhist teachings. Initially residing at Xuedou, he ascended the hall and said:
"At this place, Xuedou, a torrential waterfall plunges a thousand fathoms without pausing for even a grain of dust; wondrous cliffs rise ten thousand cubits, leaving no foothold."
"Where do you all proceed? Where do you take your next step? A monk asked, "How does one tread upon the single path of Xuedou? The Master said, "Step by step, cold flowers form;
word by word, the ice reaches the very bottom. The Master had a verse that said: "The lone monkey cries, and the moon falls from the middle crag;
The wild guest chants on, as the midnight lamp fades away. In this realm and at this moment, who attains the realization? The white clouds..."
A monk who was practicing seated meditation in a secluded place was invited by King Zhongyi to open the new Lingyin Monastery.
The following year, he moved to the Great Practice Center at Yongming, where the assembly numbered over two thousand. A monk asked, "What is the wondrous purport of Yongming?

The Master said, "Add more incense. The monk said, "Thank you for the instruction, Master. The Master said, "I am glad there is no connection [between your question and my answer]. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Listen."
Take one verse. To understand the intent of Yongming: A lake lies before the gate; When the sun shines, radiance arises;
When the wind comes, waves stir. Question: "I have long been at Yongming; why is it that I do not understand the house style of Yongming? The Master said:

"Understand it at the very point where you do not understand. He asked: "How can one understand at the point where there is no understanding? The Master said: "An elephant calf is born from within the womb of an ox."
"Red dust rises from the blue sea. [The student] asked: "Whether one becomes a Buddha or a patriarch, one cannot escape; whether one transmigrates through the six realms, one likewise cannot escape.
I do not understand where it is that one cannot escape. The Master said: "One cannot escape from the very place you ask. [The student] asked:
"The scriptures state that all Buddhas and all Buddha-dharmas emerge from this sutra. What is this sutra?"
The Master said, "It revolves incessantly for a long time; it is neither meaning nor sound. [The monk] asked, "How should one receive and uphold it?
The Master said, "If you wish to receive and uphold it, you must listen with your eyes open. [The monk] asked, "What is the Great Perfect Mirror? The Master said, "A broken sand pot.
The Master resided at Yongming for fifteen years, ordaining one thousand seven hundred disciples. In the seventh year of the Kaibao era,
He entered Mount Tiantai to bestow the precepts upon approximately ten thousand people. He constantly conferred the Bodhisattva precepts upon the seven classes of followers.

At night, he offered food to spirits and ghosts; in the morning, he released various living creatures in numbers beyond calculation. Six times a day, he scattered flowers while practicing the Way, and with his remaining strength, he recited the *Lotus Sūtra* some thirteen thousand times.
He composed the *Zongjing lu* (Record of the Mirror of the Source) in one hundred fascicles, as well as poems, gāthās, and rhapsodies.
In all, his words amounted to ten million characters and were disseminated beyond the seas.

Upon reading the Master’s teachings, the King of Koguryo dispatched an envoy bearing a letter to express the etiquette of a disciple and to present a *kāṣāya* woven with gold thread, purple crystal beads, and a golden incense burner.

There were thirty-six monks from that country, all of whom had received his seal of transmission. They returned to their native land in succession, each transforming the people of their respective regions.

In the twelfth month of the eighth year of the Kaibō era, he manifested illness. Two days later, he burned incense and addressed the assembly, then sat in the full lotus posture and passed away in tranquility.
The stupa is at Daci Mountain.
Chan Master Pengyan Guangfa of Changshou Monastery in Suzhou was the son of the Qin family of Yongjia. A monk asked, "What is the profound principle?
The Master said, "The four corners lie flat upon the ground. The monk asked, "What is the dharma that is beyond even a hair's breadth? The Master said:
"Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. [The student] said, "In that case, form is itself formlessness.
The Master said, "That too is but a madman’s talk. [The student] asked, "What is the direct word? The Master said, "A thousand detours, ten thousand curves.

[The student] said, "In that case, then everything is not not the whole. The Master said, "What kind of words are those? [The student] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "It is not easy to traverse."
A monk asked Chan Master Kehong of Danning Monastery in Wenzhou, “What is the single path of true correctness? The Master said, “Seven topsy-turvy, eight upside-down.
The monk said, “If that is so, then there is no distinction among the gates of the Dharma. The Master said, “I know you have misunderstood.
The monk asked, “When it is bright and clear, without a single thread of hair, what then? The Master said, “The head of the matter has already fallen. The monk said, “...”
He requested the Master’s instruction. The Master said, "What was just now was not established in vain. The monk asked, "I pray the Master will proclaim the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school.
The Master said, "Your question is far too late. The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall not depart as an immortal. The Master said, "I know well that you will depart in such a manner."
Chan Master Zhifeng of Huayan Monastery on Wuyun Mountain in Hangzhou was a native of Yuhang. From birth, he loathed the smell of meat and blood;
his skin and body were naturally fragrant and pure. He left home to become a monk at an early age and received full ordination at Langzhan Monastery on East Mountain in Lin’an.

He thoroughly mastered the three trainings and fully comprehended both their essential nature and their phenomenal characteristics. Once, he dreamed that he ascended Mount Sumeru and beheld three Buddhas seated in a row:
