Shuguang asked, "Why is there no reflection in the emerald pool? The Master said, "An adept playing with reflections. The monk walked from east to west and stood there.
The Master said, "Not only are you playing with reflections; you are also terrified of your own head."
Chan Master Xibian of Pumen Temple in Hangzhou was a native of Suzhou. King Zhongyi appointed him to preside over Qingtai Temple in Yuezhou, bestowing upon him the title Huizhi.
Later, he moved to the Upper Temple. Ascending the hall, he said: "This mountain monk has always lacked knowledge and insight, and furthermore, I am deficient in learning and retention.
Although I recently attended the National Teacher, I did not receive a single word of instruction. Thus, I have come to this day together with all of you..."

O virtuous ones, you have gathered here; there is not a single dharma that can assist or inspire you further, let alone enable you to distinguish between the monastic and the lay, or to deliberate upon the past and present.
Do you still find fault with this mountain monk? If there are those who do so, tell me: does such a person possess the eye of discernment or not?
Does he understand the principle of host and guest, or not? Those who are beginners and at the start of their training must...
[The Master] examined him closely. A monk asked, "What is the manifestation of spiritual powers through the Universal Gate? The Master said, "If it were so, you would find fault with this old monk.
The monk asked, "How is it when one does not find fault? The Master said, "For now, go down to the hall and reflect upon it.
In the third year of the Taiping Xingguo era, the King of Wuyue went to the imperial court for an audience; the Master accompanied the Precious Pagoda and was seen there.

At Zifu Hall, he was granted purple robes and the title Chan Master Huiming. During the Duan-gong era, he requested to return to his native village, and the Emperor issued an edict granting his request.
He was further bestowed with a poem composed by the Emperor. King Zhongyi provided gold for the Benshan Monastery in Changshu to construct a seven-story brick pagoda two hundred feet high.
Once the work was completed, in the eighth month of the third year of the Zhizhao era, he passed away and was interred in a stupa at the monastery.
In the northwest corner [of the hall]:
Zen Master Yu’an of Guangqing Temple in Hangzhou, a native of the Shen family of Qiantang, ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The priceless jewel—please bestow it upon us.
The Master said, "You are well able to express it. The monk said, "If that is so, then every person is fully endowed with it."
[The monk] departs. The Master says, “Where is the pearl? The monk bows. The Master says, “That too was empty talk.
A monk asks, “When the main points are set forth and the framework established, with both host and guest being positioned, what is the host? The Master says, “I understand this question deeply.
The monk asks, “What is the guest? The Master says, “What did I just say to you? The monk asks, “When the guest and host are in harmony, what then? The Master—

[The student] said, "Your command is not being carried out. [The Master] asked, "The moon of the mind is solitary and perfect; its light swallows the myriad phenomena. What is this light that swallows the myriad phenomena?
The Master said, "The assembly all sees you asking such a question. [The student] said, "As for the light swallowing the myriad phenomena, let the Master speak of it."
"The mind-moon is solitary and full; what is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Exert your spirit!

[The monk] said, "A heron perched in a snow nest may still be distinguished, but when its light swallows the ten thousand phenomena, the matter is difficult to clarify. The Master said, "Withdraw with care. [The monk] asked, "Green mountains and blue waters are clear everywhere.
As for the house style of our Master, I beg you to grant us a single phrase. The Master said, "It has all been spoken by you already. [The monk] said, "Not yet."
"It must be so. Please, Master, answer me. The Master said, "No need for idle talk. Another monk was just about to prostrate when the Master said, "Question and answer are both complete.
As the monk prepared to ask a question, the Master rebuked him. He ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to know the purport of Caoxi, look at the clouds flying over the mountain before you.
This is clearly the true reality; there is no need to seek elsewhere. A monk asked: "An ancient worthy once said..."
"Dust arises from the bottom of the well; waves surge from the mountain peak. "I do not understand the meaning of this; how should I regard it?
The Master said, "If you go to other places, simply ask in this manner. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Master's intent? The Master said, "What did I just say to you?

He then continued, "From ancient times until now, the tradition has been handed down such that all say: 'Dust arises from the bottom of the well; waves surge from the mountain peak. This forms a karmic bond."
"Flowers in the sky; a child born to a barren woman. How do you understand this? Is it that you are matching sounds to convey meaning, or using objects to manifest the mind?
Is it a point where the blade is hidden within the phrase, or is it fully revealed before the sound? Is it that there is the name but no substance, or is it a wondrous discourse of a different tune?
You may understand it yourself, but the intent of the ancients was not like this. Since you cannot understand it in such a way,"
How do you understand this? Elder, do you wish to understand it? Simply look at where the earthen ox walks: the mirage turns into waves;
when the wooden horse neighs, the flowers in the sky cast their shadows. Thus it is with the holy and the ordinary; the principle is clear.
Why need you stand here for long? Take care.
Chan Master Youchan of Tiantai Banruo Monastery was a native of Qiantang. He first resided at Yunju Puxian Monastery, where the Prince of Zhongyi appointed him as Chan Master Ciwu.
He subsequently moved to Upper Monastery, where his assembly numbered over five hundred. A monk asked, "The drum has just finished sounding and the great assembly has gathered like clouds;
we pray that the Master will proclaim the supreme vehicle of our school. The Master said, "What is lacking in you? The monk replied, [silently].
"If that is so, then everyone has received the grace," [the monk] said. The Master said, "Do not speak recklessly.
When Chan Master Quanken of Zhiye Monastery in Wuzhou first visited National Teacher Huizhong, the National Teacher asked him, "What is your name?"
The Master said, "I fully agree. The National Teacher asked, "What is it that you agree with? At these words, the Master attained realization and prostrated himself.
Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "If someone does not agree, will you still accept it? The Master said, "If anyone asks me, I shall simply tell them so."
Chan Master Yilong of Yushan in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "The mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all within the eyes of everyone.
Why, then, do you speak of 'understanding' and 'not understanding'? At that time, a monk asked: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are within the eyes."
The Master now wished to point further toward whom. The Master said, "It is precisely because the Elder’s destination is clear.

The Elder said, "If you had not come here to pose this question, how would I know that your skillful means were not applied in vain? The Master said, "Vaguely resembling a melody, it is barely fit to be heard;
yet it is blown by the wind into another tune."
Chan Master Xiaorong of Longce Monastery in Hangzhou was the son of the Deng family of Wenzhou. A monk asked, "The patriarchs have transmitted it from one to another;
I wonder, Master, to whom do you transmit it? The Master replied, "Do you even recognize the patriarchs? The monk Huwen then asked:
"What is a true śramaṇa? The Master said, "You are Huìwén. The student asked, "What is the great divine pearl of prajñā?
The Master said, "The great divine pearl of prajñā manifests ten billion forms; in every atom its wondrous essence is revealed, and in every world-realm it is entirely Vairocana.
The student asked, "What is the matter of daily life? The Master said, "A single thought encompasses the entire dharma-realm; this is the matter of daily life."

All things are penetrated; it is profoundly and eternally quiescent. He constantly displays his own house style. Following the small session of instruction, a monk asked: "I do not ask about matters above this;
what is the precise meaning of the 'Pavilion of Wondrous Goodness'? The Master said: "If you go to other places..."
He spoke clearly and pointedly, saying: "If it were so, then the clouds would have the appearance of leaving the mountains, and the water would lack the sound of plunging into the ravine.
The Master then rebuked him. A monk asked Zen Master Qingxiao of Gongchen in Hangzhou, "What is the家风 (house style) of Gongchen? The Master said: "Clear."
"Darkness, color, and space," [the Master] said. [The monk] asked, "If that is so, then all phenomena are non-arising.
The Master said, "What do you call 'all phenomena'? The monk bowed. The Master said, "Listen to this verse: The family style of the Accomplished One: Brightness, darkness, color, and space.
Dharma after dharma is not different; Mind after mind naturally penetrates. If you understand it thus, you have grasped the true essence of all Buddhas."
A monk asked Chan Master Jingjin of Cheshen in Yuezhou, "I have packed my bags; please, Master, give me your instructions.
The Master said, "Do not try to evade it. The monk said, "In what way have I failed the Master? The Master said, "It is you, rather, who have failed me."
Chan Master Shishu of Yanfeng in Fuzhou ascended the seat for the opening of the hall. Master Jile asked, "The assembly looks up with eager expectation;
please thunder forth the Dharma drum. The Master said, "Does the assembly understand? Can you discern it?
Today is no different from Vulture Peak, nor even from the lands of all Buddhas; whether in the heavens or among men, it is everywhere thus, throughout all eternity."
Now, it is eternally without change. How do you understand this principle of being without change? If you can understand it, then it is said:
"The realms of infinite lands are not separated from one another by so much as a hair’s tip; ten ages of past and present, from beginning to end, do not depart from the present moment.
A monk asked: "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa heard [the Buddha] directly. At the assembly on Mount Yanfeng, who is it that hears?"
The Master said, "The questioner is no weakling. A monk asked, "What is Mañjuśrī? The Master said, "His place of origin is very clear.
Chan Master Huida of Huayan in Lu Prefecture was asked by a monk, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
He was further asked, "What is the realm of Huayan? The Master said, "Everywhere before one’s eyes, there is no form or shadow."
A monk asked Chan Master Daoyuan of Qingtai Monastery in Yuezhou, "Where has the deceased monk gone after his transformation?
The Master said, "Today he has transformed in the midst of the ridge. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said, "I cannot tell you that it is the cypress tree in front of the courtyard.
Chan Master Qingxiang of Jiuqu Guanyin Monastery in Hangzhou was a native of Yuhang.

His eloquence surpassed all others, and his vast learning and powerful memory were such that he was regarded as preeminent among the disciples of the Tiantai school. A monk asked: "It is profoundly still and perfectly luminous; I pray the Master [to explain it]."
[The Master] said: "A vast lake ten li wide; a single orb of autumn moon. [The student] asked: "In the midst of perilous and evil paths, what serves as the ferry and the bridge?
The Master said: "This very thing serves as the ferry and the bridge. [The student] asked: "What is 'this'? The Master said:
"It strikes right at your nostrils. [The student] asked: "Where does one plant the rootless tree? The Master said: "From where did you get that?"
Chan Master Xingming of Kaishua Temple in Hangzhou was the son of the Yu family of that province. He took Zen Master Zhijue of Xuedou as his teacher.
When Zhijue moved to Yongming, Xingming subsequently entered the quarters of National Teacher Guanding at Tiantai and received the transmission of the Dharma.
He returned once more to Yongming to assist and support his master, becoming an object of veneration for the assembly of monks from all directions. King Zhongyi constructed six...
At Wa-ji (a temple granted the imperial title of *Kaikwa* by the Japanese court), he was invited to serve as abbot. He gathered disciples and preached the Dharma.
A monk asked, "What is the skillful means that flows forth from within the Gate of Kaikwa? The Master said, "The sound of the tide is heard twice every day.
The monk asked, "What is the lamp of inexhaustibility? The Master said, "Thank you, Reverend, for your illumination."
A monk asked Chan Master Yiyuan of Kaishan Temple at Yupu in Yuezhou: "One year departs, and another year arrives;
within the gate of skillful means, we pray that you, Master, will open it for us. The Master said, "Take this clearly to heart.
The monk said, "If so, then the lion’s roar of former times is today the elephant king’s return. The Master said, "For now, rejoice that there is no connection."
Chan Master Yuan’an of the Upper Hall at Ruiluo Monastery in Wenzhou was a native of Fuzhou. He received the Dharma from Tiantai and frequently studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.
Upon reaching the passage, "When knowledge and vision establish knowledge, that is the root of ignorance; when knowledge and vision are without seeing... [he attained realization].
"This is precisely nirvāṇa. The Master then read it by breaking the phrasing: "When knowledge and vision are established, knowledge is the root of ignorance;
when knowledge and vision are absent, this very absence is nirvāṇa. At these words, he attained realization. Someone said to the Master, "You have broken the phrasing completely!
The Master replied, "This is the point of my enlightenment; I shall not change it for the rest of my life. At that time, he was called An Lengyan (An of the Śūraṅgama). When [he reached]...

In the spring of the first year of Daoyuan, as he was about to pass into nirvana, his heir Yuren stood in attendance. The Master then spoke a verse to him: "It is not a matter carried from the mountain peak;
How could it have been transmitted from Mount Kukkutapāda? Since antiquity, all sages and worthies have been thus;
It is not I alone who today fashions this for you. Having completed his final instructions, he bathed himself, changed his robes, sat upright, and ordered the coffin to be brought forward.

Upon arriving at the chamber, after a long while, he entered the coffin himself. After three days had passed, his disciples opened the coffin and beheld the Master lying in the auspicious posture on his right side.
The fourfold assembly was overcome with grief and lamentation. The Master then rose again, ascended the hall to preach the Dharma, and rebuked them with these admonitions:
"Whoever opens my coffin again in this lifetime shall not be my true child. Having spoken these words, he once more entered the coffin and departed for eternity.
Chan Master Huiju of Longhua Temple in Hangzhou was a native of Min. Having received the essential instructions from Tiantai, King Zhongyi ordered him to reside at the aforementioned temple.
Upon opening the hall to address the assembly, he said: "Regarding the ancestral vehicle of the school, how can it be proclaimed here?"
It is just as when Śākyamuni Buddha preached the teachings of his entire lifetime—like pouring water from one vessel into another.
Even the ancient worthies have said that these are like the events of a dream or the babbling of sleep-talking. But tell me, by what principle can it be said so?

Do you understand? The Great Gate of Giving is open; how has it ever been obstructed? It gives birth to ordinary beings and nurtures sages, without leaking even a speck of dust. To speak of the "ordinary" means...
When the ordinary is fully realized, the sage is fully realized; the ordinary and the sage do not depend upon one another, for each and every one is uniquely honored. Therefore it is said:
"The mountains, rivers, and the great earth preach the Dharma at all times and radiate light at all times; earth, water, fire, and wind are each likewise."

At that time, a monk came forward to pay his respects. The Master said, "What a fine question! Ask it according to the Dharma. As the monk prepared to step forward, the Master said, "Again, you have missed the point.
The monk asked, "When the Buddhas appear in the world, they emit light and cause the earth to tremble. When you, Master, appear in the world..."

"What auspicious signs are there? The Master said, "The head of the discourse breaks of itself. He ascended the hall and said: "At Longhua, here, it is simply a matter of gathering firewood and selecting vegetables;
coming up and going down; one bowl of gruel in the morning and one meal at the time of the midday offering; drinking tea after sleep—just practice in this way.
Take care! A monk asked: "The student has not yet clarified his own nature; how can he distinguish between shallow and deep? The Master...
[The Master] said, "Recognize your own eye. [The monk] asked, "What is your own eye? The Master said, "What did I say to you?
Zen Master Yuzhen of Qiyun Mountain in Wuzhou was a native of the Yang family in Yue Province.

A monk asked, "What is the seamless stupa? The Master said, "Five or six feet. The monk bowed, and the Master said, "The stupa has collapsed. [Another monk] asked, "What is perfect clarity? The Master said, "..."
"Master, why does this perfect awareness not arise from mental thought? The Master said, "It is a perfectly clear and lucid awareness.
The monk asked, "How is it different from mental thought? The Master said, "What do you call 'mental thought'? Sitting idly on an autumn evening, he spontaneously composed this verse:

"The autumn courtyard is solemn, the wind whistles; Cold stars line the sky, the moon’s orb is high. Leaning my chin on my hand, I sit in stillness, my spirit unwearied. In the bird’s nest there is no..."
Duan blew on a tuft of cloth.
Zen Master Benshan of Ruizhu Temple in Wenzhou was the son of the Zheng family of his native province.

He visited National Teacher Tiantai, who guided him with the words, "It is not the wind or the banner that moves; it is your own mind that moves. The Master immediately attained realization. Thereafter, he instructed his disciples, saying:
When I first studied the Tiantai Dharma-gate, I attained realization upon hearing a single word.

Nevertheless, for a thousand days, throughout the four modes of conduct, it was as if an object were obstructing my chest, and as if I were dwelling with an enemy. After those thousand days, within a single day, that object no longer obstructed my chest.

The two rivals were no longer at odds; they attained peace and joy in that very moment and suddenly realized their former faults. They then composed three verses. First: "It is not the wind or the banner that moves;
it is the mind of the benevolent one that moves. He said: "Neither the wind nor the banner moves; it is only the mind that moves. This has been transmitted from antiquity down to the present day.
Hereafter, those who wander as water and clouds [monks] who wish to understand—this Patriarch is truly a fine connoisseur. Second: "Upon seeing form, one sees [the Buddha]."
The Master said: "If seeing form is itself seeing the mind, then when someone comes to question you, you will find it difficult to answer.

You will seek out various principles and explanations at great length, thereby failing the three matters of your lifelong practice as a monk. Third, clarifying one's own self: It has been thus throughout vast kalpas;
thus it is the same as heaven and the same as earth. Being the same as earth and the same as heaven, what form could there be? What form could there be?"
There was nothing he did not do. From that time on, the Master never set foot in cities or towns; his hands never handled wealth or goods; he provided no bedding or mats; he wore no silk or cocoons.
He ate but one meal a day and remained in meditative seclusion throughout the entire day. From dawn until dusk, he exhorted and guided others for more than thirty years.
His resolve became even more rigorous. Ascending the hall, he said: "Do you all see the bamboo grove hermitage, the mountain streams, the courtyards, and the assembly?

If you say you see them, then there are dharmas outside the mind. If you say you do not see them, how can you deny that the bamboo grove hermitage, the mountain streams, the courtyards, and the assembly are vividly present right here? Do you understand such an instruction? If you understand..."
It is not without its sharp utility. When there is nothing to do, do not stand. Ascending the hall: Generally speaking, in the study of the Way, it is not necessarily "learning.
Questioning the Master is not necessarily "learning. Selecting phrases is not necessarily "learning. Providing a substitute response is not necessarily "learning.
Offering a divergent response is not necessarily "learning. Unraveling the extraordinary and marvelous words within the sutras and treatises is [the true study].
Studying does not necessarily mean that merely unraveling the extraordinary words of the patriarchs constitutes true study.

If one studies in such a manner, no matter how thoroughly you may master them—reaching the seventh or eighth level of penetration—if you still lack a place of realization within the Buddha-dharma, you are called a follower of "dry wisdom" (*śuṣka-prajñā*).
Have you not heard the ancient masters say: "Cleverness cannot withstand birth and death; those of dry wisdom cannot escape the wheel of suffering"? All...
If a person is to engage in study, they must engage in true study before they can succeed. When walking, walk while studying;
when standing, stand while studying; when sitting, sit while studying; when sleeping, sleep while studying; when speaking, speak while studying;
when silent, remain silent while studying. At all times of performing tasks, at all times of performing tasks, study.
"Take it up. Since you have come to investigate at such times as these, tell me: whom do you take up for investigation? What words do you take up for investigation?

At this point, you must personally arrive at a state of clarity before you can succeed. If it is not like this, you are called a person of hasty action; then you will lack the principle of ultimate penetration.
[The Master] ascended the hall and said: "A bird calls in the deep forest; a fish leaps in the clear stream; a sheet of cloud unfurls."
[The Master] stretched out his arms. "The sound of the waterfall resounds like a sobbing cry. Do you all recognize such a multitude of phenomena? Shall I show you an entrance?
If you can recognize it, you may proceed with your study; that would be well. He ascended the hall and said:
"In the teachings of Tiantai, three gates are spoken of: Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and Samantabhadra. The gate of Mañjuśrī is all forms; the gate of Avalokiteśvara is all sounds."
The Gate of Samantabhadra is reached without moving a step. My Way says the Gate of Mañjuśrī is not all forms;
the Gate of Avalokiteśvara is not all sounds. What, then, is the Gate of Samantabhadra? Do not say it is something other than the discourse of the Tiantai teachings.
There is nothing more to do; please withdraw. Ascending the hall, he raised an example: A monk asked Changsha, "Nanquan passed away..."
"Where has the transformation gone? The monk said, "I do not understand. The monk said, "If you wish to ride, then ride;

if you wish to dismount, then dismount. Nanquan said, "If it were a person seeking to transcend the three realms and practice the Way, upon hearing these words, they would surely be filled with doubt and surely be struck with fear. Nanquan Qian.
"Where does this transformation go? It becomes a donkey for the eastern neighbor and a horse for the western neighbor. Some understand it by saying:

"A thousand transformations and ten thousand changes do not go beyond the true and eternal. Some understand it by saying: "One must realize the practice within the midst of different species before one can truly grasp these words.
Some understand it by saying: "The eastern neighbor is Nanquan; the western neighbor is Nanquan. Some understand it by saying: [silence].
"The gentleman of the eastern house; the gentleman of the western house. Some understand this by saying, "What is the eastern house? What is the western house?
Some understand this by braying like a donkey and neighing like a horse. Still others understand it thus: [and they remain silent].
What do you call the donkey of the eastern house? What do you call the horse of the western house? Some understand this by saying:

"Since he asks about his passing away, the answer lies in the question itself. Some understand it by saying: "He has gone to where the pillar stands. Others understand it by saying: [the rest of the response].

"The house to the east becomes a donkey; the house to the west becomes a horse. Wherein does Nanquan suffer loss? Thus do these various houses understand; they all find peace within the Buddha-dharma.
When Nanquan passed away, where did he go? 'The house to the east becomes a donkey; the house to the west becomes a horse.
Students do not understand this: if one wishes to ride, one rides; if one wishes to dismount, one dismounts. This matter requires no further elaboration."
One attains realization through many principles. If you see the nature of the Dharma-realm, even going and coming are without many affairs.
Take care. [Ascending the hall: The form and shadow within a mirror depend solely upon the light of the mirror to manifest.
As for all the things you people do, tell me: upon what do they depend to manifest? Do you know this yet? If you do know it, then within your study of the Way—
"Enough, enough. No more. Do not stand there. He ascended the hall and said: "All of you, during the deep sleep of the night, you were unaware of anything.
Since you were unaware of anything, let me ask you: did you possess your original nature at that time, or did you not?
If you say that your original nature existed at that time, yet you were unaware of anything, you would be no different from being dead. If you say..."
At that time, there was no inherent nature. One suddenly awakens from sleep and perceives as before. Do you understand? To not know [this] is no different from death;
yet one suddenly awakens from sleep and perceives as before. At such times as these, what is this?
If you do not understand, each of you must investigate it for yourselves. When there is nothing to do, do not stand idly. [He] ascended the hall and said: "All phenomena arise only..."
These are mental manifestations. Such speech is an excellent gateway for entry. Now, let me ask you all:

when the eye sees all forms, the ear hears all sounds, the nose smells all fragrances, the tongue discerns all tastes, the body touches all that is soft and smooth, and the mind discriminates all phenomena—just as it is with the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind...
As for these objects that are confronted: are they merely your own minds, or are they not your own minds?
If you say they are merely your own minds, why do they not merge into a single mass with your bodies and simply cease to exist?
Why, then, do these confronted objects remain outside of your eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and bodies? If you say it is because of the eyes...
The objects encountered by the ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not your own minds.
Furthermore, how can one deny that all dharmas arise solely as manifestations of the mind? These words remain in the world;
who would not raise them up? Do you understand this talk? If you do not yet understand, let us all apply our minds together to discuss and master it. Thank you.

He remained there, ensuring that no one grew weary of their studies; he told them, "There is nothing more to do, so you may withdraw. In the second month of the first year of the Dazhong Xiangfu era, he said to his senior disciple, Ruzhou:
"A stone niche should be constructed. On the full moon of the eighth month, I shall pass away. Ruzhou received the command and completed the work immediately.
When the appointed time arrived, scholars and commoners from near and far rushed to pay their respects. On that day, he conducted his inquiries as usual until noon.
Sitting in the abbot’s quarters, the Master formed the Jewel Seal with his hands and asked Dayzhou, "The ancients said: 'Ride the tiger's head, strike the tiger's tail;
as for the matter of the center, what is it? Dayzhou replied, 'It is also just like Dayzhou. The Master said, 'Ask me yourself. Dayzhou then asked."
"Ride the tiger's head; strike the tiger's tail. As for the matter of the center, how do you handle it, Master? The Teacher replied, "I too cannot bring myself to play with this.
Having said this, he suddenly passed away. He opened one eye and looked faintly before his life departed.
While Master Hongshou of Xingjiao Monastery in Hangzhou was working together with the National Teacher, he attained realization upon hearing a piece of firewood fall.

He composed a verse, saying: "Where it falls, it is not another thing; In its spreading and gathering, it is no mere dust. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth— The entire body of the Dharma King is revealed."
A monk asked Chan Master Daoyuan of Chengtian Yongan in Suzhou, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Shoo! You outcaste! The monk said, "I am a beginner; I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, "What are you asking?
The monk said, "I am asking about the Buddha. The Master said, "Shoo! You outcaste!"

Chan Master Daoci of Yunju in Hongzhou, a successor of Chan Master Qingliang Qin, was the son of the Jin family of that same prefecture. He traveled extensively through various Chan assemblies, yet his desire for study remained insatiable.
Later, he served as the librarian at Shanglan Temple. One day, Faden said to the Master, "Someone has asked me—"
[The Master asked about] the meaning of the Westward Journey. The other replied, "Neither east nor west. The Librarian asked, "How do you understand this?
The Master responded, "Neither east nor west. Yunmen said, "Even if you understand it thus, how can you attain it? [The Master] said, "Daoji is exactly like that;
I wonder what your honorable intention is, Reverend Sir? Yunmen said, "He has his own descendants. Thereupon, the Master suddenly attained clear understanding.

The essential meaning is as expressed in this verse: "Receiving beings and benefiting life is most exquisite; External birth ultimately results in unworthiness. One’s own family naturally has its own descendants;
When brought forth, they are used with perfect appropriateness. After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Who are you? The monk asked, "In a thicket of brambles there is no way out; I pray that the Master will use skillful means to clear a path for me. The Master said, "You..."
"Where do you intend to go? He replied, "I have almost not come here. The Master said, "Idle talk.
A monk asked, "If one does not avoid saṃsāra and does not seek liberation, what then? The Master said, "Have you ever questioned Jian-shan? The monk said, "The student does not understand."
He requested the Master’s expedient means. The Master said, “I grant you thirty blows. He asked, “What are the Three Jewels? The Master said, “What jewel are you? [The monk] said, “How so?

The Master said, “Earth, wood, tiles, and pebbles. The Master composed *Zhuoyuyao* (Essentials of Recorded Words), *Souxuan* (Searching for the Mysterious), *Niangu* (Culling Ancestors), *Dibie* (Discriminating Differences), and other works, which circulated widely throughout the monastic communities.
In the ninth month of the third year of the Zhide era (the Dingyou year), he manifested illness while the bell was tolling.
He gathered the assembly and said: "I, this old monk, have served as abbot in three places for over thirty years.
Throughout this time, you brothers from the ten directions have gathered here to discuss the Way, and the administrative officers and head monks have assisted with diligent hearts.
Today, as fire and wind press upon me, I have come specifically to meet you all. Do you see me? If you see me today, it is my final expedient means. [The assembly]—you all...
In what place do you see? Do you see it within the four great elements and the five aggregates? Or do you see it within the six entrances and the twelve bases?
If you can see it here, it may be said that for twenty years at Yunju Mountain, the junior disciples have had something to rely upon.
After I depart, I entrust the mountain gate and the great assembly to Qi Hui to open the hall and serve as abbot. In all matters, carry them out with diligence. Each of you must exert yourselves!
"Power! Be careful! As soon as the assembly had dispersed, the Master returned to his quarters in the western wing and passed away. He was interred in a stupa at his home mountain.

Regarding the Dharma successor of Chan Master Lingyin Song, Chan Master Daoci of Gongchen Monastery in Hangzhou: A monk asked, "The Master has ascended the jeweled throne, and the great assembly has all arrived. Then—
"Please proclaim the teaching. The Master said, "The great assembly bears witness. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then it has been thus from the beginningless past until the endless future.
The Master said, "You must still understand the meaning of these words."
Chan Master Yuanshao of Luohan Monastery in Xiuzhou was a native of Qiantang. He ascended the hall and said: "The mountains, rivers, and the great earth are true spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
They constantly preach the Dharma and perpetually deliver sentient beings. It does not hinder you, venerable monks, from investigating this for yourselves. A monk asked:

"Regarding the house style of the Arhats, I pray that the Master will grant us a single phrase. The Master said: "The grain ears of Jiahe grow together; the fragrance is transmitted to the capital. [The monk] said: "... (The text ends here).
"This is still the family style of the Jiahe [Jiaye] clan. What is the family style of the Arhat clan? The Master said, "If you go to various places, explain it clearly there.
Later, while residing at Xiangyan Temple in Hangzhou, a monk asked, "Without establishing even a speck of dust, please, Master, speak directly.
The Master said, "Everyone will laugh at you. The monk asked, "How should I understand this? The Master said, "Give me back the head of the story."
A monk asked Master Shizhi of Baoen Monastery in Chuzhou, “What is the house style of the Master?

The Master said, “Who does not see it? The monk asked, “What is the samādhi of one mark? The Master said, “Blue, yellow, red, and white. The monk asked, “Where is the one mark? The Master said, “You are indeed quick-witted.
The monk asked, “From patriarch to patriarch, the patriarchal seal has been transmitted; what is the Dharma you now transmit? The Master said—
"Who is this person? The Master said, "Before Vulture Peak, the lunar disc is bright and clear.
A monk asked Chan Master Xian of Huining in Quzhou, "What is the house style of Huining? The Master said, "Thank you for pointing it out.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, "Why do you find the old monk strange? The monk said, "I, your student..."
"No. [The monk] requested, "I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, "Was it not just now that you asked about the meaning of the Westward Coming?
A monk asked Chan Master Daodu of Guangxiao Monastery in Hangzhou, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Ask with a loud voice. The monk said, "Is it not this very thing? The Master said, "There is no connection. Later, he resided at Lingyin and passed away.
When Chan Master Neng of Baiching Monastery on Mount Xi in Hangzhou ascended the seat for his formal opening address, two monks prostrated themselves at the same time.
The Master said, "Both of you are mistaken. As the monks were about to offer a word in response, the Master immediately descended from the seat.
Chan Master Bianlong of Zhiti in Fuzhou, a native of Mingzhou, ascended the hall and said:
"The majestic and sublime reality-mark (dharmatā) fills all of empty space; its adamantine essence is indestructible. Does the great assembly see it or not?
If you say you see it, yet the essence of reality-mark is fundamentally neither blue, yellow, red, nor white, neither long, short, square, nor round—it is also not something seen."
Regarding the dharmas of hearing, awakening, and knowing—how can one explain the principle of "seeing"?
If you say one does not see, yet it is also said that the sublime reality (dharmatā) fills the void of space; why then is it not seen? A monk asked, "What is the path that leads upward?
The Master said, "Right under your feet. The monk said, "In that case, we are constantly treading upon it. The Master said, "Do not err."
[The Master] acknowledged. [The student] asked, "What is the firm and dense body? The Master said, "Nakedly. [The student] said, "If that is so, then it is not dense.
The Master said, "What have you seen?"
A monk asked Chan Master Xiyuan of Ruelong Monastery in Hangzhou, "What is the master’s house style?
The Master said, "I thank you, Venerable, for asking. The monk said, "There is no doubt that you have been asked; what is the house style? The Master said, "Sleeping fool!"
A monk asked Chan Master Xinglin Zuyin of Luohan Monastery in Nan’gang Commandery, successor to Chan Master Rou of Guizong: "The heavens shed sweet dew and the earth wells up the seven treasures;
in whose sphere of experience does this occur? The Master said, "Thank you for informing me. The monk said, "If that is so, then it is the business of a Buddha’s son."

"Abiding in this ground is precisely the Buddha’s enjoyment of going. The Master said, "You must still be thorough about this. As soon as he sat upon the high seat in the hall, a cat suddenly leaped onto his body.
The Master picked it up and showed it to the assembly, saying, "In the past, Nanquan personally slew one such as this."
"Early this morning, Yaśas showed [the truth] to the disciples of the profound; now he sells it to these various Chan guests. Is the written contract clear and certain?
After a long silence, he threw down a cat and descended from his seat."
A monk asked Master Xinxin of Tiantong in Mingzhou, “What is the secret function? The Master said, “When has it ever been secret?
The monk asked, “How is it when the path of the mind has not yet been traversed? The Master said, “What thing is obstructing you? The monk asked, “How is it when one seeks but cannot find?
The Master said, “Why seek it? The monk said, “What then is the case? The Master said, “When has it ever been lost?”

Question: "What is the realm of Tiantong? The Master said: "When the clouds have no one to plant them, how can they reach their limit? When the waters have no one to teach them, why do they flow on without returning?
A monk asked Zen Master Jueke Xinyin of Gōngshèn in Hangzhou: "The Patriarch is not on the mountains of the east or the west. [The Master replied: "He has not yet..."
"Examine closely where it is. The Master said, "Go and seek it for yourself. He asked, "What is the true-born Buddha? The Master said, "How would one dare to adorn it?
Chan Master Qingjian of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Qiantang. The Master’s conduct was solitary and pure; at that time, people said of him:
This is from the *Zhejiang Ke* (Record of the Zhejiang Guest). A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said, "I do not wish to tell you. The monk said, "Please, Reverend, tell me. The Master said, "Bodhidharma cannot come again. The Master lived at Xuedou in his later years and passed away there;
his stupa was erected in the southeast corner of the monastery.
Chan Master Chengzhi of Qixian on Mount Lu, a dharma successor of Chan Master Heng of Baizhang, was asked by a monk: "At Zhaozhou’s Stone Bridge, donkeys and horses were ferried across;
at the Stone Bridge of the Three Gorges, who should be ferried across? The Master replied, "Shrimp and earthworms. The monk said, "In that case, every single thing is moistened [by the Dharma]."
[The monk] said, “Thank you. The Master said, “You have not stepped upon it. [The monk] asked, “Yesterday, the Master finished his chanting at Xian-dong;

today, Xi-xian invites the Master to proclaim [the Dharma]. The Master said, “What will you do tomorrow? [The monk] said, “I do not yet know how to comprehend this. The Master said, “The arrow has already passed to Silla.
[The monk] asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Zhang San and Li Si. [The monk] asked, “What was the intent behind the ancients’ slaying of the snake?”
"How is it? The Master said, "You still do not know pain or itch. The student asked, "This is the field for selecting Buddhas; one returns having attained the 'first place' with an empty mind.
How can a student attain that first-place degree and return? The Master said, "Lacking talent, I respectfully withdraw. In the evening assembly, when the multitude had gathered, the Master said:
He did not meet with anyone that morning. That evening, he said, "Tonight we must not remain without speaking," and then descended from his seat.
He asked, "When the Seer Viśvāmitra took Sudhana by the hand, he saw as many Buddhas as there are motes of dust. But what did he see before he took the hand?
The Master replied, "What do you see now? Ascending the hall, the Master sat for a long while and then said, "How fortunate to have this one bowl of rice."
"One must not sprinkle pepper and ginger [into it]. Nevertheless, try taking a bite. Thereupon, he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Wanshou Dexing of Suzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The assembly gazes upon him all at once.
Questioned again, "What is the one phrase for the Master’s guidance of others? The Master said, "You should first guide yourself. He then said:
Question and answer are both complete; who among you has grasped the meaning? If you seek it elsewhere, you will merely end up acting in a perfunctory manner.

This old monk has long dwelt in the deep mountains, intending to hide his ineptitude; yet I never expected that today I would enter the gate of Wanshou, where it can truly be said that it cannot be hidden.
Since it cannot be hidden, it is clearly revealed. I wonder, among you all, who sees it first? If there is anyone...
[The Master] said, "Come forth and reveal your message before the assembly. After a long silence, he said, "I have stood for a long time; take care.
Yunmen Yongxi Chanshi of Yuezhou was asked by a monk, "What is it like when the lion has not yet emerged from its den?
The Master said, "Do not roar for now. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after it has emerged from the den? The Master said, "Step back. [The monk] asked, "What is..."
Regarding "the tracks of the ancient Buddhas," the Master said, "Who does not tread upon them? Question: "What is the place where the student lets the mind rest and ceases its intentions?
The Master said, "Have you even managed to break the staff? Question: "When the Mind-King issues an edict, what then? The Master said: [silence].
"Recite it once more and see. Question: "What is the definitive meaning? The Master said: "It must not be clung to. Question:
"What is the great purport of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "This purport is no small matter."
Chan Master Kuangsheng of Qianguangwang Temple in Hangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yongming Quan. He was the son of the Zheng family of Wenzhou.

Having left home at a young age, he thoroughly studied the Vinaya-piṭaka and listened to the *Tiantai Wenju*. He settled his mind in the Perfect and Sudden *Zhi-guan* (Calming and Contemplation). Later, he read the *Lengyan jing wen*.
The principles were vast and profound; he was unable to penetrate them fully. One night, after reciting the sutras for a long time, he dozed off at his desk.
In his dream, he saw a solar disc descend from the sky and opened his mouth to swallow it. From that moment on, he suddenly attained awakening regarding the various gates of doctrinal meaning.

He was suddenly liberated and free from all obstructions. Later, he joined the assembly at Yongming Temple. Yongming merely confirmed his previous understanding and offered no further instructions or metaphors.
Instead, he bestowed upon him the patched robe (kāṣāya) left behind by King Zhongyi as a token of faith. After taking up residence there, he ascended the hall and addressed the assembly:

"Venerable elders, the Buddha-dharma is without affairs. The sun and moon of the past are the sun and moon of today; the wind and rain of the past are the wind and rain of today; the heavens of the past are the heavens of today..."
[The Master] took his seat. Today, the Elder has finished both the formal presentation and the discourse; everything has been perfectly manifested. Take care.

In the seventh month of the fifth year of the Kaibō era, a jeweled tree and bathing pool suddenly appeared before him. The Master said, "All phenomena that possess marks are entirely illusory. Three days later, he manifested illness.
He gathered the assembly to bid them farewell, sat upright, and passed away. His body was cremated, and the *śarīra* relics were collected.
The construction of the pagoda.
At the monastery of Chan Master Zhen Cheng in the jurisdiction of Quzhou, a monk asked: "What is the sword that stabilizes heaven and earth?

The Master said: "It does not leak so much as a hair's breadth. The monk asked: "How is it used? The Master said: "One does not know. Later, during a communal work session (*pùqǐng*), a monk asked: "As for the hoe..."
"If one injures the head of a frog or an earthworm, is there still sin or not? The Master said, "Who was it that dealt the blow?
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then there is no transgression. The Master said, "Cause and effect are clearly manifest."
Chan Master Qingxiang of Chongfu Monastery in Mingzhou ascended the hall and said: "Virtuous Chan practitioners, the nature of seeing is all-pervasive; the nature of hearing is likewise so.

It penetrates the ten directions, with neither interior nor exterior. Therefore, the ancients said: 'Acting in accordance with conditions without fabrication, movement and stillness are eternally true.
Such activity is entirely the functioning of true wisdom. A monk asked: "What is the person of original nature? The Master said: [The text ends here].
[The monk] said, "Tall and majestic, six feet in height—this is very clear. [The Master] asked, "As for the person of original nature (*benlai ren*), does he still rely upon such physical appearance?
The Master said, "What do you call 'the person of original nature'? [The monk] said, "I beg the Master for a skillful means (*upāya*). The Master said, "To whom would I provide a skillful means?"
Chan Master Daocheng Tongfa of Baoming Monastery in Fuzhou, successor to Chan Master Ba’en Ming, ascended the hall and said: "As it is for one person, so it is for many. Take care!
A monk asked: "The perfect sound resounds everywhere, and the three grades hear it equally. We pray that the Master will reveal the mind of the Seer from the land of Zhushu."
[The Master] remained silent for a long while. The monk said, "In that case, the wild horse of the mind has become a precious steed, and the ox of the heart has suddenly turned into a white ox.
The Master said, "Seven tops and eight bottoms. The monk said, "If that is so, you will surely invite much laughter. The Master said, "After prostrating, withdraw.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Master’s coming from the West? The Master said, "I have never been there."
"From the Western Heaven," he said. [A monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the student’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "How long have you been in the Eastern Land? Baoci said:
"The Dharma heir of National Teacher [Fayan], Chan Master Yining of Yunju in Nankang Army, ascended the hall and said: 'There is no need to come up here; Kaundinya is already in the hall.'"
"The Elder turns the Wheel of the Ultimate Truth for all the Elders. Can it still be attained?
If you can believe this, each of you should return to the hall and investigate for yourselves.

After descending from his seat, he asked a monk, "Just as I told the Elder to investigate the Holy Monk a moment ago, what did the Holy Monk say? The monk replied, "I specifically thank the Master for raising the matter once again."
Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "The very mind is the Buddha. The student said: "I do not understand; I beg the Master for an expedient means. The Master said:
"To call it 'expedient' is already to name it 'Buddha. Turn the light back and reflect inwardly: what are body and mind?"
Chan Master Lingcen of Mount Yuntai in Quanzhou was a successor of Chan Master Chou of Chongshou. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Mount Yuntai?
The Master said, "The mountain in front and the mountain behind. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "A sleepyhead."
The Abbot of Ziguo Monastery, Monk Yuanjin of Hangzhou, asked: "What is the meaning of Danxia burning the wooden Buddha?

The Master said: "Inviting the cause while carrying the fruit. He asked: "What is the meaning of 'the cypress tree in front of the courtyard'? The Master said: "The blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head. He asked:

"An ancient said, 'If one becomes a donkey for the eastern neighbor, one becomes a horse for the western neighbor. What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "Inviting the cause while carrying the fruit."
The Master said: "One's acquaintances fill the world.
This was spoken by Chan Master Daojian of Xiqian on Mount Lu, a successor of Chan Master Ba'en. A government official asked: "When I took Jinling, I deployed my troops and slaughtered [the enemy]."
"A person has no fixed number. Does he still have offenses or not? The Master said, "I simply keep watching. Question:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The Yanglan and Zuoli rivers; waves rise even without wind."
Chan Master Huicheng of Guizong on Mount Lu was a native of Yangzhou. On the day he ascended the hall, he stood before the Dharma Hall and addressed the assembly, saying:
"When devas and humans attain the Way, they take this as proof. To dismiss you all with such words would already be excessive;

yet since you do not yet understand, I shall speak of it again. He then ascended the seat. A monk asked: "The Prefectural Governor is present at the assembly; we pray that the Master will expound the Dharma for him."
The Master said, "I am not equal to you. [The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "How could it not be?
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "I do not know. He then said, "Stop this questioning for a moment.

Even if you were to question until the end of kalpas, the question would still not reach it; even if you were to answer until the end of kalpas, the answer would still not suffice. Why is this? It is simply because of all..."
Each person has their own fundamental duty. It is perfect throughout the ten directions, spanning from antiquity to the present;
even the Buddhas dare not err regarding these people, and thus they are called the "Crowned Lineage" (*mūrdhābhiṣikta*). This is merely to assist and inspire the Elder. Therefore it is said:
"All sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm of the ten directions realize the fruit of the Sugata in every thought-moment. Since they are great men, so am I."
"How can you disparage yourselves and retreat in discouragement? You elders, do not be discouraged. Believe and accept this, and let it suffice.
When the Patriarch came from the West, he spoke only of seeing one's nature to become a Buddha; all other teachings do not equal this teaching.
Furthermore, I have another extraordinary expedient to present to you all. After a long silence, he said, "Take this clearly to heart. If you go to other regions, you must not..."
[The Master] spoke abruptly. [He remained] standing for a long time. "Take care. A monk asked, "How can one pass through where there is no passage for the wind?

The Master said, "From where do you come? The monk cited Nanquan’s question to Deng Yinfeng: "The copper pitcher is an object; there is water within it. You must not touch the object. Bring me some water.

Yinfeng then picked up the pitcher and poured out the water. I do not know—[what was his meaning?]— ...the Master said, "From where do you come? (implying that the monk's own source is the true answer). The monk then related this story. "I do not know—" [the Master continued].
"What do you think of this? The Master said, "Deng Yinfeng was indeed extraordinary, yet he was ultimately pouring out confusion.

Regarding Chan Master Bianshi of Chang'an Temple in Luzhou, a successor of Chan Master Chang'an Gui: A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master [responded].
It is said: Lingfeng of Shaoshi dwells in the nine heavens.
Chan Master Yongqing of Tanzhou Yungai was the son of Zhao of Hezhou. A monk asked, "If there is a person at the bottom of a ten-thousand-fathom well, how can they get out?
The Master said, "I am glad to have met you. The monk said, "In that case, they must pierce through the clouds..."
[The monk] went off, passing through the moon. The Master asked, "What about the matter of the thirty-three heavens?
The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Why do you speak such deceptive words? A monk asked, "What is the realm of Yungai? The Master said, "Three wells outside the gate.
[The monk] asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "The young novice. He presented a verse to the assembly, saying: "The secret instruction for locking the mouth of Yungai."
Any attempt to deliberate upon this would split one's brain; clap your hands and pursue the void. The clouds reveal the moon over the western mountains.

A monk asked, "What is the secret instruction for locking the mouth? The Master said, "Pervading heaven and pervading earth. The monk said, "If that is so, then the stone man nods his head and the pillar claps its hands.
The Master said, "A single pitcher of pure water and a single burner of incense. The monk said, "This is still just a shrimp at the bottom of a well."
The Master said, "I trouble the great assembly. He regularly moderated his food and drink, partaking twice daily with the community, merely unfolding his alms bowl.

Even when months or years passed, he did not practice physical conditioning or take medicinal tonics; this did not hinder his work. Whenever he was invited, he would certainly attend and eat his fill without any restrictive attachment.
On the second day of the fourth month in the second year of the Zhidao era, he manifested illness and passed away.
A monk asked Chan Master Congjin of Bore Monastery in Taizhou, a successor of Chan Master Yunju Xi: "What is it like when the cold spring water flows in the ancient ravine?
The Master said, "By all means, avoid drinking from it. The monk asked, "And what if one drinks from it? The Master said, "You will lose your very life."
A monk asked Chan Master Chizhao of Qinghua in Yuezhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Who are you?
The monk said, "Could it be that I am he? The Master said, "If it were so, there would be no connection."
Chan Master Fazhi of Changshou Monastery in Suzhou, a native of Wuzhou, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Changshou Yan of the eleventh generation under Qingyuan.
He initially lectured on the *Mingmen lun* (Treatise on the Gate of Illumination) and the *Yinming erzong lun* (Treatise on the Two Schools of Logic). Subsequently...

Having traveled abroad, he received the mind-seal from Chan Master Guangfa. When the regional commander Qian Renfeng invited him to succeed Guangfa as abbot, on the day he opened the hall for formal preaching, the Dharma Master of the Hundred Dharmas questioned him; by imperial command, the fourfold assembly had gathered like clouds.

[The student] said, "Regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage, I request the Master to proclaim it. The Master said, "The *Śatadharma-vyākhyāna-śāstra* (Treatise on the Exposition of the Hundred Dharmas).
[The student] asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, "All dharmas are without self. [The student] asked, "The old woman east of the city was born at the same time as the Buddha;
why did she not see the Buddha? The Master said, "If you do not see him, then speak! [The student] said, "In that case, I have seen him. The Master said, "The city..."
The Eastern Old Mother was born at the same time as the Buddha.
A monk asked Master Qihui of Yunju in Nankang, a successor of Chan Master Qi of Yunju: "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it; [place it] in a bottomless basket."
Zi Cheng was about to take [the teaching] back home. He did not know whether the Master would accept it or not. The Master asked, "Where did you get this?
Zi Cheng said, "If that is so, then it has not been bestowed in vain. The Master said, "For now, just take it away.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Beyond praise. The monk asked, "Is this it right here? The Master said, "It does not cause people to praise it."
