Chan Master Yihai of Ruiyan in Mingzhou was a native of Xiachuan. He visited the Dharma seat of Yunju, who asked him, "What thing comes like this?
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and subsequently composed a verse, which begins: "Yunju, what thing..."
Question: When touched by doubt, one becomes dazed; to simply accept it as it is is still to be buried alive. To transcend the world is to abide in the fundamental source. A monk asked:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "If you go to other places, just say that I have returned to the source and do not know how to answer questions.
Question: "What is the style of your monastery, Master? The Master said: "There are no prohibitions. [The monk] said: "What if one suddenly encounters..."
[The student] said, "This is offensive. Furthermore, how is this so? The Master said, "You do not know how to be a guest; you trouble the host.

[The student] asked, "Śākyamuni closed his room in Magadha, and Vimalakīrti remained silent in Vaiśālī. I wonder, how did they instruct the assembly? The Master said, "You do not wish for me to speak.
[The student] said, "I have not yet grasped your intent. The Master said, "Withdraw for now. [The student] asked, "What is the 'positionless'?"
The Real Man. The Master said, "There is no place here for you to arrange yourself.
Chan Master Zhiquan of Guanghui in Mingzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the fundamental matter of a patch-robed monk?"
The Master said, "Do not leave me in the lurch. The monk bowed. The Master said, "In fact, it is the assembly that leaves you, Venerable Sir, in the lurch," and he descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "What is it like when a thief does not strike the house of the poor? The Master said, "Even if I were to tell people, they would not believe me.
The monk said, "In that case, I shall bow and withdraw. The Master said, "What have you gained?"
A monk asked Zen Master Juxu of Baofu at Damei in Mingzhou, "What was the meaning behind the ancients' 'wall-facing'?
The Master said, "Just understand it in this way. The monk asked, "I do not know how to comprehend it; how should I receive and understand it? The Master said, "Prostrate yourself."
A monk asked Chan Master Weisu of Chuzhou Nanming: "The dharmas are not hidden; they have always been manifest throughout antiquity and today.
What is this manifest dharma? The Master said: "I am showing it to the assembly. The monk said: "If that is so, then I, your student, shall respectfully withdraw.
The Master said: "One who recognizes their error must surely correct it."
A monk asked Chan Master Qingxi Qing of Jingmen Commandery, "The ancient path is level and straight; how does one tread upon it?
He replied, "Are you a wandering monk?
[He was] a successor of Chan Master Zhiti Long.
A monk asked Chan Master Xuánběn of Línghyìn in Hángzhōu, "What is it like when the oyster has not yet opened? The Master said, "From where does the light come?
The monk asked, "When Linji enters the gate he immediately shouts; when Deshan enters the gate he immediately strikes with his staff. What is the meaning of this?"
The Master said, "The sky is clear, yet you are unwilling to leave. Seeing a monk reading a sutra, he asked, "What sutra are you reading?
The monk was speechless. Thereupon, the Master presented this verse: "Reading the sutra without recognizing the sutra, One merely exhausts one's eyes in vain. If you wish not to damage your eyes,"
Clearly recognize the scripture.
A monk asked Chan Master Shaozhen of Huili Temple in Linjiang County, successor to Chan Master Lianhanlin: "What is it like before the golden rooster has crowed? The Master said:

[The monk] asked, "What time is this? [The Master] said, "After the crowing, what then? The Master said, "I do not know the time. [The monk] asked, "How is it when the lion has not yet emerged from its den?
The Master said, "It is right there. [The monk] asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the den? The Master said, "Just run!"
A monk asked Chan Master Qingcong of Daining Monastery in Hongzhou: "When the Way prevails, the imperial edict is not transmitted; all people sing songs of great peace.
I wonder, what is the meaning of your teaching now, Master? The Master said, "This mountain monk is at fault. The monk asked again.
"What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru. Ascending the hall, he said: "Birth-and-death and nirvana are like a dream from yesterday.
But tell me, what excellence do the Buddhas of the three periods and Śākyamuni, the Old Man, possess?

Even so, do not misunderstand! [He] clapped his hands once and descended from his seat. A monk asked: "I have heard an ancient saying: 'The eastern mountains and the western ridges are green. What about this?"
"Please examine the meaning of this. The Master said: "The eastern mountain and the western ridge are green; it rains, yet then the sky clears.
If you ask further for the meaning within this, the magpie gives birth to the hawk."

A monk asked Zen Master Haoxian of Yao Peak in Suzhou, a successor of the Dharma heir of National Preceptor Kechan: "I am a student who has newly entered the monastic community; I beg the Master for a single reception."
The Master said, “Go. The student asked, “I have heard it said in the teachings: ‘This Dharma is equal; there is no high or low. What is this equal Dharma?
The Master said, “Mount Yao is high; Baohua is low. The student said, “In that case, does this not result in high and low?”
The Master said, "I knew you would understand it this way. Upon hearing the sound of thunder, he addressed the assembly, saying, "Do you hear the sound of thunder?
Do you know its point of origin? If you know its point of origin, you will know where body and life fall away.
If you do not even know this, as the ancients said: 'Those who do not know heaven and earth yet insist there is a Qian and Kun—better to go drink tea. He asked, "What about this?"
"What is the Way? The Master said, "To die at evening would suffice. He asked, "What is the Vajrapāṇi? The Master said, "It is of no use here.
He asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven!
Then he said, "As for that monk who finally asked, 'When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? [Shan]"
The monk said to him, "Heaven! Heaven! Tell me, where does the meaning lie? Is it perhaps in the sorrow over his passing, or in the pained remembrance of the Master?
If you evaluate it in such a way, I truly say you do not know where he has gone.
Do you wish to know where he has gone? There is no need to stand here long; simply rest. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Winter passes and spring comes; the gates of the pavilions [stand open]."
[The Master] said, “Open! If you can enter, there is no need to loiter. Venerable elders, have you yet been able to enter here?
If you can enter, then as the ancients said: ‘Every place is Maitreya; there is no gate and no Sudhana.
If you have not yet entered, it is simply because you, venerable elders, are running about in vain. I shall say no more. I have stood for a long time; take care.”
Chan Master Zhisheng of Shengshou Monastery in Wujang, Suzhou, ascended the hall and said: "If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, what further matter is there?

Therefore it is said: the mountains and rivers of antiquity and today; the sun and moon of antiquity and today; human relations of antiquity and today; the city walls and towers of antiquity and today."
This is called the Dharma-gate of Equality; it cuts off the limits of past and future. Can you all believe this?
If you can believe it, then practice in accordance with it. [The Master] stood for a long time. "Take care."
Chan Master Shouru of Kaitua, a meritorious official of Hangzhou, ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying:
"Do you know that the Holy Monk has come here together with all of you? Since you have condescended to visit us, how could I dare detain you? You have stood for a long time; take care."
Chan Master Weiyi of Nanshan Xingjiao Monastery in Hangzhou, successor to Chan Master Shi of Qixian, was asked by a monk: "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?
The Master said: "Several layers of white clouds. The monk asked: "How was it after he appeared in the world? The Master said: "A single peak of green mountains. [The monk] asked: "If..."
"What is the Way? The Master said, "Sticking one's head into the wild weeds. The monk asked, "What is it like to be a person on the Way? The Master said, "A dry piece of dung.
The monk asked, "Why did the Tripitaka Master with Large Ears fail to see the National Teacher when he went for the third time?
The Master said, "Look beneath the heels of your feet. The monk asked, "How can one come to see? The Master said, "When the heel of your straw sandals snaps off."
Chan Master Tiyou of Xiyu in Anjingshou ascended the hall and said: "One person holds fire and burns his own body; another person embraces ice and leaves his corpse across the road.
To advance is to encounter obstruction at every turn; to retreat is to have one’s breath choked and fill the chest.
Truly, there is no way to ascend to heaven and no door to enter the earth. Now that it has come to this, there is nothing to be done. After a long silence.
He said, "Wait until the snow has melted away; then spring will naturally arrive.
The abbot Weisu of Mount Dingshan in Zhenzhou asked, "What is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'? The Master said, "The heat departs and the cold arrives.
Weisu said, "If that is so, then it does transmigrate. The Master said, "Though one cries until the blood flows, it is of no use. [Another] asked, "To attain..."
Master Moxin Yin had already become enlightened. He was tested by being asked to demonstrate his "family style" before the assembly.

The Master said, "In front of my gate stands a tall pine tree; at midnight, the cuckoo comes and cries upon it. [The questioner] asked, "I know that you have thoroughly mastered the essential principles of all quarters.

When faced with the critical moment, you do not answer with the 'old-time Chan. What is the new and marvelous? The Master said, "If you go to other quarters, do not speak of this mistakenly. [The questioner] said, "..."
The student was earnestly attentive at his seat; there was none who did not regard this as something truly novel. The Master said, "Measuring the heavens with a blade of grass.
The student asked, "What is the realm of Dingshan? The Master said, "A pure breeze fills the courtyard. The student asked, "If a guest should suddenly arrive, how would you receive them?
The Master said, "Do not disdain its simplicity and coolness. He then added, "As for our family style and its environment, they are not easily matched in response."
These instances are frequently seen in designated locations where [the master] instructs others so that they cannot act according to their own will.

Once, a monk asked Dàsuí, "What is the patriarchal style (jiāfēng) of your Reverence? Dàsuí replied, "Painting a winnowing basket with red earth. He also said, "There is no placard pasted upon his belly.
Now, let me ask you all: how do you understand this? Furthermore, Jiashan, Yunmen, Linji, and Fengxue all possessed this same quality.
This talk has spread in all directions, yet each school establishes its own different system. How, then, do you understand it? The Dharma has no divergent tracks;

though paths differ, they lead to the same destination. If you wish to exert little effort and easily attain realization, simply recognize your own native roots, and you will be able to inherit the family estate.
You will be liberated wherever you are, and your functional application will manifest before you. Heaven and earth share the same root; the myriad things are one body. Call it what you will—
"Act as the eyes of the patch-robed monks; let there be no leakage even as fine as a hair. If you do not understand this, you will merely wander about in vain hardship.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "One who has teeth and wears hair. The monk said, "In that case, every person is fully endowed with it.
The Master said, "Far, far away! [The monk] asked, "How was it before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master...
[The monk] asked, "How is it to establish a family and found a career? The Master said, "Found a career and establish a family.
[The monk] asked, "What is the mountain road of Ding? The Master said, "Steep. [The monk] asked, "How is it for those who tread upon it? The Master said, "Precipitous.
[The monk] asked, "The Unsurpassed Dharma King possesses a great *dhāraṇī* called Perfect Enlightenment (*pariniṣpanna-jñāna*), from which flow forth all pure *tathatā*, bodhi, and nirvāṇa..."
[The monk] said, "I do not yet understand from where Perfect Enlightenment flows forth. The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, have a share in wearing it upon my head.
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then I shall accept it in faith and put it into practice. The Master said, "It is vaguely like a melody, just barely fit to be heard.

[The monk] asked, "How can one, throughout the twelve periods of the day, remain in accord with the Way? The Master said, "The August Heaven has no partiality; it assists only those who possess virtue. [The monk] said, "If that is so..."
"If that is so, then cultivation and realization are unnecessary. The Master said, "Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas.

Chan Master Weizheng of Jingtu Monastery in Hangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Sushu of the Pure Land, was a native of the Huang family in Huating, Xiuzhou. In his youth, he followed [a teacher] in Qiantang.
Zishengyuan’s Benru was engaged in secular affairs and was about to compete for honors with the government officials. He prayed to the Avalokiteśvara image to seek a favorable omen.

The Master declined, saying, "How could I bear to seek private advantage for myself alone? When Zhu Sha’o’an of the district heard this, he marveled at it and wished to open the treasury to provide for his ordination.
The Master sighed deeply and said, "In antiquity, the ordaining of others was based on pure intent and subtle efficacy..."

The essential point is this: nowadays things are the opposite; we have strayed far from antiquity. It was destined that I should fall into the ranks of the Three Jewels, and indeed, the time for this has arrived.

Subsequently, I encountered the grace of the *Xiangfu* amnesty and was able to fulfill my long-held aspiration. Yet, wearing only a worn-out woolen robe, my colleagues looked down upon me. The Master said:
"Is he a Buddha? Is he a Buddha? Does 'Buddha' consist merely in outward appearance? Is he a monk? Is he a monk? Does 'monk' consist merely in fine robes?
Thereafter, someone offered to provide the annual expenses for maintenance so that the affairs of the monastery might continue as before. The Master declined once more, saying:

"I have heard of begging for food with a bowl, but I have not heard of sitting at ease while enjoying offerings. I have heard of visiting the various patriarchs in succession, but I have not heard of abandoning study to take on administrative responsibilities."
"Moreover, my years are still young and my vigor intact; this is precisely the time for me to exert my physical strength in performing rites, not the season for attending to a thatched cottage.

Thereupon, he took up his staff and traveled eastward to study the Three Contemplations at Tiantai. He then returned to Mount Jing, where he consulted the veteran master Wuisu on the principles of the Single Transmission.
Wuisu was the director of the Pure Land Monastery at Mount Gongchen in Lin’an, and the Master assisted him there.

After a long time, he succeeded [the master] on the seat. He was, however, lofty and simple in character, maintaining a rigorous discipline over himself; thus, many eminent officials and great personages held him in high esteem.
When Ye Qingchen, the Internal Secretary, was governing Jinling, he welcomed the Master to discuss the Way. One day, Ye said, "Tomorrow there is a banquet at the Prefectural Office.
Although you, Master, strictly observe the monastic precepts, could you stay for one more day so that we might enjoy some pure conversation? The Master—
He agreed. The following day, the envoy was sent to invite the Master, who left behind a verse before departing, saying:

"Yesterday I made plans for today; Leaving the gate, leaning on my staff, I reflected again: As a monk, it is fitting to dwell among crags and valleys; In the midst of a state official’s banquet, it is truly unsuitable.

The guests in attendance all admired his refined bearing. The Master’s discernment was pure and clear; he was untainted by worldly entanglements and possessed a profound love for [the life of seclusion].

He would ride out and enter [the city] astride a yellow calf, with his *kamaṇḍalu*, towel, and bowl all hung upon its horns. The people in the marketplace vied with one another to gaze at him, yet the Master remained composed.
Imperial Commissioner of Hangzhou, Vice Minister Jiang, had long been a spiritual friend (*fangwai you*) to the Master.

Whenever he went to visit, he would dismount his calf at the entrance of the prefectural courtyard and engage in conversation and laughter until the end of the day before departing. Vice Minister Jiang composed a poem that said: "The Zen monk regularly enters the old capital; the yellow..."

A vase and bowl hang from a cow’s horn; sometimes he goes through clouds and snow. It would be well to paint him together with the clouds as a picture. The Master once composed a verse while in the mountains, saying:
"Ten thousand layers of peaks above the bridge, A thousand miles of water beneath the bridge. Only the white egret Sees me come here so often.
Throughout his life, he produced thirty volumes of works titled the *Jinxi Ji* (Collected Works of Jinxi). He was also skilled in... [the text continues].

His calligraphy was of transcendent excellence, and Qin Shaoyou treasured it. In winter, he would not use a brazier for warmth; instead, he would make balls from reed flowers and tuck his feet inside them.
When guests arrived, they shared in this together. In summer and autumn, he delighted in gazing at the moon;

he would sit cross-legged in a large basin floating upon a pond and spin the basin himself, chanting and laughing until dawn. He took this as his regular practice. Once, the Chan Master Shao of Jiufeng stayed with him as a guest.
In the monastery courtyard, as the Master was about to retire for the night, he invited Feng, saying, "The moonlight is like this; life is so full of toil and turmoil—who among us can truly face it?
Feng responded with a respectful "yes. After a while, the Master called for a servant to roast some meat over a fire. Feng was hungry at that moment.
He prepared medicinal decoctions and, for a while, served a cup of tangerine peel tea. Feng smiled with hidden amusement and said, "Is this not far too austere?
Someone asked, "The Master is known by the title 'Chan Master,' yet you do not speak of Chan. Why is that? The Master replied, "It would merely be a waste of words."
I am indolent and have no need for artifice; I simply trouble the myriad phenomena day and night to expound this for me.
Language has its limits, yet this Dharma is inexhaustible—it is what is called the "Inexhaustible Treasury of Creation.

On the eighth day of the first month of summer in the first year of the Huangyou era, he said to the assembly: "Movement exists in contrast to stillness, yet there is never an end to it. I have been in motion for sixty years."
There are four [stages]. Now he is at peace. Yet, what inherent existence can there be in movement or stillness? Thereupon, he passed away with serene composure.
He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Lingyin Sheng of the twelfth generation under Qingyuan.
Chan Master Yanshan Huiming of Lingyin Temple in Hangzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Is the Way far away? The monk asked, "What is the single path of true reality?
The Master said, "Not even a hair’s breadth may pass. The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall follow it and practice accordingly.
The Master said, "Do not run about in confusion. He ascended the hall and said, "I give this one thread of the Way to you, venerable ones. Now, what shall you do with it?"

To give rise to and uphold the Buddha-dharma of the Treatises, if one were to seal it off so that not even a drop of water could pass through, then even the Senior Monk would have no place to settle his body or establish his livelihood.
At such a time, even if the Patriarchs and Buddhas were to appear, they would still deserve twenty blows.
Having spoken thus, do I, this mountain monk, still have any fault? Have you not seen how when the World-Honored One was born, he took seven steps and gazed in the four directions?
Pointing one finger toward heaven and one finger toward the earth, he said: "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored. Yunmen said:
"If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to a dog.
Why? Because I value peace throughout the world. Now tell me: does Yunmen’s speaking in such a manner accord with the principles of the Buddha-dharma or not? Although...
It is indeed so. Yunmen possesses but a single eye. [I have] stood long; take care.
Chan Master Guize of Jianfu Monastery in Changzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The sound of the bell ringing by my ear."
A monk asked Chan Master Siyuan of Cuiyan in Mingzhou, a successor of Chan Master Haewon of Suiryam, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
"Buying and selling with cash; never on credit. [The monk] asked, "Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "It is well not to trust people's honesty.

Chan Master Linji Yixuan of Zhenzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Huangbo Yun. He was a native of the Xing clan from Nanhua in Caoshu. From his youth, he bore the aspiration to transcend the mundane world.
Upon shaving his head and receiving full ordination, he immediately sought out the Chan school. Initially, while in the assembly of Huangbo, his conduct and practice were pure and singular.
At that time, Muzhou was serving as the First Seat (Dìyīzuò). He asked, "How long have you been here, Senior Monk? The Master replied, "Three years.
Muzhou said, "Have you ever engaged in formal inquiry (cēnwèn)? The Master replied, "I have never engaged in inquiry; I do not know what to ask. Muzhou said:
"Why do you not ask the Abbot, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? " The Master then went there.
Before he had even finished speaking, Baizhang struck him. The Master came back down. Baizhang asked, "How did your inquiry go?
The Master said, "Before I had even finished speaking, the Abbot struck me; I do not understand. Baizhang said, "Just go and ask again. The Master went once more.

The Master asked, and Huangbo struck him again. Thus he asked three times and was struck three times. The Master said to Prefect Zhou, "I have long benefited from your encouragement in questioning the Dharma, and I have repeatedly received the Master’s blows.
I regret that due to my own karmic obstacles, I have failed to grasp the profound meaning. I shall now take my leave.
Prefect Zhou said, "If you are going, you must first bid farewell to the Master before you depart. The Master bowed and withdrew. Prefect Zhou went ahead to Huangbo.
Yunju said, "The Senior Monk who asked the question, though he is but a youth, is truly extraordinary. If he comes to take his leave, receive him with skillful means;
in the future, he will become a great tree that provides shade for all people under heaven. The next day, the Master took his leave of Huangbo.
Huangbo said, "There is no need for you to go elsewhere. Go directly to Dayu at Tancheng in Gaoyang; he will surely [resolve it] for you."
He went on to say: "The Master arrived at Dayu. Dayu asked, 'Where have you come from? The Master replied, 'I have come from Huangbo.
Dayu asked, 'What words did Huangbo say? The Master said, 'Three times I asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, and three times I was struck.'"
"I do not know whether this person has committed an offense or not. Yunju said, "Huangbo’s compassionate heart is so earnest that he has exhausted you to the very limit;
yet you come here again to ask whether there is an offense or not. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said:
"Originally, Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma consists of nothing more than this. Yuyou grabbed him and said, "You bed-wetting little devil!
Just now you were asking whether there was an offense or not; now you say, 'Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma consists of nothing more than this.
What principle have you seen? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The Master struck Yuyou three times under the ribs. Yuyou pushed him away and said:
"Your teacher Huangbo has nothing to do with my affairs. The Master took his leave of Dayu and returned to Huangbo.
Upon seeing him, Huangbo asked, "This fellow comes and goes; when will he ever reach a conclusion? The Master replied, "It is only because of your grandmotherly concern.

Having finished his greetings, he stood in attendance. Huangbo asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "Yesterday, I received the Compassionate Command of the Honored One, instructing me to practice meditation."
When Daoyou returned, Huangbo asked, "What did the old man Dayu say? The Master recounted the previous conversation. Huangbo said, "That old fellow Dayu is too talkative.
Wait until he comes back, and I will give him a thorough beating. The Master said, "What need is there to wait for him? I shall strike him right now!"
Subsequently, Huangbo struck him. Huangbo said, "This madman has come here to pull at a tiger’s whiskers. The Master then gave a shout.

Huangbo called to his attendant and said, "Lead this madman away to the meditation hall" (Miaoyan cited this to ask Yangshan: "At that time, did Linji gain the power of Dayu or the power of Huangbo? Yangshan replied:

"He not only rode on the tiger's head, but he also knew how to grasp its tail"). One day, while Huangbo was on a work assignment, the Master followed behind him. As they were returning, Huangbo turned around.
When Huaihai saw that the Master was empty-handed, he asked, "Where is the mattock? The Master said, "Someone has taken it away.

"A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. Is this the wondrous function of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*), or is it simply the nature of things as they are?
[When the Master] transformed and kicked over the rice table, the Master said, "Too coarse, you fellow. He replied, "What kind of place is this?"
He spoke of the coarse and the subtle. The next day, they went to the vegetarian feast together again. The Master asked once more, "How does today’s offering compare to yesterday’s?
Yunhua kicked over the dining table again. The Master said, "You have succeeded, but you are far too crude. Yunhua shouted, "Blind fellow!"
"What do the Buddha-dharma teachings say about coarse and subtle? The Master then stuck out his tongue. The Master and the King’s attendant went to the Sangha Hall.
The King asked, "Do the monks in this hall study the sutras? The Master said, "They do not study the sutras. [The King] asked, "Then do they practice meditation?
The Master said, "They do not practice meditation. [The King] asked, "Since they neither study the sutras nor practice meditation, what exactly are they doing? The Master—
[The Master] said, "I intended to teach him to become a Buddha and a Patriarch. [A monk] asked, "Even though gold dust is precious, if it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract.
The Master said, "I took you for a mere worldly man. Later, while the Master was ascending the hall, the two head seats of the two halls met and simultaneously let out a shout.
A monk asked the Master, "Is there still guest and host? The Master said, "Guest and host are clearly distinct. The Master then called to the assembly.
He said, "To truly understand the Linji phrase regarding host and guest, go and ask the two head seats in the hall. Later, the Master resided in the East Hall of Xinghua Temple in Daming Fu.
On the tenth day of the fourth month of the eighth year of the Xiantong era (the Dinghai year), as he was about to pass away, he spoke this verse of transmitting the Dharma:
"Following the current without ceasing, one asks: 'How is it? True illumination is boundless; I shall explain it to you. Free from all marks—"
“One who lacks the name does not receive it. When the 'Blow-of-the-Blade' has been used, one must quickly polish it.

He further addressed the assembly, saying, “After my passing, you must not extinguish my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye. Sansheng stepped forward and said, “How would we dare extinguish the Master’s Treasury of the True Dharma Eye?
The Master said, “In the future, if someone asks you, what will you say to them? Sansheng gave a shout. The Master said, “... [you have got it].”
"Who would have known that my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye would be extinguished upon this blind donkey? Having said this, he sat upright and passed away.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the northwest corner of the prefecture. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Huizhao, and his stupa was named Chengling.
Chan Master Xinghua Cunjiao of Weifu was a dharma successor of Chan Master Linji Xuanshi of the fifth generation under Nanyue.
While serving as the head seat (shouzuo) in the assembly of Sansheng, he would often say: "I, when I..."
"I traveled once through the south, yet with my staff I never once struck upon a single person who truly understood the Buddha-dharma.
When Sansheng heard this, he asked, "What kind of eye do you possess to speak in such a manner? The Master then gave a shout.
Sansheng said, "It must be you who have attained it. Later, when Da'ue heard this account, he remarked, "How could the wind ever carry it here?"
[The Master] came from within the gate of Da-jue (Great Awakening). Later, he went to Da-jue and served as the *yuanzhu* (head of the monastery). One day, Da-jue called out, "Head of the Monastery!
I have heard you say that during your travels in the south, you never once encountered a single person who had grasped the Buddha-dharma with the tip of your staff.
On what basis do you speak in such a manner? The Master then gave a shout; Da-jue struck him, and the Master [responded].

Again [Linji] shouted; Xuedou struck him again. The next day, as Linji was passing by the Dharma Hall, Xuedou summoned the head of the monastery and said, "I have a direct doubt regarding those two shouts you gave yesterday.
Linji shouted again; Xuedou struck him again. Linji shouted once more; Xuedou struck him yet again. Linji said:
"I have learned a phrase regarding guest and host from my three venerable elder brothers, but I have been completely defeated by them all.
I pray that you will grant me a dharma-gate of peace and bliss. Jue said, "You blind fellow, you come here to suffer defeat!
Take off your patched robe and let me give you a thorough beating! At these words, the Master realized the teaching of his late master Linji.
Regarding the principle of receiving the staff from Huangbo, when the Master later ascended the hall, he offered incense and said:

"This one stick of incense was originally intended for my elder brother Sansheng; Sansheng was too distant toward me. It was originally intended for my elder brother Dajue; Dajue was too remote toward me.
It is better that I offer it to my late teacher Linji. A monk asked: "Before the Many Sons Stupa, together..."
"What is there to discuss? The Master said, "One person transmits the empty; ten thousand people transmit the real. On another occasion, the Master called to a monk. The monk responded, "Yes.
The Master said, "The point is reached, yet it does not arrive. He called to another monk. The monk responded, "Yes. The Master said, "It arrives, yet the point is not reached."
A monk asked, "What is it like when [the Dharma] comes from the four directions and eight points? The Master said, "Strike the one in the center. The monk then bowed.
The Master said, "Yesterday I went to a village feast. On the way, I encountered a sudden storm;

I took shelter in an old shrine and managed to get through. He then asked the monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from the place of Cui Chan. The Master said, "Did you bring anything back?"
Cui Chan shouted, "Did you bring it? The monk said, "I did not bring it. The Master said, "In that case, it did not come from Cui Chan.
The monk then shouted. The Master then struck him. Addressing the assembly, the Master said: "I hear that people shout in the front corridor and shout in the back quarters as well.
My sons, do not shout blindly or shout recklessly. Even if you were to shout until Xinghua was cast into the void," he continued, "..."
He has not a breath of spirit left after being struck down. Wait until I have recovered and then I shall tell you that it is "not yet. Why?
It is because I have never yet scattered true pearls from within the purple silk curtains for you all. Why do you shout and clamor so wildly?
When Yunju was residing at Sanfeng Hermitage, the Master asked him: "I borrow a question for a moment, to serve as a shadow."
When he was a commoner, how was it? Ju had no reply. The Master said, "I suspect you could not answer this question, Master;
it would have been better to bow and withdraw. Twenty years later, Ju said, "Reflecting on it now, at that time it was unnecessary to say 'Why bother?
Later, Ju sent a fundraising emissary to the Master's place. The Master asked him, "When the Master was staying at Sanfeng Hermitage, I, the old monk, asked..."
[The Master] said, "That story—did you not manage it? Can you say it now? The Master brought up the previous story again.
The Teacher said, "For twenty years at Yunju, I could only say 'Why bother? Xinghua, however, is not like that; how can he compare to saying 'No need'?
The Master said to the Rector Kebin, "Before long, you shall become a leading teacher. Kebin said, "I will not enter this monastery."
The Master said, "If you understand, you do not enter; if you do not understand, you do not enter. [Kebin] said, "In neither case is it so.

The Master then struck him and said, "Venerable Kebin, you have been defeated in the Dharma-battle. You shall pay a fine of five strings of cash and provide a meal for the assembly. The next day, [the assembly gathered].
The Master himself struck the wooden gavel and said: "Venerable Kebin, having failed in the Dharma-battle, you shall not be permitted to eat;
you must leave the monastery immediately. A monk asked: "What was the meaning of the National Teacher calling for his attendant? The Master replied: "One blind man leading a crowd of blind men.
When the Master was serving as an attendant under Linji, Luopu came to visit him. Linji asked: "Where have you come from? Luopu replied: "From Luancheng."
Ji said, "I have a question to ask you; may I do so? Pu replied, "A newly ordained monk does not understand.
Ji said, "Even if one were to shatter the Great Tang Empire, one could not find a single person who does not understand. Go to the meditation hall.
The Master followed him and asked, "Just now, regarding that newly arrived monk, did you intend to humiliate him or not? Ji said, "Who am I to concern myself with whether you are humiliated or not?"
[Zhaozhou] was about to strip [the monk’s robe]. The Master said, “The Abbot only knows how to pounce on a dead sparrow on the ground;
he does not know how to cover it over with a turning phrase. Jie asked, “And what about you? The Master said, “I ask the Abbot to act as the newly arrived one.
Jie then said, “A novice does not understand. The Master said, “That is rather my own fault. Jie said, “Your words conceal the sharp point. The Master—
[The Master] prepared to deliberate. Jie struck him. That evening, Jie said again, "Today when I questioned the newly arrived one, it was like shooting a dying sparrow on the ground;
it was like striking it right in its nest. But when you produced a word, I shouted and raised it up to strike it among the blue clouds.
The Master said, "The grass-thief has been utterly defeated. Jie then struck him. When the Master saw that his fellow student had arrived, he had just ascended the Dharma seat.
The Master gave a shout. The monk also shouted. The Master shouted again. The monk also shouted. The Master stepped forward and raised his staff.
The monk shouted once more. The Master said, "Look at this blind fellow; he still thinks he is the master. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him down directly from the Dharma Hall.
An attendant asked, "What did that monk just do to offend you, Master? The Master replied, "Just now..."
There is authority; there is substance; there is illumination; there is function. Yet when I stretch my hand across his face twice, he cannot proceed here.
For a blind fellow like this, when would it be any sooner than now to strike him?
The monk prostrated himself and asked: "The precious sword you have hidden for long, O Master; today I beg to borrow it briefly on the field."
The Master said, "Not borrowed. The monk asked, "Why not borrowed? The Master said, "If it were not for Zhang Hua’s eyes, one would merely be peering at the light of the shooting star.
The monk asked, "What about one who uses it? The Master said, "Lying across the body to confront the universe—who is there to raise their head?

The monk then made a gesture of stretching out his neck. The Master said, "Ha! The monk said, "Yes," and returned to the assembly. Later, Emperor Zhuangzong of the Later Tang was on his imperial tour.

He traveled north to Hebei. Upon returning to the imperial palace at Weifu, the Emperor summoned the Master and asked, "Since I recovered the Central Plains, I have obtained a treasure, yet no one has ever offered a price for it.
The Master said, "I beg Your Majesty to let me see this treasure. The Emperor extended the legs of his *fuhou* (official headgear) with both hands.
The Master said, "Who would dare to offer a price for the treasure of a sovereign? [Xuanjue’s Probe]: Now tell me, did Xinghua accept Zhuangzong, or did he refuse him? If [you can say],...

"If you accept Zhuangzong, where is the eye of 'arousing the transformation'? If you do not accept Zhuangzong, where lies the fault? The Emperor’s countenance was greatly pleased, and he bestowed upon the Master purple robes and a formal title.
The Master declined both. The Emperor then granted him a horse for his use; the horse suddenly bolted, and the Master fell, injuring his foot. The Emperor again bestowed medicine for his treatment.
The Master called for the head attendant and said, "Make me a wooden crutch. When the attendant had finished it and brought it to him, the Master...

The Master asked, "Do you recognize this old monk? The assembly had no reply. The Master threw down his staff and stood upright.
He passed away, and was posthumously titled Chan Master Guangji.
Chan Master Zhao of Baoshou in Zhenzhou (the First Patriarch). A monk asked: "When the myriad realms come to invade [the mind], what should one do? The Master said:

"Where should I place it? The Master said, "The thousand sages are present. The monk asked, "Who can testify to this? The Master then threw down his whisk.
The monk walked from west to east and stood there; the Master struck him. The monk said, "Had you not practiced for a long time, how could you have known the ultimate point?

[Daowu] sat down. Xuanshou spread out his sitting mat and prostrated. The Master rose and entered the abbot’s quarters. Xuanshou gathered up his sitting mat and went out.

Throughout his time at the monastery, he had encountered and offended many virtuous and worthy men during his formal greetings.

When it was his turn for the formal greeting at the second seat, the Master proceeded directly to Dao-wu’s quarters. Dao-wu, having anticipated this, stood beneath the gate wearing a red head-wrap and holding a divine staff.

He was sitting inside the abbot’s quarters. As soon as the Master approached, Wuye said, “I have a question to ask you; may I do so?

Regarding "the meaning of the Westward Transmission," the Master said: "Stinking meat attracts flies" (Xinghua said: "A gadfly on the back of a worn-out donkey"). He asked a monk: "Where have you recently come from?"
The monk gave a shout. The Master also shouted. The monk shouted again. The Master shouted again. The monk said, "If you strike me with the staff, I will go blind," and he shouted.

The Monk of Dajue at Weifeng went to visit Linji. As soon as Linji saw him, he held up his whisk. The Master spread out his sitting mat.

He intended to hand it over to someone. At that time, a monk came forward and said, "I request the Master's arrow. The Master asked, "What do you call an arrow? The monk shouted.
The Master struck him several times and then returned to his quarters. He called the monk back inside and questioned him, saying:

A monk asked the Master of Zhuyuan Mountain in Jingnan Prefecture, "I have long heard that you, Master, are skilled in Chan; is this true? The Master said, "Yes.
The monk cried out, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master stepped forward, covered the monk’s mouth with his hand, and said, "Lower your voice! Lower your voice!"
The monk gave him a slap and then stepped aside. The Master said, "I have brought this upon myself. The monk brushed out his sleeves and left.
The Master laughed and said, "Had I known it would be thus earlier, I would regret not being thus. He asked, "Since it is a bamboo grove, will there be any shoots?
The Master said, "Thousands and tens of thousands of stalks. The monk said, "If that is so, then I, your student, have my share. The Master said, "What do you intend to do with it?"
The monk hesitated; the Master struck him.
A monk asked the Abbot of Fahua Monastery in Songzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Sitting alone before the five peaks."
Question: "What is the newly risen moon? The Master said: "Neither high nor low. [The student] asked: "Does this allow a student to gaze upon it with reverence?
The Master said: "Look after three days. Question: "What is the house style of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*? The Master said: "When it is cold, freeze them to death;
when it is hot, scorch them to death. [The student] asked: "What does 'when it is cold, freeze them to death' mean? The Master said: "In threes and twos."
He walked with his head covered. [The monk] asked, "What is it like to be 'killed by heat' when it is hot? The Master said, "Those who see you from east, west, south, or north will laugh at you.
[The monk] asked, "When a student holds a white blade and advances directly to the gate of the monastery, what then? The Master said, "Try it yourself and see."
The monk gave a shout. The Master seized him. The monk struck him with a palm as soon as he was caught. The Master pushed him away and said, "Today the old monk has suffered a loss.
The monk performed a dance and departed. The Master said, "A thief who strikes first."
A monk asked Chan Master Jiao of Luzu Mountain in Chizhou, a successor of Chan Master Guankui Xian: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
Today I will not answer questions. A monk said, "It is truly wonderful not to answer. The Master then struck him. A monk asked, "What is the tree at the Double Grove (Śāla-vana)?
The Master said, "The formless body within the body of form. The monk asked, "What is the formless body within the body of form?
The Master said, "An iron giant beneath a golden incense burner. A monk asked, "What is one who dwells alone on a solitary peak?"
The Master said, "At midnight the sun is bright; at noon it strikes the third watch. A questioner asked, "What is the matter beyond the extraordinary?
The Master said, "After the conditions of the Way have ended, what lies beyond empty space? A questioner asked, "When there is no door through which to advance, what then?
The Master said, "Too dull-witted! The questioner said, "It is not a matter of being dull-witted. When there is truly no door through which to advance, what then? The Master said:
The spiritual mechanism has never been discussed in terms of boundaries; adhering to the Dharma without a gate, one remains in the darkness.
A student asked, "What is the place where a student applies effort? The Master said, "When spring comes, the grass turns green of itself; when the moon rises, it is already daybreak.
He asked, "What is the place where there is no application of effort? The Master said, "Mountains crumble and stones fall; wild fires spread across the plains."
The monk Zhenzhou Tankong was a dharma successor of Master Zhīyī.
A monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master replied, “Wrapped in hemp and bound in paper. The monk asked, “When a hundred matters are finished and a thousand things are resolved, what then?
The Master struck him with his staff as he spoke. The monk asked, “I pray that you, Master, will proclaim a discourse that transcends the conventional.”
The Master said, "A narrow path does not allow the wind to pass. The monk asked, "Is it not simply this very thing? The Master then sighed repeatedly.
When the Seat-Holder Jì arrived at Nanchan in Luoyang on his pilgrimage, the military commander Zhu was hosting a vegetarian feast.

Entering the Sangha Hall, he looked around and said, "Right here! He then proceeded to distribute the incense, his mouth never ceasing its discourse. Upon reaching the Master’s presence, the Master immediately questioned him.
"What is this right here? Xingjun then gave a shout. The Master said, "Xingjun is fortunately a person who understands the Buddha-dharma;
why do you flare up in anger again? Xingjun said, "It cannot be called 'flaring up in anger. The Master then gave a shout.
Xingjun said, "The hook was in a place beyond doubt. The Master then shouted again, whereupon Xingjun ceased.
After the midday meal, he ordered the Guest Office to invite the monk who had just shouted down to him. When the monk arrived, the Master conversed with Xingjun, paying no heed to anyone else.
The Record Keeper said, "Just now, how could Xingjun tolerate this monk’s impertinence? Xingjun replied, "If it were anyone else..."
"You all, drink! This humble official has a sword. The Monastic Registrar said, "We certainly do not understand; it must be Elder Huī who can.
The Military Commissioner said, "Even if it were Elder Nanchan, he would not have even dreamed of it yet.
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The dragon soars over the vast ocean; the fish leap in the deep pool."
[The monk] asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "At night one hears the drums for the sacrificial spirits; at dawn one listens to the songs of those crossing the rapids.
[The monk] asked, "What is the house style of the High Seat? The Master said, "A three-legged toad carries a great elephant on its back."
Chan Master Yanzhao of Fengxue in Ruzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Nanyuan Yong of the seventh generation under Mount Nanyue.
He was a native of the Liu clan from Yuhang. From his youth, he abstained from meat and pungent vegetables and studied the Confucian classics.

He was to have entered the civil service examinations, but failing to succeed on his first attempt, he left home to become a monk. He relied upon Master Zhigong at Kaiyuan Temple in his native prefecture, where he shaved his head and received full ordination.
There he studied the Tiantai teachings on *śamatha-vipaśyanā*. At the age of twenty-five, he went to visit Jingqing. Jingqing asked him, "Where have you recently departed from?"
The Master said, "Since leaving the East, [have you not yet returned? Dongqing said, "Have you passed through the Small River yet?
The Master said, "A great vessel sails alone across the void; there is no Small River to cross. Dongqing said, "At Mirror Water and Mount Qin, even birds cannot fly across. Do not speak of hearsay.
The Master said, "Even the vast ocean fears the power of the *meng-lun* warship; with sails unfurled against the Milky Way, one crosses the Five Lakes. Dongqing stood upright.
Fuzi said, "What can be done about this? The Master asked, "What is this? Qing said, "Indeed, it cannot be recognized.

The Master said, "Appearing and disappearing, rolling up and unfolding—it is used by you and me alike. Qing said, "Like a ladle divining based on empty sounds; like a deep sleep accompanied by idle chatter.
The Master said, "A vast marsh conceals mountains; a principle can subdue a leopard. Qing said, "Forgive my transgressions and release my faults; let us hasten [to the truth]."

"You must go out. The Master said, "If you go out, you will lose it. He then went out. Upon reaching the Dharma Hall, he said, "For a traveler on pilgrimage, as long as one's good karmic conditions are not yet exhausted, one must not simply stop and leave.
He then returned and said, "I have just now rashly presented my petty ignorance and presumed upon your venerable countenance.
I prostrate myself in gratitude that, out of compassion, you did not grant me reprimand. Qing said, "The words you spoke just now were from [the heart]."
"Coming from the East—is that not coming from Cuiyan? The Master said, "Xuedou personally dwells to the east of Baogai.
Qing said, "Failing to cease the mad interpretations of the lost sheep, you have instead come here to recite verses. The Master said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present a sword;
if you are no poet, do not offer a poem. Qing said, "Hide the poem quickly; let me borrow the sword for a moment. The Master [yielded].
Yangzi said: "Danchou was a person who carried a sword like a cook. Qing said: 'He not only offended the norms of social transformation, but he also manifested his own coarseness.'"
The Master said, "If you do not touch upon the transformation of the wind, how can you clarify the mind of the ancient Buddhas? Qing asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas?
The Master said, "To grant permission once more; what does the Master have now? Qing said, "This monk from the East cannot distinguish between beans and wheat."
To merely hear [the teaching] and not cease [from practice]—how could one suppress [the mind] and merely stop there? The Master said, "A great wave surges a thousand fathoms;
the clear ripples do not depart from the water. Fenyang Qing said, "One phrase cuts off the stream; ten thousand functions are stilled and pared away. The Master then prostrated. Fenyang Qing said:
"Excellent, this patch-robed monk! Excellent, this patch-robed monk! When the Master arrived at Huayan, Huayan asked, "I have a 'Song of Herding Oxen';

The Master visited Nanyuan. Upon entering the gate, he did not prostrate. Nanyuan said, "Upon entering the gate, one must discern the host. The Master said, "I ask you, Master, to distinguish it for me definitively.
Nanyuan snapped his fingers once on his left knee; the Master then let out a shout. Nanyuan snapped his fingers once on his right knee.
The Master shouted again. The Abbot said, "Setting aside that one shout from the left, what about that one from the right?
The Master said, "Blind! The Abbot then raised his staff. The Master said, "Do not wield the staff blindly; seize it and strike the Abbot! Do not say I did not warn you."
The Abbot threw down his staff and said, "Today you have been thoroughly outwitted by this yellow-faced monk from Zhejiang.
The Master said, "The Abbot is much like one who has failed to obtain alms and falsely claims he is not hungry. The Abbot said, "Have you ever been to this place before, Layman?
The Master said, "What kind of question is that? The Abbot said, "I am asking you this in all sincerity. The Master said, "In that case, you cannot let me go."

[The Master] passed through [the hall] and descended. Having finished his attendance with the assembly, he returned to the Hall to pay his respects to the Abbot. The Abbot asked, "Disciple, whom have you studied under?
The Master replied, "I spent the summer retreat at Huayan in Xiangzhou together with Attendant Kuang. The Abbot said, "Then you have personally met a master.

The Abbot then asked, "Regarding the single blow of the staff in the South, how do they deliberate upon it? The Master replied, "They deliberate upon it as something extraordinary. The Master... [continued].
He then asked, "How do you evaluate this single blow from the Master here? Yuan picked up his staff and said, "In the blow of the staff there is no patience with birth;
when confronting the situation, the teacher is not seen. At these words, the Master attained a great realization of the profound principle. He subsequently remained in attendance for six years.

The fourfold assembly requested Fengxue to serve as their host for another eight years. Then, Magistrate Li, together with the officials and commoners of the entire city, invited him once more to open the hall and expound the Dharma.
He ascended the hall and said: "When the eye of study meets the critical moment, you must have the great function manifest before you;
do not confine yourself to minor details. Even if you were to attain realization prior to words, it would still be a lingering shell and a deluded enclosure. Though one may transcend phrases..."

I shall now sweep these away for you all at once, so that each one becomes like a lion cub, letting out a roar with a "tsha-ya" sound, standing upright as if carved from a cliff ten thousand fathoms high—daring anyone to look upon them with a direct eye. To look is to blind one's own eyes. At that time—

The Master said, "Reaching for the sky and groping on the ground. Later, due to the depredations of local bandits, the Master fled with his assembly to Yingzhou.
He visited the former host, Governor Li, who invited him to stay in the government office to pass the summer retreat. A great assembly was held there.
He requested the Master to ascend the hall. As soon as he had taken his seat, he said: "The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is like the mechanism of an iron ox:
if it moves away, it is sealed; if it remains still, it is broken. But as for neither moving nor remaining—would you say it is sealed, or would you say it is not sealed?"
"Is there anyone who can speak? At that time, the Elder Lupi came forward and asked, "This student possesses the device of the 'Iron Ox';
I pray that the Master will not apply his seal. The Master said, "I am accustomed to fishing for whales in the vast depths, yet you sigh over the steps of a frog in the mud.
Lupi stood there lost in thought. The Master shouted, "Elder, why do you not offer a word? As Lupi hesitated, the Master struck him.
With one stroke of his whisk, the Master said, "Do you still remember the *huatou*? Try to bring it up. As Bo was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him again with the whisk.
The Herdsman said, "I know now that the Buddha-dharma and the royal law are the same. The Master asked, "What principle do you see?
The Herdsman replied, "To hesitate when a decision must be made brings disorder instead. The Master then descended from his seat. This continued until the ninth month.
The Grand Master of Youzhou, Lord Song, donated his residence to establish a temple. He subsequently came to Yingzhou and invited the Master to reside as the abbot of the new monastery.

In the first year of the Guangshun era of the Zhou dynasty, the temple was granted the name Guanghui. The Master resided there for twenty-two years, with a community that regularly numbered over a hundred.

The student said, "I beg the Master to point directly. The Master said, "My home is on the Isle of the Sea Gate; the sun of Fusang is the first to shine upon it.
The student asked, "What is it like when the bright moon is suspended in the sky? The Master said, "It does not roll down from the heavens; let it lie buried in the earth as it pleases.

"When shooting, it reaches throughout the ten directions; where it lands, no one sees it. The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, am not like that.

"What is the Master’s arrow? The Master made the gesture of drawing a bow. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Drag this dead man out!

The Master said, "Spreading the mat and holding the bowl. A monk asked, "How was it when one has not yet reached the source? The Master said, "The crane is cold."
