A monk asked the Abbot of Lingquan Monastery in Tanzhou, "What is your livelihood? The Master said, "Not a single thing.
The monk said, "I do not understand; what do you use in your daily life? The Master gave a shout. The monk bowed. The Master struck him. [Another] asked, "The former..."
The Master said, "The Way of the Teacher: 'The Horse-Dealer's Wife on the Sands of Jinshe'—what is the meaning? The teacher said, "Countless people outside the East Gate.
[The student] asked, "What is it like when one understands it in this way? The teacher said, "Many pass to and fro upon the Tianjin Bridge."
Chan Master Shanzhao of Taiyuan, of the Shenyuan (Prince’s Monastery) in Fenzhou, was a successor in the ninth generation under Chan Master Nian of Shoushan in the lineage descending from Mount Heng.
He was the son of the Yu family of Taiyuan; having shaved his head and received full ordination, he traveled on foot with a staff.
He traveled as a wandering monk, staying briefly wherever he went and striking out questions according to his circumstances. He visited seventy-one spiritual teachers (*kishi*) in succession.
Later, he arrived at Shoushan and asked, "When Baizhang rolled up his mat, what was the meaning? Shoushan said, "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, and the entire body is revealed."
The Master asked, "What is your understanding? Xiangyan said, "Where the Elephant King walks, there is no trace of the fox. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Rising from his prostrations, he said, "The moon in the empty realm of the ten thousand ages' azure pool—only after repeatedly searching and stirring it can one truly know it.
Someone asked, "What principle did you perceive that led you to such self-acceptance? The Master replied, "This is precisely where I let go of my body and life. Later...

He traveled through the regions of Heng, Xiang, Xiang, and Mian, where local magistrates repeatedly sought to invite him to famous monasteries; though he was invited eight times in succession, he remained steadfastly reclining and did not respond.
Following the passing of Shoushan, the clergy and laity of the Western Route dispatched the monk Qichong to welcome and invite him to serve as abbot.

The Master had closed his quarters and was sleeping with his head on a high pillow. Fenzhou Cong pushed open the door and entered, admonishing him, saying, "The Great Matter of the Buddha-Dharma is of primary importance;

retiring in seclusion is but a minor detail. Fengxue feared he would fail to respond to the prophecy and worried that the fundamental teaching would fall into extinction. Fortunately there was our former teacher, but our former teacher has already passed away.
You are one who possesses the strength to shoulder the Great Dharma of the Tathāgata; at such a time as this, why do you wish to sleep peacefully? The Master [awoke].
Jue rose abruptly, took Cōng’s hand, and said, "If it were not for you, I would not have heard these words. Prepare everything quickly; I am going.
Later, after arriving at the monastery, he ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying, "At the gate of Fenyang there is a Lion of the West River, crouching right at the entrance.
As soon as anyone approaches, he bites them to death. What skillful means is there by which one might enter Fenyang’s gate and see Fenyang’s man?"
If you see one who is a man of Fenyang, he is capable of being a teacher to the patriarchs and Buddhas. If you do not see a man of Fenyang, they are all people standing dead on the spot.
Is there anyone now who can enter? You must enter quickly, lest you bring your whole life to naught.
If you are not a guest of the Dragon Gate, take care not to suffer the "dotted forehead. Who is that guest of the Dragon Gate? Point them out all at once!
[He] descended from his seat. Raising his staff, he said: "Withdraw quickly! Withdraw quickly! Take care! He ascended the hall and said: "The former sages said:
'A single phrase must embody the three mysteries; each mystery must embody the three essentials. Which phrase embodies these three mysteries and three essentials?
Understand it well! Each of you should reflect upon it: have you attained a sense of stability yet? [This was] before the time of the ancient worthies.

When traveling on foot (gyōjaku), if you hear a single kōan (in’nen) and have not yet clarified its inner meaning, your food and drink will immediately lose their flavor and your sleep will become restless.
You must resolve this with urgency; do not treat it as a minor matter. This is why the Elder Great Awakened One appeared in the world for the sake of the one great cause and condition.
Consider that those who have traveled on foot since ancient times did not do so merely to sightsee or enjoy the scenery.

Observing the splendor of the provincial and prefectural capitals, [one sees that] even a single robe and a mouthful of food are all due to the fact that one’s sacred mind has not yet attained penetration.

Therefore, one travels on foot with diligent exertion to resolve profound mysteries, to transmit and propagate the teachings, to inquire extensively of those who possess prior knowledge, and to draw near to those of high virtue.

This is primarily for the purpose of continuing the lamp of the Buddha’s mind, to perpetuate the legacy of the patriarchs, to exalt the holy lineage, and to guide those of future capacity. Thus, one benefits both oneself and others.
"Forget the traces of the past. Is there anyone present now who would engage in this discussion? If so, come forward; let us all deliberate together.
A monk asked, "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner? The Master said, "You are a wandering monk. The monk asked, "What is the phrase for discerning a patch-robed monk?
The Master said, "The sun rises in the east at dawn. The monk asked, "What is the phrase for when the true command is being exercised? The Master said, [as before].
The Master said, "Bringing it from a thousand li away, you present your old face. [The monk] asked, "What is the phrase that establishes heaven and earth?
The Master said, "In the continent of Uttarakuru, long-grained rice grows; those who eat it have neither greed nor anger.
He then said, "I shall use these four turning phrases to test the monks of the world. As soon as I see you come forward, I have already tested you. [The monk] asked, "What is..."
The Master said, "Hitting the Great Image at Jiazhou. [The student] asked, "What is the place where the student turns? The Master said, "Watering the Iron Ox at Shanfu.
[The student] asked, "What is the place where the student attains intimacy? The Master said, "Playing with the Lion in Xihe.
He then said, "If a person can understand these three phrases, they have already discerned the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan). Furthermore, there are three..."
The essential point lies herein; you must all grasp it. This is no trivial matter. I shall express it for the assembly in verse: The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials are difficult to distinguish;
When the meaning is grasped, the Way is easy to approach. A single phrase clearly encompasses the myriad phenomena; On the Double Ninth, the chrysanthemums are fresh.
Because Bingfen was bitterly cold, the Master canceled the night session. At that time, a strange bhikṣu appeared, shaking his monk’s staff.
He arrived and said to the Master, "There are six great beings (mahāsattvas) in this assembly; why do you not preach the Dharma? Having spoken, he departed.
The Master secretly recorded this in a verse, saying: "The foreign monk with the golden staff’s radiance Has come to Fenyang for the sake of the Dharma.
These six men shall become great vessels; I entreat you to proclaim it forth. He ascended the hall and said: "Every single phrase must embody the three gates of mystery (san-hsüan-men). Each..."

The Gate of Mystery must possess the Three Essentials: illumination and function. Whether it be illumination followed by function, function followed by illumination, illumination and function occurring simultaneously, or illumination and function occurring at different times—I shall first discuss with you the case of illumination followed by function.
As for function followed by illumination, you must be a person of some caliber before you can attain it. But as for illumination and function occurring simultaneously—how will you manage that?

"When life arises, it must be met [with reality]. Illumination and function do not occur at the same time; how then, monk, will you find a place to settle? A monk asked, "What is the source of the Great Way?

The Master said, "Digging in the earth to seek the sky. The monk asked, "How can it be so? The Master said, "You do not recognize the profound mystery. The monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest?
The Master said, "Joining palms before the hermitage, he asks the World-Honored One. The monk asked, "What about that? (or "How is this? The Master said, "... (text fragment)
"This is the guest within the host. The Master said, "Facing each other, there is no companion.

[The monk] asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "A mass of clouds stretches across the sea; drawing the sword, one stirs the Dragon Gate. [The monk] asked, "What is the host within the host?
The Master said, "Three heads and six arms, supporting heaven and earth; the wrathful Nanda and Upananda strike down the Imperial Bell. Ascending the hall, he said: "Fenyang has three secrets."
"It is difficult for patch-robed monks to discern; if you intend to ask further how it is, I shall drive my staff straight through your head.
At that time, a monk asked, "What are the three secrets? The Master struck him. The monk bowed. The Master said, "I shall express them all in verse for you at once.
The First Secret: Guiding others is without fixed timing; clever words cannot describe it—a moon in the blue sky amidst breaking clouds. The Second Secret: Unfolding..."

Radiantly discerning the worthy and wise, the mind that benefits sentient beings through question and answer pulls out the wedge from the eye. This is the third secret, spoken by a Hu person from the Western Regions.
When the water of the Ji River flows to Silla, the northern lands employ bing-iron. He further asked: "Is there anyone who understands?
Let those who understand come forth and communicate a message; I wish to know the extent of your realization. Do not merely memorize words and phrases in this way."
"What benefit is there in lingering for one's entire life? Do not stand for long; take care. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "A green silk fan provides sufficient breeze and coolness. A monk asked, "A cloth drum hangs at the front of the hall; who is the one who knows it?
The Master said, "He stops his hoeing, pours out the wheat meal, lies down in the grass, and does not raise his head. A monk asked, "What is..."
At the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), the Master said: "One must not set foot [there]. A question was asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said: "Piercing to the bone, piercing to the marrow. The questioner asked: "What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "Pervading heaven, pervading earth. A question was asked: "As for a person who truly cultivates the Way..."
[The monk] said, "I do not see the faults of the world. [Zhaozhou] asked, "I do not yet understand what kind of fault you do not see. The Master said, "The snow buries the night moon three feet deep;
a boat travels ten thousand li on dry land. [The monk] said, "What kind of mental activity is this, Master? The Master said, "It is actually your own mental activity.
[The monk] asked, "Of the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes, what is the True Eye? The Master said, "Blind. [The monk] said, "If that is so..."
[The monk] said, "Then it is like two people carrying a single staff. The Master said, "Singing a *bā* song in a village of three households.
[The monk] said, "In that case, you, Master, are also inside it. The Master said, "Thank you for your persistence. [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s house style?
The Master said, "The Three Mysteries open the Right Path; a single phrase shatters the heterodox schools. [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s vitality? The Master said, "..."
Ji asked, “Ordinarily, you do not hold anything in your hands; you make offerings to the monks of the Five Lakes. Ji asked, “I wonder what they eat?

The Master said, “Divine *sudhā* rice is no more than a rare delicacy; with a single flavor of fine soup, one is satisfied and rests. Ji asked, “What was it like before Ox-Head saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, “A new deity is further honored by a female shaman. Ji asked, “And after he saw him? The Master said, “The old deity is replaced by a new one.”

The Master said: "An ancient temple has once again been inscribed by a scholar. Entering the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Now, one who expounds the Dharma must possess the Ten Wisdoms Identical to Reality.
If one does not possess these Ten Wisdoms Identical to Reality, one cannot distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, nor differentiate between the monastic and the lay;
thus, one cannot serve as eyes for gods and humans to resolve what is right and wrong. It would be like a bird flying through the sky with broken wings, or like an arrow..."
When the arrow is shot, the string snaps; because the string is broken, the arrow does not hit the mark. When the wing is broken, the void cannot be traversed by flight.

When the string is strong and the wing is firm, the arrow pierces through both the void and the target. What is it that constitutes the "Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality"? I shall point them out for you, Venerable Elders:
1. Identity of Substance; 2. Identity of the Great Matter; 3. Total Identity in Practice; 4. Identity of True Resolve; 5. Identity of Pervasiveness.
1. Universality; 2. Identical fulfillment; 3. Identical gain and loss; 4. Identical birth and death; 5. Identical roaring sound; 6. Identical entry. It is further asked:
With what kind of person does one enter identically? With whom does one roar the same sound? What is it that is identical in birth and death?
What thing is identical in gain and loss? Which one is identical in fulfillment? And what is it that is identical in pervasiveness?
Universally! Who shares this true resolve? Who can be said to be a fellow practitioner? Which one shares in the Great Matter? What thing shares the same substance?
Is there anyone who can point it out? Those who can point it out do not begrudge their compassion; those who cannot point it out have yet to possess the eye of study.
You must discern this with urgency and recognize right from wrong. The face is present right now—it must not be delayed.

[The Master] stood up. "Take care. Li Hou, the Governor of Longdefu, had been acquainted with the Master for some time. He sent messengers to invite him to Chengtian Monastery three times, but the Master did not go.
The messengers were punished for their failure. When they returned once more, they said, "We must have the Master accompany us; otherwise, we shall face death.
The Master smiled and said, "I am old and ill, and have already resolved not to leave the mountain. If you insist on going, I shall simply follow behind you. What else could he do?

"Must we go together? The messenger said, "If you, Master, consent, then whether we go first or later is for you to choose. The Master ordered food to be prepared and began packing his belongings, saying, "I shall go on ahead.
He set down his chopsticks and passed away. His body was cremated, and the *śarīra* relics were collected to erect a stupa.
Chan Master Guisheng of Guangjiao Monastery in Yechuan, Ruizhou, was the son of the Jia family of Jizhou.

At the age of twenty, he left home to become a monk at Baoshou Monastery in Yizhou. After receiving full ordination, he traveled to various regions to study, eventually visiting Shoushan. One day, Shoushan raised his bamboo staff.
The questioner asked, "If you call it a bamboo stick, it is a direct hit; if you do not call it a bamboo stick, it is a missed blow. What would you call it?
The Master seized the stick, threw it to the ground, and said, "What is this? Shanshan replied, "Blind! At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.

The opening of the hall. A monk asked, "The patriarchs have transmitted one to another the seal of the patriarchs; whom do you, Master, now take as your Dharma heir? The Master said, "A Son of Heaven within the realm; a General beyond the borders.
The monk said, "I have received a drop from the ocean of your teaching as directed by the Master; what is the matter regarding the ancestral wind above this?
The Master said, "Fan Kuai’s rage before the Hall of the High Ancestor—know that ten thousand miles away, smoke and dust are utterly extinguished. The monk asked again.
"Vimalakīrti’s chamber does not take the sun and moon as its illumination. In the Master’s chamber, what serves as the illumination?
The Master said, "My eyebrows are parted in eight characters. [The monk] asked, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this. The Master said, "Both ears hang down to my shoulders.
[The monk] asked, "What is the work that transcends the Master? The Master said, "How long are the old monk’s eyebrows? [The monk] asked, "What is it to be amidst the dust?"

[The Master] manifested his body alone. The Master said, "A thousand tents in the north of the pass; ten-thousand-hu ships in the south of the river. [The student] said, "If that is so, then it is not dust. The Master said, "This is the talk of those who merely parrot words.

[The student] asked, "What is the Master’s deepest place? The Master said, "The cat has the merit of drinking blood; the tiger has the virtue of raising the dead. [The student] said, "Is this not it? The Master said, "This is the talk of those who merely parrot words.

[The student] asked, "How is it that the One Letter contains ten thousand practices? The Master said, "The cat has the merit of drinking blood; the tiger has the virtue of raising the dead. [The student] said, "Is this not it? The Master said, "This is the talk of those who merely parrot words."
[The student] said, "No. The Master said, "The pestle pounds toward the southeast; the millstone grinds toward the northwest. [The student] asked, "What is the indestructible vajra-body?
The Master said, "In a hundred pieces. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "In the end, it is but a heap of ashes.
[The student] asked, "Without falling into any conditions, please, Master, speak directly. The Master said, "It falls. [The student] asked, "What is the pure dharmakāya? The Master said, "A latrine."
The Counters at the Edge of the Pit. [A monk] asked, "What are precept, concentration, and wisdom? The Master said, "A set of broken utensils. One day the Master ascended the seat.
A monk asked, "What is it like when one has just come into the Dharma Hall? The Master struck the meditation bench once. The monk said, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this.
The Master said, "No one bids above the price; I strike it for three hundred. [Another monk] asked, "If one suddenly encounters a great manifestation..."

[The Master] called out, "People, come here! Do you still act for one another's sake or not? A monk asked, "The Dharma has long since become corrupt; where is compassion to be found? The Master said, "In old age, one becomes a demon.

He ascended the hall [to preach]: "The vital lineage of the Patriarchs—whether ordinary or sagely, Nāgārjuna and Aśvaghoṣa, heaven and hell, the cauldrons and furnaces, the ox-headed jailers, the myriad phenomena of the forest-like universe, the sun and moon and the stars—all are [the manifestation of this]."
Within this land, both sentient and insentient beings—pointing with his hand and drawing a single line—he said:
"All enter this school. Within this school, one can kill people, and one can also bring people to life. To kill people, one must possess the sword that kills;

to bring people to life, one must possess the phrase that brings them to life. What is the sword that kills? What is the phrase that brings to life? Anyone who can speak it, come forth and respond before the assembly!
"Go see for yourself. If you cannot say it, you will have brought your entire life to naught. Be careful. A monk asked, "What is the Master’s four immeasurable minds?
The Master said, "Setting fire to kill people. The monk asked, "Wherein lies compassion? The Master said, "Present it to one who has clear eyes.
A monk asked, "It is not within, not without, and not in between. In what place does it reside? The Master...
[The student] said, “The Southern Dipper has six stars; the Northern Dipper has seven. [The student] asked, “What is the Dharmakāya Lord, Vairocana?
The Master said, “Monastics are ranked by their years since ordination; laypeople are ranked by their age. [The student] asked, “Is there anything further beyond this?

The Master said, “There is. [The student] asked, “What is this matter that lies beyond? The Master said, “Go yourself to Yuzhou, ten thousand li away; when you depart, do not lament or resent others.”
[The Master] ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said: "Now, those who travel as practitioners of Chan must truly reflect.

To study, one must possess the eye of a student; to realize the ground, one must attain the phrase of the ground. Only then is there the possibility of mutual intimacy, and only then will one not be deluded by various circumstances nor fall into the evil realms.
Ultimately, how can this be fully understood? Sometimes the words reach the ear, but the meaning does not reach the mind."
Delusively taking external objects as conditions, one discriminates among reflected phenomena. At times, the meaning is reached while the words are not;

it is like the blind men feeling an elephant, each proclaiming a different version. At times, both meaning and words are reached; the realm of empty space is shattered, and its radiance illuminates the ten directions.
At times, neither meaning nor words are reached; like a sightless person wandering aimlessly, one suddenly and without awareness falls into a deep pit.
Question: "What is the path that has been no different from ancient times to the present? The Master said: "Worldly people all wear their heads wrapped.

[The monk] asked: "What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "You, O *ācārya*, have no *xiemo* (traveler’s hat). Question: "When one's own matter is not yet clear, what serves as the verification?

The Master said: "Beating the signal gong in the midst of a bustling market. [The monk] asked: "What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "Lighting a golden lamp at midday. Question: "A cloth drum..."
Striking the screen, he asked, "Who is the one who understands this? The Master said, "There is a rusty nail in your eyes. The monk asked, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this.
The Master said, "Old Qiao competing with the Southern God. The monk then requested further instruction on the story of the *póshùzǐ* (the cypress tree).

The Master said, "I am not unwilling to explain it to you, but will you believe it? The monk replied, "Since the Master speaks with such gravity, how would I dare not believe? The Master said, "Do you still..."
"Do you hear the sound of water dripping from the eaves? The monk was suddenly enlightened; without realizing it, he involuntarily let out a cry:
"Ye! The Master asked, "What principle have you seen? The monk then replied with a verse: "The water drips from the eaves, Clear and distinct."
He shattered heaven and earth; in that very moment, his mind was stilled. The Master was delighted and asked a monk, "At sunset you cast yourself into the forest;
where did you depart from this morning? The monk replied, "I am a newly ordained monk who has never studied Chan. The Master said, "You have entered hell with your living body.
Later, after [the monk] had departed, another monk brought this up to Master Zhimen Kuan. Zhimen said, "Why did he not say, 'The key is in the Master's hand'?"
One day, the Master went to the infirmary to visit a sick monk. The monk asked, "Master, the four great elements are fundamentally empty;
from where does illness come? The Master replied, "It comes from the place where you, Venerable, ask. The monk gasped for breath and asked again, "What is it like when one does not ask?
The Master said, "Cast off your hands and lie in the vast sky. The monk said, "Yes," and then passed away.
Chan Master Hongyin of Shending in Tanzhou was the son of the Hu family of Xiangshui. Since he began his travels as a wandering monk, he had worn but a single robe to endure both cold and heat.
Once, while he was with several senior elders in the region between Xiang and Mian, a certain monk raised a discussion on the vehicle of the patriarchs, displaying considerable agility and wit.

While they were having a meal at the Yefan Mountain Inn, the monks continued their discussion without ceasing. The Master said, "The three realms are mind-only; the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only.
'Consciousness-only' and 'mind-only'—who says these words? Is it the sound heard by the ear? A monk replied, "They are the words of Fayan. The Master asked, "What is their meaning?
The monk said, "Because it is mind-only, the sense organs and their objects do not reach one another. Because it is consciousness-only..."

The sounds and colors were vivid and clear. The Master asked, "Is the tongue’s perception of flavor a faculty (indriya) or an object (viṣaya)? He replied, "It is. The Master then used his chopsticks to place a vegetable in his mouth;
with it held in his mouth, he spoke indistinctly, asking, "What do you mean by 'mutual penetration'? Those seated there were startled, and the monk was unable to answer.
The Master said, "The joy of the journey does not mean one has finally arrived home; to penetrate the subtleties of intellectual understanding is not called 'seeing the Way.
One must practice with true practice, and one must awaken with true awakening. The monk bowed and withdrew.
Later, he returned to Changsha and lived in seclusion at the Sengsheng Zang on Mount Heng. A wealthy and nobleman from Xiangyin came to visit Fuyan, whereupon [he encountered] the Master.

He entered the master’s quarters and beheld his countenance, which was serene and tranquil. A single almsbowl hung upon the wall, and there were no other possessions besides. The man felt a deep sense of devotion and prostrated himself before him, saying:
"This divine cauldron is the place where my family has cultivated merit for generations. We have long lacked a patriarchal master; I pray that you, Master, will come with us.
What do you think? The master smiled and consented. He immediately loaded the master onto his own horse and escorted him back. Only after ten years did the monastery finally flourish.
His seat was a single dilapidated wooden bed used as a Dharma throne; his contentment with such austerity was beyond compare.

Furthermore, because both his virtue and seniority were great, he was revered by all quarters like the ancient Zhaozhou. A monk asked, "What is it like before one has heard of all dharmas? The Master said, "The wind whistles and the rain falls.
The monk asked, "What is it like after hearing them? The Master said, "It is good to understand the words. Another asked, "Before the fish-drum has sounded..."

[The monk] asked, "What about at that time? The Master said, "Look at the sky; look at the earth. [The monk] asked, "What about after the bell has sounded? The Master said, "Holding the bowl, he ascends the hall.

[The monk] asked, "What about 'the cold spring in the ancient ravine'? The Master said, "This is not where a patch-robed monk walks. [The monk] asked, "What is the place where a patch-robed monk walks?
The Master said, "One does not see the cold spring in the ancient ravine. [The monk] asked, "What about 'offering with both hands'? The Master said, "A vessel of honor."
[The monk asked: "How is it when one is in the hall? The Master said, "What is it? [The monk] asked: "When a student reaches the Jewel Mountain and returns empty-handed, how is that?
The Master said, "The thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month. [The monk] asked: "What is the Master’s house style? The Master said, "When hungry, one does not choose one's food.
[The monk] asked: "What is the Master’s phrase for benefiting others? The Master said, "Gathering firewood and picking vegetables. [The monk] said, "Is this not merely..."
"This is also 'neither'. The Master said, "You must still be more discerning. Question: "When one brushes away the dust to see the Buddha, what then?
The Master said, "The Buddha is also dust. Question: "What is the livelihood of a man of the Way? The Master said, "Since my youth, I have never entered a schoolroom.
An official pointed to a wooden fish and asked, "What is this? The Master said, "It startles many back to their senses."
The Master was a man who rarely dozed. An official asked, "Have you not come to this place? The Master replied, "I strike the mindless with the mindless.
He asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "A head of ash and a face of dust. The official asked, "Why is it like this? The Master said, [as before].
[The monk] said, "How can one not find the mountain monk strange? He asked, "I do not yet understand: is there anything further beyond the Dharma-body? The Master said, "There is.
[The monk] asked, "What is this matter that lies beyond? The Master said, "The golden crown upon the head of Vairocana. [Another] asked, "The Bodhi tree is fundamentally non-existent;
from where could its fruit come? The Master said, "Can you call it 'non-existent'? [Another] asked, "When the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta practiced..."

[The Master] was repairing a bridge. Someone asked, "Whose bridge is this? The Master said, "It is mine. He asked, "Whose road is this? The Master said, "It is the Buddha’s. He asked, "Who is it that repairs bridges for the Master?
The Master said, "Someone from later on. He asked, "How was it before you met the former masters? The Master said, "Walking east, walking west. He asked, "How is it after you have met them?

The Master said, "Carrying my staff across my shoulders. He ascended the hall and cited Dongshan, who said: "Greed, anger, and delusion—how utterly ignorant they are! Fortunately, today I have come to recognize them."
When walking, he strikes; when sitting, he beats. Entrust this to the Prince of Mind for detailed investigation; for immeasurable kalpas, one has not been liberated.
I ask you three: do you know, or do you not? The Master said: "The ancients spoke thus, but Shending does not agree. Greed, anger, and ignorance—truly there is no knowing.
Throughout the twelve periods of the day, let them be as they will: when walking, they go; when sitting, they follow. Entrust this to the Prince of Mind."
What can the mind-king be compared to? From immeasurable kalpas past, it has been fundamentally liberated. Why must one further inquire whether it is known or not?
Chan Master Yuncong Cizhao of Guyin Mountain in Xiangzhou first attended upon Master Heng of Baizhang during the summer retreat.
One day, as Baizhang ascended the hall, he cited the *Madhyamaka-śāstra*, saying: "Perfect enlightenment is without name or form; following conditions is itself the site of practice."
The Master then went out and asked, "What is perfect enlightenment that is nameless and signless? Baizhang said, "Do you see the pillar?

"What? the Master said. "When the roof collapses, the blue sky is revealed. [The student] asked, "When one breaks through the roof and sees the blue sky, what is the meaning?

The Master said, "It penetrates from top to bottom. [The student] asked, "If a fire breaks out in one place, you may handle it as you wish. But what about when fires break out simultaneously in all eight directions?"
The Master said, "Excellent. The monk asked, "Is there still anything further to seek? The Master said, "If you seek it out, I will burn you to death. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Even if you do not seek it out, I will still burn you to death. He addressed the assembly, saying, "If you can utter the First Phrase..."
It bursts forth from within the stone. If you can speak the second phrase, I will bring it out for you. If you can speak the third phrase, you will not even be able to save yourself.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A white cat with claws and talons so fierce; Raised in the hall, no insects dare pass.
This is clearly the method of finding one's place upon the tree; One must strictly avoid granting words to outsiders. "What is meant by 'granting words to outsiders'?"
[The Master] said: "Do not err in your response. A monk entered the room and asked, "At this very moment, is there still a teacher?
The Master said, "The lamp has shone through the night; where is it not clear? [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, what is the matter? The Master said, "Tomorrow is the Cold Food Festival."
Chan Master Yuanlian of Guanghui Monastery in汝州 (Ruzhou) was a member of the Chen family of Quanzhou. Upon arriving at Shoushan, Shoushan asked, "Where have you recently come from?
The Master replied, "From Hanshang. Shoushan held up his fist and said, "Is there such a thing as this in Hanshang? The Master said, "Yes."
“What kind of bowl is this that makes such a sound? The Master said, “Blind! The Teacher said, “Exactly so,” gave a single clap, and departed.
On another day, he asked again, “When a student has personally reached the Jewel Mountain but returns empty-handed, what then?
The Master said, “A torch before every door. At that moment, the Teacher attained great enlightenment and said, “I no longer doubt the old monks of the world.”
“Tongue,” [he said]. Dongsan asked, “How do you understand this? Tell me how it is. The Master replied, “It is simply water-gypsum on the ground.
Dongsan said, “You have understood. The Master then paid his respects. Later, after he had taken up residence, a monk asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master replied, “A red banner flutters atop a bamboo pole. (Said by Minister Yang Yi.)
A monk asked, "There is no Maitreya above in the heavens, and there is no Maitreya below in the earth.
I wonder where he is? The Master said, "Beating bricks and striking tiles. The monk asked again, "Fengxue said, 'At the head of the Jinsands Beach is the horse-herding woman.

What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Even speaking further would not suffice. A monk asked, "What is the true person of no station? The Master said, "A wooden board on top and [a wooden board] below."
Tie asked, "In that case, the retribution for the offense has a place to go. The Master said, "The Judge, drop your pen!
The monk bowed. The Master said, "Drag him out! A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Two is not many.
He ascended the hall and said, "When the two head monks of the two halls at Linji saw each other, they both let out a shout at the same time. Everyone, tell me: was there a guest and a host, or not?"
If you say it exists, you are merely a blind man. If you say it does not exist, you are likewise a blind man.
To say it neither exists nor does not exist is ten thousand *li* away from Yaizhou. If you can speak here, you too shall receive thirty blows; if you cannot speak, [you shall likewise receive them].
"Thirty more blows! When a monk reaches this point, how can he escape from this mountain monk’s circle?
(After a long silence) Alas! The frogs and earthworms leap up to the Thirty-three Heavens and crash into Mount Sumeru, shattering it into a hundred pieces.
(He picks up his staff and says: "A pack of unperforated iron hammers! Retreat quickly! Retreat quickly!"
Chan Master Zhisong of Sanjiao at Chengtian Monastery in Bingzhou went to visit Shoushan. He asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
Shoushan replied, "At the edge of the city of King Chu, the Ru River flows eastward. At these words, the Master attained realization and suddenly harmonized with the intent of the Buddhas.
He then composed three verses on the Three Mysteries (*sanxuan*), which say: One must employ it; one must employ it directly. Do not let the mind and intellect waver. Three...

The Lion’s Roar resounds through the year; throughout the ten directions, the foxes have vanished. I possess the nature of True Suchness (Tathatā), yet it remains hidden like a figure behind a curtain.

Once the gates of the six sense-doors are shattered, the Seal of Vairocana is revealed. This adamantine essence of true bone is worthy of praise; with a single sweep away of the six objects of dust, there is forever no obstruction.
The vast and empty world takes emptiness as its substance; within this substance, non-action is the true arrival home. Upon hearing this, Shan was enlightened.
"Please have some tea. The Master asked, "Did you compose these three verses yourself? The Master said, "Yes.
Sanshan said, "Suppose someone were to instruct you to manifest the thirty-two marks—what then? The Master said, "I am no wild fox spirit. Sanshan said, "Save your eyebrows!
The Master said, "How many has the Master already lost? Sanshan struck him on the head with his bamboo staff.
He said: "This fellow will cause trouble hereafter. Later, after taking up residence, he ascended the hall and said: "Mañjuśrī brandishes his sword and traverses Mount Wutai;

Tangming blocks the way with a single path, cutting off all demonic deceptions. Since the Buddhas of the three ages have not yet emerged from the vehicle of the teachings, the fish swimming beneath the net find it difficult to pass through the Dragon Gate.
Casting the hook across the four seas, one seeks only the fierce dragon; this discourse on the mystery beyond the categories is intended for those who seek to know."

Consciousness! If you were to raise up and proclaim the fundamental principle (*zongzhi*), Mount Sumeru must be ground to powder. If you were to speak of Buddhas or Patriarchs, the waters of the great ocean would have to dry up.
When the precious sword is brandished, its radiance extends ten thousand *li*. I grant you one path to speak in a way that penetrates all quarters;
yet when the throat is gripped tight, where can all of you draw breath? A monk asked: "Those of dull faculties delight in the Lesser Dharma; they do not themselves..."

"Faith is becoming a Buddha. [The student asked,] "After becoming a Buddha, what then? The Master said, "Grasping a qilin in the water. [The student] said, "If that is so, then one immediately ascends the high seat.
The Master said, "Riding an ox up to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven. [A student] asked, "The ancients would pick up, push aside, or brandish the whisk."
"What is the meaning? The Master said, "Riding a donkey, one does not wear boots. [The monk] asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not the environment'?
The Master said, "In one's hometown there is a road, yet no one reaches it. [The monk] asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not the person'? The Master said:
He secretly conveyed the Emperor’s decree and accompanied [the Master] for a hundred stages, saying: "What is meant by 'both the person and the environment are stripped away'?
The Master said: "A headless shrimp with its toes pointing to heaven. He asked: "What is meant by 'neither the person nor the environment are stripped away'?
The Master said: "The long willow lane south of the Jin Temple. He asked: "Regarding the ancient saying, 'The eastern mountain and western ridge are green,' what was the meaning? The Master said:
"Persia has large nostrils. [The monk] said, "In that case, Kāśyapa in India is my teacher here in this land.
The Master said, "Vajrapāṇi’s palm is broad. [The monk] asked, "Of the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the true eye?
The Master said, "The Stone Buddha of Kaihua claps his hands and laughs; the Lady of Jin Temple knows how to sing. [The monk] asked, "Why did Linji knock down Huangbo?"

The *vinaya* master was struck with a staff. The Master said, "A dog that is truly upright does not steal oil; a rooster runs off clutching a lamp. He asked, "What is the mechanism for cutting through people?
The Master said, "Use it whenever you need to. [The monk] said, "I ask the Master to use it. The Master said, "Drag this dead man out!
Minister Zheng asked, "On the hundred-foot pole, one plays ball alone; from the ten-thousand-fathom precipice, one has a thread tied to the waist."
"How is it now? the Master asked. Zheng replied, "Planting my feet in Youzhou, I have been wrestling in Guangnan. The Master said, "I have seen through this barbarian and Chinese hybrid.
Zheng said, "For twenty years I have been within the borders of Jiangnan; only this time have I truly seen the Chan Master. The Master said:
A blind old woman blows on a fire. A monk asked, "The two extremes must not be established; the Middle Way need not be settled. I do not yet understand the meaning of this—what is its intent?
The Master said, "Elephant tusks come from Guangnan. The monk said, "I do not understand. Please, Master, point it out directly.

The Master said, "A leather ball from the barbarian lands costs eight hundred coins. Ascending the hall, he said: "Cold and warmth, heat and chill, wearing clothes and eating food—these are naturally complete and lacking nothing."
What is there to seek everywhere? It is simply that people are unwilling to accept it. Is there anyone now who can accept it?
If there is, you must not fail the mountains, rivers, and the great earth. Be careful. Question: The Patriarch came from the West.

The Tripitaka Master was departing for the East. [A monk] asked, "What matters will you clarify on your journey? The Master said, "The Buddha Hall is being renovated; the old monk is building a Sangha Hall.
The monk said, "In that case, you have fully clarified the matter of today. The Master said, "How is the matter of today? The monk gave a shout. The Master struck him.
[Another monk] asked, "What is the place where a student applies his mind? The Master said, "Shaving the head until it is clean."

While washing his bowl, he asked, "What is the place where a student of the Way practices? The Master said, "In front of the Sangha Hall; behind the Buddha Hall. Ascending the hall, he cited a verse by Fayan:
"Seeing mountains, they are not mountains; Seeing water, how could it ever be otherwise? Mountains, rivers, and the great earth— All are but a single orb of the moon.
"The Great and Small Fayans have not yet left the Nirvana Hall," [the Master] said. "Sengjiao, however, is not like this."
"Behold the mountains, rivers, and the great earth; each uses their own awl and knife. Take care.
When a fellow practitioner arrived at Zen Master Zhisong of Tiefo Monastery in Xinzhou, the Master saw him and asked, "Do you still remember our acquaintance?
As the head of the visiting group hesitated, the second monk struck the head with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*) and said, "Why are you not quick?"
He replied to the Master. The Master said, "One arrow, two targets. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Mount Tai. The Master said, "Have you seen the Dragon King?
He replied, "Venerable Sir, please try to say something. The Master said, "If I were to say anything, it would be like ice melting and tiles shattering.
The monk hesitated, and the Master said, "You do not believe what I have said. [The Master] asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go?"
[The monk] departed. The Master said, "Going downhill, one does not run; such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter.
A monk asked Chan Master Huaiyi of Shoushan in Ruizhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
"A three-foot staff and a broken tile basin. [A monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The bottom of the bucket falls off.

[The monk] asked, "What words or phrases did the sages of the past have? The Master said, "Thus have I heard. [The monk] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Believe, accept, and practice accordingly."
Chan Master Chuping of Renwang Monastery in Chizhou asked Shoushan, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
Shoushan gave a shout. The Master bowed. Shoushan raised his staff; the Master said, "Old monk, you have no world!
Shoushan threw down his staff and said, "It is difficult to deceive one with clear eyes. The Master said, "The grass-robbers are utterly defeated."
While Chan Master Zhimen Huikai of Suizhou was serving tea to a monk-envoy from Beita, the Master rose, bowed, and said, "Envoy, please sit in the seat above.
The envoy replied, "How would one dare to nest upon the head of a hawk? The Master said, "If one does not become a dragon atop the staff, one will follow it.
He then struck once with his sitting mat (*zuoju*). After the envoy finished the tea, he rose and said, "Just now, I have inadvertently offended you, Master."
Furthermore, the Master said: "Du the Chan Guest from Jiangnan—what is he looking for with a second bowl?
When the Mountain Head Huizhao of Lumeng in Xiangzhou was asked by Attendant Yang Yi:
"If one does not fear tigers when entering the mountains, yet guards against people on the road—how is this? The monk said: "The gentleman is broad and open. A monk asked: "What is the deer?"
[At] Menshan, the Master said, "The large is large; the small is small. [The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person among the mountains?
The Master said, "Lying across or sleeping upright."
The Minister Wang Sui, a lay practitioner, visited Shoushan and attained the meaning beyond words. From that time on, he practiced and deeply clarified the Great Dharma.
At the end of his life, he wrote this verse: "The lamp in the painted hall has already been extinguished; To whom can I point my finger and speak?
Coming and going are fundamentally ordinary— The spring breeze sweeps away the lingering snow."

Chan Master Chiming Shishuang Chu’uan of Tanzhou was a successor of Chan Master Fenyang Wude Zhao. He was a native of the Li family of Quanzhou. In his youth, he served as a scholar.
At the age of twenty-two, he entered the monastic order at Yinjing Temple on Mount Xiang. His mother, who possessed virtuous conduct, encouraged him to travel abroad for study.

Having heard of Fenyang’s reputation for the Way, he went to visit him. Fenyang looked at him and silently took note of him as a vessel of potential. For two years, he did not permit him to enter the inner chamber;
whenever he saw him, he would invariably scold him or disparage various other teachers. Furthermore, when he did offer instruction, it was always of a mundane and vulgar nature.
One night, the student complained, saying: "I have been at this Dharma seat for two summers now, yet I have received no guidance. I am only increasing my worldly attachments."

"Amidst the dust and toil of worldly life, I have watched the years and months slip away in a flash. Since I have not clarified my own fundamental matter, I have lost the true benefit of leaving the household life.

Before he had finished speaking, Yang stared intently at him and scolded, "This evil spiritual friend dares to deceive and exploit me! In a rage, he raised his staff to drive him away. The Master prepared to intervene in defense, but Yang covered the Master’s mouth with his hand.
At that moment, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "Now I know that Linji’s Way transcends ordinary circumstances. For seven days, I served him..."
After a year, he took his leave and went to rely upon Chan Master Tang Ming-song. Ming-song said to him, "The Inner Secretary Yang Da-nian possesses high insight;
his entry into the Way is steady and substantial. You must go see him. The Master then went to visit Da-nian. Da-nian asked, "Facing each other, we do not recognize one another;
yet from a thousand miles away, our winds are the same. The Master replied, "Recently, I have received an invitation from your mountain gate. Da-nian said, "Is that truly so?"
Tuokong asked, "Master, last month you left Tangming. Nian said, "I just now regretted asking you that. The Master said, "An adept. Nian then gave a shout.
The Master said, "Exactly so. Nian shouted again. The Master made a sweeping gesture with his hand. Nian stuck out his tongue and said, "..."
"Truly a dragon-elephant! Nan'an said. "What words are these? He then called for the guest master to serve tea, saying, "It turns out you are one of our own household.
The Master said, "That too is unnecessary. After the tea was finished, Nan'an asked again, "What is the single phrase by which you, the Seat-Holder, benefit others?
The Master said, "Carefully. Nan'an said, "If that is so, then it is like a long-skirted bride running through the mud. The Master said, "Who?"
Nian Daosheng said, "He resembles the Inner Secretary (Li Ao). He is a master! He is a master! The Master said, "I grant you twenty blows.
Daosheng tapped his knee and said, "What kind of place is this? The Master clapped his hands and said, "Nor can I let this one pass either. Daosheng laughed heartily.
He asked again, "Do you remember the circumstances of Tangming’s enlightenment at that time? The Master said, "Tangming asked Shoushan, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
Shoushan replied, 'On the banks of the city of King Chu, the Ru River flows eastward.
Yuan asked, "Regarding these very words, what is their underlying intent? The Master said, "A lantern hanging over the water. Yuan said, "In that case..."
"In that case, I have failed the ancients. The Master said, "If you, Inner Secretary, have doubts, seek another teacher. Yuanian said, "A three-legged frog leaps up to heaven.
The Master said, "Leap as much as you wish. Yuanian then laughed heartily. He was lodged in the meditation hall, where he questioned Zhizheng day and night regarding the Dharma.
Hearing the words and deeds of the past, he regretted having met him so late. Later, while at court, he encountered the Prince Consort.
Commandant Li Gongzun said to [An]xū, "I recently encountered a practitioner of the Way who is truly a lion of the West River.

Li said, 'I am bound by official regulations and cannot go to pay my respects; what can be done? An remained silent for a moment, then returned and said to his master, 'Lord Li is one among those who follow the Buddha-Dharma.
Having heard that the wind of the Way has arrived from afar, he has a desire to see you, yet because of the laws, he is not permitted to pass with his attendants.'"

The Master followed him accordingly. At dawn, he went to pay his respects to Lord Li. Lord Li read the visiting card and sent a pageboy to ask: "If you can speak the Way, I will see you, Venerable Sir.
The Master said: "I have come specifically today to pay my respects. He then sent the pageboy again, saying: "The inscription on the monument is carved in white characters;
one should plant green pines along the path. The Master said: "Were it not for this auspicious day, such an occasion would surely be difficult to encounter on any other day."
The Official stepped forward again and said, "The Commandant says: 'If that is so, then let us meet with the Senior Monk.
The Master replied, "From head to toe. The Official then came out, took his seat, and asked, "I have heard that there is a golden-haired lion in West River.
Is this true? The Master asked, "Where did you get this news? The Official gave a shout. The Master said, "A jackal howling. The Official spoke again.
"Hai! The Master said, "Exactly so. The official laughed heartily. As the Master was taking his leave, the official asked, "What is the one phrase for you, Venerable, as you depart?
The Master said, "Take good care of yourself. The official said, "How is this different from other places? The Master said, "And what about you, Excellency?"
The Duke said, "I grant the Senior Monk twenty blows. The Master said, "Solely for the sake of its circulation. The Duke shouted again. The Master said, "Blind! The Duke said, "Go well.
The Master responded with two "Yeses" (*nyo nyō*). From then on, he frequented the gates of Yang and Li, taking the Dharma as his friend.
After a long time, he took his leave to return to Hedong. Mazu asked, "I have a phrase to entrust to Tangming; will you receive it?

The Master said, "The bright moon shines upon the traveler at night. Mazu said, "But that does not quite match. The Master said, "It may still be bearable before midnight, but after midday, it brings even more sorrow to people.
Mazu said, "Why is it that the Vajra statues in front of Kaibao Temple are recently breaking into a sweat? The Master—

Dongshan said, “If that is so, then I shall follow you, Elder. Yunyan let out a single sigh. Yunyan said, “A true lion cub; a great lion’s roar.
Dongshan said, “To let go and then pull back again. Yunyan said, “Just now I lost my footing and fell.”
Furthermore, he was helped up by a household servant. The Master said, "What end will there ever be? Nian laughed heartily.

Lord Li composed a verse, saying: "The black brush extends over a thousand li; The golden coffin reveals a pair of feet. Humans and devas alike cannot fathom it."
"Take care, Red-Bearded Barbarian. Because his mother was elderly, the Master returned south to Ruizhou, where he became the head of the assembly at Dongshan.

"I was merely wishing for it just now. After Daoyuan had been appointed as the abbot, he ascended the hall and said:
"All Buddhas and the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* of all Buddhas—all emerge from this sutra.

"What is this person within the realm? The Master said, "The one who follows the current does not look back; he chops his hand and gazes toward the Fusang tree.

The Master said, "The mouth can invite disaster. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master...
[The monk] said, “The waves in Lake Dongting overflow the heavens. [The monk] asked, “When the east surges and the west subsides, what then?

The Master said, “Seek it. [The monk] asked, “When walking alone at night’s quiet, what then? The Master said, “Three bundles of thatch. [The monk] asked, “When the precious sword has not yet emerged from its scabbard, what then?

The Master said, "A mass of earth. Question: "After he saw him, how was it? The Master said, "A mass of earth. Question: "What is it like when 'once attained, forever attained'?

Xueyan said, "Could it be my junior uncle Ju? My late teacher instructed me to seek him out. Thereupon...
The junior monk went to the guest quarters in the morning and asked the senior monk, "Are you not Master Ju Shu? Please do not take offense at my having disturbed you just now.
The Master then gave a shout. He asked again, "When did you arrive at Fenyang, Elder? Xie replied, "I arrived at such-and-such a time.
The Master said, "I have heard your name since I was in Zhejiang; yet your realization is only like this. How can your fame spread throughout the world? Xie was speechless.
He then performed a prostration and said, "I, so-and-so, am guilty of transgression. Later, the Master arrived at Xī Ān (West Hermitage) in Hángzhōu.
The abbot of the hermitage had previously met Míngzhāo. The abbot recited a verse, saying: "Upon the western peak at its highest point, who would dare face such a formidable faculty?

Transcending both the mundane and the sagely, two layers of radiance flash forth in an instant. The Master asked, "What are these two layers of radiance? The abbot replied, "The moon rises from the east; the sun shines toward..."

As he was about to pass away, the Master asked, "When the Abbot had not yet seen Mingzhao, how was it? The Abbot replied, "A full cup of oil is difficult to exhaust. The Master asked, "After he saw him, how was it?
The Abbot replied, "A mind with many thoughts is easily dried up. After [Mingzhao] took up residence there, a monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'?
The Master said, "The white chrysanthemum has just bloomed; the sun is warm once more. A gentleman of a hundred years does not meet [him]."
Chun asked, "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'? The Master said, "The great earth is cut off from all news; carefree and solitary, one simply abides in the real.
Chun asked, "What is 'seizing both person and environment'? The Master said, "The weeds overgrow and people change their countenance; both ordinary and holy are equally empty.
Chun asked, "What is 'neither seizing the person nor seizing the environment'? The Master said, "The clear breeze and the bright moon in the wilds."
The Old Man smiles as they greet one another. He ascends the hall and says: "Śākyamuni did not appear in this world; Bodhidharma did not come from the West.

The Buddha-dharma pervades the world, yet those who speak of the profound do not open their mouths. He ascends the hall again: "The bells ring and the drums sound; the magpies chirp and the crows caw.
For all of you, I have finished preaching Prajñā and expounding Nirvāṇa. Can you all believe it? Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva..."
He performed great supernatural feats before the assembly. "If you do not believe me," he said, "I shall go to other lands to save sentient beings from suffering and benefit them.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To open one's mouth is to produce redundant speech; to keep one's mouth shut is likewise to produce superfluous speech. He then declared:

"By the imperial decree of the Golden Wheel Sovereign, the customs of the thatched-roof cottage are unique. Ascending the hall again, he said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have their mouths hung upon the wall. Heaven...
"How will the Old Monk below handle this? How will you all, when traveling to various places, bring this up?
My speaking in this way is merely the result of long-standing habituation; it is like the lips worn smooth by constant use. [He lets out a shout. [Ascending the hall:
An ancient said, "If I were to exclusively exalt the teachings and the lineage, the grass in the Dharma Hall would grow a fathom deep. It cannot be used to lock you, O *dāralas* (monks)."
He turned and left the gate of the Sangha Hall. Although this is so, it is still like a tortoise on dry land playing with dust.
Entering the hall for the discourse: To speak of gradualism, he returns to the ordinary and accords with the Way; to discuss suddenness, he leaves no trace behind.

Even if one were to discuss its suddenness and return to its ordinariness, this too would be a matter of forcing it to be so. A question was asked: "When Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, why was it that..."
A hundred birds offered flowers in their beaks. The Master said, "When the fruit ripens, even the monkeys value it. The monk asked, "Why do they not offer flowers after seeing [the Master]?
The Master said, "The forest is too sparse for the birds to pass through. The monk asked, "The seven stars shine with brilliance as dawn approaches;

without violating the imperial wind, please speak. The Master said, "The general’s horse hooves are red. The monk said, "Wrong! The Master then struck him. The monk bowed and spread out his sitting mat.
When the monk finished his initial collection [of verses], the Master said, "One unfolding and one collecting; every dharma is complete. If you wish to ask anything further, what is the point?
He then asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master struck him.
Chan Master Dadao Guquan of Bajiao Hermitage on Mount Nanyue was a native of Quanzhou. He received the Dharma from Fenyang and roamed freely through Lake Xiang.
Later, he went to visit his fellow practitioner, Chan Master Ciming. Ciming asked, “White clouds hang across the valley mouth; from where have you come, O man of the Way?
The Master looked left and right and said, “What fire broke out last night that has burned out the ancient tombs? Ciming—
[Zhaozhou] said, "That is not it; speak further. The Master made a tiger's roar. Ming struck him with his sitting mat.
The Master caught it and pushed Ming onto the meditation seat. Ming then made a tiger's roar.

The Master laughed loudly and said, "I have encountered more than seventy virtuous teachers (śāstrins), but today I have finally met a true master. Later, when the Senior Monk Yu (who later resided at Fachang) came to visit, he asked:

"Is the master of the hermitage here? The Master said, "Who is it? He replied, "A traveling monk. The Master asked, "What do you want? He replied, "I wish to pay my respects to the master of the hermitage.
The Master said, "It happens that the master of the hermitage is not here. He asked, "And what about you? The Master said, "I told you he was not here;
why speak of 'you' and 'me'? He grabbed his staff and drove him out. When the monk returned the following day, the Master drove him out again. On another day, he came once more...
A visitor arrived and asked, "Is the Hermitage Master here? The Master said, "Who is it? He replied, "A traveling monk. Without waiting for the curtain to be drawn aside, he entered.
The Master grabbed him by the chest and held him fast, saying, "Tigers and wolves roam here at my place. You bed-wetting ghost, what do you want coming here two or three times?

"I see how extraordinary Fenyang was," [the monk] said. "What is the master of this hermitage? The Master said, "One must discern him upon entering.
[The monk] said, "Is it not simply this very thing? The Master said, "How many people have you deceived! [The monk] said, "Where is what was said before?
The Master said, "Listening without clarity; calling a bell a jar. [The monk] said, "When the myriad dharmas are extinguished, the whole body is manifested."

He asked, "I wonder, when a guest arrives, with what will you receive them? The Master said, "Yunmen’s rice cake; Zhaozhou’s tea. He said, "..."

The Patriarch called out, "Dharma-heir, wait! The matter remains. The Master placed his sitting cloth over his shoulder and, without looking back, ascended the hall.
