Elder, if you are indeed such a person, then even if the great earth were transformed into gold and the long rivers were churned into ghee and curd to offer to you, it would not be considered excessive. But if you are not yet such a person—
As for even a drop of water or a single thread of silk, one must don fur and wear horns, pull the plow and drag the harrow, and only then can one repay them.
Have you not seen the Patriarch say: "If one enters the Way without penetrating its principle, one must return to the world to repay the faithful offerings"?
This is a matter of certainty; it will never be in vain. Venerable Elders, time is precious; the moment does not wait for man. Do not wait for that single day.

The gaze of light falls to the ground. In the field of the monastic robes, there has not been the merit of even a single basketful of earth. Within the Iron Ring Mountains, one suffers the agony of a hundred punishments.
Do not say it is not the Way. Be careful.
A monk asked Zen Master Yue of Rui Guang in Suzhou, "What is the meaning of 'Juzhi’s Single Finger'? The Master said, "Moon."
At the third watch, he passed through the marketplace.
Zen Master Yuan of Dongshan in Ruizhou ascended the hall. A monk stepped forward and threw down his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*).
The Master said, "Caught on the first cast. The monk picked up the sitting cloth. The Master said, "Seeking cleverness and ending up clumsy. The monk said, "From of old, there has been no birth."
Verse: One must surely meet a true connoisseur. The Master said: "A Persian enters the land of Tang. The monk laughed heartily and returned to the assembly.

Chan Master Baizong of Fuyan on Mount Nanyue, successor to Chan Master Shishuang Yong, ascended the hall and said: "When the World-Honored One took seven steps, his lifting of the foot was entirely at odds [with the Way]."

Gazing about in the four directions, one encounters obstructions at every turn. That the golden robe was bestowed and passed away brings calamity upon descendants; that the jade verses were transmitted and handed down hangs upon people’s lips.

To awaken to the nature through the wind and the banner is still not to have left the realm of form and dust; to perceive the needle cast into the bowl-water is entirely a matter of narrow, partial vision.
The Patriarch sat facing the wall for nine years, yet did not perceive even a hair’s breadth [of duality]. Master Lu transmitted the robe through six generations merely to seek petty gain.
One shout from Jiangxi shows no understanding of guarding the beginning; Deqiao’s total bestowal reveals ignorance of protecting the end. As for Nan-shan’s turtle-nosed staff—
Vainly pointing to origins and traces, the withered pines of Beiyuan merely display their elegant appearance; Yunmen’s glance and reflection result in "two falls" and "three falls";
Linji’s total upholding results in "seven errors" and "eight errors. If one speaks of the five ranks of ruler and subject, it is just like paper horses crossing the river.
To further push the matter of guest and host intersecting is like a clay figure bathing; it merely transcends the realm of forms, yet it is not like a falcon chasing a rabbit.
To mingle one's traces within the dust is not yet like a dog gnawing at a pig; how is this different from leaping into a pit or falling into a moat?

It is precisely like avoiding drowning only to throw oneself into a snare. An understanding such as this remains within the ordinary path. For a man of the Way who has transcended the conventional, how can he speak of it?
"Do you not see that even the worldly man Tao Qian could perceive events and discern the opportune moment?
Now, as descendants of the ancestral house, it is impossible for there to be no blood beneath the skin. (He lets out a shout.)
A monk asked Chan Master Dayang of Jingzhou, "What is the phrase that strikes through?

The Master said, "Beyond the railing, the bamboo sways in the wind, startling the recluse from his sleep. The monk said, "The gate of Avalokiteśvara is wide open. The Master said, "A lion bites a man.
He then added, "To awaken to the Way by hearing sounds is to lose the eyes of Avalokiteśvara; to clarify the mind by seeing forms is to remain in darkness."
Mañjuśrī’s nostrils: one out, one in; half-open, half-closed. Last night the mud ox roamed the vast ocean;
even until now, he has not been seen to return. *Tuḥ!*
Chan Master Daozhen Jingzhao of Jingyin Monastery in Dongjing, successor to Chan Master Fushan Yuan, was asked by a monk: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Incense is prepared in the morning;
water is changed in the evening. The monk asked: "What is the wondrous power of wisdom of Avalokiteśvara? The Master said: "A dog barking in Henan."
A donkey brays in Hebei. [The Master] ascends the hall, takes up his staff, and says: "This staff of jili wood is well able to discourse on the Buddhas and patriarchs.
Since the deaf have now heard, the mute also understand speech. It points to white stone as jade; it designates yellow gold as earth."

If you understand it in such a way, he has not yet granted his approval. Since he has not granted his approval, do not be reckless. "Beating the drum in the south street while dancing in the north street.
Chan Master Renyue of Xinghua in Luzhou was a native of Quannan. A monk asked: "What is the great Dharma of the Buddha?"
[The student] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Three times you have come to receive blows. [The student] asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "The curved wooden meditation seat. [The student] asked, "How do you attend to guests when they arrive? The Master said, "The staff.
[The student] asked, "The entire Tripitaka is nothing but names and words. Apart from these names and words, it is like..."
"What is the instruction? The Master said, "A mangy horse rubs against a withered willow. The student said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "A camel loves to eat salt.
The student asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "Where the iron whip points, the horse neighs in vain."
A monk asked Master Fǎng of Yùquán in Jīngmén Commandery, "By what dharma do the sages of antiquity instruct people?
The Master picked up his staff. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Handed over with both hands. The monk hesitated.
The Master then struck him.
Chan Master Huicheng of Dinglin in Suzhou asked a monk, "What is the Way? The Master said, "It is right before your eyes.
The monk said, "Why do I not see it? The Master said, "Blind!"
Chan Master Ruozhu of Benjue Temple in Xiuzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Way? The Master raised his fist. The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "You do not even recognize a fist. In the hall, he ascended the seat and said: "To speak of Buddhas and Patriarchs is to bury the ancestral transmission;
to cite the ancients and discuss the present is to detain the monks. Clearing away the path ahead—who would dare stand before it? [He] stood them all down together."
The wind—no need to bring it forth. With a scale that has no markings, how can one distinguish the weight?
If you can distinguish it, Mount Sumeru weighs but half a grain; if you cannot distinguish it, break the scale and meet everyone in the land of Japan.
A monk asked Chan Master Puzi of Huayan in Tokyo, “What is the guest within the guest?
The Master said, “The traveler’s road is as vast as heaven. The monk asked, “What is the host within the guest? The Master said, “The nobleman’s gate is as deep as the sea.
The monk asked, “What is the host within the host? The Master said, “The Emperor’s decree throughout the realm. The monk asked, “What is the guest within the host? The Master said:
The General’s Command Beyond the Frontier states: "When the guest questions the host, they exchange sharp, wounding blows; when the host questions the guest, they share life and death.
When the host discerns the host, one drinks the air and swallows the sound; when the guest seeks the guest, ten thousand miles of white clouds. Thus, there is no meaning within the words;
the meaning lies within the words. If you can understand this clearly: a pair of solitary wild geese strike the earth and soar high into the sky.
Not yet clear on this point, a pair of mandarin ducks stand alone by the side of a pond. Disciples of Zen who understand the sound shall together bear witness.
Those of different streams, like shadows and echoes, must be most meticulous. After a long silence, he said: "If it were Tao Yuanming, he would have knit his brows and departed immediately."
A monk asked Chan Master Weishi of Qingyin Monastery in Nankang Prefecture, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Slanting streets and winding alleys.
The monk asked, "Who is it that walks upon the Way? The Master said, "A hundred arts, a hundred failures."
Chan Master Fenneng ascended the hall at Hengyue Temple in Tanzhou. When the patriarchal wind is raised, ten-thousand-mile clouds disperse;

when the Dharma command is executed, a thousand peaks take on a cold hue. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, white waves surge to the heavens; amidst the waves of the great ocean, red dust fills the earth.
One must reflect upon the days of Huangmei in the past and Shaoshi in former times; unable to yield to others while seeking to preserve oneself, he [the Master] consequently...
To grind the chaff in response to one’s resolve and to sever an arm to repay a heart—how does this compare to here at Mount Heng? We have mountain-field millet rice and a bucket of unsalted soup;
we dwell together in shared hardship and joy, following the high and adapting to the low. It is certainly not a matter of buying at a high price from the south.
At the northern end, they sell it cheaply. It simply causes Mañjuśrī to bow his head and Kāśyapa to knit his brows; Nāgārjuna and Aśvaghoṣa must swallow their voices and suppress their breath;
even Maudgalyāyana and Śāriputra cannot do anything about it. Why is this so? Observe the Dharma of the Dharma-King closely:
such is the nature of the Dharma-King’s Dharma.

Chan Master Fang Rui of Langye in Chuzhou, successor to Chan Master Bao Yingzhao, ascended the hall and said: "The Creator has no intention to produce things, yet every thing comes into being of itself.
Dew and rain have no intent to nourish things, yet the spiritual sprouts flourish naturally. Therefore, medicinal decoctions need not be consumed."

Yet the illness naturally subsides; the true physician is not encountered, yet the mind becomes clear of itself. Thus one knows that the wondrous wisdom and numinous light are not obtained through conditions.
Only when you reach this point may you be permitted to advance. Langye will meet you in another way—does anyone here understand?
If there is no one, one must not suppress the noble to make them base.
A monk asked Chan Master Xiyn of Mount Xingyang in Yingzhou, "What is the phrase for letting go at the edge of a precipice?
The Master said, "The bright moon shines upon the secluded valley. The monk asked, "What is the phrase for reviving after having reached the end?
The Master said, "White clouds arise in the great void. The monk said, "If that is so, then the woodcutter emerges from the forested hills, singing of spring everywhere. The Master said, "..."
This is attained through the human path. Entering the hall, he said: "To see and yet not see; having seen, it is not yet fully realized.
The traveler on the road; the bird roosting in the forest. The pagoda within the moon has twelve stories; the celestial stars wrap around the heavens five hundred times. Do you wish to understand?
Holding the talisman of night-brightness in hand, how many know the dawn? *Chan* (Examine!)."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhicai of Ruiyan in Mingzhou, a successor of Chan Master Jin of Shimen, "What is the phrase that cuts off all streams? The Master said:

"Excellent. [The student] asked, "What is the phrase of 'following the waves and drifting with the currents'? The Master said, "Following. [The student] asked, "What is the phrase of 'the casket covering heaven and earth'?

The Master said, "Closing. [The student] asked, "I have received your instruction on these three phrases; how does one distinguish between the ancient and the modern? The Master said, "Henceforth, you must not speak of them erroneously.
He ascended the hall and said: "Because Heaven is impartial, it constantly covers all; because Earth is impartial, it constantly supports all. The sun and moon..."
Because all is equal, the four seasons are eternally luminous. Because nirvana is equal, the holy and the ordinary are not two.
Because the human mind is equal, there is no contention between high and low. He held up his staff, struck once, and said:
"All you practitioners of Zen, this staff speaks the Dharma-gate of equality for you day and night. Do you hear it? If you hear it, I can guarantee that you are walking on the path."
When the matter of the feet was concluded, [the Master] said, "If one says they did not hear it, this also allows that the eyes at the crown of everyone's heads are correct. Why?
Because this Dharma is equal, with no high or low; this is called Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. After a long silence, he smiled and said:
The subsequent text is extensive.
A monk asked Chan Master Chongzhen of Puci Monastery in Runzhou, successor to Chan Master Jinshan Ying: "What is the realm of Puci? The Master said: "It emerges."
Upon entering the gate, he saw Mount He-lin. [The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm? The Master said, "As soon as you enter the gate, you see Elder Zhen.
Chan Master Zhonghe of Ruizhu in Taiping Prefecture was asked by a monk: "When one attains the seat and donning the robe, all understand; what about that which is above?"
"What is the matter regarding the vehicle of our school? The Master said, "Simply know that ice is water. [The monk] asked, "Is there anything further?
The Master said, "Stop asking how water becomes ice. [The monk] said, "One who plays in the tide must be a man who plays in the tide. The Master said, "This monk has come from Zhejiang."
A monk asked Zen Master Huaxian Yuantong of Mount Jinshan in Runzhou, "When you propagate the school's tenets, who was it that received the Dharma from you?
The Master held up his whisk. The monk said, "On the walls of the Iron Cauldron City you were certified; by the cliffs of the Azure Stream the ancestral lamp shines.
The Master gave a sweep with the whisk and said, "If you do not listen attentively to the matter, you will call a bell a cauldron."
A monk asked Chan Master Xianzhong Zuyin of Shifusi in Yuezhou, "What is the Immovable Honored One?
The Master said, "A monkey on a hot griddle. The monk asked, "What are the thousands of millions of transformation bodies?

The Master said, "Adding incense, changing the water, lighting lamps, and sweeping the floor. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma-body Lord, the Teacher Vairocana? The Master said, "The hitching post for the horse."
[The monk] asked, "What connection is there? The Master said, "I would tie this fellow to death. [The monk] asked, "One who knows how to kill the Buddhas and patriarchs is a true adept.
What is the sword that kills the Buddhas and patriarchs? The Master said, "I do not behead those already dead. [The monk] asked, "What is the sword of the Master?
The Master said, "An edict is not issued twice. [The monk] asked, "What is mutual production? The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth."
Dizang asked, "What is the arising of thought? The Master said, "A rabbit gazing at the moon. He asked, "What is the arising of the flowing stream?
The Master said, "Without interruption. He asked, "What is form and emptiness? The Master said, "A five-colored screen. Ascending the hall, he cried out, "Ho! Ho! Ho!
The fish and dragons of the ocean bottom have all been dried up; a three-legged toad flies up into the heavens; a shell-shedding tortoise!"
"Alive amidst the fire. Entering the hall for instruction, he said: "When it is not yet time, black and white are not yet distinguished;

when the time arrives, there is no illumination—mud and water are mixed together. A pillar leaps into a lantern; let that be as it may. But why are your eyebrows trailing beneath the heels of your feet?
Even if you were to understand this clearly, it would still be like a monkey wearing a bamboo hat. At this point...
It is not yet clear how this differs from the fable of the crooked legged man who wore boots. Nevertheless, those who laugh at me are many, while those who smile with understanding are few.

While residing at Jingzhai Monastery in Hangzhou, Chan Master Zhenjing visited Daguan. He then asked, "I have a superficial understanding of the sutras and treatises, yet I do not believe in Chan at all.
I pray that you, Master, will resolve my doubts. Daguan said, "Since you do not believe in Chan, how can you claim to understand the sutras?
Chan is the mainstay of the sutras, and the sutras are the net of Chan. By grasping the mainstay and straightening the net, one realizes Chan and sees the sutras. The Master said, "For..."
Jiashan said, "I speak of Chan-observation. Guanzhi said, "The text that follows is long. The Master said, "If it is so, then the Sūtras and Chan are of one essence.
Guanzhi said, "The Buddha and the Patriarchs are not two dharmas; they are like a hand forming a fist, or a fist being a hand.
Thereupon, the Master attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "For over twenty years I have used my mind to speculate, Several times I have grasped this very heart."
Ashes. Now, in my decline, I have met a true friend: Li Bai was originally a scholar.
Master Gongchen of Xiyu Mountain in Anji Prefecture ascends the hall: "Lingyun saw the flower; there was a film over his eyes."
Xuansha knitted his fingers; he suffered misfortune upon his person. Not knowing how else to pass the time, one naturally attains peace and happiness of body and mind.

He ascended the hall and said: "Principle arises from phenomena, and the mind is born following objects. When both phenomena and objects are forgotten, there are thousands of mountains and ten thousand rivers—how can one attain the state of 'just so'?
After a long silence, he said: "Do not dig into your own flesh to create a sore. The Master possessed a lineage that reached back to the ancestral source.
It was essential that thirty fascicles circulate in the world.
A monk asked Chan Master Shanduan of Panyu Monastery in Kunshan, Suzhou: "Birth and extinction are all constant phenomena;
what is it like when there is neither birth nor extinction? The Master said: "Kunlun wears boots and stands in mid-air. [The monk] said: "Is this not..."
[The student] said, "This is not a place for people. The Master said, "A barren woman adorns her hair with flowers and sleeps in the fire. [The student] said, "May the assembly bear witness.
The Master said, "Furthermore, behold the earthen oxen fighting as they enter the sea."

When Layman Li Duanyuan was a child, he resided in the state academy and frequently studied Chan texts. Although he later married and entered official service, he remained steadfast in his devotion to the ancestral Way.
Consequently, he built a dwelling resembling a *ārāma* (monastery) in his rear garden and invited Daguan to reside there.

Day and night he consulted and studied with him, to the point of forgetting both sleep and food. One day, Daguan looked at the official and said, "Were it not for the power of manifesting [this body], how could you have reached such a state?"
"Alas! What can be done about having nowhere to enter? The Duke asked, "Are heaven and hell ultimately existent or non-existent?

I beg the Master to explain this clearly. Guoan said, "The Buddhas speak of existence within non-existence; it is like seeing flowers in the sky with one's own eyes. Your Excellency seeks non-existence within existence;
it is like grasping at the moon in water with your hands. It is truly laughable that you see a prison before your very eyes, yet do not avoid it, while hearing of it from outside your mind."
"Heaven. [The official] did not realize that joy and fear were already within his heart; good and evil had become external objects.

The Grand Marshal (Taishou) need only understand his own mind, and naturally he will be free from delusion. The official asked, "How does one understand the mind? Guo'an said, "Do not deliberate upon good or evil at all.
The official asked, "After not deliberating, where does the mind go? Guo'an said, "Please, Grand Marshal, return to your residence first. The official said, "Only..."
"Where does the mind go after a person dies? Guanyin said, "If you do not yet know where life goes, how can you know where death goes?
The official said, "As for life, I already know it. Guanyin asked, "From where does life come? The official was at a loss for words.
Guanyin rose, thrust his hand toward the official’s chest, and said, "It is right here. What more do you intend to deliberate upon? The official said, "I understand. Guanyin asked, "How so?"
Huìgōng said, “I only knew how to hurry along the journey, unaware that I had lost my way. Guāntuò replied, “A hundred-year dream—only this morning have I finally awakened.
He then spoke a verse: “At thirty-eight years of age, I was muddled and ignorant; when I finally attained understanding, [it was too late].”
How is this different from ignorance? The waters of the Bian River flow on and on; the embankments of Sui lie deep and vast. Master, it is time for you to return. The arrow-like waves rush eastward.

A monk asked Chan Master Yue of Dongting, successor to the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Liang of Jianfu in Suzhou: "Without relying on verbal explanations, I beg the Master to grant me instruction. The Master said: "Great..."
The assembly all saw you ask in such a manner. [The monk] said, "Is it not simply this very thing? The Master said, "Rarely do we encounter a guest with pierced ears.
[This was] Chan Master Zhang Xi’s dharma successor.
A monk asked Chan Master Baoxuan of Huangyan in Taizhou, "If one does not wish to remain silent, yet must rely slightly upon provisional means, what then?
The Master said, "To know and yet deliberately transgress. The monk bowed; the Master then struck him.

Chan Master Xi Yu Shizi Jingduan of Anji Prefecture was a native of his own province. His surname was Qiu. Initially, upon seeing a lion being played with, he attained enlightenment regarding the essential point of the mind.
He went to visit Chan Master Longhua, received his seal of approval, and subsequently returned to his hometown, where he fashioned a lion out of dyed silk.
He wore a lion skin at that time, and was thus known as Duan Shizi (Lion Duan). Prime Minister Zhang, admiring his Way, personally invited him to open a dharma assembly at Mount Wu.
His transformative influence spread widely. On the day of the opening of the hall, the Monastic Official recited the proclamation, reaching the point: "Pushing over and turning back the head."
He kicked over [the incense burner] without supporting it; before he had even recited the seven-fascicle Lotus Sutra, the sound of the "Fisherman" song was heard first. The Master stopped him.
He then ascended the seat, picked up the incense, and after completing the prayers for the Emperor, he raised his voice and chanted: "Originally, I am but a lone fisherman of Xiao and Xiang."

"From the west, from the east, from the south, and from the north," the great assembly clamored in approval. The Master looked at them and smiled, saying, "Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma King;
the Dharma of the Dharma King is thus. He then descended from his seat. Entering the hall on the second day of the second month, the Zen Elder had this to say: "What meaning is there?"
The spring breeze touches the eyes and a hundred flowers bloom; the young nobles and sons of royalty are drunk and intoxicated day after day.

Only the cypress trees of the Chen dynasty before the palace do not conform to the tastes of the fashionable crowd. To those who follow the Zen way, this is all there is—no need for further deliberation.

After a meal, one simply drinks a cup of tea and stretches one’s legs to sleep upon the long platform bed. *Du!* (A shout). When the Master arrived at Huating, the assembly requested him to ascend the hall.
The Lion of Mount Ling, roaring amidst the clouds: the Buddha-dharma is beyond discussion; it is better to perform a somersault.
[With this, he descended from his seat. A monk asked, "What is it like when the antelope has not yet hung its horns? The Master said, "I am afraid.
The monk asked, "Since you are a *kalyāṇamitra* (a spiritual friend), why are you afraid? The Master said, "I have never seen such a strange beast."

Chan Master Zhenru Muduo of Daopei in Tanzhou, a descendant of the twelfth generation under Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Cuiyan Zhen of Fuzhou, was born to the Wen family of Linchuan in Fuzhou. A monk asked: "Zhao..."
"What is the meaning of 'The cypress in the provincial hall'? The Master said, "The wind has grown fierce tonight; the solitary traveler is already cold.
He asked, "The former master did not say those words—what then? The Master said, "Only the traveler knows the bitterness. He said, "Ten years wandering through the red dust;
today alone his body is revealed. The Master said, "Adding frost to snow. He asked, "What is the Buddha within the city?"
The Master said, “In the midst of ten thousand people, one does not plant a signpost. [The monk] asked, “What is the Buddha of the village? The Master said, “A mud pig and a scabby dog.
[The monk] asked, “What is the Buddha of the mountains? The Master said, “Where no people come or go.

[The monk] asked, “What is the one phrase of the separate transmission outside the teachings? The Master said, “It cannot be translated. [The monk] asked, “When Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch...”

"How is it? the Master said. "The hairs on one's body stand on end. [The student] asked, "After seeing [this], what then? The Master said, "Sweat breaks out on the forehead. He ascended the hall and said:
"When the moon arises as one, the vastness of heaven and earth—who suffers the injustice? When the moon arises as two, east, west, south, and north have no root.
When the moon arises as three, Sudhana specifically heads south to seek instruction. Therefore it is said: 'To let go is for the Tathāgata to extend his hand.'"
Guang seized him. "Dust and mud conceal the radiance. Now tell me, is this letting go, or is it seizing? After a long silence, he said:
"The three dots of the character *yī* are a circle; the myriad things are naturally fresh and new. He ascended the hall and said: "The ancient Buddha said:

'In the past at Vārāṇasī, I turned the Dharma wheel of the Four Truths—this was falling into a pit and a ditch. Now I again turn the most wondrous, unsurpassed Great Dharma Wheel—this is merely adding earth upon earth.'"
"Add mud. [The Master asked: "Is there anyone nowadays who, without traversing the rungs of a ladder, transcends all things alone?
After a long silence, he said: "Look out beyond the heavens; who is that person within? He ascended the hall and said: "What is this 'A-la-la'? He reflected back on the years of Po-zao-duo.
Suddenly struck by his staff, he finally realized he had been remiss toward me. With his staff, he struck the incense altar.
He gave a shout and said, "Fallen! Fallen! He then ascended the hall and said: "Reaching into space to pursue an echo—this merely exhausts your spirit.
When dreaming awakens and you realize it was not real, what further matter remains? The old man Deshan is upon the eyebrows and eyelashes of all of you. Do you perceive him yet?
If you do perceive him, then 'when dreaming awakens and you realize it was not real. If you have not yet perceived him, then reaching into space to pursue an echo will ultimately lead nowhere."

[The Master] said, "Even if you were to be straightforward and clear-sighted here, it would still be like climbing a mountain to offer tribute at court. Is there anyone who transcends all things alone?
After a long silence, he said: 'Do not pretend to be clever. A monk asked: "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat upon the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas;
why was it that he did not attain the Way of Buddhahood? The Master said: "It would have killed him with grief. He ascended the hall. [The Master said: "White Clouds..."
"Serene and limpid. Water flows into the vast ocean; the myriad dharmas are fundamentally at rest—what further matter could there be?
Therefore it is said: "There is the provisional, and there is the real; there is illumination, and there is function. When people reach this point, how do they proceed? After a long silence, he said:
"Wherever there is a path to ascend, those of superior capacity will walk upon it. He ascended the hall and said: "This mountain monk originally has no accumulated possessions, yet..."
Having obtained sufficient gruel and sufficient rice, when weariness comes, one simply sleeps; let them do as they please, whether they lean eastward or westward.
Entering the hall, [the Master said: "The ancients said: 'One Śākyamuni, two Yuanhuo, three Buddhas;
all the rest are bowl-dropping ghosts (wàn tuō qiū). Huiguang does not agree with this. One Śākyamuni, two Yuanhuo, three Buddhas—all are bowl-dropping ghosts. You people..."
Do you know where the light of wisdom falls? If you do, I grant that you possess eyes of iron and pupils of copper. If you do not, do not say:
"Having weathered many perilous winds and waves, my small boat once traveled across the Five Lakes. Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said:
"When a single speck of dust arises, the entire earth is fully contained within it. He struck the ground with the staff and said: "The world of Wondrous Joy..."
Miscellaneous fragments. Now tell me, where is the Tathāgata Acalo right now?

If one can recognize him, it may be said that one has ascended to wondrous enlightenment without moving a step. If you have not yet recognized him, he enters nirvana within the eyebrows and eyelashes of all of you.
[He strikes the meditation seat once. Entering the hall, he said: "To know without using thought; to understand without using deliberation. Lu...
The price of rice is high in Ling; the radishes in Zhenzhou are large. Entering the hall, he raised his staff and said:

"Zhihai’s staff sometimes acts as the Vajra King’s precious sword, sometimes as a crouching lion, sometimes as a probing pole or a blade of grass, and sometimes it does not function as a staff at all.
Do you all understand this thoroughly? If you do understand it, it is like a dragon finding..."

Water. Like a tiger leaning against a mountain, appearing and disappearing, rolling up and unfolding, applied freely and horizontally. If you have not yet understood this, it is very much like trying to escape one’s shadow at midday.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "The ten directions gather together; each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting Buddhas."
"The mind attains the highest rank in emptiness and returns home. Under the gate of Huiguang, one is directly uprooted and ascends, bypassing all formal categories.
Now that you have all reached this place, the wind and clouds are spread across the earth and your fangs and claws are fully formed;

you simply lack the thunderous roar to "scorch your tails. Now, for you all, I shall strike the sudden thunder! (He strikes the meditation seat with his staff and descends from the seat. The Master [lived] during the Shaosheng era.
On the eighth day of the tenth month of the second year, he spoke a verse without having been ill: "Last night at the third watch, wind and thunder suddenly arose;
the clouds dispersed across the vast sky, and the moon sank behind the eastern stream. After a long while, he took leave of the assembly and passed into stillness.

His cremation yielded about one *dou* of *śarīra*, each as large as a bean; his eyes, teeth, and fingernails remained uncorrupted. His disciples divided the relics and erected stupas in the capital and in Tan.
A monk asked Zen Master Chong’ao of Xilin on Mount Nanyue, “When there is a question and an answer, the guest and host are clearly distinguished.

When there is neither question nor answer, how does one discern them? The Master said, “Those who sit, sit; those who stand, stand. The monk asked, “What is it like when one understands it in this very way?
The Master said, “The tongue pressed against the upper palate. The monk bowed. The Master said, “Do not try to hide it.”
Chan Master Faya of Xuedou in Mingzhou, successor of Chan Master Yuan of Jiangshan, was asked by a monk: "The student does not ask about the meaning of the Westward Journey;

I beg the Master for a skillful means to point out the deluded state. The Master said: "A thunderclap passes over one's head and yet one still sleeps. The monk said: "Thank you, Master, for answering my question. The Master said: [Silence].
He opened his mouth again and asked three times, "Who is it? The monk replied, "What can I do? This student has not yet prostrated. The Master said, "Stop this evasive behavior.
Chan Master Xingyue of Shaoshou, whose secular surname was Dai and who hailed from Yihuang, presided over Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "In my school, there is no..."
Words and phrases are merely the laborious tracing of footprints on the path. Since the ready-made koan has already manifested in myriad ways, how can one bear to further enter the gates of others?
To meet face-to-face and seize the opportunity directly—what need is there for the arduous toil of *pāṭha*? *Tuḥ!*
Chan Master Wenzan of Kuangguo Temple in Langzhou, a successor of Chan Master Shuangfeng Hui, was asked by a monk: "The Dharma of non-duality—please, Master, speak of it quickly. The Master said:
The official said, "If that is so, then everyone has their share. The Master said, "It is finished. The official said, "A brocade screen is rare throughout the world;
its brilliance benefits the state and is seldom seen in this age. The Master said, "Withdraw."

Chan Master Zhiyuan of Qionglong in Suzhou, successor to Chan Master Dinghui Xin, ascended the hall and said: "When blessings arrive, I do not speak of Chan; with nothing to do, I sleep until the sun is high."
When someone asked about the meaning of the Patriarch’s intent, he struck him two or three times. Tell me, assembly: why did he act thus?
It was because that fellow would not cease disturbing the mountain monk’s sleep.

Chan Master Qixiao of Shouning Monastery in Guizhou, successor to Chan Master Yunfeng Yue, ascended the hall and said: "If you do not understand the Way when you look around you, you are still somewhat off the mark.
To wonder about the path as you take a step is to wrongly employ names and words. Gentlemen, today this mountain monk shall follow the error with the error; you..."
People such as these see that there are eyes, hear that there are ears, smell with the nose, and taste with the tongue;
why then do they not understand? After a long silence, he said: "Emperor Wu sought immortals but did not find them; Wang Qiao sat upright and ascended to heaven. *Du!* A monk asked:
"The great assembly has gathered like clouds; what should we discuss? The Master said: "A Persian enters a bustling marketplace. The monk said: "If that is so, then..."
"Grass bends as the wind passes; he has gone. The Master said, "Ten thousand *li* away, gazing toward the ancestral pass.
Zen Master Jingyin Zhen’s Dharma heir, Zen Master Changqing Huixian Wenhui of Fuzhou, was asked by a monk: "Leaving the precious land of the Upper Birth, one ascends the invitation..."
“The Sage’s place of practice—how is it that he is the Immovable Honored One? The Master said, “A solitary boat carries the bright moon.

[The student] asked, “If one suddenly encounters a situation where both oars and paddles have been stopped, what then? The Master said, “The fisherman especially loves to stay overnight among the reeds.
[The student] asked, “In the West, when advancing on the long journey of the Way, they use a wax man as a test. I wonder, what is used here as a test? The Master said, “Iron.”
Danzi asked, "What is the underlying meaning? The Master said, "The large is large; the small is small.
Chan Master Jichao of Qisheng in Fuzhou ascended the hall, held up his staff, and after a long pause, said, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time..."
All of it is right here, leaping and bounding. Does the assembly understand? The Buddhas of the past have already spoken;
the Buddhas of the future have not yet spoken; the Buddhas of the present are speaking now. I dare ask you all: what is this matter that is being spoken?
He struck the meditation desk once and said: "Sūlu sūlu.

Chan Master Xinghua Shaoqing of Tanzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Xinghua Yue, ascended the hall and said: "In the school of the Patriarchs, the Buddha-dharma does not exist; even wholesome dharmas [do not exist]."

Before the hall, one need not speak further of benevolence and righteousness. Although this is so, matters do not always follow a single path. I have heard it said that our parents grieve for us; they labored to give us life.
Desiring to repay their profound kindness, one finds that the vast heavens offer no limit to it. One dares not injure or damage even a hair or the skin of one’s body.

This was the filial piety of Zhongni of Lu. To revolve within the three realms and yet be unable to relinquish affection—only by casting aside such affection to enter the state of non-action does one truly repay that debt of gratitude.
Thus, our Great Awakened World-Honored One practiced austerities on the Snowy Mountains and attained enlightenment at Magadha;
he then ascended to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to preach the Dharma for his mother. This was the filial piety of Śākyamuni. Having attained great liberation, he...
With great supernormal powers, holding a golden mendicant’s staff in his hand and supporting a dragon-embossed bowl in his palm, he went to the gates of hell and stood there in solemn contemplation.
There he saw his compassionate mother, weeping boundlessly. This was the filial piety of Maudgalyāyana.
But what is the filial piety of Xinghua? After a long silence, he said: "Today, Xinghua does not go up to heaven, nor does he enter hell; he is at the Hall of Good Dharma."
In the center, upon the throne of the Lamp-King Buddha, he preached the Dharma for his mother to repay her labors. He then asked, "Tell me, where is my mother now?
He continued, "My mother accumulated sufficient roots of goodness during her life; there is no need to ask the Buddha, for she has certainly been reborn in heaven.

Among humans, a long life is rare in all ages; ninety years is already a reduction of one year from a full span. Having descended from the seat, he said, "I venture to trouble the assembly to offer incense."
A single stick of incense is offered to assist this mountain monk in repaying his filial debt. Since she was the mother of this mountain monk, why then do you trouble yourselves to burn incense?
Have you not heard it said: "When a member of the eastern family dies, the members of the western family offer their condolences"?
With hands beating one's breast, one cries out: "Heaven! Heaven!"

Chan Master Huilì Shànzhōu of Línjiāng Commandery, successor to Chan Master Fāng of Yùquán, ascended the hall and said: "A falcon from the vast heavens, amidst ten thousand layers of clouds, makes but a single dash."
"What is this? "Tsk! On the full moon day of the twelfth month in the first year of the Yuanyou era, the Master bathed and cleansed his hair, then spoke this verse:
"This mountain monk has dwelt at Ruijun; never before have I manifested words or phrases. Seventy-three years have come, and seventy-three years have gone.
Having finished speaking, he passed away. Five days later, his beard and hair grew back.
The Chan Master Zhikai Puyong Daoping of Dongjing, a successor in the thirteenth generation under National Teacher Dayue, ascended the hall and said:
"I, this mountain monk, do not understand the Buddha-dharma; yet I act for the sake of others."
There is no underlying cause or reason for this. At times it is half-open and half-closed; at other times it is fully released and fully withdrawn.
It is just like dropping a stone coldly into a crowd of ten thousand people: suddenly striking one person, one then realizes that [the Way] flows everywhere.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Zhaozhou has four gates; gate after gate leads to the Great Road. Yuyuan has four paths; path after path leads to Chang’an.
Gate after gate leads to the Great Road—after all, who has personally arrived? Path after path leads to Chang’an—look clearly as you take this step forward. He struck his knee once and said:
"For the traveler who has not yet returned at year’s end, the west wind outside the gate is cold. Ascending the hall, he raised an example.
Panshan addressed the assembly, saying: "It is like the earth supporting a mountain, yet not knowing the mountain's towering loftiness;
it is like a stone containing jade, yet not knowing the jade's flawlessness. When the ancients spoke thus, they were very much like those who embrace their own plunder while crying out for innocence.
Under Zhikai, everyone is resolute and spirited—capturing tigers and rhinoceroses alive, seizing fierce dragons with their bare hands; they can accommodate Mount Sumeru within their eyes."
"One could fit the waters of the great ocean within one's ears. He then took up his staff and said, "This is not for the sake of showing off one's skills to others;
the bearing of a true man of spirit ought to be like this. He struck the ground with the staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Letan Jingsiang of Hongzhou was the son of the Fu family of Nancheng in Jianchang.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Ten fingers have eight joints. The monk asked, "How is my hand like the Buddha’s hand?
The Master said, "It is difficult to distinguish gold from brass. The monk asked, "How is my foot like a donkey’s foot? The Master said, "The road at Huanglong is perilous."
[A monk] asked, "Every person has their own karmic affinity for birth. What is the Master’s affinity for birth? The Master said, "I firmly guard the critical pass;
neither ordinary people nor sages may pass through. On the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and said:

"The discourse at Vulture Peak, the pointing at Caoxi—letting go of those who first saw and then looked up with bated breath, before even asking the old, ancient sage of Longmen: 'Last night at the third watch, it turned toward the west. At this very moment—"
Someone asked, "What is the moon? [The Master replied: "If you can utter a single phrase at the point where light and darkness have not yet been distinguished, you will join hands with the ancients.
If you have not yet reached this, Bao Feng cannot help but follow the model and draw the likeness to respond to the occasion.
He then drew a circle and said: "Its pure radiance lasts for ten thousand ages and again ten thousand ages; how could it be limited to a single moment among men?"
[The Master] looked at him at night. In his room, the Master asked a monk, "When Bodhidharma returned to the West, he carried a single sandal in his hand.
Why did he not take both with him? The monk replied, "This land also required that he leave behind some trace. The Master said, "One foot is in the Western Heaven; one foot is in this Eastern Land.
What is the reason for this? The monk was speechless. [The Master] then asked another monk, "The One Sole Solidity..."
"The body manifests within all dust. What is this body that manifests within the dust? The monk pointed to the incense burner and said, "This is the incense burner.
The Master said, "It brings calamity upon the Buddhas of the three periods; they are born directly into hell. The monk was at a loss for words, and the Master struck him.
When the Master was unwell, a monk asked, "How is your health these days, Master? The Master replied, "Earth."

Before ascending to the stage of the Bodhisattva grounds, he burned two bundles of paper money. The Master would always sit cross-legged at night with his hands joined in prayer, as if facing a great guest. When first sitting, his hands were level with his knees;
by the fifth watch of the night, they would invariably reach his chest. Consequently, he was called "Xiang Chashou" (Auspicious Hand-Joiner).
Chan Master Huilán of Kuàngxiào in Wèizhōu was a man of unknown origins. He styled himself the "Immortal of the Azure Void" (Bìluò Dàorén).

He once wrote the names of the Seven Buddhas upon his robe with ink; thus, the monastic community referred to him as "Lánbùkùn" (Lán the Tunic-Bearer). A poem titled "Imitating the Song of the Hermitage" (Nǐ Cǎo'àn Gē) by him circulates in the world and is fully recorded in the *Pǔdēng Lù*.
Toward the end of the Jiànyán era, when the rebel barbarians invaded the Huái region, they captured the Master and presented him before their chieftain.
The official Chang said, "Have you heard my name? The Master replied, "All I have heard is the name of the Great Song Emperor.

Chang became enraged and ordered his attendants to strike him with a hammer; yet every time the hammer reached him, it broke into pieces. Chang was struck with wonder and marvel, and he summoned his subordinates to serve the Master with reverence.

After ten days had passed, the Master sought firewood to immolate himself, but no one dared to provide it. He personally gathered the wood and constructed a niche for his own cremation, appearing serene.
He sat upright; immediately, smoke and flames arose, and radiant light surged in all four directions. Many of the captives knelt and prostrated themselves as their skin was scorched.
When the fire subsided, he obtained five-colored śarīras. Taking his bones along with them, he returned northward. All the monks and nuns he had held captive were granted their freedom.
People of the Huo region sing of this to this day.

On the day Chan Master Dongming Renshan of Tanzhou opened the hall for his formal sermon, a monk asked, "When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, Brahma led the way in front and Indra followed behind. When you, Master, appear in the world, what auspicious signs are there?

The Master said, "Even were it hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, I would drive them all at once into the cow-pen. The monk asked, "What auspicious signs are there? The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, have never [seen any]."
A Flowering Eye.
Zen Master Xiaoqin Mingwu of Puzhao in Sizhou was asked by a monk: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed?
The Master said, "Even closer to the east. [The monk] said, "He is a true son of Guishan and a direct grandson of Zhihai. The Master—[nodded].
He said: "I laugh at those bystanders clutching their fishing rods. Entering the hall, he continued: "Reaching up to grasp at empty space—how can one ever catch up?

Turning over to cast a shadow—this merely exhausts one's own form. When it is brought forth right before one’s face, one instead lets it slip by. After all, how is it? He struck the meditation seat and said:
"In the end, you have deliberated all wrong."
Master Zunjiao of Donglin on Mount Lu ascended the hall and said: "Before the fifteenth day, one lets a move pass;
after the fifteenth day, it cannot yet be deliberated upon. Right at the fifteenth day, try and speak a single phrase."
After a long silence, he said: "The mountain colors are lush and verdant as the spring rain ceases; the incense fills the cypress courtyard as the *mulan* blossoms open.
Chan Master Zhi of Fuyan in Tanzhou ascended the hall and said: "On the peak of Fuyan Mountain, the clouds unfurl and roll up at will, morning and evening.
Suddenly they fall upon the level ground; when a guest arrives, it is difficult to find the gate."
Chan Master Dongming Qian of Tanzhou had long served under Zhenru. Later, he resided at Mount Gui.

The practitioner Zhong Daozhe of Zhenru’s hermitage held his character in high esteem and would frequently visit him. One day, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, Zhong asked: "As the sutra says: 'If I press my finger...'"
"Seal of the Ocean Emission of Light. "What is the Buddha’s intention? The Master said, "Śākyamuni would deserve twenty blows of the staff.
[The student] asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "What need is there to press the fingers? [The student] asked, "What about 'As soon as you raise your mind, the dust of worldly toil arises'?
The Master said, "That too is the Seal of the Ocean Emission of Light."
Chan Master Puyin Cijue of Kuangxiao Monastery in Quzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Xuedou Ya. He was born into the Xu family of Quanzhou.
In his meditation hall, he would ask a monk, "Before your parents were born, where were you practicing? As soon as the monk attempted to answer, he would strike him out. Or he would say, "Attain!"
"The grindstone is under your feet. When the monk attempted to look, he struck him out as well. Someone said, "Speak! Speak! When the monk attempted to open his mouth, he struck him out again.

Chan Master Puren of Qingshan Monastery in Hangzhou, successor to Chan Master Qingxian, ascended the hall and said: "Having no choice in the matter, I shall engage in some entanglements with you all."
All sentient beings suffer solely because they have not yet shed the dust of the mind and have not eliminated the limitations of their emotional attachments.

Seeing forms and hearing sounds, they drift with the waves and follow the currents, transmigrating through the three realms and drowning in the four modes of birth. This causes right view to remain obscure and leads to stagnation at every turn.

If right and wrong are both extinguished and good and evil are entirely forgotten, one sits and cuts off the heads of the *nirmāṇakāya* and *sambhogakāya* Buddhas, severing the paths of the holy and the mundane.
Only upon reaching this point does one have a slight degree of resonance. Even if it were so, for a patch-robed monk (*bhikṣu*), this would not yet be considered extraordinary.
Why is this? As soon as there is right and wrong, confusion arises and the mind is lost. *Du!* [He] ascended the hall and took up his staff.
The staff said: "Before it entered this mountain monk’s hands, the myriad dharmas were perfectly present as they are. Now that it has entered this mountain monk’s hands, what further matter is there?
After a long silence, he said: "When there is spirit, add to the spirit; where there is no elegance, there too is elegance.
He struck the staff once.
Chan Master Fashun of Jingtu was the dharma successor of Chan Master Fachen.
A monk asked Chan Master Fashun of Wanshou on Mount Lingfeng in Hangzhou, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Hugging a post and swimming like a duck. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "A ball of yellow clay. The monk asked, "What is the Sangha?"
The Master said, "I have shaved off my beard and hair. A monk asked, "Apart from the Three Jewels, is there any other way to benefit people?

The Master raised one finger. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The finger is here; look only at the moon. The wind blows, yet the banner does not move. He ascended the hall and said:
"Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout are all but ripples on a windless sea. The lantern leaps over the green mountains."
"O Heaven! The soul of the pillar is startled and its head splits asunder. Even so, it is much like adding salt to one's thirst.
(He lets out a shout.
On the day of the opening of the hall by Chan Master Shoulong of Qingshan in Hangzhou, a monk asked: "I know that you have long harbored a treasure within your bag."
"Today, I shall briefly borrow from the feast for a look. The Master said, "How very clear! [The monk] said, "When the Lion Roars, it is fully revealed; but what of Mañjuśrī leaning on his sword?
The Master said, "It would startle even this old monk to death. [The monk] asked, "When the thousand Buddhas appear in the world, each has their own extraordinary auspicious signs.
On this day, with what do you, O Master, provide verification? The Master said, "A wooden man holds a board and strikes it amidst the clouds."
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "A stone woman picks up a flute and blows it underwater. Ascending the hall, he said: "Flowers in clusters, brocade in clusters;
for years, salt and sauce have been sufficient for every need. We have kept South Stream Spring’s broken cauldron and entrusted it to a novice to cook the morning congee.
The morning congee is at your disposal to eat as you please, but how do you understand this one phrase: 'Washing the bowl'? [He added: "Much!"
Few people have doubted this.

Zen Master Yue of Huguo was a Dharma successor of Zen Master Hui Ben of Huguo in Jiangling Prefecture. A monk asked: "There is a thing that existed before heaven and earth; it is formless and fundamentally quiescent."
Liao: "I do not yet understand what kind of thing this is. The Master said, "A single stick of ink. The monk said, "If that is so, then it illuminates the past and shines upon the present.
The Master asked, "What is it that illuminates the past and shines upon the present? The monk then gave a shout. The Master struck him.
He ascended the hall and said, "What a fine occasion! Who is willing to take it up? If there is no one, it would be better to preserve it. After a long pause, he said:
A pearl from the Dragon King’s Palace used to catch sparrows.
The Dharma heir of Chan Master Zhikai Ping of the Fourteenth Generation under Nanyue.
Chan Master Jiecheng of P’an-an at Jingyin Monastery in Tokyo was a native of the Liu family of Yichun, Yuan Province.
Entering the hall, he held up his staff and said: “The fundamental nature is pure and still; how is it that mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? Look, look!
Pūrṇa has passed through the nostrils of Śākyamuni, and Śākyamuni has bored through the belly of empty space. Now tell me—”
"Where are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth? He threw down his staff and called to the assembly, saying, "The void has performed a somersault and gone off to the kingdom of Silla.
You all must take care not to mistake the leaves for the child or seek the sword by marking the boat. Entering the hall, he said:
"Throughout the vast expanse, there are only those seeking the Buddha; in all the world, it is difficult to find a man at ease. [This is] the staff and the shout."
Racing against one another creates the taboo of medicine; when one realizes this taboo is non-existent, it is not yet the true source of heaven.
Entering the hall: A servant from Mount Kunlun wears iron trousers; he takes one step for every blow of the staff. How can this compare to fishing for turtles amidst fire or hiding ice in the sun?
Shadows turn into *wangliang* spirits; empty space is bound with hempen rope. Entering the hall: Meeting on a narrow path, do not yet harbor doubt—like a flash of lightning striking a flint.
The fire has already grown slow. If you were instructed to penetrate directly through the three minds, it would be found right here in this single moment.

Reaching this point, even if one engages in a back-and-forth exchange of questions and answers—where sparks fly and stars scatter, where host and guest interchange, where illumination and function, gain and loss, surging waves and towering peaks, and the turning of jade and the rolling of pearls—there is nothing at all that can reach the eyes of a true monk. Have you not seen the [story of] the Flower?
On Vulture Peak, only Kāśyapa was permitted to receive the transmission; when the illness was inquired after at Vaiśālī, who else could have been the Golden Grain?

How could one know that a smile had already established the path? Even if one remained silent, one would still not escape the wind and waves. One must meet beyond the ordinary to truly understand the profound resonance within.
Do you understand? A single melody, vast and empty, moves through the ages; it lies to the west of the thirty-six peaks of Luoyang. *Upward.*
The Hall Master ascended the hall. "If you turn your head to look, you are already at odds with the truth; if you attempt to deliberate, when in kalpas will you awaken?
"Great assembly, the withered mulberry tree knows the wind of heaven—this is looking and not looking. The ocean water knows the cold of heaven—this is thinking and not thinking.

But what do you call the principle of awakening? With a staff made of rabbit horns, one carries the Dharma-realm; with a whisk made of tortoise hair, one dances the Three Terraces. He ascended the hall. [In] the nose...
Sound is fragrance within the ear; saltiness and sweetness are in the eye, while the tongue perceives the profound yellow. The mind can perceive touch, and the body makes distinctions.

Within the ice chamber it is like spring; in the midst of the nine-month summer it is cool. If you see it thus, you will finally know that when entering samādhi within a male body, one emerges from samādhi within a female body.
The sunflower turns with the sun; the rhinoceros-patterned horn observes the moon’s rise. Fragrant maples transform into old age.
Humans. The *mínglíng* (cicada larvae) become *guǒlíng* (wasp larvae). If you do not know this, how bitter! Buddhadāsa granted you a single eye. Ascending the hall, he said:
"In a single thought-moment, if the mind is pure, the Buddha dwells in the Demon King’s palace; in a single thought-moment, if an evil mind arises, the Demon King dwells in the Buddha’s palace.
Master Huai said: "Simply believe in this way; it is called walking with one's feet firmly planted on the ground. In the end...
There is no separate dharma, nor is there any separate principle. Having spoken thus, this old monk fears that you all will let the hawk fly after the rabbit or mark the boat to seek the sword.
Why? Because a wise host accepts neither the Goddess of Merit nor the Woman of Darkness.
Ascending the hall, he raised the staff held by Fenyang and showed it to the assembly, saying: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time are right here in this..."
[The Master] said, "Inside! Because you people have no openings, you end up running into the mountain monk’s staff, needlessly creating complications.
The Master continued, "Fenyang’s way of instructing disciples is much like carrying snow to fill a well; he acts as if no one else exists.
Today, I shall speak out for all of you. Picking up his staff, he said, 'The Buddhas of the three periods do not dare [to look at it]...'"
The program *Qiangsheng* (Forceful Birth) emerges from the mountain monk’s staff and says to all people:
"I do not dare to slight you; you shall all become Buddhas. Having said these words, he performs a somersault and departs into the city of Kuśinagara.
Throwing down his staff, he says: "If you go to various places, present this clearly. The Master [Dongshan] was the same.

When Yuanwu, Fazhen, Cishou, along with ten great Dharma masters and a thousand monks of both Chan and doctrinal schools, attended a vegetarian feast at the residence of Grand Marshal Chen Gong Liangbi, Emperor Huizong went there in private to observe the event. The Grand Preceptor, Duke of Lu, was also present.
There was one Shan Huiyuan, a "tiger of meaning" from the Xianshou (Huayan) school, who addressed the assembly and questioned the Chan masters, saying:

Our Buddha established his teachings, ranging from the Small Vehicle up to the Perfect and Sudden. Having swept away both emptiness and existence to personally realize the true and eternal, he was only then adorned with the myriad virtues and named a Buddha.
I have often heard it said that a single shout of the Chan school can transform an ordinary person into a sage.
This would seem to contradict various sutras and treatises. Now, if a single shout can enter the five teachings of our school, it is a correct teaching;

if it cannot so enter, it is a false teaching. The various Chan masters looked toward their teacher, who said, "What the Dharma Master has asked is not worthy of a response from the three great Chan masters. The junior Elder of Jingyin may be sent to the Dharma Master."

There is no confusion. The Master called out, "Shan! Shan responded, "Yes. The Master said: "That which the Dharma Master calls the 'Teaching of the Lesser Vehicle of the Dull-Witted' has the meaning of existence.
That which is the 'Initial Teaching of the Great Vehicle' has the meaning of emptiness. That which is the 'Final Teaching of the Great Vehicle' has the meaning of neither being nor non-being.
That which is the 'Sudden Teaching of the Great Vehicle' has the meaning of being and emptiness simultaneously. This is the One Vehicle."
The Perfect Teaching (Yuanjiao) is the principle that existence is non-existence and emptiness is non-emptiness (or, as some versions read: emptiness is existence and existence is emptiness).
For example, my single shout is not only able to penetrate the five teachings, but can even penetrate the arts and crafts, as well as all the various schools of thought and the hundred masters.
The Master let out a thunderous shout and asked Shan, "Did you hear it? Shan replied, "I heard it. The Master said, "Since you have already..."

[The Master] asked, "Did you hear it? He replied, "I heard it. The Master said, "That one shout was 'existence'; this can lead one into the Hinayana teaching. A moment later, he asked Shan again, "Did you hear it? Shan replied, "I did not hear it.
The Master said, "Since you did not hear it, that previous shout was 'non-existence'; this can lead one into the Initial Teaching (Shijiao).
Then, looking toward Shan, the Master said, "When I first gave the shout, you said there was sound; when the sound had long since faded away, you said there was none. To say there was none—"
Thus, when there was originally something real, the Way existed; yet now it is truly non-existent. Being neither existent nor non-existent, one can enter the Final Teaching (Jiǒngjiào).

When I utter this one shout, existence is not existence, for existence arises because of non-existence. When there is no shout, non-existence is not non-existence, for non-existence arises because of existence.
Being simultaneously existent and non-existent, one can enter the Sudden Teaching (Dùnjiào). You must know that this one [shout] of mine...
"Ha! This is not used as a mere shout; it transcends both existence and non-existence, and both intellectual understanding and emotional attachment are forgotten.
When the Way is present, not even a speck of dust can stand; when the Way is absent, it pervades the void horizontally. This single shout enters into hundreds of thousands of millions of shouts.
"Ten billion shouts all enter into this one shout; therefore, one is able to enter the Perfect Teaching. Shan then rose and bowed twice. The Master spoke again, saying:
"It is not only the case with a single shout; it extends even to a single word or a single silence, a single movement or a single stillness."

From antiquity to the present, throughout the void of the ten directions, amidst the myriad phenomena of the universe, across the six realms and four modes of birth, and including all Buddhas of the three periods of time and all holy sages—the eighty-four thousand Dharma gates, the hundreds of thousands of samādhis, and immeasurable subtle meanings—these accord with principle and adapt to capacity, forming a single entity with heaven, earth, and the myriad things;
this is called the Dharmakāya. The three realms are mind-only; the myriad dharmas are mind-only.
Consciousness. Throughout the four seasons and eight nodes, the Yin and Yang are of one accord; this is called *dharmatā* (the nature of phenomena). Therefore, the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* says:
"The nature of phenomena pervades all places—whether with form or without form, whether a single sound or a single color. Within a single mote of dust, the entirety contains these four meanings.
Phenomena and principle are boundless, pervasive without remainder; they interpenetrate without being confused, and they blend together yet are not one. Regarding this:
Within a single shout, everything is fully present; yet this is still merely the gateway for manifesting transformation, a skillful means adapted to capacities, termed a "temporary resting place.

One has not yet reached the precious site. Little do they realize that beneath our ancestral masters, mind was transmitted through mind and Dharma was sealed by Dharma—without establishing written words, seeing one's nature is to become a Buddha. There is a supreme path that has not been transmitted by a thousand sages.
Zhangshan asked again, "What is the path that leads upward? The Master said, "You should first understand it by looking downward.
Zhangshan asked, "What is the place of treasure? The Master said, "It is not within your realm. Zhangshan said, "I hope the Chan Master will show me compassion."
The Master said, "Even if the vast ocean were to change, I would never speak for you. Shan Jiao then withdrew in silence.
Those who heard this could not help but admire him with deep respect. The Emperor turned to his attendants and remarked, "The profound mystery of the Chan school reaches such depths;
even the eloquence of Jingyin is rare indeed. An attendant reported, "This is merely the overflow of that Master’s teaching."
Chan Master Yanzi of Falun Monastery on Mount Nanyue was a native of the Chen family of Longquan. He ascended the hall and said:

"If you are one who has attained the truth, your entire being is free from obstruction; your every movement is devoid of even a hair’s breadth of discrepancy. Taking my hand, you emerge from the red dust;

you pry open the upward-opening aperture and settle decisively at the head. Without violating the sharp edge, you take hold of it and bring it forth, applying it exactly as required—down to the finest detail."
Without leakage; the container and the lid correspond. Even were it any of the Buddhas or Patriarchs, upon looking at it, one’s hair would stand on end.
Do you understand? "Go drink tea. A monk asked, "What is the phrase that does not involve the waves and mists? The Master said, "The bright moon on the cold pine;
the drifting wind at the valley mouth. The monk said, "All errors are swept away; a single phrase cuts off the flow of the mechanism. The Master said, "A dot."
The monk said, “I have arrived. The Master said, “Borrowing someone’s mask to dance the Three Terraces.
He asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “A white-fanged tiger. The monk asked, “As for Dongshan’s saying, ‘Three pounds of flax,’ what does that mean?
The Master said, “A venomous snake boring into a pillar. The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “Only when you step on it will you be startled.”
Chan Master Kaifu Chongzhe of Hengzhou was the son of the Liu family of Shaoshan. He ascended the hall and said: "The wondrous body is majestic and manifest everywhere;
one must quickly turn back and take it up. Today, before this assembly, I entrust it to you in its entirety;
do not say that we have anything hidden. He threw down his whisk and called to his attendant, saying: "Why did you strike down the old monk’s whisk? A monk asked: "One..."
The water swallows the vast sky; the three peaks and steep cliffs are perilous. The lion throne has been swept and wiped clean once more;
together we rejoice that the Master has returned. I wonder how you will arrange things upon arriving home? The Master said, "Empty-handed, I clench my two fists. He asked, "What is the meaning?
The Master said, "It bursts forth, difficult to discern. He ascended the hall and said, "This mountain monk has three seals; there is nothing added, subtracted, or left out. Facing one another..."
Presented for inspection: it can transform the ordinary into the sacred. Do you all understand? If you do not yet know, I cannot help but annotate this point layer by layer.
One seal stamps the sky: the sun, moon, and stars are cast downwind. One seal stamps the mud: every head and every object reveals the true mechanism.
One seal stamps the water: the fish's head is twisted around to become the dragon's tail. The three seals are clearly manifest in their essence.
The same. At first glance, it is neither vermilion nor red; high and low shift back and forth as if not being pointed out. The green mountains remain as they were amidst the white clouds.
—The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Lektan Xiang.
Chan Master Hongfu Desheng of Taizhou was a native of Hengyang. He ascended the hall and said:
"If you all come up here in this manner, you fall into seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing. If you go down in this manner, you land in movement, stillness, and activity.
If you neither go nor come, that is precisely the livelihood of a ghost cave. How can you utter a phrase that allows for transcendence? If you can utter it—"

"Then I entrust this staff to you. If you cannot speak it, practice according to it. [The Master] planted the staff upright and descended from the seat. Chan Master Huisu of Wanshou Monastery in Jianning Prefecture ascended the hall.

A monk asked, "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder: does this [staff] also perish? Dasu said, "It perishes. Xiu Shanzhu said, "It does not perish. [The Master said: "Not so. Unprecedented!

It is like a pair of tongs grasping a ball of hot iron; one must let go immediately. If you do not let go, you will surely burn your hands. If you can let go, you will see that the staff is originally the Buddha. If you can say it, then I shall hand it over to you. If you cannot say it, follow it in practice. [The Master] planted the staff upright and descended from the seat.
[The Master] examined closely who was right and who was wrong. The Master said, "One is ruined, one is not ruined; it makes Avalokiteśvara laugh to death.

A lion pounces and bites a person; mad dogs chase after clods of earth. He asked again, "Do you understand? [The other] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "A lacquer bucket that never gets full."
He then descended from his seat. One day, a monk came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "Master, you ought to know where I have come from. The Master said, "A man carrying dung from Hunan; a guest harvesting rice in Jiangxi.
The monk said, "Master, you truly possess the divine eye. The Master struck him three times with his staff and shouted.
He passed away on the first day of the sixth month in the twenty-third year of the Xiangshu era. Having bathed and sat in the lotus posture, he wrote a verse:
"Last night, wind and thunder suddenly arose; The pillar sprouted two fingers. At dawn, the lantern laughed itself to tears;
The staff, as before, was raised up. The whisk leaped across the shifting sands; It snatched back the single sandal of the barbarian monk. Thereupon, he remained in solemn stillness.

[The Master] passed away. Chan Master Daoyuan of Xiangshan in Mingzhou was a native of that prefecture. He ascended the hall and said: "In the wine shops and fish markets, every place is a treasure trove;
the cawing of crows and the chirping of magpies are all wondrous sounds. He struck his staff and asked: "Tell me, what Buddha is this?"
The state of affairs is in great disarray. Entering the hall: Xiangshan has a "head-case" (hua-tou) that pervades the four great divine continents.

If one were to critique it using the standards of the Buddha-dharma, it would be like mistaking a horse for an ox. Since you all do not critique it according to the Buddha-dharma, [how will you deal with it?]
Ultimately, what is this principle? Striking the whisk—this thing without a bolt or lock—is never weary of its movement.
At midnight, one must reach for it with one’s pillow. [The Master] descends from the seat.
The Head Seat Daoqiong of Mukan at Kairan in Jianning Prefecture was a native of Shangrao. The monastic communities honored him as a man of venerable virtue;
Lestan also remarked that he had undergone extensive training. On the day he sat on the teaching seat, he once raised the saying: "With his single shoe, he returned to the West."

He said to the assembly, "To die while seated, to pass away while standing, or to manifest transformation while inverted—these are certainly not impossible. However, there has never yet been one who, having passed away, returned to leave behind their sandals.
Is it that the descendants of later generations do not equal the Patriarch? Or is it that the Patriarch had this one extra trick up his sleeve?
He then laughed heartily and said, "Old wild fox! In the winter of the Gengshen year of the Xiangshi era, the Prefect of Xin invited [the Master] to Chao-hua Temple.
Geyi was the first patriarch to welcome [the transmission] for the sake of Chan. The Master said to the special envoy: "From the beginning, I had no intention of remaining among men;
I wished to be a mountain-dweller solely for the sake of the lineage. However, fearing that many would not be able to go, I have already accepted the invitation.
He then took the portrait of Lestam he had preserved and the two characters "Muguan" (Wooden Hermit), and further wrote a verse to entrust to the elder Qingquan Heng to deliver.
The Dharma-disciple Huishan said, "This fellow with the sharp mouth is no good omen; he loves to stir up disputes within the monastic community.
Hand him over to the Chief Seat of Xuefeng Mountain to give him a thorough scolding—do not let him off. He then addressed the messenger, saying, "Convey my words to the Minister:
my departure is so urgent that I have no time to compose a formal reply. With these words, his voice ceased and he passed away.
Jingchun was a native of Meizhou who received ordination at Huadu Monastery. He went to rely upon Letan;

upon entering the inner room [for instruction], Letan asked, "How much does the iron ox of Shanfu weigh? The Master stepped forward with his hands folded and said, "Now tell me, how much does it weigh?"
Tán said, "The tail is in the north of the Yellow River; the head rests on the south of the Yellow River. Śāriputra has no nostrils, yet he continues to travel south in search of teachers.

As the Master hesitated, Tán struck him, whereupon he attained sudden and thorough enlightenment. Having served as his attendant for many years, he eventually retired to live in seclusion among the forests and ravines.
I once composed a verse, saying: Afraid of the cold, I am too lazy to shave my tangled hair; Loving the warmth, I frequently add more firewood.
My tattered *kāṣāya* robe is draped in disarray; Who could exert such effort to arrange it properly?
Xinzhou Huaiyu Yongxuan, the Head Seat, was the son of Peng from Siming. He became a monk in his youth and proceeded directly to a monastic center.
He attended Litan at Huangbo; one day, returning from Linchuan with his alms bowl, he encountered Litan’s evening discourse, in which it was said:

"A single leaf drifting through the air reveals autumn; the Dharma-body must penetrate the clamor of the marketplace. Upon hearing this, the Master attained realization, and Dan served as his witness.
Later, he relied upon Dahui, who also remarked that he was like himself. For this reason, eminent officials and lords of great monasteries came to welcome and pay him homage, but he did not accept.
He once composed a verse on Dayu’s response to the Buddha’s words, titled "Sawing a Scale-weight," which was modeled after the style of Old Du (Du Fu).
Poem: Red rice, pecked at until it resembles parrot droppings; Green wutong trees, where phoenixes have grown old in their perching.

Chan Master Wuxiang Fazhen of Lushan in Mingzhou was a successor in the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Lan of Guangxiao. He was a descendant of Li Jing, the Prince of Jiangnan. One day, he ascended the hall and said: "Desiring..."

To clarify the matter that transcends [the mundane], one must possess the eye of the crown of the head (*uṣṇīṣa-cakṣus*). If one possesses the eye of the crown of the head, only then does one accord with the mind of renunciation.

Having accorded with the mind of renunciation, one constantly maintains the eye of the crown of the head. Do you wish to understand this eye of the crown of the head? The people of the four capitals wear their robes and eat their meals;
the people of the two Zhe provinces are naturally content and well-fed. At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, the fragrant breeze is pure; the peach blossoms on the coiled tree are in full bloom.
Three or four trees.
The Dharma heir of Chan Master Jingyin Cheng of the fifteenth generation under Nan Yue.
Chan Master Ruyin Rusheng Fendeng of Taizhou ascended the hall and said: "Everyone claims to have mastered Śākyamuni;
each person arrogantly treats Bodhidharma as a mere equal. Yet, when questioned regarding the fundamental principles of our school, they fold their hands and all say, 'He let it pass.
It is true that he let it pass, but what about the woman emerging from samādhi, or Zhaozhou washing his alms bowl? How will you explain these? A crane appeared...
In the ninefold marshes, it is difficult for wings to soar; a horse that cannot travel a thousand *li* vainly pursues the wind.
Wuwei Jun Yefu was the Dharma Master Jishi Daocuan, a son of the Di clan of Kunshan.

Initially serving as an archer-official (*gongji*) in his county, he heard that the Senior Seat-holder (Shouzuo) Qian of Dongzhai was expounding the Dharma for both monastics and laypeople. He went to follow him and practiced seated meditation without weariness.

One day, while serving in an official capacity, he was beaten for negligence. Suddenly, beneath the staff, he attained great enlightenment. He then resigned his post and took refuge with Master Jian (Xiqian).
Jian changed his name to Daochuan (Way-River) and said to him: "In the past you were called Di San (Third of the Di clan); now your name is Daochuan. 'Chuan' (river) is simply 'three' (san).
If you can straighten your backbone and resolutely accomplish this matter, your Way will increase like a river. If you let it fall, however, it will remain as it is."

The former Di was the third [patriarch]. The Master engraved his teachings upon his heart. At the beginning of the Jianyan era, he traveled as a wandering monk with a shaven head and arrived at Tianfeng Pan’an.

Their conversation was like the clashing of sword-points; the hermit praised him highly. Upon returning, he rested in the Eastern Hall, where both monastics and laypeople showed him even greater reverence.

When someone requested an explanation of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, the Master composed a verse for it, which is now widely circulated in the world. In the first year of the Longxing era, the Court Editor...
Zheng Gong Qiaoian was transporting grain to Huaisi when he happened upon Yufu. The seat had been vacant, so they welcomed him to inaugurate the Dharma. He ascended the hall and said:
