"The masses of darkness have been stripped away and the first yang has arisen; the grasses, trees, and groves all sprout anew. Only the bottomless bowl of the patch-robed monk remains as before, filled with rice and again filled with soup.
He ascended the hall again and, citing an example, said: "One day Xuefeng took his place on the seat, held up his staff, and looked to the east, saying:"

Looking toward the east, he said, "The one on the eastern side. Then looking toward the west, he said, "The one on the western side. "Do you all still understand? Throwing down his staff, he said, "Realize it right here!
The Master said: Having looked to the east, he then gazed to the west; With his staff, he speaks again and again of the severity of winter.
A single branch of flowers, rained upon, has fallen away entirely; There is no need for the young gentleman to lean against the balustrade.

Chan Master Dongshan Liangjie Wuben of Ruizhou, whose dharma successor was Chan Master Yunyan Cheng of the fourth generation under Qingyuan,
was the son of the Yu family of Kuaiji. In his early years, he followed a teacher to recite [the scriptures].

While studying the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya Sūtra*, when he reached the passage "no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind," he suddenly touched his face with his hand and asked his teacher, "I possess eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and so forth;
why does the sūtra say they do not exist? His teacher was struck with wonder and marveled at him.
He said, "I am not your teacher. He then pointed [the way] to Mount Wuxie, where he went to pay respects to Chan Master Mo and received the tonsure.

At the age of twenty-one, he went to Mount Song to receive full ordination. On his travels, he first visited Nanquan. It happened that it was the anniversary of Mazu’s passing, and a vegetarian feast was being prepared.
Nanquan asked the assembly, "Tomorrow we shall offer a feast for Mazu; I wonder if Mazu will come? The assembly remained silent and had no reply.
The Master came forward and replied, "I shall come once I have a companion. Nanquan said, "Although this boy is of late birth, he is quite capable of being refined.

The Master said, "Preceptor, do not treat the noble as base. He then visited Muzhou Daowu and asked, "Recently I heard the story of National Teacher Huizhong of Nanyang regarding 'insentient things preaching the Dharma,' yet I have not yet fathomed its subtlety. Muzhou said, "Disciple, do not rely on memory."
"Is it so? the Master asked. Guishan said, "I remember it. Baizhang said, "Try reciting it once for me. The Master then recited it:
A monk asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The National Teacher said, "Brick walls and roof tiles. The monk said, "Are brick walls and roof tiles not insentient?
The National Teacher said, "They are. The monk said, "Can they preach the Dharma? The National Teacher said, "They preach constantly."

[The Master] spoke with fervor and without ceasing. A monk asked, "Why do I not hear it? The National Teacher said, "It is you yourself who do not hear; it cannot be that you are obstructing others from hearing. The monk asked, "I wonder what kind of person is able to hear it? The Master said, "Since you, Reverend, do not hear it, how can you know that the insentient can preach the Dharma? The National Teacher said, "It is fortunate that I do not hear it.
If I were to hear it, I would be equal to the various sages, and you would not hear me preaching the Dharma. The monk said, "If that is so, then sentient beings have no share in it.
The National Teacher said, "I preach for the sake of sentient beings; I do not preach for the sake of the sages. The monk... [continued].
[The Master] asked: "What happens when sentient beings hear this? The National Teacher said: "They are not, in fact, sentient beings. The monk asked:
"As for 'insentient things preaching the Dharma,' on what scriptural authority is this based? The National Teacher said: "It is quite evident that words do not encompass all scriptures;

this is not something spoken by a gentleman. Have you not seen it stated in the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*: 'The lands preach, sentient beings preach, and everything in the three periods of time preaches'? Having finished citing this, the Master [Nanquan] rose.
Dongshan said, "I have it here as well; it is simply that such a person is rarely encountered. The Master said, "I have not yet attained clarity. I beg the Master for instruction.
Dongshan held up his whisk and asked, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. Please, Preceptor, explain it to me.
Dongshan said, "The mouth born of one's parents shall never speak for the sake of a son. The Master said, "Is there anyone else who, at the same time as the Master, yearns for [the Dharma]?"
"Is that so? said the Master. Baizhang replied, "From here, going toward Shiling and Youxian, there are interconnected stone chambers where a man of the Way named Yunyan resides.
If you can part the weeds and catch his wind, he will surely be someone you hold in high esteem. The Master asked, "I do not yet know what kind of person this is."
Dongshan said, "He once asked me, 'When a student wishes to go and serve his teacher, what should he do?
I replied to him, 'You must completely cut off all leaks. He then asked, 'Will this not still be in violation of my teacher's instructions?
I told him, 'Above all, you must not say that I am here. Thereupon, the Master took his leave of Guishan and went directly to Yunyan.
Having concluded the preceding account of causes and conditions, he asked, "Who can hear the Dharma preached by the insentient? Yankong said, "The insentient can hear it.
The Master asked, "Does the Master hear it as well? Yankong said, "If I were to hear it, you would not be hearing my preaching of the Dharma.
The Master asked, "Why is it that I do not hear it? Yankong held up his whisk and asked, "Do you hear it now? The Master—
Xuanze said, "I have not heard it. Guishan Yan said, "If you do not even hear me preach the Dharma, how much less can you hear insentient things preaching the Dharma?

The Master asked, "In which scriptures does this teaching of insentient things preaching the Dharma appear? Guishan Yan replied, "Have you not seen that the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* says: 'The water birds and the forest trees all constantly recite the Buddha’s name and the Dharma'?

At these words, the Master attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "How truly marvelous! How truly wondrous! The Dharma is originally without words; Yet it is spoken by the myriad phenomena."
"How truly marvelous! The insentient preaching the Dharma is inconceivable. If one listens with the ears, it will ultimately be difficult to understand;
only when hearing through the faculty of the eye can one truly know. The Master asked Yunyan, "I still have residual habits that are not yet exhausted.
Yunyan said, "What have you been doing? The Master replied, "I do not even practice the Noble Truths. Yunyan said, "Have you attained joy yet? The Master replied, "Joy..."
Joy is not non-existent; it is like finding a single bright pearl atop a heap of refuse. The Master asked Yunyan, "What is it like when one intends to meet [the Buddha]?
Yunyan said, "Ask the chamberlain. The Master said, "When I have finished asking, what will you say to me? Yunyan said, "I will tell you.
When the Master took his leave of Yunyan, Yunyan asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "Though I am leaving the Master," [he continued,] "..."

[The monk] said, "I have not yet determined where I shall stay. The Master said, "Do not go south to Hunan. [The monk] said, "No. [The Master] said, "Do not return to your hometown. The Master said, "No. [The monk] said, "When will you return?
The Master said, "I shall come when I have a place to stay, Reverend. [The monk] said, "From this point on, we shall be parted forever."
"It is rare to meet," [Fayan] said. The Master replied, "It is rarer not to meet.

As he was about to depart, he asked again, "If, after a hundred years, someone should ask whether you have captured my true likeness, how would you respond? Yankuan remained silent for a long while and then said, "Just this.
The Master hesitated. Yankuan said, "Dharma-heir Jia, as you take up this matter, you must be extremely careful and discerning. The Master still harbored doubts. Later...
While crossing a stream, he saw his reflection and attained great enlightenment regarding the previous teaching. He spoke a verse: "By all means, do not seek it from another;
To do so would distance you from me. Now I go forth alone, And everywhere I encounter him. He is now precisely me, But I am no longer him.
One must understand it thus Before one can realize Suchness. On another day, while making offerings to the portrait of Yunyan...
Next, a monk asked, "The former master said, 'It is just this. Is that not so? The Master said, "It is. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "At that time, I nearly misunderstood the former master's intent. The monk asked, "I wonder whether the former master himself knew it or not?
The Master said, "If he did not know it, how could he have spoken thus? If he did know it, why would he have been willing to speak thus?"

Changqing said, "Since you know it exists, why do you speak thus? He added, "Only by raising a child does one come to know a father’s compassion. While the Master was at Letan, he saw the Head Seat, Chū, who had said, "How marvelous!
How marvelous! The Buddha-realm and the Path-realm are inconceivable! The Master then asked, "I do not ask about the Buddha-realm and the Path-realm;
I simply ask, who is it that speaks of the Buddha-realm and the Path-realm? Chū remained silent for a long while.
He was at a loss for words. The Master said, "Why do you not speak quickly? The first monk replied, "How could one possibly fail to attain it? The Master said, "You have not even spoken yet;
what do you mean by 'how could one possibly fail to attain it'? The first monk was again at a loss for words. The Master said, "Both 'Buddha' and 'the Way' are mere names and phrases.
Why do you not cite the teachings? The first monk asked, "What do the teachings say? The Master said, "When the meaning is grasped, the words are forgotten. The first monk said, "Still..."
The teacher said, "How great is the illness of one who speaks of the Buddha-realm and the Path-realm? At first, there was no response.
The next day, he suddenly passed away; at that time, people called the teacher "The One Who Killed the Head Seat with a Question.
From the end of the Dazhong era of the Tang dynasty, the teacher attracted disciples at Mount Xinfeng. Later, his teachings flourished in Gaoyang, Yuzhang.

At Dongshan, he provisionally opened up the five ranks and skillfully received those of the three capacities; he extensively expounded the single sound and widely propagated it for the myriad classes of beings.
Horizontally drawing his precious sword, he cut through the dense forest of various views; with his wondrous leaves of universal penetration, he severed the myriad ends of forced interpretation.

Furthermore, he attained Cao Shan’s profound clarification of the ultimate meaning and his sublime songs and excellent maxims; the Way accorded with the relationship between ruler and subject, as the partial and the correct interchanged and transformed. By means of this...
This was the profound tradition of Dongshan that spread throughout the world; thus, the masters of all quarters collectively honored it, calling it the Cao-Dong School.
On the anniversary of Yunyan’s death, the Master prepared a vegetarian feast. A monk asked, "What instruction did you receive from Yunyan?
The Master said, "Although I was among him, I received no instruction. The monk asked, "If you received no instruction, then..."

[The monk] asked, "Why do you hold a vegetarian feast? The Master said, "How would I dare go against him? [The monk] asked, "When you first met Nanquan, why did you instead hold a vegetarian feast for Yunyan?
The Master said, "It is not that I do not respect the virtue and the Buddha-dharma of my former teacher."
[The monk] only valued that [the Master] would not explain it for him. He asked, "When you, Master, held a vegetarian feast for your late teacher, did you accept his [teaching] or not?
The Master said, "Half accepted, half not accepted. [The monk] asked, "Why do you not fully accept it?
The Master said, "If I were to fully accept it, I would be failing my late teacher. He asked, "I wish to see the Master’s original teacher; how can I see him? The Master—
[The Master] said, "If the years and the teeth correspond, then there is no obstruction. The monk prepared to offer a reply, but the Master said, "Do not follow in the footsteps of those before;

ask another question instead. The monk was speechless. (Yunju spoke on his behalf: "In that case, you do not see the Master's original teacher. A monk asked Changqing, "What is it for the years and the teeth to correspond?
Changqing said, "The ancients spoke thus; what else are you looking for here, Reverend? Another asked, "When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them? The Master said, "Why [avoid them]?"
He did not go to a place where there was neither cold nor heat. [A monk] asked, "What is the place where there is neither cold nor heat?

The Master said, "In the cold, it freezes you to death, O *śrāmaṇera*; in the heat, it burns you to death, O *śrāmaṇera*. He ascended the hall and said, "Is there anyone who does not repay the four debts of gratitude or the three realms of existence?
The assembly had no response. He spoke again, saying, "If you do not realize this meaning, how can you transcend the afflictions of beginning and end? You must directly..."
When the mind does not touch objects, and at every step there is no fixed location, remaining constantly uninterrupted, only then can one attain resonance with the Way.

You must exert yourself directly; do not let the days pass in idleness. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from wandering the mountains. The Master said, "Have you reached the summit?"
[Daowu] said, “I have arrived. The Master asked, “Is there anyone above your head? He replied, “There is no one. The Master said, “If that is so, then you have not reached the summit.
He said, “If I had not reached the summit, how would I know there is no one? The Master said, “Why do you not stay for a while?
He replied, “I am not unwilling to stay, but those in the Western Heaven would not approve. The Master said, “I have always suspected this fellow. [The Master] then gave [the robe and bowl] to Daowu.
After the Head Seat had finished eating the winter festival fruits, [the Master] asked him: "There is a thing that reaches up to heaven and down to earth;
it is as black as lacquer. It is ever present within the midst of activity, yet it cannot be contained within the midst of activity. Tell me, where does its fault lie?"
Tai said, "The fault lies in the movement and application" (Tongan Xian adds: "He did not know"). The Master called to his attendant to remove the fruit table.
He asked Xuefeng, "Where have you come from? Xuefeng replied, "From Tiantai. The Master said, "Did you see Zhiyi? Xuefeng replied, "If I had seen him, I would have deserved an iron staff.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, "It is very much like the *haiji* horn. [End of] Question.
A snake was swallowing a frog. [A bystander] asked, "Should one save it? Or should one not save it? The Master said, "If you save it, its two eyes will no longer see;
if you do not save it, its form and shadow will not be revealed. There was a monk who was unwell and wished to see the Master. The Master went to him.
The monk said, "Master, why do you not save the sons and daughters of others? The Master said, "Whose sons and daughters are you? The monk replied, "I am..."
Jia was a man and woman from the household of a great icchantika. After the Master had been silent for a long time, the monk asked, "What is it like when the four mountains close in?
The Master said, "I myself have recently passed under the eaves of people's houses. The monk asked, "Do you yield or not? The Master said, "I do not yield.
The monk asked, "Where would you have me go? The Master said, "Into the middle of a field of parched grain."
"Go! The monk let out a single sigh and said, "Take care," whereupon he sat down and passed away. The Master struck his head three times with his staff and said, "You only know how to go like that;
you do not know how to come like this. During a night assembly, the Master did not light the lamps.
A monk came forward to pose a question, then withdrew. The Master ordered an attendant to light the lamp and called out, "The monk who just now asked a question, come forth! The monk...
The monk approached. The Master said, "Bring three or two taels of flour and give it to this venerable elder. The monk brushed his sleeves and withdrew. From that moment on, he attained realization.
He subsequently gave away all his robes and possessions to provide a vegetarian feast. Three years later, he took leave of the Master. The Master said, "Farewell.
At that time, Xuefeng was standing in attendance and asked, "As for this monk who has departed, when will he return?"
The Master said, "He only knows how to go once; he does not understand how to come back. When the monk returned to the hall, he sat down beneath his robes and bowl and passed away.
Xuefeng went up to report this to the Master. The Master said, "Even so, he is still three lifetimes behind me.
Xuefeng went up to pay his respects. The Master said, "Upon entering the gate, there must be words; you cannot say that you have already entered. Xuefeng—
Xuefeng said, "I have no mouth. The Master said, "Even though you have no mouth, that will do for now; give me back my eyes. Xuefeng was speechless.

(Yunju altered the preceding remark to say, "Wait until I have a mouth, then I shall speak. Changqing altered it to say, "In that case, I respectfully withdraw. While Xuefeng was carrying firewood, he dropped a bundle down in front of the Master.
The Master asked, "How much does it weigh? Xuefeng said, "All the people in the great earth cannot lift it. The Master said:
They struggled to reach this point. Feng remained silent. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the pagoda of the Third Patriarch.
The Master said, "Since you have come from the place of the Patriarch, why do you wish to see me, an old monk? The monk said, "The Patriarch is indeed different [from you]."
The student said, "I am no different from the Master. The Master asked, "I wish to see your original teacher; can you bring him forth?
He replied, "That too must wait until the Master himself comes out. The Master said, "Just now, the old monk was away for a moment.
An official asked, "Is there anyone who practices cultivation? The Master said, "Wait until you become a man, and then you shall cultivate."
[The Master] was walking. A monk asked, "When meeting someone, you do not bring it forth; when the intention is raised, one knows immediately. What is it like at such a time?
The Master then pressed his palms together and placed them upon his head. He asked the monk, "What have you come to do? The monk replied, "I have come to be filial toward the Master.

The Master said, "In this world, what thing is most filial? The monk had no reply. He ascended the hall and said: "There is a person among a thousand or ten thousand people who does not turn their back [on others]."
"One person. Not facing one person. You tell me, what kind of face does this person have? Yunju came forward and said, "I am going to attend the hall.
The Master sometimes said, "If you can realize the matter that lies above the Buddha, only then will you have some share in the discourse."
A monk asked, "What is speech? The Master said, "When you speak, you do not hear. The monk asked, "Does the Master hear it?
The Master said, "When you are not speaking, then you hear. The monk asked, "What is the correct question and the correct answer? The Master said:
[The Master] did not speak from his mouth. [A monk] asked, "If someone were to question you, Master, would you still answer? The Master said, "I have never even been questioned.

[The monk] asked, "Why is it that those who enter through the gate are not the treasure? The Master said, "It is best to simply stop there. [The monk] asked, "How many people have approved of the Master appearing in the world?
The Master said, "There is not a single person who has approved. [The monk] asked, "Why is it that there is not a single person who has approved? The Master—
[The Master] said, "Every single one of them has the air of a king. He asked a monk who was lecturing on the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, "It cannot be known by wisdom;
it cannot be recognized by consciousness. What kind of words are these? The monk replied, "They are words praising the Dharmakāya.
The Master said, "To call it the 'Dharmakāya' is already praise. He asked, "One constantly and diligently wipes [the mirror]; why does he not obtain the robe?"
"The almsbowl— I do not know what kind of person is worthy to receive it. The Master said, "One who does not enter the gate.
He asked, "As for one who does not enter the gate, would they still receive it? The Master said, "Even so, I cannot help but give it to him.

Then he added, "Even if one says directly, 'Originally there is not a single thing,' one has still not yet been worthy to receive his robe and bowl. Tell me, what kind of person is worthy to receive them?"
"A turning word should be spoken here. But tell me, what kind of word can be spoken?
At that time, there was a monk who offered ninety-six turning words, none of which accorded with the Master's intent; only the very last one finally satisfied the Master.
The Master said, "Why did you not speak thus earlier, *ācārya*? Another monk had been listening secretly, but he did not hear the final turning word; consequently—
He requested instruction from the monk, but the monk was unwilling to speak. Thus they followed one another for three years, yet the monk never raised the matter for him.
One day, due to illness, the monk said, "For three years you have requested that I raise the previous topic, yet you have not received my compassion. You have failed to grasp it well."
The monk departed with ill intent. He then took up a knife and said, "If you do not provide me with a turning word (*huoju*), I shall kill the Elder and leave.

When Master Qianfeng of Yuezhou ascended the hall, he said: "The Dharma-body has three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of radiance;
you must penetrate each and every one of them before you can understand how to return home and sit securely. You must know that there is yet another 'upper opening' beyond this.
Yunmen stepped forward and asked, "Why does the person inside the hermitage not know what is happening outside the hermitage? The Master laughed heartily. Yunmen said:
This was still a point of doubt for the student. The Master asked, "What kind of mental activity do you have? Yunmen said, "I also wish for the Master to understand me.
The Master said, "You must be like this before you can sit securely. Yunmen responded, "Yes, yes. He ascended the hall and said, "If you mention one, you must not mention two.
To let one thing pass is to fall into the second. Yunmen stepped out from the assembly and said, "Yesterday there was..."
A man came from Tiantai and was heading toward Jingshan. The Master said, "The head cook must not be called for general labor tomorrow," and then descended from his seat.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Tiantai. The Master said, "I hear it has been said that the Stone Bridge has broken into two pieces."
[The monk] asked, “Is it so? He replied, “From where did you, Master, receive this news? The Master said, “I thought you were a guest from the peak of Mount Huading;
it turns out you are just a man from the fields of Pingtian Village. [The monk] asked, “How can one escape the three realms? The Master said, “Call the head of the monastery and drive this monk out!
The Master asked, “When the assembly of monks revolves through the six destinies, what kind of eye do they possess? The assembly [remained silent].
[The Master] was silent. A monk asked, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? The Master said, "I am asking you.

The monk said, "Setting aside your question for a moment, Master," The Master said, "If even my own question is beyond your reach, what need is there to speak of a discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs?
A monk asked, "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions all enter the single path to Nirvana. I wonder where the beginning of this path lies?"

"Where? The Master drew a line with his staff and said, "Right here. (Later, the monk requested further instruction from Yunmen. Yunmen picked up his fan and said, "The fan leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens and strikes the nostrils of Śakra.
A sea bass from the Eastern Ocean receives a blow of the staff, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin. Do you understand?")
A monk asked the Master of Heoshan in Jizhou, "I, a student, wish to pose a question; will you, Master, answer me?
The Master said, "Heoshan has already answered you. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "Heoshan’s great summit. [The monk] asked again.
"What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Green mountains fill the eyes as white clouds arise.
He asked, "If a guest should arrive, how would you receive them? The Master said, "A full platter of flavorless *amṛta* fruit.
He asked, "In which land does the Silent Child dwell? The Master said, "The wooden horse neighs in the wind before the hall."
Chan Master Xianqi of Tiantong in Mingzhou asked Fulong, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from Fulong. The Master said, "Have you been able to subdue the dragon?
He replied, "I have never subdued this beast. The Master said, "Sit for a while and drink some tea.
Dade Jian asked, "The student has come here with great resolve; I ask the Master for his direct instruction. The Master said, "In my place, one simply defecates and then—"

[Zhao] said, "It is finished. What is there that stands out so prominently? The Master said, "If you answer questions in such a manner as this, it would be better for you to buy more sandals and travel on foot.
Jian stepped forward. The Master said, "Come closer. Jian approached. The Master said, "As for my answering you in this way, where does the fault lie?
Jian had no reply. The Master then struck him. He asked, "What is the state of 'originally having nothing'? The Master said: [The text here ends abruptly].
When stones are moist, they naturally contain jade; when ore is exceptional, it spontaneously produces gold. A question was asked: "What is the flow of true permanence?
The Master said: "Not even a single drop shifts."
A monk asked the Master of Bao’ai Mountain in Tanzhou, “In this single, leakless dwelling, what kind of person ought to reside?
The Master said, “One who is nameless and not attached to the physical body. The monk asked, “Is there still a rank or position? The Master said, “None. The monk asked, “What is Bao’ai?
The Master said, “It is not obtained from humans or devas. The monk asked, “Who is the one within Bao’ai? The Master said, “None.”
He spoke with those of his time, saying: "When the Buddha comes, what then? The Master said: "One cannot find another path. A question was asked:
"When the world is destroyed, where does this thing go? The Master said: "Even the thousand sages cannot find it. [The questioner] said: "How should people of the present age turn toward it?
The Master said: "You must simply be like him. [The questioner] said: "Is there still something that accords with it? The Master said: "No signposts are established."
Then he asked: "How does one who does not dwell in a fixed position practice? The Master said: "A fine horse neighs amidst a mass of red flames.
Chan Master Wensui of Qishan in Lizhou was a native of Fuzhou. In his youth, he relied upon Huairang of Mount Daci in Hangzhou.

Chan Master Zhong received his training under Deshan. At that time, Yantou and Xuefeng were among the assembly; upon hearing the Master’s discourse, they recognized him as a vessel for the Dharma and led him together on a journey to travel the land.
Although each of these two great masters had received the seal of transmission from Deshan, the Master remained stubbornly stuck despite their repeated exhortations.
One day, he asked Deshan, "Tianhuang spoke thus, and Longtan also spoke thus..."
"Way. [The student] asked, "I do not yet understand; how would you say it, Preceptor? Deshan said, "Try to cite what the Emperor’s Son (Tianhuang) and Longtan said.
As the student was about to offer a word, Deshan struck him. After being struck, the student returned to the Yanshou Hall and said, "It is so, it is so;
but he struck me too severely! Yantou said, "If you speak like that, you will not be able to say later on that you saw Deshan. (Fayan)
Another account says: "This is indeed a mistake; he struck me. Later, he attained realization under Dongshan and became his successor. He was twenty-seven years old [at that time].
He stayed at Mount Qin and, before the great assembly, reflected upon his own faults. He recounted the occasion when he was attending on Dongshan.
Dongshan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from Daci. Dongshan asked, "Did you see Daci? The Master said, "I saw him.

Dongshan asked, "Did you see him before his form or after his form? The Master said, "I saw him neither before nor after his form. Dongshan remained silent. The Master then said, "To leave the teacher..."
"Too early. "He did not fulfill his teacher’s intent" (Fayan said: "He did not fulfill his teacher’s intent; it is not easy to inherit from him").
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The ruler's square-foot measure; Master Zhi’s scissors.
The monk asked, "All Buddhas and all Buddha-dharmas emerge from this sutra. What is this sutra? The Master said, "It is constantly turning. [The monk] said, "I do not yet understand the sutra."
"What is being discussed in the middle? The Master said, "If you have a doubt, ask. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?

The Master said, "Brocade and embroidery, a silver incense pouch; the wind blows its fragrance along the road. When Yantou heard this, he sent a monk to say, "Deliver these words to the 'Eighteenth Son':
'Serve Master Pan well. Another monk drew a portrait of the Master and presented it to him. The Master said, "Does it resemble me or not?"
The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "Let the assembly take a look. A servant of Deshan came to visit;
as soon as he prostrated himself, the Master seized him and said, "Do you truly accept it as Qian-shan did? The servant said, "I regret that I stayed so long at De-shan;
today I have no words with which to respond. The Master then let go of him and said, "Respond as you please. The servant pushed him away.
Xiong said, "Please allow me to offer you a bit of 'passing the breath' (a spiritual greeting).
The Master said, "That might be acceptable at Deshan’s gate, but here it is of no use whatsoever. Xiong said, "I have long heard that Qingshan is devoid of human feeling.
The Master said, "Do not trouble Deshan’s reputation; go to the meditation hall. While the Master was sitting with Yantou and Xuefeng, Dongshan came by serving tea. The Master then—

[The Master] closed his eyes. Dong said, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have just emerged from meditative concentration. Dong said, "Concentration has no gate; through what have you entered?
The Master went into the bathhouse and saw a monk treading a water wheel. As the monk came down to pay his respects, the Master said, "Fortunately, it is already turning round and round;
why must you do this? The monk said, "If I did not do this, how could it turn? The Master said, "If it were not for this..."
[The monk] said, "What can Qianshan’s eye do? [The Master] asked, "What is the Master’s eye? The Master made a gesture with his hand as if brushing his eyebrows.
[The monk] said, "How could you, Reverend, act in such a way? The Master said, "It is I who acts in this way; you, however, do not. The monk had no reply.
The Master said, "Seeking battle but failing to achieve merit—what a state of frustration! After a long silence, he asked, "Do you understand?"
Mo said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Qinshan shall carry half of it for you. The Master, along with Yantou and Xuefeng, traveled across the Jiangxi region.
Upon arriving at a tea shop and while they were drinking tea, the Master said, "Those who cannot turn their bodies and pass through the air shall not be allowed to drink this tea.
Yantou said, "If that is the case, I certainly shall not get to drink the tea. Xuefeng said, "I am the same."
The Master said, "These two old fellows do not even recognize the head-word. Tou asked, "Where have they gone?
The Master said, "An old crow in a cloth bag—though alive, it is as if dead. Tou stepped back and said, "Look! Look! The Master said, "Let us set aside Master Huo for a moment;
what about Master Cun? Feng drew a circle with his hand. The Master said, "I cannot help but ask. Tou [responded].
Hehe said, "It is too far away. The Master said, "There are many who have mouths but cannot drink tea. The Zen guest Jiliang came to visit.
After prostrating, he asked, "What is it like when a single arrowhead pierces through the three barriers? The Master said, "Let out the master of the barrier and see.
Jiliang said, "In that case, one must surely correct their faults. The Master said, "When do you wait for anything else? Jiliang said, "Excellent."
A single arrow. Unable to find a place to release it, Liang went out. The Master said, "Come here for a moment, Ācārya. Liang turned his head back.
The Master stepped down from the meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Setting aside for a moment the 'one shaft piercing the three barriers,' try to let an arrow fly for Qinshan and see!
Liang hesitated. The Master struck him seven blows and said, "Let this fellow of confused principles go on doubting for thirty years! There he was.
The monk brought this up to Tong’an Cha. An said, “Although Master Liang knows how to release the arrow, he has yet to hit the mark.
The monk then asked, “I wonder, how can one hit the mark? An replied, “Who is the Lord of Guanzhong? The monk returned and related this to the Master (Zhaozhou).
The Master said, “If Master Liang had understood it in this way, he would have spared Qinshan his mouth. Nevertheless...”
Thus it is. Tong’an was not being kind-hearted; you must examine this for yourself before you can understand. A monk came to inquire of the Master.
The Master held up his fist and said, "When opened, it becomes a palm, with the five fingers distinct from one another. Now, as a fist, there is certainly no hierarchy of high or low.
Tell me, does Qingshan still allow for discussion? The monk stepped forward and, in turn, held up his fist. The Master said, "Your doing so is merely..."
A man who neither opens nor closes said, "I do not yet understand how you, Master, receive people. The Master said, "If I were to receive people, I would be just like you.
He said, "I have come specifically to study with the Master; you must at least reveal some message. The Master said:
"If you come specifically for this purpose, I must reveal it to you. The monk said, "I request you to do so. The Master struck him. The monk was speechless.

The Master said, "To sit and wait by the stump for a rabbit is to waste one's mental energy. He ascended the hall, held his staff horizontally across his chest, looked at the assembly, and said, "Is there anyone?
Is there anyone? If not, then Qinshan shall sing the *Pusa-man* (Bodhisattva-mani)! He then shouted, "Luo-lo li-li! and immediately descended from the seat. The Master [concluded].
He debated the meaning of the Dharma with a Daoist. The Daoist established his thesis, saying, "Both coarse words and subtle speech all return to the primary truth.
The Master said, "The Daoist is a slave to the Buddha's house. The Daoist said, "That is too crude, sir. The Master asked, "Where, then, is the primary truth?
The Daoist was speechless.

Regarding "sameness and difference," the Master said: "Fine and coarse fabrics do not ward off the cold.
This refers to Chan Master Caoshan Ji, the sixth-generation successor under Qingyuan. His Dharma heirs include:
Chan Master Daoyan of Dongshan in Ruizhou once took up a statement left by Caoshan, which said: "There is a person who, from the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, leaps straight down.
What kind of person is this? No one in the assembly could respond. The Master stepped forward and said, "He does not remain. Caoshan asked, "What is it that he does not remain?
The Master replied, "Only then can he avoid being smashed to pieces upon impact. Caoshan deeply approved of him. Later, there was a monk...
Question: "I request that you, Preceptor, secretly transmit the true mind. The Master said, "Why do you try to deceive me when there is no one here?
A monk asked Chan Master Congzhi Xuanming of Jinfeng in Fuzhou, "What is the true master of Jinfeng?
The Master said, "The town is not far from here; do not act so hastily, lay brother. The monk asked, "Why do you not speak of it? The Master said, "The mouth..."
[The Master] was like a foundation stone. A monk asked, "Among a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks, which one is Jinguang Peak? The Master then scratched his forehead.
Another monk asked, "When the thousand mountains are cloudless and ten thousand miles are free of rosy clouds, what then? The Master said, "Why do you not spit it out over there at Feiyuan Ridge?"
Question: "What is the meaning of coming from the West? The Master said: "There is a rat by the wall. Question: "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said:
"Before the gate of Jinfeng, there is no five-li milestone. A newly arrived monk came to pay his respects. The Master said: "No need for seasonal greetings;
speak the First Phrase. The monk said: "It is still cold in the early spring; we humbly hope the Master is well. The Master said: "Still..."
"It is here," [the monk] said. [The Master] said, "One must not allow others to inspect it. The Master asked, "Who? The monk pointed to himself.
The Master said, "It is no hindrance to being inspected by others. Picking up his pillow, he showed it to the monk and said, "Everyone calls this a pillow;
Jinfeng says it is not. The monk asked, "I wonder, what do you, the Master, call it? The Master picked it up.
"A pillow. The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall act accordingly. The Master asked, "What do you call it? The monk said, "A pillow.
The Master said, "It has fallen into the nest of Jinfeng. [Another] asked, "When the golden cup is filled to the brim, what then? The Master said:
Jinpeng was so intoxicated that he could not bear it. While a monk was sweeping the floor, the Master asked, "What are you doing?
The monk held up his broom. The Master said, "There is still this thing remaining. The monk asked, "What did you see just now, Master? The Master held up his staff. A monk came for an audience;
as soon as he entered the abbot’s quarters, the Master struck him. The monk said, "It is so, it is so. The Master struck him again. The monk said, "No."
"Yes. "No. The Master made a gesture of bowing; the monk made a gesture of striking. The Master said, "This old monk’s eyes are dim; you, *ācārya*, have deaf ears.

[The monk] said, "To feed fish with rice, one must still discipline oneself. The Master said, "By giving food, one receives the retribution of long life. [The monk] said: *Note: This dialogue is from the *Wumen Guan* (The Gateless Barrier), Case 49.*
“How many years old are you, Master? The Master said, “I do not fall within the range of numbers. “Who is it that possesses long life? The Master said, “Jinpeng.
“You truly have dimmed eyes,” [the monk] said. “It is so, it is so,” the Master replied. He asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk stepped forward.

After a long silence, the Master said, “Whom have you studied under, Lay Brother? “Studying what bowl? the monk replied. “Jinpeng has committed an offense,” the Master said. “Indeed,” the monk replied.
"Yes. Yes. After a long silence, the Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Eastern Land. The Master said, "How did you pass through the Golden Peak Barrier?
The monk said, "My credentials are clear. The Master said, "Try presenting them to Golden Peak for inspection. The monk spread his two hands wide.
The Master said, "No one has ever passed through the Golden Peak Barrier. The monk asked, "Can you, Master, pass through it?"
The Master said, "A Persian eats black pepper. He asked a monk, "What is your surname? The monk replied, "My surname is He.
The Master said, "In the end, you have not escaped the mundane. The monk said, "It is because of you that I have attained this. The Master said, "If it is so, then the fault lies with Jingu Peak.

The monk said, "I dare not [claim otherwise]. The Master said, "Truly, Jingu Peak has committed a fault. As the monk was bowing in greeting, the Master seized him and said, "Do not ever speak of this to others."
"Way! I have a kōan (nidāna) to present to you. The monk made a gesture of listening. The Master gave him a slap.
The monk said, "Why did you strike me? The Master said, "I want this story to circulate. While they were reading the scriptures, Biandao came in.
The Master held up a scripture and made a gesture as if grasping his robe, looking at him with his eyes. Bian raised both hands holding his sitting mat and looked at the Master.
The Master said, "Everyone in the human realm says you understand Chan. Bian asked, "How about you, Preceptor? The Master smiled and said:
The bandits were utterly defeated. [A monk] asked, "This body is without consciousness, like earth, wood, tiles, or stones; what is the meaning of this?
The Master descended from his meditation seat, grabbed the monk by the ear, and as the monk cried out in pain, the Master said, "Today, for the first time, I have caught this ignorant fellow.
The monk bowed and departed. The Master called out, "Acarya! The monk turned his head, and the Master said, "When you reach the hall..."
"It cannot be brought up," [the Master] said. A monk asked, "For what reason? The Master replied, "There are many who would laugh at Jingu Peak’s grandmotherly heart.
He ascended the hall and said, "Twenty years ago, this old monk had a grandmotherly heart; twenty years later, I have no grandmotherly heart. A monk asked:
"What is it like to possess the 'old woman's heart' twenty years ago? The Master said, "When asked about the ordinary, I answer with the ordinary; when asked about the holy, I answer with the holy.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like to be without the 'old woman's heart' twenty years later? The Master said, "When asked about the ordinary, I do not answer with the ordinary."
The questioner asked, but the Sage did not answer. When the Master saw the monk approaching, he raised his hand and said, "This is a matter for a person of great capacity.

Try to deliver a message for me. The monk replied, "I do not wish to deceive you, Reverend. The Master said, "Even those who know how to practice filial piety and support their parents are rare indeed.
The monk asked, "Is this not a matter for a person of great capacity? The Master said, "I, an old monk, would be deceiving you, O Kalyāṇamitra."
Lei said, "At this point, it is not easy to discern the truth. The Master said, "Truly so, truly so. The monk bowed.
The Master asked, "From where do you set out? He replied, "Just from right here. The Master said, "Not only do you deceive yourself, but you also deceive me. [He then] ascended the hall.
"If I bring it up," he thought, "I fear I will encounter malicious gossip; if I do not bring it up, I will again be met with laughter and derision.

[The monk] understood. [The Master] asked, "If it does not fall within the mechanism of the teaching, please speak directly. The Master said, "The profound moon and swift response are beyond compare. How many masters have you questioned thus far?
He replied, "I am questioning the Master right now. The Master said, "Good brother! When the clouds part, there is no need to hide the nine-tailed fox.
I grant you the remainder of your life; return quickly to your mountain retreat. Because the barbarians were in rebellion, the Master subsequently departed from Jia.
When [Dongshan] arrived at Xiangzhou, he founded Shimen Temple and once again revitalized the profound tradition. He ascended the hall and said:

"The brilliance upon the lapis lazuli palace shines daily without partiality; it blazes within the mountains of the seven jewels, with every point having its own foundation. The mud ox sets forth its steps."
The wooden horse neighs; the village elders sing and chant; the woodcutters wave their sleeves. Upon the road of the great sun, there are ancient melodies and profound sounds.
Meeting beneath the trees—what more is there to do? A monk asked, "What is it like when the moon rises above the clouds?
The Master said, "Three children embrace a flower drum. Good brother, do not come to block my path to the ball court. He asked, "What is it?"
Regarding the "house style" of the Master, the Teacher said: "He always rides a fine steed up the high tower; with his iron whip, he points out the way for all the Hu people.
[The monk] asked: "What is the realm of Shimen? The Teacher said: "Throughout the entire world, there is no color other than gold; the wandering travelers have ceased their pursuit.
[The monk] asked: "Who is the person within the realm? The Teacher said: "Formless, they do not dwell in the ranks of either ordinary beings or sages. (From the *Jingde Chuandeng Lu*)

Walking the path of birds, they leave no trace. A question was asked: "When a fierce tiger stands before one's door, what then? The Master said, "Life and nature do not exist. [The questioner] said, "In that case, you have met his deadly paw. The Master said, "Feel free to bite and chew. Question: "What is it to be among those in the Pure Land? The Master said, "Clad in fur, they roam amidst the gathering fires; wearing horns, they mingle with the dust and mud. Question: "The realm of the Way has no boundless limit. The Master said, "The Great Way is like empty space; how could there be a limit? The questioner said, "If so, then all dharmas are the Great Way. The Master said, "If you see all dharmas as the Great Way, then you are still seeing them as dharmas. If you see the Great Way as the Great Way, then you are still seeing it as the Great Way. If you can transcend both dharma and non-dharma, only then will you understand the meaning of 'the Great Way has no boundless limit. The questioner said, "How does one transcend both dharma and non-dharma? The Master said, "If you can see the Great Way as neither dharma nor non-dharma, only then will you transcend both dharma and non-dharma. The questioner said, "If one transcends both dharma and non-dharma, what is the Great Way? The Master said, "The Great Way is not something that can be grasped by the mind or known through consciousness. It is simply the Great Way. The questioner said, "If the Great Way is not something that can be grasped by the mind or known through consciousness, then who is it that attains it? The Master said, "If you can attain it without using the mind or consciousness, only then will you know the meaning of 'attaining the Great Way. The questioner said, "If one attains the Great Way without using the mind or consciousness, then what is the function of the Great Way? The Master said, "The function of the Great Way is such that it cannot be described as having a function. "How is it when the entire body is free from a single trace? The Master said: "Vast white clouds spread over the snowy peaks;
turn back upon the dark path without delay. He asked: "I do not yet know where the path for turning back lies. The Master said: "The stone man raises his hand—take note clearly;
look at the withered bones of ten thousand years as they laugh. He asked: "How is it when there is no movement in suchness? The Master said:
"What end will there ever be? [The monk] asked. "How is it so? the Master replied. "The stone door has no lock; the Prajñā Temple was consumed by fire.
Someone asked, "Since it is Prajñā, why was it burned by fire? The Master said, "A single line of iron across ten thousand miles.
The Master often responded to situations by saying, "Good brother," and was thus known at the time as Brother Monk (Dage Heshang).
A monk asked Chan Master Longguang Yin of Shaoshan, "When the Human King and the Dharma King meet, what is it like?
The Master said, "The King of Yue once brandished his sword; a single phrase from Longguang has never been deficient. He then ascended the hall, and after a long silence, said:
"No need for further formalities. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of the West's coming? The Master said, "When the wind of the Hu blows, the Han land establishes its rules.
[The student] asked, "When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then? The Master clapped his hands and looked around. [The student] asked, "What is the single phrase of Longguang?
The Master said, "Amoghapāśa" (The Unfailing Lasso). [The student] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Oṃ. [The student] asked, "What is..."
"The ultimate point is the state of being human. The Master said, "I earnestly entrust this to those who come after.

A questioner asked, "Why does one body of Piṇḍola attend offerings in the four continents? The Master said, "A single moon reflects in a thousand rivers; ten thousand households all encounter spring."
Thereupon, a verse was spoken: Upon the summit of Dragon Flower Mountain, the precious lunar disc Shines upon heaven and earth, piercing through the dark clouds.
The Venerable One does not shift from his original singular substance; A thousand homes reflect his image, ten thousand homes bask in spring.
A monk asked Master Bājiāo of Yingzhou, "How should one apply the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day?
The Master said, "Gathering it all up in a single wooden basin. The monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Sometimes three across; sometimes five vertically.
The monk asked, "What is one who walks upon the Way? The Master said, "Ceasing to raise the cloud-messenger’s letter; at midnight, the great sun shines."
A monk asked Chan Master Huiju of Shizang in Dingzhou, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The trees bear the color of the Canglang River;
the mountains stretch across as a single stroke of green. The monk asked, "What is the monastery? The Master said, "It is just this. The monk said, "..."
"What is it like to be among those within the monastery? The Master said, "What? What? [The monk] asked, "If a guest should suddenly arrive, with what will you receive them?
The Master said, "Go drink tea."

Chan Master Zhongyun Zhihui of Jingzhao Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Baishui Ren. Born into the Gao family of Xianqin, he was fond of visiting Buddhist temples from the age of seven.
He vowed to leave the household life, a resolve his parents could not dissuade him from fulfilling. After receiving the tonsure under Chan Master Wen of Guifeng, he...
He visited Baishui Temple alone, grasping its subtle teachings and penetrating its secret keys. Seeking out a site, he settled at Zhongtan and founded the Wenshi Monastery.
He constantly engaged in the practice of distributing water and dispensing medicine. There was a bhikṣu suffering from white leprosy whom the community loathed;

only the Master treated him with constant care, washing and rubbing him as usual. Suddenly, there appeared divine light and extraordinary fragrance. When the others marveled at this, the bhikṣu had already vanished.
The dried scabs from his sores emitted an intense and pungent fragrance; they were subsequently gathered together and used to fashion a statue of Avalokiteśvara for their enshrinement.
Later, the Master suddenly wished to return to his former residence at Mount Gui on Zhongnan Mountain. One day, while strolling idly among the crags and ravines, he lay down to rest as usual.

Suddenly, he beheld his patchwork robe (*kāṣāya*), prayer beads, copper water flask, and *zōng* hat—all of which crumbled to pieces upon being touched. He said to his attendant, "These were my former..."
He took his own body as the materials for the construction and established a temple there to repay his past causes.

While he was clearing away the weeds, auspicious clouds obscured the sun, gathering atop the peak and remaining there without dispersing for a long time; thus, it was named Mount Chóngyún (Heavy Clouds).

Fierce beasts all withdrew of their own accord, and when he filled in the dragon pool to clear a path, the dragon also moved elsewhere. Later, Emperor Míngzōng of the Later Táng dynasty bestowed upon it the plaque name "Cháng" (Long).
[The Master] was flourishing. Disciples gathered from all quarters. He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is it to return to the root and attain the essential meaning?

The Master said, "Already forgotten; one does not even recall the arising of dust. The monk asked, "What is it to follow illumination and lose the source? The Master said, "A home has been ransacked by thieves."
Question: "Dust does not arise from recollection; what is the single path for advancing the person? The Master said: "Grass has already grown beneath your feet;
ahead lies a pit ten thousand fathoms deep. Question: "The main road is level and smooth; how does one tread upon it? The Master said:

"If I were to point it out to you, you would go off toward the east, west, south, or north. Question: "What is the 'Scale of the Heavy Clouds'? The Master said: "Subject it to the examination of the whole world as you please."
Question: What are words that cut through iron? The Master said: "Better to die than to transgress. Question:
What is the matter that Kāśyapa heard directly? The Master said: "Heavy clouds cannot be recorded. Question: What is the realm of Heavy Clouds? The Master said: [Silence].
In the four seasons, flowers cluster thickly; throughout the three winters, the exotic grasses remain green. The Master propagated the Dharma for over forty years.

When he was a commoner, the Military Commissioner Wang Yanchao had often accompanied the Master on excursions and wished to become a śramaṇa. The Master gazed at him intently and said, "Your worldly karmic ties are deep;
you shall serve as the boundary wall for my house. Later, Lord Wang indeed governed Yongxing and offered him the rites of a disciple. The Master was about to—

Following worldly custom, he first took his leave of the prince and entrusted him with the protection of the Dharma-gate. The prince wept and said, "Master, can you truly bear to abandon your disciple?
The Master smiled and said, "Even if one were to borrow a thousand years, this would be but a single parting. Upon returning, he wrote a verse for the assembly, saying:
"I have a small cottage, Built for me by my parents. I have lived within it for eighty years, And lately I have perceived its decay. He passed away early.
He intended to move elsewhere, as the matter involved matters of attachment and aversion; he waited until the [current] site was demolished so that there would be no obstruction for either party.
He then passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture, and his stupa was erected at his original mountain.
Chan Master Youzhang of Ruilong Monastery in Hangzhou was the nephew of the Tang Prime Minister Xiahou Zhi.

At the beginning of the Dazhong era, when his uncle, the Grand Master of Works (Sikong), was stationed as governor in Guangling, the Master was seven years old. While visiting Huizhao Temple, he heard the *Lotus Sūtra* being recited and resolved to leave the household life.
His uncle initially did not grant permission, but because the Master ceased eating and drinking, his uncle had no choice but to comply.
He granted his request. Master Huìyuǎn then traveled to various Chan assemblies; at Shùshān and Báishuǐ, he received the heart-instructions from all of them.
In the thirteenth year of the Xiántōng era, he arrived in Jīnglíng. The Venerable Téngtēng instructed him, saying:
"Go to Tiantái to seek a place of stillness to dwell; when you meet Ān, stop there. Later, he encountered the Venerable Hánhánhé who patted him and recorded: "You..."
"Forty years hence, there will be a Bodhisattva beneath Mount Jingshan who shall rule over Jiangnan; at that time, my Way shall flourish.
Subsequently, he arrived at Mount Tiantai and founded Fudang Monastery in Jing’an Township, thereby realizing the words of "leisurely wandering.
He later resided at Yilong Monastery. In the fourth year of the Zhonghe era, when famine and pestilence ravaged Zhejiang East, the Master [was in] Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Mingzhou...

The three prefectures collected and buried his remains; at that time, he was called the Great Being of Profound Sorrow (Beizeng Dashi). Xuefeng once went to visit him and departed leaving behind his *tāla*-leaf whisk.
In the third year of the Tiānyòu era, Qián Shàngfù dispatched the envoy Tóng Jiàn with clothing, incense, and medicinal herbs to enter the mountains and extend an invitation.
Upon arriving at the provincial court, he was appointed as the Grand Master Zhìdé and lodged in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers, where [the Governor] attended upon him daily.

He requested instruction on the Dharma. The Master requested that a *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* (Golden Light) ritual site be established annually at Mount Tiantai, with a great assembly of both clergy and laity from all prefectures, dispersing after more than a month (the Golden Light Assembly began with this Master). As he was about to take his leave to return to the mountains, the King felt deep affection and longing;

consequently, he established Rui Long Monastery within the capital city (later renamed Bao Shan Monastery by Emperor Wenmu) and invited the Master to propagate the Dharma there. At that time, the Chan school was flourishing; such was the case.
"Hanhan’s prediction has indeed come to pass. He ascended the hall and said: "In recent years, this old monk traveled beyond the Yangtze River, through Lingnan, Jing, and Hu.
There was no community of learned masters where I did not go to inquire and seek instruction. This was solely for the purpose of gathering with you all today."
Each must know this destination. Yet, throughout all quarters, there is ultimately no divergent teaching; it simply instructs the person to let the frantic mind rest and cease seeking from others.
Simply follow the direction and allow the reality to be as it is—yet there is no reality to be allowed. Use it according to the occasion—yet there is no occasion to be used.
Even if compassion is shown through bitter words, one cannot call day night; even with further skillful means, it remains so.
In the end, one cannot point to the east and call it the west. Should one happen to be able to do so, that would merely be a supernatural feat performed as a curiosity;

it would have nothing to do with my concern. As for those who merely parrot words, who fail to reflect upon themselves and recognize their error, they are simply attempting to pluck flowers from the sky.
"Can you take the moon from the waves and bring it back to restore your own mind-power? You should each now withdraw and reflect for a moment.
Only when you suddenly agree to let go will you realize that this old man of Rui Long had no choice but to be so excessively circuitous. Do you agree now?
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Rui Long? The Master said, "Do you not see it? The monk asked, "What is the realm?"

A man of mediocre capacity asked, "The Master is truly formidable. He asked again, "When it is vast and empty with no clouds, what is the mid-autumn moon? The Master said, "The best is when there are no clouds. The man said, "In that case, the single orb hangs high, and the myriad nations behold it together. The Master said, "That too is not so. The man asked, "What about when the moon is obscured by clouds? The Master said, "It is even better than when there are no clouds. The man said, "If that is so, then the single orb hangs high and the myriad nations behold it together. The Master said, "This too is not so. The man asked, "What about when the moon is half-full? The Master said, "Even this is not so. The man asked, "What about when the moon is full? The Master said, "Even this is not so. The man asked, "What about when the moon is new? The Master said, "Even this is not so. The man said, "If all these are not so, then what is the mid-autumn moon? The Master said, "The mid-autumn moon is the mid-autumn moon. The man said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Do you understand? Do you understand? The man said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand, then listen: When the sky is vast and empty with no clouds, the mid-autumn moon is the mid-autumn moon. When the moon is obscured by clouds, the mid-autumn moon is the mid-autumn moon. When the moon is half-full, the mid-autumn moon is the mid-autumn moon. When the moon is full, the mid-autumn moon is the mid-autumn moon. When the moon is new, the mid-autumn moon is the mid-autumn moon. Even when the moon is not visible, the mid-autumn moon is the mid-autumn moon. It is simply the mid-autumn moon; it is not something else. Why do you seek elsewhere?
