The Master said, "It is difficult to speak with one who has eyes pressed shut. In the fourth month of the second year of the Tiānchéng era (the Dinghai year), he requested from the Shangfu (the Grand Marshal) a site for his burial mound and stupa.
The Shangfu ordered Lu Rénzhāng to select an auspicious location at Xiguān to construct a stupa and establish a monastery, renaming the Tiantái Yǐnlóng (Hidden Dragon) as Yǐnjì (Traces Hidden).
Once the stupa was completed, the Master entered the official residence to take leave of the Shangfu, entrusting him with the protection of the Dharma. He departed...

When the time for his peaceful passing arrived, the Senior Guardian (Shangfu) was filled with grief and sorrow. He dispatched the Chief of Monks (Sengzheng) to assemble the virtuous elders residing within the city to escort the remains into the stupa.
A monk asked Chan Master Ruguan of Mount Qingcuo in Xingyuan Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Baima Ruzhi: "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said:
[The Master] said: "A bottomless basket gathers raw vegetables. [The student] asked: "What is the realm of green chopping? The Master said: "In the three winters, the flowering trees flourish;
in the nine summers, snow and frost fly."
Chan Master Kuanghua Zangyu of Baoci in Tanzhou, a successor of Chan Master Longya Dun, was asked by a monk: "When the eye and mind see each other, what is it like?
The Master said: "What would I say to you? The monk asked: "What is the place of true seeing? The Master said: "Not separated by even a hair’s breadth. The monk said: "..."
"If it is so, then one sees. The Master said, "Nanquan had a very fine place to go. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Transmission?
The Master said, "Last night at the third watch, [the meaning] was sent across the river. [The monk] asked, "How is it when one employs [the Way] spontaneously upon encountering the situation?

The Master said, "At the top of the fruit tree in the land of海东 (Haidong), there is a heart. [The monk] asked, "What is true suchness and Buddha-nature? The Master said, "Who does not have it? [The monk] asked.
“What is the upward path? The Master said, “Chenlian Dao Yong. A monk asked, “How old are you, Master?
The Master said, “In autumn the yellow leaves fall; when spring arrives, the flowers bloom. He asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk replied, “From Wolong.”
The Master asked, "How long have you been there? He replied, "I have spent the winter and passed the summer. The Master said, "The Dragon Gate has no guests who stay overnight.
Why have you remained there for so long? He replied, "In a lion’s den, there are no other beasts. The Master said, "Try to let out a lion’s roar.
He replied, "If I were to let out a lion’s roar, there would be no more Master. The Master said, "I take pity on you."
[The Master] said, "Newcomer! I grant you thirty blows. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Hunan? The Master said, "Sloops and warships.
The monk asked, "May a student be permitted to tour and enjoy it? The Master said, "It is entirely up to you, Reverend, to go about as you please.

A monk asked, "After the Master has passed away for a hundred years, if someone asks how one should respond, what will you say? The Master said, "Remember it clearly. A monk asked, "When emotion arises, wisdom..."
"Separated. [The monk said: "When thought has not yet arisen, the substance is different. But when emotion has not yet arisen, how is it? The Master said: "Separated. [The monk] asked:
"When emotion has not yet arisen, what is it that is separated? The Master said: "This lad has not yet met anyone [who can help him].
[The monk] asked: "What is Longya Mountain? The Master said: "Over there in Yiyang. [The monk] asked: "How is it so? The Master said: "Without preconception. [The monk] asked: "If..."
"What is it not to intend to go? The Master said, "If that is so, then it is not. A monk asked, "What was the meaning of the ancients facing the wall?
The Master remained silent for a long while and then called to the monk. The monk responded, "Yes? The Master said, "Go; come back another time.

He ascended the hall and said: "One phrase pervades the entire earth; one phrase is spoken as soon as the question is asked; one phrase is not spoken even when questioned. A monk asked, "How is this?"
"This is the phrase that pervades the great earth. The Master said, "There is no lack of anything. [The student] asked, "What is the phrase 'as soon as you ask, I speak'?
The Master said, "Lower your voice. Lower your voice. [The student] asked, "What is the phrase 'even when asked, I do not speak'? The Master said, "One should simply know the proper time."
A monk asked Zen Master Shen Zhe of Mount Hanzhu in Xiangzhou, "What is the Master’s profound depth?
The Master said, "As soon as a single inch-nail enters the wood, nine oxen cannot pull it out. He asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master said:
The Son of the Spirit Tree at the Gate asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A poor man carries his child across [a river];
his affectionate love competes with the current. He asked a monk, "To say 'it exists' is not it; to say 'it does not exist' is not it;
to say 'neither existing nor non-existing' is also not it. What is your original name? The monk said, "The student has already established his name. The Master said, "Established name."
“It is not non-existent. “Ultimately, what is this called? He said, “Is it simply this? Is that so?
The Master said, “For now, let us say there is no connection. “How is it then? The Master said, “At the point of intimacy, please ask one more question.
He said, “I, your student, cannot say it; I beg the Master to speak. The Master said, “Come another day and I will tell you. He said, “Why is it that right now—”
Ma did not say anything. The Master said, "It is impossible to find anyone who can grasp this statement. He then asked another monk, "Zhang, Wang, Li, and Zhao are not your original surnames.
What is your original surname? The monk replied, "I share the same surname as the Master. The Master said, "As for sharing the same surname, let that be as you say;
but what is your original surname? The monk replied, "Wait until the Han River flows backward, then..."
He addressed the Master, saying, “I have spoken to the Abbot. The Master said, “Why do you not speak now? He replied, “Has the Han River ever flowed upstream? The Master then desisted.
A monk asked, “What is it like when one recognizes [the nature] in accordance with conditions? The Master said, “What is it? Another asked, “Who is the True Person of No Station?
The Master said, “If you try to arrange it otherwise, how could you succeed? The monk asked, “What is it like when there is no arrangement? The Master—
[The Master] said, "The True Person of No Rank. A monk asked, "What is the true scripture? The Master said, "Amitābha.
Chan Master Cunen of Xichuan was asked by a monk, "I understand how to ask about the paradoxical phrase; I pray that the Master will manifest the marvelous faculty that startles people.
The Master said, "Chao Fu did not lead an ox; Xu You did not wash his ears. A monk asked, "When a person who is fully endowed arrives, [what do you say? The Master—
"Will you take it back? The Master then struck him.
Chan Master Kuangyi Dingjue of Ziling in Fengxiang Prefecture, a dharma successor of Chan Master Huijing of Huayan, first arrived at Panlong. There he saw a monk ask: "The azure depths..."
"Clear as a mirror; where does the coiled dragon dwell? The dragon said, "Sunk in the sand, its bottom is unseen; floating on the waves, its peaks are jagged.
The Master did not approve. The dragon asked the Master to speak. The Master said, "The golden dragon soars far beyond the azure heavens;

how could it be trapped within the mechanism of the jade wheel in the abyss? The dragon approved. After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "Before one has yet taken human form, what has one been doing?"
The Master said: "A stone ox walks step by step through fire; looking back, it ceases to chew the grass at midday. Question:

"When the path of intellect and consciousness is cut off and thought and deliberation are both forgotten, what is it like? The Master said: "Ceasing imprisonment only increases wisdom; nursing an illness only brings ruin to the body."
Chan Master Wei of Tong’an Monastery in Hongzhou, successor to Chan Master Man of Jiufeng, was asked by a monk: "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said: "The spirit tree by the roadside; all who see it raise their hands in reverence. The monk asked: "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said: "Inside the room."
There is no spirit-bed; the entire household does not wear mourning. Question: Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master said: "The Jade Hare has never known the meaning; how could the Golden Crow be willing to shine at night? Question: What is the "One Song of Tong'an"? The Master said:
"The numinous lute does not share the melodies of the human world; how could those who know the music pass through the gate of Bo Ya? [The questioner] said: "I do not yet understand."
"Who can harmonize with this? The Master said, "When the wooden horse neighs, listen to it from there; when the stone man claps his hands, who hears it?

[The student] asked, "What if one encounters a true知音 (zhīyīn—a person of like mind)? The Master said, "A true知音 does not pass through the ears; how could those who have attained be the same as those who merely hear?"

One day, as the Master was wandering in the mountains followed by the assembly, he said, "The green bamboos before the steps and the yellow chrysanthemums beneath the pavement—ancient worthies called these 'true thusness' and 'prajñā.
Tongan, however, would not have it so. A monk asked, "Even the ancients were good, Master."
The Master said, "One who does not crave the taste of fragrant bait may truly be called a dragon in a azure pool. [The monk] said, "The eyes of all quarters do not find fault with Yuanming.
The Master said, "You, O *jialuo*, sit with eyes closed on the Mid-Autumn festival, yet you laugh that the moon has no light. [The monk] said, "The green bamboos before the steps..."
"The yellow flowers beneath the steps—how about that? The Master said, "When Annam has not yet submitted, how can the North of the Great Wall be brought to surrender?
The monk bowed, and the Master said, "His fame is heard everywhere. The Master asked a monk, "At dawn and at dusk, you drink and eat;
where do you hide your body? Do you say there is such a principle as this? The monk asked, "How about you, Master? The Master struck him with his whisk. The monk said, "A clap of the hands!"
A traveling monk boasted, "I am a master at this. The Master said, "Holding a whip and tilting your cap—could you really be a *śrāmaṇera*?

The monk asked, "In the Way of antiquity and today, where can one hide oneself? The Master said, "How about you, *śrāmaṇera*? The monk said, "Take care," and then departed. The Master said, "Not yet."
When Master Xiangcheng of Jingzhao Prefecture first visited Chan Master Beiyuan, he asked: "What is it like when one appears as two?"
The Master said, "One thing will deceive you. The teacher then attained realization. A monk asked, "Regarding the matter of the three lights’ scenery declining its illumination, what is it?
The teacher said, "A five-colored pennant is planted before the Peak of Chao-yi. The monk asked, "How about that which does not involve literary colors?"
The Master said, "Now you have come across the river specifically for this purpose. Ask: 'Please, Master, proclaim the one path that leads upward. The Master said, "The fishing line cannot hook it.
The questioner asked, "Does Niutou still grasp the meaning of the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "A single dot added beneath a character turns it into a thousand words.
The questioner asked, "What comes after adding the dot? The Master said, "A separate pinch of incense is offered to represent the realms of humans and devas. The questioner said, "If that is so..."
"Does not everyone possess this? The Master said, "And what about you? A monk asked, "When the bag has no silk to bind even an ant and the kitchen is devoid of crumbs to attract even a fly—what then?
The Master said, "One discards daily yet seeks; one thinks yet gains from delusion."
*Wudeng Huiyuan*, Scroll Thirteen;
*Wudeng Huiyuan*, Scroll Fourteen:
The Seventh Generation Descending from Qingyuan.

Chan Master Qing of Shanglan Monastery in Ruizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yan of Dongshan. When he first traveled to study under various masters, he asked Xuefeng, "What is the true meaning of Xuefeng?
Xuefeng struck him on the head with his staff. The Master responded, "Yes. Xuefeng laughed loudly. Later, the Master received the dharma from Dongshan.
Yinjie opened the Dharma at Shanglan Monastery. A monk asked, "What is the bladeless sword of Shanglan? The Master said, "None.
The monk asked, "Why is there none? The Master said, "Disciple, each region has its own."
When Chan Master Huimin of Tongan in Hongzhou first visited Dongshan, he asked, "By what do all the sages take their life?
Dongshan replied, "By non-interruption. The Master asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? Dongshan said, "There is. The Master asked, "What is that which is further?
Dongshan said, "That which does not follow from interruption. At these words, the Master attained realization. Later, after he had established his own monastery, a monk...
Question: "Please grant me a single phrase, Master. The Master said: "Keep this well in mind.
Zen Master Zhilong of Tianchi on Mount Lu was a dharma successor of Zen Master Zhi of Jinfeng. While they were working together at Jinfeng carrying firewood, Jinfeng asked, "Carrying firewood..."
"Does a person cross over water? The Master said, "There is one person who does not cross over water. [The monk] asked, "If he does not cross over water, does he still carry firewood?
The Master said, "Although he does not carry firewood, you must not disturb him."
Zen Master Wukong Zhijing of Guyin in Xiangzhou, successor to Zen Master Zhen of Lumeng, was asked by a monk: "What is the place where the Master turns himself around?
The Master said: "Beneath the meditation mat. The monk asked: "What is the Way? The Master said: "Fenglin Pass. The monk said: "A student... [did not finish].
[The monk] arrived. The Master said, "Go straight to Jingnan. [The monk] asked, "What is the path for returning home?
The Master said, "Do not use it. [The monk] asked, "Does this allow students to arrive? The Master said, "Where could you possibly be placed?

[The monk] asked, "How is the assembly on Vulture Peak any different from the present time? The Master said, "It is no different than now. [The monk] asked, "What is this matter that is no different? The Master—
[The student] said, "Kāśyapa did not hear the Tathāgata’s secret intent. [The student] asked, "Regarding the cold spring in the ancient ravine, what kind of person may drink from it?
The Master said, "One who is free from hunger and thirst. [The student] asked, "How can one who is free from hunger and thirst drink? The Master said, "The eastern furrow flows to the east."
The western ditch flows westward.
A monk asked Chan Master Chongzhen of Yizhou, "What is Chan? The Master said, "A clear pool where one fishes for the jade hare. [The monk] said:
"What is the Way? The Master said, "Clapping hands and laughing at the pure breeze. He asked, "What is the mark of a great man?
The Master said, "A clay statue in the shrine of the Three Officials and the Local Deity."
Chan Master Tanzhi Xingtan of Lumen in Xiangzhou was asked by a monk, “What is the ground of ultimate reality?
The Master said, “Jambudvīpa in the south; Uttarakuru in the north. The monk said, “If that is so, then all things belong to one family. The Master said, “Mount Sumeru stands between them.
Another asked, “I have traveled from afar to seek refuge with you, Master; please grant me your reception. The Master said, “From where have you come? The monk replied, “From afar.”
[The guest] came from north of the river. The Master said, "Settle down in the Southern Hall. [The guest] asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body?
The Master said, "Born in the years of Wushen and Hai."
Chanshi Xingyin of Foshouyan on Mount Lu was a native of Yanmen. He first visited Lumen, where a profound spiritual affinity was established between master and disciple.
Subsequently, he traveled to Mount Lu. To the north of the mountain, there was a cliff resembling five fingers, beneath which lay a stone cave approximately three zhang in depth.
The Master took up residence within it and was consequently known as the Monk of Foshouyan (Buddha-Hand Cliff). Although the Ruler of Jiangnan summoned him three times, he did not go.
He arose and was firmly invited to Qixian. Less than a month after ascending the hall, he secretly returned to his mountain retreat.

A monk asked, "What is the manifestation of the physical body before one's eyes? The Master held up a finger (Fayan said otherwise: "Is there anything else?"). Later, manifesting a slight illness, he said to his attendant monk:
"At noon today, I shall depart. When the appointed time arrived, the monks announced that it was noon. The Master descended from his bed, walked a few paces, and then stood motionless, passing away.
The Lord of Li prepared fragrant firewood for the cremation, and he was enshrined in a stupa on the shaded side of the cliff.
Master Dongting of Jiazhou, a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Caoshan Xiang, was asked by a monk: "What is one who has gone forth? The Master said: "The stone woman spins flaxen thread.
The monk asked: "What is one who returns? The Master said: "The pivot of the hand-fan cart is broken. [The monk] asked: "Pervading the entire world..."
"This is the Buddha-body. It instructs such-and-such a person: 'Where shall you stand? The Master said: 'A wooden man cries atop a solitary peak;
a stone horse neighs amidst glowing flames.'"

Chan Master Guiyang Huizhong of Quanzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Caonan Yixian. He was the son of the Chen family of Benzhou. He went to visit Caonan, who asked, "From where have you come?
The Master replied, "From Mount Liupan. Caonan asked, "Do you see the six eyes? The Master said, "I am not suffering from double vision. Caonan—

He did so. The Master soon returned to his former mountain. It happened that during the reign of Emperor Wuzong of the Tang dynasty, the Buddhist teachings were suppressed, and by precedent, those wearing monastic robes were treated as commoners.

When Xuanzong restored the dynasty, the Master said: "The ancients had a saying: 'A Daoist who ascends does not receive the registers; a śrāmaṇera who attains Buddhahood does not undergo full ordination.
I shall simply remain a layman, abstaining from food after midday, practicing meditation without fixed hours, and remaining within the mountains for three years."
Ten years had passed. He composed three verses to express his own realization, saying: Only after the snow has fallen do we know the steadfast nature of the pines and cypresses;

Only when the clouds have cleared can one see the division between the Ji and He rivers. Had it not been for the Imperial Preceptor’s instruction to return to secular life, How could one distinguish a flock of chickens from a flock of cranes?
For many years, worldly affairs have been a mere bustle; Though I wear the square-cut robe, I was no true monk. Today, practicing in reliance upon Shanhui, my head is [shaven]...
He kept his hair long while awaiting the lighting of the lamps; though his outward appearance changed, the Way remained ever-present.

He mingled with the secular world, yet the source of his mind never grew dim. Try reading the verses on Sudhana’s pilgrimage: at that time, how could he have been merely a śramaṇa? He said to his disciples:
"That sentient beings cannot achieve liberation is due to the burdens of their emotions. To awaken to the Way is easy; to clarify the Way is difficult. A monk asked: "How can one attain clarity?"
He departed. The Master said, "Simply shed your emotional attachments and views, and the Way will manifest of itself. Now, 'manifestation' (ming) means 'to trust.

It is like a snake-handler who trusts in the power of his incantations and the efficacy of his medicines; he can bind and play with snakes, even tucking them into his sleeves, without any difficulty."

Those who do not understand the power of mantras and medicinal herbs are terrified and flee; they merely fail to clearly perceive their own minds, and thus their emotional attachments are not destroyed.
Those who now harbor a thousand doubts and ten thousand anxieties because these methods cannot be employed have simply not seen their own minds. Suddenly, he requested incense, which was then burned.
He passed away peacefully. His entire body was interred to the east of the stupa of Master Wuliao. Several years later, the stupa suddenly cracked open for over a zhang across the steps.
The presiding monk intended to excavate it to see what was inside. That night, while in deep meditation, he saw Wuliao and said, "There is no need to excavate further.
This is now the site for the two *dharmakāya* (true-body) remains of Shen and Chen. Wuliao’s surname was Shen; he had studied under Mazu.
Chan Master Zhi of Tongan in Hongzhou was a Dharma heir of Chan Master P'i of Tongan. Before Tongan was about to pass away, he ascended the hall and said:
"The lineage son flourishes before the Many-Sons Stupa; what of the matter before the Five Old Peaks? He raised this question three times, but none offered a response. Finally—
The Master stepped forward and said, "Standing in formation outside the curtain of night-brightness, ten thousand miles of songs and chants proclaim the Great Peace.
An said, "It must be this donkey-man who can do it. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "When the two capacities do not reach [the source], how should one proclaim it?
The Master said, "Not encountered anywhere; not lost within the profound. The monk asked, "If every word and phrase falls into the present age, what about the student..."
[The student] came forward and requested, "Please, Master, point directly. The Master said, "Not manifest before the eyes; not deluded after the words.
[The student] asked, "What about the matter beyond? The Master said, "Utterly distinct and unchanging; to aim at it is to deviate."
A monk asked the Master, the Abbot of Yangshan in Yuanzhou, "What is the realm of Yangshan?
The Master said, "The gibbons cry early beneath the White Cloud Peak; the tigers rise late before the green crags. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said:
In the cold, he sat by the fire; in the heat, he walked by the mountain stream.
A monk asked Chan Master Hongzhang of Guizong, a successor of Chan Master Wenyi of Guizong at Mount Lu: "What should a student do when they have doubts? The Master said: "Doubt."
“How long has it been since you arrived? [The monk] asked. “How is it when a small boat crosses the great ocean? The Master said, “It is a bit more than that.
“How does one get across? The Master said, “Do not come over here. “How is it when flowers bloom on a withered tree? The Master said, “Bring me one blossom.
“How is it when one searches in confusion and finds nothing? The Master said, “What is this?”
Chan Master Daogyan of Shuangquan Mountain in Suizhou, successor to Chan Master Zhang of Jishan, was asked by a monk: "How is it before the great bell has been struck? The Master said:
[The Master] said, "Utter silence. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after the sound has ceased? The Master said, "Utter silence. [The monk] asked, "What is one who is on the Way?
The Master said, "No divergent thoughts. [The monk] asked, "What is the rare thing? The Master said, "A white lotus flower blooming halfway through the sky."
Chan Master Lingchong of Fenghuayan Monastery in Yangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Yunju Yue. He was a native of Shuzhou. A monk asked, "What is the one move that checks the enemy state?
The Master said, "Make your move. The monk asked, "What is it like when a single blow shatters empty space? The Master said:

He brought out a piece [of paper] to show him. A monk asked Zen Master Yaoshan Zhongyan of Lizhou: "The scriptures say, 'All Buddhas emit radiance to assist in bringing forth the meaning of the true mark. I do not ask about the radiance; what is the meaning of the true mark? The Master said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "No. The Master said, "I will explain it for you. The monk said, "Please do. The Master said, "The true mark is like empty space. It is neither existent nor non-existent. It is neither form nor mind. It is neither cause nor effect. It is neither wisdom nor ignorance. It is neither self nor other. It is neither coming nor going. It is neither birth nor death. It is neither defilement nor purity. It is neither samsara nor nirvana. It is neither Buddha nor sentient being. It is neither good nor evil. It is neither right nor wrong. It is neither high nor low. It is neither large nor small. It is neither long nor short. It is neither square nor round. It is neither light nor dark. It is neither sound nor form. It is neither perception nor consciousness. It is neither subject nor object. It is neither beginning nor end. It is neither middle nor extremity. It is neither inside nor outside. It is neither near nor far. It is neither this shore nor the other shore. It is neither here nor there. It is neither now nor then. It is neither past, present, nor future. It is neither the three realms nor the four continents. It is neither the five aggregates nor the twelve sense bases. It is neither the eighteen elements nor the six paramitas. It is neither the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment nor the eightfold noble path. It is neither the ten powers nor the four fearlessnesses. It is neither the eighteen unique qualities nor the eighty minor marks. It is neither the great compassion nor the great kindness. It is neither the skillful means nor the wisdom of liberation. It is neither the dharanis nor the samadhis. It is neither the dharmakaya nor the sambhogakaya. It is neither the nirmanakaya nor the dharmadhatu. It is neither the tathagata-garbha nor the alaya-vijnana. It is neither the sun nor the moon. It is neither the stars nor the constellations. It is neither fire nor water. It is neither earth nor wind. It is neither the mountains nor the rivers. It is neither the grasses nor the trees. It is neither the birds nor the beasts. It is neither the humans nor the devas. It is neither the asuras nor the pretas. It is neither the tiriyanchas nor the naraka-hells. It is neither the realm of desire nor the realm of form. It is neither the formless realm nor the realm of emptiness. It is neither the realm of existence nor the realm of non-existence. It is neither the realm of knowledge nor the realm of ignorance. It is neither the realm of samsara nor the realm of nirvana. It is neither the realm of Buddhas nor the realm of sentient beings. It is neither the realm of teachers nor the realm of disciples. It is neither the realm of patriarchs nor the realm of monks. It is neither the realm of laypeople nor the realm of novices. It is neither the realm of the ordained nor the realm of the unordained. It is neither the realm of the learned nor the realm of the ignorant. It is neither the realm of the wise nor the realm of the foolish. It is neither the realm of the holy nor the realm of the profane. It is neither the realm of the pure nor the realm of the impure. It is neither the realm of the bright nor the realm of the dark. It is neither the realm of the luminous nor the realm of the obscure. It is neither the realm of the manifest nor the realm of the hidden. It is neither the realm of the visible nor the realm of the invisible. It is neither the realm of the audible nor the realm of the inaudible. It is neither the realm of the tangible nor the realm of the intangible. It is neither the realm of the knowable nor the realm of the unknowable. It is neither the realm of the conceivable nor the realm of the inconceivable. It is neither the realm of the expressible nor the realm of the inexpressible. It is neither the realm of the definable nor the realm of the indefinable. It is neither the realm of the measurable nor the realm of the immeasurable. It is neither the realm of the calculable nor the realm of the incalculable. It is neither the realm of the finite nor the realm of the infinite. It is neither the realm of the limited nor the realm of the limitless. It is neither the realm of the conditioned nor the realm of the unconditioned. It is neither the realm of the compounded nor the realm of the uncompounded. It is neither the realm of the created nor the realm of the uncreated. It is neither the realm of the born nor the realm of the unborn. It is neither the realm of the arisen nor the realm of the unarisen. It is neither the realm of the ceased nor the realm of the unceased. It is neither the realm of the extinguished nor the realm of the unextinguished. It is neither the realm of the tranquil nor the realm of the non-tranquil. It is neither the realm of the peaceful nor the realm of the non-peaceful. It is neither the realm of the blissful nor the realm of the non-blissful. It is neither the realm of the cool nor the realm of the non-cool. It is neither the realm of the refreshing nor the realm of the non-refreshing. It is neither the realm of the liberating nor the realm of the non-liberating. It is neither the realm of the emancipating nor the realm of the non-emancipating. It is neither the realm of the saving nor the realm of the non-saving. It is neither the realm of the protecting nor the realm of the non-protecting. It is neither the realm of the sheltering nor the realm of the non-sheltering. It is neither the realm of the refuge nor the realm of the non-refuge. It is neither the realm of the sanctuary nor the realm of the non-sanctuary. It is neither the realm of the island nor the realm of the non-island. It is neither the realm of the lamp nor the realm of the non-lamp. It is neither the realm of the torch nor the realm of the non-torch. It is neither the realm of the light nor the realm of the darkness. It is neither the realm of the dawn nor the realm of the dusk. It is neither the realm of the morning nor the realm of the evening. It is neither the realm of the day nor the realm of the night. It is neither the realm of the summer nor the realm of the winter. It is neither the realm of the spring nor the realm of the autumn. It is neither the realm of the heat nor the realm of the cold. It is neither the realm of the wind nor the realm of the rain. It is neither the realm of the thunder nor the realm of the lightning. It is neither the realm of the clouds nor the realm of the sky.
