He declined all honors regarding official robes and titles. On the second day of the twelfth month in the fourth year of the Kaibō era, he manifested illness;
on the eleventh day, he addressed the assembly, and having completed his final instructions, he passed away reclining on his right side.
Chan Master Defu of Yunding in Huainan, a successor of Chan Master Huguo Yuan, first visited Huguo and asked: "The direct access to the source is what the Buddhas have certified;
as for picking leaves and seeking branches, I am unable to do so—what then? Huguo said: "Cease your grasping at the clouds and trees; it has been three autumns."

"Indeed. Cease playing with the solitary moon-disk in the azure pool. Thereupon, the Master was suddenly released from his doubts. Later, while residing there, the Governor of Chengdu requested him to ascend the seat in the official yamen.

A military officer of the music corps came forward, prostrated, and as he rose, looked back toward the mounting platform and said, "I do not ask about 'drinking up the waters of the West River in a single gulp,' but I request the Master to swallow this mounting platform before my steps. The Master spread both hands...
He sang out with his hand, "Rub it fine and bring it here. The military officer was suddenly enlightened.
The monk asked Zen Master Cong of Shimen in Xiangzhou, the Dharma successor of Zen Master Dayang Jian: "After Dayang passed away, where did he go? The Master said:
Riding an ox without wearing a hat; sitting upright without walking crookedly.
A monk asked Zen Master Qianian of Beichen in Tanzhou, "What is the source of the Great Way? The Master said, "The myriad streams cannot mix it.
The monk asked, "How is it when one is uniquely liberated? The Master said, "Piercing the clouds and penetrating through rocks. [The monk] asked, "What is..."
"Not falling into the phrases of the ancients or the moderns. The Master said: "The fifteenth and the sixteenth; the sun and moon pursue one another.
Chán Master Shàoyuàn of Shímén in Xiāngzhōu was originally a field overseer under Chán Master Shíchén of Shímén. Shímén asked him: "What is..."
"A water buffalo at the edge of the field. The Master said, "Its horns turn and shake heaven and earth; where there is morning sun, there is spring everywhere.
On another day, the student asked again, "Is the water buffalo well? The Master said, "It has never lacked grass and water.

[The student] asked, "What about its work in the field? The Master said, "Deep plowing and shallow sowing. [The student] said, "It is acting according to the Dharma. The Master said, "I have never acted with negligence."

After he had taken up residence, a monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed? The Master said, "In the ten directions there is no divergent path; it is revealed before Fenglin.
A monk asked, "The former master has already returned to the Wild Goose Pagoda; please, Master, proclaim the single phrase of Dangyang.
The Master said, "The asura holds the sun and moon in his palms; the yakṣa treads upon the mud-dragon beneath his feet. A monk asked, "The golden dragon..."
He does not exhale the mists of the mundane world; I pray that the Master will raise the phoenix-like pivot. The Master said: "The white-browed one does not extend his hand;
the road to Chang’an is level and plain. Question: "What is the meaning of the Westward Coming? The Master said: "A cloth bag containing a tortoise.
Question: "What is the realm of Shimen? The Master said: "A solitary peak facing Fengling. [The questioner] asked: "What is the person within the realm? The Master said: [He did not speak.]
[The Master] said: "Remnant snow upon the crags reflects light in every direction. A monk asked: "What is the Master’s secret functioning? The Master said: "Dripping water is not the essential point;
across a thousand mountains, he reveals no body. A monk asked: "When [the wind] comes from the four quarters and eight directions, what then?
The Master said: "A barefooted Persian sniffs at the heavens. A monk asked: "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said: [He remains] here.
The ashes fly and the smoke vanishes; bleached bones reach to the heavens. While the Master was applying moxibustion to a sick monk, the monk asked, "What is it like at this very moment?
The Master said, "The single thread of penetrating mystery is much like a shooting star. [The monk] asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas?"
The Master said, "A white ox lies exposed on the ground by the green stream. Question: "How can one cross the river of birth and death?
The Master said, "The wind blows the lotus leaves and the duckweed. Question: "What is the single phrase transmitted outside the teachings?
The Master said, "A goat-headed cart enters the capital city of Chang'an. Question: "How can one speak of the Way amidst the waves of birth and death? The Master said, "A fur bag hangs across."
His body was free from the need for food and drink; he would often lie in the blue stream under the spring sun. A questioner asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "The mountains are deep and the waters are cold. The questioner asked, "What is one who walks the Way? The Master said, "A golden mallet strikes a golden drum.

A questioner asked, "When the sky is overcast and the sun does not emerge, where has its radiance gone? The Master said, "An iron snake lies across the great road, its entire body black as smoke. A questioner asked, "... [The text ends here].
"What is one phrase from within the Dharma-seal? The Master said, "A spark of stone burns the mountain at night; the great earth joins its palms. Question:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; a wooden horse gallops across the high tower."
A monk asked Chan Master Huigan of Beichen in Tanzhou, "What is the phrase by which all the sages benefit others?
The Master said, "The red sun faces ten thousand doors; its light illuminates, yet it has no mind. The monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing?
The Master said, "The stone door leaves no trace of intention; the profound mystery penetrates the subtle. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "One foot short, one inch long."
A monk asked Zen Master Shouzhen of Lingzhu in Ezhou, “What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, “The monk’s staff bears the snow of the barbarian heavens;
the alms bowl fills with the spring water of the Han lands. The monk asked, “When neither delusion nor awakening enters any state, what then? The Master said:

[The monk asked: "From where do objects arise? [The Master] said: "If that were so, then all objects would cease to exist. The Master said: "A fellow who has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake.
Shu-zhou Si-mian Shan-jin Chan Master: A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "The character for 'king' (王) without the dot.

[The monk] said: "I do not understand, Master. The Master said: "The dot. [The monk] asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: [The character for 'king'] with the dot.

The mountains are cold and the waters are frozen. The Master has a verse on his hanging staff which says: "A single staff extends in all four directions; it serves as the test for dragons and elephants when the occasion arises.
If their heads and horns slightly lower or raise themselves, a flash of lightning falls upon their backs."
A monk asked Chan Master Yiqin of Chengtian in Jiazhou, "What is the realm of Chengtian?
The Master said, "Two rivers hem in a blind man; a range of mountains hides a barefoot barbarian. The monk asked, "What are words of ultimate truth?"
The Master said, "The scholar's cap is black.
A monk asked Zen Master Yicheng of Qingfeng in Fengxiang Prefecture: "The non-arising of the three periods of time—of what person is this the realm?"
The Master said, "White clouds join the snowy peaks; the bright moon blends with the fishhook. [The student] asked, "I wonder, is there anything further beyond this?
The Master said, "There is. [The student] asked, "What is the matter beyond this? The Master said, "The numinous light pierces through the color of lapis lazuli;
when the great earth is illumined, all traces of blemish vanish. [The student] asked, "What is the house style of Qingfeng? The Master said, "Facing the fire."
"Eating sweet melons.
A monk asked Zen Master Zhiduān of Guǎngdé Mountain in Xiāngzhōu, "How was it before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "Put on clothes and eat food. [The monk] asked, "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "Put on clothes and eat food. [A monk] asked, "How is it?"

"This is Mount Guangde. The Master said, "Flowers bloom easily when facing the sun; snow melts with difficulty when turned away from the shade. [The monk] asked, "What is it like for one among the people of this mountain?
The Master said, "When the morning mist does not emerge from the gate, the evening glow travels a thousand miles."
The Head Seat Jūn was a native of Taiyuan. He had resided at Shimen for over thirty years, and the monastic communities held him in high esteem.
Once, while a monk was requesting tea, he asked, "What is the Head Seat’s single point for benefiting others?
The Master said, "I still remember it from just now. The monk asked, "And what about right now? The Master replied, "Serve some good tea. One day, [he carried] a lotus...
Huineng entered the garden with his hoe. A monk asked, "Which of the three bodies goes to perform manual labor? The Master stood holding the hoe.
The monk said, "Is it not you yourself who are doing so? The Master simply walked away carrying the hoe.

Chan Master Qiyun Chichong of Xiangzhou, a successor in the ninth generation under Chan Master Guyin Yan of the Qingyuan lineage, was asked by a monk: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
A person from Fan wore a fur garment of a Hu person and said, "Student, I do not understand this principle; what is it?
The Master replied, "A deaf man leaning his ear toward a mute man singing."

Chan Master Jingxuan of Dayang Mountain in Yingzhou was a successor of Chan Master Liangshan Guan. He was the son of the Zhang family of Jiangxia. He left home as a novice under Chan Master Zhitong and became a fully ordained monk at the age of nineteen.
While attending lecture series on the definitive meaning of the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* (the *Yuanjue jing*), there was no one who could surpass him; he subsequently traveled to study under various masters.
When he first arrived at Liangshan, he asked, "What is the formless site of enlightenment? Liangshan pointed to Guanyin and said, "This was painted by the scholar Wu.
As the Master was about to offer a reply, Liangshan quickly pulled him back and asked, "This one has form;
which one is formless? At that, the Master attained realization and prostrated himself. Liangshan said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase? The Master—
[The Master] said, "I would not refuse the Way, but I fear it would take up too much paper and ink. Shanshan smiled and said, "These words shall be inscribed upon a stele.
The Master offered this verse: "In my former days as a novice, I studied the Way in delusion; I sought out knowledge across ten thousand rivers and mountains.

Though I tried to discern the past and understand the present, I could never grasp it; To speak directly of 'no-mind' only made my doubts grow deeper. Now, thanks to the Master’s pointing out, I see the mirror of the Qin era, And behold my own father."
Before his mother had given birth, what could he have attained even if he were to awaken as he does now? At night, he released a black chicken that flew off amidst the snow.

Daowei [Shishuang] claimed that the lineage of Dongshan was worthy of reliance; for a time, his reputation resounded widely. After Daowei passed away, he took leave of the stupa and went to Dayang to visit Master Jian.
Jian yielded his seat to him, appointing him as the abbot. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Dayang? The Master replied, "Emaciated."
Cranes age and old monkeys cry, their melodies resonating through the valley; lean pines and cold bamboos lock in the blue mist. A monk asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm?
The Master said, "What? What? The monk asked, "What is the Master’s house style? The Master said, "A full flask cannot be poured out;
throughout the great earth, there is no hungry person. Ascending the hall, he said: "Staggering ten thousand fathoms high, the path of birds is difficult to traverse; a blade’s edge and thin ice."
Who would dare to tread upon the wondrous phrases of the ancestral vehicle? They are difficult to express through the pathways of speech.

When it comes to the Dharma-gate of non-duality, Vimalakīrti remained silent. Thus, when Bodhidharma came from the West, he sat facing the wall for nine years until he finally met one who could understand him.
Today, Dayang is also quite groundless. Take care. Question: "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya? The Master said: "Red dust at the bottom of the great ocean."
As he was rising, water flowed horizontally across the summit of Mount Sumeru. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Hongshan.

The Master said, "Is the former master still there? The monk said, "He is. The Master said, "His presence is not lacking; please ask him to come out. I wish to meet him. The monk said, "Huh? The Master said, "This one is merely an attendant.
The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Go drink tea. He then ascended the hall for formal instruction.

All you practitioners of dhyāna must clearly understand the phrase of ordinary non-arising, the phrase of wondrous mystery and lack of partiality, and the phrase of essential clarity and inexhaustibility.
The first phrase penetrates a single path; the second phrase has no guest or host; the third phrase carries both together.
To speak the first phrase is to utter the lion’s yawn; to speak the second phrase is to utter the lion’s backward leap; to speak the third phrase is to utter the lion’s roar.
Crouching on the ground: "Zong" (縱) means to extend throughout the ten directions; "Qin" (擒) means to sit and cut them off all at once.
At this very moment, how do you communicate a message? If you cannot communicate a message, tomorrow you shall present it to the King of Chu.
Question: What is the ordinary phrase of non-arising? The Master said: White clouds cover the green mountains; atop the green mountains...

[The student] did not respond. [The Master] asked, "What is the phrase of wondrous mystery that is without partiality? The Master said, "In the jeweled palace, there is no one who does not stand in attendance;
if you do not plant the *pīng-táng* tree, the phoenix will have no reason to come. [The student] asked, "What is the phrase of the body of clarity that is inexhaustible?
The Master said, "When the finger points to space, heaven and earth turn; on the return path, the stone horse emerges from the gauze cage. [The student] asked, "What is the lion’s yawn?"
The Master said, "In the end, there is no intention to look back; how could one willingly fall into the ordinary? [The student] asked, "What is 'the lion’s backward leap'?
The Master said, "Moving about and returning, all is returned to the Father; though great functions arise in abundance, the essence remains undiminished.

[The student] asked, "What is 'the lion crouching on the ground'? The Master said, "Utterly transcending the mechanism of coming and going; throughout past and present, it never changes. [The student] asked, "What is..."
When a person from Dada came, the Master said, "It cannot be categorized as being like empty space. The man asked, "What is the pure *dharmakāya*?
The Master replied, "A white ox spits out the brilliance of snow; a black horse bears a black hen. He ascended the hall and said, "Letting go of the hand over there, beyond the thousand sages."
The Patriarch’s Hall: Long roots and sprouts at Shaoshi. A heron leaning against a snow nest is still tolerable; look further, and see a white horse entering the reeds.
Ascending the hall: At midnight, a black hen broods over a crane’s egg; when dawn breaks and it rises, a stork is born.

With feathers like a crane, a beak like an eagle, and a body like a heron, it yet keeps company with crows and ravens. Soaring high into the misty heavens, it flies low along the willow banks. Toward—
Returning late, he looked at it closely; it was vaguely like a wild goose in the clouds. The Master once explained Caoshan’s "Three Kinds of Falling":
"These three phrases must be understood through the transformation of positions before they can be grasped. 'Becoming a water buffalo' is falling by category."
The Master said: "This is the speech of a śramaṇa turning his body; it is a matter among those of different species. If one does not understand this meaning, there will be an obstruction.
It simply requires that one’s single thought be free from self-interest; then there is a path for emerging from the body. Second, not accepting food."
"This is falling into the noble. The Master said: "You must know how to finish matters on that side before coming to practice on this side.
If you do not vacate this position, you will simply sit within the noble. "Third, not cutting off sounds and forms is falling into conformity. The Master said:
"Because one does not understand sounds and forms, one falls wherever they are. You must find a way to emerge from within sounds and forms. What is this?"
Regarding the phrase "a single word beyond sound and form," it is said: "Sound does not sound itself; form does not form itself.

Therefore, it is called "not severing the pointing at the palm. But which palm should one point to? The Verse on the Five Ranks says: "The Center within the Deviation: A single wheel, pure and bright, sits precisely in the heavens."
Winding and turning, the matter of the void and mystery is not manifest; light and darkness are complete only within the shadow. Coming from the midst of partiality:
do not gaze upon the bright moon or the mirror of the Qin dynasty; it is dimly present like a lamp beneath the sun. Light and darkness blend together—whom can distinguish the shadow?
Coming from the very center: the path is profound and mysterious, utterly free of detours. Still illumination is impartial, appearing wherever one goes, like walking upon a bird’s path.
The marketplace opens; arriving amidst the partiality. When every dharma has no dependence, that is wisdom within wisdom. Transversely situated beyond all things, neither side is harmed.
The wondrous function is profound and subtle, perfectly complete. Reaching through the integration of the two; meeting the path in the wind, there is no middle way.

Do not cling to the green grass on the cold cliff; sitting amidst the white clouds, the school’s essence is not sublimated. The Master’s divine countenance was extraordinary and magnificent; he possessed a dignified gravity from childhood.
During his youth, he ate but one meal a day. Regarding the gravity of the transmission entrusted to him by his predecessors, he did not step beyond his boundary and his side never touched the mat.
At the age of eighty, lamenting that there was no one to succeed him, he composed a verse and left behind his leather sandals and a plain cotton robe.
He sent [the messenger] to Master Fushan Yuan to seek a vessel for the Dharma. The verse said: "The grass upon the peaks of Mount Yangguang— I entrust it to you to await its true value.
Where the extraordinary sprouts flourish most luxuriantly, The sacred roots remain deep and firm. At the end of the verse he wrote:

"One who attains the Dharma must remain hidden among the masses for ten years before they may propagate it. Yuan bowed and accepted it, then praised the Master’s portrait, saying: "A black dog, rotten..."
Silver Hooves. Riding a white elephant from Mount Kunlun, he was unimpeded in these two realms; a wooden horse neighed amidst the flames.

On the nineteenth day of the seventh month in the fifth year of the Shengtian era, the Master ascended the seat, took leave of the assembly, and entered nirvana. His stupa was erected at his home mountain.
A monk asked Chan Master Liaoshan Yan of Dingzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Freshly harvested aconite from Silla; *anggui* from the land of Shu."
Chan Master Liyu of Yaoshan in Lizhou ascended the hall and said: "The mountains, rivers, and the great earth;
the sun, moon, and stars—these have arisen together with you, venerable ones. The Buddhas of the three periods of time have studied together with you, venerable ones.
The holy teachings of the Tripitaka are contemporary with you, venerable ones. Can you believe this? If you can believe it, the iron ox of Shanfu will swallow you up."
Heaven and Earth. Although it is thus, one is obstructed by the Dharmakāya and cannot turn the body.
You must know that there is a path for emerging from it. What is the path for emerging for you, venerable elders? "Speak! Speak! After a long silence, he said:

"If you cannot speak, you shall sink forever into the sea of suffering. Take care. A monk asked: "I beg the Master to grant instruction regarding discourse that transcends the categories. The Master said:
"The essential Way is not difficult. [The student] said, "If that is so, then even in a ten-thousand-fathom deep blue pool, you allow a single thread to hang down?
The Master said, "The assembly will laugh at you."
A monk from Dingshou Lówén Dézhēn Mountain asked, "I beg the Master for instruction regarding the point of intimacy.
The Master said, "I am originally a man from Guangnan."
A monk asked Chan Master Daowu Chiquan of Tanzhou, successor to Chan Master Shimen Yuan: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he inherit?"
The Master said, "The Phoenix Ridge is free from partiality; today it is transmitted throughout the world. [The monk] asked, "What is the realm of Daowu?
The Master said, "Rivervalley flowers hold the jade dew; courtyard fruits fall upon the golden terrace. [The monk] asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said:

Embracing the brazier, he donned his ancient patchwork robe; basking in the sun, he rested his head against the mountain root. A question was asked: "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said: "A blue fly on a piece of jade. [The monk] asked: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said: "Ice within the flames of a red furnace."
A monk asked Chan Master Jian of Mount Yungting in Huai’an Army: “Snow falling on a red furnace—please, Master, verify this for me.
The Master said, “Old Lady Wang is cooking *zhui*. The monk said, “What about right now? The Master said, “He still complains it is too little.”
A monk asked Chan Master Guangji Fang of Dengzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Riding an ox chasing spring grass;
turning one's back on one’s young father. The monk asked, "How is it when the precious sword has not yet been polished? The Master said, "A tortoise eating black beans."
[The student] asked, "What is it like after polishing? The Master said, "A lantern hangs from a courtyard pillar. [The student] asked, "What is cultivation?
The Master said, "The courtyard pillar has a cold."
A monk asked Master Sheng of Mount Qingju in Guozhou, "Whose song do you sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed?
The Master said, "The golden rooster crows at the stone door; finding the meaning, one follows the clear waves. The monk asked, "I wonder whose son you are?
The Master said, "Thank you for coming to my gate to scold me."

Chan Master Cong of Nan Chan in Haozhou, successor to Chan Master Gan of Bei Chan, was asked by a monk: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said: "Rain in the deep forest during winter;
wind on the level ground in the third month of spring. He was further asked: "What is the root-source of the Great Way? The Master said: "Clouds arise right before one's eyes."
Midnight. Shihu’s cries resounded through the night.
The Dharma successor of Chan Master Dayang Xuan of the tenth generation under Qingyuan.
Chan Master Yiqing of Touzi in Shuzhou was the son of the Li family from Qingshe. At the age of seven, he displayed exceptional intelligence.

He went to Miaoxiang Monastery to leave the household life and received full ordination after passing the scriptural examinations. There, he studied the *Śataśāstra* (Treatise on the Hundred Dharmas). Before long, he sighed, saying, "The path of three great eons is far and distant; what benefit is there in exhausting oneself?
He then entered Luoyang to study the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, grasping its meaning as clearly as a string of pearls. Once, while reading the verses of the Bodhisattvas of the Various Forests, he said:
Upon arriving, he immediately realized the self-nature of the mind and said with a sudden awakening, "The Dharma is beyond words; how can it be expounded? He then abandoned his seat at Youzong.
At that time, Chan Master Yuanjian was dwelling at Huisheng Rock. One night, he dreamed of keeping a blue hawk, which he regarded as an auspicious omen.

When Master Jie Dan arrived, Zhenjian received him with due ceremony and instructed him to investigate the karmic conditions of the story concerning the outsider’s question to the Buddha—whether he asked for words or whether he asked for wordlessness.
After three years had passed, one day [Zhenjian] asked, "Do you remember the critical phrase? Try to bring it forth."

As the Master was about to respond, Guanding covered his mouth. The Master attained clear and thorough enlightenment, whereupon he prostrated himself. Guanding asked, "Have you wondrously realized the profound mechanism?

The Master replied, "Even if there were such a thing, it must be spat out. At that time, the attendant Zizhi was standing nearby and said, "Today Qing Huayan has recovered from his illness through sweating.
The Master looked back and said, "Shut your dog’s mouth! If you continue to chatter like this, I—"
Even though he vomited [the teachings], after another three years had passed, Yangshan Jian emerged from his cave and presented him with the fundamental tenets of the school.

[Zhaozhou] attained a wondrous realization of them all. Yangshan then bestowed upon him a pair of leather sandals from Dayang’s crown and a straight-cut robe, entrusting him, saying: "Continue my lineage and perpetuate its spiritual style."

"Do not linger here for long; it is well that you should protect and uphold [the Dharma]. He then wrote a verse to send him, saying: Mount Sumeru stands in the vast void, The sun and moon revolve as its attendants.
The myriad peaks gradually lean toward one another, While the white clouds undergo their transformations. The wind of Shaolin rises amidst the thickets; The bamboo curtain of Caoxi is rolled up.
The golden phoenix dwells in the dragon’s nest; How could the imperial moss be crushed by a carriage wheel? He was ordered to rely upon Chan Master Yuantong Xiuzhi.

When the Master arrived there, he did not inquire about anything; he did nothing but indulge in sleep. An attendant reported to the Abbot Tong, saying, "There is a monk in the hall who sleeps every day;
the regulations must be enforced. Tong asked, "Who is it? The attendant replied, "The Senior Monk Qing. Tong said, "Not yet. Wait until I have inspected him myself.
Tong then entered the hall carrying his staff and saw the Master fast asleep. He struck the meditation platform and rebuked him, saying, "I, this..."
Behind the scenes, there was no spare rice to give to the Senior Monk (Zuoshang), who, having eaten it, fell fast asleep.
The Master asked, "What am I to do as you command me, Preceptor? Tōng said, "Why not go practice Zen? The Master said, "Fine food is not for the hungry to eat.

Tōng said, "But many people will not accept the Senior Monk's [offer]. The Master said, "If they wait until they accept, what would that be worth? Tōng said, "The Senior Monk has already seen [the truth]."

"Who has come? the Master asked. Tong said, "Fushan. The Master remarked, "No wonder you are so stubborn and unruly," and they shook hands and laughed together before returning to the abbot's quarters.
From this point on, his reputation for the Way spread widely. He first resided at Baiyun, and subsequently moved to Touzi. There, he ascended the hall to preach.
He summoned the great assembly and said: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a phoenix soaring to the heavens, leaving no trace;
or a wild goat hanging from its horns, where can one find its tracks? A golden dragon does not dwell in the cold pool, and how could a jade hare nestle within the shadow of the moon?
Should host and guest be established, they must shake their heads beyond the world of Vipaśyin; when questions and answers are set forth, they still lie at the side of the profound path."
This is the chant. If one can act thus, one is still only halfway there; if you further fix your gaze, it will be a laborious endeavor even to meet [the truth].
Entering the hall: When the Dharma-gate is raised, both ordinary and sage leave no trace. The gate to the pavilion opens, and one meets another through a separate door.

Even if one attains awakening upon rolling up the curtain, how can one avoid being a bystander? Encountering peach blossoms in spring only serves to increase one’s eye disease. Therefore, the ancients said:
"The upward path has not been transmitted by a thousand sages. "Virtuous ones," [the Master said], "since it has not been transmitted, why did the Iron Ox gallop across to the kingdom of Silla?
He then shouted, "The one who attains it must know the secret alarm in the darkness. A monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed?
The Master replied, "Before the time of Vipaśyin, a single arrow pierced through two layers of mountains. [The monk] said, "..."
"What is this matter that has been transmitted from one to another? The Master said, "It is entirely because of the moon over Huai that the spring of Yingyang is illuminated.
The monk said, "If that is so, then you have entered the water and seen the long man. The Master said, "One only knows that the jade of Jing is extraordinary;
how can one discern the mind of King Chu? The monk bowed, and the Master struck him with his whisk. He then asked again, "Is there anyone else who wishes to ask a question? If not..."
Both were pleased with this exchange. The questioner asked, "Master, you have just offered incense to extend the Emperor’s divine longevity;

tell me, how many years old is he this year? The Master replied, "The moon embraces the vermilion cassia far away; the stars bow toward the North Star on high. The questioner said, "The Southern Mountain rises straight and tall, matching the Emperor's longevity;
the vast waves of the Eastern Sea compare to the source of his blessings. The Master replied, "The pair of phoenixes court the golden palace gates; the ancient melody of the green pines remains."
Gao asked, "The Emperor’s longevity has already received the Master’s instruction; as for the matter of governing and transforming the universe, what is it like?

The Master said, "It is better to seal one's mouth and withdraw; this is how one repays the imperial grace. He ascended the hall and said: "Silence sinks one into the realm of darkness; speech falls into a deep pit. To attempt to grasp it is to leave heaven and earth worlds apart;
to abandon it is to lose oneself for a thousand births and ten thousand kalpas. The vast waves are immense, and white billows overflow the heavens."
“The bright pearl of Zhenhai—by whom is it held? After a long silence, he struck his staff on the ground and said, “A hundred pieces of rubble!

He ascended the hall and said: “In a solitary village or a humble inn, do not hang up your flask and bowl. At the profound gate of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, pass straight through with your body horizontal.
Already, Su Qin has encountered a barrier; seeking a path, it is difficult to turn back. When Xiang Yu faced the river, how could he escape his fated end? You monks, when you arrive here, advance!”
Then one falls under the heavenly Māras; to retreat is to sink into the realm of ghosts. To neither advance nor retreat is to remain precisely within the waters of death.
"Virtuous ones, how can you attain stability? After a long silence, he said: "Let the three-foot snow fall as it will; it cannot suppress the single inch of the numinous pine.
The Master then composed the *Wuwei Song* (Verses on the Five Ranks), including its preface: "When the vast sky is of one color, how can the stars and moon be distinguished? Great..."

The earth has no partiality; it is only that the withered and the flourishing differ naturally. Thus, the Dharma has no "other" dharma; how could delusion and enlightenment ever reach it? The mind is not of itself the mind;
it is provisionally proclaimed by means of words and images. These words are both partial and perfect, reaching the ultimate point, encompassing all while remaining harmonious and penetrating.

This Dharma does not fall into the realm of right and wrong; how could it be concerned with the myriad phenomena? Once the profound intent has merged with the moon reflected in water, the source of the school blends its tributaries in the Golden River.
Without falling into the void or stagnation, the returning path is again wondrous. The verse says: In the midst of the center, there is partiality.

The stars and river flow crosswise before the bright moon. Vibrant vapors intermingle at night before the sky breaks. Within the hidden, all is revealed; within the dark, all is complete. Partiality...
The Centered Mean: At midnight, when the sky is bright, one feels ashamed of one’s own shadow; in the hazy colors of the mist, how can distinctions be discerned?

It is a chaotic unity that does not fall into the mirror of the Qin era. Coming from the very center: a golden rooster sits upon a phoenix terrace amidst the flames; the dark path leans against the void, its channels opening upward.
"Clouds parting, the bird-path emerges from the dust. Reaching within the 'Simultaneous' (jiānzhōng zhì). Snowy peaks enshroud the body, yet there is no evasion.

A natural warrior, both sides remain unharmed; secretly, all is provided with perfect completeness. Reaching within the 'Simultaneous' (jiānzhōng dào). One who knows how to run does not touch the Way.

This single act of picking up and holding is different from what you [ordinarily] have. Only when falling neither into right nor wrong is it truly wondrous. The Master passed away and wrote this verse:
He said, "The abbots of both monasteries cannot assist me on the Path. Take care, all of you; there is no need for further inquiry. Having spoken, he laid down his pen and passed away.

There were many miraculous signs during his cremation, which are not detailed here in full. Five-colored *śarīra* relics were obtained and enshrined together with his sacred bones in the Sanfeng Hermitage to the north of the temple.
Chan Master Qingpou of Xingyang in Yingzhou was serving as a garden head under Dayang. While he was planting melons, Dayang asked, "When will the sweet melons be ripe?
The Master replied, "They are already overripe right now. Dayang said, "Pick out the sweet ones and bring them here.
The Master asked, "For whom would you have them eaten? Dayang said, "For those who do not enter the garden. The Master asked, "I wonder, does that one who does not enter the garden [eat them]?"
Yang said, "I will not eat. The Master asked, "Do you recognize him? Yang replied, "Although I do not recognize him, I cannot help but give it to him.

He laughed and departed. Later, while presiding over the assembly, the Master ascended the hall and said: "The Great Way from the West transcends all conceptual negations. To apply the mind within the words is entirely contrary to the subtle essence.
To stop here and not proceed further would be to wrong the Patriarchs; how much more so to speak at length—what benefit would there be? Although..."
However, it is thus. Matters are not always uniform. For now, let us find a single thread of passage within the gate of proclaiming the teaching;
let everyone deliberate upon this. A monk asked: "When Sāgara emerges from the sea, heaven and earth tremble; when face-to-face presentation occurs, what is the matter?
The Master said: "The Golden-Winged Bird King presides over the universe; who among them is one who has emerged? [The monk] said: "If one suddenly encounters such an emergence..."
"How is it? The Master said, "It is like the *hudiejiu* [a type of bird]; if you do not believe me, you shall know its truth upon verifying it before a skull.
The monk said, "In that case, I shall place my hands at my chest and retreat three paces.
The Master said, "O tortoise beneath Mount Sumeru, do not wait until you suffer another defeat and turn back. A monk asked, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? The Master said:
The moon shines upon a thousand rivers in stillness; a solitary lamp is bright at the bottom of the sea. Zheng Jinbu asked, "At what time did the Master open the hall?
The Master said, "Without passing through the kalpas of the *asaṃkhyeya*, before the birth of sun and moon. While the Master was lying ill, Dayang asked him.
This body is like a bubble or an illusion; it is accomplished within a bubble or an illusion. If there were no such bubble or illusion, the Great Matter could not be accomplished.
If you wish for the Great Matter to be accomplished, recognize this bubble or illusion. [The student asks: "How so? The Master said: "That is still a matter of this side."
Yang asked, "What is the matter over there? The Master replied, "The red wheel shines across the earth;
no flowers grow beneath the sea. Yang laughed and said, "Are you so very alert? The Master gave a shout and said, "I thought I had forgotten! Thereupon, he passed away.

While Chan Master Shencheng of Fuyan on Mount Nanyue was standing in attendance by Danyang’s side, Danyang said, "There is a person whose entire body is red and festering, lying in a thicket of thorns, surrounded on all sides by fire. If you can approach this person, the marketplace will open wide.
If you cannot approach him, what do you rely upon in that moment? The Master replied, "The six sense organs are not complete. Seven... [text continues].
Shi was not entirely certain. Yang said, "Tell him to come out; I wish to see him. The Master said, "Just now there was no one else present to respond to the Abbot.
Yang said, "The official does not permit even a needle. The Master then bowed.

(Later, when the Master went to the place of Master Hualong of Huayan and recounted this previous conversation, Long said, "Cold as a grain of frost, fine as ice and snow. Prime Minister Li specifically went up the mountain and asked, "What is the Patriarch’s West?"
Regarding the meaning of his coming: the Master pointed to the cypress tree in front of the courtyard. The Official asked this three times, and the Master answered this three times.
The Official was delighted and composed a verse, saying: "Appearing and disappearing amidst clouds, filling the vast void; The original true form is, from the start, without a single speck of dust.
Time and again I have inquired about the meaning of the Western Coming; The Master points only to that single cypress tree in the courtyard."
When Chan Master Xianru of Mount Luofu in Huizhou first arrived at Dayang, Dayang asked, "Where are you from?
He replied, "Yizhou. Dayang said, "How many li is it from here? He replied, "Five thousand li. Dayang said, "Coming as you have, have you ever stepped upon it?
He replied, "I have not stepped upon it. Dayang said, "Are you able to fly through the air? He replied, "I am not able to fly."
Kongyang said, "How did you manage to reach this place? He replied, "At every step, I am not lost in direction; throughout my entire being, there is no place for discrimination.
Kongyang said, "Have you attained the Samādhi that Transcends the Quarters? He replied, "The Sage’s mind cannot be grasped; how could Samādhi manifest as a name? Kongyang said, "So it is! So it is!
You should believe that this is the total manifestation of the fundamental essence, where principle and phenomena are non-dual. Be skillful in this yourself."
[The Master] protected and maintained [the Dharma]. Later, while he was staying there, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Luofu? The Master said, "Lofty and towering, it reaches the edge of heaven;

majestic and imposing, it anchors the shores of the sea. The monk asked, "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "White clouds disperse above the head; black smoke rises beneath the feet."
When Chan Master Guixi of Baima in Xiangzhou first questioned Dayang, he said, "I am a dull-witted student; I beg you to point out to me a path of entry.
Dayang replied, "Attained. After a long silence, Dayang called to him. The Master responded, "Yes? Dayang said, "I give you a path of entry. At these words, the Master had an awakening.
Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master replied, "A good dog."
[The Master] held up a tally. A monk asked, "What is it like when a tortoise hides its six limbs? The Master said, "An arrow and bow inside a cloth bag.

The monk asked, "If one does not seek in the Buddha and does not seek in the Dharma, where should one seek? The Master said, "A villager kneeling and bowing before a stone lion. He said: [This concludes the record.]
"What is the meaning? The Master said, "A vegetarian feast is being held beneath the village tree. He then ascended the hall and said: "If you run too fast, you will miss it;
if you walk slowly, you cannot catch up. There are many great monks who are at their wits' end. Let anyone with a ready tongue come forward!"
A monk asked, "I do not ask about the full sentence; what is the half-sentence? The Master said, "Throw yourself down! The monk said, "This is the full sentence.
The Master said, "Even the half-sentence you cannot grasp. Another asked, "What is the gate of profound stillness?
The Master said, "Do not make a fuss. Do not make a fuss."

A monk asked Chan Master Hui of Dayang in Yingzhou, “When the Han Emperor [Wu] achieved great dominance over the world through seventy-two battles, you, Master, faced the assembly without employing a single blade.
By whose grace and power did you achieve this? The Master said, “When the bright sun faces the courtyard, the myriad phenomena are viewed as one.
The monk said, “If that is so, then the golden crow [the sun] gathers its exquisite hue, and the jade hare [the moon] dwells in auspicious, deep clouds. The Master said, “Drip—” (and left it there).
He poured forth his impartial intent; a single thought penetrates the profound mystery of all directions. A question was asked: "What is the master’s house style? The Master said:
"A coarse cotton robe, patched layer upon layer; a hoe for daily use, polished bit by bit. [The monk] asked: "When a guest of superior rank arrives, how do you receive him?
The Master said: "Use it whenever it is needed. [The monk] asked: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said: "The sun rises in the east."

"Look! The moon has fallen through the western door. He then showed him another verse, saying: "Morning after morning the sun rises in the east; night after night the moon falls through the western door.
Now, within the imperial palace of the Great Song, all are but golden branches and jade trees."

Chan Master Baoyin Lingyun of Yunmen Mountain in Yuezhou ascended the hall and said: "Last night, clouds and rain dispersed across the vast sky; the moon shines amidst the myriad phenomena of the universe.
Within the spiritual radiance of these myriad phenomena, there is neither inside nor outside. How can one penetrate the single phrase that clarifies this?
He did not mention that a monk once asked Master Dage, "When the moon rises above the clouds, what is it like? To which Dage replied: [The moon is revealed.]
Three children embrace a flower drum; do not come to block my path to the goal. The moon rises above the clouds—what matter does this clarify?
Three children embrace a flower drum; to conceive a thought is already to be separated from it. Do not come to block my path to the goal;
you must have a way of emerging before you can succeed. If you have no way of emerging, you will be like a black ox lying dead.
“Water. [The Master] asked: “How do you express a single phrase that issues from the body?
[The monk] replied: “There is no need for protracted standing. A monk asked Zen Master Yunjing Haipeng of Huai’an Army: “What is a person of great doubt? The Master said:
In Pipa Rock, they looked at one another and asked, "What is the person who has no doubts? The Master said, "Thus have I heard:
Mount Sumeru is ground to powder. He was asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "Bodhidharma met Emperor Wu of Liang;
Kāśyapa Mātanga encountered Emperor Ming of Han."
Furthermore, a monk asked Chan Master Jianming Jicong of Fuzhou, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "This question is not in vain.
The monk asked, "What is the realm of Dongchan? The Master said, "The waters of samādhi have never left their ancient shore;
how would the red dust of the mundane world dare to enter the waves?"
Chan Master Shanji of Liangshan in Dingzhou, successor to Chan Master Liangshan Yan, was asked by a monk: "When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then?

The Master said: "Do not let your eyes deceive you. The monk asked: "At what time will you, Preceptor, become a Buddha? The Master said: "Do not force the noble to become base. The monk asked: "Why is that?"
Ma did not consent to accept [the succession]. The Master said, "Better that good things do not exist at all. The Master offered a verse on Lu Zu’s wall-facing: "Lu Zu’s samādhi is most effortless;
as soon as he sees a monk approaching, he turns his face to the wall. If one is a person who knows the heart and understands the Way," [he would not be so constrained].
It is not that one understands [the truth] merely by raising an eyebrow.
Zen Master Dao-wu Chuan’s Dharma heir, Zen Master Qi-yu of Tianping Mountain in Xiangzhou, was asked by a monk: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed?"
[Someone] asked, "Who [is it]? The Master said, "Beating the drum on both ends. [Another] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The radish of Zhèngzhōu. The layman Shíhánchá asked, "When the Dharma is without movement, what then?
The Master said, "You have come from Lùfǔ. The layman said, "I have not taken even a single step. The Master said, "How then did you arrive here? The layman—
[The official] asked, "Master, why do you speak in your sleep? The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows. The official asked, "With no neighbor to separate us, why do we not see each other?
The Master said, "Whom should I blame? While walking along the corridor, the Master saw a monk and pointed his staff at him;
the monk stepped forward to take it, and the Master struck him.
Chan Master Fuyong Daokai of Tianting in Dongjing was a dharma heir of Chan Master Touzi Qing of the eleventh generation under Qingyuan.
He was a native of the Cui family in Yizhou; from his youth, he studied the practice of abstaining from grain.
He lived in seclusion at Mount Iyang. Later, he traveled to the capital and registered his name at Shuti Temple, where he received ordination after successfully testing on the *Lotus Sūtra*.
He visited Touzi at Haihui Monastery and asked: "The words and phrases of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are like the daily tea and rice of a household;
apart from these, is there another way to benefit people? Touzi replied: "You say that within the realm, the Son of Heaven issues his decrees; must he still rely on Yao, Shun, and Yu?"

Tang was also without [a teacher]. When the Master wished to offer some words of instruction, the Master [Tang] struck the Master’s mouth with his whisk and said, “From the moment you first conceived the intention [to seek the Dharma], you already deserved thirty blows.
The Master immediately attained enlightenment; he prostrated twice and then departed. The Master [Tang] called out, “Wait, Ācārya! But the Master did not look back.
The Master [Tang] said, “Have you reached the stage of non-doubt? The Master then covered his ears with his hands. Later, he served as the *Dian* (Director of Ceremonies).
[The Master] was seated. The Master’s son said, “The duties of the kitchen are not easy. The Master said, “I dare not say so. The son asked, “Are you boiling porridge? Or steaming rice?
The Master said, “The laborers wash the rice and set the fires; the practitioners boil the porridge and steam the rice. The son asked, “What do you do?
The Master said, “Out of compassion, the Abbot lets them go about their leisure. One day, while attending Touzi as they were walking through the vegetable garden, the son [asked]:
He handed his staff to the Master, who took it and followed him along. The Master’s disciple said, “It is only right that you should act thus.
The Master replied, “Carrying the Master’s shoes and holding his staff is not considered an extra burden. The disciple said, “There is another companion here.
The Master said, “That one does not accept instruction. The disciple then withdrew. That evening he asked the Master, “The conversation from this morning was not yet finished. The Master said:
"Please, Preceptor, give an example. The Master said, "Born in the hour of the Rabbit; born in the month of the Dog. The Teacher immediately lit a lamp and approached.
The Master said, "Your coming up and going down here has not been in vain. The Teacher said, "Being at the Preceptor’s side, it was only natural that this should be so.
The Master said, "Every household has its slaves and servants. The Teacher said, "The Preceptor is advanced in years; we cannot do without him."

The Master said, "To receive such earnest devotion. The teacher replied, "There is a share in repaying this kindness. Later, after he had taken up residence, a monk asked, "The song of the Hu family does not fall within the five musical notes;
its melody issues from the azure heavens. We pray that the Master will blow and sing it for us. The teacher said, "The wooden cock crows at midnight."
The Iron Phoenix Cries at Daybreak. [The student] said, "If so, then a single phrase contains the melody of a thousand ages;
all those in the hall, like clouds and water, are connoisseurs. The Master said, "A tongueless child can provide a sequel. [The student] said, "An adept patriarch, the eyes of humanity and heaven.
The Master said, "Stop clutching those two pieces of skin. [The student] asked, "Midnight is perfectly bright; at daybreak, nothing is revealed. What is this?"
[The Master] did not reveal the underlying matter. The Master said: "The boat is full, yet empty; the fisherman lodges among the reeds. Question:
"What is the家风 (house style) of Cao-dong? The Master said: "The rope-bench is rotted by wind and rain; weeds from outside encroach upon the abbot’s quarters.

Question: "What is the direct source of the root? The Master said: "Grass has already grown beneath your feet; with every step you fall down a steep slope. Ascending the hall, [the Master] entered during the day.
In the garden of Jeta, with the bright moon hanging in the sky, one ascends Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa at night;
yet the sun overflows the eyes, crows and ravens appear like snow, solitary geese form flocks, iron dogs bark as they soar toward the heavens, and clay oxen fight as they enter the sea.
At such a time as this, when the ten directions gather together, how can "self" and "other" be distinguished? Within the ancient Buddha-fields and beneath the patriarchs' gates—great!
A single hand emerges from the house to receive those who come and go, O worthy ones. Tell me, what kind of matter has been accomplished? After a long silence, he said:

"I have planted an extra tree without shadow, to leave for later generations to behold. Ascending the hall, he said: "The moment one ascends this seat, one has already entered the realm of worldly toil.
To further fix one's gaze upon it is to manifest one's own flaws. This one phrase of the separate transmission is like using a thief to catch a thief."
The family does not lose its original lineage; the fox and the wildcat cherish their den. Thus, *tathatā* (suchness), ordinary beings, and sages are all but dream-like words;

Buddhas and sentient beings are both merely metaphorical designations (*adhivacana*). Reaching this point, one must turn the light back upon itself and take up the burden with a letting-go of the hand.

Yet, even so, it is unavoidable that the autumn cicada clings to the withered tree, weeping until the tears run dry without ever turning back. Ascending the hall, he said: "To call it 'one phrase' is already to bury it."
The spirit of our school has been adapted to the present age, yet the general path has declined. Therefore, we borrow "function" to clarify "position," applying function where essence resides;
we borrow "position" to clarify "function," applying essence where function resides. If both essence and function are clarified together, it is like a door with two leaves opening:
one must not fixate on either leaf. As the Old Man of Xinfeng said: "The peaks and ridges are exquisite and unique, yet the cranes do not [dwell there]."

The machine stops; the numinous wood stretches far away. The phoenix has no place to perch. One must truly achieve success without dwelling upon it; like lightning and fire, it is difficult to pursue.

In the space of a single deliberation, one has traveled ten thousand miles on a long journey. Entering the hall, he said: "I shall not ask about the time before the thirtieth day of the twelfth month."
"What will happen on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month? You worthy ones, when you arrive here, even the Buddha cannot help you;
the Dharma cannot help you; the Patriarchs cannot help you; the old monks of the world cannot help you;
this mountain monk cannot help you; and even the Old Man Yama cannot help you."
You must simply exhaust this present moment. If you can exhaust this present moment, then even the Buddhas cannot do anything about it;
the Dharma cannot do anything about it; the Patriarchs cannot do anything about it; the old monks of the world cannot do anything about it;
this mountain monk cannot do anything about it; and even the Old Man Yama cannot do anything about it. You all—
Furthermore, tell me: what is the principle that exhausts the present moment? Do you understand? "Next year there will be new branches again;
the spring wind will trouble all without ceasing. Question: "What is the Way? The Master said: "A hornless mud ox gallops through the night watch. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The bells and drums clamor, yet the report is not heard; a single sound startles the person within the dream. Perfect.

"Always remain still and respond without any other business. Who says that Avalokiteśvara has a separate gate? After a long silence, he said: "Do you understand? Do not ask the guest from Potalaka Mountain;
the warbler’s song has cut through the clouds of the sea-mountain. Ascending the hall, he took up his staff and said:
"If you can realize it here, all of this is merely the peripheral activity established by the Buddhas. Even if you were to surge eastward and submerge westward, or roll up and unroll at will—"

"Present! You have not yet dreamed of the news from before the Seven Buddhas. You must know there is one person who does not receive it from others, who does not undergo instruction, and who does not fall into stages.
If you recognize this person, the business of a lifetime of study is finished.

He suddenly called to the assembly, saying, "If you look on further with fixed eyes, there is no need for us to meet. Entering the hall, after a long silence, he said, "The green mountains are in constant motion."

[The Master] took a step. "A stone woman gives birth to a child at night. He then descended from his seat. Entering the hall, he spoke in provisional words, singing of the Way, yet these have fallen into the present age.
Even if a tongueless person could speak and a legless person could walk, they still could not correspond with that one person.
Do you understand? The dragon’s roar merely makes ears prick up; the tiger’s cry is but a vain brooding. [A monk] asked: "What is it to be 'comprehensive'?"
[The Master] spoke these words. The Master said, "The wondrous function is fully deployed, encompassing the entire world;

the wooden man takes a leisurely stroll through the midst of fire. [The monk] asked, "What is the master’s family style? The Master said, "Everyone sees it. [The monk] asked, "I do not know what they see.

The Master said, "Striking the west wall with the east wall. In the first year of the Daguan era, Li Xiaoshou, the Governor of Kaifeng, memorialized the Emperor regarding the Master’s eminent spiritual conduct.
As one who has brought glory to the monastic community, he ought to be honored and distinguished. Accordingly, he was granted a purple robe and the title Chan Master Dingzhao.
When an inner court official arrived bearing the imperial decree, the Master completed his expressions of gratitude and then set forth his own resolve:

"At the time I left the household life, I made a solemn vow not to pursue profit or fame, but to study the Way with single-minded devotion to provide spiritual support for my nine generations of kin. Should I ever violate this vow, I shall cast away my very life. His parents—

"By this, you have been granted permission. If you now fail to uphold your original resolve and instead presumptuously accept this imperial favor, you would be betraying the sacred covenant of the Buddha-Dharma.

Thereupon, the Master drafted a memorial detailing his reasons. However, the Emperor again issued an edict to the Capital Prefect, strictly ordering him to compel the Master to accept it. The Master remained firm and refused to turn back; for defying the command, he was sentenced to punishment.
By imperial decree, he was sent to the Court of Judicial Review (Ji-si), where he was granted a light sentence. When the officials of the court heard that the authorities intended—
He was transferred to Zizhou. The officials said, "He has an illness," and thus he was exempted from execution. When the clerks questioned him about it, the Master said, "I have no illness.
They asked, "How then can there be scars from moxibustion? The Master replied, "Formerly I was ill; today I am cured.

The clerks ordered him to reflect on this, but the Master said, "I have fully understood your kind intentions, yet falsehood is not what I find at peace. Thereupon, he proceeded calmly toward the place of execution, and those who followed him did so as if returning home.

In the city, upon arriving at Jizhou, he rented a dwelling. His students grew even more intimate with him. The following winter, by imperial decree, he was permitted to live as he pleased; he built a hermitage in the middle of Fuyong Lake.

Monastics and laypeople gathered there like a river. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Now, those who leave the household life do so out of weariness with worldly toil, seeking liberation from birth and death.
They rest the mind and cease discursive thought, severing all attachments; thus it is called 'leaving the household. How could this be done for mere trifles?"
Gain and offerings bury one's entire life; one must simply let go at both ends and cast everything down in the middle.
Encountering sounds or sights, it is like planting flowers upon a stone; encountering profit or fame, it is like placing grit in the eye. Moreover, since beginningless time...
It is not that you have not experienced this before, nor is it that you do not know the sequence; it is merely a matter of turning the head into a tail, stopping at such a point.
Why must you cling so bitterly? If you do not rest now, when will you?
Therefore, the ancient sages taught people simply to exhaust the present moment. Once the present moment is exhausted, what further matter remains? If you can attain the mind...
When there is nothing within, even Buddhas and Patriarchs remain enemies; when all worldly affairs naturally grow cool and indifferent, only then does one correspond with that "other side.
Have you not seen how Yinyangshan refused to see anyone until his death? How Zhaozhou refused to speak of [his realization] until his death?
How Biandang gathered acorns and chestnuts for food? How Damei used lotus leaves as clothing? And the Paper-Robed Ascetic?
Jizhou simply wore paper; the Venerable Xuantai simply wore cloth; Shishuang established a "Hall of Withered Trees" for people to sit and sleep in, intending only to kill your mind.
Touzi had his people prepare rice, cooking and eating together with them, intending to let you understand the matter through frugality.
Furthermore, the various sages of old set such precedents; if you lack these long-standing virtues, how can you bear to be complacent?
"Virtuous ones, if you investigate this matter thoroughly, you will not fail others. If you are unwilling to take it up, I fear you will find it increasingly difficult in the future.

This mountain monk has no achievements to speak of, yet I have the misfortune of presiding over this mountain gate. How could I sit idly by and waste the monastery’s resources while utterly forgetting the entrustment of the former sages?
Now, following the example of the ancients, I shall establish the precedent for a *zhuchi* (abbot) and share it with all of you."
The community reached a consensus: henceforth, no one would descend the mountain, no one would attend formal meals, and no one would be dispatched as a fundraising emissary.

Instead, the annual yield from the monastery’s estates was divided into three hundred and sixty equal portions. One portion was taken each day for use, with no further increase or decrease according to circumstances.
If sufficient rice was available, it was used to prepare a meal; if insufficient for a full meal, it was made into gruel; if insufficient even for gruel—
When sufficient, rice gruel is prepared. Upon meeting with newly arrived guests, there is only tea and hot water; no further brewing or serving takes place.

Only a single tea hall is established, from which one may take and use what is needed oneself. This is intended to minimize external conditions and allow for single-minded cultivation of the Way. Moreover, all necessities are already provided in full.
The landscape is not remote: flowers know how to smile, and birds know how to sing. Wooden horses neigh long, and stone oxen run well. Beyond the heavens, the green mountains lack color;
beside one’s ears, the murmuring spring has no sound. Monkeys cry atop the ridges as the dew wets the moon at midnight;
cranes shriek among the trees as the wind turns back upon the pines at dawn. When the spring breeze arises, the withered tree roars like a dragon.
Autumn leaves wither and the flowers of the cold forest scatter; the jade steps are spread with patterns of moss and lichen, and human faces bear the hue of mist and clouds.
Sounds and traces are silent, and all news has utterly vanished. There is only a single flavor of desolation, with nowhere to turn.
