[The Master] entered hell. The Master said, "Firm. [A monk] asked, "What is the ordinary mind? The Master said, "Good morning" (at dawn), and "Take care" (in the evening).
He ascended the hall and said, "All of you here have been carrying your alms-bags and traveling abroad;
have you yet recognized your own nature? If you have recognized it, come forward and speak of it. If you have not recognized it, you are merely being led by others."
I shall now dismiss you with a word of heat. But let me ask you all: you have been studying for a long time;

you have applied yourselves to sweeping the floors and brewing tea, and you have traveled the mountains and enjoyed the waters. For now, I will pin you down: what do you call "self-nature"? You people, tell me:
that which from beginning to end is unchanging and undifferentiated, neither high nor low, neither beautiful nor ugly, neither arising nor ceasing—where does it ultimately return?
In what place do people still know where this falls? If one knows its location right here, that is the liberation-dharma gate of all Buddhas;
awakening to the Way and seeing one's nature, from beginning to end there is neither doubt nor anxiety. One may proceed freely at will;
no one can do anything to you. Every word spoken and every breath exhaled truly has its source, just as a person...
When purchasing land, one must obtain the original deed. If you do not have his original deed, it will ultimately remain unstable;
even if you were to bring the case before the authorities and obtain a formal judgment, it would still be of no avail.
Alas, if you do not secure the original deed, you will inevitably have it seized by others. You all who practice Zen and study the Way are just like this. Do you understand?
"Is there anyone who has recovered the original contract? Try bringing it forth and show it to us. But what do you call the 'original contract'?
Everyone, try to say! If one is truly sharp and discerning, upon hearing such words spoken, they will immediately know its whereabouts.
If they do not know its whereabouts, then even if they have learned a thousand kinds of cleverness from the outside and can memorize and explain them all—
"Meeting! Your mouth may seem like a pouring river, yet in the end it does not reach the ultimate; it differs as much from your own true self as heaven and earth.
Go now and seek it beneath your robes and bowl. If you have a place of realization, come here and speak of it; the old monk will bear witness for you.
If you cannot find it, then simply follow the ranks of the assembly. He was about to pass away when he took leave of the Prefect Song.
The imperial eunuch said, "The old monk is going on a pilgrimage. The Tongpan said, "This monk is mad; at eighty years of age, where would he go on a pilgrimage?
Song replied, "A great *kalyāṇamitra* has freedom to come and go as he pleases. The Master said to the assembly, "It took me forty years to finally achieve integration.
Having spoken, he passed away. He was interred in a stupa on the mountain where he resided.
When Chan Master Shouchu Zonghui of Dongshan in Xiangzhou first visited Yunmen, Yunmen asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
The Master replied, "Chadu. Yunmen asked, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? The Master replied, "Baoci in Hunan. Yunmen asked, "When did you leave there?
The Master replied, "The twenty-fifth of the eighth month. Yunmen said, "I grant you three blows of the staff. On the following day, the Master returned...
The Master asked after his health. “Yesterday I was granted three blows of the staff by you, Reverend; I do not know where my fault lay. Nanquan said, “You rice-bag!
You go off to Jiangxi and Hunan acting just like this! At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said:
Later, he went to a desolate place where there was no human habitation. He did not store a single grain of rice nor plant a single stalk of vegetable.
He received those coming and going from the ten directions, doing nothing but extracting their nails and pulling out their wedges for them;
he stripped away their greasy hats and cast off their foul-smelling cloth robes, teaching them to be free and easy, becoming monks of non-action. Is this not a joy? The Master said, "You..."
His body was as large as a coconut, yet he could open a mouth so wide. The Master then paid his respects. Later, after taking up residence, he ascended the hall and said:
"Words fail to express the matter; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded. Can you grasp this?
Within the domain of you monks, you must possess the eye that discerns the Dharma when you reach this point. As for Dongshan speaking thus—"
There is also one instance of error. Tell me, where does the error lie? A monk asked, "What is it like when traveling along a long, solitary road?
The Master said, "The weather is clear, yet you refuse to go; you wait until the rain drenches your head. The monk asked, "What about the various sages?
The Master said, "They enter the mud and the water. A monk asked, "Before the mind has arisen, where do phenomena reside? The Master said, "The wind blows through the lotus."
The leaves moved. [The monk said: "There must certainly be fish swimming. [The Master] asked: "Master, you have ascended the lion’s seat; I request that you sing of the Way. The Master said:

"When the weather is clear and dry, one opens a waterway; when there is no business, one establishes an office. [The monk] said: "If that is so, then I thank the Master for this instruction. The Master said: "..."
The shoe-selling old woman’s feet were *lì* (pronounced *lángjí*) and *qì* (pronounced *qīyì*). He asked, “What are the Three Jewels? The Master said, “One cannot reach a consensus on this.
He asked, “What is the seamless stupa? The Master said, “The stone lion at the crossroads. He asked a monk, “Where have you come from?
[The monk] said, “From Ruizhou. The Master said, “How far is it from here? [The monk] said, “Seven hundred li. The Master said, “Trample!”

"How many pairs of straw sandals have you worn out? he asked. "Three pairs," the monk replied. The Master said, "Where did you get the money to buy them? "I earned it by making bamboo hats," the monk replied.
The Master said, "Go to the hall for meditation. The monk responded with an assent. A monk asked, "What is the Dharma that allows one to escape birth and death?

The Master said, "If you see it and do not take it, you will think about it for three years. A monk asked, "Apart from the mind, intellect, and consciousness, please grant me a single phrase, Master. The Master said...
[The monk] said, "A Daoist is sitting inside a yellow jar. He asked, "It is not the proper time for an audience; I request a single phrase from the Master.

The Master said, "How would you express it before this assembly? [The monk] said, "I shall express it according to what is manifest. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows. [The monk] asked, "Where does the fault lie?
The Master said, "The offense shall not be punished twice over. He asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Three pounds of hemp. He asked, "The lotus..."
"How is it when the flower has not yet emerged from the water? The Master said, "The peak of Mount Chu stands upside down. [The monk] asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the water?
The Master said, "The Han River flows straight to the east. [The monk] asked, "What is the 'Blow-Off Hair Sword'? The Master said, "A guest from Jinzhou. [The monk] said, "..."
"How is it when one employs [this]? The Master said, "I humbly pray that you may enjoy [it]. Question: "When the cart stops but the ox does not, what then?
The Master said, "What is the use of a driver? Question: "What is the matter regarding the portion of a patch-robed monk?

The Master said, "Clouds shroud the peaks of Mount Chu; there will surely be much wind and rain. Question: "When the ocean has dried up and men have perished, what then? The Master said, "Hard to find."
[A monk] asked, "What is it like when one goes directly in this manner? The Master said, "Clouds in the blue sky; water in the pitcher.
[Another] asked, "What is it like when Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra come to visit? The Master said, "Drive them into the cowpen of the water buffalo.

[The monk] said, "Entering hell for you, Master, would be like being shot by an arrow. The Master said, "It depends entirely on your own strength. [Another] asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master—
[The Master] said, "A paper wick without oil. [Someone] asked, "How was it before Oxhead saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "A wooden staff. [The person] asked, "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "The hole enters the cloth shirt. [Someone] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said—
"Vividly clear and precisely correct. Question: "When all conditions have ceased, what is the underlying meaning? The Master said: "A stone man in a jar sells jujube rings.
Question: "What is the Sword of Dongshan? The Master said: "What? The questioner said: "I, your student, wish to know. The Master said: "..."

[The Master said: "A transgression. [The student] asked: "Heaven and earth have no fixed intent; the universe leaves no trace of the mind. If a student simply acts in this way, what do you, Master, do?
The Master said: "Mist rises at Xian Mountain Pavilion; the rapids are steep and will not hold a boat. [The student] asked: "The great assembly has gathered like clouds."
"I request that you, Master, summarize the essential pivot and briefly set forth the general outline. The Master said: "A bubble floating on the water displays five colors;
a shrimp at the bottom of the sea calls out under the bright moon. [The student] asked: "At this very moment, where are Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra?"
The Master said, "The elder is eighty-one; that tree simply will not grow. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "One does not succeed; two is not it."
A monk asked Zen Master Ledu Tan Daoxian of Hongzhou, "What is the家风 (house style) of Ledu? The Master said, "How many days has it been since you arrived, Venerable?
The monk asked, "If even a single hair's breadth constitutes dust, what is it when there is nothing at all?"
The Master covered both eyes with his hands and asked, "When one raises a cry in the open light, who is it that hears it?
The Master said, "This old monk does not suffer from deafness. The Master asked, "Awakening has no gate; how can one enter? The Master said, "Who taught you to ask such a question?"
Chan Master Fengxian Shen of Jinling was invited by the Ruler of Jiangnan to open the hall.

As soon as he ascended the seat, the Rector struck the gavel and said, "In this Dharma assembly of dragons and elephants, you should contemplate the primary truth. The Master then said, "Indeed, you do not recognize it;
this will leave people utterly frustrated. At that moment, a monk stepped forward and asked, "What is the primary truth? The Master replied, "Fortunately, I have just said..."
[The Master] said, "Understood. [The monk] asked, "How do you understand this? The Master said, "Quickly prostrate three times.
He further said, "Tell me, everyone: where does this failure lie? Once, while the Master was among the assembly with Master Ming, he heard a monk ask Fayan:
"What is form? [Yunyan] held up his whisk vertically. One said, "The cockscomb flower. Another said, "An undershirt that fits the flesh.
The three men went specifically to seek further instruction. They asked, "We have heard that the Master has three kinds of discourse on form; is this true? Yunyan said, "Yes.
The Master [Baizhang] remarked, "A hawk passes over New罗 (Luo)," and then returned to the assembly. At that time, King Li was in the audience hall and did not approve.
He then said to Fayan, "Tomorrow I shall prepare a tea ceremony and invite you two masters to engage in further dialogue.

The next day, after the tea was finished, he prepared a chest of colorful silk and a sword, saying to the two masters, "If the Senior Seat (the abbot) succeeds in his inquiry, I shall bestow this chest of miscellaneous silks as a reward;
if his inquiry is not successful, I shall grant him only this sword. Fayan ascended the seat. The Master [Dongshan]...
He came out again and asked, "Today you were granted an imperial decree to engage in dialogue; did the Master grant permission? Wenyen said, "I did. [The Emperor] said, "A hawk flies over Silla.
He then took up the ceremonial robe and departed, and the assembly dispersed at once. At that time, Faden was serving as the *karmadāna* (rector).
He struck the bell to assemble the community and examined the Master before the Sangha Hall. When the assembly had gathered, Faden asked, "I have heard that the two Senior Elders have long been..."
Yunmen said, "There is a most extraordinary karmic connection here. Let me cite one or two cases for you to deliberate upon. The Master said, "An ancient said:
'A white egret descends to the field—a thousand dots of snow; a yellow oriole perches on a tree—a single branch of blossoms. Venerable Director, how will you deliberate upon this?
As Deng hesitated, the Master struck him with his sitting mat and returned to the assembly. Later, the Master traveled with Master Ming to Huai.
Heshan saw a man pulling in a net when a fish leaped out from it. The Master said, "Brother Ming is truly brilliant;
he is just like a true monk. Ming replied, "Even so, how could this compare to not having walked into the net in the first place?"
The Master said, "Brother Ming, you still owe me an awakening. It was not until midnight that Ming finally realized it.
A monk asked Chan Master Yu of Shuangquan in Suizhou, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "One turns back and never looks behind. The monk asked, "What is the second phrase?
The Master said, "Before a word is spoken, it has already been entrusted. The monk asked, "What is the third phrase?"... [text continues]
Regarding the third phrase, the Master said: "Even with the roots attached, it still carries bitterness. Ascending the hall, he said: "The First Patriarch did not transmit in vain;
the Second Patriarch did not receive in vain. As for those great men, why did they reach such a state? He then descended from his seat.
Later, while residing at Haihui in Shuzhou, a monk asked: "What is the realm of Shuzhou? The Master said: "The washing-water flows upstream; the mountains bare their bones."
[The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "The ground has venomous snakes; the sand has lice.
Chan Master Zhiji of Piyun in Shaoshan was asked by a monk, "What is the realm of Piyun?

The Master said, "In broad daylight, there are no idle people. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'? The Master said, "The height of the mountain does not obstruct the flight of white clouds. [The monk] asked, "... (The text ends here).
"It is not formed by the character 'yi' (以). It is not the character 'ba' (八). I wonder what kind of character it is?
The Master said, "Listen to this verse from an old monk: 'It is not the character yi; it is not the character ba. The myriad phenomena of the universe are revealed herein.

Even if one were to skillfully explain a thousand kinds of wonders, It is not the *ou-ā*, nor is it a sutra. Question: "What is form-emptiness (*rūpa-śūnyatā*)? The Master said, "Pick up the fallen [leaves]."
The peony grows on old branches. A monk asked, "What is 'one speck of dust'? The Master said, "Before one's eyes are green mountains.
The monk asked, "What is 'within the treasury of Vairocana there is a great scripture'? The Master said, "It cannot be grasped. The monk asked, "Why can it not be grasped?"
The Master said, "In vain, it turns instead into sorrow.
Chan Master Yishao of Shunfeng Peak in Shaoyou was asked by a monk, "What is it like when the True Dharma is beyond words? The Master said, "Words."

The monk said, “I, a student, do not understand. I beg the Master for the definitive point. The Master said, “This is a double case. The monk asked, “Is there no expedient means? The Master said, “Impoliteness cannot be tolerated.
A monk asked, “Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, “The sun rises in the east; the moon sets in the west.
When the Sangha Director arrived at the abbot’s quarters, he said, “Why is it so dark in the abbot’s quarters? The Master said, “A rat.”
Zheng said, "It would be better to let the cat in. The Master said, "Try letting it in. Zheng had no reply. The Master clapped his hands and laughed.
While the Master and an elderly practitioner were crossing a river, the Master took some coins and gave them to the ferryman. The practitioner said, "If there were any copper pieces in your bag...
The Master bowed and said, "Venerable sir, do not laugh."
At Nanyue Banruo Monastery, Zen Master Qiyou was asked by a monk: "In the Western Heavens, a wax figure is used as a test;
how about in this land? The Master said: "A Korean person’s straw sandals. The monk asked: "What is the principle that all sages return to in common?"

The Master said: "Until one reaches the realm of suffering and emptiness, there is no one who does not sigh in admiration. He ascended the hall; when the assembly gathered upon hearing the sound of the wooden board, the Master presented this verse:

"How wondrous! Three strikes of the board, And all the masters and disciples come to inquire. Since you are well-versed in discerning the proper timing, I shall not speak further. He then descended from his seat.
A monk asked Chan Master Miaoshengzhen of Rufu, "Why did the Golden Grain Tathāgata descend into Śākyamuni’s assembly?
The Master said, "South of Fragrant Mountain; north of the Snowy Mountains. The monk asked, "What about the matter of Jambudvīpa?"
The Master said, "The waters of the Yellow River are swift and its spray is coarse. A questioner asked, "What is the path that leads upward?
The Master said, "A single stream of Ji Water flows all the way to Silla."
Chan Master Chenggu of Jianfu in Ruzhou was of lofty and pure conduct and possessed a nature that was empty and luminous.
He visited Chan Master Jingxuan of Daguang, who remarked, "He is merely a fellow of the weeds. Thereupon, he went to visit Master Ya of Fuyan, who likewise said:
He was simply a liberated monk. Consequently, he remained silent all day long, deeply investigating the grand regulations of the former masters.
One day, upon reading the words of Yunmen, he suddenly attained awakening. From then on, he lived in seclusion, seeking no fame or renown.
He resided at the site of the stupa of Chan Master Hongjue at Yunju, where scholars from all directions flocked to him; thus, he became known as "The Old Stupa Master. Jing...

In the fourth year of the Yuanshou era, Lord Fan Zhongyan was appointed as the governor of Poyang. Having heard of the Master’s virtue and realization, he invited him to reside at Jianfu Temple to propagate the ancestral teachings.
A monk asked, "Great Teacher of Virtue, with what do you instruct people? The Master said, "Do not. The monk said, "If that is so, then there is questioning and answering.
The Master said, "Do not. The monk asked, "The verdant bamboos are all True Suchness; the lush..."
"Yellow flowers—none but Prajñā. What is Prajñā? The Master said, "In the Yellow Springs, there are neither old nor young.
The monk said, "When spring comes, the grass turns green of itself. The Master said, "One's reputation shall not decay. The monk said, "If that is so, even the blue-eyed barbarian monk would frown.
The Master said, "Step back three paces. The monk said, "Suffering! The Master then uttered "Hūṃ, Hūṃ. [The monk] asked, "When Linji raised his whisk, the student..."
A monk raised his fist. "Is this the same or different? The Master said, "False words confuse the multitude. The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall act according to your command.

The Master said, "To the ends of the earth and the corners of the sea. The monk asked, "One shout distinguishes guest and host; illumination and function proceed simultaneously. What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "Dry firewood and damp reeds. The monk then shouted. The Master said, "Blazing red flames reaching to the heavens. He ascended the hall for formal instruction.
Now, those who have left the household life do so for the sake of the unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*). Within the unconditioned dharma, there is neither benefit nor merit.

Lately, those who have left the household life have become greedily attached to blessings and wisdom, which is entirely contrary to the Way. If you seek blessings and wisdom, you must first clarify the mind;
yet if you wish to realize the Way, there is no place for you to apply the mind. Therefore, I constantly advise all people: do not study the Buddha-dharma; simply [be yourself].
Rest the mind. Those of sharp faculties attain liberation at the moment of hearing; those of dull faculties may take three or five years, or at the longest no more than ten.
If you do not awaken, I, this old monk, shall cast you into the Hell of the Plucked Tongue. *Chan*.
The National Preceptor of the South invited Zen Master Zhiming of Qingliang in Jinling to ascend the hall.

A junior elder asked, "All words and phrases fall into the realm of expedient means; as for that which does not fall into expedient means, I pray the Master will speak quickly. The Master replied, "The National Preceptor is here;
I dare not be disrespectful."
Chan Master Fayun Daocun of Nantai in Tanzhou ascended the hall and said: "Regarding the ancestral vehicle of the past, how should one grasp its essential principles?
How should one discourse upon it? Can the two words 'Buddha-dharma' encompass it? Can 'True Thusness' and 'Liberation' encompass it?

Nevertheless, while this may be so, in the subtle realm not even a breath can pass; yet in the vast realm, even carriages and horses may traverse it. If we speak from the perspective of the gate of principle and phenomena..."
As soon as a single word is uttered, heaven and earth are shaken; the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are at peace, the seas are calm and the rivers clear.

The Buddhas of the three periods of time appear before one preaching the Dharma. If you understand this clearly, you will ascend together to the other shore from before the Hall of the Ancient Buddhas. There is nothing more to do. Be careful.
Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "Going downhill, one does not run. Question:
"How was it before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "He put on his robes and ate his meals. Question: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said:
"The alms bowl was hung upon the wall. Question: "How is it that True Suchness contains all things? The Master said: "It is perfectly clear. Question: "Why is that?"

[The monk] asked, "Are there those of sharp and dull faculties? The Master said, "The drums are beaten in the four heavens; the bells are struck atop the towers. [The monk] asked, "What is the realm of the Southern Terrace?
The Master said, "The Vajra-hand points toward heaven. [The monk] asked, "What is form-emptiness? The Master said, "The Daoist wears true crimson."
Question: "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, how is it that at every moment one is not separate from time?

The Master said: "Attentively. Chan Master Jingqin of Shuangfeng in Shaoyou was a native of Yizhou. On the day he ascended the hall, Master Yunmen personally attended to witness and certify his dharma transmission.
A monk asked: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "Only when the sun rises does one know the world."

Lǎng. [He said: "There is no oil for the lamp before the Buddha. A question was asked: "What is the realm of Shuangfeng? The Master said: "At night, listen to the water flowing through the bamboos behind the hermitage;
by day, watch the clouds rising from the mountain before you. A question was asked: "What is the one phrase of the Master for benefiting others?
The Master said: "Using the wind to blow the fire. He ascended the hall and said: "To take a step forward is to lose sight of principle; to take a step back is to lose [the Way]."

[The Master said: "As for this matter, even if you remain perpetually in a state of blank stillness, you would be the same as an insentient thing. A monk asked, "How can one avoid being the same as an insentient thing?
The Master said, "In movement and activity, in acting and responding. [The monk] asked, "How can one avoid losing the principle while engaged in phenomena? The Master said:
"Step forward! Step back! The monk prostrated. The Master said, "In the past, there were those who understood it in this way, but I did not approve of them.
The monk asked, "I request the Master to point directly to it. The Master struck him with his staff. The monk asked, "What is the Eye of the True Dharma?

The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. The monk asked, "What is the Sword of the Dharma King? The Master said, "A dull lead blade may be vainly displayed, but it is not as good as—" [He struck him.]
Longquan said, "What of one who employs it? The Master said, "Even concealing the point is not permitted; how much less can one endure exposing the blade?
He asked, "When Piṇḍola provides offerings throughout the four worlds, does he still manage to reach them all? The Master said, "It is like the moon entering the water. He asked again.
"How is it that one acts without being entangled? The Master said, "Before the Hall of the Bright Moon, jade dew hangs down;
within the Crystal Palace, true pearls glisten. A practitioner asked, "When I encounter bandits, if I kill them, I violate the Buddha's teachings;

if I do not kill them, I violate the King's decree. I wonder what your intention is, Master? The Master said, "In official matters, even a needle cannot pass; in private affairs, a carriage can go through."

Master Ma Guangzhu once personally inquired about the essentials of the Dharma. Xihui bestowed upon him the name Zhen Guangwu. When he was about to pass away, he told his disciples: "I shall not remain in this world for long.
You should go to the mountain peak and begin the construction of my burial mound and stupa in advance. When the work was completed, he informed him.

The Master said, "At the hour of the rat tomorrow, I shall depart. When the appointed time arrived, he was conversing at night with seven people, including Master Yunmen Shang, when the attendant announced that it was the third watch.
The Master requested incense, which was burned, and with palms joined, he passed away.
A monk asked Zen Master Quan of Zifu in Shaoyou, “I do not ask about the Dharma-lineage; I request the Teacher’s mind-seal. The Master said, “I will not answer this question.

The monk asked, “Why do you not answer? The Master said, “It does not accord with what was previously said. The monk asked, “When one is face-to-face yet difficult to encounter, how can one look into the mirror and utter ‘Heh’?
I beg the Teacher to bestow half a verse, so as to spare future generations from doubt. The Master said, “Before the blade’s edge.”
"A single phrase transcends the Tamer. [The monk] posed the question: "How has he been at odds with him for kalpas? The Master said:

"If that is so, then people know of the eastern mountains and western ridges; but I wonder, who enjoys the wind and moon before Zifu’s courtyard? The Master said: "For now, take my previous words to heart."
On the day Master Huang Yunyuan of Guangzhou first opened the hall for teaching, he struck the rope-seat with his hand and said, "Do you all recognize this vast seat of Mount Sumeru?
If you do not recognize it, I, the old monk, shall ascend the seat. The Master then sat down.
A monk asked, "What is the realm of the Great Han? The Master replied, "Songs and chants fill the roads. He then ascended the hall [to teach]. Regarding the ancients...
The Way is never absent from what meets the eye. Why do you not speak when the opportunity arises? This mountain monk is not like that:
the Way is never absent from what meets the eye, but when the opportunity arises, what would you say? Take care.
Chan Master Lun of Longjing in Guangzhou ascended the seat for the opening of the hall. Raising his whisk, he said, "Do you understand? If you do, you add a head atop your head;
if you do not, you must sever your head to live. A monk asked, "What is the家风 (household style) of Longjing?
The Master said, "Jackals, wolves, tigers, and leopards. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Diligently plow the fields. The monk said, "I study..."
The person would not [understand]. The Master said, "The harvest has already been gathered. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Yellow Clouds.
The Master said, "What is the phrase for benefiting others—'Yellow Clouds stumbling, coquettish, and smeared with rouge'? The monk had no reply.
He addressed the assembly, saying, "What is the phrase for taking one's ease upon the long benches? Bring it forth!"
Chan Master Shuang of Yunmen Mountain in Shaoyou State ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Ten thousand years to the Emperor's person.
The monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya? The Master said, "A radish growing on a silver incense stand."
Chan Master Wumen of Baiyun in Shaoyang entered the hall for the formal discourse. After a long silence, a monk stepped forward and asked, "The single path of Baiyun is entirely due to this very day.
The Master said, "It is not so; it is not so. The monk asked, "How about you, Master? The Master replied, "The single path of Baiyun."

"The weeds are a fathom deep. He then descended from his seat and asked: "I intend to pose a question; will you answer me, Master? The Master said: "Hanging from the top of a locust tree; the wind blows, yet it does not form a melody. He asked:

"Having received the offerings of a patron, with what do you repay them? The Master said: [The weeds are a fathom deep. He then descended from his seat. (Note: The Master’s final response to the second question is the same as his initial statement.)
[He] became an ox and became a horse.
Chan Master Zhang Chansi of Jingfa in Shaoyou was asked by the Ruler of Guang: "What is Chan? The Master remained silent for a long time.
The Ruler could not fathom it, and consequently bestowed upon him that title. A monk asked: "When the sun and moon shine again clearly, what is it like? The Master said: "The sun and moon..."
"Though bright, it does not reflect what lies beneath the overturned basin. Question: "Since it is a mountain of gold, why is stone being carved?
The Master said: "A mountain of gold, stone being carved. Question: "What is the Way? The Master said: "A journey of more than one hundred thousand miles."
A monk asked Chan Master Man of Wumen Mountain in Shaoyou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “The *svastika* is inscribed upon his chest.

The monk asked, “What is the Patriarch? The Master said, “He did not travel to the Western Lands. Someone pointed to a painting on the wall and asked, “Since it is a thousand-foot pine, why is it beneath the roof?
The Master said, “How about this: ‘A mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru’? What do you say to that?”
Question: "When one sees a horn over a wall and immediately knows it is an ox, how is that? The Master struck him. Question: "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Have you ever studied the classics? Question: "Why did the Prince not recognize his parents when he was first born?
The Master said, "He was utterly majestic and noble."
A monk asked Chan Master Yingzhou Dayong Yin, "What is the water of Dayong? The Master said, "Give me back a single drop.
The monk asked, "When Maitreya descends to be born in the future, what will it be like? The Master said, "In Maitreya’s palace, the grass grows throughout the three springs.
The monk asked, "What is true emptiness (*śūnyatā*)? The Master said, "Remove the attachment to Yang. The monk asked, "What is wondrous function? The Master said, [as before].
The Master then clenched his fist. The monk said, "The wondrous function of true emptiness—how far apart are they? The Master brushed him away with his hand.
The monk asked, "I do not ask about the long snake and the crescent moon; what about the lone horse and single spear? The Master replied, "At the foot of the Maja Bridge."
"Do you understand? [The monk] said, "I do not. The Master said, "Before the gate of Shengshou Temple. [The monk] asked, "Since you are Dayong (Great Acceptance), why did you drive the monk away?
The Master said, "The great ocean does not admit dust; a small stream has much detritus. [The monk] asked, "What is the single path of the ancient Buddhas?
The Master pointed to the ground. The monk said, "I am not asking about this. The Master said, "Go! The Master was once with an elderly practitioner. [They were walking together.]...
He had agreed to go elsewhere, but due to certain circumstances, he did not go. A monk asked, "The Buddha’s word is without duality. The Master said, "The Dharma is not unidirectional.
A monk asked Chan Master Luoshan Chong of Guangzhou, "What is the territory of the Great Han? The Master said, "When the jade dog barks, the sky is not yet dawn;
where the golden cock crows, it is the beginning of the fifth watch. A monk asked, "When Danxia visited the laywoman, the girl..."
"How is it when one does not carry a basket? The Master said, "One must still come here for a turn. He asked, "What is the realm of Luoshan?
The Master said, "A thousand fathoms of spreading water."
Chan Master Changbao of Yunmen in Shaoyang ascended the hall and said: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes picking and choosing.
He continued, "Is there anyone here who picks and chooses? At that time, a monk asked, "Within the lands of the ten directions, there is only the Single Vehicle Dharma.
What is this Single Vehicle Dharma? The Master said, "The sun and moon are clearly manifest. The monk said, "I do not understand, Teacher. The Master said, "A clear breeze fills [the world]."
At Linxi Jingtuo Chan Master’s monastery in Yingzhou, a monk asked, “What is the Dharma-body? The Master said, “Guests from the four seas and five lakes.
The monk asked, “What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, “An eye of clarity laughs at you. [The monk] asked, “How is it? The Master said, “... (text fragment).
"This is the person from the very beginning. The Master said, "The wind blows dust all over his face. A monk asked, "How was it before Niu-t'ou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "In wealth and honor, there are many guests. The monk asked, "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "In poverty, there is no coming or going."
Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "At the crossroads. Question: "What is the Dharma? The Master said: "In a village of three households. Question:
"Are the Buddha and the Dharma one or two? The Master said: "A pillar crossing the Three Rivers still harbors resentment for its length.
Question: "What is the seamless stupa? The Master said: "The city of Fuzhou. Question: "What is the stupa? The Master said: [Silent].
A man of average capacity asked, "Master, what is the one phrase for your guidance?
The Master said, "Using the wind to blow the fire. He continued, "At Longxing Temple, Zen Master Guangwu of Shaoyang was asked by a monk: 'What is the one phrase for your guidance? The Master said:
'Using the wind to blow the fire.'"
A monk asked Chan Master Hui of Huayan in Guangzhou, "I have heard an ancient saying: 'When the deluded mind has no place, that is bodhi.
At the very moment of delusion, is there still bodhi or not? The Master said, "The sound of your coming has already been illuminated. The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "'The deluded mind has no place'—that is bodhi."
A monk asked Chan Master Zheng of Mount Changle in Shaoyang, “Who can grasp the patriarchs’ mind-seal?
The Master said, “The stone man’s skillful hand remains. The monk asked, “Does the student have a share in this as well? The Master said, “The wooden man adjusts what is uneven.”
While Master Guanyin of Yingzhou was digging a well, a monk asked, "How deep is the well? The Master replied, "It reaches down to your nostrils.
The monk asked, "What was it like before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "Guanyin of Yingzhou. The monk asked, "What was it like after he saw him?
The Master said, "Guanyin of Yingzhou. The monk asked, "What is the wondrous power of wisdom of Avalokiteśvara? The Master said:
The wind strikes the broken window and makes a sound.
A monk asked Master Linsui of Shaoyou, "What is the master of Linsui? The Master said, "The white rock beneath the cliff."
[The monk] asked, "What is the家风 (household style) of the forest springs? The Master said, "Welcoming guests and attending to visitors. [The monk] asked, "What is the Way?

The Master said, "Far, far away. [The monk] said, "If one understands it in this very way, what then? The Master said, "For one who has long since forgotten all conditions, how could they harbor feelings of coming or going?"
A monk asked Chan Master Yunmen Xu of Shaoshan, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, “What is the meaning right now? The monk said, “Exactly so. The Master then gave a shout.
Chan Master Fajie of Huangbo in Ruizhou was asked by a monk, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "To serve as a model for all people under heaven. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Thick eyebrows and large eyes.
He ascended the hall and, after a long silence, said, "If you can recognize the Huangbo curtain, the business of your lifelong pilgrimage is finished. Take care!"
A monk asked Chan Master Kang Guoyao of Xinzhou, "What was the matter between Mañjuśrī and Vimalakīrti as they conversed?
The Master said, "Only when you understand it behind the skull will you have attained it. The monk asked, "An ancient said, 'Realize it within the skull. What does that mean?"
The Master said, "Have you realized this yet? He replied, "If so, then a man from afar has met with the Master.
The Master said, "Do not speak falsely."
Chan Master Feng of Gusang in Tanzhou was asked by a monk: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed? The Master said:

"The plum blossoms bloom on the snowy peaks; the old monk in the cloud-cave is startled. He ascended the hall and said: "A fine horse differs before the mechanism; a traveler has [the jewel] suspended from his elbow.
Since you have come as a guest from beyond the clouds, try to see it for this old monk. At that moment, a monk just stepped forward, and the Master immediately—
[The Master] struck him and said, "Why did you not bring forth your head sooner? He then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Kuangguo of Luohan Temple in Yingzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the 'blow-off-hair sword'? The Master said, "Finished. The monk asked again.
"Master, after you have passed away, if someone were to ask where you have gone, how would you respond?

The Master said, "In the future, when you meet a true adept, present this clearly to them. [The monk] asked, "Who is it that truly knows? The Master said, "One who truly knows would not ask in such a manner.

[The monk] asked, "What about when one 'borrows light by boring through a wall'? The Master said, "Wrong. [The monk] said, "But what can be done? It is so painful! The Master said, "It is precisely because it is painful that you must practice."
The monk focused his mind intently. The Master said, "Wrong! Wrong!
Chan Master Lin of Cangxi in Dingzhou asked: "The Dharma abides in its own place; the characteristics of the world are eternally present.
Where has Master Yunmen gone? The Master said, "Do you see him? The monk said, "Wrong. The Master said, "Wrong! Wrong! [Another] asked: "..."
"What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "Not so. On another occasion, the Master presented this verse regarding a matter:
"The path before heaven and earth— let not people of the age force it to shift. To give rise to conceptual understanding therein is like adding eyebrows above one's own eyebrows."
Chan Master Qingbing of Dongshan in Ruizhou was the son of the Li family of Quanzhou. He went to attend upon Yunmen. Yunmen asked, "Where did you depart from today? He replied, "Huilin.
Yunmen raised his staff and said, "The Great Master Huilin has departed in such a manner; do you see him? He replied, "I deeply appreciate this question.
Yunmen looked to his left and right and smiled, that was all. From then on, the Master entered the room for formal instruction and received certification.
Wu was invited by the ruler of Jinling to reside at Guangmu Temple. Before long, he was summoned to the Chengxin Hall to compile the essential sayings of various regions.

After ten years, he was welcomed to take up residence at Dongshan. On the day of his formal opening of the hall, the rector struck the gavel and declared: "In this Dharma assembly, there is a multitude of dragons and elephants."
"One should contemplate the primary meaning (*paramārtha*). The Master said, "What a fine message! I only fear you will misunderstand it.
At that time, a monk asked, "Master, you personally sang the 'One Tune of Yunmen. What is the matter with Xinfeng today? The Master said, "I want to say it, but I cannot."
Chan Master Wutong Ji of Beichen Monastery in Qizhou ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said:
"The Buddhas of the past, future, and present, and the bodhisattvas as numerous as motes of dust—all at once turn the Great Dharma Wheel upon the tip of this staff."
"They all pass right through the nostrils of everyone present. Do you see them? If you do, bring them here for me.

If you do not, you are very much like a man standing there already dead. After a long silence, he said, "The wind is calm and the waves are still; it is better to return to the hall. He then questioned a monk.

"Where have you come from? he asked. The monk replied, "Huangzhou. The Master said, "Where did you spend the summer? He replied, "At Zifu. The Master said, "What resources does 'Fú' (Blessing) provide? He replied, "A double case. The Master said, "But what can you do while it is still in Beichen’s hands? He replied, "If it is in your hands, then take it back. The Master struck him. The monk was dissatisfied, and the Master chased him out. Later, the Master asked, "What is the Buddha? He replied: The Master said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The monk asked, "What about when there is no wind? The Master said, "The banner flutters. The monk asked, "What about when there is neither wind nor banner? The Master said, "The bell tolls. The monk asked, "What about when there is neither wind, nor banner, nor bell? The Master said, "The staff stands upright. The monk asked, "What about when there is neither wind, nor banner, nor bell, nor staff? The Master said, "The staff is broken. The monk asked, "What about when there is neither wind, nor banner, nor bell, nor staff, nor broken staff? The Master said, "The staff is restored. Facing [each other] across a thousand *li*.
A monk asked Master Nantianwang Yongping of Luzhou, "What is the meaning of the West?
The Master said, "I do not scatter sand. The monk asked, "What is the realm of Nantianwang? The Master said, "View it as you please. [The monk asked,] "What is..."

A man from Jingzhong asked, "Master, first attend to the previous statement. The Master said, "Just attend to the previous statement. The man asked, "Having fought long on the battlefields, why is it that you have not achieved fame and merit?
The Master said, "It is simply because of sleeping in the frost and lying in the snow for so long.
The man said, "If that is so, then you shall lay down your weapons and return to court with hands bound. The Master said, "The commandant has not yet arrived."
A monk asked Master Lang of Yong’an in Hunan, “What is the家风 (household style) of Dongyang? The Master said, “One sees it as soon as one enters.
The monk asked, “How is it that one sees it as soon as one enters? The Master said, “The guest is the host’s counterpart.
Another monk asked, “What is the discourse on the ultimate? The Master said, “The suffering of separation from what one loves.”
A monk asked Chan Master Mingzhao of Xiangtan in Hunan, "What is the realm of Xiangtan? The Master said, "The mountains connect to Mount Deyue;
the waters join the Xiao and Xiang rivers. The monk asked, "Who is the person within this realm? The Master said, "One ought simply to know the times. The monk asked again.
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A hundred delusions merely weary the spirit.
A monk asked Zen Master Cheng of Mount Daimen in Qingcheng, Sichuan, "What is the Wheel-Summit Peak? The Master said:
[Zhang] said, "It rises straight to the edge of the misty peaks. [The Master] asked, "How is it regarding the matter that lies beyond? The Master said, "Three feet and five inches underground.
[Zhang] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The drum beats *dong-dong* before the Xingyi Gate. [Zhang] said, "I do not understand."
The Master said, "Three thousand blows in the morning; eight hundred blows in the evening.
A monk from Xingyuanfu Putong Fengchan Monastery asked, "How does this assembly today compare to that at Vulture Peak? The Master said:
It shakes heaven and earth. A question was asked: "What is the universal realm? The Master said: "The bamboo in front of the courtyard is elegant through the three winters;
within the door, there is no lamp, yet it is bright at midnight."
Chan Master Jingyuan Zhen of Dengfeng in Shaoyang ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all True Suchness.
If you, the assembly, attain True Suchness, then mountains, rivers, and the great earth are hidden away; if you do not attain it, you contradict the ultimate words of the ancients.
Let anyone among you who can express this come forward and speak. If you cannot express it, it is better that each of you remain as you are."
Return to the hall. Take care. A monk asked, "How was it before Bodhidharma had come? The Master said, "In the villages of three families, they go out in twos and threes.
The monk asked, "And after he came? The Master said, "A thousand crooked paths are not equal to one straight road.
A monk asked, "I do not ask about the mark of the extinction of all dharmas; what is the mark of the world? The Master said, "The real does not conceal the false. A monk asked, "How is it..."
"This is a single phrase for the sake of others," said the Master [Zhaozhou]. The Master replied, "Without exerting effort.
Zen Master Yuan of Dafan in Shaoyou, upon seeing the Holy Monk (Śākyamuni), asked the monk, "How old is this Holy Monk?
The monk replied, "He is exactly the same age as you, Master. The Master shouted, "This fellow is a thorough scoundrel; it is no easy matter to say such a thing!"
A monk asked Zen Master Yuan Guang of Yaoshan in Lizhou, "The lineage of lamps from Yaoshan continues; to which generation do you belong?
The Master said, "Everyone who meets me says they have retired from office, yet I have never seen a single person beneath the trees. He then asked, "What of one who does not traverse water or land?"

The Master returned to receive him, saying, "Suru suru. The Master asked the newly arrived monk, "Did you come from the south or the north? He replied, "From the north. The Master said, "Without falling into verbal explanations, speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk said, "I am a man of the Way from Fujian; I am well-versed in our local dialect.

The Master said, "Go join the assembly. The monk said, "It is indeed so. The Master said, "If you leap about even one more time, I shall strike you! [The monk] asked: The Master returned to receive him, saying, "Suru suru. The Master asked the newly arrived monk, "Did you come from the south or the north?

He replied, "From the north. The Master said, "Without falling into verbal explanations, speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk said, "I am a man of the Way from Fujian; I am well-versed in our local dialect. The Master said, "Go join the assembly. The monk said, "It is indeed so. The Master said, "If you leap about even one more time, I shall strike you! [The monk] asked:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "What are you saying?
Chan Master Yunzhen of Goose Lake in Xinzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "You are not."
He asked a monk, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "From the Two Zhe regions. The Master said, "Have you brought the 'Blow-off-Hair' sword with you?
The monk spread his two hands. The Master said, "I thought you were a 'Lan-ke' immortal; it turns out you are merely a gambler. He then asked another: [The question follows].
"What is the house style of鹅湖 (Ehu)? The Master said, "The guest is the host's teacher. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then I shall thank you for your hospitality.
The Master said, "It is difficult to lay out Chen Fan’s couch."
A monk asked Chan Master Qingyao of Kaixian on Mount Lu, "What is the meaning of 'the lamp never ceasing from lamp to lamp'?
The Master said, "The green willows cast their shadows one upon another. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Singing empty names beneath a rootless tree.
Another asked, "The Master himself sang the phrase of Piyun; what is the matter for Changqing today? The Master said, "Every household has Avalokiteśvara."
Question: "What is the realm of 'Piercing the Clouds'? The Master said: "A single flask of green water placed beneath the window; this shall suffice for one's livelihood through many autumns.

Question: "What is the realm of 'Changqing'? The Master said: "The old monk in the hall has hair as white as snow. Question: [continued]... (The Master said: "The old monk in the hall has hair as white as snow. Question: [continued]...

"The two realms converge in the same destination; they ought to be distinguished by principle. The Master said, "Wherever one is, one encounters doubt. A questioner asked, "Regarding the cold spring in the ancient ravine, who is able to reach it?
The Master said, "Dry. The questioner said, "If that is so, then you have reached it. The Master said, "How deep is it?"
A monk asked Chan Master Qinghai of Fengguo in Xiangzhou, "The green bamboo stalks are all True Suchness (Tathatā).
What is True Suchness? The Master said, "The guest who turns iron into gold hears the name but does not see the form.
The monk said, "If that is so, I shall take my leave with gratitude. The Master said, "Old delusions from the past persist even now. Another asked, "I have heard it said of old: 'Seeing the moon...'"
Cease observing the finger; return home and stop asking about the journey. "What is home? The Master said, "Try bringing up the *huatou* (the critical phrase) and see.
Question: "If you let it pass, one speaks of east as west; if you do not let it pass, how would you speak of it? The Master said, "Two years are the same spring."
A monk asked Zen Master Ciguang of Shaoshan, "The teaching that 'this very mind is Buddha' is a word used to guide and instruct; it does not follow the tracks of the past.
How do you instruct us? The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment the directions of east and west, what is the matter with north and south?
The monk said, "In that case, I am unable to fathom it. The Master said, "A dragon's head and a snake's tail."
A monk asked Chan Master Huizhen of Shuangfeng in Shaoyang, "What is the one phrase by which you, the Master, benefit others outside of the formal time?
The Master said, "Have you even received the staff yet? The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
A monk asked Master Mi, the Chan Master of Baonan in Tanzhou, "What is it like when a mustard seed rolls and lands in a needle's eye?
The Master said, "Where does it land? (Liangshan said, "It lands in your own eyes. The monk asked, "What is it like when one does not strike against the sharp edge of words?
The Master said, "Tiantai and Nanyue. The monk asked, "What is it like when one goes off in just this way? The Master said, "Jiangxi and Hunan."
Chan Master Yunmen Faqiu of Shaoyou was asked by a monk, "What is the Great Way that came from the West?

The Master said, "At that time, deluded thoughts have continued unabated until now. The monk asked, "What is the sword of Yunmen? The Master said, "The vast sky does not enclose the color of its sharp edge.
The monk asked, "And what of one who uses it? The Master said, "The four seas are purely clear; the sun and moon shine bright. The monk asked, "As for... [text fragment]
"What is the Way? The Master said, "Above the head and below the feet. "How is it for one who is on the Way? The Master said, "Go freely east or west.
A monk asked, "What is the 'color-changing mani jewel'? The Master said, "Color is not non-existent;

what is the jewel? The monk said, "I do not understand; I specifically request your instruction. The Master said, "Clouds have the power to leave the mountains; water has no... [the Master’s response was cut off].

While in meditative concentration, he asked: "Setting aside the throat, lips, and mouth, I beg the Master to speak quickly.
The Master said, "Fuchang’s mouth is narrow. He asked, "Why, Master, is your mouth so narrow? The Master said, "Give me back the words you spoke. He asked:

[The Master] was wearing his boots backward. A questioner asked, "When the golden crow surges from the east and the jade hare sinks in the west, what then?
The Master said, "A scholar does not ride a donkey. The questioner said, "If that is so, then I thank you for your guidance. The Master said, "You must still be more careful. Question:
"How was it before Ox-head saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "A prayer-bead rosary. Question: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "Iron."

A monk asked Chan Master Zhizhen of the Fourth Patriarch at Qizhou, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "The old, weathered bark of a many-year-old pine tree. He asked, "When the leaves fall and return to the root, what then? The Master said, "Year by year, it withers and flourishes."
Chan Master Fenneng of Xinghua in Xiangzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Long hair; a monk’s appearance is ugly.
Chan Master Huiman of Tianmu Mountain in Tangzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "An old peach tree."

The Master said, "Every three years there is an intercalary month. He asked, "What matters should one discuss? The Master said, "The ninth day is the Double Ninth Festival."
A monk asked Chan Master Jian Fozhi Tong of Ezhou, “What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, “The parrot yearns for Western Qin.
The monk bowed; the Master said, “Listen to this verse: Yunmen’s ‘penetrating the Dharma-body’— what kind of person is this Dharma-body?

A monk asked Chan Master Zongben of Yanqing in Xiangzhou, "What is it like before a fish leaps through the Dragon Gate?
The Master said, "Waving his hand, he enters Chang'an. The monk asked, "And after he has leaped through? The Master said, "Though Chang'an is pleasant..."
A monk asked Chan Master Byeonghyeon of Dae龙山 (Daeryongsan) in Dingzhou, "Regarding the words of our former master: how does one penetrate the Dharmakāya?
The Master said, "The phrase before the ten-thousand-fathom peak does not level with the white clouds. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that moves heaven and earth?

A monk asked, “How is it when the lotus has not yet emerged from the water? The Master said, “The lotus. [The monk] asked, “How is it after it has emerged?
The Master said, “The lotus leaf. He ascended the hall and said, “All of you, carrying your staffs slung across your shoulders, leave one grove and enter another.”
First, regarding "a grove": you should say how many kinds of groves there are. There may be a sandalwood grove surrounded by sandalwood;
there may be a thornbush grove surrounded by thornbushes; or there may be a thornbush grove surrounded by sandalwood.
There may be sandalwood groves surrounded by thorns; it is just like these four kinds of groves.

In which of these groves do you all establish yourselves and sustain your lives? If you have no place to establish yourselves and sustain your lives, you will have wasted your straw sandals for nothing;
there will come a day when King Yama demands payment for those sandals from you. [Ascending the hall: Xuefeng rolls the ball.
The Arhat’s calligraphy; Guizong cutting the snake; Daisuī burning the slash-and-burn field. Tell me, what matters are being clarified here?
Is there anyone who can clarify them? Try saying something. If you cannot clarify them, it is for this reason that it is said: "To cut a snake, one must have the hand that cuts a snake;
to burn a slash-and-burn field, one must be the person who burns a slash-and-burn field. If a speck of emotional dust stirs, deluded views arise; there is no sinew in the eyes.
