Thus, mind transmits to mind and dharma seals dharma. But how is it transmitted? How is it sealed? Raising up his whisk, he said: "This..."
This is thus witnessed by both humans and devas. If it is so, they shall testify to one another. For those who have not yet understood, I ask you to pose your questions.

A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The path through the iron gate is perilous. At the conclusion of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "The ninety-day period of restraining the feet is now complete; what is the ritual for the *pravāraṇā* ceremony? The Master—
[The student] said, "A monkey chasing a butterfly; it rests once every nine steps. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master presented a verse, saying: Two children carry a wooden drum; When the left beats it, the right dances.
In an instant, a hundred thousand forms appear; I show them clearly to you—take heed! [The student] asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said:
The tortoise breaks through the wall. Entering the hall: resting on stone and rinsing in the stream, one follows the spontaneous and natural state.
As the ancients said: "Pushing aside the mists and sweeping away the snow, one blends with the mica; digging into the rocks and moving the pines, one finds the *fuling* fungus.
At such a time, what more need be said? Do you Zen practitioners wish to understand? Listen to this verse: The long sky clears after the snowfall; wild geese fly across the vast fields.
Cloud fragments drift westward and eastward.
At Mount Hanzhu in Xiangzhou, Chan Master Bin was asked by a monk, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master said, "Blind. The questioner asked again.
"What is the master’s pivot? The Master held up his whisk. The monk then gave a shout. The Master struck him.
A monk asked, "What are the teachings of the Three Vehicles? The Master said, "Shang Daren. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Transforming three thousand."

Master Kaixian Zhao of Mount Lu, a Dharma successor of Master Piyun Ji, was asked by a monk: "I beg the Master to grant instruction regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage. The Master said:
"When the white clouds are severed, one sees the bright moon. The monk said: "This is still a point of doubt for me, a student. The Master said: "When the yellow leaves fall, one hears [the sound]."

[The Master] was pounding clothes. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "A single log from a cold mountain stream; those who gain its strength surpass their descendants.
The monk asked, "How is it used? The Master said, "Into a hundred fragments. He ascended the hall and said, "The regulations of the monastic groves are the house style of the ancient Buddhas:
one period of meditation, one request for instruction, one bowl of porridge, one meal. But tell me, what do you clearly realize through this? As for all of you..."

The human mind is incessant; thought after thought does not abide. If one can rest where there is no resting, and maintain mindfulness where there is no mindfulness, one naturally accords with the principle of non-arising.
To speak in such a manner is to make others laugh until their mouths split. Investigate!
A monk asked Master Tianbao of Jinling, "What is it like when white clouds embrace a secluded rock? The Master said, "This is not your realm.
The monk asked, "What is the Master’s house style? The Master said, "Arranged as five, made into three. The monk said, "I do not yet understand.
The Master said, "The nostrils and the needle-case."
Chan Master Xilan of Taoyuan Mountain in Cizhou, successor to Chan Master Shunfeng Shao, was asked by a monk: “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
“If there were any meaning in his coming from the West, I would have cut off this old monk’s head. The monk asked: “Why is it so? The Master said: “Because there is none.”
Seeing the Path, he sacrificed his body for the Dharma.
Zen Master Fayan Zhiyan of Anzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Dharma-assembly site of the ancient Buddhas? The Master replied, "The mountains are green and the waters are blue."
A monk asked Zen Master Zhen of Lantian County, a successor of Chan Master Rouru Baoyan, "What is the gate of great concentration? The Master said, "Picking up firewood and selecting vegetables."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "A mountain is formed by relying on the first basket of earth; a long journey is undertaken by relying on the first step.
Elder, you have just now come from the side of the hearth—is this the same as the first step, or is it different? If you say they are the same, you do not understand 'non-migration.
If you say they are different, you likewise do not understand 'non-migration. How do you understand this, Elder? Do you understand? This is no ordinary place."
There. There is not here. Now tell me: is it one place or two places? Is it shifting or non-shifting?
Is it coming and going, or is it not coming and going? If you can clarify this point, then past and present will be as one, and the beginning and end will be identical.
From this moment on, every thought-moment is impermanent; every mind is eternally extinguished. Therefore it is said: "By observing the direction one knows that another has departed;
yet the one who departs does not arrive at a destination. Elder, you have just now come in such a manner; now, please depart in such a manner. *Chan*.

Master Xuefeng Qingshan of Xichuan, a successor of Chan Master Miaoshengzheng, ascended the hall and said: "Yesterday was one; today is two. There is no need for deliberation—quickly, you must have a sudden realization.
If you do not realize it, you will have missed your entire life, leaving you with nothing to hold onto. *Du!* (A shout)"
Chan Master Shoumi of Jingjie Monastery in Hezhou, successor to Chan Master Jianfu Gu, was asked by a monk: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Prostrations! Prostrations!"
The monk asked, "Does a student have a share [in this realization] or not? The Master said, "A bow! A bow! The monk performed a dance and departed.
The Master said, "It resembles it, indeed it resembles it; yet it is not yet it."
Chan Master Xifeng Yunhuo of Jizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Qingliang Ming.
He was the son of the Zeng family of that prefecture. Early in his career, he sought instruction from various masters;

later, he visited Qingliang. He asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Qingliang replied, "Clouds veil the trees at the sea gate. The master asked, "After he appeared in the world..."
"How is it? Liang asked. [Fengxue] replied, "Splitting open the Iron Ring Mountains. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Liang certified his realization.

He returned to reside at Baolong, where disciples gathered like clouds. Emperor Zhenzong dispatched an envoy to summon him; the Emperor inquired about the essentials of the school and kept him at the Imperial Garden for some time. There he sat in meditation without food.
The Emperor marveled at his extraordinary state and bestowed upon him the title Yuanjing (Perfect Purity). He took leave to return, receiving a profusion of precious gifts.
Lung [of the imperial edict] was all declined. He composed poems to honor the Master’s journey and changed the name of Baolong to Xiangfu to commemorate the Master’s residence there.
Once, someone asked about the essential principles of the *I Ching*, and the Master said: "The spirit arises from the formless and is perfected through the formed.
Only by proceeding from the existent to the non-existent can one then accord with the Way of the wondrous, perfect, and correct enlightenment. Therefore, from..."
From the forty-nine *yuan* up to eleven thousand five hundred and twenty, they exhaust the principles of the world and fully realize the nature of all beings;
this is no different from the teaching of our Sage. On the day he entered parinirvāṇa, he said to the assembly:
"The heavens are not high, and the earth is not thick; from now on, people of this age will not be able to see through them. Simply look at the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month."
5. As before, he faced south and gazed at the Northern Dipper; then, with eyes closed, he passed away. Upon cremation, śarīras were obtained and a stūpa was erected.
He was a dharma successor of Chan Master Wenshu Zhen of the ninth generation under Qingyuan.
When Chan Master Xiaocong of Dongshan in Ruizhou was traveling, he served as the head of the lamp-hall at Yunju.
He heard a monk say that the Great Sage of Sizhou had recently appeared near Yangzhou. Someone then posed this question: "If he is indeed the Great Sage of Sizhou," [why has he appeared here?]
"Why, then, did he appear in Yangzhou? The Master said, "A gentleman loves wealth, but he takes it by the right way.
Later, a monk recounted this to Master Xiang of Lotus Peak. The Master was greatly surprised and said, "An heir of Yunmen still remains!

In the middle of the night, he gazed toward Yunju and paid him homage. After [the Master] took up residence there, a monk asked, "Before Bodhidharma transmitted the seal of the mind-ground, and before Śākyamuni..."
He untied the jewel from within his topknot. At that time, if one were to ask about the meaning of the West, would there still be a "meaning of the West" or not?

The Master said, "In the sixth month, the rain pours down; it broadens the hearts of the myriad people. The monk said, "If so, then the clouds disperse and every house has the moon; spring arrives and flowers bloom everywhere.
The Master said, "From the soles of your feet down to the Diamond Water-limit, how many fathoms is that? The monk was speechless.
The Master said: "The Patriarch came from the West specifically to sing this matter.
It is because you, Senior Monk, have not realized it that those who enter through the gate do not possess the family treasure. To mistake the shadows for the head—is this not a great error?
Since the Patriarch came from the West specifically to sing this matter, why need he speak further at length before the assembly? Take care. [A monk] asked: "Regarding the rootless tree..."
"Where was it planted? The Master said, "A thousand-year permanent residence for a single morning. A monk asked, "What is the phrase that transcends sound and form?
The Master said, "Jambudvīpa; Uttarakuru. The monk said, "In that case, this student knows gratitude and does not forget it.
The Master said, "How deep are the four great oceans? [The monk] asked, "How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said, "..."
"This is not far from Hanyang. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after grinding? The Master said, "The Yellow Crane Tower before the Parrot Isle.
He was asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "When principle prevails, one follows it. Ascending the hall, he said: "How could I, this mountain monk, say anything at all?
The ancient is the present; the present is the ancient. Therefore, the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* says: 'Pines are straight and thorns are crooked; cranes..."*

"The white crane is black; do you still know this? Although it is so, it is not necessarily the case that pines are always straight and thorns are always crooked, or that cranes are simply white and crows are simply black. Dongshan said:

"Right here there are also crooked pines, there are also straight thorns, there are also black cranes, and there are also white crows. [He stood for a long time. Upon ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The student..."
"When one cannot advance and yet cannot retreat, what then? The Master said, "He clasps his head and cries out to the blue heavens. The monk was speechless.
The Master said, "Do you know where the alms bowl and the cooking pot have fallen? If you can know where they have fallen," [he continued].
"I have also come for your sake to ask this. Thirty years from now, even if you were to suddenly bring it up, it might not be certain. He ascended the hall and cited Hanshan, who said:
"Red dust arises from the bottom of the well; white waves rise upon the high peaks. A stone woman gives birth to a stone child; tortoise hair grows inch by inch.
If you wish to study Bodhi, simply look at these appearances. After a long silence, he asked: "Do you know where this falls?"
If you do not know where it falls, look: behold, Bodhi has entered the Sangha Hall! I have stood here for a long time.
Ascending the hall: The spring cold is freezing; last night there was fine snow. Do you see it? The great earth is covered in vast white snow, yet the spring wind remains as cold as ever.
To speak of Chan or speak of the Way is easy; to become a Buddha or a Patriarch is difficult. Be careful! Ascending the hall: The morning cock announces the dawn with spiritual clarity.
After the congee, it was already dawn. The lanterns were still dozing, while the pillar was wide awake. He spoke again: "If it is wide awake, say it is wide awake;
if it is clearly conscious, say it is clearly conscious. Tomorrow morning and the days to come, do not mistake the servant for the master. Take care."
On account of certain matters, he addressed the assembly: "When the sky is clear, one repairs the roof; when the weather is dry, one reaps the grain.
Having paid the king’s taxes early, one beats the belly and sings the *bā* song. He asked: "Deshan’s 'stick upon entering the gate' was still merely following a model and drawing a likeness.
Linji’s 'shout upon entering the gate' could not avoid being like pressing one's eyes until flowers appear. Apart from these two paths, I wonder how Dongshan would have acted?"

The Master said, "It has been a long time since the sky cleared and it rained; recently, clouds have begun to rise. He asked, "If someone were to ask you about the fundamental tenet of Dongshan in the future, how would you instruct the student to express it?
The Master replied, "The vegetables in the garden are withered; I am carrying water to sprinkle on the spinach.
One day, feeling unwell, the Master ascended the hall to bid farewell to the assembly, reciting this verse on the Dharmakāya: "Studying Chan..."
"The Way is not obscure. Ask through until you penetrate the North Star hidden within the Dharma-body. "I am now old and decrepit, extremely frail;
seeing others, I have no strength left to deliberate with them. Only my spade knows my intent: when planting pine trees, it ascends once more to Mount Jingang.
Having finished speaking, he passed away. He was enshrined in a stupa on Mount Jingang.
Chan Master Faguang of Gaoyang in Ruzhou, successor of Chan Master Qin of Nantai, was asked by a monk: "What is the great compassion of a thousand hands and eyes? The Master said:

Falling into a pit or a ditch. A monk asked Chan Master Jiecheng of Shishuang in Tanzhou, "The ancients said: 'Rolling up the curtain, it is broad daylight; moving the seat, one faces the green mountains. What is 'rolling up the curtain, it is broad daylight'? The Master said, "Bring me the water pitcher. The monk asked, "What about... [The Master struck him. The monk said, "How is it? [The Master struck him again. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand, go ask the old man at the gate. The monk went to the gate and asked, "What is 'rolling up the curtain, it is broad daylight'? The old man at the gate said, "The wind blows through the window. The monk returned and reported this to the Master. The Master said, "This fellow has a mouth like a bellows. The monk asked, "What about 'moving the seat, one faces the green mountains'? The Master said, "Go wash your feet. The monk bowed and withdrew. The Master said, "This fellow has eyes like a well. The monk asked, "Why did you strike me twice when I first asked? The Master said, "Because you have no eyes. The monk asked, "Why did you strike me twice when I asked about 'moving the seat, one faces the green mountains'? The Master said, "Because you have no mouth. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'the wind blows through the window'? The Master said, "It is because you have no ears. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'wash your feet'? The Master said, "It is because you have no legs. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'this fellow has a mouth like a bellows'? The Master said, "It is because you have no tongue. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'this fellow has eyes like a well'? The Master said, "It is because you have no eyebrows. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no ears'? The Master said, "It is because you have no nostrils. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no legs'? The Master said, "It is because you have no feet. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no tongue'? The Master said, "It is because you have no teeth. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no eyebrows'? The Master said, "It is because you have no forehead. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no nostrils'? The Master said, "It is because you have no face. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no feet'? The Master said, "It is because you have no body. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no teeth'? The Master said, "It is because you have no mouth. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no face'? The Master said, "It is because you have no head. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no body'? The Master said, "It is because you have no life-root. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no head'? The Master said, "It is because you have no Buddha-nature. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no life-root'? The Master said, "It is because you have no Dharma-body. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no Buddha-nature'? The Master said, "It is because you have no Nirvana. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no Dharma-body'? The Master said, "It is because you have no emptiness. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no Nirvana'? The Master said, "It is because you have no suchness. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no emptiness'? The Master said, "It is because you have no reality. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no suchness'? The Master said, "It is because you have no truth. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no reality'? The Master said, "It is because you have no principle. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no truth'? The Master said, "It is because you have no Way. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no principle'? The Master said, "It is because you have no mind. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no Way'? The Master said, "It is because you have no self. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no mind'? The Master said, "It is because you have no consciousness. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no self'? The Master said, "It is because you have no ego. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no consciousness'? The Master said, "It is because you have no perception. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no ego'? The Master said, "It is because you have no attachment. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no perception'? The Master said, "It is because you have no delusion. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no attachment'? The Master said, "It is because you have no greed. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no delusion'? The Master said, "It is because you have no ignorance. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no greed'? The Master said, "It is because you have no craving. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no ignorance'? The Master said, "It is because you have no birth. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no craving'? The Master said, "It is because you have no death. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no birth'? The Master said, "It is because you have no beginning. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no death'? The Master said, "It is because you have no end. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no beginning'? The Master said, "It is because you have no source. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no end'? The Master said, "It is because you have no destination. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no source'? The Master said, "It is because you have no root. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no destination'? The Master said, "It is because you have no branch. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no root'? The Master said, "It is because you have no stem. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no branch'? The Master said, "It is because you have no leaf. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no stem'? The Master said, "It is because you have no flower. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no leaf'? The Master said, "It is because you have no fruit. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no flower'? The Master said, "It is because you have no seed. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no fruit'? The Master said, "It is because you have no harvest. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no seed'? The Master said, "It is because you have no cultivation. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no harvest'? The Master said, "It is because you have no enjoyment. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no cultivation'? The Master said, "It is because you have no practice. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no enjoyment'? The Master said, "It is because you have no realization. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no practice'? The Master said, "It is because you have no attainment. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it is because you have no realization'? The Master said, "It is because you have no enlightenment
He moved his seat to face the green mountains. The Master said, "Put it back in its original place. Ascending the hall, he said: "Outside the mind there is no dharma;
outside dharmas there is no mind. Flowing freely according to conditions, do not hesitate any longer. All of you, as soon as you step onto the stairs and path, you ought to turn back.
Why must you wait for a second ladle of foul water to be poured upon you?"
When a monk asked Chan Master Zhixian of Deshan in Dingzhou, a successor of Chan Master Deshan Yan, "What is it like when one sees form and thereby sees the mind? The Master said:
"The horned bow bends like the moon; the precious sword is as sharp as frost. [The Master] asked, "How do you understand this?

The teacher said, "The golden armor is like fish scales; the vermilion banners are like flames of fire. [The Master] asked, "I have come from afar to seek refuge with you, Master; I beg you for a reception. The teacher said, "No reception."
[The student] said, "If that is so, then I have extended this question in vain. The Master said, "Rarely does one encounter a guest with pierced ears; often does one meet a man who marks the boat.
[The student] asked, "When the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, why was he unable to attain the Way of Buddhahood?
The Master said, "He gazed greedily at the moon in the sky and lost the pearl in his palm. [The student] asked, "What is it like when military orders are urgent? The Master said—
[The Master] said, "Dust covers one's face at the crossroads. [The student] asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "Knowing it, yet intentionally committing it.
[The student] asked, "What is the discourse on non-action (*wuwei*)? The Master said, "Stone rams and stone tigers chatter away. [The student] asked, "What kind of teaching is this?
The Master said, "Long passages could not exhaust it; short verses leave nothing for people to hear. [The student] asked, "What is 'one invocation' (*yicheng*)? The Master said, "..."
"Homage to the Buddha. The Master said, "All shall attain the Way of the Buddha.

Zen Master Heishui Yiqin of Mount Emei, a successor of Zen Master Heishui Jing, ascended the hall. A monk came forward and prostrated. The Master said, "The great earth is a medley of a hundred things..."
[He] shattered [the bowl] and immediately descended from the seat.
A monk asked Zen Master Hetan Huicheng, the dharma successor of Zen Master Wuzu Ji, "That which sees is form; that which hears is sound. Apart from these—"

"Between these two paths, I request that you, Master, provide another way. The Master said, "An ancient temple with a new plaque. He asked, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion?
The Master said, "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. One day, seeing a monk wearing his patched robe, the Master said, "How fine are those stitches!
The monk replied, "I simply want them to be sturdy. The Master said, "Why strike the grass to startle the snake?"
Mou said, "When a guest comes, one must see them. The Master said, "There is only this; is there anything else? Mou said, "Clouds arise upon the mountain peaks.
The Master said, "Not yet; speak further. Mou said, "Water drips from between the rocks. [Another] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Mañjuśrī is Mañjuśrī; liberation is liberation."
Chan Master Zibo of Dongshan in Ruizhou ascended the hall and said: "Everyone is like this—windless and calm, with no waves. Where did you get that?
Suddenly, when you encounter vast, surging billows and white waves lapping at the heavens, at such a time it would be difficult even to find a single sailor.
Is there anyone among you who can pull me back? No one in the assembly responded. The Master said, "You have deceived the entire shipload of people."
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Long waist and short legs.
Chan Master Siguang of Beitou in Fuzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the transformative and adaptive activity of a patch-robed monk?

The Master said, "Surging eastward and submerging westward. The monk asked, "After such transformation and adaptation, what is it like? The Master said, "The earth is fertile; the eggplants are tender. [Another] asked: "If..."
"What is the family style of our Preceptor? The Master said, "Writing the character on the right with the left hand. [The student] said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "A head like Ou and legs like Liu."
The Dharma-body Verse of Chan Master Fourth Patriarch Duan of Qizhou states: "A lamp-wick pricks the foot of a stone man;
In haste, go and invite the learned physician Zhou. On the road, he meets Master Pang, who asks him: 'Is the sun in the sixth month being dried out by the heat?'"
A monk asked Master Chan Master Ziyong of Yungai in Tanzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The inscriptions on ancient temples are difficult to read. The monk asked, "What is the significance of this? The Master said, "All who read them knit their brows."
A monk asked Chan Master Tong of Haihui in Shu Province, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A persimmon bucket and a bamboo hat.
The monk said, "I do not understand, Master. The Master said, "When walking, it is worn on the head; when sitting, it is hung on a high wall."
A monk asked Chan Master Miaoyuan of Dongshan in Ruizhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “The head and brain are alike.
A monk asked Chan Master Zixiang of Yitai in Qizhou, “What is the realm of Yitai? The Master said, “There is no one who picks up what has been dropped on the road.
The monk asked, “What is it like for those within the realm? The Master said, “The dog of Jie barks at Yao.”
A monk asked Chan Master Huaiqing of Tiantong in Mingzhou, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, “Dust does not settle in the eye. The monk asked, “How should one comprehend this? The Master said, “Water does not remain in the ear.
The monk said, “If that is so, then I shall prostrate myself. The Master said, “When the neighbor to the east lights a lamp, the neighbor to the west sits in the dark.”
A monk asked Chan Master Shuzhi of Baoyan in Yuezhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “An earthen body and wooden bones.
The monk asked, “What is the underlying meaning? The Master said, “Five-colored gold ornamentation. The monk said, “If that is so, I shall prostrate myself.
The Master said, “The *zhilu* staff of Tiantai.”
A monk asked Zen Master Xiu of Wuzushan in Qizhou, "It is said that 'there being no dharma to be preached, this is called preaching the Dharma.

Since there is no dharma to be preached, with what then does one preach? The Master said, "The frost is cold and the ground is frozen. The monk said, "'Śūnyatā-born did not understand sitting in the mountain cave;
he provoked the heavenly flowers to come swarming from the earth. The Master said, "The sun rises and the ice melts. The monk hesitated. The Master said, "..."

"Why do you not speak? The monk remained silent. The Master said, "A cart should not be pushed sideways; principles must not be judged with partiality. Chan Master Bian of Baima in Xiangzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "When the water comes, the river swells. The monk asked again: [How about when the water recedes? The Master replied: "The riverbed remains. The monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied: "The sky is blue, the clouds are white. The monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s leaving for the East? The Master replied: "The wind blows, the grass bends. The monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s sitting in meditation? The Master replied: "The mountain is high, the valley is deep. The staff is the Dharma of the One Vehicle. Which one is the condition? "If you can investigate and see the Old Man Śākyamuni right here, then go buy [your sandals]."
"One who travels with straw sandals may not pass through the gate of a patch-robed monk; I shall break your waist!
He then asked, "Tell me, upon what does a patch-robed monk rely? After a long silence, he said, "Thirty years from now, do not let people down. He struck his staff and descended from the seat.
A monk asked Zen Master Chuanzong of Chengtian in Quanzhou, “When the great function manifests before one, and no rules or regulations remain—what then?
The Master said, “Today at Chengtian, we hoist the flag of surrender high. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, “A descendant of Linji!”
The monk shouted again. The Master struck him. The monk asked, "What is the essence of prajñā? The Master said, "Blue peaks shrouded in clouds.
The monk asked, "What is the function of prajñā? The Master said, "The moon reflected in a clear pond."
A monk asked Chan Master Mingri Shen of Chuzhou, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the teachings the same or different?
The Master said, "The reflections of water and sky merge into azure. The monk asked, "Ultimately, are they the same or different? The Master said, "The sounds of pines and bamboos share a coldness."
Chan Master Fanzong of Touzi in Shu Prefecture (then known as the "Wayman") was asked by a monk, "What is the家风 (household style) of the Wayman?
The Master said, "A *kāṣāya* wrapped around straw sandals. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Barefoot, heading for Tongcheng."
A monk asked Chan Master Xuanbao of Tiantai: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Majestic and imposing, over eight feet tall.
Chan Master Xiansheng of Mount Junshan in Yuezhou ascended the hall and said: "The Great Square has no exterior; it encompasses the ten voids. This ultimate principle..."

Formless, it is perfectly interfused throughout the three periods of time; transcending names and appearances, its wondrous essence is fully manifest. It stands far beyond past and present, its true mechanism uniquely revealed.

Grasping the dragon pearl, it reflects all things, and every phenomenon radiates its brilliance; casting the precious sword, it sweeps through the void, and the very emptiness of emptiness leaves no trace.
To hold fast is like Mahākāśyapa closing his room or Vimalakīrti stymying his words; to let go is like Shide shaking his head.
Hanshan claps his hands. "Tell me, whose realm is this? He picks up his staff and strikes once, saying:
"In the place where eyes blink and brows are raised, rely on you to examine it closely."
Huijin, the kitchen steward of Shuiyue Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture, studied under Mingjue at Xuedou. Upon hearing the master cite the story of Mount Sumeru, he attained silent realization.
One day, wishing to go and inquire further, he encountered Mingjue in the corridor of the hall. Mingjue asked, "What is your name?"
He said, "Huijin. Jue said, "Who gave you gold? He replied, "I intend to go to the abbot’s quarters in a moment to offer my thanks.
Jue said, "Right now, then? He replied, "In this place, even the Master cannot be accommodated."
The compiler, Layman Zenghui, had lived in the same quarters as Mingjue since childhood; however, upon reaching adulthood, they followed different paths.
During the Tianxi era, when the official was serving as the governor of Chizhou, the two met one day at Jingde Temple.

The official then cited the *Zhongyong* and the *Daxue*, interweaving them with passages from the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and the sayings of the Chan school to question Mingjue. Mingjue said, "This [teaching] does not even accord with the scriptural vehicles (jiao-cheng), let alone..."
"Is this not the Middle Way and the Great Learning? A scholar must understand this matter through a direct and swift path. Then, snapping his fingers once, he said, "Just realize it in this way.

The Master (Gong) attained the essential meaning beneath these words. At the beginning of the Tiānshèng era, while Gong was governing Sìmíng, he sent envoys with gifts to welcome the Master to take up the abbacy at Xuědòu.
Once the Master had arrived, Gong said, "Recently, I discussed the matter of Zhaozhou with Elder Qīng."
Regarding the story of the old woman’s examination: I do not know for certain whether there was a point where she was truly examined and seen through.
Jue said, "What did Elder Qing say? Gong said, "He went off in that way again. Jue said, "Let us let Elder Qing off with one stroke."
"Scholar, do you know that the monks of the world cannot escape this old woman’s snare? The Official said, "There is another way to approach this.
Zhaozhou, had he not exposed her, the old woman would have suffered a lifelong injustice. Jue said:
"He has seen through it. The Master laughed heartily.

Chan Master Juzhe Zuyin of Lushan Yuan Tong was a successor of Chan Master Yongrong of Yanqing. He was a native of Zizhou and surnamed Jian. From birth, he was exceptionally brilliant and outstanding.

He could recite from memory anything he read upon a single reading. At the age of eleven, he left home to become a monk; at seventeen, he passed the examination on the *Lotus Sūtra* and received ordination.

After receiving full precepts, he studied at lecture halls where many senior monks looked down upon him. Upon meeting a Chan practitioner returning from a southern journey, he was earnestly encouraged to practice meditation.

Thereupon, he traveled extensively throughout the regions of Jing and Chu, yet still attained nothing. Eventually, he reached Dongshan in Xiangzhou, where he remained for ten years. Because of this...
While reading the *Avataṃsaka-śāstra*, he attained a profound realization. Later, he traveled to Mount Lu, where his reputation for the Way grew daily. He moved from Guizong to Yuancong Temple.
When Emperor Renzong heard of his fame, at the beginning of the Huangyou era, he issued an imperial decree for him to reside at the Jingshan Jingyin Chan Monastery.

The Master claimed that due to eye ailments, he was unable to comply with the decree; by imperial order, he was required to recommend someone to take his place. He consequently recommended Da’jue Lia to respond to the summons. Upon being presented [to the Emperor],...

[The Master] replied, "Yes. When asked about the great purport of the Buddha-dharma, his response accorded with the questioner's intent. A wise teacher of the world truly knows men. A monk asked, "What is it like when a patriarchal monastery is restored?
The Master said, "The man is on Mount Pòtóu. [The monk] asked, "When power is once in one's hand? The Master then struck him.

Chan Master Huaixiang of Huiyin Monastery in Lin’an, a dharma successor of Chan Master Baizhang Ying, ascended the hall and said: “The southern mountain is high; the northern mountain is low. The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night.
The white ox climbs the tree and cannot be found; the black rooster enters the water, and everyone knows it. Now tell me, where is it?”
"Even after you have found it, what then? After a long silence, he said, "What can be done with it?
A monk asked Chan Master Yining of Huilin in Lin’an Prefecture, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said:
Lady Māyā asked, "What is it like after leaving the world? The Master said, "Prince Siddhārtha.

Chan Master Nanhua Yuan, a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Xinghua Yanqing of Qizhou, ascended the hall and said: "If you can realize it before words, you betray your entire life; if you seek it after phrases..."
To seek through expedients is entirely to deviate from the essence of the Way. Leaving aside these two paths, how was it under the gate of our Ancestors?
After a long silence, he said: "The pupils in their eyes blow wooden flutes."
Chan Master Baoshou Xingde of Shaoyang was invited to Nanhua during the winter. Addressing the assembly, he said:
"In this new winter, the new Baoshou speaks words that are the same as those of old. If you would understand the meaning of the Westward Journey, it is like a Persian merchant boarding a ship."
Chan Master Shousheng of White Tiger Mountain in Shaoyang was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "He has eyes but no nostrils.
He was a successor of Chan Master Xian of Beichen.
Master Chaoxian of Xinghua in Tanzhou ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said: "The entire Tripitaka is merely used-up toilet paper.
Discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs is but a means to deceive and alarm the common folk.
As for the gate of the patch-robed monks, not even a single point is of any use. What, then, is the matter within the gate of the patch-robed monks? After a long silence, he said:
"Better a little reality than much emptiness. [The Master] struck the incense stand and descended from his seat.
Chan Master Fachang Yiyu of Hongzhou was the son of the Lin family of Zhangzhou. In his youth, he left home and received the full precepts at Chongfu Monastery in the prefecture.
Possessing great ambition, he traveled to various places after his ordination and became renowned in the monastic community. Master Fushan Yuan...
Once, pointing [at his own practice] to others, he said, "This is the model for a student on pilgrimage. He went to visit Beichan (Nanquan Puyuan).
Beichan asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master replied, "Fuyan. Beichan asked, "How much longer is Sida’s nostrils?
The Master replied, "The same as what you saw at that time, Master. Beichan asked, "Tell me, when I saw them, how long were they? The Master replied, "Master..."
"It seems you have never been to Fuyan. Chan said, "You are just a person who parrots words. He asked again, "When you arrived, was Master Mazu well?
The Master replied, "He is well. Chan asked, "What did he say to you? The Master replied, "He told me not to be so disorderly.
Chan said, "Out of consideration for you being a newcomer, I could not beat you. The Master said, "I, too, let him off."
He was still too forward. After the tea had ended, Zen asked, "Where is your hometown? The Master said, "Zhangzhou. Zen asked, "What is Sanping doing there?
The Master said, "He speaks of Chan and speaks of the Way. Zen asked, "How old are you? The Master said, "I am the same age as a pillar.
Zen asked, "That is fine so long as there is a pillar; but if there were no pillar, how old would you be? The Master said, "Without a pillar, one."
He was not yet old. Chan said, "At midnight, release the black chicken. The Master stayed at Beichan for the longest time;

thus, the master and disciple engaged in a dynamic exchange of challenge and response, their subtle brilliance reaching its peak for the era. Later, he went to Xishan, where he took a liking to the seclusion of the Two Peaks and resided there for three years.

He first accepted the invitation of Fanchang. While the Master was at Shuangling accepting the invitation, he took his leave of the two head seats, Ying and Sheng, saying, "We have been together for three years;
there is nothing we do not know. Yet, when examined, there is no lack of leakage.
He drew a line with his staff and said, "Let this matter rest for now. As for the affairs of the Zen school, what is it? Ying replied, "Mount Sumeru is stable."

[The Master] pointed to his nostrils. The Master said, "In that case, looking down at the water from the edge of a cliff, one suddenly finds cause for great anxiety. Yingshan said, "Deep-sand [demons] glare with wide-open eyes.
The Master said, "How can it be otherwise? For the holy and the mundane there is no different path; yet there are many gates to the skillful means. Yingshan said, [silently].

as for this matter here, what is it? The Master then struck him with his palm. Ying said, "You man from Zhangzhou, do you have no sense of propriety? The Master said, "You..."

A man of keen faculties, upon hearing it mentioned, raises his eyebrows and immediately knows its place of descent. If you step forward further, it would be better to take up the staff.

"I want someone who does not understand Chan to serve as National Teacher. Ascending the hall, he said: "If you withdraw a thousand feet, I shall sprout right where you stand.

Mingzhu was such that water could not wet him and wind could not penetrate him; he was like a solid iron hammer without a hole.
But tell me, did Fachang have any way to benefit others? After a long silence, he said: "A sharp blade may cut the flesh, yet the wound eventually heals;

but words that wound others leave a resentment that never fades. He ascended the hall and said: "The spring mountains are green; the spring waters are lush. It is all but a dream in the Southern Branch of the Dream of the Red Chamber."
The first line of the dream: Carrying my staff, I stride freely out through the pine gate. Here, the fragrance of peach blossoms is rich and pervasive.
This makes me think of the old master Lingyun of old; for thirty years, I have sought him in vain. Now everyone vies to pluck the willow catkins;

"Whether it be right or wrong, set them aside all at once; for now, let us take up our staffs and depart through the triple gate. Thereupon, he trailed his staff and descended from the seat.
Zen Master Huiyin of Daochang in Anji Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "At the head of the Shaoshi ferry, a boat lies across the wild waters. Fen...

Amidst the surging waves, the oars push through the solitary smoke. Clouds and moon have no partiality; streams and mountains are not otherwise. When a single word meets the path, ten thousand *li* share the same wind.
I venture to ask you all: what is the phrase for "sharing the same wind"? After a long silence, he said: "Where are the eight thousand disciples now?
Ten thousand *li* of mountains and rivers belong to the Emperor’s house."

Chan Master Miaohui Wenyi of West Lake in Lin’an Prefecture ascended the hall and said: “Do you understand? You have already been deceived by the heat. This morning, upon rising, there was nothing to be said.
I got out of bed and put on my shoes; went to the back hall to wash my face; entered the hall to spread out my bowl and eat porridge;
after the porridge, I dozed off; when I woke from sleep, I drank tea; saw a guest and called out to them; at mealtime, I ate rice. Day after day...”
"It is just like the sun; what fault is there? Nevertheless, even so, there is another matter that makes me laugh:
'A diamond falling to the ground is but a heap of mud. He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Chan Master Zongyi of Lingquan Mountain in Chuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Fine jade is hidden within coarse stones; the lotus flower emerges from the mud.
You must know that within the realm of afflictions, if one awakens, it is itself Bodhi. *Du!* (A shout)"
Chan Master Chuhui Zhenji of Puzhao Temple in Sizhou was the son of the Zhao family of Chuzhou.

On the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked, "When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, golden lotuses sprang up from the earth. When you, Master, appear in the world, what auspicious signs are there?
The Master said, "Sweep away the snow before the gate."
A monk asked Chan Master Ning of Nanchan in Changzhou, "How do you respond to the question regarding the price of rice in Luling? The Master said, "The confession comes from the prisoner's own mouth.
Chan Master Xiaotong of Shifosi in Yuezhou ascended the hall and said: "Cold as the moon in an autumn pond, it merges with the Great Void without artifice."
The mountain is high and the flowing water is swift; where can the wandering fish find rest? A monk asked, "What is the Sudden Teaching?

The Master said, "The moon sets into the cold pond. The monk asked, "What is the Gradual Teaching? The Master said, "Clouds arise in the azure sky. The monk asked, "How is it when there is neither gradual nor sudden?
The Master said, "An eighty-year-old old woman does not speak of marriage."
Chan Master Foyun Weibai Foguo, successor to Chan Master Fayun Xiushou, ascended the hall and said: "If Li Lou had intent, the white waves would have merely overwhelmed the heavens;
if Wangxiang was without mind, the bright pearl suddenly appeared in his palm. He struck a circular gesture with his hand and called out, "Great Assembly!"
The assembly asked, "Did you see it? After a long silence, he said, "If you look, there is a share.

He ascended the hall, held up his staff to show the assembly, and said, "I, this mountain monk, have presided over this monastery for more than seventy days, yet I have never once moved this [staff]. Now, I cannot help but manifest a small measure of supernatural power as an offering to all of you.
He then struck the ground with the staff and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall again and said, "That which has passed is already past."
Do not calculate the future; attend strictly to the affairs of the present. This morning, on the fifteenth day of the first month, the bright moon is perfectly full.
The drum is beaten to invite everyone to look. It is not that the assembly does not look, but what exactly do you call "the moon"?
Do not seek it in the heavens; do not search for it in the water. The Master’s *Continued Record of the Lamp* consists of thirty fascicles and has been included in the Imperial Canon.
Chan Master Ziying Baoning of Jiankang Prefecture was a native of Qiantang. One day, he ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said:
"The sun and moon cannot match its brilliance; rivers and seas cannot compete with its depth; Mount Sumeru cannot equal its height; heaven and earth cannot rival its stability.
Even the wisdom of sages and ordinary beings cannot reach it. Now tell me, what excellence does this thing possess? After a long silence...
He said: "The joints and nodes are distinct; from birth, it has been straight and upright. When struck by ice and snow, it splits open piece by piece;
when pierced by white clouds, it receives this power. [He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it."
A monk asked Zen Master Xianyan Jingchun of Wenzhou, “Regarding the staff of Deshan and the shout of Linji, how does the Master employ them?
The Master said, “I am tired today. The monk then shouted. The Master said, “In fact, it is you who are alert.”

Chan Master Shoune of Guangjiao in Ningguo Prefecture (the principal disciple of Yuanzhao, commonly known as "Master Ne"): A monk asked, "What is the phrase that has existed eternally throughout antiquity and the present?
The Master said, "An iron ox lies across the seashore. The monk asked, "What is the true eye of a patch-robed monk?
The Master said, "Not a needle can pierce it."
Chan Master Cong of Ciji in Xingyuan Prefecture was asked by a monk, "What is the Way? The Master said, "From here to Chang’an, it is thirty-seven stages.
The monk asked, "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, "Bumping heads and knocking foreheads. Another asked, "It is not the wind moving;
it is not the banner moving. I wonder, what is it that moves? The Master said, "Lower your voice! Lower your voice! Another asked, "As for suchness..."
"What is the 'color-following' mani jewel? The Master said, "The lush green bamboo; the dense yellow flowers.
[The monk] asked, "What is the 'true color'? The Master said, "Step back! Step back! [The monk] asked, "Śākyamuni has already passed away and Maitreya has not yet been born.
I wonder who serves as the leader? The Master said, "Even an iron ox must emerge from the mud. [The monk] said, "Is this not the very point of acting for others?"
"No. The Master said, "Look closely at the previous story. He was asked, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? The Master said, "The iron ox of Shanzhou.
Entering the hall, he said, "The scriptures of the Three Vehicles are not the true exposition; pointing directly to one's own mind is not yet the ultimate principle.

If there are gentlemen of superior capacity who have penetrated the mind, men of lofty character who have cast off all constraints, come forth and meet me! Thereupon, he looked around at the assembly.
He said, "Rest. He ascended the hall and said: "Throughout the day, you strive busily for one another, acting exactly like someone trying to pull an ox up a wall.

Great assembly, why do you thus greedily pursue life, wandering about in such petty toil? If you call out but cannot turn back your heads, what can be done? He ascended the hall again and said: "One is simply one; two is simply two.
When the essential passageway is firmly secured, where can there be any breath to escape? He took up his staff and said: "That person has no sores of their own."
"Do not harm it. *A single strike of the mallet.* He descended from the seat.
Chan Master Tonghui Gui of Baizhao Mountain in Anzhou ascended the hall and said: "Fortunately, we have met with this auspicious occasion; one must gather rare insights."

Now that you have encountered this mountain of treasure, do not leave empty-handed. Do not wait for some other time or another day to speak such great words from behind a door or in the corner of a wall.
From the exhaustion of heaven and earth to the continuity of past and present, it is simply this one self-nature of yours.
Within this, there is nothing else. All of you, every day when walking, walk upon it; when lying down, lie upon it; when sitting, [sit upon it].

At times he sits in meditation; when responding in speech, his words fill his mouth. Even down to the raising of eyebrows and twinkling of eyes, the expression of anger and joy, love and hate, or remaining in silent stillness and playful activity, there has never been an interruption.
For what reason, then, do you refuse to accept this and simply rest within yourself?

It is because for immeasurable kalpas, the weight of your passionate desires has been heavy and the path of birth and death has been long; you have turned your back on awakening and united with the dust of the senses. Yourself—
They give rise to doubt and confusion. It is like a bird flying in the sky, not knowing that the sky is its home; or a fish swimming in water, forgetting that water is its very life.
How can they restrain themselves and instead ask others for answers? This is much like holding a bowl of rice while claiming hunger, or crying out for thirst while standing at the riverbank.
If you all wish to attain rest, each of you must settle your spirits right where you stand and focus with single-mindedness.

Turning the light back upon itself, one suddenly illuminates oneself. How is this different from the crimson sun moving alone and impartially in the sky, or the bright pearl on a platter turning of its own accord without being pushed?
Nevertheless, although it is thus, this is only for the sake of beginners; as for the higher mechanism, they have not yet stepped upon it.
Furthermore, tell me: what is this "upward-moving mechanism"? After a long silence, he said: "Looking up at the sky, one does not see the sky.
Chan Master Jingming Fayin of Chang'an, Luzhou, ascended the hall and said: "In the heavens the moon is full; in the human world it is half-moon."

"Seven or eight" is a number; the reality, however, is difficult to calculate. Setting aside for now the failure to distinguish between the hidden and the manifest, when black and white have not yet been distinguished, how do you speak this one phrase?
After a long silence, he said: "Meeting within the autumn colors, conversing together in the midst of the bright moon. He then ascended the hall.
The wondrous secret of the Patriarchs has nothing else to be said; even with a beak like a nail and a tongue of iron, one cannot avoid turning cleverness into clumsiness.
Vimalakīrti has already leaked the celestial mechanism.
A monk asked Chan Master Shouchu of Fuyan on Mount Fucha, "What is the samādhi of utilization?

The Master said, "Picking up the spoon and setting down the chopsticks. The monk asked, "What is the single direct path? The Master said, "It cannot be stepped upon. The monk asked, "Once it has been stepped upon, what then?
The Master said, "The four quarters and eight directions. He then said, "If one discusses this matter, to let it go is Caoxi..."
On the road, the moon is white and the wind is clear. If you hold fast, the clouds are gathered and the mists are rolled up before the peak of Shaoshi.
Such discourse has already wandered into many paths; it is only through the resonance of a single thought that one may truly believe this is not obtained from another.
The assembly, tell me: from what place is it obtained? After a long silence, he said: "The flowing water originally resides in the sea; the setting moon does not leave the sky. (End)

The hall is the characteristic of nature; the single expanse of clear sky is the nature of characteristics. When a thousand waves rise in competition, if one penetrates the source, the clear current flows without obstruction.
Thus, by raising a single thought, the dharma-gates as numerous as dust motes and sands are suddenly revealed;
by grasping a single hair, the realms of boundless lands are simultaneously manifested. But tell me, where are Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra? Going downhill—do not...
"Go! A favorable opportunity is difficult to encounter. He then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Rende Shanren of Dingzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Venerable Immovable One? The Master said, "Coming in thousands, going in tens of thousands.
The monk said, "If that is so, then one's heels do not even touch the ground. The Master said, "It is actually you who understand this. He ascended the hall and addressed the assembly:
"The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes discrimination. Simply do not harbor hatred or attachment, and all will be transparently clear. I, this mountain monk, am not like that.
The Ultimate Way is most difficult; it requires discrimination. If there were no hatred or attachment, how could one perceive clarity?"
Chan Master Yongmin of Shengshou Xiangji Monastery in Lizhou ascended the hall and said: "The wooden horse breaks through the path of a thousand riders;
the iron ox penetrates ten thousand layers of barriers. Where are the wooden horse and the iron ox right now? After a long silence, he said:
"Startled from the evening sky, a flight of wild geese on the sand takes off in two or three rows, slanting away toward the sea gate."
Chan Master Ruixiangzi of Ruizhou ascended the hall and, looking over the assembly, said: "As a patriarch of our school, one must take up the guiding thread wherever one is.
Responding to stimuli through question and answer, one employs killing or giving life as the occasion demands. With the eye of the mind refined and sharp, how can there be room for demons?
If you seek realization from the staff or accept it under a shout, you bury the ancestral style and bring shame upon those who came before. This is the path of turning back."
Do not hesitate. With a single breath not yet returned, one is still the same as a dead man.
O Great Assembly, even if you reach this state, it is still merely words buried within; there is as yet no path of liberation. I dare ask you all:
what is this path of penetration and liberation? Is there anyone who can speak of it? If there is none, this mountain monk cannot help but speak for you.
He broke [the silence]. After a long while, he said: "The jade leaves the mountain peak of Jing, its cold radiance stirring; the sword emerges from Fengcheng, its purple vapor spanning the sky.
Chan Master Congyi of Luzhou Zhenkong ascended the hall. "The mirror of the mind is a clear reflector, free of obstruction.
He then picked up his staff and said: "To call this 'staff' is an obstruction; not to call it 'staff' is also an obstruction. To depart from..."
Beyond this, how is it ultimately? Do you wish to understand? Is there obstruction or not? Who is there to confront it? The great earth, mountains, and rivers are utterly pulverized into nothingness.
Chan Master Guang of Qianming on Fenghuang Mountain in Xiangzhou ascended the hall and said: "The sun rises from the east; the moon sets in the west.
Coming and going as swift as a shuttle, they urge us toward white bones. This mountain monk has a dharma that serves as a technique for preserving life:
birth and death do not interfere with it; it shatters the den of the spirit. *Du! Du!* What thing is this? It is not the multitude."
"Born, yet not a Buddha. Examine!
This was Zen Master Zhi-ming Fo-hui of Yongxing Huayan Temple in Dongjing, a successor of Zen Master Chong of Hui-lin, whose secular surname was Shi of Changzhou. He ascended the hall and said:
If we discuss this matter: in the heavens, it arrays the myriad phenomena and manifests them all at once; on the earth, it moves through the four seasons and brings forth growth;

in humans, it appears and disappears, rolls up and unfurls, and the six sense-faculties function interchangeably. But tell me, as for that which is upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff—how is it?
After a long silence, he struck the ground once and said: “It is manifest in the high; it is manifest in the low.”
Chan Master Zhenzhou Yongtai Zhihang ascended the hall and said: "To disperse [the spirit] into qi is the dilution of the Way; to adapt to change is the corruption of the Dharma.
The numinous mechanism is never obscured, spanning from antiquity to the present. When the great function manifests before one, what can be gained and what can be lost?
Even so, if you suddenly encounter an unperforated iron hammer, how will you explain it? He then brandished his staff.

He said, "It has been pierced through. He ascended the hall and said: "The dragon soars through the azure heavens, its transformations beyond measure; the phoenix flies through the blue sky, who knows its traces?
When it is time to go, it goes, without departing from the hundreds of thousands of samādhis; when it is time to stop, it stops, never forgetting the myriad phenomena of the universe.
Therefore it is said: 'It cannot be grasped, it cannot be relinquished; within that which cannot be obtained, it is simply obtained. And yet—"
"What have you attained? After a long silence, he said, "Do not engage in false imaginings.
A monk from the Shousheng Temple in Jiangyin County asked, "Setting aside both the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings, how can one quickly attain Buddhahood?
The Master said, "That which has attainment is ultimately not it; that which is the Buddha is also not the True One."
A monk hesitated to respond. The Master rebuked him, saying, "What was the meaning of that phrase?
Chan Master Dao-rong Jue-yin of Xuedou in Mingzhou, a successor of Chan Master Chang-lu Fu, was born into the Chen family of the local district. A monk asked: "When Hanshan meets..."
"When you pick it up, what is it like? The Master said, "Raising an eyebrow, a flash of lightning flies. The monk asked, "What else is there?
The Master said, "Opening the mouth, a ray of light is emitted. The monk asked, "What is the path that leads upward? The Master said, "Seven, six, eight."
Chan Master Cijue Zongze of Changlu in Zhenzhou was the son of the Sun family of Luozhou. A monk asked, "When Bodhidharma faced the wall, what was the principle behind this?
The Master remained silent for a long time. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Today, I have been caught by this monk’s question."
He was left speechless. He ascended the hall and said: "Winter has passed; it is the hundred-and-fifth day since the Cold Food Festival. On the path that brings life, there are countless dead.
They thrust their heads into thorny thickets, imagining this to be the suffering of sentient beings. As for the matter of visiting graves: they merely add earth to a heap of bones.
Only those who have left the household life do not tread upon the path of non-arising. Tell me, assembly: toward what destination do they head?"
"Go! Do you understand? To the South, Tiantai; to the North, Wutai. Enter. Ascending the hall, he said: "In New Ra (Silla), there is no other secret instruction.
When speaking, one does not avoid having one's tongue cut out. But if one can achieve the correspondence of mind and mouth, one will never fully exhaust its utility throughout a lifetime.
Now tell me, what is the phrase for the correspondence of mind and mouth? After a long silence, he said: "A scorched brick strikes through the ice to the very bottom. "Enter. A monk asked:
"When the six gates have not yet ceased [their activity], how is it? The Master said, "Incense is burned within the nostrils.
[The student] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "A drum is beaten within the ears. [The student] asked, "What is the merit of meritless merit?

The Master said, "The clay ox does not move its feet; there is no fallow field under heaven. [The student] said, "In that case, then merit is not bestowed in vain. The Master said, "Although it is vast..."
Even those with great supernormal powers cannot avoid receiving a painful blow from him. Entering the hall, he said: "Though gold dust is precious, when it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract.
Once the gold dust is removed, where is the eye? If you think like this, you have not yet emerged from the thicket of thorns;

to seek realization at the tip of the staff or to take responsibility under a shout is precisely to remain within the den of Jingu Peak. Entering the hall, he said: "Beyond the tower, the color of the Purple Gold Mountain..."
Xiu: "Before the gate, the sound of the nectar-water is cold; beneath the shade of the ancient locust tree, amidst the clear breeze, let me point it out once more for you all.
He picks up his staff and says, "Do you see? He strikes the incense table and says, "Do you hear?

He leans the staff against the wall and says, "If the eyes and ears are unobstructed, one is sufficient wherever one is; the sound of the water and the colors of the mountains flow on of their own accord."
Chan Master Huiri Zhijue Guangdeng of Pingjiang Prefecture was the son of the Mei family of that same district. He ascended the hall and, after a long silence, said:
"Rest! Rest! Rest! All in vain, drifting aimlessly. The fishing rod remains firmly in hand; the fish are cold and will not swallow the hook. With a shout, he struck.
Descend from your seat.

Chan Master Linquan Ziling of Jia Shan in Lishui was a successor of Chan Master Furu Cai of the Buddha-Sun lineage. He was the son of the Zhou family of Changzhou. A monk asked: "The golden rooster pecks..."
Breaking through the lapis lazuli shell, the jade hare pushes open the gates of the azure sea. This is but the light and shadow of the human world;
what is the pivot of the Patriarch? The Master said, "A needle cannot pierce it. The monk asked, "How would you speak of it before even a trace has arisen?
The Master raised his whisk. The monk asked, "How should one comprehend this? The Master said, "Gazing upward with bared brows toward the rising sun."

Question: "What was it like before the primordial chaos had divided? The Master said: "The spring breeze blows gently. Question: "What was it like after it divided? The Master said: "The spring days linger slowly. Question:
"Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said: "There are three hundred and sixty days in a year. He ascended the hall.
After a long silence, he looked at the assembly and said: "The golden crow runs through the moon; who says there is not a single thing?"
"On the eastern wall of Zhaozhou hangs a large gourd. *Chan!*" He ascended the hall; after a long silence, he drew a circle and said, "The five thousand-plus scrolls cannot fully explain it;
the Buddhas of the three periods have failed to praise it sufficiently. This makes one recall the oil-seller.
He hurriedly descended from the rope-seat and stood there. *Chan!* He ascended the hall; he then forgot all contrivances and maintained silence. Already...
Having been preempted by Jin-su, you intended to deploy the sharp edge of your verbal prowess, yet you fell behind Gautama.
Apart from these two paths, what is the single way for a patch-robed monk to break through and escape? After a long silence, he said: "It is truly laughable where Nanquan brought it up:
the sickle for cutting thatch grass is all bent and curved. *Chan.*
Chan Master Qingman of Yuanfeng Monastery in Weizhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Tianbo Yuan, was the son of the Tian family of Cangzhou. A monk asked: "What is the Buddha?"
The Master said, "The sky is cold and the earth is freezing. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "I do not speak of it.
The monk asked, "Why do you not speak of it? The Master said, "The Way is but a mundane name. He ascended the hall and said, "Without divergent thoughts, listen attentively, listen attentively!
Yesterday was cold; today is cold. Shake up your spirit and exert yourself to look! Exert yourself to look! Looking and looking, one becomes increasingly dull-witted."
Do not be careless. Look! Examine! Entering the hall, he said: "That which is fit to be a beam becomes a beam; that which is fit to be a pillar becomes a pillar.
A sharp-witted monk will immediately know where it falls. He suddenly picked up his staff and said, "Do you know what this is fit to be?
He struck the incense stand once and said, "Do not say it has no use. He struck it again and said, "Examine!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Look, look! The Elder Woodworker in the hall was slapped by the Holy Monk and went to see the Rector, only to be slapped twice by him.
The pillar laughed aloud. Seeing this injustice on the road at Yuangfeng, I shall right it for you.
He took up his staff and said, "Come, come! Even though he is the Holy Monk, he must still receive a blow of the staff."

He struck the incense stand and descended from his seat. On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and said: "I recall in the past, when I lived in the mountains and was without grain, I had a verse which I shall now present to the assembly:
'Hungry, I eat the leaves of pines and cypresses; thirsty, I drink the spring water in the ravine. Having finished gazing at the green bamboo, I sleep soundly in my robes.
O Assembly, I have further thoughts from the mountains to speak for you: this year’s year is last year’s year. He then ascended the hall.
Matters concerning the edge of a sword can only be mastered by those who are "Han-men" (true men) upon the edge of a sword.

There are certain types of people, seekers of fame and profit, who act as teachers to gods and humans while hanging the head of a sheep to sell dog meat; they ruin the beginners and latecomers, and extinguish the great principles of the ancient sages.
When you all hear of such matters, do your hearts not turn cold? Because of this, they delude and mislead sentient beings, causing them to fall into the Avīci Hell and suffer.

"Alas! What suffering! To seek pleasure for a single lifetime and receive the remaining calamities of ten thousand kalpas—what kind of desperate urgency is this? You have come to be a disciple of the Śākya, yet you act thus!
He shouted, "A deaf man merely tilting his ear! and then descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he gave a shout and said, "It is not the Way; it is not Chan.
Whenever the third or fifth night arrives, the bright moon is at its full perfection. *Chan!* Whenever the Master saw a monk, he would...
He said, "Buddha-dharma and worldly dharma are like flowers in the sky seen by those with eye disease. A monk asked, "What is it like when the cataract is cleared away and the flowers vanish?
The Master said, "I took you for someone who was quick-witted and sharp."
A monk asked Chan Master Faben of Dinghui Monastery in Qingzhou, "When ancients reached this point, why did they fold their hands and surrender?
The Master said, "It was fitting that it should be so. The monk asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "Sleeping at night and walking during the day."
Zen Master Shansheng Zhenwu of the Western Capital ascended the hall. To raise the sound while seeking to stop the resonance, one does not realize that sound is the root of resonance.

To play with the shadow while fleeing from the form, one does not realize that the form is the source of the shadow. To inquire about the Dharma by means of the Dharma, one does not realize that the Dharma is fundamentally not-dharma.
To transmit mind by means of mind, yet not to know that the mind is fundamentally without mind. When the mind is fundamentally without mind, one knows the mind is like an illusion;

one realizes that dharmas and non-dharmas are as dreams. Knowing that dharmas and the mind are not real, do not vainly pursue them. They are but dreams, illusions, and empty flowers—what need is there to grasp at them?
Arriving here, the Buddhas of the three periods of time, the entire Great Canon, the words and phrases of the patriarchs, and all the elder masters under heaven...
The Master’s spreading of the "wisteria vines" renders all else useless. Why? For it is said: "Peace itself was brought about by the generals;
yet the generals are not permitted to witness that peace."
Chan Master Tánzhèn Zhēnjiè of Yùwáng Monastery in Míngzhōu, successor to Chan Master Hóng of Ruìyán, ascended the hall and said: "Today the mouth of the cloth bag is opened;
is there anyone here who wishes to buy or sell? At that time, a monk came forward and said, "There is. The Master said, "Neither making it expensive nor making it cheap—how would you do it?"
He offered a price for his life, but the monks remained silent. The Master said, "The old monk has lost out.
Chan Master Chengfu Deng of Wangwu Mountain in Shuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Xiqian of Qixian, ascended the hall and said: "Heaven cannot cover him; earth cannot support him."
"A single room has no private space; where is there that is not included? O Great Assembly! Even if you understand it in this way, it is still a ghost playing with its own spirit.
How can one speak of the principle of 'ever-present'? After a long silence, he said: "The golden wind arose last night; everywhere the ground is covered in yellow chrysanthemums."

The assembly’s leader, Jingzhong, was the Dharma heir of Chan Master Guangdeng Weizhan of Zhaoji Temple in the Western Capital; he was a native of Jiahe. A monk asked, "What is the patriarchal style of the Master?
The Master said, "Autumn winds scatter yellow leaves; distant peaks see white clouds return. The monk said, "This is specifically for the sake of its circulation."
The Master said, "How do you express it right now? The monk then gave a shout. The Master then struck him. He ascended the hall and said: "Biased or not biased? Correct or not correct?
That matter has never been easy to compare. With wind and rain filling the heavens, one’s very bones and hair grow cold.

Why need one further enter the *nāga-samādhi*? He planted his staff and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall and said: "The six sense-objects are not evil; they are identical to perfect enlightenment. He struck the horse.
Who is that fair-faced young man from such-and-such a house? Piercing through flowers and breaking willows, he hangs his kerchief at the corner of his cap.

Last night, he was drunk to the point of oblivion atop the Bright Moon Tower; calling for the dice, he gambled away his golden mansion. With falcons on his arms and hounds running before him, he does not even return home.

The women with蛾眉 (arched brows) and皓齒 (brilliant teeth) are powerless to scold him. How many can truly understand this heart? Those with yellow heads and blue eyes do not recognize it. *Loro lori!* Clapping hands.
One bow. Descend from the seat.
Dharma Successor of Chan Master Faying Ben of the thirteenth generation under Qingyuan.
Chan Master Chuming Baoyin of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an, a member of the Zhang family from the Hundred Yue region, ascended the hall and said:
"The Mind-Seal of the Patriarchs is neither long nor short, neither square nor round, neither internal nor external, nor is it in between. Now I ask the assembly:
what form does it definitely take? He held up his staff and said, "Do you see? Ancient seal-script, not forming characters; it flies—"

Silk and difficulty are of the same substance; from the very beginning, they have been clearly distinct. Why must you again insist on making them so? [He] struck the meditation seat and descended from his position.
