Chan Master Fǎhǎi of Xīzhú Monastery in Píngjiāng Prefecture was the paternal aunt of Lǚ Jiāzhī, whose courtesy name was Bǎowén.

She first studied under Master Fǎyún Xiù and later received the transmission of the Dharma from Mǎfǎ Zhēn. Although several renowned scholars repeatedly entreated her to appear in the world for the sake of others, she did not comply.
Jian did not comply. On the day of his passing, he spoke a verse, saying: "Upon the frosty sky, clouds and mist entwine; The mountain moon shines with a cold luster.
At night, I received news from my native land; At dawn, the traveler does not know. When morning came, he sat upright and passed away.

Chan Master Guàn of Zishòu in Shòuzhōu, a successor of Chan Master Yóng of Tóuzi, ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said, "To disperse just like this would already be a tangle of complications;
if you continue to chatter on, what benefit would there be? He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.
A monk asked Zen Master Jiang of Bai Ma Chong Shou in the Western Capital: "I know that you have long harbored a treasure within your bag;

today, as you open the hall, I beg to borrow it for a moment. The Master said, "I do not lend it. The monk asked, "Why do you not lend it? The Master replied, "To sell gold, one must be a buyer of gold."
A monk asked Zen Master Xiangyan Zhizhe Haiyin of Dengzhou: "The Dharma-thunder has already resounded and the field for selecting the Buddha has opened;

since you do not obscure the fundamental vehicle, I pray that you will point directly to it. The Master said: "On the third day of the third month, a thousand flowers and ten thousand blossoms unfold."

[The official] said, "Throughout heaven and across the earth, all receive the power of your grace; the immortal blossoms in the garden of awakening have opened overnight. The Master said, "Be careful not to follow after him.
He then said, "Commissioner of the Ministry of Personnel, today you have commanded this mountain monk to open the hall to offer prayers for the Emperor and to continue the ancestral lamp.
But how is the ancestral lamp to be continued? Have you not seen what the ancients said: 'The bells and drums resound through the six streets'?"
*Dong!* Right here, in this world spread with gold, where the ponds grow lotuses and the courtyards grow cypresses—what further dharma could one use to expound the True Principle?

To speak in such a manner is also because there is no other way. Should someone who cannot bear it from the sidelines come forth, pull the mountain monk down from his meditation seat, and give him a severe beating, I would grant that he is a monk of genuine caliber. If not...
He possesses the skillful hands and feet of a true master. One must not act with haste or negligence.

If you fail to examine the ground beneath your own feet until it is found unstable and your head has nowhere to go, you will surely have to take a blow from the handle of Xiangyan’s mattock—do not say I did not warn you.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The treasure-store of my house is not held in stinginess; it is presented face-to-face, yet few recognize it. It illuminates the present and shines upon antiquity, its essence—"
When it is perfectly round, its light shines upon earth and heaven, brilliant and crimson. What makes the beautiful jade of Mount Jing precious?
It cannot compare to the bright pearl of Hezhou. Ask who would dare to offer a price for it: the Persian’s nostrils are three feet long! *Du!* (A shout of realization).
The layman Prime Minister Fu Bi, whose courtesy name was Yanguo, followed the exhortations of his father, the Duke Qingxian, and strove day and night to advance in this Way.
Hearing that Chan Master Yong was presiding at Touzi and that his Dharma assembly was preeminent throughout the Huaidian region, he went there to resolve his doubts.
It happened that Yong was ascending the seat for the assembly; seeing his gaze and movements like those of an elephant-king turning in a circle, the Prime Minister gained a subtle realization.
Adopting the etiquette of a disciple, he hurried to the master’s quarters. He instructed an attendant to request admittance into the inner room.
As soon as Zhenrong saw him, he said, "The Excellency has already entered; Fu Bi is still outside. Upon hearing this, Gong broke into a sweat that soaked his back, and he attained great awakening.

He subsequently sent a verse to Yuanzhao Ben, saying: "Upon one sight of Master Zhenrong, my realization entered deeply; Through successive conditions, I have transmitted the heart-mind of the Elder Teacher."

To the southeast, one might vainly speak of the distance of mountains and rivers, yet here the eyes face the Lingguang and Miaoyin [Pagodas]. Later, he submitted a memorial requesting the posthumous title of Master Yong for [Master] Yong.
When Yong ascended the hall to express his gratitude, he said: "That one occasion of my being misled by him led me to follow error with error. The Duke composed a verse in praise, which says:
"Ten thousand trees and a thousand flowers are about to flourish, Yet the Sleeping Dragon has not yet emerged from the vast ocean. The crimson clouds..."
Colored mists manifest auspicious omens; as before, the Southern Mountain is a single hue of green.
Chan Master Wenzhao of Miaozhan Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture—a successor to Chan Master Shuiganlu—was a native of Wenling. She ascended the hall and said: "The wondrous source is unmoving."

What does this wondrous essence rely upon? This vivid, solitary luminosity—whose radiance is it? If you say it is the True Suchness or the Ultimate Reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), it is much like gouging a sore into healthy flesh.
To further deliberate upon the "Patriarchal Meaning" is precisely to lose one's head while chasing its reflection.
Let us set aside the old barbarian’s forty-nine years of preaching dreams; in the Sangha hall, the Elder Kauṇḍinya will now speak for all of you.
"Awakened ground—do you still remember it? After a long silence, he said, "Take care of your eyebrows.
Chan Master Chuyou of Wannian in Taizhou, a successor of Chan Master Ruiyan Ju, ascended the hall and said: "Where the ancient sages could not reach, the common folk have just arrived."
Once ordinary beings have arrived, even the former sages do not know it. Whether they have arrived or not, whether they know it or not—leave all of this aside at one side.
It is just like when a monk asked Qianfeng, "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions all share the single path to the gate of Nirvāṇa;
I wonder where the head of that path lies? Qianfeng took his staff, drew a line, and said, "It is right here. Now tell me, what about this old man?
How far apart are these former sages and the common run of people? "The tiger of Nanshan bites the stone sheep"—one must discern life and death within this very moment.
[This concludes the section on] Chan Master Guangling Zu, a Dharma heir.
A monk asked Chan Master Huaiyi of Xianyan in Jingyun, Chuzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Why do you trouble yourself?
The monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "You have already spoken it. The monk asked, "Is there anything further beyond this?"
The Master said, "No. [The monk] said, "In that case, it is a small emergence meeting a great encounter. The Master said, "I only fear it is not so.
[The monk] said, "It is indeed so. The Master said, "And yet, it goes on just like this."
Chan Master Tichun of Gushan in Fuzhou, successor to Chan Master Jingyin Yue, ascended the hall and said: "Yi You’s bow and arrows were not for shooting at field frogs."
Mr. Ren’s silken line must be cast into the vast ocean. When launched, it pierces the willow and hits the mark; when caught, it is a long whale or a giant tortoise.
Once a single arrow has entered the deep city, how could a long pole be used to fish in shallow water? Is there anyone here now who can swallow the hook or bite the barb?
If not, this mountain monk will roll up the line and break the bow and arrows. [He throws down his staff and descends.]

[The Master] took his seat. Zen Master Changqing Yingyuan of Pingjiang in Yuezhou, successor to Zen Master Qianming Jue, ascended the hall and said: "The cold air is about to fade and spring has arrived. No...
Seeking the lost ox, it leaps and bounds everywhere; it strikes the nostrils of Kunlun. It topples Sumeru, turning it into refuse.
The cowherd boy has finished his whipping; he no longer blows the holeless flute. Clapping his hands, he laughs "he-he. Go back! Go back!
He lies down, clothes and all, in the depths of the misty clouds. After a long silence, he said: "Be careful not to fall asleep!"

Chan Master Huishen Cishou of Hui-lin in Dongjing was a dharma successor of Chan Master Changlu Xing. He was the son of the Xia family of Shouchun Fu. At his birth, an auspicious light appeared in the house;
Chan Master Wenshu Jian saw it from afar and suspected it was a fire. When dawn arrived, he learned that the master had just been born and went to visit him.
Whenever the Master saw Huijian, he would smile. When his mother permitted him to leave the household life, at the age of fourteen, he severed his worldly attachments and shaved his head.
Four years later, he went abroad to seek the Way, relying upon Jingzhao at Zisheng Monastery in Jiahe.

Jingzhao recounted the karmic occasion of Liangsui meeting Magu and asked, "What is the place where Liangsui attained understanding? The Master immediately realized it with deep clarity. He subsequently left to reside at Zifuku, until his sandals were worn out.
Outside, Chan Master Fajian Qin of Jiangshan arrived while the master was out on his alms rounds. After the tea ceremony concluded, the master led him on a tour of the quarters.
Upon reaching the "Thousand-Man Street" (Qianren Jiefang), Fajian asked, "Since this is the 'Thousand-Man Street,' why is there only one person here? The master replied:
"Better a little reality than much emptiness. Jie said, "Is that so? The Master was abashed. At that time, the court converted Zifu Temple into a Shenxiao Palace;
consequently, the Master left for Jiangshan, leaving behind Xian'an Chen to seek further instruction. Jie said, "Zifu knew this sort of matter and simply let it go.
The Master said, "I am truly not yet at ease. I hope you, Reverend, will not treat me as an outsider. Jie then cited the story of the "Borrowed Woman."

Regarding the "Discourse on the Departed Soul," he examined it repeatedly until his doubts and obstructions were completely cleared away. He presented a verse, saying: "It is merely the place where I have always walked;
To casually mention it is already a source of confusion. Last night a gale arose all at once; How many peach blossoms did it blow down?
Jian struck the desk and said, "Is this not the living meaning of the Patriarchs? Shortly thereafter, he was summoned by imperial decree to reside [at a monastery].
At Mount Jiao, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A yellow face is not a gilded mask. The monk asked, "What is the matter beyond the Buddha?
The Master said, "One arrow, one lotus. The monk prostrated, and the Master snapped his fingers three times.
A monk asked, "When one knows the Way but cannot speak it, what then? The Master said, "A mute man eating honey. The monk asked, "When one can speak the Way but does not know it, what then?
The Master said, "A parrot calling out to people. The monk bowed, and the Master rebuked him, saying, "You mere messenger!"
Question: "What kind of person is not swallowed by impermanence? The Master said: "I only fear that he has no place for the mouth to descend upon. [The questioner] said:

"If that is so, then with a single thought penetrating the profound mystery, the three *śi* demons lose their craftiness. The Master said: "You have a 'single thought'; you will certainly be swallowed by it. [The questioner] said:
"What about when there is not a single thought? The Master said: "I have caught you, *āyuṣmat*. [He] ascended the hall and said: "The Ancients..."

“This is the Way. Endurance, endurance—through this, the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time reach their ultimate end. Abundance, abundance—through this, ten thousand calamities and a thousand misfortunes are extinguished.
Silence, silence—through this, unsurpassed Bodhi is attained. The Master said: “If you understand these three kinds of words, you are a fine fellow who is not easily satisfied.
This mountain monk simply takes an ox from one person and returns a horse to another; he splashes water and spits upon others.”
[The Master] stuck out his tongue and scolded them. Holding up his staff, he said: "Come forth! Come forth! He ascended the hall and said: "From which mountain does the cloud arise?
From what ravine does the wind spring? What a fine point of entry! Yet few travel the official road. He ascended the hall and said: "It is not an object, nor is it the mind;
even when called 'Buddha,' it sinks into oblivion. Within this, there is fundamentally no hierarchy; one must strictly avoid [falling into the trap of] 'no hierarchy.'"
To search within the stages is to fail to search at all; the error remains profound. Only by smashing Yunmen’s rice-bag can one finally realize that red earth is gold. *Tu!*
Chan Master Ruigui of Wanshou Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture was born into the Wei clan of Jianning. On the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked, "What is the scenery of the Suzhou Terrace?
The Master said, "The mountains stretch out, majestic like lions; the waters connect with the clear Lake Tai. The monk asked, "Who is the person within this scenery?
The Master said, "After the imperial regalia of the Great Song, before the rites and music of the Great Zhou. Whenever the Master saw...
The monk inevitably asked, "How have you been lately? As the monk was about to respond, [the Master] struck him on the back and said, "Inconceivable.
When he was about to pass away, the assembly gathered; he spoke again, "Inconceivable," and then passed away with his palms joined.
The Chan Master Tianyi Ruzhe of Yuezhou’s lineage and native place are unknown. After retiring from his monastic seat, he resided at Wanshou Monastery in Pingjiang.
He was indiscriminate in what he ate and drank, and many people mocked him. Once, someone questioned him regarding the koan of calling out "Host" at Ruiyan.
The Master replied with a verse, saying: "Ruian constantly calls out to the 'Lord of the House,' Suddenly emerging from the highest peak of Mount Sumeru.
The great earth is overturned, yet there is no place to find him; A single song of the flute and lute resounds within the painted pavilion. One day he said, "I am going.
He ordered his bamboo sedan chair to be wiped clean, then wrote a verse to inform the assembly: "The Way is found in its application; it is applied in the moment of death."
At that time, people were preoccupied only with seeking pleasure and refused to study the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*).

Having recounted his past inquiries and exhorting the assembly to advance in their practice, he suddenly raised his fist and said, "Tell me, everyone, where does this fall? The assembly was speechless.
The Master struck the table once and said, "I entrust it all at once to the autumn wind," and then entered his sedan chair, sitting upright.
[The Record of] Master Zhizhe Fhuan of Wuzhou. Entering the Hall: "To strike the profound pivot, one must possess integrity and be utterly resolute;
only those who can cut through nails and sever iron—those who are starkly unbending—will succeed. If you are one who hides behind a blade or avoids it..."
"An arrow! Those who are merely mediocre will find this immediately within their reach. [The Master] struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.
A monk asked Zen Master Zhinan Miaokong of Jingshan in Lin’an Prefecture, "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "Sitting for too long leads to fatigue. The monk asked, "And after he saw him? The Master said, "It does not hinder my walking eastward."
Traveling westward:

Chan Master Jue Ran Baoyue of Ba’en Monastery in Changzhou, a successor of Chan Master Huizong of Jinshan and a native of the Zheng family of Yuezhou, ascended the hall and said: "Students have no..."
Matters are empty of substance; one must seek wondrous enlightenment. To abandon wondrous enlightenment and merely engage in empty talk is like chasing after a foul odor.
Nevertheless, though this is so, those who have pierced their ears are rare, while those who mark the boat are many.
One day he said to the assembly, "Worldly conditions are easily defiled, but the work of the Way is difficult to accomplish. You all must exert yourselves. Having finished speaking, he passed away.

Chan Master Shaoxian of Zhiye Monastery in Wuzhou was a successor of Chan Master Fayun. He was a native of Tanzhou. Entering the hall, he said: "The sense faculties and their objects share the same source; bondage and liberation are non-dual.
Without moving so much as a hair’s breadth, one sports throughout the ten directions. Though the dog of Zihu is fierce, how can it compare to the [lion of] the South Mountain?"
Huangbo said, "Everyone, look beneath your feet! He then ascended the hall and said: "It cannot be gathered into a ball, nor can it be dispersed by stirring;
it does not dry in the sun, nor does it rot when soaked in water. It hangs casually within the great void, left to the cold gaze of onlookers."
Chan Master Zhongyi of Fusheng Monastery on Mount Mian in Yizhou ascended the hall and said: “One, two, three, four, five. Ascending the hall, the Dharma drum is struck.
Crowds gather and come forward together; one by one, we face each other. Autumn colors fill the empty courtyard;
autumn winds stir the universe. If you ask further about the Zen of the Patriarchs—Xuefeng went to Touzi. *Du!* (A shout)”
A monk asked Zen Master Huihai Yueyin of Huilin Temple in Tokyo: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style do you succeed? The Master said:
"A jade pavilion upon a golden ground. The monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said: "In the third month, the people of Luoyang wear flowers. He ascended the hall and said: "Upon the ground of pure gold, those with true eyes are not yet willing to settle;
within the thicket of brambles, the one who abides in his own fundamental nature cannot be detained.

As for departing from these two paths, what is the place where a patch-robed monk walks? After a long silence, he said: "Raising one's head amidst the mist and haze, one sees the home in its dim outlines."
Shan ascended the hall. Looking over the assembly, he struck the meditation seat once and said, "This briefly expresses that it is not empty.
He then descended from the seat. Chan Master Yuan of Jianlong in Yangzhou was the son of the Xia family of Gusu. Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "Buying a hat to fit the head;
following a pattern to draw the likeness. Let the rustic old man frown as he pleases; Master Zhi was no idle monk."
[The Master] leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Weishang of Guangfu Monastery in Lin’an, a successor of Chan Master Baoning Ying, first visited Jueyin, who asked him: "Nanquan slaughtered the cat."

"Boy," [Nanquan] said, "what is your meaning? Baizhang replied, "It must be Nanquan who can achieve this. Nanquan then cross-examined him with his previous words, but the Master was unable to respond.
Upon returning to the Sangha Hall, he suddenly attained great enlightenment and said, "The ancients said, 'From this day forward, I shall no longer doubt the tongues of the old monks of the world.
Now I truly believe it. He then composed a verse and presented it to Nanquan, saying: "It must be Nanquan."
The first person: unaware and unawakened, a spike drives straight into his head. If there were no blue or white eyes before one's face, it would still be like a *gan-er* bird guarding an empty pond.

Before he had even finished speaking, Yinzhang held up his fist and said, "At this very moment, what do you say? The Master overturned the meditation bench. Yinzhang then shouted. The Master said, "Drawing the bow after the thief has fled," and then departed.
While staying at Guangfu, [he said: (Note: The phrase "gan-niao" refers to a mythical water-bird; the context here suggests a futile effort to find something where nothing exists.)
In his quarters, he asked a monk, "When I lift this up, how do you understand it? He further said, "Tell me, what is this that requires one to lift it up?
Chan Master Faning of Xuedou in Mingzhou, a native of the Du family of Quzhou, ascended the hall and said: "The hundred rivers have different flows, yet..."

The ocean is the ultimate limit. The myriad phenomena of the universe take emptiness as their ultimate limit. The four classes of noble beings and the six realms of ordinary existence take the Buddha as their ultimate limit.
A clear-eyed monk takes his staff as his ultimate limit. But tell me, what is the ultimate limit of the staff?
If someone can say it, I shall hand it over to them with both hands. If not, it is better to lean idly against the side of the meditation seat and leave it at that.
He points out the way for his children and grandchildren.
Regarding the question asked by a monk to Chan Master Xiyong of Yanchang in Luzhou, a successor of Chan Master Kaixian Xun: "What was the meaning of Shaolin’s wall-gazing? The Master said:
A sense of shame can kill a person.
Chan Master Zong of Kaixian in Luzhou ascended the hall and said: "One does not do it; two does not rest. Turn the nostrils around; press down the clouds.
Heyshan understands how to beat the drum of Yanguan; Wang Xiu does not paint the oxen of Dai Song. Rice from Luling."
Touzi’s oil; Xuefeng still rolls his twin balls. Last night the wind brought news from Hengyang; a single cry from a cold wild goose amidst the frosty moon.
Master Gānlù Yóng was a successor of [Chan Master] [Name].
A monk asked Master Yuan of Guangxiao in Yangzhou, "What is the家风 (household style) of the Master? The Master said, "Seven topsy-turvy, eight upside-down.
The monk asked, "If a guest should suddenly arrive, how would you receive them? The Master said, "A cast-iron caltrop smashed into their mouth."
Chan Master Dazhi of Xuefeng in Fuzhou was a successor of Chan Master Rong of Xuedou. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master held up the handle of his whisk to show him. The monk said, "This belongs to Xiangyan; how about you, Master? The Master then gave a shout.
The monk laughed loudly. The Master rebuked him, saying, "This wild fox spirit!
Chan Master Zongyan Yuanjue of Xuefeng in Fuzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Yuankuang of Yuanfeng, was a native of Enzhou. A monk asked: "Not admiring the various sages..."
"How is it when one does not value one's own spiritual nature? The Master said, "The confession comes from the prisoner’s mouth. [The monk] asked, "How is it when one understands it in this very way?
The Master said, "Changing hands while beating one’s breast. [The monk] asked, "What is the mind of a great *kalyāṇamitra* (good spiritual friend)?
The Master said, "A single tile on the crossroads. On the day he took leave of the assembly, a monk asked, "What is the one phrase for the parting of the ways? The Master said:

There was a man riding a horse; another was walking on foot because he had no horse. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter on the road? The Master said, "The lowly yield to the noble. He ascended the hall and said:

"To cast aside delusion in search of enlightenment, one does not realize that delusion is the very hammer of enlightenment. To cherish the holy and loathe the ordinary, one does not realize that the ordinary is the very forge of the holy.
But as for the single phrase where both holy and ordinary are extinguished, and both delusion and enlightenment are forgotten—how shall it be?"
The Way arises. At midnight, colored clouds enshroud the jade image; at daybreak, five-colored clouds veil the mountain peak. Wang Dafu of Wei Prefecture left behind his name;
having become weary of the phenomena of the world due to the loss of his wife, he went to attend upon Yuanfeng.
Under Yuanfeng’s words, he knew where to return. One day, Yuanfeng said to him, "You are the Lu Xuan of today. Gong [Wang] immediately covered his ears. Once—
He then returned to the south of Mount Tan and lived there, dwelling in a thatched hut for three years. Once, he sang this song: "Within Mount Tan, how long is the day!
On the ridges of green pines, the realm of white clouds. Chanting birds and crying monkeys form my place of practice.
With hair disheveled, I gather ferns and sing again with laughter; Let people call me a wild man gone mad."

Chan Master Zhen of Yue-lin in Mingzhou, a successor of Chan Master Yuwang Zhen, ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'At the beginning of autumn and the end of summer, there ought to be thirty blows of the staff for failing to examine one's heart.
Yue-lin, however, does not agree with this. At the assembly on Vulture Peak, the World-Honored One held up a flower, and Kāśyapa smiled."
At such a time as this, thirty blows of the staff are well-deserved. Why?

Because in such a season of great peace, you have needlessly raised the sword and spear, commanding others to blow the Great Dharma Conch and beat the Great Dharma Drum. When taking a step, golden lotuses tread beneath one's feet;
when sitting upright, the precious throne stands majestic and high. Brahmā leads from the front, with fragrant flowers swirling about, while Śakra follows behind.
Thereafter, dragons and elephants crowded together, causing descendants in later generations to emulate one another in groups of three or two;

all claimed to possess extraordinary character and style, wandering through kalpa after kalpa and never willing to return home to sit in seclusion, merely drumming their lips and wagging their tongues.
It is like the resonance of bells, chimes, pipes, and flutes. With arms raised and chest thrust forward, he is more numerous than rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds.

He further displays his mastery in wandering through mountains and playing by waters, parting the grass to gaze at the wind; before the assembly, he speaks until even stones nod their heads, and flowers fly down from the heavens to cover the ground.
"He too deserves thirty blows. Now tell me: when rewarding one for the labor of the summer retreat, how does one bestow the recompense? After a long silence, he said:
"When the myriad treasures have achieved their perfection, what thickness or thinness is there? When the price of a thousand-jin weight is set, it naturally rises or falls."
A monk asked Master Guanyin of Huating in Xiuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Zhaochizhan: "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A tortoise walking through fire at midnight.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Empty space has no front or back. The monk bowed, and the Master then—
Beating. A successor in the fourteenth generation under Qingyuan,
a dharma heir of Chan Master Ming of Jingci.
Chan Master Xiang of Jingci Temple in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Shanyin in Yuezhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said:
'When a single film obscures the eye, empty flowers fall in confusion. [He] picked up his staff and said: 'Jingci has picked up this staff;
is this not "a single film obscuring the eye"? Within the tip of this staff, the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas all manifest in their sixteen-foot purple-golden bodies.'"
With this body, one mounts that land and travels through the ten directions, preaching all dharmas and delivering all beings—is this not like empty flowers falling in confusion?
Right now, is there anyone who can sit and cut it off before the staff has even been picked up?

"Come forth and meet with Jingci. If you do not, take care not to fall into error by clinging to the notion that space is fundamentally devoid of flowers or that the eye is fundamentally devoid of cataracts.
Thereupon, he threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Xuefeng Ling of Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "One is not it; two is not it. The mouth eats rice; the nose breathes air.
Desist from saying 'the Big Dipper hides its body. What need is there to speak of the 'tortoise-nose' at Nanshan? When the family estate is moved for transport, one may settle the transaction."
I urge you not to compete for the sharpness of a needle’s point.

Chan Master Dazhu of Ganlu in the Prefecture of Zhenjiang, a successor of Chan Master He of Changlu, was a native of Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "Sages and worthies are not distinguished; past and present are one."
It is but one. One might say: fire seeks the dry; water flows to the moist. Dig a well and drink; till the fields and eat. O Great Assembly:
The old king of the eastern village has departed and does not return; the yellow leaves fall in profusion, left in vain disarray.
Chan Master Huichun Yuanzhi of Lingyin Temple in Lin’an Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "My mind is like the autumn moon, clear and bright within the azure pool.
He then gave a shout and said: "Hanshan’s talk has fallen into error! "All you Chan masters," he continued, "it is bright and pure, free from dust."
How could it be compared to the moon on the Mid-Autumn Festival? Its void clarity is beyond all dependence; it cannot be equated with the world-illuminating pearl.

It stands alone, revealing heaven and earth; its light swallows the ten thousand phenomena. It shines throughout the heavens and across the earth, illuminating the past and soaring through the present. But tell me, what is this?

After a long silence, he said: "On this night, the single orb is full; where is its pure radiance not present? Chan Master Yuet-tang Dao-chang of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture was a Dharma heir of Chan Master Xuefeng Hui. He was a monk from the Wu clan of Baixi in Huzhou. His secular surname was Rong. His monastic name was Daochang. His courtesy name was Fuxing. His style name was Yuefang. He was also known as the Great Master of the Moon Hall. He was born in the year of the Water Monkey (1092) during the Yuanfeng era of the Shenzong Emperor of the Great Song dynasty. His father was named Rong, and his mother was née Zhao. From childhood, he possessed a sharp and penetrating intelligence. At the age of seven, he entered the household of the local temple to study the scriptures. At thirteen, he received the tonsure and began his formal studies. At nineteen, he received full ordination at the Great Bao’en Monastery in Hangzhou. Subsequently, he traveled to various regions to seek out eminent teachers. He first visited Master Wuzu at Mount Yunju, where he studied for three years. When a person of the highest capacity suddenly encounters one of middling or inferior capacity, how should they guide and receive them?
The Master did not answer. The monk said, "It is not only the Master who is at a loss; I, too, am utterly defeated. The Master said, "In thirty years, you will understand.
The monk asked, "I have heard it said in the past that 'sentient beings do not know what they use in their daily lives. I wonder, what is it that they do not know?"
"What is this? The Master said, "Speak. The monk said, "What is it like after one suddenly attains realization? The Master said, "One hundred and eight thousand [miles].
The monk raised his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*) and said, "What about this? The Master then gave a shout. He ascended the hall and said:
"Heaven and earth share the same root as I; the myriad things are one body with me. From head to foot, they are arranged horizontally and vertically. In the continent of Uttarakuru, fire..."

It ignited, setting the eyebrows of Śakra ablaze. The Dragon King of the Eastern Sea could not endure the agony and let out a thunderclap so violent that it overturned the seas and toppled the mountains, darkening the vast sky with clouds.

At that moment, the Old Man Chou at the crossroads, startled awake from his drunken slumber, clapped his hands and laughed heartily, saying, "In the city of Yunchang, there have been few thieves lately! Thereupon, he picked up [his staff].
Holding up his staff, he said: "Thief! Thief! Ascending the hall, he said: "When the Way prevails, the Son of Heaven’s edict is not transmitted;
all travelers sing songs of peace. 'Five nines make forty-five. Has anyone come from Huai Prefecture? If so, do not forget the fermented soybeans of Linjiang Commandery.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The World-Honored One held up a flower; Kāśyapa smiled. Holding up his staff, he said: "Dong..."
The Master picked up his staff and said, "What should you all do? He struck the incense table and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall again and said:
"The trousers have no crotch; the breeches have no opening. On one's head are three or five pecks of green ash. Old Zhaozhou is showing off too much."

Thus it is said: "When the state is clear, the talented are esteemed; when the family is wealthy, the children are arrogant. Yet, alas, while the grain and millet do not flourish in the sunlight, people compete to plant peach and plum trees in spring.
This, in turn, causes those who plow with their own strength to become, for the most part, sellers of human beings. Entering the hall: the two words "Buddha-dharma."
It is truly difficult to encounter. There are people who do not trust their own Buddha-work;

they rely solely on a few echoes and traces of the ancients, on the realms of knowledge of a semblance-prajñā, and on dharma-gates of fixed characteristics. As soon as they move, they turn their backs on awakening and unite with the dust of the senses;

they become stuck and cannot escape. Or, when students come, it is like using a seal to stamp clay—they transmit and bestow these things upon one another, not only failing to [awaken themselves], but...
This is an error. It would also lead others into error. Under Dongshan’s gate, there is no Buddha-dharma to give to people; there is only a single sword.
To every person who comes before him, he cuts them off one by one, so that their life-force does not remain and both seeing and hearing are extinguished.
He then meets them face-to-face before their parents were yet born. As soon as they step forward, he cuts them off. Thus it is said: "Rigidly..."
"Though a blade be sharp, it does not slay one who is innocent. Is there anyone here who is innocent?
Even so, they shall receive thirty blows of the staff. [He ascends the hall. "In the school of Dongshan, if you wish to walk, you walk; if you wish to sit, you sit.
To defecate in the alms bowl or spit into the water pitcher is to practice by clinging to the Dharma, like an ox pulling a millstone. [He ascends the hall. "In the school of Dongshan..."
Sometimes he blends mud with water; sometimes he stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
If you all intend to see Dongshan in the place where he blends mud with water, Dongshan is not to be found in that place where he blends mud with water.

If you intend to see Dongshan in the place where he stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, Dongshan is not to be found in that place where he stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. If you intend to see him in any place whatsoever—
To see Dongshan—Dongshan is not to be found anywhere at all. You intend not to see Dongshan, yet the nose-rope is already in Dongshan’s hand.
Should you nod off, he will pull the rope with a jerk; you will find only your own eyes blinking, and even then, you will still not recognize him.
I do not require you to recognize Dongshan; it will suffice if you simply recognize yourself. (End)
The Hall. Fenyang, do not harbor deluded thoughts. Juzhi’s finger—here, the matters of the Buddhadharma of all time and antiquity come to rest all at once.
Rest! Rest! Yet I recall Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman; even where there is no elegance, there is elegance.

He held up his staff and said, "Exerting my utmost strength for the sake of the assembly. Entering the hall, he said: "Tou-tuo Rock is shrouded in moss and lichen; Throw-Pen Peak is entangled by *bìlì* vines."
At Chan Luan’s Arhat Hall, three practitioners were ordained each year. At Guizong Temple, after the formal session, they would gather for tea.
Entering the hall, the Master said: "The lion does not eat the leftovers of the eagle; the swift falcon does not strike a dead rabbit. Let loose the great dragon of Linji!"
He set aside Yunmen’s “single glance” and, raising his staff, said: "Clouds move and rain falls; the three types of grass and two kinds of trees [all flourish].

On the first day of the tenth month in the first year of the Chongning era, he manifested illness. On the *wang* day, he recovered. He brought forth his ritual implements and distributed them among his disciples.

At midnight on the following day, he bathed, changed his robes, and sat in the lotus position. When the assembly requested him to preach the Dharma, he presented a verse and his final instructions for the Great Lineage of the School.
Briefly: Having finished speaking, he passed away. He was cremated; the flames formed five colors, and white light ascended. Wherever the smoke reached, there were śarīras.
His bone relics were divided and enshrined in stupas at Letan and Xinfeng.
Chan Master Yuanyou of Yunju Zhenru Monastery in Nankang Commandery was a native of the Wang family in Xinzhou.
A monk asked, "What is the essential meaning of Daolin? The Master said, "Zha. The monk asked, "When following the flow, one recognizes one's nature; there is neither joy nor sorrow."
The Master asked, "How much does your leather bag weigh? He replied, "Look with eyes raised high. The Master said, "Take it yourself and leave.
He asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A jade qilin buried under the snow of the barbarian heavens.

He asked, "What is it like when a tortoise hides its six limbs? The Master said, "Its patterns are already manifest. The student said, "But what can be done? It leaves no trace anywhere. The Master said, "..."
He said, "Leave it to him to drag through the mud and carry water. The monk asked, "What is it like when one goes in this very manner? The Master said, "As expected. He ascended the hall and said:
"The Tathāgatas of the past do not need to examine you further; the Bodhisattvas of the present must not let you pass."
Those who practice and study in the future must not deceive others by even a single point. Therefore, it is said in the teachings:

"If one wishes to thoroughly understand all Buddhas of the three periods of time, one should contemplate the nature of the dharma-realm: everything is created solely by the mind. Although this is so, [one must still be careful].

At Yunju’s gate, it is truly like gold dust falling into one’s eyes. [He] ascended the hall and said: “The vision of ordinary beings and the vision of sages are like spring clouds flashing with lightning;
true speech and false speech are like flowers in the sky or the moon reflected in water. This brings back to mind Changzi seeing Shitou, who could say: ‘A single point of snow on a red furnace.
[He] struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall. [He] ascended the hall again and said: “Using tortoise hair for arrows and rabbit horns for a bow—Narāyaṇa [wrathfully]...”
In a fit of rage, he shot an arrow that pierced through space; space collapsed, causing the torrents to fall and the peaks to topple.

The walls, tiles, and rubble emitted brilliant light as he took refuge in the Tathāgata’s Great Perfect Enlightenment. Striking the meditation seat, he descended from it. Ascending the hall, he said: "The moonlight blends with the clouds into white;
The sound of pines carries the chill of dew. What a truly authentic message! Rely on you gentlemen to examine it closely. Master Huanglong [Hui-nan] harmonized his entire being—
"Overturned! Is there anyone who can still support it? An unresolved matter from the Patriarchs and Ancestors brings calamity upon descendants.
[He] struck the meditation seat and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, [he said]: "All sounds are the Buddha's voice. Striking the meditation seat with his whisk, he said:
"The Brahma-sound is deep and far-reaching; it causes people to delight in hearing it. He further said: "All forms are the Buddha's form. Thereupon, picking up the whisk, he said: "Now..."
The Buddha emits radiance to assist in the realization of the meaning of the True Mark (dharmatā). Those who have already attained it should receive it upon their heads and practice accordingly;

those who have not yet attained it should know it thus and believe it thus. He struck the meditation seat and descended from it. The three pagodas currently found in various regions were first established by this Master.
Chan Master Daopei Huaxiu of Tanzhou was the son of the Ying family of Yingzhou. A monk asked, "In the past, the Water Buffalo of Mount Gui;
since it was let loose, its traces have vanished. Today we are fortunate to meet the Master ascending the seat;
where, then, should people of this age seek it? The Master said, "One must not trespass upon the crops. The monk said, "If that is so, then its head and horns are already clearly manifest."
The Master said: "In vain you hold the iron whip given by the mountain boy.

Chan Master Huangbo Weisheng Zhenjue of Ruizhou was the son of the Luo family of Tongchuan. While he was living among the assembly of lecturers, his fan happened to strike against a window lattice with a sound.
Suddenly, he recalled a passage from the teachings which says: "When drums are struck in all ten directions, they are heard in all ten places at once."
At that time, upon hearing [the words], he attained great enlightenment. He informed his original lecturer, who instructed him to go and inquire further. The Master went directly to Huanglong.
Later, because the Governor of Ruizhou commissioned Huanglong to select a successor for the abbotship of Huangbo, Huanglong gathered the assembly and presented this koan:

"Reciting hymns on the bell tower; planting vegetables beneath the bed. He said, "If anyone can speak of this, they shall go to reside as the abbot. The Master stepped forward and replied: "Fierce! (Měng!)
The tiger sat blocking the road. The Dragon was greatly pleased and consequently sent the Master forth;
from this, he came to be revered by all quarters. Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "Linji’s shout and Deshan’s staff are left for Zen practitioners as models.
Guizong’s whetstone and Xuefeng’s ball—this kind of teaching style receives those of superior capacity. If it were Huangbo, however, it would be otherwise: there would be neither shout nor staff."
It is not to be ground, nor is it to be rolled like a ball. Before you is the fore-mountain; behind you is the main mountain.
It blocks your eyes and presses against your face. If you can see into this, you will attain the stage of non-retrogression for as long as the future endures.
Do not seek it from others; if you fail to find it upon seeing it, the supreme flavor of *amṛta* (clarified butter) will instead turn into poison. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Silent and desolate—like a bright moon shining down into an empty valley. Vast and expansive—like the blazing radiance of the sun streaming across the four seas."
On the road to Caoxi, the passage of people is cut off; before the Many-Sons Stupa, the crowds are as dense as at a marketplace.
Even if you can realize this with such boldness, it is still not the true livelihood of a patch-robed monk.
A man of great character must strike the shackles and break the chains within the dark prison, set fire to the ranks of hungry ghosts to seize their gruel, and topple the Tower of Maitreya.
"Tear down the Palace of the Empty King! Uproot the auspicious sprouts and rare grasses by their very roots! Let thorns grow everywhere as they please.
Chan Master Yousheng Faju of Longxing Prefecture was the son of the Zheng family of Chaoyang. In his later years, he met Huanglong and received his profound seal of approval.
He ascended the hall and said: "This matter is like a physician’s diagnostic prescription for an illness; yet, with poison filling the belly, it is not easily overcome."

To treat a disease, one must necessarily use medicine that causes dizziness and nausea before it can be cured. Even if one were to administer such medicine merely to satisfy one's own desires, it would only serve to cause further delusion and aggravate the chronic ailment.

To seek a cure for a disease while acting in such a contrary manner—is this not perverse? The weeds before the Dharma Hall have grown deep, yet they do nothing to increase the afflictions within the mind.

Chan Master Ziqi of Kaiyuan Monastery in Qizhou was the son of the Xu family of Quanzhou. He relied upon Chan Master Zhina of Kaiyuan and received full ordination after passing the scriptural examinations.
He mastered the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and the *Awakening of Faith*, then departed to visit Chan Master Zhen of Cuiyan, where he inquired about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma.
Zhen spat on the ground and said, "Where does this single drop fall? The Master rubbed his chest and said, "Today, my spleen [is in pain]."
Zhenxiéyán (True Smile) took his leave to visit Jīcuì. After more than a year, he had fully mastered the Way.

On one occasion while attending Jīcuì, they were discussing matters of antiquity and the present when it began to snow heavily. Jīcuì pointed and asked, "Can this be swept away with a single broom? The Master replied, "It cannot."

That being so, when the sky clears and the sun rises, and the clouds and vapors disperse and dissolve, do they truly exist? One who knows this reaches a state where all words and phrases are like splitting bamboo;
though there be a hundred joints, they shall be severed at the stroke of a blade. How could there be any room for sound within the bounds of conceptual deliberation?
One day, Cui sent a monk to ask in advance, "How are the Old Monk’s Three Barriers? The Master replied with a stern voice:
"How can you understand matters of such long ago? Hearing this, Huicui was even more amazed. Thereupon, his reputation became renowned throughout the monastic community.

After Huicui passed away, Chan Master Sijuzu Yan appointed him to share the seat [of the abbot]. In his quarters, he posed a koan, saying: "A person has a mouth, yet cannot speak; who is it that bears this name?
Later, when this teaching was transmitted to Donglin, Chan Master Zong sighed and said: "The Head Seat Qi is like..."

The Iron Mountains rise ten thousand fathoms high; it is ultimately difficult to follow the flow of his discourse. Not long after, Kaiyuan was established as a Chan monastery, and the Master was invited to serve as its first patriarch.
He ascended the hall and said: "Space has no interior or exterior; phenomena and principle have their lengths and brevities.
To follow them is to realize Bodhi; to oppose them is to produce affliction. The lantern-lamp is always dozing; the pillar is also vexed. The Great Way is right before one's eyes."
[The Master] stepped forward. "Where else shall we seek it? He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and ascended the hall.
"On all four sides there are no doors; throughout the ten directions there are no walls. With hair unkempt and ears prominent—every one of these men is a great hero.
How could they allow themselves to be bound without ropes? Tell me, how do you express the single phrase of total liberation? After a long silence, he said: "Treading through the weeds."
Walking barefoot with shoes on his feet. A monk asked, "I do not ask about Mount Sumeru containing a mustard seed; but what of when the Great Dharma Wheel is turned within a mote of dust?
The Master said, "One step forward, another step forward. The monk said, "If that is so, then arriving in India in the morning and returning to Tang China in the evening.
The Master said, "Being a guest is not as good as returning home. The monk said, "I have long admired your reputation for the Way; I pray you, Master, grant me an audience."
The Master said: "The clouds and moon are the same; the streams and mountains are each different.

Chan Master Xingwei of Yangshan in Yuanzhou was a native of Hexi. He received full ordination at Dafu Temple in the Eastern Capital and studied the *Complete Enlightenment Sūtra* (Yuanjue), yet harbored some slight doubts.

Taking his travel-bag, he wandered to seek instruction from various quarters, specifically seeking to inquire into the meaning of the Patriarchs. He eventually arrived at the Dharma of National Teacher Nan.

While sitting in the sixth position in the sequence of the stars, he was summoned for an interview one day; as soon as he was about to step through the door, he was shouted out, and he suddenly realized the profound meaning.
He subsequently went forth into the world at Yangshan, where his reputation for the Way became widely renowned. Entering the hall, he said: "Does the assembly understand?
The affairs of antiquity cannot be concealed; the affairs of daily life cannot be hidden. Since they cannot be hidden or concealed, they manifest before us in our daily use. Now, let me ask you all—"
"Person! As for the matter before you, what is it? Investigate! [He] ascended the hall and said: "Does the great assembly see? When the eyes are open, one universally contemplates the ten directions;
when the eyes are closed, one encompasses all existence. Neither opening nor closing—what is its form? Do you still see its form?

Those of long-standing practice and high virtue will understand immediately upon hearing this raised. But those who are beginners and newly entered must recognize the form; do not merely continue on."
Greedy for sleep! When you are asleep, what do your eyes see? If you say you see nothing, how are you any different from a dead man?
Even if the Painter of the Immortals were to paint green mountains and blue waters, or peach blossoms entwined with bamboo, on the tip of his brush, it would still be merely a semblance.
Even if a stonecutter were to carve out herds of sheep and running beasts with his chisel, they too would be merely a semblance.
The appearance. If it were the true appearance, even a hermit or a stonecutter would have no place to apply their hand.
If you all wish to see it, you must truly open your eyes. After a long silence, he said: "Broad, it is a single thread;
narrow, it is one and a half inches. He struck the meditation seat with his whisk. As the drum sounded, the assembly gathered like clouds. Everyone ascended...
"Contemplating. The mountain monk looks down; looking up, what does he contemplate? Looking down, what does he look at? After a long silence, he said:
"Facing one another, we do not recognize each other. Entering the hall, he said: "The Way is not in sound or form, yet it is not apart from sound and form.

Every word and every silence, every movement and every stillness—whether hidden or manifest, whether expansive or vertical—all are nothing other than Buddha-work. It is present in daily life, throughout the past and the present."

He remained in a state of profound stillness. How could his realization have been at variance with the truth? The Master himself inscribed his own portrait, saying: "My true likeness is difficult to capture; it is mottled and variegated.

Should I attempt to arrange it, the very first stroke of the brush would be wrong. He passed away. Upon cremation, five-colored śarīras were obtained, along with bone fragments and stones linked together by cords.
These were enshrined in a stupa to the east of the monastery.
Chan Master Cigan of Fuyan on Mount Nanyue was the son of the Du family from Tongchuan. He ascended the hall and said: "The mind of the ancient Buddhas is right here and now.
If you do not understand it, you will suffer in deep reflection. The autumn rain falls gently; the autumn wind whistles. Moving hither and thither, how shall one respond?
On the sandy banks, reeds and flowers are intermingled in green and yellow. Upon what can the Chan practitioner rely? After a long silence, he said: "Zha! (A sharp, decisive sound).
Chan Master Shouzhi of Yungai in Tanzhou was the son of the Chen family of Jianzhou.

While traveling, he arrived at Daling in Yuzhang, where at that time Chan Master Fachang Yu was sequestered in the Western Mountains. Hearing that the Master had undergone extensive training, Shouzhi went to see Chang and asked:
"Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Da Ning. Chang asked again, "The three gates collapsed last night;
did you know of it? The Master was startled and said, "I did not know. Chang said, "In Wuzhong, there is a stone Buddha that many people have never seen. The Master was left bewildered.

He immediately performed prostrations. Chang sent him to pay his respects to Chan Master Zhen of Cuiyan; although he remained there for a long time, he had no realization. Yet he did not waste a single moment of time.
When he finally visited Huanglong at Jicui, he was able to resolve all his doubts. Later, he led the assembly at Shishuang and subsequently established the Dharma lineage at Dagui.
He then moved to Yungai. A monk asked: "There is a stringless lute that is not made of worldly wood. Today it is carried..."
[The monk] came forward and requested, "Please, Master, play a tune. The Master struck his knee once. The monk said, "The golden wind rustles in harmony with your pure melody;
I pray you, Master, use your skillful means to grant us another note. The Master said, "An iron ox emerges from Shanfu. He ascended the hall [and said]:
"Tightly laced water-proof boots tread upon the moon over Lake Xiang. Grasping an iron caltrop in hand, he breaks through the lair of the dragon and tiger, then turns over and falls."
Climbing the tree, he first perceives that there is neither arising nor ceasing; he turns and laughs at Old Gautama, who snaps his fingers and leaps beyond Maitreya. Entering the hall, he said:
"Yesterday, watching for fish from atop a high mountain, one walks while riding a horse and loses the donkey. Someone has picked up the camel and gone off with it."
"A reward of a thousand pieces of gold is not enough for this one instance. If you can offer a recommendation here, I will not even require the payment for your straw sandals.
[The Master] ascended the hall and, citing Zhaozhou’s question, "Monk, where have you been? to which the monk replied, "I went to pick tea," Zhaozhou said, "Idle. The Master said: "Idle."
Whether you hit upon it or not, where can you grope for it? A dragon’s scales behind; a donkey’s feet before. A somersaulting handstand;
a solitary cloud and a wild crane. A-he-he! To the assembly: "Without leaving this very place, it is ever serene; seek it and you know it cannot be seen.
Although the ancient sages spoke thus, first fashion a mold to cast it away. If you can emerge...
"You cannot. You have merely grasped what the ancients possessed. Only if you can bring it forth will there be some slight correspondence.
Yun-gai, however, was not like this: "Riding a fine steed around Mount Sumeru, passing over mountains to seek the tracks of ants—how many people could possibly know?
The Master resided in the East Hall of the monastery. In the *Xinmao* year of the Zhenghe era (1111), after Si-xin had retired from Huanglong, he entered the mountains from Hunan.
Upon his arrival for an audience, the sun had already set. An attendant monk announced his presence, and the Master, dragging his sandals, walked along speaking:
"Bring a candle! Let us see what his face looks like—how he has brought such fame to shake the universe. Dead Heart (Sīcitta) also cried out, "Bring him closer!
I want to see if this is a true master-uncle or a false one. The Master then struck him once right between the chest.
[Zhaozhou] made a fist. Sīxīn said, "This is indeed the real thing. He then prostrated himself; guest and host were in perfect accord, and their joy was great.
When Sīxīn returned to lead Huánglóng and passed away during the Jiǎwǔ year of the Zhènghé era, the Master, who was then residing at Kāifú, received the news. He ascended the hall and said:

An unfortunate event for the Dharma: the banner of the Dharma has been toppled; within the mountain of the five aggregates, all is turned to ash. Last night, the clay ox passed through a single thread;
from this moment on, Huanglong enters the cycle of saṃsāra.
Chan Master Xiansha Hedong Wenminghui of Fuzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Private paths allow for carriages and horses.
The monk took a step forward, and the Master said, "The official road does not admit even a needle."
Chan Master Zhaokong of Jianlong Monastery in Yangzhou ascended the hall. "The new year has begun and passed in an instant;

it is already the first day of the second month. The weather is harmonious and mild. I intended to bring up a seasonal cause and condition to discuss with you all, but Śakra and Brahmā have already poked their heads out from the willow-eyes outside the gate and spoken a verse first: *Niǎo...*"
Fluttering light tufts of silk follow the wind coming and going; one after another, balls of cotton roll by. Do not say, "I am but a tuft of silk.
At that time, having collided with an asura, he was seized and told, "Let you be a tuft of silk as you please.

Suddenly encountering a west wind blowing across the Wei River, leaves fall thickly over Chang'an—how do you speak this single phrase? Thereupon, Śakra Indra shrank his head and entered the eye of a willow.
After a long silence, he said: "Enter.
Chan Master Huìyuán of Bào běn in Āngjì Prefecture was the son of the Ni family of Cháo zhōu. At nineteen, he became a fully ordained monk (*mahāśramaṇa*).

He traveled extensively through various monastic assemblies and attained awakening under the teaching of the "Three Barriers" of Huánglóng. After he took up residence [at Bào běn], a monk asked: "The Buddhas do not appear..."

"World, Bodhidharma did not come from the West. At such a time as this, I do not know whether he came or not. The Master said, "I have struck right at your nostrils. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
"The white clouds disperse; the red sun rises in the east. Look up at the sky; look down at the earth.
East, west, south, and north—let you freely behold the sights. The eyes of Bodhidharma cannot be measured even by bushels. Yanluo, what is there to say?"
[The Master] once recognized the shadow. If Sudhana had not gone south, the nostrils of the patch-robed monk would pierce through the vast heavens;
having reached this point, they are all at once pierced through. A monk came forward and bowed, saying, "I have a question; will the Master answer it? The Master said, "I answered you yesterday.
[The monk] asked, "How about today? The Master said, "Come tomorrow. He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "All..."
"The various teachings spoken by the Buddha are all skillful means, are they not? The Master said, "Yes.
The monk asked, "Why is it that the mark of the quiescence of all dharmas cannot be proclaimed in words? The Master said, "Do not misunderstand this. The monk drew a circle with his sitting cloth.
The Master shouted, saying: "The mark of the cessation of all dharmas cannot be proclaimed in words.
Now, when students see that the Way cannot be proclaimed in words, they immediately attempt to sever their thoughts and forget external conditions, shutting off their sight and hearing.

With such an understanding, they have not yet attained a share of true mastery. Do you all wish to understand the mark of cessation? When you step out the door, not even a single hair can be seen. Full...
With white clouds for his eyes and green peaks for his screen, the Master sat but did not lie down for over thirty years before passing away. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on Mount Hyeom.
Zen Master Gyeonghan of Insan Nonggyeong Hermitage in Jiju was the son of the Jo family from Fuzhou. His mother dreamed of a foreign monk...
He was given a bright pearl, which he swallowed and subsequently became pregnant. When she gave birth, a white light illuminated the room. From childhood, she did not approach wine or meat.

At the age of eleven, she renounced the secular life; at seventeen, she received full ordination; and at twenty, she traveled extensively to visit various masters. Later, she went to see Huanglong at Huangbo.
Huanglong asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Bazhang. Huanglong asked, "When did you leave there? The Master replied, "The thirteenth day of the first month. Huanglong—
[The Master] said, "Your heels ache; give him thirty blows! The Master said, "Not merely thirty blows.
Long shouted, "After traveling on pilgrimage for so long, you have not a breath of spirit left! The Master said, "Even the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are likewise thus.
[Long] asked, "Coming as you do, when have you ever reached even a hair’s breadth of the Buddhas' realm? The Master said, "The Buddhas have likely never reached it either."
Regarding the realm of Qingxian: Long asked, "What is the place of your birth? The Master said, "In the morning I ate white congee;

now I am feeling hungry again. Long asked, "How is my hand like the Buddha’s hand? The Master said, "Playing the lute under the moon. Long asked, "How is my staff like the Buddha’s staff? The Master said, "Hanging up clothes on a bamboo pole."
"What are my feet like? the Master asked. "They are like a donkey's feet," [the other] replied. The Master said, "A heron standing in the snow is not of the same color.
Longze sighed and looked at him, saying, "You have shaved off your hair and beard; for what purpose do you do this? The Master said, "I simply wish to be without affairs.
Longze said, "If that is so, then with a few clear strokes of the chime, one is beyond right and wrong—a free man in the world between heaven and earth. The Master said, "What words are these?"
[The monk] said, "Is it so? The Master said, "An intelligent patch-robed monk [like you] does not even deserve this. Long said, "There is a Venerable Bian here; you must exert your full brilliance.
The Master said, "What longings for excellence does he have? Long said, "If he were to strike you once on the back, what would you do?
The Master said, "What would that amount to? Long said, "He would extend both hands. The Master said, "Where did he learn such empty pretension?"

The falling of flowers and the blooming of flowers have their own appointed times. He then descended from his seat.
