There was a man who once played by scooping up mountain stream water with his cupped hands during the day; at night, he thought of it and suddenly saw the water filling the room, cool and clear.
He tried to draw some, but could not. At that moment, the mundane world vanished of its own accord, and he exclaimed, "The net of worldly existence has been torn asunder!

He went to rely upon Master Zhaojue for ordination and received the full precepts. Later, while practicing among the assembly and seeking instruction, Zhaojue one day asked the Master, "Upon the high, high peak summit..."
[The Master] stood. "Walking at the bottom of the deep sea—how do you understand this? At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and said, "My heels are nailed down!
Yuanjue picked up his whisk and asked, "And what about this? The Master smiled and departed.
He served diligently for seven years. He traveled south to the capital, passing through Huai and Zhe. Later, he met Master Wuzu Yan at Haikai and went forth to ask:
"I do not yet know the pivot; it is difficult to cross Zhaozhou’s bridge. "I shall not ask about Zhaozhou’s bridge," [Wuzu replied].
"What is the pivotal bolt? The Patriarch said, "You stay outside the door for now. The Master stepped forward and withdrew with a single kick.
The Patriarch said, "After all this time of tea and rice, it turns out there is someone who knows its flavor. The next day, he entered the inner room.
The Patriarch said, "Are you the monk who questioned me yesterday? I certainly know your point of view;
it is simply that you have not yet passed the White Cloud Barrier. The Master said, "Take care," and then he departed. At that time, Yuanwu was serving as the attendant.
The Master inquired of him regarding the meaning of the White Cloud Barrier. Yuanwu said, "You should simply realize it directly. The Master laughed and said, "I am not [that]."
"Not so; it is simply that I am not yet familiar with it. I shall wait until I see this old fellow and settle the matter with him.
The next day, Linji went to Shucheng, while the Master and Wujue followed after him. They happened to meet at Xinghua. Linji asked the Master, "Do you remember meeting me in the prefectural seat?

The Master replied, "I was fully attending to my duties. Linji looked at Wujue and said, "This fellow is too talkative. From that time on, he [Wujue] was known as "Liaosheshan" (The Talkative Mountain).

This was a meeting of minds through karmic conditions. Upon returning from his travels at Mount Lu, the Master related to the Fifth Patriarch the words he had received while "standing atop the highest peak and walking upon the deepest ocean floor.
The Patriarch said, "I have previously questioned my late master about this matter. My late master said, 'I once asked Venerable Yuan;
Yuan replied, "A cat has the merit of drinking blood; a tiger has the power to raise the dead. "
"Virtue: one who has not long mastered the fundamental source cannot reach it. Because the Master had served him for so long, the Patriarch held him in special affection.

Later, when [Daowu] took his leave to return westward, the Patriarch gave a small discourse (*xiao-can*) and further sent him off with a verse, saying: "For over forty years I have been away from my hometown, And for a time I forgot the dialect of Shu.
When you, O Chan practitioner, return to Chengdu, You must take care to remember the dialect of Lu. At that time, Huairang was still in good health.
The Master again attended him. His fame spread widely, and he subsequently went forth to reside at Changsong, later moving to Baofu Xinsiang. A monk asked:
"The Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of the six generations all fail to get out of this circle. What is this circle?"
The Master Guishan said: "The rim of a well. He then ascended the hall and raised this case: Yangshan asked Zhongyi, "What is the meaning of Buddha-nature?"
Yi said, "I shall give you a parable; you will understand it at once. Suppose there is a room with six windows, and inside there is a monkey.
Outside, a monkey calls from the east, 'Singing-sing! and the monkey inside responds. Thus it is with all six windows: they call together, and he responds together.
Yang then prostrated himself, saying, "I have now received the Master’s instruction. I have [a realization]..."
Doubting, Yangshan said, "What is it that you doubt? Nanquan said, "Suppose the inner monkey is asleep, while the outer monkey wishes to meet him;
what then? Nanquan descended from his meditation seat, took Yangshan by the hand, and said, "The *xingxing* has met you.
The Master said, "Do you all wish to see these two elders? I shall tell you about them as well."
This is an analogy. In Zhongyi there was a man who closely resembled a goldsmith. Yangshan brought a piece of gold and had the goldsmith appraise it;
the goldsmith offered a price that matched its full value. As they were about to complete the transaction, the seller added extra weight to the scales.
Although the goldsmith felt secretly pleased, he could not help but harbor a hidden suspicion in his heart. Why? Unless he were a spy, he must surely be a thief.
[The master] finished his discourse and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Dayuan Zhi of Da Meishan in Tanzhou, a dharma heir of Chan Master Dalin Yi, was a native of Siming. He ascended the hall and raised the example of Nanquan’s saying: "Three..."
"The Buddhas of the three worlds do not know it exists; the tabby cat and the white ox, however, do know it exists.
The Master said, "If the Buddhas of the three worlds do not know it exists, how could the tabby cat and the white ox have ever dreamed of it?

It is evident that you must know there is one who knows it exists above this level before you can attain it. But what kind of person is one who knows it exists? They drink the official wine and lie on the official street."
To be executed on the spot. To be buried on the spot. Limitless heroic men upon the battlefields; their corpses pile up like mountains and accumulate like peaks.
The Dharma heir of National Teacher Xiu of the Fifteenth Generation under Master Nanyue Huairang.
Wendeng Gong Hu Anguo was a lay practitioner (upāsaka) styled Kanghou. Having long relied upon Shangfeng, he attained the meaning beyond words.
During the Chongning era, while passing through Yaoshan, a Zen practitioner raised the story of Nanquan killing the cat and questioned the Gong about it.
The Gong replied with a verse: "In hand, the pivot of life and death that governs heaven and earth; To deploy them freely or restrictively depends on the moment. The Jade Hall..."

A hare or a horse is not a dragon or an elephant; the grand function, majestic and imposing, is entirely unknown. Again, sent from Shangfeng, it says: "Mount Zhurong resembles the heavens above Ducheng;
ten thousand ages of rivers and mountains are before one's eyes. One must believe that Sīxin has never truly died;
last night the autumn moon was once again full."
Chan Master Fozu Yuanxu of Puxian Monastery in Fuzhou, a native of Jianning, was a successor of Chan Master Shangfeng Cai. He ascended the hall and said: "The army follows the seal’s turn;

beyond three thousand miles, smoke and dust are extinguished. The general pursues the talisman’s path; throughout the six periods of the day, one is utterly naked and bare. There is no need for iron banners."
The iron drum rolls; naturally, the grass bows and the wind blows. What need is there for seven releases and seven captures? It reaches the point where none fail to submit without thought.

As it is said: "When a great man wields the sword of wisdom, with the sharp edge of Prajñā and the flames of Vajra, he not only shatters the minds of externalists, but has long since struck terror into the hearts of the celestial Māras. At such a time, tell me: who is the commander?
[The Master] lets out a shout. He ascends the hall and says: "Nanquan said, 'At eighteen, I already knew how to make a living.
My bags had no thread to tie even an ant; my kitchen lacked enough grain to gather flies. Zhaozhou said, 'At eighteen, I already knew how to break up the family and scatter the household.
I bought cheap at the southern end and sold dear at the northern end. When examined closely, both of them deserve thirty blows of the staff."

Let this one move pass for now. Why? "Having once been a wanderer, he feels particular compassion for travelers; naturally loving wine, he spares those who are drunk. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
"Before a word is spoken, the matter is already entrusted; should you attempt to deliberate, ten thousand mountains stand between you.
Do not say that the Buddha-dharma is nothing much—it is also very difficult to penetrate the profound barrier. But how does one penetrate this profound barrier? *He let out a shout.*
One shout.
Chan Master Shantang Sengxun of Gushan in Fuzhou, a native of the local Ruan clan, ascended the hall and said:
"Huangbo’s sixty blows from his staff—had he not understood the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, he would have been somewhat deficient. But as for Dayu’s strike upon his ribs..."
He clenched his fists three times and said, "Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma consists of nothing more than this. This is truly a case of being "killed by dullness.
You must know there is one person who, when struck over the head with a great club, does not turn back; who, when struck across the face with an old fist, still pays no heed.
But tell me, who is it? Ascending the hall, he said: "The north wind sweeps the ground, rolling up the yellow leaves; Outside the gate, a thousand peaks show a chilling hue. At night..."
A half-turtle flies with snow; the stone woman frowns her two brows by the stream. (He plants his staff and says: "Everyone is here.
Now tell me, is it the sky that is cold or the people? (He gives a shout and says: "Return to the hall!"
Chan Master Biefeng Zuozhen of Gushan in Fuzhou was a native of the Lin family of Xinghua.

A monk asked, "Zhaozhou circumambulated his meditation seat once and said that he had finished reciting the entire Tripitaka. What is the principle behind this? The Master replied, "When painting a dragon, look at its head; when painting a snake, look at its tail.
The monk asked, "The old woman said, 'I have come to request you to recite the complete Tripitaka. Why did you only manage to recite half of it?"
"What do you think about this? The Master said, "If a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely have immediate anxieties.
[The monk] asked, "I wonder where it is that one turns the entire Tripiṭaka? The Master said, "If one is not a true knower, it is a vain labor to speak of the severity of winter.

Ascending the hall, he said: "To seek the ox, one must follow its tracks; to study the Way, one prizes the absence of mind. When the tracks are found, the ox returns; when there is no mind, the Way is easy."
[The Master] searched. Holding up his whisk, he said, "This is the track. Where is the ox? Even if you can see its horns clearly, its nostrils are still in the hands of Fashí.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said, "The path that leads upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages.
He struck the ground with his staff and said, "If you understand it this way, you are still a hundred thousand eight thousand miles away. After all, what is it like? Peach red, plum white.
The white rose is purple; when questioned about the spring breeze, it knows nothing at all. He addressed the assembly, saying:

"The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet for all its presence, it is difficult to behold. If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, it is not apart from sound, form, and speech.
He struck the meditation staff and said, "This is sound. He held up the staff and said, "This is form. What do you call the Great Way?"
The true essence of the Way: even if you were to see it here, it would still be like leaving Zhengzhou to head for Cao Gate.
To the assembly: if one discusses this matter, it is like a person eating a meal; when full, one simply stops. If one is not yet full, there will surely be a mind that longs for food.
Yet if one eats too much, there is the affliction of indigestion. Having reached this point, how can one attain the state of being just right?
He departed. After a long while, he said: "For now, return to stay overnight at the base of the cliff;
let us look together upon the bright moon.
Chan Master Chéng'ān Zéchóng of Jiànfú in Ráozhōu, a dharma heir of Chan Master Fēng of Huánglóng, was a native of Níngguó Prefecture. He ascended the hall and, citing a case, said: A monk asked—
An ancient worthy asked, "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them? The Worthy said, "The firewood crackles and the bamboo bursts, startling the ears.

The monk said, "I do not understand. The Worthy said, "The house dog’s barking is fierce and does not cease at night. The Master said, "Do you all wish to understand? The firewood crackles and the bamboo bursts, startling the ears;
red dust rises from the bottom of the vast ocean. The house dog’s barking is fierce and does not cease at night."
Traveling thirty thousand *li* by land in a boat, the Earth Goddess Sthāvarā laughs heartily.
King Sumeru peers with his eyes and sniffs with his nose; taking her hand, she walks east but heads west. The southern mountain’s voice echoes within the northern mountain.
The Thousand-Armed Great Compassionate One opens his eyes to look: whose is this immeasurable compassion? After a long silence, he says: "Long head, short legs; little joy, much anger."
Ascending the hall, he asked his attendant, "Do you remember the circumstances from yesterday? The attendant replied, "I do not remember.
He then looked toward the assembly and said, "Do you remember? The assembly remained silent. Raising his whisk, he asked, "Do you remember?
After a long pause, he said, "It has been forgotten as well. Not established in three places, nor existing as one—since you all do not understand this, [the Dharma] is lost."
He said, "Pillar, do not open your mouth. With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat and descended from it.

Chan Master Wushi Jiechen of Yuyang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Zhuo of Tianning; he was born into the Zhang family of Wenzhou. He took leave of the administrative officials and ascended [the hall].
In a fathom there are ten inches; those who recognize this are still rare. At the end of a scale there are no stars; do not mistake them for such.
If you wish to determine the lightness or heaviness of past and present, or to compare the merits of Buddhas and patriarchs, simply apply a single eye to the midst of it.

If you can truly return the ten inches to the one fathom, and see that eight *liang* are originally half a *jin*, then naturally there will be harmony within and without, and peace for the family and the nation.
Matters. Today, this mountain monk has already handed it over with both hands. Do you all accept and practice it with conviction?
A ruler and measure, a knife and scissors, pervade the world; Master Zhizhe was no idle monk. [Ascending the hall:
"The wisdom of Mañjuśrī, the conduct of Samantabhadra—this is the calendar of many years. The staff of Deshan, the shout of Linji—these are heroes of a chaotic age. You..."
When people like you pass through the Sangha Hall and enter the Buddha Hall, do you realize you are crossing a perilous pass beyond the Iron Ring Mountains?
Suddenly, you might tread upon the crown of Śākyamuni’s head or bump your forehead against the Holy Monk; you cannot avoid a great calamity. Entering the hall [for discourse], I say:
"If I speak of existence, you will be hindered by existence. If I speak of non-existence, you will be hindered by non-existence. If I speak crosswise..."
Furthermore, you cannot leap over it; if I speak vertically, you cannot leap out from it.
If you wish for the monastic community to be peaceful and everyone to be free from trouble, it would be better to topple King Aśoka. But tell me, how can King Aśoka be toppled?
He called to the assembly, saying, "Exert yourselves! Exert yourselves! Then he said, "Alas! Alas! King Aśoka has been toppled by others."
Furthermore, is there anyone who, seeing injustice, draws their sword to come to one's aid? If not, this mountain monk cannot help but fall down by himself and rise up again.
(He strikes the whisk and descends from the seat. The Master was by nature firm and resolute; he presided over the assembly with ancient methods, and was thus called "Iron-Face Chen" at the time.
Chan Master Puming Huelin of Daochang Monastery in Anji County was a native of Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said:
"The leaky bamboo sieve, the stainless wooden ladle; the white peonies in the courtyard, the red peonies in the railing.
Thinking back on the man who sat facing the wall for nine years—until the end, he did not recognize this one point. Now tell me, what is this one point? He struck the meditation seat with his staff.
The seat below the platform; ascending the hall: one is many, many is one. At the crown of Vairocana’s head, as bright as the sun, there is neither one nor many.
This realized public case is free of ambiguity. Picking up the old felt clappers, we sing the song of peace together in this time of clarity.
Chan Master Wuchuan Ju-hui of Daochang Monastery in Anji County was the son of the Wu family of that same prefecture.
He ascended the hall and said: "Zhong Kui sings the Liangzhou melody in his drunkenness; his younger sister merely nods her head at the gate.
After the sea-roaming yakṣa has met him, everyone claps their hands atop the high tower. If you, the assembly, can understand this, you will lock the tongues of all people in the world. If..."
[The monk] could not understand it. He thought, "I suppose this old monk has some other extraordinary secret. He ascended the hall and said:

"Playing with shadows atop a hundred-foot pole Not only deceives you, but deceives Heaven as well. Laughing at myself for my whole life on the forked path, Now that I have returned in my old age, I possess not a single coin.
He ascended the hall again and cited Linji’s address to the assembly: "One person stands atop a high peak; there is no way out..."
The Road. One person stands at a crossroads; there is neither front nor back. Tell me, which one is in front and which one is behind?
The Master said, "There is yet another person who is neither on the high mountain peak nor at the crossroads.
Why did Old Man Linji not know this? Having said this, he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Yuanchi of Songtang at Xianning Temple in Lin’an Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "The reeds are white; the smartweed is red.
By the stream, the tall bamboos are enshrouded in green mist. Idle clouds embrace the secluded rocks; jade dew drips from the mountain thickets.
Last night the tortoise transformed into a turtle; this morning the water buffalo realized Perfect Penetration. *Du!* (A shout)"
Chan Master Liangfan Weian of Wuhui, Anjingshou, ascends the hall: "The events prior to kalpas of dust are majestic, with no front or back;
movement and stillness cannot encompass them, their unfolding as swift as lightning. Do not say that ordinary people do not know them—the Buddha himself cannot see them.
Where exactly do they reside? Close these two lips. Whether you realize it or not, for the sake of all of you, I shall speak further."
He passed through the single line. After a long silence, he said: "The world is at peace; the imperial wind fans forever. He ascended the hall and raised the following case:
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "The ultimate Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes picking and choosing. Is this the nest of people of this age?
Zhaozhou replied, "Someone once asked me this, and I was unable to explain it clearly for five years. The Master called to the assembly, saying: "Zhaozhou possesses the eye on the crown of his head."
With your own eyes, discern the black from the white within the sparks struck from flint; clarify the taking and giving within the flash of lightning.
Why, then, were you unable to distinguish them for five years? Do you understand? It is easy to distinguish flour in the snow, but difficult to identify soot in ink.
Chan Master Wen Guan Lingguang of Benji was the son of the Ye family of his native prefecture, Wenzhou.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Tathāgatas of the past have already perfected this gate; better not to have had such a thing. The Bodhisattvas of the present each now enter perfect clarity;
better not to have had such a thing. Those who practice and study in the future should abide according to this; better not to have had such a thing."
"If it is as if there were nothing, do you still understand? Aside from Master Chen of Mount Hua, who among men does not carry along right and wrong?
*Chan.* Chan Master Wuzheng Huichu of Deshan in Changde Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Huanglong Zhen, was a native of Jingjiang Prefecture. He ascended the hall and looked around.
The assembly asked, "Do you see? In heaven they form the celestial bodies; on earth they take shape as forms. In the sun and moon, they become the dark and the new moon;
in the four seasons, they become cold and heat. They are stirred by thunder and lightning, and moistened by wind and rain.
But tell me, within the sphere of a patch-robed monk, how is it? With one kick, he overturned the four great oceans; with one punch, he toppled Mount Sumeru.
Mount Mi. One cannot remain within the station of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Furthermore, he blows his fishing flute at the Bay of Muro. Entering the hall:
"On the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month, we gather our heads together to raise it up; we blind the Eye of the True Dharma and cast away Yunmen’s ‘Universal.
Deshan did not understand how to speak Chan, yet he won the right to sing village songs and perform community dances. A-he-he! La-lo-li! Thereupon, he performed a dance and descended from the seat.
The Seat-Holder:
Chan Master Wannian Yi’s Dharma heir, Chief Seat Fabang of Ba’en Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture, was a native of Kaifeng. He was a descendant of the Prime Minister Xue Juzheng.

In the seventh year of the Xuanhua era, he received the tonsure under Huayan Yuanshi of Yiyang, Changsha. He traveled extensively among the monastic communities and delved deeply into the ocean of meaning within the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.
From Huxiang to Wannian, he went to visit Xuechao; their spiritual faculties were in accord, and Xuechao appointed him to manage his correspondence.
Later, he led the assembly at Baoen Temple. In his quarters there was only a single low couch, and he possessed no other belongings. In the Gengzi year...
In the ninth month, he told the monks of the temple, "After one month, I shall no longer remain here. On the twenty-first day of the tenth month, he went to the abbot’s quarters for a meal.
As dawn approached, he wrote a *Yúfǔ* (Fisherman) lyric on the door of his room, then sat upon his couch with his legs drawn up and passed away.
The lyric reads: "This matter has often been revealed in the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*. Where plum blossoms, snow, and moonlight intermingle their radiance, A single laugh rings out vast and empty—"
Ten thousand ages: the wind-chimes speak. Lofty and clear, the Milky Way stretches across the heavens. In the dream of the *Nanhua*, the butterfly flutters joyfully;

who is it that treads upon the tiger of Fenggan? Now, I have forgotten the path by which I came. The mountains and rivers darken at twilight; from the ends of the earth, my eyes watch the wild geese fly away.
A monk asked Chan Master Shu of Yanqing on Mount Lu, the Dharma heir of the Patriarch Abbot of Mount Yue: "Before the Many-Sons Stupa, what did they discuss together? The Master said:
"Every time we meet, we grow older; how much longer can we remain as brothers? The monk bowed, and the Master said: "Tangxing."
Today’s loss of fortune.

The Dharma successor of Master Jingchan of Shengyin, Chan Master Puxin of Meng’an at Wanshou Monastery in Lianshui Commandery, ascends the hall and says: "The remaining snow has completely melted; the spring breeze..."
Day by day they increase. If one were to meet them through the seasons, what would the Buddha-dharma be like?
Tell me, are the conditions of the seasons and the principles of the Buddha-dharma the same or different? After a long silence, he said: "A shadowless tree planted where no one sees;
its blossoming and fruition are naturally fragrant."
Chan Master Xingdao of Meian at Huiji Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "The gathering clouds are about to snow, yet the snow has not fallen;
the beloved sun seems radiant, yet its light does not shine. Cold sparrows chirp noisily among the fences, and the biting north wind dances across the curtains.
If you wish to understand Yangshan’s intimate verse, I shall bring it to mind for you face-to-face this very day. He struck his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Guo Min of Guangxiao Temple in Guangde Commandery was a native of Taoyuan, Changde. He ascended the hall and, citing the story of Nanquan’s beheading of the cat, said:
"Nanquan raised it up and brought down the blade to execute it; even a six-armed asura could not have saved it."
Even if both halls were to speak the Way, blood would surely flow to fill the streets.
Chan Master Huizhong of Xuefeng Qiutang in Fuzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Xuefeng Niu, ascended the hall and said: "All day long in a bustle, yet that matter remains unimpeded."
"What is that matter? After a long silence, he said: "The heart does not betray others; the face shows no shame.

Master Yuan of Penglai in Qingyuan Prefecture was a Dharma heir of Chan Master Jiao of Tiantong. He resided on the mountain for thirty years without his feet ever crossing the threshold. Both monastics and laypeople revered him.
Looking up at it, the Master spoke a verse: "A newly-sewn paper quilt, warmed by the fire, brings a peaceful sleep until the fifth watch.
Hearing the bells and drums of the upper realm resonate, another day is added to this floating life."
Chan Master Shouhui Chongzhen Miyin Tonghui of Yuan Tong on Mount Lu in Jiangzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Yuantong Min, ascended the hall and said:
"One only knows today and tomorrow, unaware of the end of autumn and the beginning of the next. Walking with steady steps across the level plain, one returns to one's native village. Then...
Riding the bright moon across the Azure Isle. *Ei!* Those who have not undergone bitter toil do not understand this.
The Chan Master Huanglong Daoguan of Longxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "An ancient said, 'The eye and form, the ear and sound—by these, the myriad dharmas are accomplished.
Why is it, you all, that from morning until evening, the various dharmas do not encounter one another? He then let out a shout.
With a single shout, he said: "The ox is led into your nostrils. Calamity does not enter the door of a prudent house.

The Layman Fan Chong, Grand Councilor and styled Zhixu, was serving as the Governor of Yuzhang from the Han-yuan academy. While passing through Yuan-tong to pay his respects to Chan Master Min, after the tea had been served, he said:
"I am now approaching old age; I have fallen among those in the ranks of the purple-robed officials. I am somewhat distant from this matter..."
"Far away. The Master addressed him as "Naihan" (Internal Secretary). The Master responded with an acknowledgment. The Master said, "How can there be such a thing as 'far'?

The Master [Zhaozhou] replied with a leap of joy, saying, "I beg the Teacher to grant me further instruction. The Master said, "From here to Hongdu, it is four stages of travel. The Master stood in thought for a moment. The Master said, "When you see it, you see it;
if you try to deliberate upon it, you are already astray. Thereupon, the Master attained a sudden and profound realization.
The layman Wu Juhou, a Grand Councilor, returned to Zhongling with his official insignia.
He visited Chan Master Yuan Tong Min and said, "Some time ago, when I was traveling to the provincial examinations, I passed through here and crossed Zhaozhou’s Barrier.

I asked the former abbot, Elder Ne, about the matter of penetrating the barrier, and he replied, 'Go ahead and take up your official post. Now, before I knew it, more than fifty years have passed. Min asked, "Have you ever attained clarity?"
"Is this the matter of passing through the barrier? The official said, "I have passed through it eight times; I have always maintained this thought, yet I am still not entirely free and easy.
Yunmen took up a fan and gave it to him, saying, "Please use this fan. The official immediately fanned himself. Yunmen said, "Where is there anything that is not free and easy?
The official suddenly attained realization and said, "Then please grant me the final word. Yunmen then fanned him twice. The official said:

"Kindness! Kindness! Min said, "The tongue of Old Man Ji-liao stretches three thousand li. Layman Peng Rulin, the Imperial Censor, had handwritten a copy of the *Avalokiteśvara Sūtra* to offer to Yuan-tong. Tong picked it up and asked, "Which of these is the *Avalokiteśvara Sūtra*, and which is the Censor’s own sūtra? The official replied, "This is what I personally wrote. While the layman Minister Lu Hang was warming himself by the brazier with Yuantong, he asked: "There is no need to laboriously bring up the various ancestral cases;
I ask the Master to point directly to a single phrase. Yuantong pointed at him with a stern voice, saying: "Look at the fire! The Master hurriedly reached out to poke it.
Yi suddenly attained great enlightenment. He thanked [the Master], saying, "It is clear: the Buddha-dharma is not so very much. Tong shouted, "Put it down!
Yi responded, "Yes, yes."
The Layman Du Xiang, Director of the Left Bureau, asked Yuan Tong, "This Dharma cannot be understood through thought or discrimination;
how should one approach it? Yuan Tong said, "Enter the mass of fire with your whole body. The Layman said, "Ultimately, how does one comprehend it?
Yuan Tong said, "Go straight ahead. The Layman hesitated. Yuan Tong said, "Would you like some more tea? The Layman said, "There is no need."
Tong said, "Why do you not understand it in this way? Gong realized the essential meaning and said, "It turns out it is far too near.
Tong said, "A hundred thousand eight thousand [miles]. Gong then offered a verse: "Inconceivable! This is a great mass of fire.
To go thus, one does not depart from the very place. Tong said, "Ei! There is still this thing remaining. Gong said, "I beg the Master to grant me further instruction. Tong said, "Just so!"
"Go thus. "The cauldron is cast of iron. The Master bowed his head in thanks.
Zen Master Xuanmi Li of Shitai in Yangzhou, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Mingzhao Hui, was asked by a monk: "Are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth the same as oneself?"
"This is different. The Master said, "On a cool night at a long pavilion, the moon is often spread out for the traveler.

The monk said, "Thank you, Master, for your reply. The Master said, "The net is so large it is hard for birds to pass; the line must be thick to catch fish. The monk performed a dance and returned to the assembly.
The Master said, "The long river serves as a inkstone, frequently writing letters of severed ties. He then ascended the hall and raised the story of Baizhang and the wild fox, saying, "It is not so."
The hand that turns back the surging waves merely boasts of leaping over the sea; when Yi You draws his arrow, the many monkeys on the branches are startled.
[Ascending the hall,] he went before the seat, seized a monk, and pulled him up onto the Dharma seat. The monk, terrified, was about to run away, whereupon the Master pointed to the seat and said:
"This shed—if one were to lead a donkey up there, it would surely defecate upon it as well. Why, then, do you all refuse to go?
With his staff, he drove them all away at once and, looking back at his attendant, said, "How narrow it was!"
Chan Master Lingyan Hui of Mount Emei, a successor in the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Zhen of Fushan, was asked by a monk: "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas;
I wonder, who is the teacher of Mañjuśrī? The Master replied: "The young woman at the sands of Jinsha."
Chan Master Chūn of Bào-cí in Hún-nán, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Lì of Xiáng-fú, ascended the hall and said: "A single glance from the blue eyes, and the Golden One knows where to return.
Coming with hands extended, it is like a king’s precious sword. Yet nowadays, people open up their own schools and each propounds divergent doctrines; this may indeed be called 'the ancient road.'"
When the ground is level, thorns grow; when the Dharma-eye is upright, it blinds itself. Thus one fails the former sages and buries one’s own spiritual brilliance. Now tell me:
if there is no burying and no failing, how can the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye be revealed?
Is there anyone who can reveal it? Come forth and reveal it! If there is none, then take your poetry and books and return to your old hermitage; let the wild flowers weep.

Chūdo Chisoku (also known as Ōrai Hōgo), the Dharma heir of Zen Master Ungan Yū, was the son of the Chen family of Tiantai. He followed the Huoguo Monastery in his youth. Regarding the phrase "like a bird returning in spring" (*nyō-hyaku-shun*), the *Rinzendō* records it as "Ōrai Hōgo’s words.
Zen Master Chūdo Chisoku of Jing Mountain in the Lin’an Prefecture was a native of the Tiantai region, born into the Chen clan. In his childhood, he relied upon the Huguo [Monastery].
Sengchu shaved his head and at nineteen went to Guoqing Temple, where he visited Master Jishiguang and attained a sudden, clear realization.
He subsequently visited Dayuan at Wanshou Temple in Mingzhou. Dayuan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Tiantai.
Dayuan asked, "Have you seen Master Zhiyi? The Master replied, "Even now, he is not lacking. Dayuan asked, "Why then is he right under your own feet?"
The Master said, "Right before your face, you have missed it. Yuan said, "This Honored One flourishes without weeding, and stands straight without support. One day, he took his leave and departed.
As Yuan saw him off at the gate, he patted the Master on the back and said, "The treasure house is near; this city is not real. The Master did not nod in acknowledgment.
He then went to Yuzhang to visit Dian-niu, traveling by way of Yunju. Snow and wind blocked the road, and he sat there for forty-two days.
At the first hour of the noon period, the sound of the wooden board rang out with a sharp *keng*. Suddenly, he attained great enlightenment.

Upon arriving at the gate, Dian-niu pointed specifically at the Master and said, "Where have you seen gods and ghosts come from? The Master replied, "I heard the sound of the board at Yunju and came. Dian-niu asked, "What is it?"
The Master said, "Shatter empty space; it has no handle at all. Niu said, "The matter beyond this is not yet resolved.

Later, after taking up residence, he ascended the hall and cited the teaching: "As it is said in the scriptures, 'If one sees me by form, or seeks me by sound...'"
"This person walks a deviant path and cannot see the Tathāgata. Although it is thus, it is precisely like catching a mouse and breaking an oil jar.
Master Huai said, "Where are your eyes? Although he thus exposes the old Śākyamuni, what can be done?
He is still licking his fingers with a pinch of incense. If it were Tu-du, it would not be so; he would not seek through forms or sounds.
"It is not an obstacle. Amidst the shadows of a hundred flowers, one embroiders mandarin ducks. Since learning the secret of the golden needle, one may let the wind blow as it will;
the fragrance fills one’s sleeves. When the Master was about to pass away, he ascended the seat to bid farewell to the assembly and instructed his disciples to offer a written memorial for him.

As the Master sat upright and listened intently, when the words "May you enjoy the offering" were reached, he broke into a smile. Two days later, he bathed, changed his robes, and gathered the assembly.
He spoke in verse: "The four great elements have now dispersed; smoke and clouds return as they please. On an autumn night of frost and moonlight, its radiance shines across ten thousand li.
Shortly thereafter, he passed away peacefully. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the foot of the Eastern Ridge.
The monk asked, "What is the source of the Great Way? The Master said, "The Yellow River has nine bends.
The monk asked, "What is the decree that cannot be transgressed? The Master said, "An iron snake cannot be pierced. As the monk was about to speak further—
[The student] deliberated [on this]. The Master then struck him.

Chan Master Wanshan Xinwen Tanben of Taizhou was a native of Yongjia. While residing at Jiangxin, he ascended the hall after recovering from an illness.

"Vimalakīrti, while ill, exhausted all principles in his discourse. Longxiang, while ill, suffered from incessant coughing; though he coughed incessantly, he exhausted all principles in his discourse.
Though he exhausted all principles in his discourse, he coughed incessantly. Do you all recognize the meaning within this?"

The meaning is not yet there. Originally, the long river gathered cold winds; instead, you have caused the pillar to suffer from a headwind. Entering the hall, he said: "To see it once is to see it at once:
an octagonal millstone turns in the void. To obtain it once is to obtain it forever: vermilion and cinnabar are as black as ink.
The autumn wind blows over the Wei River—this has already fallen within the three phrases of Yunmen. Fallen leaves fill Chang'an; how many [can truly perceive them]?
Now, you have been deceived by your own eyes. [The Master] held up his fly-whisk and said: "Whether you can be deceived or cannot be deceived, it all rests in the hands of Wanyan.
Do you see? On Flower Peak, the moon embraces the Hand-Waving Stone; at the Broken Bridge, the water falls over the Body-Abandoning Cliff.
A monk asked: "What was the meaning of Baizhang rolling up the mat? The Master said: "Drawing the bow after the thief has fled. The Governor of Siming presented snow... [text ends]
Dong commanded the Master to preside over it. The Master declined with a verse, saying: "In the midst of the noisy basket, I have just found respite;
But now the drum has retreated, yet its beat does not cease. Do not take the thousand-fathom snow of Nanyue Peak To come once more and exchange for my pair of eyes."
Chan Master Tian Tong Cihang Liaopu of Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The scorching heat is like being burned, impossible to restrain;
it blazes so fiercely that it seems as if gold were melting. Beyond the night-bright curtain, no one arrives; the numinous tree stands far off, turning its shade green.
He ascended the hall again and said: "Long rain has not ceased; half-asleep and half-awake—this may be called heaven and earth merging in harmony."
"Virtue! The sun and moon harmonize their brilliance; the four seasons harmonize their order; the ghosts and spirits harmonize their auspiciousness and misfortune.
He then shouted, "Stop! Stop! The inner trigram is already formed; do not seek further outer images! He struck his staff on the ground and said, "Just now you cast 'Thunder over Heaven:

Great Strength' (Lèitiān Dàzhuàng); now it has transformed into 'Earth over Fire: Illumination in Obscurity' (Dìhuǒ Míngyī). He ascended the hall and said, "The ox-hide drum covers the pillar; the pillar makes a chirping sound."
A chirping sound. The lantern feigns ignorance; its empty brightness shines of itself. The aged *chifen* (glazed roof-ornaments) atop the palace ridge hears this and laughs aloud.
At the side-gate, they lean their ears to listen, then climb up and circle about, striking it. It is like the ten-day chrysanthemum: once fully blossomed, who needs it? Aha-ha!
It is not necessarily that the autumn fragrance withers in a single night. An iron smoothing-iron for brewing tea is not the same as a cauldron. The Room.

But what if it is the middle of the third watch, and a person's face looks like a thief’s, while a thief’s face looks like a person’s? How do you distinguish between them? He ascended the hall and said:

"Guanyin Rock is jingling and clinking; Taibai Stone is ting-ting and dong-dong. The caterpillars on the vegetables in West Garden seem unfit for eating, yet the flowers blooming in East Valley are truly reckless."

If you cannot discern this, Xuefeng will overturn your rice bucket; if you can discern it, Ganji will prostrate before the steamer. *Pauses.* Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
"When Deshan enters the gate, he immediately strikes with his staff; when Linji enters the gate, he immediately shouts. At the place where Linji shouts, it is right at the tip of Deshan’s staff."

Deaf! When Deshan wielded his staff, Linji’s eyes were blinded by his shout. Although one strike and one lift are entirely life-giving and entirely killing, [Linji] then let out a shout and struck the ground once with his staff, saying: "I dare ask you all: is this life or is it death?
After a long silence, he said: "A gentleman may be eight."
Chan Master Zonghui of Xiyuan in Nanjian Prefecture was a native of Wuzhou. Having long relied upon Master Wushi, he attained a profound realization of the Dharma-patience (*dharmakṣānti*).
Once, when a temple monk reported a violation of the tea prohibition to the authorities, the officials arrested the administrative official (*karmadāna*).
The Master said to the assembly, "If we do not plead his case, the guilt will fall upon me; yet if we plead it ourselves, he will instead suffer punishment. I cannot bear to do this. He then ordered—
He struck the drum and ascended the seat. He spoke a verse, saying: "The county official’s summons never pauses; how can one compare it to the clarity of long-past affairs?
Previously there was a song of non-arising; rejoice that today its melody has been perfected. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
National Preceptor Tantan of Goryeo succeeded to the throne at a young age. He deeply revered the Vehicle of the Patriarchs (Zongcheng).

While traveling by sea, he encountered the merchant Fang Jingren, who brought back from Siming the recorded sayings of Wushi. Upon reading them, the Master attained enlightenment. He immediately abdicated his position and shaved his head.

He then composed a letter containing the essentials of the teachings and four verses on the four deportments (*catur-īryāpatha*), instructing Jingren to present them to Wushi. Wushi replied: "The Buddhas and Patriarchs..."
He appeared in the world and did not bestow a single dharma upon others; rather, he caused them to have faith, awaken, realize, and arrive [at truth] for themselves.

Possessing great knowledge and vision, he spoke according to what he saw and acted according to what he spoke. The mountains, rivers, the great earth, and the grasses, trees, and forests all bear witness to this together;
it has been so for a long time. Later, there was also the transmission of the Dharma lineage. His writings state briefly: "Birth..."

The Dead Sea is vast; eons pass away together within it. To encounter a master of one’s own fundamental portion and have that dharma verified and confirmed by means of the seal of the three essentials is truly what is meant by "a blind turtle encountering the hole in a floating log."
Chan Master Wuzhu Ben of Longhua in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Guǎngdé. He ascended the hall and raised the following case:

When the Great Master Yúnmén held up a sesame cake and said, “I only provide offerings for those from the Two Zhè regions; I do not provide offerings for those from the north,” the assembly remained silent.
Yúnmén himself provided a substitute response, saying, “The weather is cold and the days are short; two people share one bowl. The Master [Wuzhu] remarked, “The old man of Shàoyáng...”
"Han" means "there is an echo within. When the needle pricks the spot of pain, if you examine it closely, it turns into a poisonous drug.
Do you all understand? Half is south of the Yellow River, half is north of the Yellow River; a single expanse of empty stillness, as black as ink.
To contemplate this in cold silence brings one to the brink of despair. How vexing is this old thief Yunmen! Thief! Thief! [He] descended from the seat and did not even go on patrol through the hall.

Chan Master Ji of Dongshan in Linjiang County was a successor of Chan Master Lin of Daochang. When Li Chaoling and his nephew, the lay practitioner Xianglin (Xiang Gongzi Yin), went to visit him, they asked: "When the 'house-thief' troubles one, what then? The Master said, "Who is the house-thief? Li replied, "I am. The Master said, "If you are it, who is troubling whom? Li was at a loss for words. The Master then said, "The thief has gone; you may close the door. Li bowed. The Master then asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Li replied, "The sky is blue, the clouds are white. The Master said, "You have already been robbed. Li again asked, "What about the patriarchs and Buddhas? The Master said, "They too have been robbed. Li said, "How can one avoid being robbed? The Master said, "If you wish to avoid being robbed, you must first recognize the thief. Li said, "How does one recognize the thief? The Master said, "The thief is right here—do not look for him elsewhere. Li said, "How can one subdue the thief? The Master said, "If you wish to subdue the thief, you must first know where he hides. Li said, "Where does he hide? The Master said, "He hides in the place where you do not look. Li said, "How can one capture the thief? The Master said, "If you wish to capture the thief, you must first know how to use the net. Li said, "How does one use the net? The Master said, "The net is spread out before you—do not wait for the thief to enter. Li said, "What if the thief does not enter? The Master said, "If the thief does not enter, you will never find him. Li said, "What if the thief is already caught? The Master said, "If the thief is caught, you must not let him go. Li said, "How does one deal with the thief after he is caught? The Master said, "After the thief is caught, you must cut off his head. Li said, "How does one cut off his head? The Master said, "If you wish to cut off his head, you must first know where the neck is. Li said, "Where is the neck? The Master said, "The neck is right here—do not seek it in the four elements. Li said, "How does one sever the neck? The Master said, "If you wish to sever the neck, you must first know how to wield the sword. Li said, "How does one wield the sword? The Master said, "The sword is held in your hand—do not wait for the thief to appear. Li said, "What if the thief does not appear? The Master said, "If the thief does not appear, the sword will be useless. Li said, "What if the thief is slain? The Master said, "If the thief is slain, you must bury him deep. Li said, "How does one bury him? The Master said, "If you wish to bury him, you must first know where the grave is. Li said, "Where is the grave? The Master said, "The grave is right here—do not dig elsewhere. Li said, "How does one perform the burial? The Master said, "If you wish to perform the burial, you must first know how to turn the earth. Li said, "How does one turn the earth? The Master said, "The earth is turned over before you—do not wait for the body to be placed. Li said, "What if the body is not placed? The Master said, "If the body is not placed, the burial will be incomplete. Li said, "What if the burial is complete? The Master said, "If the burial is complete, you must build a stupa. Li said, "How does one build a stupa? The Master said, "If you wish to build a stupa, you must first know how to lay the foundation. Li said, "How does one lay the foundation? The Master said, "The foundation is laid beneath your feet—do not seek it in the mountains or forests. Li said, "How does one erect the stupa? The Master said, "If you wish to erect the stupa, you must first know how to raise the spire. Li said, "How does one raise the spire? The Master said, "The spire is raised above your head—do not wait for the work to be finished. Li said, "What if the work is finished? The Master said, "If the work is finished, you must offer incense and flowers. Li said, "How does one offer incense and flowers? The Master said, "If you wish to offer incense and flowers, you must first know how to prostrate. Li said, "How does one prostrate? The Master said, "Prostration is performed with the body—do not wait for the mind to be empty. Li said, "What if the mind is not empty? The Master said, "If the mind is not empty, the prostration will be false. Li said, "What if the prostration is true? The Master said, "If the prostration is true, you must receive the blessing. Li said, "How does one receive the blessing? The Master said, "The blessing is received within yourself—do not seek it outside. Li said, "What if the blessing is received? The Master said, "If the blessing is received, you must maintain it throughout your life. Li said, "How does one maintain it throughout one's life? The Master said, "Maintaining it throughout one's life means never forgetting the thief. Li said, "What if the thief is forgotten? The Master said, "If the thief is forgotten, you will fall back into delusion. Li said, "What if delusion arises? The Master said, "If delusion arises, you must recognize it as the thief. Li said, "How does one recognize it? The Master said, "Recognizing it is simply seeing that the thief is not other than yourself. Li said, "What if I am the thief? The Master said, "If you are the thief, there is no one to be troubled. Li said, "What if there is no one to be troubled? The Master said, "If there is no one to be troubled, then who is asking these questions? Li was struck with realization. He then composed a verse: "The thief is the master; the master is the thief. If you wish to know the thief, look at the thief. The thief is not in the mountains or forests; the thief is not in the rivers or lakes. The thief is not in the heavens or the earth; the thief is not in the sun or the moon. The thief is not in the past, present, or future; the thief is not in the six senses or the five aggregates. The thief is not in the twelve links of dependent origination; the thief is not in the eighteen realms. The thief is not in the eighty-four thousand afflictions; the thief is not in the three poisons or the eight winds. The thief is not in the ten stages of a bodhisattva; the thief is not in the four fruits of arhatship. The thief is not in the two vehicles or the three bodies; the thief is not in the ten powers or the four fearlessnesses. The thief is not in the eighteen unique qualities; the thief is not in the eighty minor marks. The thief is not in the thirty-two major marks; the thief is not in the six perfections. The thief is not in the four foundations of mindfulness; the thief is not in the four right efforts. The thief is not in the four bases of psychic power; the thief is not in the five faculties. The thief is not in the five powers; the thief is not in the seven factors of enlightenment. The thief is not in the eightfold noble path; the thief is not in the three gates of liberation. The thief is not in the four dhyānas or the four formless absorptions; the thief is not in the nine successive stages of cessation. The thief is not in the ten thousand dharmas; the thief is not in the myriad phenomena. The thief is not in the scriptures or the commentaries; the thief is not in the sutras or the treatises. The thief is not in the precepts or the meditation; the thief is not in the wisdom or the liberation. The thief is not in the Dharma-body; the thief is not in the Sambhogakaya. The thief is not in the Nirmanakaya; the thief is not in the Dharmadhatu. The thief is not in the emptiness or the form; the thief is not in the permanence or the impermanence. The thief is not in the self or the non-self; the thief is not in the purity or the impurity. The thief is not in the existence or the non-existence; the thief is not in the coming or the going. The thief is not in the birth or the death; the thief is not in the arising or the ceasing. The thief is not in the cause or the effect; the thief is not in the beginning or the end. The thief is not in the near or the far; the thief is not in the large or the small. The thief is not in the high or the low; the thief is not in the bright or the dark. The thief is not in the sound or the form; the
[The Master] raised his fist. The Master said, "The thief’s body has already been exposed. Li said, "Do not try to deceive people. The Master said, "The evidence is right here.
Li was speechless. The Master showed him with a verse: "The domestic thief vexes the person—what can be done? Even the thousand sages turn their faculties back for his sake.
Pervading the world and pervading space, he leaves no trace; Without dependence, without abiding, he cuts off all nets and snares. Thief! Thief!"
Fierce generals and heroic soldiers cannot capture him; he is suspected of killing the old Chan masters of the world. He makes the ancient Maitreya in the bustling marketplace laugh to tears.
Stop! Stop! There is no need to seek with the mind outward. In a single glance, you turn back and the thief’s body is revealed;
caught with the stolen goods, he has no peer in the world. No peer in the world—truly worthy of veneration. From this point on, one no longer boasts of clever skills; all is peaceful and secure.
When the family business flourishes, the myriad phenomena of the universe clap their hands in unison.
Chan Master Lǎn'ān Dàoshū of Língyǐn Monastery in Lín'ān Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Huì of Dào-chǎng; he was the son of the Xú family of Sī'ān in Wúxīng. Initially, he resided at...
At which mountain? Subsequently, he moved to Huazang. At the beginning of the Longxing era, an imperial edict summoned him to reside at Lingyin.

Emperor Xiaozong invited him to the inner palace and inquired about the essentials of the Way of Chan. The Master replied: "This matter lies within Your Majesty’s own majestic daily life where you respond to circumstances;

fundamentally, it is free from the confusion of arising and ceasing in cognition and view, and devoid of the distinction between sage and ordinary, delusion and enlightenment. Simply maintain right mindfulness, and then—"

When one accords with the Way and the emotions are withdrawn from external objects, karma cannot bind them. Once the maladies of dullness and agitation are entirely eliminated, one naturally forgets the intent of question and answer;
how much more so now, while occupying the position of the Regent Bodhisattva within the radiant light of the Buddha’s Prajñā—what could not be seen?
The Master nodded his head several times. He then addressed the assembly, saying: "The immortal Zhang Guolao rides a donkey..."
He passed through the marketplace; one could only hear the splashing sound of his hooves. Who would have known they were made of paper?
Later, he retired to the Mingjiao Yong'an Hermitage, living in carefree contentment. He inscribed a verse on the wall that read: "The plum blossoms in the snow are the news of spring;
The moonlight upon the pond is the spirit of the night. It seems there has been no fine delight these years past; Do not take this family tradition and show it to others."
In the eighth month of the Bingshen year of the Chunxi era, he manifested a slight illness, wrote a verse, and passed away. He was interred in the Yong’an Pagoda.

This was the day when the Head Seat Wuchu of Guangde County’s Guangxiao Monastery—successor to Chan Master Ming of Guangxiao—was presiding over the assembly from his seat and presented the public discourse on the dialogue concerning the wind and the banner. When he reached the section on Ren...
This is where the mind moves; thus he said, "When the Patriarch spoke thus, he deceived an entire shipload of people. Monks of the present day must not understand it in this way either.
Since you must not understand it in this way, after all, how is it? After a long silence, he said, "In the sixth month, it is good for making soy sauce;
one must simply avoid putting too much salt in it."

The Dharma successor of Chan Master Wannian Ben of the seventeenth generation under Nanyue, Chan Master Xian of Lin’gang Hermitage in Wenzhou, ascended the hall and said: He cited Chongshou’s instruction to the assembly, which said: "Recognize the bench."
"It is more than a full cubit [in height]. Yunmen said, "If you recognize the bench, heaven and earth are vastly different.
The Master said, "The old fellow Chongshou sits people to death; the Great Master Yunmen runs people to death. Longming, however, is not like this:
"If you recognize the bench, its four legs rest firmly on the ground; when you wish to sit, you sit; when you wish to rise, you rise. He ascended the hall and cited [the preceding exchange].
A Verse on Zhaozhou’s Examination of the Old Woman: A lady of ice and snow, her countenance most extraordinary; She constantly takes up her jade flute and blows toward the people.
Within the melodies, boundless hearts are moved; To the Lord of Spring alone, she grants the honor of being the foremost branch.
Chan Master Daopeiyi of Daming Monastery in Tanzhou was a native of Kuaiji. He ascended the hall and said: "The trees have shed their leaves and the sky is empty;
the heavens are cold and the waters are frozen. The Old Śākyamuni has nowhere to hide his body.

Demolishing the eastern fence to patch the western wall, he runs straight into Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Unobstructed Vision, who requests instruction on the Samādhi of Buddha-Recitation. How truly extraordinary! Yet [the Master] replies: 'Golden light.'"
Mingyun: After the formal session, go for tea. Entering the hall: The Old Barbarian opened up a single path;
how direct it is! He simply said: "Rest, and that is Bodhi; the nature is pure and the mind is luminous; it is not obtained from others.
Yet later generations failed to find its gate, racing north and south, traveling east and west, exhausting years and seasons without a single place of rest. Do you people still...?
"Can you rest? Cease! Cease! [The Master] ascended the hall and said: "I cite a case: One day, Master Huìtáng asked a monk, 'Where have you come from? The monk replied, 'From Nánxióng Prefecture.

Huìtáng said, 'What do you intend to do upon coming here? The monk said, 'To visit venerable elders. Huìtáng said, 'It would be better for you to return home. The monk asked, 'I do not know, Master; what is the meaning behind your command that I return home?

Huìtáng said, 'In one's native village, there are three..."* *(Note: The source text appears to be truncated. The final phrase likely refers to the "Three Sages of the Village," a common Zen metaphor for the Buddha-nature inherent within all beings.)*
He bought a piece of salted fish, about the size of a palm. The Master said, "I would rather have my body shattered into fine dust than ever again blind the eyes of a monk.
Huìtáng was a notch better; some people say it was because he could not forget what he was familiar with.

There was no place for further conversation. He ascended the hall and presented the kōan of the King of Kasmīra questioning Venerable Siṃha regarding the emptiness of the aggregates (*skandha-śūnyatā*).
The Master offered this verse: "When did the Venerable One ever attain the emptiness of the aggregates? The King of Kasmīra needlessly cut down the spring breeze himself.
After the rain, the peach blossoms have already fallen away; They have dyed the flowing waters of a mountain stream crimson."
The Five Lamps Compiled (Wǔdēng Huìyuán), Volume XVIII and Volume XIX:
The Eleventh Generation under Nanyue.
Chan Master Yangqi Fanghui of Yanzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Shishuang Yuan.
He was the son of the Lü family in Yichun of that commandery. From his youth, he was alert and quick-witted; by the time he reached the age of twenty, he had already attained maturity.

He did not occupy himself with brush or inkstone, but was registered as a tax collector for trade. When his tax quotas were highest yet he was reprimanded for dereliction of duty, he fled by night to Mount Jiufeng in Ruizhou.
There, he felt as though he were returning to a place he had visited before; overcome with affection, he could not bear to leave and subsequently shaved his head.

Whenever he read the sutras, his mind merged with them and his spirit attained realization. He humbled himself to seek instruction from veteran masters. When Ciming moved from Nanyuan to Daowu and then to Shichuang, the Master served as his assistant in both places.
Regarding the affairs of the General Office (Zongyuan): although he had relied upon him for a long time, no instructions or insights had yet been granted.

Whenever he consulted him, Yuanming would say, "The affairs of the storehouse are many; go for now. On another day, when he asked again, Yuanming said, "In time, the *jiansi* (superintendent) will have disciples and grand-disciples filling the world;
why be in such a hurry? One day, just as Yuanming was about to go out, it suddenly began to rain. The Master scouted him on a small path; having seen him, he seized him.
Zhuzhu said, "This old fellow must speak for me today; if you do not, I will beat you. Ming said, "Abbot, if you know such a thing, then let it be.
Before he had finished speaking, the Master attained great enlightenment and prostrated himself on the muddy ground.
He asked, "What is it like when we meet on a narrow path? Ming said, "You just get out of the way! I have somewhere I need to go. The Master then returned.
The next day, he prepared his formal robes and proceeded to the abbot’s quarters to offer thanks. Yuanmiao scolded him, saying, "Not yet.
From then on, whenever Yuanmiao went out for a walk in the mountains, the Master would invariably wait for him to emerge; even if it was late, he would strike the drum to assemble the community.

Yuanmiao would then return in haste and say angrily, "In the monastic groves, one does not ascend the seat in the evening. Where did you get this rule? The Master replied, "This is the 'evening session' (wanchan) of Fenyang. What do you mean?"

Is this not like a measuring line? One day, when Master Ming was ascending the hall, the Teacher came forward and asked: "An elusive bird warbles its song; as it leaves the clouds to enter the jumbled peaks, what then?
Ming said: "I walk through the wild weeds; you, again, have entered a deep village. The Teacher said:
"The official does not permit even a needle to pass; let me ask one more question. Ming then gave a shout. The Teacher said: "A fine shout! Ming shouted again. The Teacher also shouted.
Baofu Ming let out two consecutive shouts. The Master prostrated himself. Ming said, "This matter can only be taken up by one who is a true person.
The Master shook his sleeves and departed. When Ming moved to Xinghua, the Master took his leave to return to Jiufeng. Later, monastics and laypeople welcomed him to reside at Yangqi.
Next, he moved to Yun’gai. On the day he accepted the invitation, he held up his dharma robe and showed it to the assembly, saying, "Do you understand?
If you do not, today you have, for no reason, entered the ranks of the water buffalo. Do you know where? At Jiuxiu in Yunchang, at Pingshi, and at Yangqi.
He then ascended the seat. At that time, a monk came forward, and the Master said, "Before the old fisherman has cast his hook, the leaping scales..."

A wave came up. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "I did not believe you. The monk clapped his hands and returned to the assembly. The Master said, "How much wind from the Dragon King can he endure?
A monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed? The Master said, "If there is a horse, ride it; if there is no horse, walk.
The monk said, "An elder with such youthful vigor possesses great strategic skill. The Master said, "I am mindful that you are advanced in years."
"I grant you thirty blows. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A three-legged donkey prancing on its hooves.
The monk said, "Is it not just this very thing? The Master said, "Elder of Hunan. Then he asked, "Is there anyone else who wishes to ask a question?"
Come forth and meet me! Yangqi’s life today rests in your hands; you may drag him about as you please, pulling him this way and that. Why is this so?
A man of great character must make his decision before the assembly. Do not act like someone pressing down on a gourd underwater in secret.
Bring it forth for testing in public; do not let your face turn red. Is there anyone who can do so?
"Is there anyone? Come forth and let us resolve this! If not, Yangqi has lost ground today. The Master then descended from his seat.
Monk Jiufeng Qin held him back and said, "Today I am delighted to find a fellow practitioner.
The Master asked, "What is the matter of being a fellow practitioner? Qin replied, "Jiufeng plows the furrow; Yangqi drags the harrow. The Master said, "At such a time as this..."
Yangqi was before him; Jiufeng was before him. As Qin hesitated, the Master pushed them open and said, "I thought we were fellow practitioners;
it turns out you are not. A monk asked, "When both person and dharmas are completely cast aside, that is not yet the ultimate standard for a patch-robed monk.

When both Buddha and patriarchs are simultaneously extinguished, that is still a point of doubt for a student. I wonder, how do you, Reverend, guide people? The Master said, "You simply want to test me."
A new elder said, "In that case, one should burn freshly cut green wood along with its leaves. The Master said, "Seven times nine is sixty-three.
A monk asked, "What was the intent behind the ancients' 'facing the wall'? The Master said, "The people of the West do not understand the language of Tang.
He ascended the hall and said: "Mist locks the long sky; wind arises in the great wilderness. The hundred grasses and trees let out the roar of the Great Lion, expounding the Dharma."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā: the Buddhas of the three periods of time turn the Great Dharma Wheel beneath the feet of you all.
If you can understand this, your efforts will not have been in vain; if you do not understand, do not say that the terrain of Yangqi Mountain is steep—there is yet a higher peak ahead.
[He] ascended the hall and cited an ancient kōan to bestow upon the assembly. It is truly excellent.
Jiurui said: "The mouth is fit only for eating rice. Entering the hall, he said: "Treading upon a scale-weight, as hard as iron; a mute man has a dream—whom can he tell it to?
Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, waves surge to the heavens; within the great ocean, one is scorched by fire. *Chan*! Entering the hall.
Yangqi’s One Essential Matter: a thousand sages share its wondrousness. He bestows it upon the great assembly; striking the meditation bench once, he says:
"Truly, one loses sight of it. *Chan*! Ascending the hall, he says: "Yangqi’s single phrase—look with quickened eyes! On the long benches, picking up the spoon and grasping the chopsticks.
Ascending the hall, he takes up his staff and says: "The one is all; all is the one. He makes a single stroke and says: "Mountain."
The great earth and the rivers crumble into a hundred fragments. What, then, are the nostrils of all you people? After a long silence, he said:
"The sword leaves its precious sheath because of injustice; the medicine comes from the golden jar to save the sick. He gave a shout and struck the ground once.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Yangqi has no core meaning. He plows the fields to earn his meal. Old Gautama is but a dream-teller. What?"
Seeking traces in their dwelling places—*he lets out a shout* and *strikes the meditation seat once*. Ascending the hall: "Living at Yangqi with meager merit, my strength has declined over the years.
The cold wind withers the fallen leaves; yet I rejoice that an old friend has returned. La la li! Taking up this head of dead firewood, let us for now remain where there is no smoke or flame.
Ascending the hall: "Just settled at Yangqi, the walls of the house are thin; the entire floor is covered in [leaves]."

Xue Zhenzhu shrank his neck and sighed again. After a long while, he said, "I am reminded of the ancients who dwelt beneath the trees. Ascending the hall, he said: "In this matter, Yungai is not as good;
his preaching of Chan is like swallowing a chestnut. If you can understand it at this point, the Buddha-dharma and the world will be as far apart as heaven and earth.
Ascending the hall, he threw down his staff and said: "The Old Śākyamuni sits cross-legged and laughs in secret."
Yungai spoke at random: "Even though the world is level and plain, one must still use diligence to compensate for lack of skill. He ascended the hall and said:
"When Śākyamuni was first born, he took seven steps, looked around in the four directions, pointed one finger toward heaven, and pointed one finger toward the earth.
Nowadays, all you patch-robed monks merely imitate his form; you simply say, 'In the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am the honored one.'"
"Venerable One, Cloud Canopy did not spare his own life, yet he also provided a model for all people," he said.
Then he addressed the assembly: "When the Yang energy arises, there is no hard ground. He held up his staff and said, "This staff is now displaying its spiritual powers before you all.
He threw it down and said, "It has truly caused heaven and earth to tremble."
It splits; the mountains and peaks tremble. Do you understand? Has it not been said: "The wisdom of all wisdoms is pure"? [Yunmen] struck the meditation seat and said:
"Thirty years from now, do not say before those with clear eyes that Yangqi has a dragon’s head and a snake’s tail. A monk asked: "When one parts the clouds and sees the sun, what then?
The Master said: "Those who come from the east sit in the east. The monk asked: "Heaven attains the One and becomes clear. The Master said: "The earth attains the One and becomes vast."
"The earth attains tranquility by obtaining the One. The patch-robed monk who obtains the One—what can he do? The Master said: "The mouth of the alms-bowl points toward the sky.

On the anniversary of Ciming’s death, when the assembly had just gathered, the Master placed his two fists against his head before the portrait, drew a line with his sitting cloth, struck a circular mark, burned incense, stepped back three paces, and assumed the posture of a woman.
The person bowed. The Head Seat said, "Stop making such strange antics. The Master said, "How about you, Head Seat? The Head Seat said, "Preceptor, stop making such strange antics.
The Master said, "A rabbit eating cow's milk. The Second Seat stepped forward, drew a circle, and then offered incense.
He also withdrew two paces and performed a woman’s bow. The Master stepped forward and made a gesture as if listening. As the Second Seat hesitated, the Master—
He gave a slap and said, "This lacquer bucket has been acting recklessly! When Master Longxing Zizhou passed away, a monk arrived to deliver his final letter.
The Master asked: 'When the World-Honored One entered nirvana, he revealed his two feet from within the coffin. Now that you, Master, have returned to the truth, what sign do you leave behind?'"
The monk remained silent. The Master struck his chest and cried out, “Heaven! Heaven! He then questioned a monk in the hall, “How will you swallow the thorny chestnut?
How will you penetrate the diamond circle? One day, three newly arrived monks came.
The Master said, “When three travel together, there must be one who possesses wisdom. He held up his sitting cloth and said, “Head monk, call this thing...”
"What is it? he asked. "It is a sitting mat," he replied. The Master said, "Is that so? "Yes," he replied. The Master spoke again, "What do you call it? He replied, "[A sitting mat]."

[The Master] was sitting on his meditation mat. Looking around to left and right, he said, "The head of the assembly has eyes after all. He then questioned the second person: "If one wishes to travel a thousand li, the first step is the beginning. What is this very first phrase? [The Master] finished [speaking]. He asked the third person: "Where did you depart from recently? He replied, "Nanyuan. The Master said, "Today Yangqi has been exposed by you, Senior Monk.
Sit and have some tea. He asked a monk: "Amidst the fallen leaves piled like clouds, where did you depart this morning? He replied, "Guanyin."
The Master said, "Regarding the phrase 'under Guanyin’s heels,' how would you say it? A monk replied, "I have already seen it just now.
The Master asked, "How was that matter of seeing it? The monk had no response. The Master said, "Let the second seat act as the head monk and speak for him.
He also had no response. The Master said, "Both are merely obstructing one another. Addressing the assembly, he said, "The spring breeze is like a blade."

The spring rain is like rich cream; the laws of nature proceed in their proper course, and the sentiments of all things are stirred. You say, "Planting one's feet firmly on the ground"—how will you speak?
Speak it out! Try to speak it where the east surges up and the west sinks away. Even if you could speak it, it would still be just a verse by Liangshan.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "When body and mind are pure, all environments are pure; when all environments are pure, the body [is pure]."
With a pure mind, do you still know where the Old Man of Yangqi has gone? "Losing a coin in the river, one must fish for it in the river.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The scenery is newly bright, and all things are at ease. In every step, there is a thousand-fold Maitreya;
in every movement, there is a Śākyamuni everywhere. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are both right here. Is there anyone among you who will not be deceived?"
It is said that Yangqi was selling flour mixed with bran. Nevertheless, it is like a needle contained within a cloth bag.
To the assembly he said: "Snow! Snow! Everywhere it shines with brilliant purity. The Yellow River is frozen and locked, cutting off even the finest currents.
Within the blazing light of the sun, one must burst forth. One must burst forth! Nanda eats thorns upon his head; from beneath Vajrapāṇi’s feet, the stream flows out."
Xuè. In the first year of the Huángyù era, he entered nirvana. His stupa was enshrined at Yúngài.
He was the twelfth-generation descendant of Nányuè and the dharma heir of Chan Master Yángqí Huì.
Chan Master Shouduan of Baoyun in Shuzhou was the son of the Ge family of Hengyang. In his youth, he devoted himself to calligraphy and literature;

Suddenly, if there were a man who came forth and said, "White Cloud, stop your drowsy chatter," everyone should take note of this turn of phrase. — Three Buddhas.

While attending his master at a pavilion, they conversed late into the night. Upon returning, the lamp had already been extinguished. In the darkness, the Master said, "Each of you must offer a turning phrase.
Fojian said, "A variegated phoenix dances in the crimson sky. Foyan said, "An iron snake lies across the ancient road."
Foguo said, "Look beneath your feet. The Master replied, "It is you, Keqin, who will extinguish my lineage.
On the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month in the third year of the Chongning era, he ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying, "The Venerable Zhaozhou has a 'final phrase.
How do you understand it? Come forward and speak. If you can understand it, you will be free and at ease without hindrance. As he spoke...
"Perhaps not. How can this good matter be explained? After a long silence, he said, "It has been explained, yet you all simply do not know.
Do you wish to understand? The wealthy lament that a thousand mouths are too few; the poor regret that a single body is too many. Take care.
At that time, there was construction work at the mountain gate, so he went in person to supervise it and said, "Exert yourselves; I shall not come again."
He returned to his chamber, shaved his head and bathed his body. At dawn, he passed away in peace and auspiciousness. That evening, the mountains collapsed and rocks fell;
for forty li around, the cliffs and valleys shook and roared. Relics fell like rain during the cremation, and a stupa was erected on the southern slope of Mount Dongshan.
Chan Master Zhiben of Yungai Mountain in Tanzhou was the son of the Guo family in Ruizhou.
On the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked, "When the Buddhas appear in the world, the heavens rain down the four flowers; when the Master appears in the world, what auspicious signs are there?
The Master said, "A thousand hearings are not equal to one seeing. The monk asked, "What is it like after seeing? The Master said, "Blind. A monk asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master—
[The Master] said: "A household cannot be considered that of a gentleman if it lacks even the lowliest servants. [A monk] asked: "If one seeks the mind with the mind, how can it be found?
The Master said: "It is like a Persian learning the Chinese language. [A monk] asked: "What is the place where the student emerges?

The Master said: "Xuefeng was originally a man from Lingnan. [A monk] asked: "When presenting one's true face, what then? The Master said: "A scene of utter ugliness and clumsiness. [A monk] asked: "Every person..."
"I possess a single ancient mirror. What is the student’s ancient mirror? The Master said, "Bring it here and break it, and I will tell you. [The student] said, "It is already broken.
The Master said, "A bamboo shoot sprouting in winter in a foreign land. [The student] asked, "An ancient said, 'Speak that which cannot be practiced;
practice that which cannot be spoken. I do not know how one speaks that which cannot be practiced. The Master...
[The Master] said, "The mouth is beneath the feet. [The monk] asked, "Regarding that which cannot be spoken, how does one act? The Master said, "Tread upon your own tongue.
[The monk] asked, "I know you have long harbored a treasure within your bag; today, I beg to borrow it briefly for the stage. The Master said, "Just now, it was borrowed away by someone else.
He ascended the hall and said: "Those who depart have their nostrils reaching the heavens; those who come tread firmly upon the ground. Now tell me—"
"Where does the Patriarch’s intention lie? After a long silence, he said: "I have long harbored regret that spring has departed with no place to be found;
I know not how it has flowed into this very midst. Ascending the hall, he said: "The high platform’s core essence—open your mouth and it is right there.

But if it is already 'right there,' what core essence is there? The moon is cold, the wind is high; the waters are clear, the mountains are verdant. Ascending the hall again, he said: "Using a wedge to extract a wedge—what end is there to this?"
Rest. Desiring to attain rest, use one wedge to drive out another. (He lets out a shout. He ascends the hall and calls out loudly to his attendant.
