The Hall. His mouth is full, yet nothing comes forth; every word is perfectly clear. His eyes are full, yet there is nothing to be seen; mountain upon mountain, layers of chaotic green.
You do not understand the sound of the drum, let alone the tolling of the bell. (He lets out a shout. He ascends the hall:
The patriarchs were bold and outstanding; their descendants are cramped and petty. They have places to hide their heads, but no place to show their horns. I ask you, monks: [What is it?]
"How do you grope for it? He ascended the hall and, holding his staff horizontally across his chest, said:
"Teeth like swords, face like iron; eyes flashing lightning, the light never ceasing. Grasping ten thousand catties of thorny seeds, he casually knocks down the moon from the edge of heaven.
He struck once. A monk asked, "What is the man-eating lion? The Master said, "Before the Five Elders Peak. [The monk] said, "This one..."
"How could it possibly bite anyone? The Master said, "Today you have recovered your life. Ascending the hall, he said:
"With the Mount Sumeru upon one's head and the four great oceans under one's feet, a breath stirs wind and thunder, and movement gives rise to the five colors.
If you can recognize this person, let the years and months pass as they may. But tell me, who is it that recognizes this person? He gave a shout and said, "You servant boy!"
Chan Master Yongqi of Langya in Chuzhou was a native of Xiangyang. A monk asked, "Why does the person inside the hermitage not see what is outside the hermitage?
The Master said, "The neighbor to the east lights the lamp; the neighbor to the west sits in darkness.

The monk asked, "What is the matter inside the hermitage? The Master said, "Where are your eyes? The monk said, "I am bowing with palms joined at the main gate. The Master said, "What business do you have there?"
Sheshao said: "The waning moon falls at the end of the fifth watch; when dawn breaks, white clouds fly. This is clearly an event before one's eyes, yet it is not the mechanism of the present moment.
Since it is an event before one's eyes, why is it not the mechanism of the present moment? After a long silence, he said:
"From here to the Western Heaven, the road stretches ten thousand miles and more. Ascending the hall, after a long silence, he clapped his hands once and said: "A-ha!"
"Ha! A-he-he. Do you understand? Every dharma is fundamentally the Dharma. He then picked up his staff and said, "This here is the mountain monk’s staff;
which one is the fundamental Dharma? Can you definitively determine this? *He struck the ground once with the staff.*
A monk asked Chan Master Shu of Baofu in Yingzhou, "How was it before all Buddhas appeared in the world?
The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. The monk asked, "How is it after they have appeared? The Master said, "The great earth, mountains, and rivers.

The monk said, "In that case, it is the same as before. The Master said, "Beating bricks and striking tiles. Another asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "As large as a bowl."
The bowl was small. [The monk] asked, "When guests arrive, how will you receive them? The Master said, "One ladle, two ladles. [The monk] asked, "What about those who are not yet full?
The Master said, "Eat little; eat little. He asked, "What is the Great Way? The Master said, "In the midst of the bustling marketplace. [The monk] said, "..."
"What is it like to be one who walks the Way? The Master said, "Leave it for others to look upon. The monk asked, "What is Chan?
The Master said, "Autumn winds blow over the ancient ferry; the setting sun is unbearable to hear. The monk said, "I do not ask about this kind of Chan.

The Master said, "Which Chan are you asking about? The monk said, "The Chan of the Patriarchs. The Master said, "Beneath the pine shadows outside the Nanhua Pagoda, drinking dew and chanting in the wind."
More. A question was asked: "What is the true and authentic path? The Master said: "Go out the gate and look at the milestone. He then continued:
"Where did Śākyamuni pass away in Kuśinagara? When has Maitreya ever been in Tuṣita? To seek Samantabhadra in the west is truly shameful;
to search for Mañjuśrī in the north is a source of grievance. Sitting upon Vairocana, sweat flows from his brow; walking while striking Guanyin, blood flows from his nose."
Turning his head, he felt for his carrying pole and said, "What a fine wooden-handled ceremonial tablet! He gave a shout and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Guo of Chongsheng Monastery in Yuanzhou ascended the hall and spoke on the public case of Shigong drawing his bow and setting his arrow to test the student's mettle.
He offered this verse: "For thirty years I have gripped my bow and arrow; As soon as Sanping arrived, I split open my chest. Half a Saint..."
People ultimately cannot attain it. When will one encounter the lute-string beyond the notes of Dadian?
Guo Xiangzheng, styled Gongfu, was a lay practitioner known as Jingkong. He delighted in the seclusion of springs and rocks and had no envy for worldly splendor.
Consequently, he went to visit Baiyun. As Baiyun ascended the hall, he said: "Last night, while upon my pillow, I composed a mountain verse to express my gratitude to Gongfu."
Mr. Gongfu is a great Confucian scholar and a long-time associate from his twenty years at Mount Lu. His diligent effort in visiting me from afar today must be presented to the assembly;
after I have finished speaking, you must clearly recount this to the various quarters. This verse is not merely to thank Mr. Gongfu the great scholar;
it is intended to strip away the flesh-and-blood sweatshirt from every monk in the world who possesses a nostril. Do not say otherwise.
He did not speak. Instead, he said: "The Great Man Above, Qiu Yi Ji; he transformed three thousand, seventy scholars; you, little student, eight or nine disciples;
well-composed benevolence, one may know propriety. The Master was deeply perplexed. Later, hearing a child reciting it, he suddenly attained realization.
He wrote to Yun to report this, and Yun replied with a verse: "To hide one's person, one need not contract the head; to withdraw one's traces, what need is there..."
He withdrew his feet. The golden crow traverses the vast heavens at midnight; the jade hare cannot catch up with him.

During the Yuanyou era, he went to Nanchan in Quzhou to visit Quan Wanjuan and requested to ascend the seat. The Master stepped forward, offered incense, and said: "A withered tree by the sea, once it enters my hands, becomes incense.
When burned within this brazier, it pierces horizontally through the nostrils of the Incense Accumulation Tathāgata. To perform such a great matter, one must..."
Only after announcing the transgression before the assembly can one truly attain it. The Elder Yunju had a seamless monk’s robe which he entrusted to Nanzen.
When the Zen Master put it on, it was neither too long nor too short; advancing, all Buddhas yielded their thrones; retreating, the waves of the sea became still.
Today, with a single yawn, the six kinds of earth tremors occurred. He then called out, "Great Assembly, do you understand?"
"When there is spirit, add to that spirit; where there is no elegance, be elegant. Yuanquan said, "We have been mutually obstructing one another.
The Master asked, "By whom was this brought about? At the beginning of the Chongning era, he went to Wuzu and requested that Wuzu ascend the seat.

The Master stepped forward, offered incense, and said, "This single portion of incense, burned within the brazier, is offered to my Dharma-elder brother, the Zen Master of the Hall. I prostrate myself..."
I pray that upon this expansive seat, you will part the opening of your face and manifest the form of our former master for others to depict.
Why is this so? "We met long ago by the cliffs of Baiyun; the affairs of those days and the present are not the same."
The night is still and the water cold, so the fish do not feed; a single brazier of incense drifts away from White Lotus Peak. The Patriarch then said: *Namo satvata paraya*.
Thus, thus—how many times have I gazed upon the yellow plum blossoms blooming amidst the snow while looking out over the white clouds at the mountain stream?
Not thus, not thus—the tender willows hang down golden threads; one must simply wait for the right moment. No.

The Master replied, "Wait until you can suck up all the water of the West River with a single mouthful, and then I will tell you. "O Assembly!
To suck up all the water of the West River with a single mouthful is to reach the very bottom of a ten-thousand-fathom deep abyss. A rickety footbridge is not Zhaozhou’s bridge; it is clear!"
"How can the moon and the clear breeze be compared? Later, he went to Baoning, where he was also invited to ascend the seat.

The Master held up the incense and said, "The Dharma drum has already sounded, and the precious incense has just been lit. At the gate of Yangqi’s crown, I request the Master to drive in the wedge once more.
Baoning struck his staff once and said, "The driving of the wedge is finished; may the assembly bear witness. He struck it once again and then descended from the seat.
He arrived at Yunju again and requested that Master Foyin ascend the seat. The official held up the incense and said: "Meeting on the ground of awakening—how early!
The foul-smelling monk’s robe is now cast off. If you wish to recognize the one mysterious phrase of Yunju, take care:
the donkey eats grass in the back garden. He called to the assembly, saying: "This single portion of incense goes up to heaven and scorches the earth! Foyin said: "Today..."
[Zhaozhou] was about to put on his robe when the Master [Yinju] slapped him right in the face and said: "Thank you, sir, for coming from a thousand li away to visit me;
we shall talk together of the deep bamboo paths of Mount Dongshan. I lend you a dragon to ride out of the cave; should you encounter a drought, let it bring down the rain.
He then threw down his staff and descended from the seat. As the official rose to bow, Yinju asked: "Have you caught the dragon? The official replied: "It is already here."

Master Yin said, "How do you ride? The Master snapped his fingers, made a dance-like gesture, and walked away. Master Yin clapped his hands and said, "Only this fellow has some measure of comparison."
Chan Master Zhuiyuan of Shousheng on Mount Yuezhang in Yingzhou, a successor of Chan Master Yong of Baoning, was asked by a monk: "I do not ask about the Patriarch’s intent coming from the West;
what is 'one color'? The Master said: "Before my eyes there is no *śrāmaṇera*; here there is no old monk. The monk said: "If that is so..."
"It is so. How should one understand this? The Master said, "Receive the meaning at the tip of the hook; do not fixate on the zero point of the scale.

He then said, "In every instance of question and answer, it is like striking a stone to produce sparks, flowing forth inexhaustible treasures of the Dharma for the three types of grass and two types of wood."
"Universally moistening its bounty"—this is letting go. "Clouds arise at the valley mouth; mist shrouds the vast sky"—this is holding fast.
Even the blue-eyed barbarian monk would have no recourse. Such proclamations as those of Shousheng are still merely the gate of transformation;
they do not yet constitute the very core of a patch-robed monk. I dare ask you all: what is this core of a patch-robed monk? After a long silence, he said: "Spread."
The needle opens both eyes; toward which end do you look?
Chan Master Chuwen of Shousheng Monastery in Wuzhen, Anji County, ascended the hall and held up his staff, saying:

The mountains shook; the waters were stirred until the waves overflowed. Suddenly, when he seized them firmly, every matter was governed by law and regulation. Where one wished to resist, one could not resist;
where one wished to bend, one could not bend. He suddenly called to the assembly, saying: "Do not say that there are eyes upon the staff as bright as the sun;
the radiance upon its surface is nothing but lacquer. With these words, he struck once. Entering the hall, he delivered a single thrust and a single jab.
Skin and bone joined together; every squeeze and every lift. Sticking to the hands and adhering to the feet. A flash of lightning, a spark from flint. Head drooping, tail drooping.
Faster than a split arrow or a chasing wind. Half-alive, half-dead. Striking and bumping against things. What eyebrows are there to seek? Bright head, dark head.
What kind of eyes are these? It is not like this at all. One is right in the middle of the way; even if one were to employ the total mechanism, one has not yet reached the further shore.
Even if it were utterly bare and starkly clear, with nothing to grasp, there would still be a trace of lingering attachment. When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, [it is so].
Furthermore, what is the use of making a fuss at the entrance? After a long silence, he said, "Heh! Keep some for eating.
On the day of the opening of the hall, Chan Master Baoji Zongying of Lingjushan in Xinzhou held his staff crosswise and said:
Great assembly, here there is neither kin nor stranger; naturally, one is not alone. There is neither within nor without;

Adapting the teaching to the faculties, they mutually interact. Look at the staff of Ratnakūṭa: its black lacquer shines with luster, its two ends perfectly corresponding.
"A-he-he! What words are these? After a long silence, he said, "Matters of the world should be judged by the standard of public justice;

This was ultimately excessive. Furthermore, a monk stepped forward from the assembly and drew a circle in the air. The Master made a single stroke with his hand. The monk performed a dance and returned to the assembly.

Regarding the meaning of the Dharma: if you can believe and attain this, every phenomenon is fundamentally and spontaneously perfected, and every thought-moment is entirely complete.
If you cannot believe it, then today, as I walk along, I shall not hesitate to swing my arm and speak these verses once more for you.
*He strikes once.* He descends from his seat.

Reaching this point, even those with eyes of iron and pupils of copper must be shattered into a hundred pieces. Is there any monk who does not shrink from peril? Come forth and try!"
As they were about to look, two monks came out together. The Master said, "A single arrow brings down two eagles.
The monks said, "We have not yet even asked our question; why are you in such a hurry? The Master said, "Are you perhaps monks from Silla? As the monks hesitated, the Master said:

[The Master] struck the pillar and said, "Strike! He asked, "What is the matter on the side before one has appeared in the world? The Master said, "A shrimp at the bottom of the well swallows the moon.
He asked, "What is the matter on the side after one has appeared in the world? The Master said, "A heron steps upon and breaks a withered reed branch.
He asked, "Setting aside these two paths, what is the Master's way of acting for the sake of others? The Master said, "A perfectly complete, excellent thing."
A diamond drill. Laid out on the street, to whom would it be sold? He asked: "What is the many-year-old water buffalo?

The Master said: "Teeth sparse, eyes dim. He asked: "When meeting in a bustling marketplace, what is the matter? The Master said: "Going east, he buys cheap; going west, he sells dear. [The student] said:
"If suddenly he neither acts as dear nor acts as cheap, then what? The Master said: "Zhengzhou."
“Radish. [The student] asked, “All sentient beings possess Buddha-nature. Since they possess Buddha-nature, why do they nevertheless enter the wombs of donkeys and horses?
The Master said, “Knowing it yet deliberately committing the offense. [The student] asked, “I wonder, in what place does one repent?”
The Master struck him and said, "I am merely treating a dead horse. He asked, "What is it like when one presents oneself face-to-face?
The Master said, "Half a catty in the left eye; eight taels in the right eye. The monk lifted up his sitting cloth and said, "What about here? The Master said, "No need to bring it out.
Then he looked around left and right and said, "When the Yellow-faced Old Man took seven steps, the very spot beneath his feet was just right for—"
A needle. That blue-eyed barbarian sat upright for nine years; what a pity for that single notch upon the crown of his head!

Had there been at that time a monk who exerted himself for the sake of the assembly and could have brought down this lethal blow, it would have spared the picking of flowers and the faint smile that needlessly broke the Buddha’s countenance, and the standing in the snow waist-deep that turned into a mere track in the mud. From then on, taking error for truth, they have beaten one another like baskets.
The basket eventually bore five fragrant leaves; a thousand lamps continued their flame. On the curved wooden seat, he sang "two" as "three";
with his *khakkhara* staff, he pointed south as north. He could advance and retreat at will. Those seekers who inquire about the Dharma or the Mind lean against the gate or the wall;
those who seek the Buddha or the Patriarch point to the cypress tree in the courtyard and immediately call it by name.
The Patriarch’s intent in coming from the West was "viewing the mountains in broad daylight. Yet people further mistake this for their own self;

they fail to realize that this Great Matter is fundamentally numinous and luminous, uninterrupted throughout the bounds of the future, requiring no cultivation or realization, and existing beyond the reach of thought.
Though Śāriputra had things he could not know, it was not something Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra could have debated—had they but seen Mazu.
One shout! Baizhang was deaf for three days; Baoshou’s command was carried out. The entire city of Zhenzhou was blind.
Great capacity and great function are like a sudden thunderclap—unstoppable. One call and one response are like a precipitous cliff—impossible to tread upon.
At such a moment, the Buddhas of the three periods can only look on from the sidelines; the Patriarchs of the six generations have the right to bear witness. Great!
"Everyone, tell me: is there anyone present today who can provide proof? After a long silence, he said, "A formal document! He ascended the hall and said:
"Shiqi carries the firewood; Hanshan burns the fire. Only Fenggan sits coldly within his cave. Tell me, what excellence does Fenggan possess?
After a long silence, he said, "If one has no minor servants at home, one cannot be a gentleman."

Chan Master Foguo Keqin of Zhaojue Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Wuzu Yan, the fourteenth generation descendant of Nanyue. He was a native of the Luo family in Pengzhou; his ancestors followed the Confucian tradition.
When the Master was a child, he could memorize a thousand words a day. Once, while visiting Miaoji Temple, he saw Buddhist scriptures;

upon reading them three times, he was filled with a sense of longing, as if he had recovered a long-lost possession. He said, "I am surely a śramaṇa from a past life. He immediately left his home and took refuge under Zizheng to receive the tonsure.
He followed Wenzhao to master the exegesis of the sutras and received the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* from Minxing. Suddenly, he fell ill and was on the verge of death, whereupon he sighed: "All..."
"The Buddha’s path to Nirvana does not reside within words and phrases. I intended to seek it through sound and perceive it through form; it is only fitting that I have failed.
He then departed and went to the seat of Chan Master Zhenjue Sheng. At that time, Sheng was just beginning to cut his own arm to draw blood.
The Instructor pointed [at him] and said, "This is a single drop from Caoxi. The Master was startled; after a long while, he said, "Is the Way truly like this?
He then immediately set out on foot and left Sichuan. First, he visited Yuquan Hao; subsequently, he relied upon Jinluan Xin, Dayue Zhe, Huanglong Xin, and Donglin Du.
All of them designated him as a vessel of the Dharma, and Huidang remarked that one day he would become the successor of the Linji lineage.
He was a follower of the Fifth Patriarch. Having exhausted his skillful means before the Patriarch, he received no approval.

He then remarked that the Patriarch was forcibly changing people around and spoke insolent words; departing in a fit of indignation, the Patriarch said, "Wait until you are struck by a severe fever, and only then will you think of me.
Later, when the Master reached Mount Jin, he contracted a case of smallpox (or a severe cold) and became extremely ill. Recalling what he had seen on ordinary days...

He tested him in various situations, but the man showed no signs of progress. Tracing back the words of the Fifth Patriarch, he made a vow to himself, saying, "When my illness subsides slightly, I shall return to the Fifth Patriarch.
Once his illness was cured, he returned immediately. Upon seeing him, the Patriarch was pleased and ordered him to enter the hall at once.

He then entered the quarters of the attendants (*śaikṣa*). Only half a month had passed when an imperial commissioner, returning from his post to Sichuan, visited the Patriarch to inquire about the Way. The Patriarch said:
The Provincial Inspector said, "I am young; have you ever read the *Xiaoyan* (Minor Beauties) poems? There are two lines that are quite similar:
'Frequently calling for Little Jade is originally for no reason; it is simply so that the husband may recognize the voice. The Inspector responded, "Yes, yes. Zuzhao said, "But listen carefully."
Just as the Master returned and stood in attendance, [Dongshan] asked, "I heard you, the Abbot, recite a poem with erotic undertones. Does the Judicial Commissioner understand it?
Jue said, "He only recognizes the sound. [The Master] said, "It is precisely because he wants his lover to recognize the sound. Since he has already recognized the sound..."
"Why is it not so? The Patriarch asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
[Baizhang] replied, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. At this, the Master had a sudden realization. He hurried out and saw a chicken flying onto the railing, flapping its wings and crowing.
He said to himself, "Is this not sound? He then tucked incense in his sleeve, entered the room, and presented what he had attained, offering this verse: Golden Goose...
The incense has faded from the brocade curtains; amidst the sounds of pipes and singing, he is drunk and supported home.

This one episode of youthful elegance can be known by the fair lady alone. The Patriarch said, "The great matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is not something that those of inferior capacity and weak roots can attain.
I rejoice with you. The Patriarch then addressed the elders of the mountain community at large, saying, "My attendant has realized Zen."

Consequently, wherever he went, he was esteemed as a preeminent leader. During the Chongning era, he returned to his hometown to visit his parents; the fourfold assembly came out to welcome and pay their respects to him.
Guo Gong Zhizhang, the Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and Governor of Chengdu, invited him to propagate the Dharma of the Sixth Patriarch at Zhaojue Temple.

During the Zhenghe era, he retired from public affairs and again traveled south through the Gorges. At that time, Zhang Wujin was residing in Jingnan, where he considered himself a master of Daoist learning and had rarely encountered anyone [of such caliber].
He consented. The Master moored his boat to pay him a visit, and they engaged in an extensive discussion on the essential meaning of the *Avataṃsaka*.

[The Master] said: "The realm of direct perception (*pratyakṣa*) in the *Avataṃsaka* is the total reality of both principle and phenomena; there is not the slightest trace of artificiality therein. Thus, from the one comes the many, and the many are understood as the one.
One follows upon one, and the many follow upon the many—vast and inexhaustible. Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings are non-different in these three; their unfolding and retracting are entirely free."
"Unobstructed and perfectly interfused. Although this is the ultimate principle, it is ultimately but ripples in a windless sea. At this, the Duke involuntarily drew his seat closer.
The Master then asked, "At this point, is this the same as or different from the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Duke replied, "It is the same. The Master said, "That still does not touch upon it. The Duke’s expression turned sullen. The Master said, "Have you not seen the clouds..."
The gateways, the paths, the mountains, rivers, and the great earth—wherein not even a hair’s breadth of fault or affliction exists—are still merely "turning phrases.

Only when one reaches the point where not a single form is perceived is this "half-raising" of the banner. Yet, one must further know that there is a time for the "total raising" of the banner above this. Such was the case with Deshan and Linji.

The Master laughed and said, "Not so. This is still within the measure of the *dharmadhātu*. For as long as the measure of the *dharmadhātu* has not been extinguished," [he continued].

Upon reaching the Dharma-realm of the non-obstruction of phenomena and phenomena (*dharmadhātu-pratītyasamutpāda*), where the dimensions of the Dharma-realm cease, only then can one properly speak of Chan.

The Emperor summoned him for an audience and bestowed upon him exceedingly generous honors. At the beginning of the Jianyan era, he was again appointed to Mount Jinshan.

[The Master] snatched it away. The teacher said, "Take it back. [The student] asked, "What is it like when both person and environment are not snatched away? The teacher said, "Let go.

The mirror does not look outward. Even if you were to realize the entire great earth such that there is not a single thread of leakage, you would still be halfway there.

Contemplate it as if viewing spread-out brocade: within each of the three hundred and sixty joints and bones, there appears an infinite, wondrous body;

A single phrase: How do you speak it? "To test jade, one must pass through fire; to seek pearls, one does not leave the mud.
Ascending the hall: Originally there is no form or segment; how could there be lips or a beak? To suddenly proclaim it widely is merely to substitute for him and explain his principles.
But tell me, who is he? Ascending the hall: Before the fifteenth day, even a thousand oxen cannot drag him back. After the fifteenth day...
Afterward, even a swift falcon could not catch up. It was precisely the fifteenth day; heaven and earth were level, light and dark were identical.

The great chiliocosm of sand-grain worlds did not transcend this very place, yet it could encompass and expel the ten voids. To take a single step forward is to transcend unspeakable seas of fragrant water;
to take a single step back is to sit and cut off the white clouds of a thousand miles and ten thousand leagues. To neither advance nor retreat—do not...
"O Dharma-ācārya, even this old monk has no place to open his mouth. Raising his whisk, he said, "At such a time as this, how is it? Sometimes he holds it aloft upon a thousand peaks;
he cleaves through the autumn clouds, not allowing them to rise high. Entering the hall, he said: "The ten directions gather together in one assembly;
the original body is not obscure. Each and every one studies non-action; with tongs and hammers upon the crown of the head—this is selection."
The Buddha-field is profound and vast, beyond measure. One returns having attained the "honorary degree" of the emptiness of mind; even a sharp sword is not equal to a needle-point.
Layman Pang’s tongue reached up to the Brahma-heaven and his mouth encompassed the four seas. At times he takes a single blade of grass and makes it the sixteen-foot golden body of the Buddha;
at other times he takes that sixteen-foot golden body and makes it a single blade of grass—how truly extraordinary! Nevertheless, even so...
One has never moved the upward barrier. But what is this upward barrier? Casting seals and building high altars. Entering the hall:
there is a phrase and there is no phrase; it transcends the school and surpasses the standard. It is like a vine leaning against a tree, a silver mountain and an iron wall.
When the tree falls and the vine withers, how many people lose their sense of smell? Even if you were to gather it all back together, you would already be a thousand miles away.
Ten thousand miles away. But how was it before there was any such news? Can you penetrate it? "The wind is warm and the birds' songs shatter;
the sun is high and the flower shadows deepen. Entering the hall, he said: "If you realize the first phrase, you beg for the life of the Patriarch.
If you realize the second phrase, the gods and humans lose their courage. If you realize the third phrase, you cast yourself into the tiger’s mouth. This is not following the beaten track."

"Guarding the tracks" does not mean changing the tracks or shifting the path; if you penetrate it, you may have six arms and three heads, yet even if you do not penetrate it, you are still among men and in the heavens.

Furthermore, as for that one phrase beyond the three phrases—how can you speak of it? "One's livelihood lies solely upon the fishing line; under a bright moon, a small boat drifts across the Five Lakes.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "A single word cuts it off completely; the voices of the thousand sages are silenced. A single sword [stands] before..."
The head. A corpse lies across ten thousand *li*. Therefore it is said: "Sometimes the phrase reaches but the meaning does not; sometimes the meaning reaches but the phrase does not.
The phrase can eradicate the meaning, and the meaning can eradicate the phrase. When meaning and phrase race against one another, this is the 'nose' of the patch-robed monk.
If you can turn about in such a manner, even the blue sky must receive a blow of the staff. But tell me, by what means? How pitiful, the infinite [beings]."
The one who plays with the tide ultimately perishes within the ebb. Addressing the assembly, he said: "To let go of hand atop a ten-thousand-fathom cliff requires a man of true mettle;
when a crossbow of a thousand *qun* is released, how could it be for a mere field mouse? Yunmen and Muzhou missed the mark right before their faces;
Deshan and Linji were merely deceiving the common folk. As for all others who establish boundaries and triggers, or create nests and dens—they are nothing more than that."

"This is the extinction of the Hu lineage. Furthermore, regarding the single phrase "How shall one speak of solitary liberation?"—the shifting and changing of myriad conditions is but a trivial matter;
in the fifth month, the mountain hermitage is as cold as ice. On the *jǐyǒu* day of the eighth month in the fifth year of the Xiǎngxìng era, he manifested a slight ailment.

Sitting cross-legged, he wrote a verse to leave for the assembly, then set down his brush and passed away. Upon cremation, his tongue and teeth remained uncorrupted, and five-colored *śarīra* appeared.
He was enshrined in a stupa beside Zhaojue Temple and posthumously titled Chan Master Zhijue.
Huìqín, the Chan Master Fǎjiàn of Tàipíng in Shūzhōu, was the son of the Wáng clan of that same prefecture. At the age of seven, he took the preceptor Guǎngjiào Yuánshēn as his teacher;
upon testing his mastery of the studies, he received ordination. He constantly contemplated the verse: "This one reality alone is true; the other two are not real. He relished its meaning...

Feeling a sense of dissatisfaction, he traveled extensively to consult renowned masters. He had spent many years coming and going at the gate of the Fifth Patriarch, yet he resented that the Patriarch would not provide him with a seal of certification.

Consequently, he departed together with Yuanwu. When Yuanwu returned to the Fifth Patriarch’s monastery and was about to attain thorough realization in the abbot’s quarters, the Master suddenly arrived, intending to travel elsewhere.
Yuanwu urged him to register as a resident monk and said, "It has been only a month since I parted from you, brother."
"How have you been since we last met? The Master said, "This is precisely what I have been wondering about.
He then entered the hall. One day, he heard the Patriarch cite a monk’s question to Zhaozhou: "What is the master’s house style?
Zhaozhou replied, "I am old and hard of hearing; ask with a loud voice. When the monk asked again, Zhaozhou said, "You ask about my house style, yet I recognize you."
The family style was thus understood. The Master immediately had his doubts completely dispelled and said, "I beg the Honored One to point out the ultimate principle.

The Patriarch replied, "The myriad phenomena of the universe and the ten thousand images are all sealed by a single Dharma. The Master prostrated himself. The Patriarch then appointed him to oversee calligraphy.
Later, while conversing with Yuanwu, he raised the kōan concerning Dongsi’s question to Yangshan about the "Bright Pearl of the Tranquil Sea," up to the point where it becomes irrational.

When it was said that he could "stretch forth" [his argument], Yuanwu challenged him, saying, "Since you say you have 'collected' it, yet when this pearl is sought, you say there are no words with which to respond and no principle with which to stretch forth. The Master was unable to provide a further answer.
The next day, he said to Yuanwu, "Dongsi merely asked for a single pearl, and Yangshan immediately poured out an entire basketful. Yuanwu deeply approved of this and told him, "The old..."
"Brother, you should go and attend upon the Old Monk even more closely. One day, the Master went to the Abbot’s quarters;

before he had even spoken, he was rebuked by the Patriarch and withdrew in embarrassment. He returned to his cell, closed the door, and lay down to sleep, harboring resentment toward the Patriarch without ceasing. Huineng already knew this in secret.
He immediately went and knocked on the door. The Master asked, "Who is it? Wuzhu said, "It is I. The Master then opened the door. Wuzhu asked, "How did you see the Old Monk [yourself]?
The Master said, "I originally had no intention of going, but I was deceived by you and dragged into this; I have suffered this old fellow's insults."
Wu laughed heartily and said, "Do you remember the words you spoke the other day? The Master asked, "What words?
Wu said, "You said that Dongsi only asked for one grain, yet Yangshan poured out an entire basket. At that moment, the Master was suddenly relieved.
Wu then led the Master together to the abbot’s quarters. As soon as the Patriarch saw them, he immediately said, "Brother Qin, first—"
He was delighted that the great matter had been concluded. The following year, he appointed the Master as the First Seat (*dìyī zuò*).
When Dàpíng Língyuán departed for Huánglóng, his seat became vacant; Língyuán then recommended the Master to Sūn Dǐngchén, the Governor of Shū, who subsequently ordered him to fill the position.
The Fifth Patriarch had entrusted the dharma robe to him; the Master received it, held it up to show the assembly, and said: "In the past, Śākyamuni Buddha, with his sixteen-foot golden body..."
The *lánjiāshā* (tiered robe). It covers the body of the thousand-fathom Maitreya Buddha; yet the Buddha’s body is not long, nor is the robe short.

Do you understand? It is simply this pattern, with no other pattern. Thus, the Way of the Dharma was widely disseminated. At the beginning of the Zhenghe era, an imperial decree ordered him to reside at Zhihai in the Eastern Capital.

After five years, he requested to return home and received permission to dwell at Jiangshan. The Imperial Secretary Deng Gongzi Chang submitted a memorial requesting that he be granted an honorary title.
Zhenfu. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "When you eat vinegar, you know its sourness; when you eat salt, you know its salinity.
The monk asked, "What is it like when the bow is broken and the arrows are spent? The Master said, "A scene of utter embarrassment.

[The monk] asked, "Who is it that does not take companionship with the myriad dharmas? The Master said, "He squeezes the pillar until it breaks. [The monk] asked, "When there is no road back to one's hometown..."
"How is it? The Master said, "The royal journey has its limits. [The monk] said, "Three before, three after—what about that? The Master said, "Six times six is thirty-six.
[The monk] asked, "I have heard that you, Reverend, personally saw the Fifth Patriarch—is this true?
The Master said, "An iron ox chews up golden grass. [The monk] said, "If so, then you have personally seen the Fifth Patriarch. The Master said, "I shall give it to you..."
[The monk] asked, "What a profound grievance! Tell me, what was the meaning behind Bodhidharma’s audience with Emperor Wu?

The Master said, "The barbarian tongue is easy to discern; the Han language is difficult to clarify. [The monk] asked, "Why did he cross the Yangtze River in secret, looking so weary and anxious? The Master said, "He took advantage of the wind to ride upon its power."
Question: "What is the guest within the host? The Master said: "Advancing and retreating—this brings grief unto men.
Question: "What is the host within the guest? The Master said: "Words of truth become false speech. Question: "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said: [silence].
When the Master was traveling and encountered hardship in Chen, he asked, "What is the Lord among Lords? The Master said, "We travel together all day long, yet we are not companions.
[The questioner] said, "I have already received the Master’s instruction regarding guest and host; as for the matter of the Supreme Vehicle above this, what is it like? The Master said:
A great axe chops; one rubs the hands. He asked, "I do not ask about 'this very mind is Buddha. But as for 'neither mind nor Buddha,' what is it?
The Master said, "Yesterday a monk asked this, and I did not answer. The monk said, "I wonder how far apart this is from 'this very mind is Buddha'?
The Master said, "If near, it is a thousand or ten thousand miles away; if far, it is not separated by so much as a hair's breadth. The monk said, "..."
Suddenly, the student was cut off at both ends and returned home to sit securely. [The Master asked: "How about this? The Master said, "Where is your home?
He replied, "Within the great chiliocosm, there is one free body. The Master said, "You have not yet arrived home; speak further.
He replied, "When the student reaches this point, he truly cannot distinguish east from west, nor north from south."
The Master said, "This is not beyond one's capacity. He ascended the hall and said: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes discrimination.
The peach blossoms are red, the plum blossoms are white—who says they blend into a single color? The swallows chatter, the yellow warblers sing—who says their 'guan-guan' is but a single sound?
If you do not penetrate the pivot of the Patriarch’s gate, you will vainly take mountains and rivers for your own eyes. He ascended the hall again on a certain day.
Day after day the sun sinks in the west; day after day the sun rises in the east. If you wish to study Bodhi, he threw down his staff and said:
"Just look at this appearance! On the anniversary of the Fifth Patriarch’s death, he ascended the hall and said: "At this very time last year, a flake of snow flew from a red furnace."
Today is the anniversary of last year’s time. Cao E reads the night stele. The final phrase—no Buddha-eye can peer into it.
Upon the peak of White Lotus Mountain, the crimson sun circles Mount Sumeru. Birds peck at the coral tree; the whale swallows the water-leaving rhinoceros.
"The family estate of Great Peace remains; for a thousand ages it has been inherited from Yangqi. He ascended the hall, held his staff horizontally and said, "First illumination, then function.

Holding it upright, he said, "First function, then illumination. Turning it upside down, he said, "Illumination and function are simultaneous. Striking the ground once with it, he said, "Illumination and function are not simultaneous.
You people have all been swallowed up in one gulp by this staff! It is simply that you yourselves..."
Awaken! If you can utter a turning phrase here, you will avoid this bout of stifling frustration.
If not, the old monk loses today. Ascending the hall, he said: "The golden crow is swift; the jade hare is fast. In the rapid flow of time, it is the tenth day of the seventh month.
Endless travelers do not return home; even if they do return, they merely stand before the gate. Standing before the gate, [the master] takes hold of the hand."
He leads him along, yet he refuses to enter. Ten thousand miles ahead, one looks and sees not a blade of grass. Fallen blossoms lie upon the ground, but no one gathers them.
No one gathers them; with every passing rain, they grow ever more damp. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The World-Honored One has a secret word;
Kāśyapa did not conceal it. He then continued: "You usually speak of yellow and black, and pass judgment on the ancients and the present. Is this not a secret word? You..."

In the ordinary course of moving about, bowing, and rising; picking up the spoon or grasping the chopsticks; or offering a prostration and a "ten-thousand-fold blessing"—these are instances of concealment or non-concealment.
Yet, when one suddenly glimpses it, even that cannot be known. Do you wish to understand? The World-Honored One has a secret word: "Winter arrives;
Cold Food Festival, the hundred-and-fifth day. Kāśyapa did not conceal anything; though it was as impenetrable as water, his guilt was already exposed. O sharp-witted patch-robed monks!
As it was attained in the assembly: "One layer of snow upon another layer of frost. Entering the hall, he said:
"The matter prior to the fifteenth day is like adding flowers upon brocade. The matter after the fifteenth day is like a single bubble rising from the sea.

On the fifteenth day itself, it is much like a one-foot mirror reflecting images from a thousand miles away. Although it is empty space where all traces are cut off, how can one deny that the ocean-seal radiates light?"
"Let the incense pillar bloom as it may; what need is there to speak of the hundred uglinesses on the Buddha’s face? Why?
In the end, the frosty night moon falls naturally into the stream before us. He ascended the hall and raised an example: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the meaning of non-transmigration?
Zhaozhou made a gesture with his hand as if flowing water, and the monk attained realization. Another monk asked Fayan, "Not grasping at appearances, suchness..."
"Movement. How is it not grasping at appearances? Seeing suchness, one is unmoving. The monk said, "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night.
The monk also attained realization. If you can see it thus, only then will you know that while whirlwinds topple mountains, they are fundamentally and eternally still;
and while rivers compete to flow, they have never actually moved from their source. If this is not yet so, you cannot avoid further [instruction].
To speak at length: the heavens rotate counter-clockwise, while the earth turns clockwise. From antiquity to the present, how many cycles have passed? The golden sun flies and the jade hare runs;

having just emerged from the gates of the sea, it already sets behind the green mountains. The waves of the rivers and streams are vast and boundless, the surges of the Huai and Ji are long and steady;
they flow day and night directly into the azure ocean. Then he cried out in a loud voice: "O practitioners of Zen! Do you see Suchness?"
"One? In the master’s quarters, there were six wooden dice, each face of which was inscribed with the character "one" (幺).

As soon as the monk entered, the master threw them and asked, "Do you understand? Before the monk could even consider it, the master struck him out. This occurred on the eighth day of the ninth month in the seventh year.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Mind-Seal of the Patriarchs is like the device of an iron ox: when it departs, it is sealed; when it stays, it is broken.
Even if one neither departs nor stays, this is still not the place where a patch-robed monk walks. But what, then, is the place where a patch-robed monk walks?
Wait until after the tenth month, and I shall explain it for you. On the eighth day of the following month, he bathed...
He bathed and changed his robes. Sitting upright, he wrote several letters by hand to bid farewell to his old friends. Setting down his pen, he passed away.
His remains were cremated, and his sacred relics (śarīra) were collected and enshrined in a stupa at his home mountain.
Chan Master Qingyuan Foyan of Longmen in Shu Prefecture was the son of the Li family of Linqiong. He was dignified and upright, speaking sparingly.

At fourteen, he received full ordination and relied upon the Vinaya to investigate its doctrines. Later, while reading the Lotus Sūtra, he came to the passage: "This Dharma cannot be understood through thought or discrimination.
He took this up and questioned his lecture master, but the master was unable to answer. The Master sighed and said, "The meaning..."

He realized that studying names and characteristics was not the way to resolve the great matter of birth and death. He subsequently rolled up his robes and traveled south to attend the Dharma seat of Chan Master Yan of Taiping in Shuzhou.
While begging for alms in Luzhou, he happened to stumble and fall to the ground in the rain; amidst his distress, he thought:
Hearing that the two men were cursing each other, the mediator said, "You are still harboring afflictions. At these words, the Master attained a realization.
Upon returning, whenever anyone asked him a question, Yan would simply say, "I am not as good as you; you understand it well enough yourself."
Someone said, "I do not understand; I am not as good as you. The Master became even more doubtful and went to consult the Chief Seat Yuanli for a definitive resolution.
Yuanli then took the Master by the ear with his hand and led him around the brazier several times. As they walked, he spoke, saying, "You understand well enough yourself.
The Master said, "I hope you will enlighten me; why are you merely teasing me? Yuanli replied, "You will realize it later."

"Go," [he said]. Only then did he realize the twists and turns of that day. When Taiping was about to move to Haihui Monastery, the Master sighed with regret and said, "I have just returned from begging for alms;
to follow him again to a desolate temple—how could I possibly resolve the matter of my own life?

I must depart. He then composed a verse to take his leave and went to Jangshan to spend the summer retreat. There he met Chan Master Lingyuan by chance, and their friendship grew ever deeper. One day, as they were conversing at ease...
In the midst of their conversation, the Master said, "Recently, I have seen that a certain venerable elder in the capital has words that seem to have a karmic affinity with you.
Lingyuan replied, "Master Yan is the foremost patriarch under heaven; why would I abandon him to travel so far? To which [the Master] said, "That which is called 'having a karmic affinity'—"
It seems that the Master’s understanding and realization accorded with his original aspiration. The Master followed this encouragement and proceeded directly to Haihui Monastery.
Later, he was appointed to oversee the reception hall. Once, sitting alone on a cold night, he stirred the ashes of the brazier and saw a spark the size of a bean.

He was suddenly filled with joy and said, "Stirring deeply, there is something here; the affairs of my entire life are just like this. He immediately rose and read the *Lamp Records* (Denglu) on the desk.

In the *Lù* (Record), it is said that upon reaching the account of the causes and conditions concerning Pòzuò Duò, [Yuánwù] suddenly attained great enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "Each stroke of the axe brings the forest birds’ cry;
Clad in robes, I sit through the entire night. Shifting the embers, I awaken to my whole life; Exhausting the spirit, I return to the broken hearth. The matter is clear, yet people remain deluded;

who can harmonize with such subtle and profound tones? Thinking of this, I shall never forget it; the gate stands open, yet few pass through. Thereupon, Yuánwù went to his quarters and raised [this matter].
Qinglin tested him with a story from the local dialects, saying, "It is said that from ancient times until now, no one has been able to produce [a verse for this].
How do you understand it? The Master replied, "What difficulty could there possibly be? Wu said, "As for what he said: 'The Iron Wheel-turning King’s decree throughout the realm'—what is its meaning?
The Master replied, "I say: An amnesty proclamation is issued from within the palace of Śakra. Wu withdrew and said to others, "I am glad."
"Brother Yuan already possesses phrases that bring life to others. Thereafter, he lived in seclusion at Dazhong Hermitage on Mount Sishian.
When the entire country was newly restoring Chongning Wanshou Temple, the Governor of Shu, Lord Wang Huanzhi, commanded the Master to open the Dharma there.

Subsequently, he succeeded to the abbacy of Longmen, where his reputation for the Way flourished even more. Later, he moved to Baoci Temple in Hezhou, where the State Councilor Deng Xunwu submitted a memorial requesting the Emperor grant the Master [the title of Chan Master].

Addressed as "The One in Purple Robes," he ascended the hall and said: "On the road to Mount Tiantai, travelers are extremely rare; before the Hall of the Broken Oven, there is no ground upon which to express gratitude. The courtyard cypresses are buried in snow, and the winding stream is locked in ice.

Though I am here at the hearth in the South, I do not enter the pickle-jar of others. Look now: on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, it is still as cold as in the early spring.
