Whenever the Master presided over the assembly, his countenance was invariably stern. He never turned his back on his sleep or his meals.
The assembly sang the Way without weariness. In the tenth month of the Gengwu year of the Xiangshu era, he manifested a slight illness.

On the eighteenth day, the Head Seat Faquan requested his final instructions. The Master said, "Exhaust this mind and will; support one another with the Way. Having spoken these words, he passed away.

After the fire, his eyes, teeth, and tongue remained unburnt. That spot of ground emitted light throughout the night. Those who obtained *śarīra* (relics) were beyond counting, continuing for over a month without ceasing.
Huang Guan Luo Zhao had regularly sought the Way from the Master. Once, returning from outside, he alone had obtained nothing. His aspiration for the Way was earnest and intense;
just as he was eating with a guest, while chewing, something felt like an object in his mouth. Upon spitting it out, it was a relic.

It was beneficial. It was as large as a soybean and its color was like amber. A person fond of such things took it away, whereupon [the master] performed two prostrations at the site of the cremation.
Hearing a sound from the incense casket, he opened it immediately; what he obtained was as before, yet slightly reddish and lustrous.
His disciples enshrined the remains and divided them to build stupas at Mount Mao and Xihu. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Dawu.

Chan Master Fuxing Fatai of Da Mei in Tanzhou was a native of the Li clan of Hanzhou. A monk asked, “When principle follows the transformations of phenomena, it encompasses all existence yet remains a single expanse of void-stillness;
when phenomena follow the integration of principle, they equalize a thousand differences yet all return to the ultimate reality.
What is the realm of principle? The Master said, “Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. The monk asked, “What is the realm of phenomena?”

The Master said, "The myriad phenomena are dense and manifold. [The student] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between principle and phenomena? The Master said, "East, west, south, and north.

[The student] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between all phenomena? The Master said, "Above, below, and the four intermediate directions. He then ascended the hall for discourse.
Pushing to the limit of truth, truth has no marks; exhausting delusion, delusion has no form. When both truth and delusion are non-existent, the eyes are revealed in vast clarity.
Once the eyes are revealed, what do you see? The morning sun melts the snow upon the crags;
the northern wind blows open the wax-plum blossoms. [Ascending the hall: When the precious sword is drawn, it is used immediately—how could there be any hesitation? The eyebrows...

Lifting up the whisk, he immediately departs; there is no further room for hesitation or evasion. In every place, he illuminates the present and radiates the ancient; in every place, he cuts through all nets and cages.

He does not strike against the sharp edge of the blade, nor does he look back into the mirror. Setting aside for a moment the matter of his solitary transcendence beyond all things, what is it like when the ten thousand functions have been utterly exhausted?
"In the eighth month of autumn, where is there heat? He ascended the hall and said: "There is no other path to Nirvana; expedient means..."
Many gates. He raised up his staff and said: "Look! Look! This staff of mine has swallowed the waters of the West River in a single gulp.
A carp from the Eastern Sea leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens. Indra, filled with wrath, strikes Mount Sumeru with a single blow, shattering it to pieces.
The Earth Goddess Sthāvarā joins her palms in praise and says: 'Behold clearly the Dharma of the Dharma-King; the Dharma-King...'"
Such is the nature of the Dharma. [The Master] struck the meditation seat with his staff and descended from the seat to ascend the hall.

To realize the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of phenomena is not yet to be called the ancestral style of the Buddhas; to embody total function and total illumination is likewise not the essential subtlety of a monk.
One must directly shatter the sturdy barrier and recognize the single aperture above. What is this aperture above? "The spring chill is biting."
"Freezing the youth to death. [The Master] ascends the hall: "Today is the halfway point of the first month. Everywhere the lanterns and fires are in disarray;
the entire city is filled with crowds in silks and brocades, coming and going in turns to enjoy the sights. Mañjuśrī has run into the midst of the bustling crowd;

Samantabhadra sits upright in a high tower watching. But tell me, where is Avalokiteśvara? [He then] beats the painted drums until they shake the heavens and plays the instruments until they deafen the earth.
Flute and song. Ascending the hall: Vast and remote, encompassing the ten directions; level and expansive, transcending form and appearance.
The eyes wish to look, yet the pupils wither; the mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have no skill at all.
Linji and Deshan did not hesitate to proclaim [the truth]: a tortoise swallowed the iron ox of Shanzhou; a snake bit the Great Image of Jiaozhou.
This terrified the carp of the Eastern Sea, which remains bloated to this very day. Heh! Entering the hall: the fiery clouds scorch the field crops.
The source of the spring has cut off its flow; the great Dragon King Sāgara does not know where he is.
Striking the meditation seat with his staff, he said, "He is right here! Look, look! Clouds rise on the southern mountain, and rain falls on the northern mountain.

I, the old monk, shall further provide the sound of thunder to help manifest his majestic radiance and spread it far and wide. Then, in a loud voice, he said, "Hōng-nòng, hōng-nòng! He ascended the hall and began his discourse.
The mouth is sometimes wrong; when opened, it is sometimes right. Whether coarse words or subtle speech, all return to the primary meaning.
The old man Śākyamuni’s bowl rings out its sound; Bodhidharma’s coming from the West is the stench of excrement. Only the water buffalo before the mountain.
Light from the hair-tuft on his body radiates, illuminating heaven and earth. Entering the hall, he said: "Whether mindfulness is attained or lost, there is nothing that is not liberation.
What kind of talk is this? Whether the Dharma is established or destroyed, it is all called Nirvana. To speculate otherwise would be irrelevant. Whether wisdom or folly, both are collectively Prajna.
Whether the blunt and coarse Buddha-nature, or the dharmas accomplished by Bodhisattvas and non-Buddhists—these are all Bodhi. Thus...

A mere trifle. Nevertheless, even so, it is like Emperor Yang losing his camel. [The Master] ascends the hall and says: "If you wish to know where the Buddha has gone, it is simply this sound of speech.
*Dot!* "Master Fu did not recognize good from evil; he attempted to corrupt the men and women of the family by teaching them about that 'brightly manifest, spiritually alert' state.
He was rebuked by Master Zhigong with a shout: 'Great Master, do not speak in such a manner! [He continues: "It is another matter..."
"Speak further! The Great Being (Mahāsattva) spoke another verse: "Holding a hoe in empty hands, Walking while riding a water buffalo.
A person passes over the bridge; The bridge flows, but the water does not flow. Master Zhigong laughed heartily and said:

"The beginning was still somewhat tolerable, but the end is even more distressing. Ascending the hall, he said: "I recall in days of old when I traveled abroad, I obtained two things. The first is..."
The Vajra Hammer. This is the skeleton of the thousand sages, which I have carried through the universe;
its majestic presence stands high and imposing. Thus it has been for thirty years, used as my standard. Now that I am old, what can I know of this single thing?
I cast down the Vajra Hammer and smash the skeleton of the thousand sages, throwing it onto the crossroads; I cannot cherish it any longer—let it go as it will.
Passing through this floating life, I point south when I should point north; I call a tortoise a softshell turtle and name beans millet.
May those with clear eyes laugh at me for lacking the guiding line and square.
Chan Master Cihu Guo Cigan Jingyuan of Taizhou was the son of the Zhang family of Nanxi in Yongjia. At the age of eighteen, he relied upon Xigong at Lingshan Monastery.
After receiving full ordination, he studied the Tiantai teachings for three years; subsequently, he left them to visit Yuanwu at Zhongfu.
The Master read from the recorded sayings of Sīxīn’s informal sermons, saying: "Since one is deluded, one must attain awakening.

Since one has awakened, one must recognize the delusion within awakening and the awakening within delusion. When both delusion and awakening are forgotten, one establishes all dharmas from the place where there is neither delusion nor awakening."
Upon hearing this, the Master was filled with doubt. He immediately hurried to the Buddha Hall and pushed open the door panels with his hands;

at that moment, he attained a sudden and great enlightenment. Thereafter, as an attendant, his eloquence and wit burst forth with brilliance. Yuanwu dubbed him "The Stubborn Attendant Yuan," and subsequently inscribed his own portrait.
He handed it over, saying: "Throughout my life, I have spoken only of 'head-banging' Chan. When one encounters such a head-banger, it is like hitting an iron wall.

To strip away the cage and cut through the heels—taking up the entire earth, it is as pitch black as ink. In my later years, I have become even more 'knife-less,' brandishing the Vajra mallet to shatter all nests and dens.
If you wish to recognize the face of Yuanwu at some future time, I shall present it all to you at once. Yuan.
Wu returned to Shu, while the Master returned to Zhedong. He concealed his brilliance and buried his light, seeking neither fame nor high office.

When Governor Geng Yongxi of Kuacang—who had once sought instruction from Yuanwu—read the Master’s recorded sayings, he gained insight into the Master’s character upon reaching the inscription on his portrait.

Consequently, he invited the Master to propagate the Dharma at Nanyue Mountain (Nanming Shan) and dispatched an envoy to search for him. Upon arriving at Ba’en Temple in Tai, the envoy found the Master among the assembly.

The abbot’s quarters were pressed upon him to accept the appointment. Fangzhang Gugu was a high disciple of Lingyuan; hearing of his proclamations, he too was deeply struck by their extraordinary nature.
A monk asked: "Sansheng said, 'Whenever I meet a person, I come forth; yet when I come forth, I do not act for others. What is the meaning of this? The Master said:
"An eighty-year-old old man chewing raw iron. [The monk] asked: "Xinghua said, 'Whenever I meet a person, I do not come forth.'"
[The monk] said, "As soon as he comes out, he becomes a human being. [The Master asked,] "And what about that? The Master said, "Waves overturning the void atop the peak of Mount Sumeru.
[The monk] asked, "What is this thing that heaven cannot cover and earth cannot support? The Master said, "A solid iron hammer with no hole.

[The monk] said, "Gods, humans, and all classes of living beings all receive the power of its grace. The Master said, "Do not engage in false conceptualization. [The monk] asked, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have spoken..."
"A phrase that does not reach the bottom—please, Master, speak quickly. The Master said, "Blinking your eyebrows. Question:
"In years past, the site of Sanping was restored. On that day, Yuanwu held high the ancestral seal; it began with your transmission. What is the Linji school?
The Master said, "To kill or to give life without blinking an eye. [The questioner] said, "Drawing back the mirror before one's eyes—who among those who comprehend it..."
[The student] asked, "How is the Yunmen school? The Master said, "The three eyes on the crown of the head illuminate heaven and earth.
[The student] said, "Before it is raised, one knows; before it is spoken, one sees. "How is the Guiyang school? The Master said, "Pushed forward, he does not go ahead;
held back, he does not retreat. [The student] said, "The triple world is mind-only; the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only. "How is the Fayan school? The Master said, "The point of the arrowhead."
They face one another directly, yet do not yield to one another. [A monk] asked, "In the building of transformation, how can one practice the Bird Path?

In returning to the source, how does one again manifest the marvelous family style? "How is the Cao-Dong school? the monk asked. The Master said, "Holding a night-bright talisman in hand, how many know the dawn of heaven?
"Is there still a path above this? the monk asked. The Master said, "There is. "What is the path above? the monk asked. The Master said, "A vast blackness."
Mandi. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "By coveting another’s single grain of millet, he loses his own store of grain for half a year. He ascended the hall and said:
"Before the time of King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja, this group of fellows was off by seven or eight;
after the time of King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja, this group of fellows was off by two or three. Now, this group of fellows sits and stands with solemn dignity. Tell me, are they off by seven?"
Eight errors, two falls, three falls—will you still be able to emerge from this? Raising his whisk, he said: "Hūṃ, hūṃ! Bathing the Buddha.
He ascended the hall and said: "This old Śākyamuni, as soon as he was born, acted as a source of amusement; with one finger he pointed to heaven..."
He pointed one finger at the ground and said, "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.
Later, Master Yunmen said, "If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to a dog, so as to ensure peace throughout the world."
Yet there are still those who refuse to let it go, saying instead that one must be Yunmen to truly praise the Patriarch.
But tell me, where is the point of his praise? Is it at the moment he strikes with a staff? If so, you are mistaken; I am glad we have no connection here.
Today, as I, Nanming, take up residence as abbot for the first time, I can only let this matter pass. If I did not let it pass, then all the people in the entire world would...
Only by begging for their lives can they be spared. Now, as there is no other recourse, let us join the assembly and go before the Buddha Hall;
give each of them one ladleful. Why? Have you not heard it said: "It is better to violate a rule than to overstep a precedent"?
[The Master] strikes the meditation seat with his whisk and descends from the seat. Entering the hall: The jackal howls; the lion roars. He opens his eyes; he reveals himself.
"Moving the Southern Star, staggering the Northern Dipper—does the great assembly know where this falls? A Vajra-demon crouches beneath the steps; a divine tortoise runs through the flames.

The Master retired to West Mountain. When Minister Geng Longxue invited him to ascend the seat at Jingguang Monastery, the Ancient Chan Master Lingfeng cited the kōan of Baiyun seeing Yangqi, wherein Yangqi instructed him to cite the verse on awakening to the Way by Chaling. [The Master] was requested to...
The Master critiqued them, saying: "O Zen practitioners! Yangqi’s great laughter—his eyes look to the southeast, yet his intent lies in the northwest.
Baiyun’s realization was based on a false hearing; he mistook the bell for a jar.
When examined closely, even the old fellow Yangqi is all along on the shelf, taking the wrong for the right. If Nanming were here, it would not be so. I have—"
"A single bright pearl—take care not to let it slip past you head-on. Although it is presented face-to-face, it must still be shattered with a single blow.

Raising his whisk, he said, "Do you understand? When a chess game meets its match, one's moves cannot be hidden; when a poem reaches the point of being recited again, its merit finally becomes visible.
The Master manifested illness and requested Chan Master Ying’an Hua of Xitang to serve as the seat-head (zuo-yuan) and to take charge of the monastery’s affairs.

Regarding his final affairs, he gave instructions as was his custom. Suddenly, he clenched his fists and passed away. Upon cremation, five-colored śarīras were obtained; his teeth, tongue, and right fist remained entirely undamaged.
He was interred in a stupa before Liu-Ruan Cave to the east of the monastery. He was fifty-three years of age.
Chan Master Xiansha Shengzao of Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "In the heavens there is no Maitreya; on the earth there is no Maitreya.
Tell me, where is Maitreya? After a long silence, he said: "When walking at night, do not step on white;
it is either water or stone."
Chan Master Yunbian of Nanfeng in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of that region. He received full ordination under Zhiyuan of Ruipeng in Min. Upon returning home, he visited Qionglong Yuan;
there, he suddenly attained realization and subsequently shared his insights with him. Yuan said, "Although you have gained entry, you have not yet reached the proper standard.

You must truly spur yourself forward. Thereupon, he took his leave to visit various seats of practice. Later, he went to attend on Yuanwu, arriving just as the master had entered the room for private instruction. Hardly had [Yunbian]—
Wu followed him to the door. Wuzhuo said, "Look under your feet. The Master struck a pillar once. Wuzhuo said, "Why do you not speak a single phrase that hits the mark?
The Master said, "If the teacher shakes his head, the disciple wags its tail. Wuzhuo said, "Try wagging your tail for me."

The Master performed a somersault and exited. Huizhu laughed heartily; from this, he became well-known. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not the environment'?
The Master said, "The hegemon arrives at Wu Jiang. The monk asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not the person'?
The Master said, "Building the altar to enshrine the generals. The monk asked, "What is 'taking away both person and environment'? The Master said, "Ten thousand *li*..."
"The mountains and rivers have attained great peace. [The student] asked, "What is it like when both the person and the environment cannot be taken away?

The Master said, "When the dragon roars, mist arises; when the tiger howls, the wind is born. [The student] asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "You have missed it right before your face.

[The student] said, "Truly a master craftsman! The Master said, "A ghost deludes people in broad daylight. One day, while entering the city with a group of monastics and laypeople, they reached the tenth...
Langxiang. Someone asked, "The lane is here; where is the 'Tenth Lang'? The Master raised his arm and said, "Follow me.
Lingyin Huìyuǎn Fóhǎi Chánshī of Lín'ān Prefecture was the son of the Pēng family of Méishān.
At the age of thirteen, he followed Zōngbiàn of Yàoshī Temple to become a monk. He went to Dàcí to study, but then left to rely upon Chánmāster Huī of Língyán. Wēi...

He had a realization. Later, when Yuanwu returned to lead Zhaojue, the Master went there. Upon hearing Yuanwu’s general discourse (*pǔshuō*), Yuanwu cited the anecdote concerning Layman Pang asking Mazu, "How can one not be a companion to the myriad dharmas? At that moment, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and collapsed among the assembly.
As the assembly helped him up, he said, "I have awakened from my dream. That night, during the minor *cān* (general address), the Master stepped forward and asked: "Nakedly pure, empty..."
"I have not a single thing. I am as poor as a bare skeleton with not a single coin. My household is ruined and my family lost. I beg the Master for relief.
Wu said, "The seven treasures and eight jewels are all seized at once. The Master said, "Calamity does not enter the door of a careful house.

Wu said, "The pivot does not leave its place; you have fallen into a sea of poison. As soon as these words were spoken, the Master let out a shout. Wu struck the meditation seat with his staff and said, "Eat!"
"Have you received the staff yet? The Master shouted again. Wuzhuo shouted twice in succession. The Master then bowed.

From that time on, his spiritual acumen became sharp and penetrating, such that he encountered no opposition. When Yuanwu passed away, the Master traveled eastward. He moved through several famous monasteries in succession;

by imperial decree, he resided at Chongxian on Gaoting Mountain after his tenure at Huqiu. He was subsequently appointed to Lingyin by another edict. Emperor Xiaozong summoned him for an audience and bestowed upon him the title "Buddha."
Chan Master Hai ascended the hall and said: "The new year has its reasons; brewing tea and ascending the wine tower. A pair for two feet, half a thing with three heads.
Suddenly manifesting, it is difficult for the spirit to discern; meeting it, even ghosts are distressed. Blowing the holeless flute upside down."
To the accompaniment of the *liángzhōu* dance, he exclaimed, "Hu! Hu! Then he ascended the hall and said: "How pleasant it is that mid-spring is gradually warming!

How much more so on this Cold Food Festival and Qingming! Ten thousand layers of clouded mountains rise in emerald splendor; the wind and moon fill the heavens as noble neighbors. Everywhere the flowers are red and the willows are green;

the lake and sky are calm, with waves stilled and winds hushed. The mountain birds on the branches chirp repeatedly—again and again, in their trivial and fragmented ways, they offer their earnest instructions."
"Chiding! Chiding! You tell me: what was it he was chiding and entrusting? [He] struck the meditation staff and said: 'Remember this day next year;
it will still be Cold Food Festival and Qingming. [He] ascended the hall and cited: A monk asked Muzhou, "I do not ask about removing one layer after another;
but when one does not remove one layer after another, what then? Muzhou said, "Yesterday..."
"Planting eggplants; today I plant winter melons. The Master said, "The questioner asks well but does not understand the answer; the respondent answers well but does not understand the question.
Today, this mountain monk plucks meat from the talons of a hungry eagle and thrusts his body across the mouth of a fierce tiger to show you all a model.
A Daoist ascending the altar wears light feathered robes, yet though his power of incantation may be exhausted..."
The Dharma turns anew. With his thumb he splits open the darkness of heaven and earth; the serpent’s head falls, and ghosts and spirits are startled.
A monk asked, "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, how should a student apply their mind? The Master said, "Dipping into the snow to eat winter melon.

The monk asked, "In the midst of vast dust and confusion, how does one discern the master? The Master said, "At the tip of a wooden ladle, a sickle cuts vegetables. [The monk] said, "Is this not the Harmony itself?"
"Furthermore, there is no place for a person. The Master said, "Grinding the pestle and stirring the noodles. The monk asked, "What is it like at the time of 'this very mind is Buddha'?
The Master said, "A topknot with three points. The monk asked, "What is it like at the time of 'neither mind nor Buddha'? The Master said, "Earrings of gold rings.
The monk asked, "And as for 'neither mind, nor Buddha, nor thing,' how is that? The Master said, "A shaven-headed monk practicing meditation."
[The Master] performed the *zhazhi* dance. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'The Eastern Mountain walks upon the water'?
The Master said, "The first and third days of the month; there is no need to choose a day. A monk asked, "Manjusri is the teacher of the seven Buddhas;

why was he unable to emerge from the woman's samadhi? The Master said, "No needle is hanging from his shoulder. A monk asked, "In the past, there was a scholar who composed a 'Treatise on the Non-existence of Ghosts. Once the treatise was completed—"
A ghost shouted, "What can you do about me? What do you think? The Master struck his forehead with his hand and said, "How does it compare?
The ghost asked, "As for Wuzu making his hand into the beak of a magpie and saying 'Gu-gu-gu,' what about that?
The Master said, "Go away and deal with it yourself. He was asked, "Why does the person inside the hermitage not know what is happening outside the hermitage? The Master—
He said: "I carry a staff across my shoulder, with iron caltrops dangling from it. A monk asked: "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion?
The Master said: "His feet tread upon a revolving wheel. One day, as the drum was beaten for the assembly to enter the hall, the Master sat hidden within the curtain.
An attendant monk went to look for him; the Master suddenly pulled back the curtain and said: "He is right here. Why do you not see him? The monk had no reply. The Master [continued]: "..."
He said: "The great axe chops the three gates. He asked the monks: "The entire Tripitaka is harsh speech;
what is the original body of Vairocana? A monk replied: "Tiantai’s communal labor; Nanyue’s mountain tour. The Master gave a separate saying:
"The Lake Anavatapta is forty zhang deep and forty zhang wide. In the autumn of the year Yimwei (1175), during the intercalary month of the second year of the Chunxi era, he addressed the assembly.
On the first day of the ninth month of autumn: Do not show your head in a bustling place; fix your gaze upon the cold ground.

Brightness and darkness do not interfere with one another; they are divided into two halves. When everyone acts as a nobleman, who is left to sell firewood and charcoal? I tell you: it must not be destroyed.
"Beyond praise; his essence is like empty space, without shore or limit. Calling out to one another, 'Come back! Come back!'—the Lantern Festival is surely on the fifteenth day of the first month.

These words were circulated throughout the capital with widespread suspicion. The following year, he suddenly contracted a slight illness and, as predicted, composed a verse on the Lantern Festival, sitting upright and passing away.
The verse says: "Snap the scale-weight in two, overturn the official proclamation, and the pivotal function bursts forth."
Previously, when a crow flew over, it could not pass; he remained there for seven days, his complexion unchanged. He enshrined his entire body in a stupa on Mount Wu at the temple.
Chan Master Ziwen of Hongfu Temple in Taizhou ascended the hall and said: "How do you understand that which is neither obscured nor falling?
Even if you understand, you will still fall as a wild fox. One night a cool wind arises from the painted horn; the bright moon fills the boat as it drifts upon the rivers and lakes."
Chan Master Zhengfa Jian of Chengdu Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have no horns.

Without a single hair, without a single filament, they are like mountains and like peaks. Upon the point of a needle, a lion performs a somersault; within the hollow of a lotus root, a great garuḍa spreads its wings."
Casually he passed beyond Uttarakuru; the sun, moon, and stars were all at once darkened.
Chan Master Anmin Huizang Miyin of Jiankang Prefecture was the son of the Zhu family of Jiading Prefecture.

Initially, he lectured on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* in Chengdu and became a refuge for those studying the doctrinal teachings (*yixue*). At that time, Yuanwu resided at Zhaojue Temple. The Master and Chan Master Sheng...

He became a friend to Wuzu. Consequently, he went to visit him and heard Wuzu’s *xiaocan* (small public discourse). Wuzu raised the kōan concerning the National Teacher’s three calls to his attendant.

Zhaozhou commented on it, saying: "It is like a person writing characters in the dark; though the characters themselves are not formed, the traces of their brilliance are already manifest. "Where is it that the traces of brilliance are already manifest?
The Master harbored doubts about this and requested an audience by offering incense and entering the room. Wuzu asked, "Preceptor, what sutra do you lecture upon? The Master...
Yangshan said, "In the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, there is the 'Investigation of the Mind in Seven Places' and the 'Discrimination of Seeing through Eight Returns.
Ultimately, where does the mind reside? The Master offered many displays of intellectual understanding, but Yangshan would not accept them. The Master again requested further instruction.

Yangshan told him to compose a verse on the principle that "the literary pattern is already manifest in all places. Later, when a monk requested instruction on the *Ten Mysterious Gates*, Yangshan was just beginning to raise the topic when he asked: "I ask you, what is the Seal of the Mind?"
"What face do I have? Wuzhuo shouted, "The patterns are already manifest! Upon hearing this, the Master attained a realization and subsequently sought certification.
Wuzhuo applied his authentic hammer and tongs, but the Master was at a loss for words. One day he said to Wuzhuo, "Master, do not bring up these stories;
wait until I speak them myself. Wuzhuo consented. The Master said, "When one normally brandishes the mallet or raises the whisk, is that not the teaching of the Sutras?"
"Dao! All the various marks that exist within all worlds are, in their very essence, the wondrously luminous true mind of bodhi.

Wuxue said with a smile, "So you have been making your living right here all along? The Master spoke again, "When you let out a shout or strike the meditation seat, is this not 'returning the hearing to hear one's own nature,' whereby that nature achieves the unsurpassed Way? Wuxue said, "Have you not seen it stated in the sutras: 'Wondrous...'"?
The nature is perfectly luminous and free from all names and signs. Under these words, Master [Wu] attained sudden clarity. He departed from Sichuan and resided at Jia Shan.

While Master [Xuefeng] had ceased his lectures and was traveling in attendance, Wu presided over the night assembly for the community. He raised the kōan concerning the ancient sail not yet hoisted; upon hearing it, Master [Wu] did not yet comprehend it.

He then sought a definitive resolution. Huineng said, "Ask me. The Master recounted the previous story. Huineng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. At that moment, the Master attained complete and penetrating clarity.
He said to Huineng, "The ancients said, 'It is like a single drop falling into a vast ravine,' yet they did not realize that the great ocean can fall into a single drop.

Huineng smiled and said, "What can be done about this fellow? Not long after, he ordered him to share the teaching seat. Huineng then spoke a verse: A single drop falls into the great ocean; The great ocean falls into a single drop. The ocean and the drop are both empty; Where can one find the place where they meet?
He said: "Stop boasting about the *Sifenlü* and laying aside the *Lengyan*. Lower your mental state and investigate thoroughly to the very bottom.
Do not emulate Master Liang who went personally to Mazu, nor be like Deqiao who visited Longtan. For seven years he traveled back and forth at Zhaojue;

for three years he soared above the Azure Cliff. Today, I trouble you to serve as the First Seat; amidst a thicket of a hundred flowers, you manifest the *udumbara*. Later, he paid his respects to the Buddha.
Regarding Jian: Jian asked, "Foguo has a phrase that he never spoke in a confused manner for anyone;
has he ever spoken it to you? The Master said, "Shut your dog's mouth. Jian said in a thunderous voice, "This is not the principle. The Master said, [“... (implying silence or a non-verbal response).
"No one has stolen your salt and tea bag. What is it called? Jue said, "If Foguo would not explain it for you, I shall explain it for you.
The Master said, "When a monk is in doubt, he should leave the monastery and seek instruction elsewhere. Jue laughed heartily.

Not long after, the Master began teaching the Dharma at Baoning, then moved to Huazang, and finally returned to his hometown to lead Zhongfeng. He ascended the hall and said: "The multitude sells flowers, yet I alone sell pines;
though their green hue is not as red as theirs, when calculated, they ultimately do not harmonize with the times. Return, then, to the midst of the verdant mists!
"How laughable that the ancients spoke thus! It was much like fleeing from a mountain peak only to rush into a ravine, or avoiding drowning only to fall into a fire."
Casting fire [into the sea]—how can this compare to acting according to one's capacity? Reaching the point of the eight-foot staff and the five-inch hoe, seek out one or half of one.
Although it is thus, Baoning does not want even half of one. Why? "The wealthy regret that a thousand mouths are too few; the poor lament that a single body is too many.
On the day of the Winter Solstice, he ascended the hall and cited Master Yuquan Hao, who said: "Snow, snow—flake by flake, there is no distinction. He then descended.

When the twelfth month arrived, they continued as before without ceasing through the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth, and eleventh months of the following year.
They were frozen to death and starved to death, so that they would no longer engage in wild and confused talk.
The Master said, "This was not an insult, nor was it a praise; it surpasses Linji and Deshan, yet it is not like Yunmen."
He resided as an Arhat. Now tell me, what was the intention of Yuyuan? After a long silence, he said: "If only the snow could melt away, the spring would naturally arrive.
Later, the Master passed away at his home mountain. During the cremation, a great many relics remained;
commoners dug the earth about a foot deep and all obtained them. These were especially radiant and pure, and even his heart and tongue remained uncorrupted.
Chan Master Ch’e-an Tao-yüan of Zhaojue Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture was the son of the Deng family from Mianzhou. In his youth, he received full ordination at Jiangji Temple.
He traveled east to visit Chan Master Daobie Dao, where, while contemplating the words "Vast emptiness—no sage," he suddenly burst into laughter and said, "Damo has been here all along!
Dao praised him, and he subsequently went to study under Chan Masters Fojian and Foyan.
Having received his recognition, he followed Yuanwu at Jingshan and informed him of his insights; however, Yuanwu did not approve.

When Yuanwu was summoned by imperial decree to Yunju, the Master followed him. Although he attained a degree of conviction and entry, he remained suspicious that a "thorn in his chest" had not yet been removed.
Yuanwu asked a disciple, "When the time of birth and death arrives, what then? The monk said, "The incense altar laughs at the Master. Yuanwu then asked the teacher (Zhaozhou), "What about you?
The teacher said, "The grass bandit is utterly defeated. Yuanwu said, "If someone asks you this, how would you respond?
As the teacher was about to answer, Yuanwu rebuked him, saying, "The grass bandit is utterly defeated! At that moment, the teacher attained thorough realization. Yuanwu [said]:
He struck him with his fist. The Master clapped his hands and laughed loudly. Yuanwu asked, "What did you see that you act like this? The Master replied, "The poisonous fist has not yet been repaid;

it will never be forgotten for kalpas. Yuanwu returned to Zhaojue and appointed the Master as the head of the assembly. When Yuanwu was about to pass away, he entrusted the seat of the abbacy to the Master.
Chan Master Ren of Zhong Tianzhu [Ren-2 + Huan] Hall in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Luoyang. In his youth, he left the household life at Fengxian Monastery in the Eastern Capital.
At the beginning of the Xuánhuā era, he was granted a certificate at the Qìngjī Hall.

After shaving his head and receiving full ordination, he traveled between the Tripitaka Translation Institute and other centers, thoroughly investigating the sutras and śāstras; however, he remained particularly unconvinced by the Chan school. At that time, Yuánwù...

Dwelling at Tianning Monastery, he went to pay his respects at dawn. At that time, Yuanwu was entering the room for a session with the assembly. Upon seeing him, the Master [Zhaozhou] felt deep reverence and, summoning his resolve, stepped forward.

Yuanwu said, "To interpret the meaning based on the scriptures is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three ages; to depart from even a single word of the scriptures is to speak like a demon. Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
As the Master prepared to respond, Yuanwu struck him across the mouth with his staff, causing him to lose a tooth. He attained great enlightenment immediately and remained at Tianning.
"Qing. Thereupon, the teacher and disciple reached a profound accord, and he questioned him without interval. Later, Fayue opened the Dharma for Great Enlightenment (Dajue).

He moved to Central India, and subsequently relocated to Lingfeng. Ascending the hall, he said: "More than half of the spring's ninety days have passed; the weather for nurturing flowers is perfectly harmonious."
"The warbler’s song is fine upon the branches of the *hai-tang* tree. Do those of the current age perceive this?
Even so, how shall one express the phrase that penetrates both sound and form? 'The golden-reined horse neighs on the fragrant grass;
the jade-pavilion person is drunk beneath the peach-blossom sky. He ascended the hall and raised the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature, saying: "A beauty of sixteen years embroiders."
Late. Beneath the purple wisteria flowers, the yellow oriole warbles. How pitiable, this boundless sentiment of spring’s end; it all lies within that moment of silence while the needle is still held.

On the eighth day of the fourth month in the Jiamu year of the Chunxi era, Emperor Xiaozong issued an imperial decree for [the Master] to enter the palace, where he was granted a seat to preach the Dharma.

The Emperor cited the karmic cause and condition of "not being a companion to the myriad dharmas" and commanded him to provide an *niantí* (critical appraisal). After the Master had finished his appraisal, he spoke in verse:
"A scale-weight squeezed out oil; Idle talk and long-winded speech are at an end. A hundred thousand strings of cash girding the waist, Riding a crane up to Yangzhou.
In the year Guihai, he ascended the hall, addressed the assembly, and passed away.
Chan Master Yuanjue of Mount Xiang’er in Mei Prefecture was the son of the Yuan clan of that commandery. He entered the monastic order and studied the *Lamp of the Dharma*.

Having passed the scriptural examination, he received ordination; his original name was Yuánjué (Complete Enlightenment). However, when the Prefectural Governor filled out the temple registration document, he mistakenly wrote the character "Yuán" (Yuan) instead.

Suspecting that the Master might be displeased, the governor jokingly said to him, "Is it appropriate to have a name of only one character? The Master laughed and replied, "Even one character is already too many. The governor marveled at this. Once—

Having received full ordination, he departed from Shu and visited all the venerable masters of the Way. Later, he went to Daopei to rely upon Foxing. After a short while, he entered the room to present his insights.
Foxing said, "You are still far too distant," yet recognizing him as a vessel for the Dharma, he appointed him as an attendant and charged him with receiving guests.
Whenever the Master attended upon Foxing, Foxing would invariably cite the four characters of the *Lotus Sūtra*: "Opening, showing, awakening, and entering," and command him—
He gave a low response. [Dongshan] said again, "Wait until the moment I nod my head upright; only then will you be correct. By chance, he was dismissed from his post for failing in his duties.
Having no place to rely during his period of confinement, he stayed at the home of a layman. One day, while reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*, he reached the passage:

"Furthermore, they do not know which is fire and which is the house. At that, he attained sudden enlightenment. When the period of confinement ended and he returned home to visit his parents, Xingjian nodded his head in approval. Yuanwu—
He received an imperial decree once more to reside at Yunju. When the Master arrived there, he reported his realization to Wuzhuo. Wuzhuo rebuked him, saying, "This is originally a place of purity;
why are you defecating here? At these words, the Master’s doubts were suddenly resolved. In the Ding-si year of the Xiangxing era, the seat at Xiang’er in Mei became vacant.
The Prefect said, "This monastery has long been a nest for vermin; none but men of renowned character and superior virtue could restore it from its ruins.

The various Chan masters recommended the Master [Zhaojue] to accept the invitation. He once said to a guest: "Suduo (Su Shi) said, 'I take this stone back with me; within my sleeves lies the Eastern Sea.
Huanggu (Huang Tingjian) said, 'Huichong’s misty reeds and wild geese make me feel as if I were sitting amidst the Xiao and Xiang rivers and Lake Dongting. He wished—
"Calling for a small boat to return home—those bystanders say it is a painting; this is the very marrow of Zen.
He further said, "When I strike the meditation seat and raise the whisk, Śākyamuni and Confucius are both standing downwind.
When someone cited these words to Chan Master Fohai Yuan, Yuan said, "These are Old Jue’s words. Here in my place, we do not act in such a manner."

Chan Master Zu’jue of Huayan at Zhongyan in Meizhou was the son of the Yang family of Jiazhou. From childhood he was intelligent; having merely glanced over books and history, he could recite them from memory.

He once composed a work to refute Buddhism, whereupon a terrifying vision suddenly appeared before him. Repenting his transgression, he left the household life and relied upon Chan Master Neng of Huimù.
Not long after, an abscess broke out on his knee; for five years no physician could cure it. Consequently, he began writing the *Huayan He lun* (Combined Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra).

When he finished [the recitation], he was moved by a strange dream that night. At dawn, he immediately cast aside his staff and began walking. One day, while reciting the "Chapter on Manifesting Signs," he reached the passage:
"The Buddha-body has no birth, yet it can manifest birth; the nature of phenomena is like empty space, and all Buddhas dwell therein.

Dwelling nowhere and going nowhere, the Buddha is seen everywhere. He then attained enlightenment regarding the fundamental tenets of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. Subsequently, when he was enrolled in the monastic registers, the Prefect...
The Military Commander invited the Master to lecture at the Qianbu Hall. His eloquence was grand and expansive, earning the admiration and respect of all present.

At that time, Chan Master Jing of Nantang happened to visit him and said to the Master, "Observing your lectures, you are peerless in the southwest; it is only a pity that you have not yet transcended the marks of words and letters.
If you were to seek the Way beyond the mundane, you would be the Zhi Jin-gang of today. The Master joyfully ceased his lectures. South...

While traveling, he stayed with Yuanwu at Zhongfu. One day, he entered the inner room for instruction. Yuanwu raised the following case: "Luoshan said, 'When there are words, one seizes the tiger’s head and gathers its tail;
beneath the first phrase, the fundamental principle is clarified. When there are no words, the sharp point of the faculty is exposed, like a flash of lightning or a stroke of a broom.
How do you understand this? The Master was unable to respond. He investigated it day and night, until suddenly he attained realization. He composed [a verse]: [Verse omitted per instructions]
The verse presented to Wuzhu said: My home is atop a solitary peak; for many years the gate has been half-closed. I lament that my body is already old;
I entrust my livelihood to my children and grandchildren. Upon seeing this, Wuzhu gave his approval. The next day, the Master entered the room. Wuzhu asked again, "How was yesterday’s *kōan*?
As the Master was about to respond, Wuzhu shouted, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter of such a principle. The Master remained there once more.

For five years, he became increasingly bewildered and distressed. Later, while reading the *Xuezhilun* (Treatise on Eliminating Attachments) by Chan Master Fushan Yuan at Qixian Monastery on Mount Lu, he read the passage:
"If one says that there is intimacy or distance in awakening, how could there be stinking weeds growing within a sandalwood forest?

At this, he attained a sudden and profound realization. He composed a verse and sent it to Yuanwu, saying: "Leaving the forest, I have returned once more to the thicket; The heavenly net is vast and wide, not..."
"One might flee; who would believe that with karmic conditions there is no place to avoid? Returning, one need not fear a loud voice. He was greatly delighted by this realization.
Holding it up to show the assembly, he said, "I have thoroughly penetrated the *Awakening of Faith in Mahāyāna*.

After he took up residence, a monk asked, "From the first Buddha, King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja, to the last Buddha, Śikhin—what person did they actually encounter? The Master replied, "My home is in the city of Daliang; ask further about the tall [man]."
Anlu said, "As for Deshan carrying his commentaries on his travels—what was his intention? The Master said, "To press your eyes until they burst.
Anlu said, "How far apart are you and the Master’s realization of the *Avataṃsaka* doctrine? The Master said, "Same path, different tracks.
Anlu said, "Deshan of the past, the Master of the present. The Master said, "The evening sun goes west; the water flows east."
[The Master] ascended the hall. He raised the case concerning the passing of Master Shishuang, whereupon the assembly requested the Head Seat to succeed him as abbot.
Regarding the koan posed by Attendant Qian, the Master said: "In the sphere of action of a true master, it is like fire melting ice.

Having passed through the barrier of right and wrong, the total functioning is free from gain and loss. Everyone says that the Head Seat was stuck in 'one color,' yet the Attendant’s insight surpassed his teacher."
One might say that while the essence is subtle, the fundamental principle has been lost; one is utterly confused regarding what to pursue and what to avoid.

Little do they realize that the Head Seat stands like a heron amidst the snow—his species distinct from others—while the Attendant soars like a phoenix through the crimson heavens, unentangled by golden nets.
One stands atop the highest mountain peak; the other walks the depths of the ocean floor. Each comes from his own direction, yet they have gathered together within the ninefold city.

[The Master] turns [the whisk] inside out. Now, do you wish to recognize these two people? He raises the whisk and says: "The dragon lies in the azure depths; the wind is chilling. He lowers the whisk and says:
"The crane returns to the void; its back brushes the heavens. A monk asks: "What is the one shout that is like the Vajra King’s precious sword?
The Master says: "Blood splatters against the Brahma Heaven. [The monk] asks: "What is the one shout that is like crouching..."
Dishi Zi asked, "Master, [your shout] would startle a wild fox to death. The Master said, "How is it that one shout is like a probe or a blade of grass?
The Master said, "It allows me to examine you until your very bones are exposed. [He asked again,] "How is it that one shout does not function as a shout?
The Master said, "You must recognize the person holding the needle; do not merely praise the fine plumage of the mandarin ducks."
Chan Master Fuyan Wenyuan of Tanzhou was the son of the Yang family in Chengdu Prefecture. A monk asked, "What is the true master of Dinglin?
The Master said, "He cuts off the tongues of all people under heaven. The monk asked, "How should one approach him? The Master said, "To look upon him is to go blind. Ascending the hall, he said:
"When one sits squarely and decisively, the traces of both ordinary and sage beings are severed. When one lets go with the hand, heaven..."
The ground turns back. It reaches the point where sun and moon intersect, tigers roar and dragons cry;
in every head and every object, heard by the ear and seen by the eye—what is this upon the *anvaya-satya* (the truth of establishment)? Do you understand thoroughly? *Astaḥ*. *Tuḥ*.
Chan Master Tanyuan of Mingyin Monastery on Mount Xi in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of the Huang family of Wenzhou.

Having traveled extensively to study under various monastic assemblies, he returned to Zhongfu (Mount Jiuhua) in the gengzi year of the Xuanhua era. At that time, the imperial court had decreed that monks be renamed "virtuous scholars" (deshi).

The Master, along with several like-minded companions, entered the Doutu Rock to live in seclusion, subsisting on pine nuts. After some time, Yuanwu was summoned by imperial edict to reside on this mountain, where he personally [encountered the Master].
He went to Yan’s location and had his hair and beard shaved. Upon attaining enlightenment, he was summoned by imperial decree to serve at Tianning Monastery in the capital;

he went there together with the Master and was appointed to oversee the Incense Water Sea (Gandhodaka). Not long after, while striking the drum with a mallet, he suddenly realized the Great Dharma. Whenever anyone questioned him, he would invariably reply, "Do not try to understand.
Consequently, his peers all referred to him as "Mo Li Hui" (One Who Says "Do Not Try to Understand"). Later, while presiding over the assembly in the Dharma Hall, he addressed them: "You..."
There is one pair of eyes; I too have one pair of eyes. If you deceive others, you deceive yourself.
If you become a Buddha or a Patriarch, I, this old monk, shall have no share of it. If you become a donkey or a horse, I, this old monk, shall be unable to save you.
The various donors entered the mountain and requested that he ascend the hall. He spoke a verse, saying: "I have no superior qualities; my name is a hollow claim.
I thank you for coming here with such earnest devotion. Since I have no Dharma to be entrusted, I merely open the mountain gate for you."
Chan Master Xueting Yuanjing of Huqiu in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of Shuangxi. He ascended the hall and said:
"For those who know there is [the Way], ten thousand years pass as if they were a single day; for those who do not know there is, a single day passes as if it were ten thousand years.
Have you not seen how Master Sijian [Sixin] said: 'This mountain monk has been traveling on pilgrimage for over thirty years, and I have treated every ninety days as a single [unit]...'"
In summer, one cannot add a day; one cannot subtract a day. One cannot take it; one cannot let it go. Within that which is unobtainable, there is simply this obtaining.
Yet, as for where Cuiyun sees it, it is not so. For thirty years or more, I have been traveling on pilgrimage;
who cares about one day or ninety days? There is neither obtaining nor non-obtaining. It is thus at every place.
"Come to see Maitreya. But tell me, where is Maitreya? "The golden wind blows over the Wei River; fallen leaves fill Chang'an.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To speak, one must see; to see, one must also be able to speak.

If you can see but cannot speak, you fall into the realm of shadows and your understanding will be biased and withered. If you can speak but cannot see, you fall into the trap of timing and circumstances."
"A sea of poison. If you belong to the school of Cuiyun, even if you can explain it and perceive it, I shall give you thirty blows;
if you cannot explain it and cannot perceive it, I shall also give you thirty blows. For Cuiyun to speak thus, he too deserves thirty blows.
He then called out loudly to the assembly, "Danger! He ascended the hall and said: "Day after day the sun rises in the east, day after day the sun..."
It sets in the west; at that time, people know it exists. From antiquity to the present, it has been as numerous as hemp seeds or millet.
Suddenly, when the pivot of the discourse is turned, it neither emerges from the east nor sets in the west. Tell me, from where does it emerge and set?
If one is a person who has penetrated the barrier, upon hearing such a statement, they will certainly know that the five-li milestone stands outside the city gate. If one is... [penetrated].
As for those who do not pass through [this barrier], they often deceive people halfway up the path. A monk asked, "What is the phrase for arriving home?
The Master said, "Sitting and watching success and failure. He asked, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion? The Master said:
"Distant relatives are not as good as neighbors. [The Master] said, "When you can suck up the waters of the West River in a single gulp, I will tell you.
[The monk asked,] "What about that? The Master said, "Neighbors are not as good as distant relatives. [The monk] asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go?
The Master said, "On top of a dung heap. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Striking it, bumping into it."
Chan Master Nantang Fansi of Tiantong Monastery in Quzhou was the son of the Zhu family of Sutaishan. He ascended the hall and said:
"He kicks over the sea of birth and death and tramples down the shore of nirvana. There are no living people in the world, and no dead men in the Yellow Springs.
He then took up his staff and said: "Today, Nantang’s staff has a place to be entrusted. Is there anyone here who can take it up?"
"Who is there? Come forth and take up this burden! Is there anyone? Is there anyone? After a long silence, he threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
He ascended the hall and said: "Those who know it exist eat porridge and rice; those who do not know it also eat porridge and rice.
How can one directly verify whether they have it or not, whether it is right or wrong, whether it is deviant or correct? If you cannot verify this, [you have failed]."
"The matter of studying the Way is vast and far-reaching. [He lets out a shout. He descends from his seat. Entering the hall, he says:
"I am the fourth-generation descendant of Yangqi. This old fellow has a public case concerning a three-legged donkey that walks on its hooves. Although everyone can cite it,"
It is simply that you do not know where it lands. This mountain monk, without sparing his own eyebrows, shall provide a footnote for all of you:
"An octagonal millstone rolls through the void."
Chan Master Fozhao Jue of Mount Yu’s Junshan Monastery ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'The more one looks up at it, the higher it seems;
the more one drills into it, the harder it becomes. One gazes for it to be in front, and suddenly it is behind. Do you all recognize this? If you do not recognize it, I shall explain it for you:
'The more one looks up at it, the higher it seems'—not separated by so much as a hair's breadth. At the vital ford, the way is cut off; even Buddhas and Patriarchs find it difficult to pass."
He flees! The more you drill into it, the harder it becomes. The true body is spontaneous; the birds sing and the flowers laugh before the emerald cliff.
Looking for it as if it were right in front, it is neither orthodox nor biased. It cuts off the ten directions and its majesty subdues the great chiliocosm. Suddenly it is behind—what a leakage!
How laughable that Yunmen hides his body in the Big Dipper! *Du!* (A shout)
Chan Master Xian of Baohua in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of that region. Entering the hall, he said: "The porridge has been eaten;

this is like placing a head atop a head. Go wash the bowl; this is like drawing legs for a snake. If you ask further how it is, you will only bring about your own defeat. After a long silence, he called out loudly to the assembly.
When the assembly raised their heads, the Master said, "Return to the hall to drink tea. Entering the hall again, he said: "Do not practice Chan."
Cease from studying the Way; let the mind rest and forget its artifice, for it is ever vast and open. The ready-made koan is already too much complication;
even this very "no-mind" is already a fabrication. Even if you could sit and cut off all existence prior to birth, it would still be difficult to penetrate—this old monk says: "Wrong, wrong, wrong!"
Chan Master Jue of Mount Dongshan in Shaoxing Prefecture later resided at Yingsheng. He ascended the hall, and after the three rounds of drums had ceased, he said:
"Everyone has come forward one by one, intending to investigate the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. Do you know that the sword has long since been lost?"
Even if one were to attain awakening directly, it would still be like cutting off one's head to seek life. Dongshan, having no other choice, shall for now examine and press upon the second head.
(He struck the meditation seat with his hand and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall: The flowers are in full bloom; the scenery is warm and bright.
Do not speak of there being another heaven within the flask. If you can recognize it at the tips of the hundred grasses—Dong is three zhang high, and Xi...

Width: eight inches. Entering the hall, he raised an example: "In the past, the butcher Guang'e went to the Buddha's dwelling one day, cast down his butcher’s knife, and said, 'I am counted among the thousand Buddhas.
The World-Honored One said, 'So it is, so it is. Now, in the monasteries of today, people assume that Guang'e was a Buddha in a past life who manifested as a butcher by means of expedient means.
To see Guang'e in such a way is truly a cause for joy—there is no room for dispute."
Sheshuo said, "Guang'e was precisely a man who would not blink when killing people; yet he cast down his butcher's blade and became a Buddha on the spot.
For now, let us say there is no connection. He further said, "When Guang'e cast down his butcher's blade, he said, 'I declare myself one of the thousand Buddhas.
Sheshuo, you are clearly one Buddha yourself. For now, let us say there is no connection. Do you wish to recognize Guang'e?"
On the road back through peach blossoms after wind and rain, where can horse hooves avoid the lingering red petals?
Master Jue of Tiantong in Taizhou ascended the hall and said: "Within the realm of non-arising, there is no place for settled dwelling;
atop a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, how could one afford to set foot? For now, cast your hands free into the void; as for that phrase of turning the body directly beneath—how do you speak it?"
When a person encounters good fortune, their spirit becomes refreshed; when entering fire, their true golden color becomes even more brilliant.
When the Head Seat Daozu of Chengdu’s Zhaojue Monastery first met Yuanwu, he attained enlightenment under the phrase "This very mind is Buddha.
After some time, Yuanwu ordered him to share the seat [of the Dharma hall]. One day, while leading the assembly into the inner quarters, there were about twenty people remaining; the Master...
Suddenly he asked, "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them? The monk had no reply. The Master threw down his whisk and passed away suddenly.
The assembly was all struck with astonishment. They immediately informed Wuzu. When Wuzu arrived, he called out, "Head Seat Zu! The Master opened his eyes and looked at him.
Wuzu said, "Rouse your spirit and pass through the barrier. The Master nodded his head and finally entered nirvana.
The head seat Yunju Zongzhen of Nankang Commandery was a native of Danqiu.
While attending Yuanwu at Yunju, one day as he gazed up at the bell pavilion, he suddenly attained realization. When someone questioned him about it, the Head Seat responded with three verses.
The last of them reads: "I have a single device, Directly shown to you right now: A thunderclap in the blue sky, Lightning rolling, stars racing past. Deshan... [approached].
Ji replied, "The mere application of staff and shout does nothing for the ineffable mystery; what loss is there to you? Upon realizing this, he was greatly delighted.

Ultimately, he maintained his integrity with high self-respect, and his reputation for the Way grew ever more profound. He once wrote on a wall: "Dwelling upon the highest peak among a thousand crags, My years approach sixty, yet I remain carefree and at ease.
I shall not allow my name to be mentioned by others' teeth; I am content to be a monk of a hundred clumsinesses this very day."

Xu Fu, styled Shichuan and titled the Layman of East Lake (Donghu Jushi), served as a Grand Secretary. Whenever he attended his father, the late Dragon Diagram (Longtu) official, to visit Fachang and Lingyuan, they would engage in discourse all day long.

Upon hearing of this, the official regarded it with disdain. However, when he learned that Fachang had passed away amidst casual conversation, he was struck by its significance and began to place firm faith in this Way.
Later, while observing the mourning period for his father, he reflected on how he might repay his boundless debt of gratitude.
He summoned Lingyuan to the site of Xiaozhi to preach the Dharma. Upon ascending the seat, after the questions and answers were concluded, he said:

"Virtuous ones, as for Longtu’s lifelong study of ten thousand scrolls of books—transmitted like water from one vessel to another without a single drop being lost—tell me, where did he usually keep them?
Now, after he has cast off his consciousness, what of those ten thousand scrolls that he kept?"
"Where would you place it? Upon hearing this, the Duke was suddenly enlightened and said, "I have no further regrets.
As Yuan descended from his seat, he asked, "Scholar, what did you just perceive that led you to speak in such a manner? The Duke replied, "If there were anything perceived..."
"Then you have simply set the Master aside," Yuan said. Gong replied, "In that case, the old monk is not as good as you. Yuan asked, "What kind of mental state do you possess, Master?

Yuan laughed heartily. At the beginning of the Jingkang era, while serving as a Ministerial Secretary (Shangshu Waibang), he joined with fellow officials of like mind to hang his alms bowl in Zemo Hall at Tianning Temple, where he applied himself diligently to the study of Yuanwu. Yuanwu, too, rejoiced in his insight.
Dichao Mai went to the office of the Secretary one day and pointed to Wuzhu’s neck, saying, “This old fellow’s heels have not yet touched the ground.
Wuzhu turned his face away and said, “How could a turtle ever escape from inside a jar?
Dichao Mai said, “I am glad that this old fellow’s heels have finally touched the ground. Wuzhu said, “Do not slander him. Dichao Mai then withdrew.

The Prince of Jun, Zhao Lingjin, styled Biaozhi and known as the Recluse Chaoran, served as the governor of Nankang. His administration was successful and his affairs were few; he frequently associated with Chan monks.

He occasionally converted the public hall into a "room of ten feet" (a hermitage) for Moke (Vimalakīrti). It happened that Yuanwu was residing at Mount Ou; the Prince joyfully submitted himself to his guidance.
Yuanwu did not grant him any concessions, yet the Prince pressed his request firmly. Yuanwu said, "In this matter, one must..."
"It must be so; one must simply undergo death once more before it can be attained. The Master (Gong) understood this intuitively and once composed a draft of his realization, the gist of which says:
"My house is poor and has been plundered; who knows that nothing remains? The empty house is unoccupied; how many times have robbers come and struck it?

Having attained this awakening, he instructed [his disciples] to provide him with protection. In the winter of the Gengshen year of the Shaoxing era, the Master was together with the Imperial Secretary Wang Zao, the Minister of State Li Bing, and others.
When Minister Ceng Kai went to Mount Jing to visit Dahui, Dahui heard of his arrival and ordered the drum to be beaten for him to enter the room.
The Minister joyfully approached with incense tucked in his sleeve. Dahui said, "Regarding the story of Zhaozhou washing the alms bowl, how do you, Layman, understand it?"
The Duke said, "What bowl are you looking for? He brushed out his sleeves and went out. Huì rose up, grabbed him, and said, "The ancients attained awakening right here;
why do you not attain it? As the Duke prepared to reply, Huì struck him and said, "What bowl are you looking for?"
The Duke said, "Only by returning this old man can it be accomplished.
Li Mison, a Minister of the Court of Judicial Review and known as the Layman Puxian, had read books at a young age, his eyes moving through five lines of text simultaneously.

At eighteen, he passed the provincial examination and attained the jinshi degree in the capital. He subsequently rose through various high and important offices until, at the age of twenty-eight, he served in the Secretariat.
The Attendant (She-ren) frequently entered Yuanwu’s quarters. One day, returning from the morning court audience, he reached Tianjin Bridge when his horse bolted;
at that moment, he had a sudden realization, and sweat poured from his entire body. He went straight to Tianning Monastery, where it happened that Yuanwu was stepping out the gate.

Seeing him from afar, Yuanwu called out, "Layman, congratulations! Your great matter is now finished. The Attendant replied in a sharp voice, "Monk, why are you deluding your own eyes? Yuanwu then gave a shout.
The Duke also shouted. Thereupon, their exchange of sharp points was swift and decisive; in all his dialogues with Wuzhuo, he never yielded when the moment was right.

Later, the Duke was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and requested a temple stipend to return to Lianjiang in Fujian, where he built a hermitage for his own enjoyment. One day, he suddenly manifested a slight illness.
He immediately requested hot water. Having finished his bath, he sat in the full lotus posture and composed a verse, saying:

"In vain have I spoken of Mu and Hu from of old; today, I reveal it clearly. The void crushes down Mount Sumeru—what need is there to speak of the path above? Having cast aside his brush, he passed away.
The Daoist woman Zhu of Ju’ān was the niece of You Cha-yuan of Jian-ning. From her youth, she resolved not to marry and devoted herself to the ancestral Way.
Upon hearing the words of Yuanwu’s public address, she attained clear and thorough understanding.
Yuanwu said, “You must further cast away what you have seen before you can attain true freedom. Zhu replied with a verse: “The pillar protrudes its horizontal bones; Space plays with its claws.”
"Teeth. Even if you were to grasp this through profound insight, it would still be like sand in your eyes.

Lingren Benming called himself "The Illuminated Chamber. Having personally attained resonance with Yuanwu, he traveled extensively to consult renowned masters, all of whom granted him their seal of approval.
On the full moon of the second month in the Gengshen year of the Xiangxi era, he personally wrote three verses and sent them to Caotang Qing, subtly revealing his intention to pass away.
At the end of the month, he bid farewell to his relatives and passed away. Caotang appended a colophon to the verses, which were later published.
Dahui also once offered words to elucidate them. The verses say: "I do not recognize afflictions as bodhi; if one follows after afflictions..."
This is ignorance. At the moment of arising and ceasing, one must understand it. When a hawk flies over Silla, the people do not know it;
they fail to recognize that afflictions are bodhi. Pure flowers grow from the mud. When someone comes and asks me what I am doing, I have finished eating my gruel and rice and am washing my bowl.
Do not concern yourself with it; do not concern yourself with it. All day long, you are a fool playing with sea sand. If you wish to know the source, [look here].
The true face that comes forth is the single wooden sword (ekadaṇḍa) of the Patriarch. Those who cannot speak it die beneath the sword;
those who can speak it also die beneath the sword. Ultimately, how is it? Do not travel by night; you must arrive at dawn.
Lady Fan of Fan County in Chengdu Prefecture had lived as a widow for many years; she usually sat and did not lie down.

Hearing that Yuanwu was residing at Zhaojue Temple, she went there to pay her respects and requested instruction on the causes and conditions for entering the Way. Yuanwu instructed her to contemplate: "It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha."
"It is not an object. What is it? For a long time, Fan could find no point of resonance. He wept and said to Wù, "Master, what skillful means can you provide to allow me to understand this easily?
Wù replied, "There is indeed a skillful means. He then instructed him to simply look into: "What is this?
Later, Fan had an awakening and said, "I never realized how close it was all along!"
Chan Master Wenshu Xindao of Changde Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Taiping Qin. He was the son of the Xu family of Meizhou. At the age of thirty, he received full ordination.

He went to Chengdu to study the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi* (Consciousness-Only), believing that he had reached the ultimate understanding. A fellow student challenged him, saying: "The three realms are mind-only; all phenomena..."
"Only consciousness! Now, with the myriad phenomena manifest before one's eyes, where does the mind-consciousness reside? The Master was at a loss and did not know how to respond;

he subsequently left the mountain pass and wandered through the Jianghuai region. Upon arriving at Taiping in Shu, he heard Chan Master Fojian’s night discourse, in which he raised the story of Zhaozhou’s "Cypress Tree.
When it reached the point where Jue Tiezui said, "The former master did not say this; do not slander the former master," [the Master attained enlightenment].
"Excellent. Because of his great doubt, he had been reflecting for a long time until one night it suddenly dawned upon him.
He immediately went to the master’s quarters, intending to recount what he had realized. Upon seeing him arrive, Huian closed the door. The Master said, "Master, do not deceive me.
Huian replied, "The ten directions have no walls; why do you not enter? The Master punched through the window paper. Huian then opened the door, grabbed him, and said:
"Way! Way! The Master took up a mirror with both hands, blew upon it, and departed. He then presented this verse: "Zhaozhou has a story about the cypress tree;
Zen students have transmitted it throughout the world. Most merely pluck the leaves and seek the branches, Unable to understand it directly at its source.
Jue says there are no such words; This is truly like reviling someone in their face with foul language."

If a practitioner of Zen possesses the eye that penetrates all directions, they should take care to discern the true from the false within this. Jia Shen deeply agreed with this and frequently praised it to his guests.

Later, he appointed [the Master] to share the seat with him. When Liu Xiang, the Regional Inspector, invited him to open the Dharma at Tianning Monastery, he was promoted shortly thereafter to Wenshu at Dayue.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The lion yawns; the elephant king roars. Yunmen hides his body within the Big Dipper. White.
For what reason is a cloud called a "hand"? The Buddhas of the three periods cannot know it; yet the "tawny cat" and the "white ox" do indeed know it.
But tell me, what is this matter of their knowing? Rain beats upon the pear blossoms as butterflies fly; the wind blows the willow catkins as they roll away.
[Ascending the hall, he took up his staff and pointed directly upward, saying: "At such a time, one pierces through arrogance."
Śakra’s heel strikes the ground once and says: "At such a time, it shatters the crown bone of King Yama. Then, pointing toward the east, he says:
"At such a time, it pierces the eyes of the carp in the Eastern Sea. Pointing toward the west, he says:

There is much moisture; each [item] should be dried frequently in the sun. In the first year of the Xuanhua era, an edict was issued to change the title of *bhikṣu* to *de-shi*. He ascended the hall and said:

Clad in a silver-brown crane-feather robe, with a banana-leaf turban wrapped about his head, this guest of the forest and springs has received the sovereign’s grace twice over.
Thus it is said: "If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season.
But tell me, what is the current season? Vairocana wears a jeweled crown to manifest the conventional within the absolute; Mañjuśrī is old...
Old man, draped in a crane-feather cloak, you must likewise conform to the exigencies of the times. As it is so for one person, so it is for all; together we shall establish a monastic grove.
How joyful it is that a gathering of immortals has been assembled! Let us together sip the wine of the Immortal of Confusion (*míxiān zhòu*) and chant the *Bùxū* hymns in unison.

At times we shall read the *Língbǎo Dúrénjīng*, and at other times discuss the elixir of longevity and immortality. We shall play the zither beneath the moon, our fingers— (Note: The provided text ends abruptly with "指," which translates to "fingers" or "pointing.")
The sound of the primordial antiquity issues forth; like a chessboard spread before the hall, its wondrous manifestation transcends the realm of divine mechanisms.

As for that phrase, "neither advancing nor retreating"—how would you explain it? Even if one were to transcend and become an immortal on the path of the Three Purities, it remains ultimately nothing but the cycle of saṃsāra.
The Illusory Body. In the ninth month of the second year, he was reinstated as a monk. Ascending the hall, he said: "Unfettered by the field-robe, he dons the feathered garment;
