false interpretations are fabricated; and the scriptures are edited and excised. The sound of the gongs and cymbals ceases, while the begging bowl is augmented with a base—such are the many forms of deceitful pretension.
Having deceived the Sagely Sovereign, we rely upon Your Majesty, the Emperor, whose sagely virtue and sagely brilliance do not forget the sacred entrustment and do not abandon the Teaching.
You have specially bestowed your Imperial Calligraphy for circulation throughout the world, and further permitted monks and nuns to once again don the monastic robes.
This is truly like cold ashes catching fire again or withered wood flourishing anew; without leaving one’s secular form, one assumes the form of a monk, yet does not depart from the realm of Māra.
He enters the Buddha-realm; he sounds the Dharma-drum again and re-establishes the sagging disciplinary code. The delusive immortal wine is transformed into ambrosial jade nectar;
the *Buxu* lyrics are turned into songs for returning home. He lays down the silver wooden tablet and takes up the *niṣīdana*.
Yesterday morning, I bowed my head and raised my hands; today, I offer greetings and inquire after your well-being. Only the outward appearance has changed, not the person of old.
I venture to ask the assembly: Is the person of old one, or is it two? After a long silence, he said: "Even the autumn wind understands how to loathe disorder;
it blows away the ashes of the Way from those years. In the spring of the third year of Jianyan, he addressed the assembly, citing:
Regarding the circumstances of Linji’s entry into extinction and his entrustment to Sansheng, the Master said: "The treasury of the true Dharma-eye has been extinguished by a blind donkey.
Where did Linji ever say such a thing? People of both past and present have all spread this falsely; do not believe it, but simply wait and see after three months.
When the intercalary third month arrived, the rebel Zhong Xiang rose up, and his followers wished to lead the Master southward. The Master said: "In the study of the Way..."
Having fully understood birth and death, what is there to avoid? When the bandits arrived, the Master said, "Kill me quickly to satisfy your hearts.
The bandits immediately raised their spears and struck him; his blood was all white milk. The bandits were terrified; they drew their mats over him and departed.
Chan Master Zhibing of Nanhua in Shaoyou was a native of Yongkang in Shu. He ascended the hall and said: "This matter is most extraordinary; it is not obstructed by direct speech.
The old farmer of the eastern neighbor, following custom, has obtained a piece of the truth. It not only penetrates sound and form, but also accords with the times.
If you ask what school this belongs to, the eight characters do not apply to anyone. He struck the meditation seat and descended.
[The Master] ascends the hall. Day after day I speak; from time to time I raise [the topic]. It is like the earth upholding a mountain—how much effort does it take?
The parrot of Longxi is beloved by people; it is mostly because he can speak. Cease your deliberations; keep your companions. When the wise hear even a little, they should seize it with vigor.
There is yet another thing that is truly marvelous: the cat is uniquely adept at catching mice. [He] ascends the hall. With...
He brandished his staff toward the air and stirred it, saying, "I stir the long river into butter and milk; yet the shrimp and crabs still have their eyes covered in rheum.
He struck once and said, "I transform the great earth into gold; yet the destitute fellow remains, as before, bare-boned and naked.
Is it that he himself has no share? Or is it that he refuses to accept it? Among them, there may be a man capable of bearing this burden—how many such are there?
"A person loses their money and meets with calamity. He struck the meditation seat once more and said, "Do you understand? When you reach the Treasure Mountain, you must open your eyes;

do not let yourself return in haste with empty hands. Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring light is lush and flowers compete to bloom; the nightingale cries as the moon sets behind the western mountains.
Qiaofanbodi sticks out his tongue in long astonishment. To whom can this clear matter be explained? Agh! Ascending the hall, he said:
Delusion does not delude itself; it is established in opposition to awakening. Awakening does not awaken itself; it is spoken of because of delusion.
Therefore, awakening is the substance of delusion, and delusion is the function of awakening. Both delusion and awakening have no source; within this, there is neither distinction nor commonality.
Without distinction or commonality, it cannot be moved away. The Patriarch did not bring it here; its nostrils weigh a thousand catties.
Chan Master Longya Zhicai of Tanzhou was the son of the Shi family in Shuzhou. Early on, he served diligently at the Dharma seat of Fojian, never declining difficult tasks;

thus, his reputation had already spread throughout the monastic community. When he traveled to other regions toward the end of his life, he arrived at Huanglong, where it happened that Sisi was at the main gate.
When asked where he had come from, he stated his name, and it was immediately recognized that he was from Shuzhou.
Taiping was then the Master Cai. The following day, he entered the room, and Sīxīn asked him:
"If you understand the first phrase, you understand the final phrase; if you understand the final phrase, you understand the first phrase.

Setting aside both the first and the final, how do you understand the story of Baizhang and the wild fox? The Master replied: "Upon entering the door, I already knew the understanding with which he came."
"What need is there to further mention being trampled in the mud? Xinxin said, "The new elder has already died in the hands of the senior monk.
The Master said, "Though the words differ, the ultimate principle is without discrepancy. Xinxin asked, "What is this matter that is without discrepancy?"
The Master said, "If one does not strike the horn of Huanglong, how can one know the pearl beneath his chin? He struck him immediately.
When he first resided at Yuelu, on the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked, "Regarding Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout—today I request the Master to comment upon them.
The Master said, "Suru suru. The monk said, "Suru suru—is there still the meaning of the West [the Zen tradition] within this or not? The Master said, "Suru suru."
"Ruo. For this reason, the monastic community called him Cai-sou-lu. Later, he moved to Longya.

Because Emperor Qinzhong had ascended the throne, the officials requested that he take the high seat. After offering his prayers for the Emperor’s longevity, he took his place, picked up his staff, struck it once, and said:
"The Preface to the Imperial Edict states: 'The originally profound realm, the wondrous field of all Buddhas. Just now, with this staff, I have already [revealed it] for everyone."
I have spoken. If you awaken to this, there will be no principle that is not revealed and no phenomenon that is not encompassed.
Should it still be otherwise, I cannot help but provide another message: Under the sun of Shun, the four seas are bright; with harmony filling the heavens, all rejoice in peace and prosperity.
Master Yanxiang’s staff brought forth joy; as it was cast to the ground, a cry of "Ten Thousand Years! resounded like a mountain echo.

[The Master] threw down his staff and descended from the seat. Entering the hall, he snapped his fingers once and said: "With a single snap of the fingers, the eighty thousand gates are perfectly realized; in a single instant, the three great kalpas are extinguished."
If you can see it and practice it, when you are energetic, walk in *caṅkrama*; when you are weary, rest. If you do not understand, it is like two mandarin ducks carrying a single turtle.
[The Master] ascended the hall and cited the small assembly instruction (*kṣudra-upadeśa*) of Master Sīxīn, saying:
"As for this matter, it is like a family that has three sons. The first son is intelligent and wise; he filially supports his parents and receives guests who come and go. He was the master...
He took charge of the family estate. The second son was fierce, stubborn, and cunning; he was greedy, lewd, and addicted to wine, lying drunk in the streets and alleys, ruining the family estate.
The third son was blind, deaf, and mute; he could not distinguish between beans and wheat, nor could he do anything at all—he only knew how to eat his meals.
Among these three, Huanglong wished to select one for a specific purpose. Furthermore, there are four lines: "Within death there is life; within life..."
"Among them is death; within death there is constant death; within life there is constant life. Take these four lines and test the monks of the world.
The Master said, "What do you call these 'four lines'? What are the surnames and names of the three men?

The flower has departed. The three people share a single substance where function is non-function; the four lines share a single resonance where emptiness is non-emptiness.
If you wish to recognize these three people and the four lines: the golden crow first emerges as a mass of red.

The Master resided at Longya for thirteen years, governing the assembly with austerity; the monks revered him. Grand Marshal Xi Gong Zhenqian invited him to reside at Yunxi, where he stayed for four years. He succeeded [to the abbacy].
In the eighth month on the full moon of the year Wuxu, he suddenly gathered the assembly and entrusted them with the affairs of the temple. He then wrote this verse:

"On the day of the Mid-Autumn Festival in the year Wuxu, I have completed my tenure as the abbot of this mountain home. Upon my departure, even my own self does not exist; how could there be any empty space left to be sought?"
He continued to bestow his instructions as usual. On the twenty-third day, he gathered the assembly once more and posed this question:
"Nirvana and birth-and-death are both but flowers in the sky; Buddhas and sentient beings are merely metaphorical designations. How, then, do you all respond?

The assembly offered various responses, but none were in accord with the truth. The Master shouted, "Suffering! Suffering! He then said, "White clouds surge from the earth; the bright moon hangs in the heavens."

Having finished speaking, he departed with a faint smile. Upon cremation, five-colored *śarīra* relics were obtained, which were enshrined together with his sacred bones in a stupa at the northwest corner of the temple.
Zen Master Penglaiqing of Mingzhou ascended the hall and said: "A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. For now, let it be as it is."

He raised his whisk and said: "Look! Look! One tune, two tunes—no one understands them. After the rain has passed, the autumn waters in the night pond run deep. [He] ascended the hall. Du.

who can understand how to pluck blossoms from a rootless tree? Raising his staff, he said: "This is the rootless one.

Now tell me, does it open its flowers or not? After a long silence, he said: "Simply because of the rain throughout the night, another year of spring has passed. He ascended the hall and gave this discourse.
Fayan said, "Recognizing the bench, it extends beyond its circumference. Yunmen said, "Recognizing the bench, heaven and earth are vastly different.

Chan Master Shouxun Fodeng of Heshan in Anji County was the son of the Shi family of that prefecture. He went to study under Chan Master Guangjian Ying but did not find resonance there.
He then proceeded to Taiping, where he joined the assembly and requested instruction, yet for a long time he made no progress. Thereupon, he folded his bedding and prepared to depart.

"A sweet melon is sweet to the very stem; a bitter gourd is bitter to the very root. [The Master] ascends the hall and cites the story of the old woman burning the hermitage.

hearing a chorus of frogs suddenly croaking, he mistakenly took it to be the sound of the shaving board. He hurried toward the source, where someone enlightened him, saying, "Those are the cries of frogs, not the sound of the board.
The Master was struck with sudden clarity and went to the Abbot’s quarters to disclose his realization. Foyan said, "Is it not..."

When Rāhula did not appear, the Master abruptly stopped him, saying, "Master, there is no need to mention this; wait until he leaves and you shall see for yourself. Before long, Rāhula attained realization and composed a verse, saying:
"In a dream I heard the sound of wooden boards; upon waking, the frogs croaked. The frogs and the sound of the boards—mountains and peaks all at once became one.

The Master firmly declined, saying, "This is no small matter. It is like piercing the eye with a golden needle; if there is a discrepancy even as slight as a hair's breadth, the pupil will be destroyed.

Out of humility and harmony, he is naturally accustomed to turning the light inward. He does not realize that he is already atop the azure clouds."
He once again allowed his body to enter among the assembly during his later years. When a student earnestly requested instruction, he could not refuse.
Later, he spoke a verse, saying: "Because all dharmas are empty, my mind is empty; Because my mind is empty, all dharmas are the same. All dharmas and my mind have no separate essence;
They exist only within this present single thought. "Tell me," he said, "which one is this thought? The assembly was at a loss. The Master shouted.
He ended with a single shout.

The Gishi (Court Gentleman) Feng Jie, the lay practitioner Jichuan, had sought instruction from various renowned masters since his youth.

Finally, he resided at Longmen, where he followed Chan Master Foyan Yuan for two years. One day, while walking together with Yuan in the Dharma Hall, a temple boy happened to run across the courtyard.

In the Ding-si year of the Xiang-sheng era, he was appointed as a Censor. It happened that Chan Master Dahui was presiding over the opening of the hall at Mingqing Temple.

When Dahui descended from his seat, the official pulled him back and said, "Every time you speak before the scholar-officials, Master, you say: 'In this life, I shall certainly not [become a monk]...'"
"This wretched creature! Why has he suffered defeat today? Huì said, "The entire great earth is this Venerable Gǎo. Where do you see him?
As the official was about to respond, Huì struck him with his palm. The official said, "I brought this upon myself.

He sealed this with a verse: "The Sanskrit and the Chinese are forged into one mass. How lamentable, these worldly people!"

He then took up his staff, rested it upon his knees, and passed away with a serene expression. The Commissioner of the Circuit requested, saying, "Your Reverence’s coming and going is so free and at ease;

It is said: "The first three and the eleventh; the middle nine and the last seven. When the old man’s words were exhausted, Guige’s eyes turned red, and he finally departed for eternity.

[The questioner] asked, "What is it like after emerging from the water? The Master said, "A fragrant scent pervades the entire world.

Chanshi Shutou Zihui of Diaoyutai, Tazhou, was a dharma successor of Chanshi Jingsu of Daisui. He was a native of that same prefecture. By profession, his family had been stone masons for generations. Although...

He was illiterate, yet his mind aspired to the school of emptiness (*śūnyatā*). He frequently requested that others orally transmit the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* to him until he was able to recite it from memory.

Abandoning his home, he entered the service of Dàsui, where he provided for the sweeping and cleaning. The temple authorities ordered him to quarry stones from a cliff; while his hands never ceased holding the hammer and chisel, his mouth never stopped reciting the sutra.
As he worked, he spoke aloud: "Today there is a hollow thud; tomorrow there will be a hollow thud. When birth and death arrive..."

"What is the ultimate resolution? The Master was startled; he set down his vessel, performed a prostration, and expressed his wish to hear the ultimate Dharma. Consequently, he followed [the Master] to the abbot’s quarters.

[The Master] then ordered him to cease reciting the sutras for a time and instead contemplate the kōan concerning Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman. The Master kept this thought in mind at every moment, never letting it depart from his heart.
After some time, while he was chipping away at a stone, the stone became somewhat hard. He struck it with all his might, and upon suddenly seeing a flash of fire, he attained sudden enlightenment.
Chè ran to the abbot’s quarters, prostrated, and presented this verse: "Exhausting every effort, there is not a shred of clue; The sparks fly apart, yet they were always right here.
The Master, filled with joy, said, "You have penetrated [the truth], Chè! He then offered a verse on Zhaozhou’s interrogation of the old woman:

"Broom! Sweep away the dust and smoke until it is empty and void! Suikě followed this instruction, whereupon [the Master] conferred upon him the monastic robes.

Because he had been a stonecutter by trade, he was known as "Huishító" (Stone-Turning). He ascended the hall and said: "To study the Way through Zen meditation is much like calling out for thirst from the bottom of a well;
one fails to realize that one has merely blocked one's ears and eyes, unable to escape the situation. Take, for instance, the twelve..."

At all times—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down; whether moving, turning, or acting—who is it that causes you to do these things? When you see with your eyes and hear with your ears, where is there that is not the beginning of the path?
If you can recognize this beginning of the path, it is the Great Path of Liberation. Only then will you know that I, this old man, bear witness for you;
the mountains, rivers, and the great earth bear witness for you. Therefore it is said: "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions..."
Brahmā: "The single path to the gate of Nirvāṇa. O virtuous ones, generally speaking, when there is a thing confronting you, you must see the source of that thing;
when there is no place for a thing, you must see the source of that thing. Once you have seen the source, the source has no source.
Since the source is not a source, where would it not be perfect? O practitioners of Zen, look at this old man—what does he have?"
"You are superior in this matter. What is there about these people that is not equal to this old man? Do you understand?
Thirty-six thousand acres of Taihu Lake—the moon speaks from its heart upon the waves; to whom does it speak?"
Chan Master Husheng Yuchou Jujing of Tongchuan Prefecture was the son of the Yang family of Chengdu.
At the age of fourteen, he took refuge with Anhui of Baima as his teacher. Having heard of the renown of Nantang, he went to rely upon him.

When Nantang raised the koan of Xiangyan’s "Dragon Roars within a Withered Tree," the Master engaged in a back-and-forth exchange of inquiry and challenge until he attained great enlightenment beneath the master's words. One day, Nantang asked him:
"Do not remain in the cold crags where the strange grasses turn green. Sitting amidst white clouds, the essence of the school is not yet perfected.

How will you do it? The Master said, "You must brandish the sword. If you do not brandish the sword, the fisherman will take up residence in the nest. Dongshan was startled and said, "This little fellow!"

The Master said, "Take care," and departed. He went to reside at Dongyan (East Rock). Upon ascending the hall, he said: "The moon gives birth to one. "Having newly settled at East Rock, my sorrow and solitude increase.

The dusty roads of the mundane world have many twists and turns, Yet in the granaries and storehouses, there is not a single grain. The cliffs are my companions, the springs my match. A refreshing breeze comes sweeping into the room;
The Mountain King and the Local Deity busy themselves in secret, While the cloud-slabs, bells, and fish-shaped chimes steal [the light]."

Tear drops. Let not the people of the world say that one who guards an empty cliff has nothing to do; there is also the striking of the eastern fence with the western wall. He once said to the assembly:
"The most essential point of study does not go beyond what the former Nantang spoke of—the initial phrase and the final phrase.
Those who penetrate these have completed their life's work. Should you not yet have done so, I shall further divide them for you into ten gates, each to be verified."

Has your own mind yet attained stability? First, you must believe in the separate transmission outside the teachings. Second, you must know that there is a separate transmission outside the teachings.
Third, you must realize that the preaching of the insentient is no different from the preaching of the sentient.
Fourth, you must see your nature as clearly as looking at an object in the palm of your hand, with every stage of realization stable, secure, and distinct. Fifth, you must...
1. One must possess the eye of the discernment of dharmas (*dharmapravicaya*). 2. One must practice the bird-path and the profound way. 3. One must be proficient in both civil and military arts. 4.
One must suppress the heterodox and manifest the orthodox. 5. One must possess great capacity and great function. 6. One must act among those of different species.
If you wish to perpetuate the lineage of the Dharma, you must exhaust these essential principles; only then can you sit upon this curved wooden seat and receive the people of the world.
Prostrations. To dare to take the Buddhas and Patriarchs as one’s teachers, one must reach such a state;

otherwise, it is merely a constant pursuit of empty formalities. At some future time, Old Yama will not let you off. Among the students, there were those who each composed verses on the various gates and presented them to the Master.
The Master showed them his own verse, saying: "The essential points of the ten gates are applied within the palm of the hand; when the opportune moment arrives, action follows naturally."
The author need not arrange them in a fixed order; for the most part, the beginning and the end constitute the foundation.
Chan Master Sheng of Nan Yan in Jianzhou ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "To protect life, one must kill; only when all have been killed does one dwell in peace.
If you understand the meaning within this, you are clearly still halfway there. But tell me, what is the phrase for arriving home?"
"How is it? [The Master said: "Śākyamuni and Maitreya have vast capacities, yet upon examination, they are still merely his servants.

Regarding these causes and conditions, there are many nowadays in the monastic groves who proclaim them and not a few who deliberate upon them.

To wash and rinse—this too is a sickness; one must simply let go and not grasp at it. Furthermore, there are those who instead seek understanding in some remote corner of the feet.
If you understand in such a way, this sickness is the most difficult to cure. This is because his words possess a place of subtle artistry that is difficult for students to grasp suddenly;
as soon as you attempt to direct the mind toward them, you have already missed the mark. The predecessors called this:

Then, taking a single step before the ten-thousand-fathom peak, you can encompass past and present and cut off all under heaven.
The human tongue—does anyone nowadays still possess such a thing? If there is, come forth and speak! If not, listen further to this verse:
A three-legged donkey prances on its hooves, Straight through the ten-thousand-fathom pit of Vipaśyin.
Clouds atop the ridge peak never find rest; Water flowing down the ravine is far too busy. Which Elder of Hunan understands this? Passersby...

"Furthermore, it lies beyond the green mountains. He ascended the hall and said: "Heaven attains the One and becomes clear; Earth attains the One and becomes tranquil; the Sovereign attains the One and brings order to the world.

But tell me, what is this extraordinary thing within the gate of the patch-robed monks? Heaven attains the One..."

The constellations of the Ox, the Cow, the Woman, the Void, the Peril, the Room, and the Wall; when earth attains this One, the myriad phenomena—both the vast array of forms and the common rubble—are all there.
When a sovereign attains this One, those above and below, in the four directions, have no equal. But tell me, how is it when a patch-robed monk attains this One?

If you wish to see where the guest comes from, observe: "Holding a scripture idly, he stands leaning against a pine. On the occasion of the Buddha-Bathing ceremony, the Master raised the example of Yaoshan’s bathing of the Buddha.

"This one. Simply turn the handle of the wooden ladle toward him; while he is hesitating, splash it right across his face.

The Master’s Ten Oxherding Pictures and their verses circulate in the world.
On the occasion of the summer retreat, Chan Master Mo Tang Shaowu of Nengren Monastery in Jiazhou ascended the hall and said: "The first step:
throughout the ten directions, the entire body is manifest. The final word: within a single mote of dust, it is deeply locked away. Sometimes he brings this forth.

It is like a long sword leaning against the heavens, its radiance illuminating the universe. At times it is set aside, like snow falling upon a red furnace; it contains all phenomena within its emptiness.
When one reaches such a state, the heavenly demons and external paths surrender with folded hands, and the Buddhas of the three periods of time likewise submit.
At one time, having prostrated, you may take Great Perfect Enlightenment as your monastery. Within a single hair-tip, you manifest jeweled royal lands;
thus, going to the Western Heaven in the morning and returning to the Eastern Land in the evening is also the practice of *jinzu* (staying within bounds).
Sitting amidst clusters of a hundred flowers or walking through brothels and taverns is likewise *jinzu*. Although it is so, this has never been moved.
A single step back. If it is thus, then the ninety days [of the summer retreat] will have no wasted effort; the hundred kalpas will have their utility in this very moment.
This is sufficient to repay the unrequitable debt of gratitude and to assist in the transformation of non-action.
This is precisely the wondrous mind of *nirvāṇa*, the precious sword of the Vajra King. I dare ask the assembly: how does one reach this field? It is like a person ascending...
"Mountains. Each of you must exert yourselves. He ascended the hall and presented the case of Zhaozhou visiting the two hermitage masters.
He offered this verse: One mountain ends, and another begins; Severing the solitary peak, look closely. Mist rolls away and clouds disperse; the mountains are still.
The sky of Chu is vast and wide, a single cold orb.
Zhizhiziyan, the Hermit of Tuxi in Pengzhou, was a native of Mianzhou. When he first arrived at Dawsui, he heard the verse that Master Shitou presented to the assembly;
suddenly, he attained realization of its meaning and returned to live in seclusion at Tuxi. Between precipitous cliffs and deep ravines, there was a rock resembling a crouching strange beast;
the Master carved it into a dwelling, from which a miraculous spring gushed forth, neither drying up nor overflowing. The fourfold assembly...

He marveled at this. After thirty years had passed, the transformative influence of his teaching spread widely. On the day his hut was completed, he composed a verse, saying: "A single blow completes the stone hermitage;
In every direction, spontaneity is attained. Cool and clear, it holds no summer heat; Pure and pristine, it possesses sweet springs. Vast and expansive, it encompasses the realms of sand;
Silent and still, it is severed from all conditions. Within this, there is boundless meaning: Wind and moon, one sleeps upon a single bed."
Jianmen Nan was a man of profound integrity who practiced the Way. Since his initial realization through a single word of accord with Dazui, he had served him with unwavering diligence.
Later, he went to visit Chan Master Chonghua Yun. During their meeting, Yun questioned him regarding the "Three Seals of the Zen School.

Nan replied: "The seal on the sky, the seal on the mud, and the seal on the water; from level ground, cold waves rise up in competition. Even if one were to exercise every degree of skill in coming and going," [it would still be so].
This is like the numinous tortoise dragging its tail;

do not take it as the characters of the *Shangshu*. His family lineage was from Fennings in Yuzhang. Because of official duties, he traveled to Western Sichuan, where he visited Chan Master Nantang Jing to inquire about the essentials for resolving his mind.
Nantang instructed him to maintain mindfulness toward a "good place. Just as he happened to enter the latrine, he suddenly heard—

A foul odor suddenly struck him; he quickly covered his nose with his hand and attained realization. He immediately presented this verse: "From of old, my natural grace has loved elegance; I have often laughed at those who seek it outwardly.
Though there be ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences, there is no place to find it; The moment it is attained, it is right here on the tip of the nose.
Nantang replied: "When one dharma is penetrated, all dharmas are complete; its wondrous function extends in every direction—what more could there be?"
Seeking it out, a blue serpent emerges from its case and the demonic armies prostrate; the blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head.

He asked Nantang, “I have a certain point of view, yet as soon as someone questions me, I am unable to speak.
I do not know where my fault lies. Nantang said, “The fault lies in having a certain point of view. Nantang then asked, “When did you take office?
The official replied, “On the fourth day of the eighth month last year. Nantang said, “Since you were appointed as an Inspector, when did you leave the yamen? The official replied:
On the twentieth day of last month, the Master said, "Why is it that one cannot open one's mouth? At this, Gao attained awakening.

The table stands upright. Hanshan and Shide laugh heartily. They point to the old pine tree before the gate.
Tell me, what is it they are pointing at? Suddenly, when the wind blows it down, it is but a great pile of firewood.
Chan Master Miaoguang (Hui’gan) of Jiaozhong, a native of Quanzhou and a descendant of the Li clan of Min, was the dharma heir of Chan Master Dahui Zonggao of Mount Jing.
He was the sixteenth-generation successor in the lineage descending from Mount Nanyue. From childhood, he was rarely seen smiling or speaking.
He took pleasure in hearing Buddhist chants (brahmaghoṣa). At fifteen, he followed the Chan Master Wenhui at Youyan, where he shaved his head and donned the dyed robes;
yet he still delighted in reading various secular books. One day he said, "Since I have already shaved my head and donned the dyed robes, I ought to aim for thorough awakening.

How can I remain intoxicated by worldly classics? Thereupon, he left the mountain ridges and went to visit Chan Master Yuanwu at Yunju. Subsequently, he studied under Chan Master Xiang of Huangbo and Chan Master Wu of Ga’ān. [The following are] his recorded sayings and dialogues.

He was in accord with them all. However, as bandits rose up in Huai and Chu, he returned to pay his respects to Fuxin. It happened that Dahui was residing in Guangzhou, so the Master went there to follow him.
Dahui said to him, "Try to cite one or two instances of what you have attained while at Fuxin's place, and let me see.

they saw only one side. Huazang has no livelihood to establish, nor any house to break.
Whenever he meets someone, he throws out a punch of old age, wishing for them to arrive directly at the moment. But tell me, what is it like after arriving? The thirty-six peaks."
"Observation is insufficient; turn back and ride a donkey backward upon level ground.

The ground has no needle-point; turning my steps, I return. The Buddha is not it, nor is the mind. To accept it directly in its very essence is to be free from all dependence.

It is like the moon in the empty expanse over the green depths of ten thousand ages; only after searching for it again and again can one finally come to know it. [He ascended the hall. After a long silence, he called to the assembly, saying:

only then will one manifest the entire body throughout the ten directions of the world. Master Dahui said, "If you wish to see Changsha, take another step forward. He continued, "Preserve..."
"Truly not so. Do you wish to see Changsha? Take another step back. After all, how is it? 'Changing the bones and washing the intestines to reorganize;
with eyes all over one's body, one must still investigate. When the Master arrived at Lingyin, he was invited to ascend the hall and said:

'The orthodox lineage of Vulture Peak—those who have attained it are still deluded. Whether light comes or darkness comes, who can discern it? To grasp both and let go both—whom can one distinguish?"'
The very beginning of it: even if a thousand sages were to appear, they would have nothing but their tongues tied.
Why? Because a person becomes noble only when returning to a great state; water is truly clear only upon reaching the Xiao and Xiang rivers. He spoke again:
"Just now, Master Songyuan brought up the story of the bamboo stick to cause Tiantong to suffer defeat. Do you all wish to know? Listen to this verse: Black-lacquered bamboo."
The comb is gripped and raised; a sudden thunderclap leaves no time to cover one's ears. Deshan and Linji stand utterly bewildered; how can those who are dazed and ignorant insert their beaks?

The Master praised himself, saying: "A rustic fellow whom no spoon can lift; not a single speck of literary refinement in his breast.
He once pried the very bones from empty space, and his ill repute has won him fame throughout the rivers and lakes. Later, he passed away and was interred in a stupa at his home mountain.
Chan Master Daomiao Fabao was a native of Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "To call it a bamboo stick is to encounter resistance;
not to call it a bamboo stick is to turn one's back. You must be like a lion that bites a man; do not act like a hound that chases after a clod of earth. A-he-he!"
Whether it be so or not—beneath the feet of Vajrapāṇi lies the Iron Kunlun; he has seized the doltish Baguài of Míngzhōu. Entering the hall:
A thousand words, ten thousand metaphors, all intended only to tell you to return home early. Last night a mass of black clouds arose;
do not let them cause you to lose the path ahead on the mountain. *Duḥ!* (A shout)
Chan Master Tanyi of Yuyuan in Fuzhou had long relied upon Yuanwu, regarding his realization as beyond doubt.

At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, he went forth to reside at Xiangyun in Xinghua, where his Dharma assembly was quite flourishing. When Dahui entered Min, he realized that Tanyi’s insight was not yet definitive and sent him a letter inviting him to come.
Tanyi delayed; Dahui then gave a small-scale sermon (xiaocan) and severely rebuked him, subsequently posting a public notice for the fourfold assembly stating that Tanyi could not... [be admitted].

Having finished his summer retreat, he went to visit him. Dahui interrogated him regarding what he had realized. After a while, Dahui said, "With such a view and understanding as yours, how dare you claim to be the successor of Elder Yuanwu?
The Master withdrew from the monastery to attend upon him personally. One day, during a private interview, Dahui asked, "I want someone who does not understand Chan to become National Teacher.
The Master replied, "I am ready to go and become the National Teacher. Dahui shouted at him and sent him out. He lived there for no [long time].
He asked, "What? and said to him, "Xiangyan’s place of awakening was not at the edge of the struck bamboo;

Hui ascended the seat. He raised [the case]: One day Yunmen held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying: "Ordinary people truly say it exists; those of the Two Vehicles analyze it and say it does not exist;
Pratyekabuddhas call it illusory existence; Bodhisattvas realize its emptiness within its very substance.

Chaozhe said, "I am not like the old man Yunmen, who carves out a hollow in empty space. He then suddenly picked up his staff and said, "This staff does not belong to existence;
it does not belong to non-existence; it does not belong to illusion; it does not belong to emptiness. He struck the ground once with it and said:
Ordinary beings, followers of the two vehicles, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—all turn toward this very place. Each, according to their own capacity, attains its full utility.
Yet, within the domain of the patch-robed monk, it acts as a source of harm and enmity; when one wishes to walk, one cannot walk, and when one wishes to sit, one cannot sit.
Step forward, and you will have your path blocked by this staff. Step back, and you will have your nostrils pierced by this staff.
Is there anyone here now who cannot bear this? Come forth and meet this staff!
If there is none, next year there shall be new branches again; the spring wind’s vexation shall never cease. It is exactly thus.
"How is it when they act together? He descended from his seat. "I trouble Yùquán to bring this out for the sake of the assembly. The Master ascended the seat;

after finishing his expressions of gratitude, he brought up the previous conversation, saying: "Just now, the Abbot’s critique was much like a weary fish stopping in a shallow pond, or a sick bird perching on reeds.
If it were Yùquán, it would not be so. He held up his staff and said: "This staff can—"

There is the ability to exist, the ability to be non-existent, the ability to manifest illusions, and the ability to be empty. There are ordinary people, those of the Two Vehicles, Pratyekabuddhas, and Bodhisattvas.

[The Master] gives a single blow and says: "Right here, everything is shattered into a hundred fragments. Only within the domain of the patch-robed monk is it like a dragon finding water or a tiger relying on a mountain;
when he wishes to walk, he walks; when he wishes to sit, he sits. To take a step forward, heaven and earth tremble; to take a step back, the weeds... [are swept away].
Walking against the wind. Now tell me, how do you express the single phrase "neither advancing nor retreating"? After a long silence, he said:
"Holding a scripture in hand, leaning against a pine tree, he smiles and asks the guest from where they have come."
Chan Master Wuben of Jianfu Temple in Ruzhou was a native of Jiangzhou. He had served under Miaoxi at Yunmen in Jiangxi and subsequently traveled to Xiaoxi in Quannan.
At that time, many men of outstanding talent had gathered there, and those who received his seal of approval were numerous.
The Master felt personally slighted and intended to depart. Miaoxi, knowing this, said to him: "You need only focus your mind on practice."
"Exhaustive! If there were anything to be attained, I would have recognized it even before you opened your mouth.

Later, when he heard that the Master had entered the room for private instruction, he said to him, "Attendant Ben has been practicing Chan for many years, yet day after day he says nothing but 'I do not understand.
The Master rebuked him, saying, "You little devil, even before you were born, I had already visited the Huoshan Temple three times!"

[The Master] withdrew his teeth [in realization]. "I shall let you know," he said. Thereupon, he further sharpened his resolve; taking up the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature, he focused on the word "Mu" (無) to maintain mindfulness.
One night, at the third watch, while leaning against a pillar in the hall and drifting off to sleep, he did not realize that the word "Mu" was escaping from his lips.
Suddenly, he attained sudden enlightenment. Three days later, Miaoxi returned from the prefectural city. The Master hurried to his quarters.
No sooner had his feet crossed the threshold than he had not yet uttered a word when Miaoxi said, "This time, Bare-Faced One, you have finally reached the very top.
Later, after taking up residence, he ascended the hall and said: "To one who bows high to Śākyamuni but does not pay homage to Maitreya, I give thirty blows of the staff. Why?
Because such a person only knows how to climb higher step by step, but does not know how to let go from the void. While the neighbor to the east pulls the plow..."
"To those who drag the rake home, I give thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because they only know how to let go from the void; they do not know how to ascend step by step.
When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, is there any fault in it? Is there anyone among you who can examine this and find it out?
If you can examine it and find it out, we shall walk hand in hand to the southern side of Mount Sumeru. If you can examine it and find it out...
Nothing can be found. An old crow in a cloth bag—though alive, it is as if dead. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Śākyamuni closed his room in Magadha;
Vimalakīrti sealed his mouth in Vaiśālī; Subhūti proclaimed 'no-speech' to manifest the Way;
Śakra and Brahmā ceased their seeing and hearing as they rained down flowers. O Great Assembly! This crew of incompetent fellows has, for no reason, taken the ancestral fields..."
When a private garden is partitioned by contract, each side is demarcated according to its four boundaries—square, round, long, or short—and all is settled at once.
This causes one’s descendants in future generations, even after a thousand years, to have not a single tile to cover their heads above, nor a spot large enough to set a needle upon below.
If Boshan had seen this at that time, he would have dug a bottomless deep pit at the crossroads and called out:
Let us bury this matter once and for all, so as to avoid mutual stagnation and frustration. Why is this? Have you not heard it said: "When the family prospers, filial sons are born;
when the state is hegemonic, there are strategic ministers. [The Master] ascends the hall: "The Gandharva King once performed music, and the mountains, rivers, and the great earth all danced.
But how can they compare to the lame old Yunmen, who could say, 'The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month'?"—Boshan.
Today, where there is no branch to grasp, one must grasp at precedent; it is necessary to respond to this particular occasion.

Suddenly picking up his staff, he rests it horizontally across his knees and makes the gesture of playing the zither, saying: "Is there anyone here who can hear the strings and appreciate the music? After a long silence, he says:
"Even if you were to cry out like a phoenix, who in the end would understand the method of the pointing finger? He struck the meditation seat once and descended from it.
Chan Master Dayuan Zunpao of Yuwang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of Fuzhou. In his youth, he studied the Way alongside Yuquan Yi under Yuanwu.
After several years, he returned to his hometown and assisted Yi at Xiangyun in Pufeng. In the *jiayin* year of the Shaoxing era, Dayuan...

Huìjū was staying at Yangyù. The Master went to visit him. As they entered the room, Huìjū asked about the dialogue concerning whether the Three Holy Ones and Xinghua "came forth" or "did not come forth," and whether they were "persons" or "not persons.
He said, "Tell me, do these two old fellows have a way to manifest themselves, or not?"
The Master struck Hui once on his knee. Hui said, "Was this single punch of yours to vent your anger for Sansheng, or to vent your anger for Xinghua?

Chan Master Nengren Kumu Zuoyuan of Yanshan in Wenzhou was the son of the Lin family of Min.

What was marvelous fifteen years ago Is, as before, just this very thing. Hui presented him with a verse in response:
Releasing the body atop a ten-thousand-fathom cliff—rising up, one remains as alert as ever. Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, there is nothing at all to do;
what need is there to discuss whether one is the person of old or not? In the spring of the Yisi year of the Xiangxing era, [the Master] went forth to reside at Nengren Temple.
He ascended the hall and said: "Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; treading upon a scale-weight, it is as hard as iron. Where there is no Buddha, pass quickly by; beneath one's feet..."
The grass is three feet deep; three thousand miles away, do not err when meeting a person. The Northern Dipper hangs from Mount Sumeru. If it is so, then one does not go.

People of this time must recognize the ground of peace in the snowy courtyard; their nostrils remain pressed against their upper lips.
Raising his whisk, he said: "The Patriarch has arrived! Do you see him? If you can see him, realize it right now. If not, then..."
"The road from here to the Western Heaven is long, over one hundred thousand *li*. A monk asked, "When humans and devas meet, how do you instruct them?

[The Master said: "A sleeping cat beneath a peony flower.
Chan Master Shanzhi Yian of Jiangshan in Jiankang Prefecture was a native of Yunmeng in De'an.

Xuanji said with delight, "I have heard that you people of Anzhou are skilled at wrestling; is this true? The Master then assumed a wrestling stance.

Xiji said, "Who would have known that from within cold ashes, a single grain of bean has burst forth? While at Baoning, he ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas never appeared in the world;

They bow loftily to Śākyamuni and do not prostrate before Maitreya. It is only right to be thus—severing the path of the thousand sages, standing alone."
To traverse the sands of the great trichiliocosm is not considered beyond one's capacity.

If you can realize it at the place where the Buddhas appear in the world, and take up the responsibility at the place where the Patriarch came from the West, you will still be unable to save yourself and will suffer humiliation for a lifetime.
Is there no true man who can take up the task of a true man? Come forth and contend with Baoning! If this is not yet the case, it would be better to simply drag [the matter] away.
"Excellent! He then descended from his seat. One day, while Chancellor Zhuren Jinqing was hosting a tea gathering with various mountain masters, he raised the koan of "The phrase has it;

Finally, the Master said: "Zhang beats oil; Li beats oil. They do not beat the whole body, they only beat the head. Chen [Jinqing] [applauded].

Great Joy. On the occasion of Master Wanshou Zifeng of Jianzhou ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said, 'If a person recognizes their own mind, there is not an inch of land in the great earth.
Wanshou, however, does not say so. If a person recognizes their own mind, that is not yet the ultimate point. And how so?
"The inner is the ultimate place. [The Master] picks up his staff and strikes it once, saying: "The sweet melon is sweet all the way to the stem; the bitter gourd is bitter down to the root.
Chan Master Liaohan Jingyun of Daopei in Tanzhou ascends the hall. "One song from Yunmen: the twentieth day of the twelfth month."
5. Auspicious snow falls from the void, piling up across the mountains and valleys. On the steep ridges, the cold plum blossoms are just beginning to bloom.
Grasping the Mount Sumeru mallet, he laughs as he beats the drum of emptiness. This startles Kātyāyana, who breaks into a cold sweat that pours down like rain.

Before the Peak, I have also previously cited this in error.
When Chan Master Shu'an Liaoyan of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture ascended the hall, he said: "The face-gate is crushed through; heaven and earth are vastly different.
Having smashed through the sturdy barrier, white clouds stretch for ten thousand miles. Even if you were to cut off both ends and take another turn, [it would still not be it]. Three.
"Sixty kalpas have passed, yet it has not even appeared in my dreams. He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
Chan Master Cizhao of Guangxiao Temple in Taizhou ascended the hall and, citing the story of the woman emerging from samādhi, said:
"From of old, beating the drum and playing the lute requires meeting with one who understands; when the jade pendants and phoenix bells have finished their song and dance, [the music ceases]."
The setting sun slants as it did before the gate.
Zen Master Yongwen Chongsheng Puci of Xuefeng in Fuzhou, a native of the Shen family of Hongzhou, addressed the assembly, saying:
A sandalwood grove surrounded by sandalwood; a lion grove surrounded by lions; a tiger-and-wolf grove surrounded by tigers and wolves;
a thornbush grove surrounded by thornbushes. O Great Assembly, among these four kinds of groves, which one would be best for the summer retreat?
If you can understand this clearly, within ninety days, it is guaranteed that each and every one of you will—
One becomes a Buddha and a Patriarch; yet, if this is not so, the groves of Prajñā wither year after year, and the weeds of ignorance grow longer every day.
Chan Master Daoneng of Lianyun in Chuzhou was a native of Hanzhou; his secular surname was He. A monk asked: "Regarding Jingqing’s 'Six Scrapings'..."

“What is the meaning? The Master said, “I have already pierced through your nostrils. The monk asked, “If a student has nostrils, they can be pierced; but if one has no nostrils, what is there to pierce?
The Master said, “To cry out in grievance while clutching the stolen goods. The monk asked, “What is ‘scraping the dust off the fur’?
The Master said, “Yun, Yuan, Qian, Ji—[the monks] with brushes stuck in their hair. The monk asked, “What is ‘scraping the fur off the skin’? The Master said...
[The monk] said, "Shicheng and Qianhua talk and scold one another. The Master said, "How is it 'scraping the skin off the flesh'?
[The monk] said, "Jia, Mei, Guo, and Lang; there is a lawsuit in his breast. The Master said, "Zhang, Quan, Fujian; their heads are as flat as fans.
[The monk] said, "How is it 'scraping the bone from the marrow'? The Master said, "Yanglan and Zuoli; there is no..."
The wind and waves arose. [The student] asked, "What about scraping the marrow? The Master said, "Eighteen, nineteen; the foolish person runs off at night.

[The student] asked, "I have already received your instruction on the six scrapings. As for the meaning of this direct statement, how is it? The Master said, "There is a share for one whose tongue is tied."
Chan Master Zu’an Daoyin of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Hanzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The tiger beneath Mount Daxiong;
the turtle-nosed snake of the Southern Mountain. If you happen to run into them by chance, embrace the prize and return home. But if you do not spare your skillful hands..."
He then pulled out the heavy tooth [of the staff] and asked, "Is there one? Is there one? He ascended the hall and said: "Five times five is twenty-five. The drum of emptiness is shattered;

the great earth cannot admit a needle; throughout the ten directions there is not an inch of soil. What more need be said of spring growth and summer flourishing? The sweet is sweet, and the bitter is bitter.
On the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and cited the story of Master Mazu with Xitang, Baizhang, and Nanquan.
The "Nanquan Plays with the Moon" koan. The Master said: "Master Mazu’s thousand-fathom line is cast with his intent fixed upon the deep pool.
Xitang shakes his mane and Baizhang wags his tail; though they may surge through the waves and stir the billows, they cannot avoid being caught on his hook and line.

Nanquan claimed for himself that he had leaped past the Yu Gate, yet who would have known that he remained, as before, trapped within the great net? Is there anyone here now who can break free from this snare?"
Have you emerged from the cage and broken out of the old mold? You should also come forth and reveal some news, so that it may be known that beneath the Gate of Huazang there is no desolation.
If this is not yet the case, then: "This night the single orb is full; where is its pure light not present?"
The abbot of Zongyuan Hermitage at Zhuyuan in Jianning Prefecture was Master Lian of the same prefecture. Having long relied upon Dahui, he was assigned a seat at Xichan Monastery.
When Chancellor Zhang Gong Jin governed the Three Mountains (Fujian), he invited him to head several monasteries, but he did not accept; instead, he returned to his native village.
He thatched a hut and named it the Garden of Myriad Wonders. Elder monks and lay practitioners came together to request that he open the Dharma for them. Addressing the assembly, he said:
"If you investigate this matter, it is like having lost a key; you simply keep searching and searching until, suddenly, you strike upon it—*Aha!*—and right here you open the lock.
Then you see your own storehouse, and there is nothing among all its provisions that is not fully present."
"There is no need to seek it elsewhere; what other matter is there? He addressed the assembly, saying: "In all quarters, people pull out nails and extract wedges, untie adhesions and remove bonds.
Here, I add more nails and insert more wedges for people; having added more ropes and more bonds, I send them off into a deep pool to wait for them to settle their affairs on their own.
He addressed the assembly again, saying: "A person who presides over the Dharma must have a spirit that swallows the universe."
I am a great Dharma King. Even if Śākyamuni Buddha or the Great Master Bodhidharma were to appear, I would have them join their palms and stand behind me;
it would not even be considered extraordinary that their hair stood on end with cold awe. One day...
Case: When the World-Honored One was born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, saying, "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.
The Master said, "If you do not find it strange when you see what is strange, the strangeness will dissolve of itself. He then offered this turning word: "This very moment."
It is just like encountering a murderer: if you do not kill him, he will kill you.
This was the case with the attendant San-shan, who had long served Da-hui and once silently investigated the "cane" koan without reaching any realization.
One day, after entering the room for instruction, he requested guidance. Huì said, "You are a person from Fuzhou. Let me give you a metaphor:
it is like taking a fine grade of lychee and peeling off the skin and shell all at once, then placing it directly into your mouth with your hand;
yet you do not know how to swallow it. The Master could not help but laugh and said, "Venerable Sir, if I were to swallow it, it would be a disaster!"
Later, Huì asked the Master, "Regarding the lychees you swallowed the other day, it was simply that you did not know their flavor.
The Master said, "If one were to know their flavor, it would only lead to further trouble."
Chan Master Miaodao of Jingju Nunnery in Wenzhou was the daughter of Huang Shangshu of Yanping. On the day she ascended the hall, she said:

"Let the formal questioning cease for a moment. Even if one possessed the eloquence that overturns the ocean and the spiritual mechanism that topples the mountains, not a single point would be of use in the gate of the patch-robed monks.
Furthermore, before the Buddha appeared in the world, there was absolutely nothing at all. Our Patriarch from the West..."
Since its arrival, many establishments have arisen; their pagodas stand in rows like stars scattered across the heavens, continuing down to this day and reaching even to our descendants.
Thus, I, this mountain monk, before this great assembly of humans and devas, stir up waves where there was no wind, transmitting a message through the gate of the second meaning.
That which transcends both speech and silence pervades the vast expanse, yet it cannot be fully expressed through words or explanations.

Pervading all places throughout the *sāhasra-lokadhātu*, his entire body is eyes; confronting the practitioner face-to-face, he moves with the speed of lightning and shooting stars—how can one find a foothold here?

Dahui said, "When a monk asked Zhaozhou, 'Does a dog have Buddha-nature? Zhaozhou replied, 'No. Just look at it like this.
Later, the official attained enlightenment upon seeing a cypress tree, composing a verse that says: Zhaozhou’s Cypress Tree.
How utterly groundless! To pursue it within the realm of objects is too difficult. At every turn, green willows are fit to tether a horse;
at every door, one may pass through to Chang’an.
Layman Wu Weiming, whose courtesy name was Yuanshao, served as a Circuit Intendant for Judicial Review. He had long studied under Chan Master Zhenxie Le and attained self-realization.
He took *samādhi* as his ultimate goal. Later, he visited Dahui at the Yangyu Hermitage. Following the assembly, he entered the room for private instruction.
Dahui brought up the koan regarding the dog having no Buddha-nature to question him. As the Master was about to answer, Dahui struck him with his bamboo staff; the Master was left speechless.

He remained there to seek instruction. One day, Huì said to him, "There is no need to display your cleverness; you must simply 'crack' and 'snap' through it. Only then can you confront birth and death.
If you merely display your cleverness, what end will there ever be? He then took his leave. While traveling along the Yanping River, he suddenly attained realization.
He wrote several verses and sent them to Huì, all concerning the questions he had previously asked in the master's room. Among them was this one: [Verse omitted per instructions]
It is said: "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. His entire body is a single set of golden chain-bones.
Zhaozhou personally saw Old Nanquan, who could say, "In Zhenzhou they produce radishes. Hui spoke a verse to certify this, saying: "His entire body is a single set of golden chain-bones;
he is fit to serve as a model for gods and men. If you wish to recognize Linji’s little page, look right here!"

This was the "white-handed thief" of that year, the layman Huang Yanjie, whose courtesy name was Jiefu and whose style name was Miaode. Under Dahui’s single shout, his state of doubt was suddenly cast off.
Dahui bestowed his robe upon him. Once, while discussing the story of Shoushan’s bamboo cane, they reached the point where [the monk] stepped forward at Ye County.
He snatched it away, snapped it in two, and threw it down the steps, saying, "What is this? Shanshan said, "Blind!
The official said, "When Miaode reaches this point, he is utterly incapable. He then recalled a quatrain he had once composed on wax plum blossoms:
"About to chew the wax upon the branch, The startled fragrance resembles that of orchids. Deep within the snow of the village ahead, Do not mistake them for mountain plums."
Lady Ji Fazhen of the Qin state, having lived as a widow, cast aside all worldly splendor and constantly subsisted on vegetarian food while practicing conditioned dharmas.
Consequently, Dahui sent the Chan practitioner Qian to inquire after her son, Duke Wei. Duke Wei detained Qian, who used the ancestral Way to guide him.
One day, Fazhen asked Qian, "How does the Abbot of Mount Jing usually instruct people? Qian—
He said, "The Master teaches people only to contemplate the kōan of the dog having no Buddha-nature, or the bamboo stick.
It is simply that one must not offer a word, must not engage in deliberation, must not seek understanding at the moment the stick is raised, and must not take it up at the moment the mouth opens.
'Does the dog have Buddha-nature? 'No. He teaches people to contemplate only in this manner. Zhen then attained realization.
Xin sat in meditation that night and diligently investigated the previous conversation. Suddenly, he attained a state of clear penetration without obstruction.

He returned with humble words, and Zhen personally wrote a brief account of his entry into the Way. He composed several verses to present to Huì, the last of which says: "Reading the scriptural texts day by day Is like meeting an old acquaintance.
Do not say there are frequent obstacles; With each recitation, it is renewed."
Chan Master Ying’ang Tanhua of Tiantong in Mingzhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Hujiu Long. He was the son of the Jiang family of Qizhou. From birth, he was extraordinary and outstanding.
At the age of seventeen, he shaved his hair at Dongchan Monastery and first relied upon Chan Master Sui of Shuinan, where he tasted the flavor of the Dharma. Thereupon, he traveled extensively...

He traveled across the rivers and lakes, engaging in spirited debate with various elders, finding accord with all of them. Upon reaching Yunju, he paid his respects to Chan Master Yuanwu, who, at first sight, sternly exhorted and inspired him.
Later, when Yuanwu went to Sichuan, he directed him to visit Zhangjiao. When Zhangjiao moved to Huqiu, the Master attended him there;

within less than half a year, he suddenly attained clear realization of the Great Matter. He then went to visit Cican, who assigned him a seat at Lianyun. Subsequently, he opened a Dharma hall at Miaoyan.
Later, he moved to various great monasteries. During his tenure at Guizong, Da-hui was at Mei-yang.
A monk transmitted to him some of the Master’s instructional verses; upon seeing them, Da-hui praised them with utmost fervor. He later sent a verse to him, saying:

"Severing the path atop the First Peak of the Golden Wheel, A thousand demons and a hundred monsters all hide their traces. In recent years, I have received a true report: It is said that Yangqi’s orthodox lineage continues."
The pulse is unblocked. Such is the weight of his return. Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "Nine years facing the wall ruined the descendants of this eastern land;
the single sandal returning to the West left the Yellow-Faced Old Man at a loss. He drew a line with his staff and said: "A stone ox blocks the ancient road;
one horse gives birth to three tigers. Entering the hall, [he said]: "Old blind shaveling Dechang has never had any flavor. Having picked it up..."
[He] lost his nose. At the second watch and second point of the third watch, he sings a folk song; for no reason, he startles the sleep of the Brahma King.
With a shout, he says: "I walk through the wild weeds; you, again, enter the deep village. Ascending the hall, [he said]:
"The meaning of Linji receiving the staff three times at Huangbo’s place—have you all yet seen through it? Even if you were to take a single bite..."
[If you] cut it off immediately, you are still not a true Great Man (mahāsattva). The Buddhas of the three periods have their mouths hung upon the wall;
with what will the old monks of the world eat? He ascended the hall and said: "Before the fifteenth day, the water rises and the boat floats higher.
After the fifteenth day, the mud increases and the Buddha grows larger. On the very fifteenth day itself, the carp of the Eastern Sea strikes once, and the rain falls."
It was as if a basin were being overturned. The entire great trichiliocosm and all sentient beings within it were filled with joy, saying:
"To strike this one blow is truly timely and appropriate for repaying his kindness.
Unconsciously, their whole bodies leaped with exultation, and they composed a verse to present to the assembly: "A dragonfly may well be a fine dragonfly, Flying here and there, yet never..."
[The monk] had stopped [speaking]. I seized him and plucked off both wings; he was just like a large iron nail. Ascending the hall, he said:
"If you deliberate upon this as a single phrase, who among you does not know how to eat rice gruel?

If you do not deliberate upon it as a single phrase, the worms in the dung pit will laugh you to death. He brandished his staff and said: "The offense of this staff fills the heavens. It shall be banished!"
Facing the two Iron Ring Mountains, tell me: does Jianfu have any fault or not? [He] plants his staff and says: "To be late by even a single moment.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Light does not see darkness; darkness does not see light. When light and darkness are both forgotten, one is no different from a common master.
A jackal howls; a lion roars. A lion roars; a jackal howls. That stinking monkey from the village of three houses."
The price increases tenfold. As for the bright moon pearl beneath the jaw of a black dragon, it is not worth a single coin.
If you act as a patch-robed monk’s core essence, where would you have obtained it? Thirty years from now, even if you change hands and beat your breast, that will not yet be the ultimate suffering.

[Ascending the hall: Beside a grain basket, inside a lacquer bucket—let me spit at you, and I allow you to splash water; let me scold you, and I allow you to jab with your beak. The Yellow River three...
Once in a millennium, the waters are clear; once every five hundred years, the peach of immortality blooms.
Helana clenches his teeth; King Zhu-ding laughs heartily. Guizong has a public case from fifty years ago that he now presents to you all.
But tell me, what kind of public case is it? "Officer Wang has lost his warrant. [He ascends the hall.]

With the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics, from morning until evening, he chattered and prattled, speaking of yellow paths and black ways, unaware of where the two periods of the day lay.
When ascending the hall to eat gruel or rice, he did not notice that he had bitten his tongue;
the blood splashed up to the Brahma Heaven, raining down in abundance beneath the four heavens. The Jade Emperor issued a decree to summon the Dragon King of the Eastern Sea.
"O King! I shall interrogate you at the summit of the Golden Wheel Peak. In a mere instant, I will summon all of you to serve as witnesses.
For now, each of you must testify according to the facts; avoid evasion at all costs. Should you speak falsely, you shall lose your lives.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "Zhaozhou serving tea—I am afraid of him too. If he is not a creditor, then he is an enemy. Leaning against the wall..."
They form a wall in a great throng; who knows who can distinguish the dragon from the snake? Entering the hall:

Regarding the meaning of the five hundred laborers lifting the rock—walking with hands let go atop a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, the world of the ten directions is a single mass of iron, and white fur grows upon the back of empty space.
Even if you were to cast off your greasy cap and strip away your foul-smelling monk’s robe, [you must still stand] before the gate of Baoen.
Just right for being struck with a staff. Why? At midnight, he rose and sat with knees bent; the Morning Star appeared before the patch-robed monk. Entering the hall, [the Master said]:
"The Buddhas of the three periods have no sinews in their eyes; the six generations of patriarchs have no blood beneath their skin.
Mingguo bites down on his teeth and leaps about, yet he cannot escape their circle. Why? Because Nanquan slaughtered the cat."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Those who practice Zen must take care not to apply their minds erroneously. To seek awakening and clarify the seeing of one's nature is to apply the mind erroneously.

To aspire to become a Buddha or a patriarch is to apply the mind erroneously. To study the sutras and expound the teachings is to apply the mind erroneously. Walking, standing, sitting, and reclining are applications of the mind that are erroneous.
Eating gruel and eating rice are applications of the mind that are erroneous. Defecating and urinating are applications of the mind that are erroneous. One...

To move from stillness to activity, or to go and come back and forth—this is a mistaken use of the mind. There is yet another place where the mind is mistakenly applied, which Guizong does not dare to explain through to the end for you all.
Why? "When a single character enters the official gate, even a team of nine oxen cannot pull the cart out. He ascended the hall and said:
"Before a master craftsman has appeared, jade and stone are not distinguished; when a skilled smelter is absent, gold and sand are mixed together. Even if..."
Awakening spontaneously without a teacher—under the gate of Tiantong, it is precisely right to strike three thousand times in the morning and eight hundred times in the evening.
He suddenly grasps his staff and says: "To call this a staff is to fail to distinguish between jade and stone; not to call it a staff is to confuse gold sand with grit.

Among them, perhaps one or two may skillfully discern the underlying principle; take it for granted that they will stride level-footed across the vermilion clouds. Should they, however, remain otherwise...

[The Master] said, "Yes. He leaned on his staff and said, "Quickly, fix your eyes upon it! A monk asked, "When the old woman questioned Yantou, she did not ask about presenting the oar or dancing with the paddle;
rather, tell me, from where did the child in the woman's hand come? Yantou struck the side of the boat three times. What was the meaning of this?
The Master said, "A scorched brick strikes a frozen surface through to the bottom. [The monk] said, "If he had been asked at that time by the Master..."

"Furthermore, how would you respond to him? The Master said, "I would strike him dead with a single blow. [The monk] said, "This old monk is much like someone buying a hat who measures the head first.
The Master said, "Where did you see Yantou? [The monk] said, "Zha! (A note of realization). The Master said, "You fabricated Chan practitioner. [The monk] said, "..."
"Vipaśyin gave birth to seven sons; six did not meet with those who could appreciate their worth. This one alone was not even worth keeping, so he cast him into the water.
[The monk asked: "And how about that? The Master said, "Don't show off too much. [The monk] said, "At that time, Yantou unconsciously stuck out his tongue."
"What do you think? The Master said, "If one finds joy, one shares it. [The student] asked, "A monk asked Yunmen, 'What is the pure Dharma-body?
Yunmen replied, 'Flowers and medicinal herbs in the garden. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Deep-sand demon, bulging eyes. [The student] asked again.
"This is merely burying oneself; this is merely failing the former sages. Setting aside these two paths, at the point where mud and water are blended, please speak, Master.
The Master said, "A jade chopstick propping open a tiger's mouth. [The student] said, "A single word, when spoken, is as weighty as gold and stone;
ten thousand matters, when cast off, are as light as a goose feather. The Master said, "Do not deceive this old monk. [The student] asked, "Everyone fears..."

"Scorching heat! I love the length of summer days. A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. At this moment, how should one act? The Master said, "Cast down the spears and lay aside the armor.
On the anniversary of the death of Huqiu, he held up the incense and said: "Throughout my life I have had no luck, for I have encountered this witless old monk.
I have exhausted every skill and artifice, yet I could never find a way to settle with him. From this day forth, I shall cast off the weapons of war."
He wore his robes and ate his meals according to his means; for twenty years he sat upon a curved wooden chair, hanging up a goat's head while selling dog meat.
What credentials did he have? Nevertheless, on this day when incense is burned once a year, it causes people’s resentment to deepen through the ages.
Because the Master was able to forge and refine even the elderly within his quarters, the world refers to the residence of both Dahui and the Master as "the place where the aged were tempered."

He established two gates to the ambrosia. He once admonished his disciples, saying: "For a monk to don straw sandals and reside in a monastery—is this not more than a mere snake clinging to its burrow?
On the thirteenth day of the sixth month in the first year of the Longxing era, he passed away suddenly. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at his home mountain.
Chan Master Tan of Qingliang in Fuzhou was a successor of Chan Master Yu of Yuyuan. A monk raised the story of Dahui’s bamboo stick for instruction, and the Master showed him with this verse:
“Jingshan has a bamboo stick; Directly beneath it, there is no other principle. The Buddha Hall, the kitchen, and the main gate—”
Passing through the eyes and ears of the patch-robed monks, that monk attained realization upon hearing these words.
Chan Master Shui’an Shi-yi of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an was the son of the Ma family of Wuzhou; he received the tonsure at the age of sixteen.
He first visited Chan Master Xuefeng Huizhao. Zhao raised the koan of “Hiding the body leaves no trace” and questioned him.

It was only after several days that the Master attained clarity. He presented a verse, saying: “The body hidden leaves no trace, yet there is nothing further to hide; The entire being is without reliance, and thus it directly confronts all.
The ancient mirror does not need to be polished back to life; Pale smoke and mist moisten the autumn light. Huizhao tested him, asking: “Ultimately, what is that?”
"The interior is the place where one hides the body without leaving a trace. The Master said, "Ha! Zhao said, "Since there are no traces, why should one not hide the body?
The Master said, "The stone tiger swallows the wooden sheep. Zhao deeply approved of this. Later, while presiding over an assembly, he gave a discourse, citing [the previous exchange].
Master Yuanwu said: "When practicing Chan, practice until there is no more practicing; when practicing until there is no more practicing, you have finally reached the head.
Water Hermit (Shuian) said it is not so: "When practicing Chan, practice until there is no more practicing; when practicing until there is no more practicing, you have not yet reached the head.
If you wish to exhaust the view from a thousand li, you must simply ascend one more story. [He] ascended the hall. The frozen clouds were about to snow, but had not yet snowed.
Samantabhadra’s elephant carriage towers majestically; the mountain plum blossoms are half-closed and half-open, leaking forth the splendor of Shaoshi.
To go on in this manner is still but a partial presentation. What, then, is the matter of the full presentation? Do not speak before those without wisdom.
"I will strike you until your head is shattered and your forehead split open. He ascended the hall and raised the case:
Fayan showed the assembly, saying, "Throughout the entire ten directions of the world, all is bright and radiant. If there is even a single thread of hair, it remains a single thread of hair.
The Master held up his whisk and asked, "Do you see? Piercing through the skull, one still does not awaken. Fadeng said, "Throughout the entire ten directions of the world, it is naturally bright."
"Brilliantly clear! If there were even a single thread [of doubt], it would not be a single thread. The Master said, "The moonlight last night was most excellent;

today the autumn mountains are boundlessly pure. Ascending the hall, he said: "To speak as the ancients did—'Tranquil and unmoving, yet responding and penetrating at once'—is much like scratching before the itch has arisen.
If one were to cause them to step upon the pivot of a monk’s realization..."
"I shall surely find another way of life. With a shout, he struck his *zhuzhang* (staff) and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Wuan Fazhuan of Daochang Monastery in Anji Prefecture was the son of the Chen family of Gusu. Monk Chuan of Dongzhai shaved his head.
For a long time, the Master relied upon Fozhi; whenever he entered the inner chamber for instruction, Fozhi used the "dog has no Buddha-nature" koan.
He questioned him about this, but the Master had no reply. One day, hearing a monk cite the verse of the Fifth Patriarch—“Zhaozhou’s drawn sword”—he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
He composed a verse: “The drums and pipes thunder; he bares one shoulder. Incense billows from the Dragon Tower as the boat of Yizhou sails.

Sometimes he goes barefoot, playing with the bright moon, Treading through the sky beneath the waves of the Five Lakes. After he took up residence [at the monastery], he ascended the hall and said: “If you wish to manifest...”
[He] steps forward. "Do not dwell on favorability or opposition. Holding up his staff, he says:
"The Great Master of the Third Patriarch transforms into a horse-faced yakṣa and goes to Pūrvavideha in the east, Aparagoyānī in the west, Jambudvīpa in the south, and Uttarakuru in the north.
Yet he returns to the hands of this mountain monk. His head and body were originally but a single black-lacquered staff. Do you see it? Even if you were to see it—"
[He] attained it. "Entering hell is like being struck by an arrow. [With this,] he planted his staff and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said:

"All of you here, each and every one of you, stand with your heads reaching heaven and your feet planted on earth; with a *zhuli* staff slung over your shoulders, you travel everywhere on pilgrimage to test and examine the various quarters."
"What more do you seek by coming here? As soon as you give me the slightest pressure, you speak of 'Tiantai’s general assembly' and 'the mountain tour of Nanyue.
Let me ask you: have you ever recovered the precious sword from the kingdom of Daśapura?
He planted his staff in the ground and said, "Be careful not to have a horn stuck in your mouth. A monk asked, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master [replied].
He said, "In the world there are no poor people. When asked, "What is it like after seeing this? the Master replied, "Throughout the four seas there are no wealthy men.

On the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month in the year Jichou of the Qian Dao era, as he was about to enter nirvana, the assembly requested a verse. The Master stared with wide-open eyes and looked down.

When the assembly’s request became even more insistent, he then wrote the two characters "Wu-Wu" (No-No) and cast aside his brush, passing away. After the cremation, relics of five colors were found, which were enshrined in a stupa.
At Jindou Peak, Chan Master Huiseng of Yanfu Hermitage in Quanzhou— originally from Jianning— ascended the hall and, letting out a shout, said:
"The entire world of the ten directions and all the ages of the ten periods of time are, in their entirety, contained within this very place, packed and crammed to the full."

If one were to let go for even the space of a needle’s point, the great ocean would flow westward, the massive mountains would stand overturned, and turtles, crocodiles, fish, dragons, shrimp, crabs, and earthworms would all surge forth as waves upon level ground, swimming and frolicking.
Yet, even though this is so, you must still take another step forward from atop the hundred-foot pole; then, with every step, you will turn over the voidless.
The wheel of the treasury is exhausted; only then does one know that the nostrils rest upon the upper lip and that the eyebrows do not lie beneath the eyes.
Do you understand this thoroughly? Again, he let out a shout and said: "Be most careful not to turn your throat and touch upon a taboo."
