Chan Master Huitong Qingdan of Tanzhou was a successor of Chan Master Daowei Tai and a native of the Yan clan of Pengzhou. Having first left the mountain passes, he arrived at Deshan, where he encountered Master Tai ascending the hall.
Tai quoted Zhaozhou, who said: "The old woman of Mount Tai has already been thoroughly exposed for you. Now tell me—"
"Where does the meaning lie? After a long silence, he said: "Picking up yellow leaves from the ground, entering the mountains to push forth white clouds.
Upon hearing this, the Master was relieved. The next day, he entered the room. Baizhang asked: "In the former case, when Baizhang said 'causes and effects do not fall,' why did he fall as a wild fox?
In the latter case, when Baizhang said 'causes and effects are not obscured,' why was he freed from the wild fox? The Master replied: [The text here ends abruptly].
"I would rather bury them all in one pit. After he took up residence [at the monastery], he ascended the hall and said: "To speak of Buddhas and Patriarchs is like gouging a sore into healthy flesh;
to cite examples from the past and present is like serving leftover gruel and spoiled rice. To attain enlightenment upon hearing it once already falls into the second head;

to act immediately upon being prompted is already a failure to find the proper occasion. You must know that this matter is like the sky covering all universally, or like the earth supporting all universally."
The lion roams alone, seeking no companion; the strong man extends his arm, borrowing no outside strength.
The Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot lift it up; even a monk wishing to see it finds no door. Delusion and enlightenment are both forgotten; the paths of sage and ordinary person are cut off.
But tell me, by what dharma have the sages of old instructed people? He lets out a shout and says: "Do not engage in false imaginings. This is the anniversary of the late Master Foxing.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A three-legged donkey trots on its hooves; step by step they follow one another, yet never meet.

A pair of fish startle from the treetops; brought forth, one is old and one is not. Out of pity for the pines and bamboos, it draws in the pure wind; alas, once one steps out the door, it is all weeds.
Because the patron was called to recognize him, the great capacity and great function were both cast down. [He] burned incense.
Examining and verifying, one sees the root source. Amidst a heap of refuse, one picks up a treasure. The vast monastic communities debate it in vain;
I urge you not to slander the former masters.
Chan Master Zhong’an of Lingyan in Liuzhou became a bhikṣu in his youth. In his prime, he traveled to lecture halls; later, he visited Yuanwu at Jiangshan.

At that time, Foxing was the seat-head (zhuazuo), and when the Master questioned him, he immediately grasped the essential meaning. When Foxing went to reside at De Shan, the Master followed him there.
The Master was sent to Zhongfu Mountain to deliver a letter of succession. Yuanwu asked, "You have traveled a thousand miles to come; you have not disgraced our ancestral tradition.
The public case is already complete—how do you communicate it? The Master replied, "Presented face-to-face, with no further evasion.
Yuanwu said, "This is Deshan’s; which one is yours, Venerable Sir? The Master replied, "How could there be a second person? Yuanwu said, "Behind you—"
"Bottom? Hmm? The Master threw down the letter. Wuxue laughed and said, "A master Chan guest has naturally something to show. The Master replied, "I entrust it to Jiangshan.
Next, he went before the Sangha Hall and, holding the letter, paid his respects to the Head Seat. The Head Seat said, "Xuan Sha’s blank paper."

"From where does this come? The Master said, "I have long kept this essential point hidden; I did not strive to speak of it hastily. Today I present it to you; I hope you will deign to look at it once.
The Head Seat gave a shout. The Master said, "A masterful Head Seat. The Head Seat shouted again. The Master struck him with the letter.
As the Head Seat hesitated, the Master said, "You do not yet understand three, eight, or nine; you cannot help but brood over it yourself. The Master struck him again with the letter.
[The Master] said, "At the time of the encounter, Yuanwu and Fuyan saw it. Yuanwu said, 'I have beaten my Head Seat to death.
Fuyan said, 'It is like two official horses kicking each other; what evidence is there for that? The Master said, 'Why speak of "two official horses kicking each other"?
This is precisely the treading of dragons and elephants. Yuanwu called the Master to him and said, 'I am the head of five hundred people; why did you beat me?'"
Touzi said, "The Master must also have one meal before it is finished. Wuzu looked at Fuyan and stuck out his tongue. Fuyan said, "Not yet.
He then turned to the Master and asked, "Empty-handed, holding a hoe; walking, riding a water buffalo. A person passes over the bridge;
the bridge flows, but the water does not flow. What is the meaning of this? The Master bowed and said, "All that I have submitted is the truth."
Yuanxiao said, "So you are originally a person of this house. He then went to see Master Wuzu Zizheng and presented a letter from his dharma relatives.
The Master asked, "What does the letter say? Yuanxiao replied, "The patterns are already manifest. The Master asked, "Ultimately, what does it say?
Yuanxiao replied, "Brandishing a precious sword in broad daylight. The Master said, "Come closer; here, you do not know even a few characters."
The Master said, "Do not feign defeat. The Patriarch looked at his attendant and asked, "Where did this monk come from? The attendant replied, "This elder once studied under you, Master.
The Patriarch said, "No wonder he is so slippery-headed. The Master said, "He has been left behind by the Master’s dullness.
The Patriarch then held the letter over the incense burner and fumigated it, saying, "Namo Samantabhadra."
The Master stepped forward and merely snapped his fingers; the Patriarch then opened the letter. When he returned to Deshan, Foguo and Foyan both composed verses to see him off.

Before long, the seat at Lingyan was vacant, and monks submitted petitions requesting the Master to take charge as abbot. He accordingly followed the Dharma [of his predecessors]. Entering the hall for formal instruction, he said:
"If one does not investigate the source and root of Chan practice, every encounter will become an obstacle. Therefore, one must maintain..."

Silent and still, pure, tranquil, empty, and at ease—yet you have fallen into a sea of poison. You seek to overcome the strong with weakness, asserting your own rightness while disparaging others, establishing the measure of self versus other.

Your perspective is biased and one-sided, leading to a failure to distinguish between superior and inferior; thus, your illumination fails to engage in actual function, and your function remains trapped within its old nest.

This is not a profound matter of training; it is entirely a matter of worldly convention. Reaching this point, you must know that there is penetration through the midst of killing, and the concealment of the mechanism within the midst of life.
Even the Buddhas cannot know it, and the Patriarchs cannot fathom it. Therefore, the ancients said: "Sometimes there is first illumination and then function;
let me discuss this with you. Sometimes there is first function and then illumination; you must be a man of true caliber."
Only then can you attain it. Sometimes illumination and function occur simultaneously; how will you respond to that? Sometimes illumination and function do not occur simultaneously;
where will you settle and rest? Do you understand? It is like an arrow piercing the willow-branch and a line that startles the world.
"This is not something acquired through temporary study.
Chan Master Zhengfahao of Chengdu Prefecture ascended the hall and, citing the anecdote of Yongjia’s visit to Caoxi, said:
Do you wish to recognize Yongjia? He overturned the seas and mountains to seek a true friend. Do you wish to recognize the Patriarch?

He stirred the heavens and earth to establish a time of great peace. Where have these two elders gone? [He] struck his staff and said: "The patriarchal wind has spread its glorious fame for a thousand ages."
Chan Master Bian of Zhaojue in Chengdu Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth.
A person on the other side of the river sings a *zhègū* lyric, yet mistakenly takes it for the 'Eighteen Taps' of the Hu flute. Do you wish to understand?

If you wish to manifest [the truth] before you, do not harbor notions of compliance or resistance. Who contends over the misty waves of the Five Lakes? Since one has already left, returning is now possible."

Chan Master Jianguang Xingji of Guoqing Monastery in Taizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Huguo Yuan. He was a native of that prefecture and surnamed Yang. His appearance and bearing were exceptionally distinguished.
He was a leader among the Confucian scholars. At the age of twenty-five, he abandoned his wife and children to study the supramundane Dharma.

Later, upon meeting this Hermitage (Cian), he attained a profound realization in secret. He went forth to serve at Mount Wan, where he practiced "sword-plowing and fire-seeding" as a solitary practitioner for seventeen years.

He once composed a verse that says: "The hearth-stove has no fire, the traveler’s bag is empty; The snow falls like willow blossoms as the year draws to its end. I have gathered up some broken hemp..."
Wearing out his patched robes, he was unaware that his own person remained in a state of solitude. He would often say to others, "I am still not yet settled;
how could I take delight in my affairs by dwelling in the mountains? One day, while casually watching a tree being felled as it fell to the ground, he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
The obstruction that had long weighed upon his chest dissolved completely, like ice melting away. Not long after, he received an invitation from Yuan Tong in Jiangzhou, whereupon he said:
"My Way is about to be realized," he said, and with a joyful smile, he took up his staff and departed. Ascending the seat, he preached the Dharma, saying:

"The Perfect Penetration (Yuántōng) does not open a pharmacy for the living; it sells nothing but the heads of dead cats. Who knows which one, free from calculation, will take a bite and have cold sweat flow down their entire body?
Upon ascending the hall, he spoke solely to clarify the self: "To delight in [sensual] objects is the cause of suffering; to pursue the School of the Patriarchs leads to hell."
He remained for a kalpa. He would attend once every five days; on the thirtieth day of the third month, he gave a general discourse, exposing his own family’s disgrace.

Furthermore, if one were to ask about principle or phenomena, or about mind or nature, he was utterly unable to endure it. If one is a man of heroic spirit, they will not peer over the fence to enter, nor will they taste the contents of the cauldron.
Thus, they immediately transform their bodies before the birth of Buddhas and patriarchs, and then walk upon the great official highway of the present age.
Moving with swift strides and wide steps, one ultimately does not enter the rat’s den or dabble head-in-and-head-out in the grassy thickets.

If your fundamental nature is base and inferior, yet you seek to gnaw upon that which has flavor, you will encounter masters of scholastic learning who will constrain and fetter you one after another;
even if you can speak with clouds rising and rain appearing, it is merely a frog transforming into a dragon—yet in the end, you will still be nothing more than a creature eating [its own kind].
"Eating mud and soil—what can it possibly accomplish? Ascending the hall: On the first day of the eighth month, the mid-autumn season, a fresh coolness enters the courtyard and chambers.

Without revealing a single word of essential character, the sorrowful person knows the night is long. Ascending the hall: Only those without a debt of gratitude from the past may study the Chan of Linji.
There is a willingness to accept and affirm, yet it is difficult to continue the Yangqi lineage. When one is impoverished, one is scalded; when one is hungry, one is parched.

The Great Ocean uses only a broken chopstick to stir it; you die and I live. A fierce fire blazes in a cauldron to boil the Buddha’s tongue. Only through such action can one support the gate and prop up the household.
To further speak of "the voice harmonizing with the echo" or "the form being straight so the shadow is upright"—even in a donkey’s lifetime, you would not have dreamed of this. (Monk)
Question: Three Sages asked Xuefeng, "The golden fish that has passed through the net—what do you take for food?
Xuefeng replied, "Wait until it comes out of the net, and then I will tell you. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Same path, different tracks.
[The questioner] said, "Three Sages said, 'A teacher of fifteen hundred people does not even recognize the head of the conversation. Xuefeng said, "I, this old monk, dwell..."
[The student] said, "The matters to be maintained are numerous. Furthermore, how is it? The Master said, "The first arrow was still light;
the second arrow is deep. [The student] said, "As for Xuedou saying, 'A pity he let him go; he should have been given thirty blows,' not even a single blow of this staff could be spared.
Truly, a master of rare encounter—what is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Discussing military treatises when the battle has already been lost. [The student] said, "This staff..."
These three sages should have eaten it; Xuefeng should have eaten it. The Master struck the meditation seat with his whisk and said, "Realize it here!
He addressed the assembly, saying, "As for the staff of a patch-robed monk, if it is not used, that is one thing; but when it is used, it is like a poison-bird falling into the water."
Fish and turtles all die. Holding straight and pulling sideways, the wind whistles as one walks alone upon the Great Way; killing and giving life are within my own grasp. Thus it is said:

"A thousand people pushing against a door are not equal to one person pulling open the bolt. If one person pulls open the bolt, then thousands and tens of thousands can reach the field of peace and bliss.
Do you know? "The embroidered mandarin ducks are finished for you to behold; I do not..."

He handed the golden needle to another person and addressed the assembly, saying: "Contemplating form as emptiness constitutes the perfection of great wisdom; therefore, one does not dwell in birth-and-death.
Contemplating emptiness as form constitutes the perfection of great compassion; therefore, one does not realize nirvana. Thus, one does not dwell in birth-and-death, nor does one realize nirvana."
The land of Han does not contain it; the land of Qin does not govern it. Tell me, where does it establish its dwelling and sustain its life?
Is it that which is luminous within the mind and eyes, yet its form cannot be seen; shining amidst the sensory dust, yet its principle cannot be divided?
Is it that which follows one constantly whether rising or sitting, and dwells together with one whether speaking or remaining silent? If it is thus...
"Ma! This is all nothing but clashing against the skull. You must know that those who transcend measure possess their own transcendent function.
But what is this transcendent function? "The Northern Dipper conceals its body"—though these words exist, few know the news that stands apart from the crowd.
Chan Master Tiyu of Or’an at Mount Jiao in Jiangning Prefecture was the son of the Luo family of Taizhou.

He ascended the hall and, citing the public case of Linji’s “Four Shouts” addressed to the assembly, called out to the congregation: "This public case has been handled by many veteran masters throughout the land;
however, I fear that none have reached perfection. I, Jiaoshan, cannot help but set all four corners firmly upon the ground for you all."
I have clearly annotated this once. What is the lion crouching on the ground? *Tut!* What is the Vajra King’s precious sword?
*Tut!* What is the probing pole and the shadow-grass? *Tut!* What is the single shout that does not function as a single shout?
*Tut!* If you have not yet understood, let this staff reveal it for you, Jiaoshan. (He strikes once and says: "Ha!"
"A knife is inside. He struck the table once and said, "A venomous snake has no eyes. He struck the table once more and said, "I cannot restrain my impatience.
He struck the table once again and said, "The road lies outside the gate. There is yet another pivot: even an elder who raises this story cannot fathom it.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The annual Buddha-bath is held this very day; witnessing [the Buddha] at Kapilavastu, the path is not far. Indeed...
This was once manifested at that time; it is only fitting to pour foul water over one's head. Entering the hall: In the heat of summer one must fan oneself;
when cold comes, one puts on clothes accordingly. If you say the days are passing in vain, it is much like being ignorant of the times. Entering the hall: The Dao gives birth to One.
The hornless iron ox sleeps at Shaoshi; from one comes two. The Patriarch opens the field and expounds the Great Meaning; from two comes three.
Between the rafters, the purple swallows warble their "ninan"; from three come the myriad things. The man’s livelihood lies beyond the nest and the lair.

Add where there is much, subtract where there is little. The tiger fears the raw heart of a living man. As if there were when there is; as if empty when it is real. How can one conceal the black dragon?
“The dragon’s bright moon-jewel—this is indeed so. But as for that one phrase of Jiaoshan which cuts off the tongues of all quarters, how would you say it?
[The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended from it. A monk asked:
"What is 'this very mind is Buddha'? The Master said, "Dingzhou produces fierce and contentious deities.
"What is 'neither mind nor Buddha'? The Master said, "Fujian and Sichuan share the same customs. "What is 'neither mind, nor Buddha, nor thing'?
The Master said, "A bottomless pit is difficult to fill. Question: "What is it like when arising and ceasing do not cease? The Master said, "Thank you for your offering."
Yang asked, "I have a stringless lute that has long resided in the wilderness. It is not that I do not know how to play it; it is simply that I have not yet met one who understands its sound.
Now that I have met such a person, I wonder how one should tune and play it? The Master said, "When the bell is struck, it rings as a bell; when the drum is beaten, it sounds as a drum.
Yang asked, "What is the meaning of Yunmen’s 'three blows of the staff' given to Dongshan? The Master said, "To fall prostrate with the whole body."
Heshen struck him and said, "You rice-bag! If you go off to Jiangxi and Hunan acting like this, what then? The Master replied, "Tears flow from a heart of agony.
Heshen said, "True gold must be forged in a red furnace; white jade requires the hand of a master craftsman to polish it."
The Master said, "To add even a single point would be difficult. In his teaching hall, he frequently held up the handle of a broom and asked his students, "It is vaguely like a broom handle;
it is faintly like a red-spotted snake. None of the assembly could offer a response that accorded with the truth. When a monk requested further instruction, the Master showed him this verse:
"It is vaguely like a broom handle; It is faintly like a red-spotted snake. If you can realize the patience of non-arising beneath the staff," [He would strike.]

Ji did not recognize his father. On the first day of the eighth month of the Jihai year of the Chunxi era (1179), he manifested a slight illness. He took up the brush to bid farewell to the Prefectural Governor, Mr.
Zeng. By midnight, he wrote a verse to take leave of the assembly, saying: "The iron tree blooms; the rooster lays an egg. Seventy-two years have passed; the cradle rope has snapped.
Having cast down his brush, he demonstrated his entry into nirvana.
Chan Master Zhantang Zhishen of Huazang in Changzhou was a native of Wulin. On the anniversary of the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa, he ascended the hall and said:
"Descending from Tuṣita Heaven and manifesting extinction at the Twin Śāla Trees—digging up the earth to seek the heavens, nailing a wedge into empty space. For forty-nine years..."
Stirring up dust and scattering soil across more than three hundred assemblies, he exhausted every flaw and flawlessly deployed his nets and snares;
yet he could not avoid calling a tortoise a turtle. Finally, by the side of the city of Kuśinagara, he displayed his double-soled sandals within the coffin.

To an onlooker with cold eyes, this appears much like a case of overreaching skill resulting in clumsiness. (He strikes the meditation staff and says: "If it were not for this principle, how could [the truth] be known ten thousand generations hence?"
"Who is it that speaks with their mouth? Tell me, what principle is this? One must strictly avoid leaking [the truth] before a fool.

The lay practitioner Qian Duolì, Governor of the Political Council, whose courtesy name was Chùhé and style name Sōngchuāng, attained enlightenment regarding his own fundamental matter at this hermitage.

Later, he reached the ultimate depths regarding every point of the essential purport of the Chan school. In the winter of the *bingshen* year of the Chūnxí era, Jiàntáng returned to reside at Píngtián, and [Zhìyǎn] subsequently began to correspond with him.
In the autumn of the *dingyou* year, Zhìyǎn fell slightly ill; he wrote a letter summoning Jiàntáng and the abbots of Guōqīng and Ruìyán, expressing words of parting.
When Jiàntáng and two other *chán* masters arrived at his bedside, the Master rose and sat in the full lotus posture, conversing and laughing as the time passed.
At that time, he immediately wrote: "The floating world is illusory; fundamentally, there is no coming or going. The four elements and five aggregates must ultimately reach their end.
Even Buddhas and Patriarchs, though endowed with great majestic power, cannot escape this one point.
Among all the old monks of the world and all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), is there anyone who can leap over it? It is simply because of earth, water, fire, and wind."
Through the convergence of conditions, things meet for a brief moment; do not mistakenly take them to be your own. A great man is磊磊落落 (liǚ liǚ luò luò)—vast, open, and unencumbered.
When it is time to act, he holds fast; wherever he stands, all is true. Like a sail driven by the wind, he may go with or against the current as he pleases.
Because of this vegetarian feast, he celebrates and praises; whether going or staying, he is free and at ease. This is the single path of Great Liberation opened by the sages of the past.
The Gate of Liberation. It is the realm of primordial purity, emptiness, and stillness; it is the Great Way of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*). Now that I am thus, how joyful I am!
The external conditions of worldly toil have been swept away all at once. I am grateful for the grace of the various mountains who have looked upon me, and I pray that you will all bear witness.
I humbly entreat you to take care of yourselves. Setting down his brush, he looked at Jiǎntáng and asked, "Is it better for me to go sitting or to go lying down? Jiǎntáng said:

"Minister, you may go now; what need is there to concern yourself with whether I am sitting or lying down? The official smiled and said, "Dharma brother, you should cherish yourself for the sake of the ancestral path.
Thereupon, he closed his eyes and passed away.

Chan Master Qi-ji of Chuan-an on East Mountain in Qingyuan Prefecture, a dharma successor of Chan Master Yuan of Lingyin, was the son of the Xie family from Qiong Prefecture. He ascended the hall and spoke, citing a verse by Master Xiu:
"The pillar does not see the pillar; The non-pillar does not see the pillar. When 'is' and 'is not' have both departed, Is..."
Do not grasp at the mat. He called to the great assembly, saying: "If you can grasp it, then 'the flower moves along with the butterfly.
If you cannot grasp it, then 'carrying the spring water, one returns with the moon. To say 'this is good'—Zhengzhou pears surpass Qingzhou dates.
To say 'this is not good'—the Elephant Path leads into Penglai Island. Even 'this' has no connection; treading upon the scale-weight, hard as iron—even 'that' has no connection."
He steps forward. A vajra-jewel sword cuts him across the head. "A-he-he! Do you understand? When one knows little, there is little affliction;
when one knows many people, there is much contention. A fellow practitioner from the Lotus Society requests that I ascend the hall.

Gradually the skin becomes like chicken-skin and the hair like crane-feathers; the father is young while the son is old. Look at how his gait has become unsteady—this will surely cause Master Muzhou to be filled with doubt. Even if...
"Jade and gold fill the hall. Take care of the thief who steals in broad daylight. How can one avoid decay, old age, sickness, and death?
It is precisely here that you must exert your utmost brilliance. "Let you have a thousand kinds of joy; he shall surely be free. Impermanence will inevitably arrive.
Return to the hall for tea. There is only the direct path of cultivation. As before, they go around beating the drum. Simply recite the name of Amitābha Buddha. Recite!
This will not suffice to save you. He spoke again: "Alas! This path of life has already been pointed out directly by the Venerable Shandao.
You all travel back and forth along this very road morning and evening; why then do you pass Amitābha Buddha right before your eyes?
If you can realize it here and now, you may immediately cast off the barrier of delusion and pull out the arrow of hesitation."
Cut through the net of doubt; sever the river of ignorance and craving; fell the dense forest of the mind; wash away the turbidity of mental defilements;

straighten the mind’s deviousness; and cut off the mind’s cycle of birth and death. Only then may you turn toward that other shore. Lift up your feet and take one step further into the place where Buddhas and patriarchs have never trodden.
Open your mouth and utter a single word in the place where Buddhas and patriarchs cannot reach with their explanations. Call them back!
Master Shandao: To seek a separate path for practice is like abandoning one’s father and fleeing;
wandering through foreign lands, bumping into this and that—how bitter! Amitābha Buddha!
Chan Master Guiyun Ruyouben of Shushan in Fuzhou was a native of Taicheng. He ascended the hall and said: "The long rains have not ceased;
the *wu* stem is in the *bing* and *ding* positions. My whole body is covered in mud and water, yet my eyes are revealed. Tell me, what kind of eyes are these? He struck his staff and said:
"In the forest, the mud-slipper bird cries out two or three times."
The Venerable Master Gaku’a was a descendant of the Fujiwara clan of Japan. At fourteen, he received the tonsure and the full precepts;

he studied both the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna teachings and gained a reputation for his learning. At twenty-nine, a merchant returning from the Central Kingdom spoke of the flourishing state of the Chan school.
Gaku’a was stirred by this and, accompanied by his Dharma brother Kinkei, set sail across the ocean. Carrying incense in his sleeve, he paid homage to Chan Master Fuhai of Lingyin. Fuhai—
When asked about his origins, Ache wrote down his response. He further wrote: "In my country there is no Chan school; we only lecture upon the sutras and śāstras of the five schools.
Our sovereign has no family name or surname and is titled the Golden Wheel King (Cakravartin). He changed the reign era to Jiaying and subsequently abdicated the throne to enter the monastic life."
His name was Xingzhen. He was forty-four years old, and the Prince was seven; he was ordered to receive the throne, and it has now been five years.

Regarding the ordination of monks, there have been no further contributions, yet those whose exegesis of the teachings is eminent are granted rewards. We, [the undersigned], look up to and revere the fame of the Venerable Master Cien of the Sagely Court.
We have come specifically to the chamber to pay our respects, wishing to receive the seal of the mind so as to ferry those lost across the ford. Furthermore, as for the mind and the Buddha—
"And sentient beings—these three are without distinction. They are free from marks and free from words; they are manifested through provisional speech.
The Zen Master asked, "How would you instruct them? Hai replied, "Sentient beings have deluded perceptions; they see Buddhas and they see worlds.

Ao asked, "From what cause does ignorance arise? Hai struck him. Ao then requested that Hai ascend the seat to resolve his doubts. In the autumn of the following year, he took his leave to travel to Jin.

Ling arrived at the riverbank of Changlu. Upon hearing the sound of a drum, he suddenly attained great enlightenment; for the first time, he understood the intent behind the Buddha’s reaching down with his hand.
He returned to Lingyin and composed five verses to describe what he had realized, then took leave of Hai and returned east. The verses say:

I sailed across the sea to seek the transmission outside the teachings, Seeking to leave behind all views and knowledge, to cast off the trap and the snare. Having traveled everywhere, my straw sandals are worn through; The water remains in the clear, still pool.
The moon is in the sky (I). Sweeping away all entanglements and intellectual views, whatever is grasped by the hand is the total manifestation of reality.
The radiant circle behind the head penetrates the great void; a thousand mechanisms and ten thousand functions turn all at once (II). How can this wondrous state be explained to others?
Falling to the ground, one rises immediately; it is self-evident. Suddenly, one treads upon one’s own original ground. With the head-wrap tucked back, one walks alone upon the solitary path.
(Verse Three) Seeking the true to extinguish the false is not at all subtle; taking the false as the true to clarify the real is entirely an error.

How laughable is that ancient master of Mount Lingyan, who cast down his broken wooden ladle right before our eyes! (Verse Four) Raising a fist and letting out a shout is but a slight display of skill. To speak of this...
It is said that he did not enter the mud and water; cutting off a thousand differences, he ceased all pointing and directing. With a single sound, he returned to "Di-luo-luo-li" (5).

Gensha praised him highly and presented this verse as a parting gift. When he returned to his own country and resided at Enzan-ji, the letter conveying the transmission of the Dharma arrived, but Gensha had already entered into nirvana.
The Gentleman-in-Attendance (Neihan) Zen Master Kai, whose courtesy name was Tianyou, had long studied under Yuanwu and had been visiting Dahui’s gate for many days.
In the Xunwei year of the Shaoxing era, Fohai was appointed to Guangxiao Temple in Quzhou;
the Master and the Gentleman Zhao Chaoran went to visit him and asked, "What is a true spiritual friend? Fohai replied, "The lanterns, the pillars, and the cat."
“Dog! The Official said, “Why is it that praise brings joy and disparagement brings affliction? Hai replied, “Minister, have you ever seen a true teacher (kalyāṇamitra)?
The Official said, “I have been seeking instruction for thirty years; why do you say I have not seen one? Hai said, “Go see him where there is joy;
go see him where there is affliction. As the Official hesitated, Hai let out a thunderous shout and gave a blow. The Official was about to respond when Hai—
He said, "The one who opens his mouth is not [the true one]. Gong was bewildered. Hai called out, "Where did you go, Minister? Gong suddenly attained realization and nodded his head.
He then spoke a verse: "Alas, the blind donkey! A pestilence to the monastic groves. With a single roar that shakes the earth, the celestial mechanism has been leaked.
If someone asks further what the meaning is, I will lift my whisk and strike them right across the mouth. — Hai.
[The Master] said: "I have only attained one peg.

The Prefect Ge Tan, a lay practitioner whose courtesy name was Qianwen and whose style name was Xinzhai, had achieved high honors in the imperial examinations in his youth; he devoted himself to the joy of Chan meditation.
He first visited Chan Master Wuan Quan to seek guidance. Wuan instructed him to investigate the saying, "The very mind is Buddha. After a long time, he had no realization.
He requested, "Master, what expedient means can you provide so that I may gain entry? Wuan replied, "Layman, you are simply too insatiable."
Shortly thereafter, Fohai came to reside at Jianchi. The Master followed him there and brought up the words shown by Wuan, requesting that he preach them for the assembly.
Fohai expounded upon them, saying: "Mind is Buddha, eyebrows trailing the ground; Non-mind is non-Buddha, two eyes staring wide.
In the dream of the butterfly, home is ten thousand li away; On the branch of the cuckoo, the moon is already at the third watch. He remained for ten days.
He returned the following day. One day, [Wumen] raised the phrase: "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. Suddenly, he attained clear and thorough enlightenment.
He composed a verse, saying: "Not mind, not Buddha, nor yet a thing; Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, the mountain looms high.

In the midst of the brilliant sun, he turns his body upside down; The wild fox leaps into the golden-haired lion’s den. Wu’an approved this, immediately sent a letter with the verse to present to the Buddha (Foguo Yuanwu).
Zhaojue Hai said, "This matter cannot be fully expressed by paper or brush. Layman, if you can pass me, you shall hear something.
He then went back to Huqiu. Zhaojue Hai met him and said, "Your understanding, Layman, is sufficient only to enter the realm of the Buddhas."
He had not yet entered the realm of Māra. The Master (Gong) continued his courtesies without ceasing.

Guishan Haiyun maintained a solemn countenance and said, "Why do you not say that the golden-haired lion leaps into the den of the wild fox? Thereupon, the Master realized it deeply. He once asked various Chan masters:
"If a husband and wife are fighting and their son acts as witness, tell me: does he bear witness for the father, or does he bear witness for the mother? Oran [responded]: "It is both."

The Chan Master added a comment, saying: "A small emergence meets with a great encounter. In the sixth year of the Chunxi era, while serving as the governor of Linchuan, he contracted an illness in the eighth year.
One night, he suddenly asked for a brush and wrote this verse: "Beating the drum within the vast ocean; Hearing the bell atop Mount Sumeru."
The karmic mirror suddenly shattered; turning his body, he emerged into the void. He summoned his subordinates and showed them [the mirror], saying:
"Life and death are like day and night; there is nothing strange about this. If one speaks in terms of the Way, how could there be birth or death?
To interpret it in terms of birth and death is to be far removed from the Way. Having finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away.

Chan Master Biepeong Baoyin of Mount Jing in Lin’an was a successor of Chan Master Huazang Min. He was a native of the Li clan of Jiazhou. From childhood, he was well-versed in the Six Classics but grew weary of worldly affairs;
he subsequently received the tonsure and full ordination under Chingsu of Deshan. Later, he studied the Avataṃsaka Sūtra and the Awakening of Faith.
Xin, having exhausted his explanations, abandoned his reliance on Mimi Yin at Zhongfeng. One day, Yin raised a case:

A monk asked Yantou, "What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? Yantou shouted, "Who is it that arises and ceases? The Master attained awakening upon hearing this and immediately nodded in affirmation.
When Yuanwu returned to Zhaojue, Zhimen Yin sent the Master to visit him. Consequently, he entered the room with the assembly.
Yuanwu asked, "How did the sages of antiquity receive people? The Master held up his fist. Yuanwu said, "That is what I, this old monk, use.
What is it that the sages of antiquity use? The Master struck him with his fist. Yuanwu also raised his fist and crossed them, laughing heartily.
He stopped there. Later, he went to Mount Jing to visit Dahui. Dahui asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From West Sichuan.
Dahui said, "Before you even left Jianmen Pass, I would have given you thirty blows of the staff! The Master replied, "It was not fitting for me to trouble the Master by coming here."
Huì was delighted and swept his quarters to invite him in. Huì moved southward, and the Master then returned west. He presided over several monasteries in succession;
later, he crossed the gorges again and resided at Baoning, Jinnshan, Xuedou, and Jing Mountain. Upon ascending the seat for the opening of the hall, he said:
"When the World-Honored One first attained perfect enlightenment in the Deer Park, he turned the Dharma wheel of the Four Noble Truths, and the bhikṣu Kauṇḍinya was the first to realize it."
Regarding the Way: Later, when Chan Master Zhenjing first took up residence at Dongshan, he remarked, "Today, within the cave of Xin’feng, I shall merely turn this staff.
He then held up his staff, placed it to his left side, and asked, "Is there anyone here who attained enlightenment from the very beginning?
If not, a man of spirit naturally possesses the will to soar to the heavens; do not walk where the Tathāgata has already trodden. He then let out a shout.
"Ha! Descend from your seat. If it were Master Yin, he would not have spoken thus.
Today, within this Phoenix Mountain, there is no leisure to turn the wheel of the Four Noble Truths, nor is there the strength to turn this staff.
I only instruct all of you to walk with slow steps and speak in low voices. Why? If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata.
The Turning of the True Dharma Wheel. Ascending the hall: The Buddhas of the three periods of time expound hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of phrases from a single phrase;
yet they gather those hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of phrases back into that single phrase. Under the gate of the Patriarchs, there is not even half a phrase.

It is just like this—how many painful blows of the staff should one receive? O worthy ones, as for whether the Buddhas are [the truth] or the Patriarchs are [the truth]: if you say the Buddhas are the Patriarchs...
It is not so. To say "the Patriarch is the Buddha" or "the Patriarch is not the Buddha" is to fail to forget grasping and rejecting.

If you say that Buddhas and Patriarchs are simultaneously right and simultaneously wrong, you are being far too crude. Furthermore, how would you express the single phrase that cuts off this entanglement?
A tiger wearing a paper hat—amusing, yet startling. Again, it is said: A monk asked Yantou, "In the midst of the vast and turbulent dust, [how does one...]"
"What distinguishes the master? Yanhou replied, "A copper gong filled with oil. The Master said, "Yanhou, great as he was, has lost his nostrils.

Suddenly, someone asked Baoning, "In the midst of vast dust and confusion, how does one distinguish the master? He answered him: [The Master said: "If someone asks you this, simply answer them: 'The copper gong is filled with oil.'"
The weather was so cold that he did not even have time to remove his hat before ascending the hall. On the first day of the sixth month, the sun scorched the void;

at the crossroads, the snow was a foot deep. There was no leisure for sweeping, nor could one avoid it; it froze the beard of Old Liao from the eastern village until, in the dead of night, he stood upon the water wearing boots.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "If you try to use the mind to eliminate delusion, delusion is difficult to eliminate; realize the mind within delusion, and the Way is revealed."

He turned away from the circuitous path; having kicked through the bottom of the bucket, he was free from all inhibition. At every casual step, there was a lotus flower. When the Master arrived at Mount Jing, he stayed for a full year.

Emperor Xiaozong summoned him to have an audience in Xuande Hall, where his words met with imperial approval. Upon entering the presence of the Emperor, the latter granted him a palanquin within the Donghua Gate.
In the second month of the tenth year, the Emperor annotated the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* (Yuanjue jing) and dispatched a messenger to deliver it to him, ordering him to compose a preface.

The Master was advanced in years and grew increasingly weary of serving as abbot. In the winter of the fifteenth year, he submitted a memorial requesting permission to dwell in a hermitage, and his request was granted.
In the eleventh month of the first year of the Shaohsi era, he went to visit the incoming abbot, Chan Master Zhice, to bid him farewell. Zhice asked him the date of his departure.

The Master said, "When the water arrives, the channel will be completed. He returned home and requested paper to write the nine characters: "On the night of the seventh day of the twelfth month, at the hour of the cock's crow. As scheduled, he passed away.
His physical remains were escorted back to the Dharma Hall of the monastery and remained there for seven days; his complexion remained bright and lustrous.
His hair grew long and his head remained warm. Seven days later, he was buried on the western ridge of the hermitage. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Ciben, and his stupa was named Zhiguang.
He was a dharma successor of Chan Master Zhaojue Yuan.

Master Fengxi Huiquan ascended the hall and said: "The fallen leaves are exhausted in the village ahead; the cassia flowers have withered in the deep courtyard. This is the beginning of winter tonight;
from now on, it will grow particularly cold. Therefore it is said: 'If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season.
When the time and season arrive, the principle reveals itself naturally. He gave a shout and said, "Speaking in such a manner, one becomes a true person."
Few [attain success]; those who ruin themselves are many.

Chan Master Daowen of Wenshu was a dharma successor of Chan Master Huifang of Chu'an in Tanzhou. He was the son of the Xu family of that prefecture. He went to Mount Dabi to attend upon Chan Master Daowen.
Before long, the temple was converted into a Shenxiao Palace. While traveling south along the Xiang River on a merchant vessel, he heard a person on the bank speaking his native dialect.
The man called out in a sharp voice, "Jiaona! At this, he attained realization and immediately spoke a verse:
"A single cry from the heart of the river at Mian— Only now do I realize my lifelong purpose. After many years of parting, we meet again; All sages return to the same source."

Travelling along the way, he arrived at his residence and ascended the hall to address the assembly. "Only now, in my old age, do I assume the title of Abbot; I possess not the slightest bit of mysterious mechanism.
When I open my mouth, nine out of ten words are perverse. To ask about the East, I answer with the West. To transcend the world in such a manner—what profound mystery could there be?
At times I set aside three and let go of two; at times I act according to the established command. Even so, only those of the same path will understand. And so it was.
"How is it with that matter which the Way knows? You must strike through the nostrils before you will succeed. Ascending the hall, he said: "The Patriarch Bodhidharma is beneath one's feet;
if you cannot tread upon him, you cannot lift him up. Look closely at what is right before you and let it go.
Where did the illness lie in those days? Zhang was skilled at diagnosing the pulse; Li was skilled at administering medicine. The two of them vied with one another to heal him."
At one time, it was not used; the medicines did not harmonize. A mistake, a mistake! "Go drink tea.
Master Wenshu Siye of Changde Prefecture was a butcher in his former life. One day, while slaughtering a pig, he suddenly attained profound penetration into the source of the mind.
He immediately abandoned his trade and became a bhikṣu, composing a verse that said: "Yesterday, the mind of a yakṣa; today, the mind of a Bodhisattva."
The Master’s face. The Bodhisattva and the yakṣa were not separated by even a single thread.

When he went to see Mañjuśrī, Mañjuśrī said, "What did you see when you were in the midst of slaughtering a pig that you shaved your head and set out on foot? The Master then made the gesture of brandishing a butcher's knife.
Mañjuśrī shouted, "This butcher, go to the hall! The Master then descended and went to the hall. While residing at Wenshu, he ascended the hall and raised [the following] for discussion:

Regarding the story of Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman, it is said: "The old woman was thoroughly exposed; her face turned green and her eyes blackened. This old fellow Zhaozhou could not deceive me.
He was a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Heshan Xun.
Chan Master Liaoyun of Chouyan in Yiwu, Wuzhou, ascended the hall and presented the koan of Zhaozhou’s “The dog has no Buddha-nature.
He then said: “Zhaozhou says, ‘The dog has no Buddha-nature. Ten thousand layers of green mountains conceal an ancient mirror;
A barefoot Persian enters the Great Tang; Eight-armed Nezha executes the true command. *Du!*”
The lay practitioner Pan Lianggui, whose courtesy name was Yirong, was forty years of age when he turned his mind toward the ancestral gate.
Wherever he went, he hung up his alms bowl and joined the assembly to inquire into the Way. Later, he relied upon Fodeng; after a long time, however, they did not reach accord.

He therefore complained, saying, "I simply wish to know: what is it like at the moment of death? Fodeng replied, "What a fine wrapping! Keep it for future use. At present, this matter remains unresolved.
Later, when he went there, the other had suddenly replaced the envelope, leaving him with no way to rectify the situation.

The Master again asked about the story of Nanquan killing the cat, saying, "I have contemplated this for a very long time, yet I have never fully penetrated it. I pray that the Venerable One will show me compassion."
Deng said, "You only manage to understand the cats of others' houses; you do not realize that you have lost your own dog.

At these words, Gong was as if awakened from a drunken stupor. Deng spoke again, saying, "Not easy. Once you have taken this step forward, you must further know that there is a matter beyond this before you have attained it.
Nowadays, when scholar-officials speak of Chan or speak of the Way, they merely rely upon intellectual principles."
"He is simply happy. For the most part, it is like buying oil-cakes with money; once eaten, one is no longer hungry.
To say anything else would be to deceive him, which is also quite laughable. Gong replied, "Yes, yes."

Chan Master Shouyuan of Shu'an, known as Wuwai of Hanzhou, was a successor of Chan Master Ming of Letan. He was a native of that same prefecture and belonged to the Shi clan. At the age of thirteen, he suffered from blindness in his eyes;
consequently, he went to rely upon Chan Master Neng, Huimudian, of Qixian Temple. After receiving full ordination, he crossed the gorges and traveled to Baofeng, where he encountered Master Baofeng.
The Master ascended the hall and raised up Yongjia’s verse: “The single moon universally appears in all waters;

all the moons in the waters are subsumed within the single moon. Upon hearing this, the Master attained a clear and complete realization. Later, when he was presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and said: “To unify the myriad through the one:

the single moon universally appears in all waters. To bring the myriad back to the one: all the moons in the waters are subsumed within the single moon. When expanded, it encompasses the entire Dharma-realm; when withdrawn...”
Not even a hair’s breadth remains. Although the ways of gathering and unfolding differ, this matter fundamentally has no diverse meanings.
Only when you can fix a single eye upon the root source will you see that all Buddhas of the three periods and the ancestral masters of successive generations have all manifested from within this;
and that the Tripitaka, the twelve divisions of scripture, and all the sutras have all flowed forth from within this.
Heaven and earth, the sun and moon, and the myriad phenomena of the universe are all established from within this.
The three realms and nine stages, the seven destinies and four modes of birth, all emerge from and dissolve back into this.

The hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates and immeasurable subtle meanings—even the various worldly crafts and arts—all manifest and function through this. Therefore, when the World-Honored One held up the flower, Kāśyapa immediately [smiled].
The Buddha smiled; Bodhidharma faced the wall. Thereupon, the Second Patriarch found peace of mind. When the peach blossoms were in full bloom, Lingyun’s doubts were completely purified.
When the bamboo struck and made a sound, Xiangyan suddenly forgot all that he knew. This extends to Panshan awakening to the Way at a meat counter, and Maitreya meeting people in a fish market.
Truly, it can be said that even in moments of haste or distress, one must always abide in this. Thus says the Sutra.
Walking, sitting, and reclining are all contained within it. Since it possesses such wonders, it further possesses such radiance;
since it possesses such vastness, it furthermore possesses such omnipresence. Why, then, do you people still have delusion and enlightenment?
Do you wish to know? "Fortunately, there is no place of partial illumination; yet, there is still a time of non-illumination."
Chan Master Wuan Desheng of Yunju in Nankang Commandery was a dharma heir of Chan Master Longxiang Gui. He was the son of the He family of Hanzhou. At the age of twenty, he received full ordination;

after studying the exegesis of the scriptures for a long time, he abandoned that path to visit Chan Master Wenshu Dao, seeking the essential points of the Buddha-dharma. Wenshu showed him this verse: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
The Khitans broke the Persian camp and seized a precious pearl, which was sold in the village.
A poor beggar at the crossroads had it hanging from his waist as a mark of elegance. As the Master was about to respond, Shu said, "Do not err. The Master withdrew to reflect for three years.
Only then did he grasp the essential meaning and go to see the Buddha-nature, but his faculties were not in accord. He traveled to Min Province and went to Drum Mountain (Gushan) to pay his respects.
He immediately asked, "Regarding the National Teacher’s statement, 'I do not step over the stone gate'—what is its intended meaning? Zhuan’an responded with a shout, saying, "Idle words."
The Master immediately attained realization. After he had taken up residence [as abbot], a monk asked: "I do not ask about the True Man who does not rely on the three realms and transcends them;
what is the True Man of No-Rank? The Master said: "Rich and noble when heard of; poor and destitute when seen. The monk said:
"Lifting the head requires covering the ears; tilting the palm, one turns the body over. The Master said: "Where is the True Man of No-Rank? The monk said: "Old man!"
The Master said, "I do not even recognize your *huatou* (critical phrase). The Master added, "I grant you thirty blows.
Chan Master Lu’o’an Huìwēn of Lángshān in Tōngzhōu was a native of Fúzhōu; his secular surname was Zhèng. He traveled extensively to study under various masters.
In his later years, he relied upon Zhuan’an at Donglin. Not long after, Zhuan’an retired from his duties.
The Master then visited Gao’an Wu, Nanhua Bing, and Caotang Qing; all of them recognized his potential. When Zhuan’an moved to Qianyuan in Min, the Master returned home to visit him.

Zhuan’an asked: "When emotion arises, wisdom is obstructed; when conceptualization changes, the essence becomes distinct. Without lingering in the prison of the intellect, bring me a single phrase of the Way."
The Master was then relieved and composed a verse, saying: "Having been squeezed until my whole body has become a mouth, what prevents me from scolding the rain and rebuking the wind?

Last night, a fierce tiger in the village ahead bit to death a great beast of the South Mountain. The head of the hermitage nodded in approval. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and said:
"Śākyamuni Buddha spent forty-nine years planning behind the curtain; Maitreya Bodhisattva has carried water for ninety-one kalpas."
Dragging through the mud: ordinary sentiments and sagely measures cannot be eradicated; intellectual illumination and conscious awareness still remain as mere proclamations.
To take the Buddha’s intent and the Patriarchs’ intent as being like using fish eyes for bright pearls, or to mistake orange peel for a fierce fire—such is the state of the Great and Small Vehicles.
All you people must open wide the treasure-trove of your own breast and bring forth the precious jewels of your own house to bestow universally upon the poor at the crossroads.

If, among the crowd, there should suddenly emerge a person of keen intelligence who says, "Fine food does not satisfy one already full," I would simply say to him: "Yuzhou may still be tolerable; most painful is Silla."

Chan Master Shuanglin De-yong of Wuzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Yunju Wu, was the son of the Dai family of that same prefecture. He ascended the hall; taking up his mallet and raising his whisk, he said:

"Under the gate of the Patriarchs, they used yellow leaves to stop a child's crying; to speak of the wondrous and discuss the profound is like looking for plums at a plum grove before the eyes of a patch-robed monk."
Thus one quenches thirst. Today, Ji Shan has cast it all away—this "it," "that," and "so-and-so.

No longer pointing east or sketching west, he pours out his heart from within the life-vein of the Buddhas of the three periods and from the very marrow of the six generations of patriarchs, speaking it through for you all.
After a long silence, he said: "To cry until the blood flows is of no use; It is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring."

Chan Master Daoxian Wuzhuo of Wannian in Taizhou was the son of the Hong family of that same prefecture. He ascended the hall and said: "To meet the challenge with one’s full capacity is still to be halfway there;
'cracking and pecking at the same moment' leaves ten thousand miles of white clouds behind. As soon as a trace of manifestation arises, one has already fallen into the second or third rank.
Not revealing even a glint of one's edge—what kind of principle would that constitute? Tell me, how should the matter of the ancestors from of old be handled? [He then] shouted.
"The fault of man: to impose punishment upon him for his crime. [The Master] ascends the hall and cites Qianfeng’s instruction to the assembly:

"If you raise one, you must not raise two; to let one point pass is to fall into the second. Yunmen stepped forth from the assembly and said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan.
Qianfeng said, "The head cook shall not be required to join the communal labor tomorrow. The Master said, "Mutually..."
"Seeing this, there is no need for anger; you are destitute and I am poor as well. "I say that while you claim to rise early, there are still those traveling by night.
Chan Master Zhongji Shanneng of Fuzhou was a native of Yanling. He had traveled back and forth between Longmen and Yunju for many years without attaining any realization.
One day, while they were engaged in communal labor (pǔqǐng) of weeding vegetables, Gao'an suddenly threw a cat into the Master's arms.

The Master was about to deliberate, when Chan’an lunged forward, seized him by the chest, and kicked him down. Thereupon, the Great Matter was clearly understood. He ascended the hall and said: "Ten thousand ages of eternal sky;

a single day of wind and moon. One must not let the eternal sky of ten thousand ages be obscured by the wind and moon of a single day, nor must one fail to clarify the wind and moon of a single day through the eternal sky of ten thousand ages. But what, then, is the wind and moon of a single day? Everyone..."
Fearing the heat, I cherish the length of summer days. A fragrant breeze comes from the south, bringing a subtle coolness to the halls and pavilions.
Whether you understand this or not, you must by all means refrain from taking it upon yourself.
Chan Master Yunju Puyun Ziyuan of Nankang Commandery was the son of the Yong family from Mianzhou. At the age of nineteen, he passed the scriptural examinations and received full ordination.
He remained in the garden of the teachings for five years before crossing the pass and traveling south. There, he visited various eminent masters in succession; eventually, he went to Longmen.
One day, while observing a painted image of a barbarian in the corridors, he attained a realization. That night, he reported this to Gao’an, who then raised [the following case]:
The Verse of the Dharma-Eye says: "Head adorned with a sable-fur cap, Waist girdled with a horned awl; His speech cannot be understood by others— One must have a person to translate it for them.
He then struck a match and showed it to him, saying, "I have finished translating it for you. Thereupon, the Great Dharma became clear and manifest. He presented this verse:
"The sounds and tones of foreign lands are inexhaustible, Yet beneath Qiyun Pavilion, they were all at once understood. [The Master’s] mouth..."
The gate is vast and boundless; it swallows up Yangqi’s “thorn-bush acorns. Master An sent him to rely upon Foyan.
Foyan said to him, "My Way shall go East. He ascended the hall and raised the following case: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya?"

The Gatekeeper said: "Hiding one's body within the Big Dipper. The Master said: "North, south, east, and west—ten thousand, ten thousand, a thousand; heaven and earth, above and below—both are boundless.
Meeting and seeing one another, we laugh 'he-he'; counting on our fingers and looking up, the moon is half-way through the sky."

Chan Master Xiaotui’an Xiū of Jianfu Monastery in Rǎozhōu, a successor of Chan Master Wùjù Xíng, ascended the hall and said: "Is it the wind that moves, or the banner that moves? Is it the wind that sounds?"

"The bell rings? "It is not the wind that makes the bell ring; it is not the wind that moves the banner. This land and the Western Heaven are but a single pair of black lacquered buckets, deceiving and deluding the people of the world.
Look, look—the Hu race is being extinguished! This mountain monk can do nothing about it; he chases after them and joins in the fray. The gourd is curved and bent;
the winter melon is straight and blunt. [Ascending the hall: At the time of the summer retreat, the left eye is half a catty.

At the conclusion of the summer retreat, eight *liang* were taken from his right eye. He merely claimed it was a ninety-day *an-gu* (summer retreat), yet he gained nothing but a belly full of delusive thoughts.
Even if one were to pierce through the seven apertures and eight openings, one could not avoid the mountain monk’s staff.

Nevertheless, a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt does not fire its trigger for a mere field mouse. [He] ascended the hall and said: "The former master constantly used a hammer behind the head to dismantle [delusions]."
This eliminates the many crookednesses within the scholars' chests. In his day, the Vinaya Master Kebin once encountered this poison from Xinghua;
often throughout the monasteries of the world, this is called "transcending the lineage and possessing a different eye. Not only does this betray Xinghua, but it also brings disgrace upon Kebin.
If one were a true descendant of Linji, they would never merely cling to the grass or attach themselves to the wood. Zifu was pleased.
Seeing his fellow practitioners, he emptied his heart and poured out his guts this day. He then planted his staff upright, gave a shout, and said: "Do you know where the former master fell?
You dead-end Zen monks are as numerous as hemp and millet! He ascended the hall and said: "When speech issues forth, it is not sound—what is this?
Before form, there is no object; do not confuse the needle and the chisel. Having passed through the Dragon Gate, the wind and waves become even more perilous. *Du!* (A shout)"
Chan Master Huiguan of Guifeng in Xinzhou, a native of Jianning, ascended the hall and said:

"For several days the heat has been like that of a furnace; this whole body has nowhere to rest. To contemplate it thus is already a source of affliction for people. This is not yet the true affliction;
rather, when there are matters regarding one's own fundamental nature that remain unclarified, that is truly affliction. Therefore, Bodhidharma..."
The Master was vexed. He wished to swallow all people at once, but his throat was too narrow; he wished to spit them all out, but his teeth were in the way.
Unable to take them and unable to let them go, he remained in this state of vexation for nine years.

Had he not been willing to sacrifice his own life for the sake of the Second Patriarch, there would have been no way for him to turn his body [toward enlightenment]. He was so vexed that he wished for death, which is what is meant by "the patriarchal lineage remains unresolved."
The calamity extends to their descendants. Later, when the Hermit of Lotus Peak arrived here, he was vexed and refused to stay.
When Nanyue Huairang arrived here, he was vexed and refused to leave the mountain.

Furthermore, Linji and Deshan exhausted all their own efforts, yet they were vexed that their alms bowls lacked handles. Today, Guipeng creates endless trouble for them on account of this idle matter.
"Clear! For all of you, I shall break it open from the very beginning. He struck the meditation staff once and said, "One person has his cheek exposed behind the head;
another has no teeth at the front door; and there are several more whose nostrils are missing half. No need for further investigation."
All of you, do not stand here drowsing; you simply do not realize that the rice baskets and cooking pots in your own homes have all been lost at once.
If you do not believe me, simply go home and check for yourselves.
Chan Master Shouren of Qian’an at Changlu in Zhenzhou was a native of Shangyu in Yue. He relied upon Xuedang at Wugu, where he heard a general discourse (pǔshuō) which said:
"The way our fellow practitioners nowadays apply themselves to their practice is just like learning archery: first, one must steady one’s feet."
Later, he practiced that method. Although he had no conscious intent, because of his long practice, every arrow he shot hit the mark.

He let out a shout, saying, "The arrow is released right now! Look! Look! The Master unconsciously threw himself down, making a gesture of dodging the arrow, and suddenly attained great enlightenment.
He ascended the hall and said: "Of the hundreds of thousands of samādhis and immeasurable wondrous gates, today I shall, for the sake of this hut, not spare my very life and simply perform—"
"I have a single phrase to say to you all," he said, then stood his staff upright and descended from the seat. He once offered this verse on the story of the Old Lady of Mount Tai:
"He opened a shop for lamp-wicks and soap nuts, Seeking a pint or two daily to pass the days and nights.
Because the wind and rain have persisted so long, Both principal and interest are lost; now he leans wearily against his gate."
Master Ruru of Qingyuan in Jizhou was a successor in the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Baifeng Shun. A monk asked, "What is it like before Bodhidharma arrived?
The Master said, "A cast-iron K'un-lun. The monk asked, "What is it like after he arrived? The Master said, "A five-colored painted door-god."
Chan Master Yuanji Yancen of Yingjing in Taiping State was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yunju Ru. He was a native of Taicheng. Entering the hall, he said:
"Han Xin’s assault on the pass could not avoid wounding his blade and injuring his hands; Zhang Liang’s burning of the granaries was much like a tortoise dragging its tail. Since this is the case..."

The four seas and the nine provinces are all brought under the imperial transformation. You. Ascending the hall, [the Master] cited the case of Chan Master Zhengtang Bian, who asked his students in his quarters: "Why does the earthworm transform into a lily? The Master said:

Chan Master Bao’en Cheng of Ezhou ascended the hall and said: "The autumn rains have brought a sudden chill.

Chan Master Juebao Qing of Pingjiang Prefecture, successor to Chan Master Daochang Bian, ascended the hall and said: He cited a monk’s question to Yunmen: “What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?

Ascending, the rocks press down upon bamboo shoots that emerge askew; on the precipitous banks, flowers hang with their blooms turned downward.
The head seat Renshou of Mount He in Anji Prefecture was a native of Gusu.

Having served Zhengtang for a long time, during one occasion when he entered the room for instruction, Tang asked, "Why does the cat always prefer to catch mice? Renshou replied, "When an object meets its master, its eyes stand bolt upright. Tang was pleased.

Zen Master Xiangxi Jixiu of Chengdu Prefecture, a successor of Zen Master Huanglong Zhong, ascended the hall and cited the public case of Mazu’s Illness, saying:

Where the two wheels are raised, smoke and dust arise; swift as lightning, rushing like a shooting star—what could possibly stop them? Before one’s eyes, the mechanism of coming and going is unimpeded;
the True Command is fully deployed, without inside or outside. The spirit of the great man naturally pierces the heavens: "I am I, and you are you."
Master Xishi Xixiu, the second-generation successor of Master Xichan Lian of Suining Prefecture, ascended the hall and said: "The autumn light is nearly at its midpoint;

The dew is like pearls. Even if one were to encounter such a brilliant opportunity, one would still not avoid mistaking a tortoise for a turtle.

Tell me, how do you express the phrase that accords with the time and the season? "The wild colors merge into the moon over the Three Islands; the stream’s radiance divides the autumn of the Five Lakes."
Chan Master Wuxiang Fadeng of Jingju Nunnery in Wenzhou, successor to Chan Master Wen of Jingju Nunnery, ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he struck it and said:
"Avalokiteśvara comes out; Samantabhadra enters. Mañjuśrī stands on the water wearing boots. Lifting his head, the hawk flies over to Silla. *Shihuo* (a spark from flint).
"A flash of lightning cannot be pursued.

*Du!* Chan Master Yonggu Zonglian of Yuyuan in Jingmen Commandery, a dharma successor of Chan Master Daomiao Guo of Dayue, was the son of the Dong family of Hezhou. On the day he ascended the hall, a question was asked:

Having answered, he said: "When a patch-robed monk engages in a question-and-answer session before an assembly of devas and humans—employing seizing and releasing, contracting and expanding, pushing and pressing—he must possess the adamantine eye to succeed.
As for those who merely parrot words, you go to West Qin while I go to East Lu; they are of no benefit whatsoever within the School of the Patriarchs. This...
This matter does not reside in speech, nor does it reside in silence; it is neither obstructed by speech nor obstructed by silence.
When the ancients offered a single word or half a phrase, it was like a state’s weaponry—employed only when there is no other choice.

Whether spoken horizontally or vertically, the sole purpose was to guide people toward the point of entry. In reality, it does not reside within words and phrases. People of the present day are unable to grasp this.
To directly penetrate and realize the root source, yet to take mere words and letters as the ultimate Way— coming with one phrase and going with another,
calling this "Chan" and "the Way," calling it "upward" and "downward," referring to it as "Bodhi and Nirvana," or as "the nostrils of the Patriarchs"—
is truly like leaving Zhengzhou only to arrive at Caomen. Among the assemblies of the ancestral masters of old, such instances have often occurred in reality.
Those who take the practice of pilgrimage as their primary task, as soon as they encounter a point of doubt, immediately resolve it before the assembly.

Through a single phrase, they realize the truth with clarity, establishing the direct, untransmitted school of the Buddhas and Patriarchs for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the bounds of the future.
To attain and realize together is still not yet the place of ultimate rest; how could it be merely opening one’s lips to babble words of Han or Hu?

Therefore, Nanyuan addressed the assembly, saying: "In other quarters, people possess only the eye for the simultaneous moment of the chick pecking and the hen pecking, but they do not possess the function of the simultaneous moment of the chick pecking and the hen pecking.
At that time, a monk asked: "What is the function of the simultaneous moment of the chick pecking and the hen pecking? Nanyuan said: "A master."
"Not by pecking or hatching; if one pecks and hatches at the same time, one loses. The monk said, "This is still the point where a student asks.
The Master said, "What is your own point of inquiry? The monk said, "I have lost it. The Master then struck him. That monk did not attain realization. Later, he went to the assembly of Yunmen.
Because two monks brought up this story, one monk asked, "At that time, why did Nan-yuan’s staff break?
That monk suddenly attained awakening and immediately returned to Nan-yuan, but the Master had already passed away. At that time, Feng-xue was serving as the *karmadāna* (steward).

He asked, "Are you the monk who asked about the 'simultaneity of the hen pecking and the chick hatching' to the late Master? The monk replied, "I am. Feng-xue said, "How did you respond at that time? The monk said:
"At that time, I was as if walking within the shadow of a lamp. Xue said, "You understand. The Master then called to the assembly, saying:
"Darkly threading the jade thread; closely weaving the golden needle. Like water entering water; like gold meeting gold. I dare ask the assembly:"
The simultaneous moment of the chick pecking and the hen hatching is the point of intimacy; why, then, do you miss it?

If you can understand this, you will be worthy of repaying the unrequited debt of gratitude and assist in the transformation of non-action. You may then cast yourself across the universe and stride alone through the Great Way.
If you cannot leap out, you remain as before beneath the rack. [Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "It shatters the darkness of ignorance and cuts off..."
To cross the stream of birth and death, to traverse the city of the three realms of existence, and to sail upon the sea of non-action, one must first recognize this very thing.
He then called to the assembly, saying: "If you call it a staff, you strike against it; if you do not call it a staff, you turn your back on it. If you can recognize it..."

"Letting go in the midst of thorns; casting oneself across the sea of right and wrong. If you have not yet realized this, then Universal Worthy rides his white elephant, and the Earth-Ruler mounts his clay ox.
*Chan.* [The Master] ascended the hall and said: "All these numbered phrases—what connection do they have with my numinous awareness?
The Master said, "Yongjia speaking thus is much like seeking Chang'an while already atop the Han-yuan Palace."

Little do they realize that wherever there is water, it contains the moon; and no mountain exists that does not carry clouds. Although this is so, thirty years hence, Old Lady Zhao will be selling vinegar.
Entering the hall, he said: "When the Dharma-vehicle is proclaimed once, divergent paths are severed; the myriad distinctions and thousandfold differences are all extinguished.
Though one has a mouth all over one's body, it is difficult to explain or clear away. Three pounds of iron behind the Diamond [Head]. "Good brother," a monk asked.

What was the meaning of this? The Master said, "The gentleman is moved by profit. [Sansheng] asked, "Was it because there were eyes in the staff, or did he act according to the occasion?
The Master said, "A monkey tied to a pillar. [Sansheng] said, "As for what Sansheng said—'If you lead people in such a way, you will blind the people of Zhinzhou'—"
"City-person’s eye. [The monk asked: "And how about this? The Master said, "Adding another layer of flowers upon brocade.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when a traveler encounters people? The Master said, "One is not; two are not. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when a traveler does not encounter people?

[The monk] said, "It is born. The Master said, "An iron stone egg submerged in water. [The monk] asked, "Regarding the Way of the Three Sages: 'When I meet a person, I come forth;
